abstract: The trial for former PA House Democratic Whip Mike Veon will go into its sixth week. Veon is accused of directing state bonus money for campaign work while he was in office. The outcome of the case will determine how the proceedings of the corruption trials of PA Representative Bill DeWeese and PA Rep. John Perzel will go. It will also have an impact on PA Attorney General Tom Corbett's gubernatorial election outlook.

headline: An Unproductive Bump
abstract: Since there haven't been many layoffs in government until recently, bumping provisions in civil service regulations or labor contracts have been passed forward over the years with minimal scrutiny. When cuts do happen, an individual who is axed in a layoff takes the job of someone with less seniority, it can set off a domino effect. The bumped person bumps another, who bumps another and so on.

headline: Voices multiply for Sestak to come clean
abstract: Republican Pat Toomey has joined the chorus pressuring Democrat Joe Sestak to disclose exactly who at the White House offered him exactly what administration position in exchange for dropping out of the U.S. Senate primary. Sestak had previously defeated Democrat U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, who was heavily favored by the President Barack Obama, in the Democratic senatorial primaries

headline: Chamber's anti-Sestak ad revised a little, back on air
abstract: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce was forced to change its anti-Sestak ad in order to be allowed on the air at some PA television stations.  The Sestak campaign successfully exposed the ads as false.  The ad claimed that Sestak had a 100% voting record with Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi.

headline: Toomey kicks off his bus tour
abstract: US Senate Candidate Pat Toomey, 48, a former congressman from the Lehigh Valley and a former small-business owner who also worked on Wall Street, kicked off his four-day bus tour across Pennsylvania, sharing his vision. Toomey and Joe Sestak, 58, are seeking the seat now held by US Senator Arlen Specter, a Republican-turned-Democrat whom Sestak beat in the May primary.

headline: Parking perks would outweigh price hike, CEO says
abstract: The chairman and CEO of LAZ Parking, which would manage 12 garages and 8,000 street meters in Pittsburgh citywide under a proposed 50-year lease, is going to the corporate community to pre-empt any complaints, brandishing a package of enhanced services meant to take the pain out of inevitable jumps in parking prices. Business owners are likely to be among those most affected by the proposed parking lease, which would roughly double Downtown hourly rates at city-owned garages. Despite that impact, the corporate community has been publicly silent on the proposed lease, floated by Mayor Luke Ravenstahl in an effort to raise money to shore up the city's depleted pension fund.

headline: Obama: Hire Rendell, He'd make a good chief of staff
abstract: The author feels that President Obama has done a poor job of highlighting his accomplishments, articulating a strategy, and exploiting opportunities. He feels that PA Governor Ed Rendell and Michigan Governor Jennifer Granholm would both make a great chief of staff for Obama. The author favors Ed Rendell, because of his varied experience in Pennsylvania.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: GOP Blocks COLA Increase
abstract: House Republicans thwarted a Democratic effort to award $250 checks to Social Security recipients facing a second consecutive year without a cost-of-living increase. President Obama and Democrats urged approval of the one-time payment, saying seniors barely getting by on Social Security checks faced undue hardships without the COLA increase.

headline: Federal Money for Rail Projects Does Not Include Scrant...
abstract: Although President Obama made high speed rail projects his top priority on Thursday afternoon, one local project--one that would restore passenger rail service between New York City and Scranton--was not on the funding list.

headline: Revenue must increase or taxes go up, Rendell tells area business leaders
abstract: Governor Rendell stated that his budget proposal that would tax Marcellus Shale extraction and lift 69 tax exemptions is necessary for the state to avoid a fiscal "tsunami" ahead of the end of federal stimulus money in 2012 and pension payments due in 2013.  The state needs revenue in order to avoid financial troubles.

headline: Impact on bay cleanup not known
abstract: Marel Raub, PA Director for the Chesapeake Bay Commission during a House Majority Policy Committee hearing Tuesday at Lycoming College, said that while the impact of shale development on Chesapeake Bay cleanup goals is uncertain. The PA Department of Environmental Protection's expedited permitting process, does not give citizens and concerned agencies enough time to review and comment on potential impacts, Raub said.

headline: Crimes in Pittsburgh fall for 3rd year
abstract: Crime in Pittsburgh fell for the third straight year in 2009 as reported by FBI statistics. The city's declines in both property and violent crime mirror a nationwide trend, the statistics show. In Pittsburgh, violent crime fell 8.07 percent and property crime was down 6.7 percent. Violent crime was down 2.8 percent in 2008, and just 1.4 percent in 2007. Homicides fell 45.8 percent -- from 72 in 2008 to 39 last year. Deputy Chief Paul Donaldson said the drops can be attributed to the  "nurturing of partnerships between the police and the community".

headline: State DEP criticized over new discharge permit
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Protection  has issued a water discharge permit that will eventually stop the illegal discharge of polluted water from the workings of RRI Energy.  Citizens for Pennsylvania's Future, the Sierra Club, Defenders of Wildlife and PennEnvironment praised the DEP for its renegotiation of the water discharge permit.

headline: Road, bridge woes aren't going away
abstract:
PA Governor Ed Rendell, talking Monday about addressing the state's very real crisis in meeting its highway, bridge and mass transit needs, said the time to act is now. Rendell, despite stating the urgency of the transportation problems in the commonwealth, appears to be in the distinct minority.
The immediate barrier to action, is the election coming in a couple of months.

headline: GOP ad attacking Manchin embarrasses Raese camp
abstract: Republican John Raese's surprisingly robust US Senate campaign against West Virginia Democrat Joe Manchin was dealt an embarrassing blow Thursday when it was revealed that "hicky"-looking actors were sought for a GOP attack ad on the governor. The GOP pulled the ad within hours of a report by Politico, but the damage was already done. Down in the polls to Mr. Raese, Mr. Manchin's team has lately been trying to tag the wealthy industrialist as out of touch with regular West Virginians.

headline: Charter school in Penn Hills in 2012?
abstract: A Carlow University faculty member has submitted a proposal to make a charter school in Penn Hills School District. The new curriculum would focus on critical thinking, and the creation of a micro-society of government, business and other community entities within the school. A charter school is funded by school district funds but operates independent of the district and must provide an educational program that is different from what is offered in district schools.

headline: Officials outline city's plan for snow removal
abstract: Pittsburgh’s Public Works Department has designated 220 miles of ‘emergency snow routes in anticipation of heavy snowfall. A map delineating the routes will be posted on the city website and included in a brochure that will be sent to all city households.

headline: Monica Yant Kinney: Ed Rendell, Capitol wordsmith
abstract: Stephen A. Cozen, an influential Philadelphia lawyer with political ties to Governor Rendell, was instrumental in getting legislative approval for the Foxwood's casino.  Cozen donated 143,000 dollars to Rendell's gubernatorial campaign and was able to get a face-to-face extension for his stalled South Philadelphia casino project.

headline:
County drops objectionable mental health agency name
Department of Mental Health and Mental Retardation/Early Intervention is now Mental Health and Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
abstract: Chester County commissioners have dropped the name "retarded" from the name of the county's mental health facilities citing the words offensive nature. States across the country have banned the word while adopting other words to take its place. Rosa's Law at the federal level took the word out of all federal publications and documents.

headline: Experts: Hospital report card needs easy language
abstract: Consumer advocates are giving Illinois fairly good marks for an online report card meant to allow patients to choose hospitals based on their quality and safety records. Patients can use the Web-based tool to see how their hospitals measure up on safety, nurse staffing levels and even prices. But national patient safety experts say they want the report card to use plainer language.

headline: Would higher gas tax offset car repairs?
abstract: An author writes that  Karl P. Sieg, vice president of the American Society of Civil Engineers' Pittsburgh has an idea that will provide dedicated funding for transit in PA. A 25-cent-per-gallon increase in the state gasoline tax (or "user fee" as Mr. Sieg calls it) would raise more than $1.5 billion. For a driver who goes 15,000 miles a year at 25 miles per gallon, the annual cost would be $150. Sieg says, "...for less than half what we pay each year to repair the damage to our cars caused by worn-out roads, we could fix the roads.." The ASCE, released its 2010 Report Card for Pennsylvania's Infrastructure, assigning it a D overall and a D minus for roads and public transportation.

headline: Program at Pitt helps felons become their own bosses
abstract: Convicted felons are being trained to be entrepreneurs under a new program aimed at getting those convicted of felonies a chance at a normal life outside of prison.  The program is part of the Institute for Entrepreneurial Excellence in the Katz Graduate School of Business at Pitt and was done in conjunction with the Mon Valley Initiative with funding from the Heinz Endowments.  Students attend a class once a month and learn techniques by listening to speakers.

headline: Do something
abstract: A study recently estimated it would take about $3.5 billion annually to fully fund the state's transportation needs. As a result PA Governor Ed Rendell is urging the state legislature to take action to repair the states 5,646 structurally deficient bridges, the most in the country, and more than 10,000 miles of roadway in need of repair.

headline: Rep. Kotik eyes House speaker post
abstract: PA Representative Nick Kotik, 60, announced his candidacy for Speaker of the House at a news conference at the Capitol Wednesday. He was first elected to the House in 2002 and represents a number of the western suburbs in Allegheny County. He was a staunch opponent in June 2009 of Governor Ed Rendell's call for increasing the state income tax.

headline: Johnstown train station given to heritage group
abstract: The Johnstown train station, established in 1916, was once a bustling transportation hub. The station, which has fallen into disrepair, has new owners who are hoping to inject new life into the station. The new owners hope to have the station reopened in 2011.

headline: Local congressmen explain tax votes
abstract: Four U.S. congressmen representing parts of Berks County give reasons behind their votes on extending current tax rates, set under former President George W. Bush.

headline: County councilman tries to stop closing of UPMC Braddock
abstract: Allegheny County Councilman Charles P. McCullough filed suit against the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center on Monday in a last-ditch effort to stop the scheduled Jan. 31 closing of the UPMC Braddock hospital.

headline: Editorial: Attention to county's health is overlooked
abstract: A report from the University of Wisconsin Population Health Institute and the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation ranked Delaware County the 36th healthiest county in Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania was also ranked 47th in the United States in funding from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention by the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation.

headline: State reps: County failed to send gun permit notices
abstract: PA Representative Phyllis Mundy, D-Kingston, and Representative Ed Staback, D-Archbald sent a letter to the Luzerne County Sheriff's Office on March 29.  The letter said that the Sherriff's office has not been complying with a state mandate to notify gun owners when a license to carry a concealed weapon is about to expire, according to two state legislators.

headline: Pennsylvania Sen. Jeffrey Piccola to propose extending mayoral control of Harrisburg School District
abstract: Pennsylvania's 10-year-old Education Empowerment Act, which handed the district’s reins to the mayor, is to expire at the end of June. Republican state Senator Jeffery Piccola of Dauphin county has introduced a proposal that would extend Mayor Linda Thompson’s control of the city schools for three years. Members of the elected school board were outraged by Piccola’s plan, but still doubted it would go far in the Capitol.

headline: Agency rated 'psychologically healthy'
abstract: VisitPittsburgh, Allegheny County's official tourism promotion agency was chosen by the Pennsylvania Psychological Association to receive the Psychologically Healthy Workplace Award.  The awards recognize workplaces that make a commitment to well-being.  VisitPittsburgh is a nonprofit agency with 81 employees.

headline: Doctors urge caution as state sees more whooping cough
abstract: Earlier this month, PA health officials put out a health advisory warning that there had been an uptick in whooping cough cases since April, especially in the Philadelphia suburbs. The state announced this week that it was offering several free vaccine clinics in York and Delaware counties to encourage residents to keep their vaccines for the disease up to date.

headline: Allegheny County Health Department avoids closure
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department has avoided a state order to vacate Building One in its Clack Health Center complex in Lawrenceville by simply closing the door on a second-floor bathroom in the building where a series of inspections had found unhealthy levels of lead dust. Health Department Executive Director Bruce Dixon said on Wednesday that the PA Department of Labor and Industry "retracted" the order to vacate the building that was to take effect Saturday.

headline: Port Authority shifts to holiday schedule for Thanksgiving
abstract: A public transportation announcement: Port Authority bus, T and incline service will operate on holiday schedules for Thanksgiving. The authority’s customer service phone line will have special holiday hours, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The downtown service will not be in service on Thanksgiving.

headline: 12 News at 12:30
abstract: Advocates of a single payer health bill currently pending in the PA legislature are working to make their case to the public. The executive director of a group called Healthcare 4 All says Governor Ed Rendell s committed to signing the reforms into law.

headline: Harrisburg considers major tax hikes, asset sales to avoid bankruptcy
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson is hopeful that by implementing some recommendations proposed by a financial consulting firm that the city might be able stave off bankruptcy.  The report lists 21 actions it says the city needs to take to avoid the bankruptcy court.

headline: Countdown begins for 2010 census
abstract: Local governments across Pennsylvania are attempting to promote residents to fill out the 2010 census forms to gain access to federal funds. The article highlights Pittsburgh's efforts to get local residents to be census workers in their local neighborhoods as a way to quell fearful perceptions of the census.

headline: Inmates bilk Uncle Sam for millions
abstract: Investigators say Monroe County jail inmates in Key West, Florida had been filing false tax return forms for jobs they never had as far back as 2004, and getting thousands of dollars a pop in refund checks. The indictments charging them and their family members with conspiracy to defraud the Internal Revenue Service and filing false income tax returns came four years after the IRS was notified of discovery of the scheme in 2006.

headline: Formula could cost Phila.'s needy students free lunch
abstract: A proposal in Congress would establish free lunch eligibility by a family's presence on food-stamp and welfare rolls, a method known as direct certification. Philadelphia's own system called Universal Feeding, could be threatened by the new law. The change could deny free lunches to as many as 51,182 students - 46 percent of the Philadelphia children who now receive those meals. Free lunch eligibility in Philadelphia is calculated using the family's income. But critics say surveys like Philadelphia's are too expensive and complex for most school districts- direct certification is the more workable model. US Senators, Bob Casey and Arlen Specter support Philadelphia's program.

headline: The Orie case: Plenty of questions deserve their day in court
abstract: After testimony in the Orie case reached a third day, Judge McDaniel ordered state Sen. Jane Clare Orie, R-McCandless, and her sister, Janine Orie, held for trial.  Although the case does not reach the level of corruption uncovered in the Bonusgate scandal, the case still has merit and many unanswered questions.

headline: DiFrancesco sees threat in burner debt
abstract: Nick DiFrancesco acknowledges that the issue of debt will remain after he departs as a Dauphin County commissioner. The county, along with Harrisburg, is a guarantor of the $288 million debt on the incinerator, which hasn't been generating the cash needed to service that obligation.

headline: Rendell urges action on Marcellus Shale tax
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wrote a tough letter Wednesday to Republican Senate leaders, urging them to stop stalling and meet with House leaders to forge an acceptable compromise tax on the natural gas that's pumped from underground Marcellus Shale. Rendell said the state needs the $100 million or so in revenue from the new shale gas tax to protect local roads and the environment from possible damage from shale drilling, as well as to fill a hole in the state budget. Some critics say the House's shale gas tax proposal would be the highest tax in the nation and would make Pennsylvania noncompetitive with other gas-producing states.

headline: Scranton mayor approves council's choice for auditor
abstract: Mayor of Scranton PA, Chris Doherty, signed legislation appointing Robert Rossi & Company as the city's auditor for 2010 through 2013. The total cost for all four years will be $192,000. The city council selected this company in a 3-2 election.

headline: MSNBC News Live
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell comments on the Tea Party movement’s size and impact on American politics.

headline: Williams raises possibility of race for governor
abstract: If he does nothing else by talking about a possible run for governor, State Sen. Anthony H. Williams says, he wants to raise the awareness of the four current Democratic candidates that they need to start openly addressing the concerns of black Pennsylvanians.  According to Williams, whether it be President Obama or Governor Rendell, Democrats win statewide elections only when they generate a large voter turnout in Philadelphia--and that means exciting African American voters to believe they have a strong stake in the outcome.

headline: Murtha's ex-aide Mark Critz gets Democratic support
abstract: Mark Critz, former District Director to the late US Representative John Murtha won local support from local Democratic district delegates, sending a message to the state Democratic executive committee as to who the district supports to fill the late congressman's vacant seat. Critz beat former PA State Treasurer Barbara Hafer.

headline: Carney, Kanjorski dominate fundraising in races for Congress
abstract: Democratic U.S. Representative Chris Carney in the 10th Congressional District race, raised $238,614.04 and spent $53,829.25 in the first quarter, leaving him with $665,190.95 cash on hand. U.S. Representative Paul E. Kanjorski in the 11th Congressional District race, raised another $258,828, spent $57,271.71 and had $1,175,948.77 left.

headline: Lawmakers consider Internet gambling bills
abstract: US Democrat Representative Barney Frank supports legalizing internet gambling which could bring in $42 billion dollars in revenue. The House is considering two Internet gambling bills. One would legalize it. The other would require people to declare winnings from online gambling to U.S. tax authorities and set a 0.25 percent tax on wagers of all federally licensed bets. Internet gambling is not actually illegal, but under a law that takes effect in June, it soon will be illegal for financial institutions to knowingly accept payment in online gaming transactions. The exceptions to the law are fantasy football and horse racing.

headline: Grant to help city deal with hospital layoffs
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh has been awarded $500,000 by the state Department of Labor and Industry.  It will be used to save the jobs of 1,500 West Penn Hospital employees in danger of being eliminated through health system consolidation.  West Penn Hospital's emergency room will still close and the number of beds will be reduced from 505 to 202.

headline: Nutritious school meals feed the fight against obesity
abstract: This month a child nutrition bill passed unanimously in the Senate, an issue of special interest for first lady Michelle Obama. The bill has since been referred to the House budget committee. Mrs. Obama called the bill, the Healthy, Hunger-Free Kids Act of 2010, a groundbreaking piece of legislation.

headline: Holy ignorance: Americans know less about religion than they think
abstract: According to the latest survey by the Pew Forum on Religion & Public Life, most Americans don't know what they're talking about when it comes to their faith or the religion of others. Incredibly, the survey says the most religiously informed group is atheists and agnostics, presumably because they make an effort to research the religions they're rejecting. The poor state of religious knowledge puts the fiery debates over Quran burnings and the ground zero mosque into perspective.

headline: Sewer project’s price tag: $55M
abstract: Johnstown lays at the bottom of the sewer line, which comprises 20 municipalities. When there is wet weather surface water rushes into the sewer system, causing an overflow of untreated waste. Marie Mock, a Johnstown Councilwoman, is urging for a public education on the matter. Residents at the top of the line may be ordered to fix illegally connected downspouts and drains.

headline: News 8 at 11:00
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell unveiled a plan allowing individuals who owe back taxes to pay without penalties. Applicants must apply for the program online.

headline: 2 students help determine speed limit for Lewis Township road
abstract: Two Marantha Christian School students are assisting the engineering firm Wentz and Webster to conduct a speed and safety study of Gold Road in Lewis Township.  At the end of the study, the two students will have a say in the speed limit for Gold Road.  The firm is trying to introduce the students to the field of engineering and how mathematics, physics and technical writing go hand in hand.

headline: All signs point to electric deregulation failure
abstract: An opinion piece by PA Representative Camille "Bud" George that discusses how deregulation of Pennsylvania's electricity company didn't produce lower prices through competition. He cited that energy companies charge a service reliability premium to customers meant to encourage more electricity generation. He claims that the citizens of Pennsylvania should demand the return of their service reliability premiums.

headline: Prosecutors want law changed
abstract: The law that makes it mandatory for children under the age of 8 to be restrained contains a provision that says, evidence a driver broke the restraint law cannot be used to prosecute the driver for any crime other than failing to restrain a child. Dauphin County First Assistant District Attorney Fran Chardo would like to see PA lawmakers change what they call a loophole in the state's child safety seat law.

headline: U.S. Senate race in Pennsylvania a toss-up after Sestak's victory over Specter, analysts say
abstract: This editorial discusses the election ahead for US Representative Democrat Joe Sestak against Republican Pat Toomey in the US Senatorial race. Analysts say US Senator Arlen Specter  (who changed parties earlier this year from Republican to Democrat) would have been an "easier target".  Now the race has become unpredictable.

headline: Pittsburgh public transit riders brace for a rough ride
abstract: The Port Authority is expecting to lose as many as 46,000 transit riders as a result of draconian cuts to their system.  The cuts could amount to 35% of overall service.  Many riders complain they would be cut off entirely.  Fifty neighborhoods would lose all of their bus service if the cuts go through.  Riders are urged to contact their legislators to express their concerns.

headline: Stimulus funds for battle against hospital-acquired infections
abstract: The Health Care Improvement Foundation of Philadelphia and the Washington, D.C.-based Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology, with support from the Pennsylvania Department of Health, said this week they are expanding and extending through December 2011 a collaborative effort aimed at reducing health care-associated clostridium difficult infections in southeastern Pennsylvania.

headline: Monroe, Pike not prime for gas drilling, says initial testing
abstract: When the Delaware River Basin Commission releases its regulations for companies that intend to drill Marcellus Shale in its watershed, the industry interest in the Poconos could rise. David Yoxtheimer, an extension associate at the Penn State Marcellus Center for Outreach and Research, said the region is not yet particularly well-mapped for Marcellus Shale density. According to PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources geology figures, a very small piece of Barrett Township is the only area of the county with deposits that could be as thick as 100 feet.

headline: Former President Bush names Romney as favorite GOP presidential contender
abstract: Former President George H.W. Bush wants former Massachusetts Gov. Mitt Romney to be the GOP's 2012 presidential nominee. The Republican party took back control of the US House and picked up six senate seats and seven governorships. Party officials feel confident in their ability to defeat incumbent US President Barack Obama in 2012.

headline: NBC 10 News at 4
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell, along with the Arts and Business Council of Greater Philadelphia, praised the arts community for its contributions to the city at an event at the Pennsylvania Convention Center.

headline: WHP CBS 21 Morning News
abstract: Governor Rendell said on "Face the Nation" that Republicans are refusing to work together with Democrats in the US Congress on job creation. He said that Democrats supported former US President George W. Bush's proposals but the Republicans won't show the same support with President Obama's policies. He called the meeting between US House Republicans and the president "discouraging."

headline: Obama pitches health care plan during visit to Pennsylvania college
abstract: US President Barack Obama made a speech at Arcadia University decrying insurance companies and urging healthcare reform.

headline: Attend forum on Pa. constitution convention
abstract: The League of Women Voters of Monroe County held a forum for those interested in learning about a constitutional convention at Stroudsburg Junior High School.

headline: Powerball, Mega Millions up again
abstract: Powerball's cash jackpot is up to $99 million after no one won it all Saturday night. Tomorrow's Mega Millions jackpot will be $64 million for the annuity, $41.8 million in cash.

headline: High humidity, sweltering temps to hit today
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department has issued a heat warning to residents saying that the heat on Thursday will be severe enough to cause problems for those with compromised health.  They suggest people affected stay indoors and that all people drink plenty of fluids.

headline: Prison assault reports Study finds incidents of rape, sexual assault at county lockup
abstract: A prison inmate report found 0.8 percent of inmates at the county prison in that time period were victims of nonconsensual sexual acts. Nationally, 2 percent of inmates in county jails reported being raped or sexually assaulted. The report found that 3.5 percent of the 231 inmates surveyed reported "sexual victimization," sexual activity, willing or unwilling, as well as touching in a sexual manner - at the county prison.

headline: Study: Hands-only CPR saves more lives in cardiac arrests
abstract: According to a new study more adults survived cardiac arrest when a bystander gave them continuous chest presses to simulate a heartbeat, compared to traditional CPR with mouth-to-mouth breathing. With hands-only CPR, advocates say, potential rescuers don't have to contemplate what for some could be the "yuck factor" of putting their mouth to an unconscious person's mouth and breathing for them. The rate of bystanders attempting any type of CPR increased from 28 percent in 2005 to 40 percent in 2009.

headline: Lehigh Valley middle school students to take Keystone Exams this spring
abstract: Seventh- and eighth-grade students will take the Keystone Exams for the first time this year. This exam could replace the PA System of School Assessments. If the U.S. Department of Education approves the change, Pennsylvania will use the biology, Algebra I and literature Keystones to track whether student test scores are on track with the requirements of the federal No Child Left Behind Act.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: State officials are working to add more staff to the new tax amnesty program, which allows people to pay their late taxes without penalties. They hope to increase the amount of phones lines available to people from 33 to 93.

headline: WHP CBS 21 Morning News
abstract: Governor Rendell says at least 11 Pennsylvania hospitals are volunteering to accept severely injured Haitians. Health officials said it is still unclear exactly when the victims may arrive, since the federal government activated more of its national disaster medical system.

headline: Auction draws hundreds of railroad devotees
abstract: The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission held a deaccession auction to sell off outdated and old Pennsylvania railroad items. Money made from the auction will be used to buy more artifacts for the PHMC and not to go to the state's general fund.

headline: Blue Cross, Aetna fast-tracking parental coverage for children under 26
abstract: Two major health insurance companies, Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania and Aetna, announced their decision to accelerate the commencement of the federal program allowing young adults to stay on or return to a parent's insurance policy until age 26. The federal law is not set to take effect until Sept. 23, prompting Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania’s decision to move forward with the plan starting June 1 to bypass coverage gaps for recent college graduates.

headline: Phila. D.A.'s Office anticipates changes in tracking data
abstract: District Attorneys over the years say they were not interested in numbers, that is when the Philadelphia Inquirer performed an investigation that showed nearly two-thirds of all defendants accused of violent crimes walked free of all charges. Current Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams, has now obtained a $492,000 grant to equip his office with software that, for the first time, will be able to routinely produce conviction data.

headline: Sands lets the games begin
abstract: Gamblers lined up for the chance to be the first to gamble at the state's new table games that have been introduced at the Sands Casino Resort in Bethlehem.  The article interviews a number of gamblers including one who plays poker professionally.  He hopes to make up to $300 a day to pay the bills.

headline: Senator discusses state issues with locals
abstract: PA Senator John Eichelberger, R-Hollidaysburg, discussed the budget deficit, roadways, pensions, the private sector and excessive state expenditures with members of the public Thursday at the Allensville Community Hall. For the 2011 budget, the PA Senate is expecting a real increase in state gross domestic product and tax revenue of 3.2 percent, but Eichelberger is less optimistic.

headline: In Business With Margaret Brennan
abstract: According to the Washington post interim Chief of Staff Pete Rouse is the anti-Rahm Emanuel, who is all staff, and Rahm Emanuel is all chief.

headline: The Spectrum, Stalwart Philly Arena, to Be Razed
abstract: A wrecking ball will soon drop on the more than 40 year old Spectrum, a Philadelphia arena for professional sports and entertainment. The 76ers and the Flyers once called the spectrum home. Pearl Jam played the last show there on October 31, 2009. The arena is being demolished to make way for a retail, restaurant and entertainment complex.

headline: U.S. attorney nominee Zane Memeger clears Senate panel
abstract: President Barack Obama’s pick for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, Zane D. Memeger, was unanimously approved by members of the Senate Judiciary Committee. Once confirmed by the Senate, Memeger will lead an office of more than 130 attorneys that prosecutes all criminal cases brought by the feds and handles all civil actions brought on behalf of, or against, the U. S. The office has been without a Senate-confirmed appointee since the resignation of Patrick Meehan in 2008.

headline: WJAC-TV News at 6 PM
abstract: Governor Rendell will propose a bill to tax natural gas drilling in the Marcellus Shale region of Pennsylvania. The tax could raise millions in revenue that would either go to local governments, school districts, or the state budget.

headline: To advance healthcare reform, Obama comes down on insurers
abstract: US President Barack Obama, speaking at Arcadia University has railed against health insurance providers for raising healthcare premiums unjustifiably. Insurance providers, along with the group America's Health Insurance Plans, say that the majority of the cost increases should be blamed on hospital and healthcare providers. US Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius has called on insurance providers to publicly justify healthcare premium increases.

headline: World looks better as Earth Day turns 40, but work remains to be done
abstract: Many of the country's environmental initiatives, especially locally, are led by young people who devote time to organizing events at their schools and in their neighborhoods in an attempt to raise awareness. More than 1 billion people in at least 170 countries are expected to take part in Earth Day activities.

headline: STATE COLLEGE AREA SCHOOL DISTRICT: State College board considering swap suit
abstract: A State College Area school board meeting will be held to give details on the district's situation. Earlier in the year, State College Area school board voted 8-1 to cancel the district’s financial contract with the Royal Bank of Canada if the cost to do so was less than $5.5 million.  the actual amount will cost them more than $6million. The district decided to file a lawsuit against the bank.

headline: State initiatives disappear with dismal economy
abstract: State spending is down $3 billion since 2008, so the state government has been undertaking fewer projects.  These projects keep people employed and keep the economy moving in PA.  45 such programs have been eliminated over the last two years.  Stimulus dollars have masked the effect on surviving programs.

headline: Medicare to Cover Smoking Cessation
abstract: Thanks to the Affordable Care Act (ACA) Medicare will now cover tobacco cessation counseling the US Department of Health and Human Services announced. Of the 46 million Americans who smoke, about 4.5 million are Medicare beneficiaries over age 65.

headline: Fox 29 News at 11AM
abstract: Democratic party leaders worked the Sunday morning talk shows to minimize the damage in preparation for the mid-term elections. PA Governor Ed Rendell appeared on face the nation and argued President Obama has done a better job than people realize.

headline: Papers' new publisher, CEO to push digital content
abstract: Former President and Publisher of Newsweek, Greg Osberg, has been chosen as the new publisher and chief executive of the Daily News, Inquirer, and Philly.com. The announcement came less than two days after the papers’ former lenders successfully bid $135 million for control of the operation. Osberg’s work as CEO cannot officially begin until the auction results are approved by the bankruptcy judge and the sale is officially closed.

headline: 12 News Today
abstract: Governor Rendell will not be at a white house meeting with other great lakes states concerning the spotting of Asian carp near Lake Michigan. The fish threatens to devastate the populations of perch, walleye, and steelhead populations in the great lakes.

headline: Education funding: Something has to give -- but what?
abstract: The author states that the state should look closer at a costing-out study of Pennsylvania's public school that showed that the state's public school funding was $4.6 billion behind where it should be. This has prompted PA Governor Rendell to increase education funding in recent years. The author cites PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola's efforts to look closer at the costing-out study to develop a more cost-efficient school spending plan that gets the best results.

headline: DePasquale promotes jobs-related bills
abstract: State Rep. Eugene DePasquale, D-West Manchester Township, promoted a package of bills focused on job creation and retention, and business and workforce development. The bills include an employment and training tax credit for businesses, a plan to let employers reduce work hours instead of laying off workers, and expansion of current programs aimed at helping small businesses.

headline: New player emerges on NEPA drilling scene
abstract: Besides Encana Oil & Gas USA Inc., Tulsa, Okla.-based Williams, is planning to develop wells on Northeastern Pennsylvania's portion of the Marcellus Shale. Williams has obtained leases amounting to thousands of acres in Columbia County and hundreds of acres nearby in Luzerne County. Williams also owns a pipeline crucial for getting the gas to market. The US State Department of Environmental Protection records show Williams has recently been issued two gas well permits for Benton and one for Sugarloaf Township in Columbia County, but nothing for Luzerne County - yet.

headline: County transportation projects impacted by economy
abstract: Montgomery County officials are finding that their ambitions regarding transportation infrastructure are going to have to be pared back due to the economy.  Nothing new is expected to get started in the county.  The article lists the few projects that will be completed throughout the county.

headline: Collection efforts intensify
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue offered a tax amnesty program that enticed delinquent taxpayers to pay back taxes without penalties and for only half the interest that had accrued, which resulted in the recovery of $261 million in delinquent taxes. Since then, the revenue department dedicated more of its staff to its enforcement efforts.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 8
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is trying to stop rumors he's being considered for White House chief of staff position. Rendell says the rumors of him working for president Obama are "ludicrous." Former White House chief of staff Rahm Emanuel left the post to run for mayor of Chicago.

headline: Attorney: Levdansky won't challenge results
abstract: Rick Saccone has very narrowly beaten PA Representative David Levdansky in the race for the 39th Legislative District. His attorney has said that Levdansky will not challenge the results. Some attorneys nonetheless raise concerns over the lack of paper trail on Pennsylvania's touch screen voting machines.

headline: Friends, critics reflect on Christie's first 100 days
abstract: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie's first 100 days in office are profiled.

headline: Editorial: Build on this foundation
abstract: The author submits that US President Obama's proposal to revamp the nation's school system should not destroy the positive methods of former US President George Bush's No Child Left Behind Act. He said that the Obama Administration should try to modify parts of NCLB and not completely discount it.

headline: Wernersville State Hospital preparing for Allentown patients
abstract: Wernersville State Hospital is preparing to take in patients from Allentown State Hospital, which was shut down on January 28th by the PA Department of Public Welfare.

headline: Pennsylvania offers $500 rebates for home-heating upgrades
abstract: Rebates of as much $500 are being offered to Pennsylvanians who upgrade their home heating systems. The Department of Environmental Protection is urging residents to apply to “reserve” their share of the $11 million in federal money allotted for the program.

headline: Not for life: Non-capital juveniles deserve a shot at redemption
abstract: In a 5-4 ruling last week, the U.S. Supreme Court decided that young people serving life terms for crimes other than killing their victims must have an opportunity for parole. With the opportunity for parole, the majority said that would be cruel and unusual punishment. The editorial writer says that young people have been left out of this argument to their detriment and accuses some Justices of imposing their own morality onto others.

headline: It's time to end the special funds for state lawmakers
abstract: In an era of severe budget cutting, the continued use of "walking around money" is especially offensive to residents of PA.  While nobody is accusing such funds as being entirely wasteful, they money's use is not subject to the same democratic procedure as other expenditures.  The money often goes to worthy projects around the state.  The bottom line, however, is that walking around money is mostly just a use of taxpayer dollars to convince voters to vote for a candidate again.

headline: View from a classroom: The teacher's perspective
abstract: Critics blame teachers for students’ failure to reach state and federal mandates and PSSA benchmarks. Any rational person knows that there are myriad social and economic conditions that predestine many children to underachieve.

headline: The Last Word With Lawrence O'Donnell
abstract: The founder of fire dog,.com Adam Green has been critical of President Obama on health care and other policy issues as his presidency has gone on. PA Governor Ed Rendell, on the other hand has been Obama's biggest supporters. Rendell says the thing he hates in politics are robots who just will go along with anything and any kind of flip-flop or broken promise a politician does.

headline: Contract negotiations in progress
abstract: Teacher contract negotiations are heating around the state, but remain subdued in the Central Bucks School District. Leaders of Central Bucks Education have said that both sides are contributing to progress. The school board may want to introduce the salary matrix, which awards teachers who pursue masters and doctoral degrees with higher pay.

headline: Rendell calls for session on transportation funding
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has called for a special legislative session following the Federal Highway Administration’s rejection of the commission’s application to toll I-80. Rendell’s decision to call the session came as a result of Act 44 not providing a substitute revenue source to replace the proceeds from the tolling of I-80 if federal approval was not obtained.

headline: Pa. Gaming Board Head Questioned on Foxwoods License
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board has not decided what happens after they decide to pull Foxwoods Casino's license for a Philadelphia Casino. PA Representative Douglas Reichley said the legislature will be watching the situation closely.

headline:
Pitts calls for cuts
Deficit 'immoral,' he tells town hall crowd
abstract: US Representative Joe Pitts, representing the 16th district of Pennsylvania, says that government projections of new government programs are historically under-projected. He doubts the healthcare reform bill passed by congress, which Rep. Pitts has scrutinized for possibly costing more than the administration anticipates. He called the government's deficit "immoral."

headline: Holocaust survivor: 'Nobody should hate'
abstract: Hilda Matelmacher of Harrisburg, shares her experiences as a Holocaust survivor of the Auschwitz and Bergen-Belsen concentration camps.

headline: State will seek bids for new Family Court building
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said that the state would take over development of a new Family Court building in Philadelphia. Rendell said he would release the $200 million for the courthouse but would require competitive bids, even if that means delays, to make sure the project is removed from any conflicts of interest. The PA Governor's announcement means the apparent end of the court system's two-year-old development deal with Donald W. Pulver, a developer from Conshohocken. Philadelphia Chief Justice Ronald D. Castille and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter were also in attendance.

headline: Table Game Revenues Leap Out of Gate at Local Casinos
abstract: The first weekend of revenue results have come in for PA's new table games, and the news is good.  Vice-president for marketing Darlene Monzo at Bensalem's Parx Casino said that Sunday's first day of table games exceeded expectations.

headline: Rising enrollment strains, crowds Western
abstract: Colleges and universities in Western Pennsylvania and across the nation are coping with problems of increased freshman enrollment. Enrollment is rising because of a lack of jobs, employers' demands for a bachelor's degree and more older students returning to the classroom. A 2009 report by the National Center for Education Statistics projected that America's undergraduate enrollment will increase by 12 percent between 2007 and 2018.

headline: FOX 43 News at 6:30PM
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is celebrating a decline in medical malpractice cases in the state. Rendell says there was a 61 percent decrease since 2003 in payouts from the state's medical malpractice fund, or "m- care". This is the lowest it's been in 19 years, and the number of serious m-care claims has also dropped 44 percent.

headline: Teachers, district agree on arbitration
abstract: The Pennridge School Board and the district's teachers will continue to negotiate a contract. Both sides have agreed to use non-binding arbitration to help reach an agreement on a new contract. The union wants a five-year contract, which would raise salaries 2.47 percent a year on average.

headline: Creditors buy papers at auction
abstract: Philadelphia Newspapers L.L.C., which owns The Inquirer, the Philadelphia Daily News, and Philly.com, was bought by its largest debt holders after losing a bankruptcy auction to its senior creditors. The $139 million price tag included $39.2 million in debt and $69 million in cash equity, plus the value of the company’s real estate, estimated at $30 million for the purposes of the auction.

headline: City challenge: $100M + deficit
abstract: The City of Philadelphia is faced with a $100 million budget deficit for the 2010 budget that may grow to between $500 and $700 in the next five years. In order to plug the gap the Nutter Administration plans to cut city services and staff. The city has already made cuts to services like libraries.

headline: Pa. historical sites to offer free tours, survey visitors Sunday
abstract: Due to state budget cuts to the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission has forced state museums to come up with new ways to make money. The Drake Well Museum in Titusville has considered cutting days the museum is open. The PHMC will start getting input from locals as to how to better reach their visitors' needs.

headline: Rendell convenes special session of Legislature
abstract: A special session of the legislature will convene to deal with the issue of tolls for Interstate 80. Federal officials refused to approve the tolls, which the state was expecting to generate $472 million for roads, bridges, and mass transit. The discussion over interstate tolls is expected to coincide with the debate over adopting a new state budget of $28 million to $29 million for the new fiscal year beginning July 1.

headline: pennsylvania governor ed rendell was in new castle today making his case for increasing funding for education in the upcoming budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced plans to allocate an additional $354 million to education in the upcoming budget. Gov. Rendell said he plans on paying for the increase by taxing companies drilling for natural gas, enacting a tobacco tax, closing the Delaware loophole, and getting rid of the discount given to retailers who pay their sales tax on time.

headline: Problems arise at area drill sites
abstract: Neighboring property owners are complaining that new wells drilled in their areas are affecting drinking water.  This has led two companies to stop doing business in the area.  Chesapeake Energy Corp. of Towanda, Bradford County and T&F?Exploration of Pittsburgh are the owners of the wells in question.  One neighbor in particular in accusing the drilling of making his family's water taste salty.

headline: Night, passengers, phones can be deadly for young drivers
abstract: According to the Texas Transportation Institute (a Texas A&M-affiliated group that studies transportation issues) nighttime driving and distractions such as cell phones and passengers pose greater risks to young drivers than alcohol and speed. Proposed federal legislation would require states to adopt stricter driving guidelines for people younger than 18 before they could get their driver's licenses.

headline: Twin Tiers Tonight-Late Edition
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is urging state Senate leaders to enact a severance tax on natural gas extraction. In a letter to Senate president Joe Scarnati, Rendell says Scarnati hasn't offered any evidence of his intention to put he severance tax up for a vote in the senate before the session is adjourned. PA state police took 200 more trucks off the road last week, during another crackdown of trucks hauling gas drilling wastewater.

headline: War On Dissent Town Hall; Documenting a failed and dangerous US intelligence network (Videos)
abstract: The PA Office of Homeland Security hired the Institute for Terrorism Research and Response (ITRR) for intelligence services. A mistakenly sent email from the company's director shows that the "intelligence" reported almost exclusively on activities and events organized by anti-tax Tea Party, environmental, LGBTQ and animal rights activists who challenge the government and private sector interests. PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly have expressed their outrage.

headline: Recent Sales of Large Newspapers
abstract: Details of the recent sales of the Minneapolis Star Tribune, Newsday, and the San Diego Union-Tribune.

headline: Pittsburgh mentioned in Pistons' relocation speculation
abstract: Speculation has arisen suggesting a possible selling of the National Basketball Association franchise Detroit Pistons to an owner that would move the team to Pittsburgh. The owner of the Pistons is considering offers and its been suggested that Pittsburgh's new Consol Energy Center would be a suitable fit for an NBA franchise.

headline: Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania ends 2009 with $251 million surplus
abstract: Health insurance provider Blue Cross of Northeast Pennsylvania ended 2009 with a $251 million surplus. The surplus is substantially down from previous years due to a downturn in global markets and members moving out of the area. The non-profit also paid off operating losses to their subsidiaries and a payment to the Commonwealth Medical College.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: John Baer: Contrarian poll sees Specter and Sestak even
abstract: A poll shows Democratic Senator Arlen Specter in a virtual tie with challenger Joe Sestak.

headline: state budget is due in about four weeks
abstract: With the deadline for a state budget looming, PA Governor Rendell held a meeting of legislative leaders at the Governor's mansion. Gov. Rendell said he would have to lower his proposed $29 billion budget while Senate Democrats agreed that there would have to be some tax increases. The state faces a $1.5 billion budget deficit. PA Senator Dominic Pileggi said that there will have to be increased cooperation on the part of Gov. Rendell if they budget is to be passed on time.

headline: Casino revenue decreases property taxes for many
abstract: 177,000 homeowners in 30 districts in the middle of the state will get a combined $25.3 million break on their property taxes as a result of the windfall of casino revenues the state has experienced since legalizing gambling.  The average tax cut is $59.  Only a person's first home qualifies for the rebate.

headline: US Senate campaign is a race to the political middle
abstract: As many as 13 Senate seats are considered toss-ups this year, but the divergent voting records of US Representative Joe Sestak and former PA Representative Pat Toomey make the race for Pennsylvania's US Senate seat unique. The National Journal, ranked Toomey the third-most-conservative member of Pennsylvania's 19-member delegation in 2004, and ranked Sestak the fourth-most-liberal member last year.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 8
abstract: The state of PA will announce that 58 million social security recipients will not get a cost of living adjustment. this marks the second straight year that retirees won't get a rise in monthly benefits. US Congressman Todd Platts is currently working on a bill that would change the way adjustments for seniors are made.

headline: Quinnipiac poll: Toomey leads by 5 points, Corbett up by 10 points
abstract: A Quinnipiac University poll shows Republican US Senate nominee Pat Toomey leading Democrat incumbent Joe Sestak by 5 points. Also, the poll shows Republican nominee Tom Corbett beating Democrat Dan Onorato with 52 percent over 42 percent. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus 2.8 percentage points.

headline: First offshore wind farm in U.S. approved
abstract: The Obama administration has approved the $2 billion Cape Wind project, clearing the way for the nation’s first offshore wind farm. The project has faced much opposition from two Indian tribes, as well as environmentalists and residents, who warn the 130 windmills to be located 5 miles off Cape Cod could mar the ocean view. The lead federal agency reviewing the project, the Minerals Management Service, issued a report saying the project poses no major environmental problems.

headline: Stout leaving state Senate; DeWeese will run again
abstract: PA Senator Barry Stout announced that he will not run for re-election in 2010 while PA State Representative Bill DeWeese said he will run again.

headline: More local homeowners faced mortgage trouble in January
abstract: In the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre/Hazleton area, 6.9% of homeowners are over 90 days delinquent on their mortgages and 2.5% of them are facing foreclosure, up from 2009. However, The Real Estate Owned Rate is lower than in previous years. Economists have cited a stabling of the housing industry, indicating that lenders will start more foreclosures in the next year in order to sell properties.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Pay cut severe for most of tax board
abstract: A variety of op-ed pieces discussing issues within the city of Philadelphia concerning the PPA, Board of Revision of taxes, and the controversial Deferred Retirement Option Plan.

headline: governor rendell has signed the "pie bill"
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has signed the "pie bill" which would allow non-profit organizations to sell certain types of baked goods and not be cited for doing so.

headline: Better service draws traffic
abstract: More and more passengers are being attracted to Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport with the addition of American Airlines service to Chicago.  More traffic into the airport is also expected to lower prices for those wishing to fly from the area.  The passenger count has increased 3.1% from this time last year.  The airport is modern and attractive, but has not been as successful in marketing.

headline: PA Governor Ed Rendell is urging state lawmakers to take action
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is urging state lawmakers to take action, on the state's transportation funding shortfall. Rendell is looking to fill a multi-billion dollar transportation funding gap. some of the suggestions include, raising the gas tax, or increasing the fees for drivers licenses, and car registrations.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 5
abstract: US President Obama is pushing a $50 billion transportation plan to upgrade our nation's roads and create jobs. Governor Ed Rendell joined the president, as well as governors and mayors from around the country in support of this plan. Rendell says Obama's plan will help create jobs, especially in this struggling construction industry.

headline: Jobless rate here drops from 7.8% to 7.3%: Biggest month-to-month drop since 1996
abstract: The unemployment rate in Lancaster County fell from 7.8 to 7.3 percent in September 2010. The PA Department of Labor and Industry said this was the biggest month to month drop since 1996. Some think that this is a sign that a recovery to the economic downturn, which started in 2007, has taken root.

headline: IUP student wins Fulbright
abstract: Erin O'Brien, a history and Asian Studies double major in IUP's honors college, is one of 14 students in the nation that has been chosen for a Fulbright English Teaching Assistantship.

headline:
Sprague quizzed at Harrisburg hearing
Is the Pennsylvania Casino Assn. trying to influence legislators or educate the public? Opinions differ.
abstract: Chairman of the Pennsylvania Casino Association defended the PCA against not registering as a lobbyist group when they performed lobbying activities. The PCA said there activities did not fit the criteria of lobbying under state law but would register if no more allegations were brought as to them not previously registering. The also cited a conflict of interest between the board members and interests in the casino industry.

headline: State Dems back Critz
abstract: The Pennsylvania Democratic Party's executive board selected Mark Critz, former district director to late US Representative John Murtha, to run in the election to fill Murtha's unexpired term on May 18. A Republican candidate has not been announced.

headline: Social Security payments to be direct deposited
abstract: The Treasury Department announced its decision to eliminate about 136 million paper checks sent by the Social Security Administration, Department of Veterans Affairs, Railroad Retirement Board and Office of Personnel Management. The switch to direct deposit for most Social Security and other federal benefits payments will take effect by 2013.

headline: this is the second major problem at a marcellus shale gas well in the state in a matter of days
abstract: Two Marcellus Shale gas well explosions that happened in the matter of days have injured people. PA Governor Ed Rendell has ordered the company that owns the well, EOC Resources, to halt any drilling until an investigation is completed.

headline: Provide funds to fix roads
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell wants lawmakers to come back to work early to try and figure out the state's transportation infrastructure funding dilemma.  The federal government has put the brakes on the state's plan to toll I-80 across its northern tier.  The governor has advanced a plan including a series of tax and fee increases to help raise the money needed to fix the roads.  PA has 5,600 structurally deficient bridges and 7,000 miles of state highway that are in poor shape.

headline: Would you be willing to pay more for better roads?
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell believes most Pennsylvanians would be willing to pay for better roads, as result Rendell is proposing a plan to raise 1 billion dollars to fund transportation projects. The governor's plan would include measures such as raising registration fees, measures which many legislators are not willing to support.

newspaper: CNN - National Programming (Cable News Network) Cable
headline: CNN Newsroom
abstract: President Obama tried to pump up the democratic base at a rally in Pennsylvania, a state where his party could lose a number of seats in the mid terms. Pennsylvania's top democrat Governor Ed Rendell also spoke at today's rally. Rendell says that Republicans were with the same people who brought us to the brink of economic disaster, and the democrats and the President got rid of $60 billion that was going to companies.

headline: FDA Issues Warning to Four Loko, 3 Other Drink Makers
abstract: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued letters of warning to four companies that add caffeine to their malt alcoholic beverages. The products are being charged as unsafe. Under federal law the drinks could be seized. US Senator Charles E. Schumer led the charge against the companies.

headline: Dent leading Callahan
abstract: A poll showing Republican Charlie Dent with a 43 percent to 31 percent lead over Bethlehem Mayor John Callahan suggests a competitive race with the election still six months away.

headline:
Monica Yant Kinney: A high-energy welcome
Mural Arts has a bravura plan to spiff up the airport.
abstract: Philadelphia's transportation department, artists, and the mural arts program are teaming up to paint the largest mural in the city on the parking garages at the Philadelphia Airport. The exhibit called "How Philly Moves" will span half a mile and will feature poses of Philadelphians dancing.

headline: 'Drowning in Alzheimer's': Minorities struggle with dementia
abstract: According to an Alzheimer's Association report, minorities are more likely to have Alzheimer's disease. The study said the disease is not genetic but may be specific to the filial culture of minorities. Minorities are less likely to get medical care and typically insist on familial care rather than nursing home care.

headline: Veterans' disability claims should get greater respect
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter introduced a bill that would require the Veterans Court to excuse late filings upon a showing by the veteran of "good cause". The bill would apply not just to future appeals, but also to those already dismissed for failure to meet filing deadlines, so that appeals such as the one of retired Veteran David L. Henderson for in-home care would be reinstated.

headline: McDonald’s recalls millions of Shrek glasses made in N.J.
abstract: Glasses made in Millville, NJ have been recalled for containing the chemical Cadmium that the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission worries some children may ingest. The glasses were being sold nationally at McDonald's restaurants and were themed after the popular children's movie, Shrek. 12 million glasses have been recalled.

headline: Sepsis threatens hospital patients (and others), study finds
abstract: Using data from over 350,000 patients, researchers showed that sepsis occurred in 2.3% of those patients, and septic shock occurred in 1.6%.  They also found that the death rates of those afflicted by sepsis is far worse than those with other dangerous conditions.  Severe sepsis strikes an estimated 750,000 people per year in the US alone.

headline: Erie County Commissioner Grossman to push for the proposed community college
abstract: Erie County Commissioner Grossman said his meeting with PA Governor Ed Rendell about getting state finding for a proposed community college in Erie, was a success.

headline: ABC27 News Daybreak at 4:30am
abstract: The company that built the Dallas cowboys practice facility that collapsed during a storm in 2009, which injured a dozen people and paralyzed a coach has a number of buildings in PA. The PA Department of Transportation says the company behind that building has a bunch more here in midstate. PennDot now has to use 32- million dollars in tax money to replace the domes statewide.

headline: John Boehner Elected Next Speaker, Nancy Pelosi Will Lead Democrats
abstract: The November 2010 elections ended with the GOP in control of the US House. Minority Leader John Boehner will become Speaker of the House. He said he is committed to making the House into the "People's House." The House Democratic Caucus elected Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi as their leader for the next session of Congress.

headline: Free life insurance for low-income families
abstract: The Community Action Committee of Lehigh Valley and other Lehigh Valley nonprofits are joining Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Co. to give away free $50,000 term life insurance policies to benefit children of working families throughout the Lehigh Valley. Parents and legal guardians between the ages of 19 and 42 with at least one or more dependent children under the age of 18 are eligible to apply for the coverage.

headline: Hilton restructuring, not selling
abstract: The Hilton Pittsburgh Downtown will not be sold but will be restructured with other owners joining current owners Shubh Hotels Pittsburgh LLC. The restructuring plans will allow the hotel owners to continue with construction on an addition to the hotel that has remained unfinished after the contractor working on the addition walked off the job due to unpaid debts.

headline: Schools, borough mull prof's water test plan
abstract: Camp Hill School District agreed to test water in its five buildings for lead. The goal is to establish a baseline before Pennsylvania American Water begins flushing pipes this spring so it can be compared after chloramine is added. Chloramine's opponents have said the chemical causes lead to leach from water pipes, resulting in lead poisoning.

headline: High-rises fail to get census forms in mail
abstract: Residents of Philadelphia’s Society Hill Towers and another high-rise on the north side of the city did not receive U.S. Census forms in the mail due to mistakes in the address listings. While addressed questionnaires have been delivered to all units, those wishing to complete the form by telephone should call 1-866-872-6868.

headline: Bill to force city to cover parade-policing is vetoed
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter has vetoed a bill that would have forced the city to pay for police services at community and cultural parades and events. The mayor said the bill would have added $2 million in costs to the city in 2009. The bill was introduced by Councilwoman Maria Quinones Sanchez.

headline: Commissioners ratify regional agreement
abstract: Lycoming, Montour, Snyder, Union and Columbia counties are coming together to form a region solid waste plan.  Lycoming County's commissioners are the most recent county to ratify the agreement.  The state Department of Environmental Protection requires that a solid waste plan be updated every decade.

newspaper: CNN - National Programming (Cable News Network) Cable
headline: Fixing Pennsylvania's struggling economy
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell believes that the PA state government and the federal government need to do two things to turn around a poor economy. One thing the legislature needs to do is pass the small business bill which would $30 billion for small business loans, and secondly, the president's got to do something about infrastructure.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 8
abstract: Pennsylvania has joined a multi-state group as part of a mortgage probe. Sate attorney generals and mortgage regulators from all 50 states and the district of Columbia have banned together to investigate whether lenders or mortgage companies have violated consumer protection laws.

headline: State grant to help equip electric BARTA vehicles
abstract: Momentum Dynamics has been awarded a grant from the PA Department of Environmental Protection  to develop a cordless charging technology for two electric vehicles, which will be used by BARTA. The grant will purchase two paratransit electric vehicles with wheelchair lifts for use by BARTA, and will be outfitted to work with the to-be-developed charging system.

headline: Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs signs on hotel developer
abstract: Mohegan Sun has signed an agreement with a developer to build a $60 million, 300-room hotel. Robert Soper, president and CEO of the casino would not identify the developer, who would finance construction of the hotel. The construction is expected to take about 18 months.

headline: Pa. Sen. Stout to retire; Rep. DeWeese will not
abstract: PA Senator Barry Stout announced that he will not run for re-election in 2010 while PA State Representative Bill DeWeese said he will run again.

headline: Specter says alleged job offer to Sestak is a federal crime, if it happened
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter said that if US Representative Joe Sestak was offered a job in the Obama Administration in exchange for nut running against Specter then it was a federal crime.

headline: Specter, Sestak woo voters, trade jabs
abstract: Just one month out of the primary, Democratic Senator Arlen Specter and his Democratic primary challenger Joe Sestak have continued their criticism of each other’s campaigns.

headline:
North Shore firm's software tracks illness outbreaks
Flying cars and other 21st-century ideas
abstract: A software company out of Pittsburgh's North Shore called Health Monitoring Systems has created software that would be able to track trends of diseases and illnesses based on a network of information from emergency rooms and doctor's offices. The team hires locally and is planning to double in size in the next year.

headline: Public: Drilling rules must be stronger
abstract: Patrick D. Henderson, executive director of the state Senate Environmental Resource Committee has proposed a set of updates to the state's natural gas drilling regulations.  The committee, chaired by Sen. Mary Jo White, R-Franklin, has been taking testimony from experts regarding the state's drilling regulations.  The main focus of nearby residents is the safety of their drinking water.  Rules being proposed require drillers to use cement well casing and regular inspections.

headline: Hear that bell? It’s first day of school for some
abstract: Today is the first day of school for some students in the Philadelphia area. Most schools, including Philadelphia public and parochial schools, will open next week after the Labor Day holiday weekend.

newspaper: FBN - National Programming (Fox Business Channel) Cable
headline: The Willis Report
abstract: The state of Pennsylvania, in their initial budget this year basically took higher education spending out of the budget.

headline: Hearing on punishment for Rep. Charles Rangel set for Thursday unless he waives proceeding
abstract: Charlie Wrangel, former member of the Ways and Means Committee in Congress, will soon be punished after a jury of congressional peers concluded that he violated House rules. Among the many counts of misconduct, he used a subsidized New York apartment, which was designated for residential use, as a campaign office.

headline: Penn Hills teachers agree to new pact
abstract: After negotiations of more than a year, Penn Hills teachers and the school district came to an agreement, ratifying and approving a five-year contract that included modest raises, increased contribution to health-care premiums and early-retirement incentives.

headline: Cranberry welcomes North Catholic High School relocation
abstract: The Diocese of Pittsburgh has bought 71 acres of land in Cranberry to relocate North Catholic High School from Pittsburgh's Troy Hill neighborhood. The entire project is expected to cost between $54 million to $60 million. The diocese still needs to go through the municipal approval process of Cranberry and Seven Fields.

headline:
Forecast Links Aviation Activity and National Economic Growth
Key FAA Modernization Projects Essential for Improvements
abstract: The Federal Aviation Administration predicts that increasing safety and efficiency in America's aviation system will see more planes and passengers in future years while encouraging growth in the economy. The administration stressed Next Generation satellite radar improvements as one of the efforts of the administration to make the aviation system more safe and efficient.

headline: Education remains our best investment strategy
abstract: The legislative debate over the funding of public schools has continued, spurred on by the sluggish economy and potential increases in contributions to the public employees’ retirement system by local education agencies.

headline:
What America's cities need
In Philadelphia and elsewhere, education and immigration are keys to progress.
abstract: The author states that due to Philadelphia's changing demographics city policies must react to them more readily in order for Philadelphia to remain a rich economic center. A Brookings Institution report noted that metropolitan areas including Philadelphia have changed educationally, with more people having college degrees, but less people achieving a high school diploma, and demographically, by becoming more culturally diverse.

headline: Gas company to maintain Lehman Twp. Roads
abstract: Encana Oil & Gas USA Inc. will begin drilling in Lehman Township this summer, as well as take over operation of the area's backroads.  Residents are told to be proactive about reporting problems.  Encana's trucks will be making heavy use of Meeker and Slocum roads in Lehman Township to reach state Route 118.  The company has agreed to maintain the roads in equal or better condition during the drilling process.

headline: PA executions a rare occurrence
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, a death-penalty supporter, has signed 113 execution warrants during his two terms, but it appears likely he will leave office in a little more than four months without seeing any of them carried out. Since Pennsylvania reinstated the death penalty in the 1970s, only three men have been put to death; all had given up their appeals. Rendell says he considers the death penalty a deterrent, but only when executions are carried out relatively quickly.

headline: Official at center of PA terror-alert flap quits
abstract: The director of the Pennsylvania Office of Homeland Security James F. Powers Jr. has quit, telling PA Governor Ed Rendell that he made the decision after reflecting on the uproar over anti-terrorism bulletins that tracked the actions of peaceful citizens' groups. Rendell, who has apologized for the monitoring reports that were widely disseminated among law enforcement, said Powers will work one more week.

headline: Upper Gwynedd commissioners begin 2011 budget debate
abstract: According to commissioners President Ken Kroberger, Upper Gwynedd will see no new taxes as part of the next budget. Some have expressed uncertainty over this statement. Electricity, wastewater treatment and labor account for the largest cost increases in the budget, according to township Manager Len Perrone.

headline: Sentencing for Veon, aide, is delayed
abstract: A judge has delayed the sentencing of former state Rep. Mike Veon and a former aide found guilty in a government corruption probe known as Bonusgate. According to Veon’s attorney, the postponement was due to scheduling conflicts involving co-counsel Dan Raynak of Arizona.

headline: Security costs for G-20 summit come in under budget, mayor says
abstract: Security for the G-20 summit of world leaders came in under budget. The city spent $12.24 million when they had budgeted $16 million. Most of the money will be reimbursed by state and federal authorities like the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency and the US Department of Homeland Security.

headline: More consumer information hits the Web -- weights and measures reports
abstract: The state has begun posting weights and measures through the Department of Agriculture’s website  at http://www.pda.state.pa.us/WMInspections Annual inspection reports for adult daily living centers are also available through the Pennsylvania Department of Aging at http://www.aging.state.pa.us . Also available are summaries of technical service bulletins from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. The summaries are free at http://www.nhtsa.gov/ .

headline: Lenfest offers 500G to cover parade costs
abstract: Philanthropist Gerry Lenfest has donated $500,000 to the Greater Philadelphia Traditions Fund to help defray costs the city of Philadelphia would otherwise have footed the bill for. Philadelphia City Council has amended a bill that would force the city to cover costs of parades that occur in the city.

headline: Prudential outsourcing NEPA jobs
abstract: Internal documents from Prudential Financial show that they are planning on outsourcing work at their Scranton facility and outsourcing it eventually to India.  The plan shows that they are interested in moving 30 jobs at first to India with an undisclosed amount being moved in the future.  U.S. Rep. Paul E. Kanjorksi, D-Nanticoke, has scheduled a meeting with Prudential officials to discuss the job cuts.

headline: Editorial: Cupcake crackdown
abstract: Early last week, a Philadelphia building inspector was charged with helping the Department of Licenses and Inspections' Nuisance Task Force live up to its name. Authorities say Kenneth Gassman waged a campaign of harassment against a Fishtown man who had refused to sell his auto-repair shop to him. To show its muscle L&I, punished a cupcake vendor,  who having infringed on the city's cupcake-free zone for the second time, had her truck confiscated.

headline: Daley offers help with state forms, applications
abstract: PA Representative Peter J. Daley, D-Washington/Fayette, wants area residents to know they can receive help with state forms and applications at various locations during the month of October.

headline: Harrisburg plans to close police dispatch center by March
abstract: Harrisburg is a cash strapped city. Mayor Linda Thompson has announced the city will close its police dispatch center to save $500,000.
