The responsibility will be handed over to the Dauphin County 911 center, which already handles fire, medical and cell phone emergency calls originating in Harrisburg.

headline: Election games: Iraq may be maneuvering for the U.S. to stay
abstract: The author suggests the Iraqi government’s failure to establish a credible government is a masked attempt at maintaining the flow of funds and protection from the U.S. to the region. The sooner a viable and stable government is established.

headline: Trial against ex-Rep. Veon begins
abstract: The trial for former PA State Representative Mike Veon and his former legislative staffers started today. The prosecution looked into whether Veon's staffers conducted campaign activities on taxpayer-paid time and whether he was involved in handing out bonuses to House Democratic caucus staffers for campaign work. The defense cited PA Rep. Bill DeWeese as the one in control of the caucus.

headline: 200 soldiers will deploy to Iraq
abstract: 200 soldiers from the 298th Maintenance Company will be deployed to Iraq to repair machinery and help ship back supplies for US President Barack Obama's planned withdrawal deadline in 2011.  This is the company's second tour in Iraq.

headline: Childhood obesity: A generation at risk
abstract: New research from the National Institutes of Health reports that, among children age 10 to 17, the obesity rate grew from 14.8 percent in 2003 to 16.4 percent in 2007. First Lady Michelle Obama is spearheading a campaign called 'Let's Move", aimed at giving parents the support they need to help kids become active.

headline:
Common education standards reached
Most states will adopt the same goals on what students should know, and by when.
abstract: A project by Common Core State Standards aims at making education achievement at all levels uniform among all states. The program aims to create uniform standards for students in public schools to achieve. It is being called a way to make every student in America college or job ready by the time they graduate high school. Alaska and Texas have not signed onto to the proposal.

headline: Raise gas taxes?: Gov. Shameless
abstract: The editorial disagrees with the proposed hike the gasoline tax advanced by Gov. Ed Rendell.  The tax would make PA's gas tax the sixth highest in the nation.  It cites alleged overspending in economic development projects and contracts awarded to personal business acquaintances as reasons why the Rendell administration shouldn't be trusted with more revenue.

headline: First human tests on stem cells are near
abstract: Scientists are poised to inject cells created from embryonic stem cells into some patients with a progressive form of blindness and others with devastating spinal cord injuries. Researchers are eager to move from the laboratory to the clinic and for patients hoping for cures. The US Food and Drug Administration has demanded extensive experiments in the laboratory and on animals to provide evidence that the cells are safe enough to test in people and hold great promise.

headline: State Supreme Court: Duquesne High transfer rule unlawful
abstract: The PA General Assembly violated the state constitution when it wrote a law to control student transfers and teacher hiring's connected to the 2007 closing of Duquesne High School, the State Supreme Court ruled. Education officials said Thursday the decision will have no immediate effect on where students go to school.

headline: Charlie Dent supports 3-month unemployment benefits extension, but bill fails House
abstract: The US House of Representatives failed to pass a bill extending unemployment benefits for three months. According to the US Department of Labor Statistics, tens of thousands of Pennsylvanians will lose their benefits. 16 of the 19-member congressional delegation in PA voted in favor, including Republican Congressman Charlie Dent from the Lehigh Valley.

headline: Rendell nominates Gluck as education chief
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has nominated Thomas Gluck to succeed Gerald Zahorchak as state education secretary.

headline: Kids from Haiti fly here for care, as local pediatric-medicine teams head there
abstract: Three children were flew from earthquake-ravaged Haiti to Philadelphia for medical treatment despite a US government suspension of military evacuation flights from Haiti. Also, a 12-member crew from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia flew to Haiti to provide medical treatment on those afflicted by the earthquake.

headline: Harrisburg's finances: Still in trouble and in need of City Council's oversight
abstract: The author suggests that Harrisburg City Council should hold a larger part in the city's finances as Harrisburg struggles to pay off its massive debt. The city was saved in March when the Harrisburg Authority found $2 million in funds to help pay the debt. The city owes another $3.8 million in April and another $35 million in December.

headline: Poor packing can prove costly for motorists
abstract: State police warn that motorists failing to properly secure items to their vehicles will be subject to citations. Motorists who come across violations are urged to contact the state police for assistance.

headline: 1 Powerball ticket wins $261.6 million
abstract: A Powerball ticket sold in Ohio hit the Powerball jackpot of $261.6 million, with a $135 million cash payout.

headline: US Airways reports $279M quarterly profit
abstract: US Airways Group Inc. posted profit of $279 million for the most recent quarter.  US Airways doesn't have any immediate plans to hire more employees at the moment.

headline: Tax liens list shows locals owe $37.1M
abstract: A 1,482-page list of tax delinquents in PA totaling more than $200 million, was released publicly this month and for the first time includes a Chester County company that owes the fourth highest amount in all of PA and a shuttered business run by a local township commissioner. All of these delinquents are on the list for what the PA Department of Revenue claims are failure to pay a series of state taxes. Governor Ed Rendell had promised to step up enforcement when a tax amnesty program ended last year.

headline: Supplies of gas up, so prices go down
abstract: Natural gas prices at two of Western Pennsylvania's three largest utilities are down from a year ago, starting today. Peoples Natural Gas Co. reports the lowest price at $5.49 per thousand cubic feet, down 7 percent from last October.

headline: Gov. Ridge: Let's make sure Marcellus Shale is developed correctly
abstract: Former Governor Tom Ridge at the Barnes & Noble in Camp Hill promoting his book: PA is blessed with abundant natural resources that will make it a global leader in the production of clean energy. This transformational opportunity has spurred me to work with our governor-elect to make sure the industry is developed correctly. I have therefore joined the Marcellus Shale Coalition.

headline: 34th House District: Democrats for change should go with Dodaro
abstract: Author feels Richard Dodaro, who aims to cut the size of the Legislature to save money, is the best choice for the 34th Legislative District.

headline: Early draft of the Constitution found in Phila.
abstract: An early draft of the United States Constitution was found at the Historical Society of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia. The document was a precursor to the constitution written by James Wilson called "The Continuation of the Scheme." Historians are deciding now whether to move it into the collection of other drafts of the Constitution.

headline: lawmakers take no action in the latest effort to ban gay marriage in pennsylvania
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee tabled a bill with a vote of 8-6 that would define marriage in Pennsylvania as between a man and a woman in the state constitution. Disabled people are asking PA lawmakers and PA Governor Rendell to restore cuts to supplemental payment programs in the past year's budget. The cuts would cost the state $10 million this year and $20 million next year.

headline: State Senate approves study of Scranton-to-W-B train service
abstract: The PA state Senate gave approval for a study on the cost of establishing light rail service between Scranton and Wilkes-Barre. The study is part of a plan that would restore rail service between Scranton and the New York City Metropolitan area.

headline:
An all-American store
Even the bottles and boxes at this N.Y. business are made in the U.S.A.
abstract: A man has opened a store called the "Made in America Store" that only sells things that are strictly made in America.

headline: Port Authority crisis: Of its own making
abstract: This editorial blames the Port Authority of Allegheny County for its own budget woes.  It cites projects like the Wabash Tunnel and the Airport Busway as projects that taxpayers have been fooled on.  The editorial believes that the authority has acted irresponsibly for decades.

headline: Rendell Backs Turnpike in Funding Spat With Penndot
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is siding with the Turnpike Commission in a dispute with PA Department of Transportation (Penndot) over how much funding the turnpike is required to provide for roads, bridges and mass transit in the state. Even though the federal government has rejected I-80 tolls, Penndot lawyers think the law obligates the turnpike to provide the full amount.

headline: W-B woman claims $1 million in lottery
abstract: A city woman has claimed the winnings from a $1 million lottery ticket that was sold at a Wilkes-Barre convenience store. According to the Pennsylvania Lottery, Laberta Ruminski claimed the prize Thursday on behalf of a group of people.

headline: State legislators need to be back at work
abstract: The author is upset that the PA legislature will vote on no new items although the session is far from over: I wrote legislators about the importance of passing teacher pension reform, which was passed unanimously. They are voting nothing else. PA Legislators are some of the highest paid in the US and it is unjust that they get pay for "doing nothing."

headline: Testimony ends in Lower Merion redistricting suit
abstract: Testimony has ended in the case of nine South Ardmore parents who have alleged in federal court that the Lower Merion School District improperly used race as a factor in choosing to reassign their children as part of a redistricting plan. The redistricting effort was part of a community-based initiative to build two new $100 million high schools, replacing outdated facilities.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Gambling pays off for riverfront
abstract: The Penn Treaty Special Services District has been granting out money to community groups through funds they received from SugarHouse Casinos. Community groups, from Fishtown, Northern Liberties and parts of Kensington and Port Richmond, which the SSD covers, are available for grants that are available through a community-benefits agreement the casino group has with its Delaware riverfront neighbors. The funds are meant to give back to the communities the casino has affected.

headline: Athlete Jon Runyan officially enters congressional race
abstract: Former Philadelphia Eagle offensive lineman Jon Runyan has officially entered the primary for the 3rd congressional district race in New Jersey. Runyan will run as a Republican and plans to target Democratic incumbent John Adler's voting record in congress. Runyan said he will be a 'commonsense conservative.'

headline: Rendell wants tax changes for reserve fund
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for five tax increases and revisions in hopes of leaving a reserve fund in anticipation of upcoming financial difficulties. These increases and revisions include drawing revenue from the Marcellus Shale, taxing cigars and smokeless tobacco, eliminating the vendor sales tax discount, and a revision of the state’s tax code.

headline: Pa. lawmakers divided over amended teen-driving bill
abstract: House Bill 67, a bill introduced in the state legislature to create safer driving environment for drivers under 18, has gone from the PA Senate to the PA House of Representatives. The bill has been amended so much that original supporters are now against the bill. The bill limits the number of passengers a driver under 18 can have in his car and makes the use of a handheld cell phone a secondary offense.

headline: Schooling for teachers in Pittsburgh district's plans
abstract: Along with K-8 students, teachers will be learning at the Pittsburgh School Districts' new teacher training academies at Brashear High School and King K-8.  The district hopes to attract $40 million in grant money from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.  It requires improved teacher training.  Teachers would work with up to 50 clinical instructors.  They would receive their full salary while training.  For those that don't make the cut, the district would have the option to not offer them permanent placement.

headline: Joblessness up again, 10.4 in
abstract:
Joblessness in the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre/Hazleton metro area continued its disappointing march upward in July, increasing two-tenths of a percentage point to a seasonally adjusted 10.4 percent.
The PA Department of Labor and Industry reported today that declines in employment outpaced declines in the labor force: those able and willing to work. The imbalance pushed the jobless rate to its highest level since September 1992.

headline: Property rights fight develops over drilling in Pennsylvania
abstract: Senator after senator in Harrisburg has voiced opposition to a concept that could be used to force holdout landowners to lease their below-ground gas rights under certain conditions. Under the proposed policy landowners would be paid for the methane drawn from beneath their turf, and no well would be drilled on their land but they'd be unable to say no to a drilling company. Opponents say the concept, called pooling, is tantamount to government taking of property rights to benefit private companies.

headline: No tax increase needed in Dauphin County's proposed 2011 budget
abstract: The Dauphin County Commissioners released their general fund budget, which will include no increases in taxes. Spending is up 1.5 percent and to balance the budget the commissioners plan to dip into reserve funds. If adopted, this will be the sixth consecutive year that property tax rates have not increased.

headline: Decentralization would help Haiti
abstract: Dr. Rodrigue Mortel, a native of Haiti and former professor at the Penn State University College of Medicine, suggests a comprehensive decentralization of power concentrated in the government offices in Port-au-Prince is essential to the rebuilding of post-earthquake Haiti.

headline: Abington, Grand View to treat Haitians
abstract: Eleven hospitals in Pennsylvania will receive patients from earthquake-ravaged Haiti. This comes as the US military resumes medical evacuation flights out of Haiti. The PA Department of Health will coordinate patients to hospitals upon arrival and the PA Department of Public Welfare will find housing for the patients.

headline: Republicans facing challenges in 13th and 8th District races
abstract: In the 13th and 8th congressional districts, Republican primary contenders have had their ballot petitions challenged by fellow GOP voters. In the 13th district, all 3 GOP candidates are challenged and unchallenged Democratic challenger Allyson Schwartz is said to have encouraged GOP voters to challenger the petitions. James Jones of the 8th district has had his ballot petitions challenged also.

headline: 2 students slashed at Allen
abstract: A 16-year-old Allen High School student was arrested for slashing two students in the face with a knife in an incident that forced a lockdown at the school.

headline: Flubbed Philly road projects mean more delays
abstract: Two unfinished Philadelphia road projects have been further delayed due to construction complications. The JFK Boulevard bridge is having paint work done to it which was formally ruined; that project was originally funded by PennDOT for $17.9 million. The South Street bridge needs work under the bridge and was funded by the Philadelphia Streets Department.

headline: Legislation targets racial death sentences
abstract: Pennsylvania and Texas have the highest percentage of minorities on death row according to a Villanova Law School professor.  Robert Dunham testified at a hearing on a bill that would reduce the disparities in minority sentencing.  Minorities comprise 69 percent of death row inmates.

headline: Game Commission: Some out-of-state game is prohibited in Pa.
abstract: PA Game Commission Executive Director Carl G. Roe reminds hunters that, in an effort to prevent the introduction of Chronic Wasting Disease (CWD) into the Commonwealth, the agency prohibits hunters from importing specific carcass parts from members of the deer family: including mule deer, elk and moose from 18 states and two Canadian provinces. First identified in 1967, CWD is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (TSE) that affects cervids, including all species of deer, elk and moose.

headline: Cities in Debt Turn to States, Adding Strain
abstract: Harrisburg, PA is among those cities that have sought refuge in havens that states provide as alternatives to bankruptcy court. A growing number of towns, cities and other local governments are seeking refuge in similar havens that many states provide as alternatives to federal bankruptcy court. Pennsylvania will have 20 cities and smaller communities in its distressed-cities program if Harrisburg receives approval.

headline: LVIA upgrades a decade in the making
abstract: The Lehigh Valley International Airport has been significantly upgraded. The airport decided to remodel even though it is struggling to pay a $26 million court judgment. The president of the airport terminal said that sometimes it is best to make improvements during recessions, a time when the airports sees less passengers.

headline: Bill calls for eliminating Pennsylvania's municipal governments, switching to county-based system to save taxpayers money
abstract: Rep. Thomas Caltagirone has introduced legislation calling for a state constitutional amendment to have Pennsylvania’s 67 county governments absorb all the municipalities within their borders, and operate under a single countywide structure. Among his reasons for the plan are the rising cost of government and increasing property taxes.

headline: Dems line up for Melio seat
abstract: Democrats have begun the endorsement process for the seat in the PA House of Representatives left vacant by retiring PA Representative Tony Melio. Bristol Mayor John Monahan and community activist Mike Slipp are up for the Democratic endorsement. Republicans are expected to make their decision in coming weeks.

headline: Center City hit-and-run kills 2 Asian community leaders
abstract: Zhihua Lin and Chun Liang Li, two prominent members of the Asian-American community, were killed during a hit-and-run car accident in Philadelphia. Both were elected to the Fujian Association of Pennsylvania.

headline: Witness implicates Perzel in computer schemes
abstract: At a preliminary hearing on corruption charges for state Rep. John Perzel, William Tomaselli, a self-described troubleshooter for Perzel, testified to having had numerous conversations with the state Representative about the use of technology in campaigns. Perzel is accused of directing a criminal scheme to spend upwards of $10 million in tax money on campaigns, primarily through the purchase of computer programs and equipment.

headline: Foxwoods seeks more time to salvage casino deal
abstract: Philadelphia Entertainment and Development Partners have submitted a request for more time to work out a deal for the proposed Foxwoods Casino in South Philadelphia to PA State Gaming Control Board. The PEDP said they need more time after an investment deal with casino-owner Steve Wynn fell through. The PEDP is also trying to fend off the revocation of its $50 million casino license which the gaming board has threatened to take away.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at Noon
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell responds to questions about the airlifting of orphans from earthquake ravaged Haiti.

headline: Charter school group Propel looks to expand in Allegheny County
abstract: Propel Schools plans to use $3.4 million in federal grants to open five more schools in Allegheny County. Propel received one of 12 grants awarded nationally worth $50 million from the US Department of Education's charter schools program, which seeks to expand high-quality charter schools that have had academic success in recent years. President Obama's administration plans to invest more than $256 million this year to help in the planning and implementation of public charter schools and is seeking $310 million next fiscal year.

headline: Sharing city's pain: It's premature to rule out commuter tax before any plan is even on the table
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson has filed for distressed-city status under the state law known as Act 47. This would allow the city to increase the wage tax on city residents and nonresident workers as long as the court approves. PA Representative Ron Marsico has introduced legislation to take that option away.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Pa. lawmakers' special transportation-deficit session
abstract: In the wake of the Federal Highway Administration’s rejection of the state’s application to toll I-80, Governor Ed Rendell has called for a special session of the legislature to tackle the issue of funding. The state is faced with a $470 million gap in its transportation budget, jeopardizing road and bridge repairs as well as SEPTA projects such as a “smart-card” fare system and a remodeled City Hall subway concourse.

headline: Pa. hospitals will take Haiti earthquake patient overflow
abstract: Coordinating centers set up by the US National Disaster Medical System to give medical relief to those affected by the earthquake in Haiti in the Northeast United States, including those in Pennsylvania, are expected to take patients that cannot be taken by coordinating centers in Georgia and Florida. The PA Department of Health and the PA Department of Public Welfare are involved in coordinating patients.

headline: State's jobless rate rises to 8.9%
abstract: Pennsylvania's unemployment rate raised by one-tenth of one percentage point to 8.9% in February, staying below the national unemployment average of 9.7%. The industry of 'eds and meds,' those in the education and medical fields have kept the state afloat by hiring new workers, yet eds and meds lost 7,800 jobs in February.

headline: Port authority riders caught up in transit, union dispute
abstract: Port Authority drivers used printed materials that mistakenly said buses on the new G2 route would drop off passengers at the Bell Station in Carnegie. Port Authority officials failed to notice the mistake until the week before route changes took effect, asking drivers to unofficially keep Bell Station a full-service stop.

headline: Philadelphia plans more cuts in services
abstract: Philadelphia Budget Director Stephen Agostini has alerted city departments of spending cuts of 2% while freezing spending on new equipment and supplies. Tax hikes on sugary beverages and property taxes were rejected by Philadelphia City Council. The decision comes as a result of low tax revenues and the uncertainty of state funding due to last year's budget stalemate between PA Governor Rendell and the state legislature. Agostini will also withhold $13 to $14 million from the pervious year budget to prepare for the upcoming year.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at Noon
abstract: The PA gubernatorial election is discussed.

headline: Districts use grants to make change
abstract: At Central Dauphin East High School, teachers are being encouraged to focus on rigor, relevance and relationships. Those ideals will be part of a new overhaul of CD East that begins this year with a staff and administration meeting, following an announcement late last week that the school is in line to receive $2.1 million in school-improvement grants.

headline: Yet another woman sues PHA's Greene, cites sex harassment
abstract: Another woman has come forward to allege that Carl R. Greene, the former Philadelphia Housing Authority executive director, sexually harassed her, then retaliated when she rejected his advances. In a civil-rights lawsuit filed in federal court yesterday, Laura Leibert, 29, claimed that Greene stalked her, repeatedly asked her out for drinks and dinner, called her on her cell phone at late hours and forced her to salsa dance with him at a PHA event. The PHA Board of Commissioners, led by former Mayor John Street, fired Greene last month after an internal investigation deemed him a "serial sexual harasser."

headline: Easton Area girls in bracelet suit can attend dance
abstract: Two middle school girls, along with their mothers are suing the Easton Area School District after being suspended for wearing "I (heart) boobies!" wristbands in support of breast cancer awareness. The American Civil Liberties Union of Pennsylvania is helping the girls and a federal judge has made it possible for the girls to attend the Snowball Dance.

headline: Global partners: A Pittsburgh group is a key link to the Middle East
abstract: The Pittsburgh Middle East Institute, which was established in 2008, has become increasingly active in fostering relations between local business and institutions and possible partners in Middle Eastern countries. The author suggests the region develop its commercial and investment links to the rest of the world as rapidly and deeply as possible in order to remain competitive in the global market.

headline: Municipal policing contracts opposed by state police
abstract: A bill proposed by PA Senator Kim Ward would allow local police forces with inadequate police forces to contract state police officers for local protection. PA State Police officials have rejected the proposal due to questions of cost. The Pennsylvania State Troopers Association and the Pennsylvania State Association of Township Supervisors have supported the bill.

headline: Breakdown of health care overhaul's benefits released
abstract: US Rep. Henry Waxman has released a report by the US House Energy and Commerce Committee that highlights benefits of a proposed health-care overhaul in every congressional district in the United States. The report shows how many people would be eligible for healthcare subsidies and how many would benefit from the new law that insurers cannot bar coverage based on pre-existing conditions. Many congressional delegates from Pennsylvania stand to see their districts benefit from the proposal.

headline: Scitech students to get access to e-books
abstract: Students at the Pittsburgh Science and Technology Academy will be able to access more than 500 nonfiction works online along with at least a dozen works of fiction. Students will now be able to access materials online from their school-issued laptops.

headline: Pittsburgh City Council approves $640,000 grant to Carnegie Library
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council has approved a $640,000 grant to the Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh to help keep branches open. The council expressed concern over the library's closed board meetings and their closing down of libraries. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl has criticized council for officering the library a "blank check."

headline: Morning Joe
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell briefly mentioned during a morning political analysis program.

headline: Fewer teacher vacancies as school is about to start
abstract: Only 38 teacher vacancies remain for Philadelphia school district officials to fill before school starts one week from today, a district official reported yesterday. This is a drop in vacancies compared to 45 around this time last year, and 289 empty positions in 2008, according to district figures reported last year. A hiring freeze imposed this spring and lifted for most subject areas last Friday helped reserve enough jobs for the large number of teachers in need of new assignments in September.

headline: Two more Camden officers indicted in rogue-cop probe
abstract: Two Camden police officers assigned to protect some of the city's most drug-infested neighborhoods instead used their badges to break the law, according to a nine-count federal indictment unsealed Thursday. The two officers were charged with stealing drugs and money from narcotics dealers, planting evidence, conducting illegal searches, falsifying police reports, and lying under oath. The two, arrested Thursday morning, pleaded not guilty at preliminary hearings in US District Court in Camden.

headline: Air Products among 'Best Places to Work' for lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender employees
abstract: Air Products, along with several other Lehigh Valley companies, received a "Best Places to Work" distinction from the Human Rights Campaign, a civil rights group advocating lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender equality. This was the 9th annual survey by the group that analyzed and rated the work policies affecting these groups.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: 16 food companies to cut back salt
abstract:
As part of a national effort to cut Americans' sodium intake by 20 percent,
16 food companies plan to cut the amount of salt in bacon, flavored rice, and dozens of other products. The sodium cuts are part of a voluntary National Salt Reduction Initiative, a public-private partnership by New York City. Among the 16 companies taking part in the initiative are H.J. Heinz and Starbucks.

headline: The 'prevailing wage': Stupid, stupid, stupid
abstract: The author disagrees with the recent actions by Pittsburgh City Council to enact a prevailing wage for large companies who receive certain public subsidies. He says that the bill restricts development and is socialistic.

headline: Middle class struggling with health care costs, report finds
abstract: A report from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation released Wednesday found that a growing percentage of America's middle class has no health insurance. The report showed that due to the downturn in the economy employers have had to cut down on coverage to their employees and raise their share of premiums. Hospitals have also seen an increase in those coming in for treatment uninsured.

headline: Penn Hills teachers slated to vote on contract today
abstract: Penn Hills teachers are scheduled to vote on whether to accept a five-year contract that raises salaries significantly less than the school district's previous offer and would require teachers to contribute more money toward the cost of their health insurance.

headline: Toomey hits Sestak on job offer, cap and trade
abstract: US Senate candidate, Republican Pat Toomey, has criticized his Democratic opponent US Rep Joe Sestak for not releasing a job offer from the Obama Administration earlier in the campaign. Toomey also criticized Sestak's support of Cap-and-Trade legislation.

headline: FOX 29 News at Five
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has endorsed a number of reforms targeting perks offered to employees of the Delaware River Port Authority.  He would eliminate free toll privileges and curtail car allowances.

headline: Family points finger at Woods
abstract: The parents of a 19-year-old man with the mental abilities of a preschooler have filed a criminal complaint alleging he was assaulted last week at Woods Services, the residential center that has been the focus of recent state and local investigations following the deaths of two clients in less than a year. Woods officials called the family's allegations "unfounded," adding that its internal investigation showed the injuries were the result of a "long standing medical condition."

headline: Nutter revisits Harrisburg to testify about PHA
abstract: Testifying before the PA Senate Urban Affairs and Housing Committee, Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter reiterated his belief that the Philadelphia Housing Authority (PHA) board deserved much of the blame for the scandal that has engulfed PHA and that brought down its executive director, Carl R. Greene. Nutter advocated changing the five-member board's structure so that the mayor would make the majority of appointments. Currently, two members are chosen by the mayor and two by the city controller, the fifth is a tenant representative elected by the other four.

headline: Dems pick House leaders
abstract: PA Representative Frank Dermody of Allegheny County was elected behind closed doors as the new minority chairman of the PA House. The current chairman of the House Transportation Committee Joseph Markosek took out Representative Dwight Evans of Philadelphia in the race for the House Appropriations Committee chairmanship. PA Representative Dan Frankel will be the new caucus chairman.

headline: Bill passes, helps preserve jobs
abstract: The state House of Representatives has passed a bill allowing businesses in Pennsylvania to reduce work hours for all or a portion of their workforce, helping to control costs without resorting to layoffs. Workers affected by the reduction would be eligible to offset the lost income with unemployment benefits in proportion to the percentage of work hours lost.

headline: Penn Hills teachers' strike continues
abstract: Penn Hills teachers have begun to strike after negotiations between the school district and the teachers' union could not reach a deal in recent negotiations. The two sides are in dispute over the teachers' annual raises and how much teachers should pay into healthcare benefits.

headline:
Man receives double hand transplant at UPMC
Susquehanna Township man lost hands in a farming accident
abstract: Chris Pollock, a farmer from Susquehanna Township, had to have both of his arms amputated after they were caught in a corn picker. Pollock had a double hand transplant, only the third hand transplant to be performed at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center.

headline: Rivers Casino completes first annual payment for hockey arena
abstract: Rivers Casino owners completed their first of 30 annual $7.5 million installments toward the new Penguins arena. The casino is splitting the cost of the $321 million Consol Energy Center with the Penguins organization, which pays $4.2 million a year; and the state, which pays $7.5 million a year.

headline: Workers keeping public pools in the swim
abstract: Inspections into public pools are being conducted to preclude the spread of diseases spread by fecal matter and insufficient amounts of chemicals in the water. A federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention study found that one in eight public pools in 13 US states had to be shut down for complications in 2008. A study by the PA Health Department found one in 20 pools in Pennsylvania had to be shut down due to complications.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: Look, a state in worse shape than Pa.: NY calls "extraordinary session" to talk about FMAP money
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has warned residents that if Congress doesn't cough up the nearly $850 million in federal Medicaid contributions, the budget will have to be reworked to deal with the shortfall.  In New York, Gov David Paterson has called a special session of the legislature to deal with the issue's impact in NY.  Rendell has made it clear that he doesn't plan on calling a session like this one in PA.

headline: School goes on despite Hempfield high's flooded classrooms
abstract: A broken water line flooded seven classrooms at Hempfield Area High School on Sunday night, almost delaying the first day of school. It took volunteer firefighters, district custodians and maintenance workers until 1:30 a.m. Monday to pump out the water and clean the classrooms so school could start on time.

headline: Expired: Council trashes the best plan to support pensions
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council has rejected Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's plan to lease Pittsburgh parking facilities. Under the Mayor's plan J.P. Morgan Asset Management and LAZ Parking would have paid the city $452 million for the opportunity to lease and run the city's parking facilities, which would have paid off the debt on the parking garages, brought the city's pension account to a 50 percent funding level. One of the biggest criticisms of the mayor's plan was that it wouldn't have "solved" the city's $1 billion pension problem.

headline: Commuters shouldn't pay for city mess, lawmakers say
abstract: PA Senator Jeff Piccola and Representative Ron Marsico have introduced bills that would prevent Harrisburg from levying high wage taxes on those who work in the city. Piccola, a Republican whose district includes the bulk of Dauphin County, said the goal is to protect the thousands of workers who already contribute to Harrisburg's economy. Mayor of Harrisburg Linda Thompson and several City Council members blasted the legislation.

headline: Special needs students find outlet in singing, rapping
abstract: Pace School, a private school and licensed psychiatric program that serves special needs students is helping students learn  and develop through music and arts.

headline: Abuse allegations concern veterans
abstract: The Pennsylvania American Legion expressed concerns over reports in the Pittsburgh Tribune Review about the mistreatment of Veterans at state-controlled veterans homes. The PA Department of Military and Veterans Affairs runs the veterans homes.

headline: WASD to work with borough to keep school resource officer
abstract: The Waynesboro Area School District will work with the Borough of Waynesboroto to submit a grant application to the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency to continue their school resource officer position, despite uncertainty about the officer’s funding. The PA Department of Education says the school district can provide funds for the position while the board's solicitor says it legally cannot.

headline: Pittsburgh's maglev competitors seem to have higher hurdles
abstract: Maglev Inc. is awaiting the Federal Railroad Administration's approval of its final environmental impact statement on Pittsburgh’s plan for a $5.25 billion train. Once the statement is approves, the Federal Department of Transportation must give the final go-ahead in order for construction of the project to begin. $28 million set aside for the project remains in limbo, posing potential problems for its development. Similar projects in Las Vegas and Georgia have faced similar obstacles.

headline: Mon, upper Delaware on list of 'most endangered' rivers in U.S.
abstract: The Monangehela River and the Upper Delaware River are on the list of "Most Endangered Rivers" due to the threat posed by Marcellus Shale gas drilling in Pennsylvania, according to a report by the group, American Rivers. The large use of chemically treated water to frack the shale is being blamed as causing contamination to the rivers.

headline: Agora Cyber Charter School approved for five more years
abstract: Agora Cyber Charter School, which allows parents to send their kids to school through use of cyber-learning, has won approval to operate in PA for the next five years.  The school almost lost its charter last year and operates along side 11 other cyber charter schools.  The school is planning to expand its online tutoring and planned to open up more learning centers in Philadelphia and 16 other sites for face-to-face help.

headline: Region's jobless rate continues to climb
abstract: The Pittsburgh region's unemployment rate followed the PA trend by ticking up one-tenth of a percentage point to 8.4 percent for July, the PA Department of Labor and Industry reported this morning. The state reported that the seasonally adjusted number fell by 1,800 jobs in the seven counties that make up the Pittsburgh Metropolitan Statistical Area.

headline: Chester county highways get $33.9M in stimulus money
abstract: Chester County's six highway projects funded by $33.9 million in stimulus money from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act has paved roads, built the first phase of bike/jogging trail, paved sidewalks and fixed handicapped curb cuts on state highways. In all, some 442 jobs were either created or retained. Projects had to be "shovel ready," the Obama Administration specified before it released the stimulus money in 2009.

headline: Pa. taking wrong approach with senior care
abstract: The author applauds Auditor Jack Wagner and PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett for their actions on the Medicaid problem. He thinks that we need to examine Pennsylvania’s poorly constructed and antiquated long-term care system that favors funding for institutionalized care over less expensive home and community-based services. PA should follow the lead of other states that have restructured by providing more in-home care.

headline: Thomas Gluck nominated as Pennsylvania secretary of education
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has nominated Thomas Gluck to replace Gerald Zahorchak as the new education secretary.

headline: E-mails offered in trial of Veon
abstract: E-mails presented in the trial of former PA House Democratic Whip Mike Veon's show him and his staffers coordinating taxpayer-paid bonuses to caucus staff. Former House Democratic Caucus Chief of Staff Michael Manzo testified against Veon as part of a plea-bargain deal the PA Attorney General's office.

headline: Head count: When people do the census, local dollars add up
abstract: The author states that residents should not fear filling out the census form. The author states that not filling out the census form costs the government money because they have to hire workers to go door-to-door. The government has $400 billion to allocate to state and local governments, meaning it is imperative that Pennsylvania residents fill out the census.

headline: Biden arrives today for first visit as vice president
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden will be making a brief visit to the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport for a rally and fundraiser in support of U.S. Senator Arlen Specter. The visit comes just as the race between Specter and his democratic opponent, Joe Sestak, is heating up.

headline: World Environment Day conference convenes in Pittsburgh
abstract: Pittsburgh chose water as a focal point for the 2010 World Environment Day held in Pittsburgh. The conference heard from speakers from corporate, environmental, and the university sectors on how to best preserve this natural resource. Speakers from the Blue Ocean Institute and Carnegia Melon University were heard.

headline: Proposed N.J. legislation would change charter school guidelines
abstract: A bill backed by NJ Gov Chris Christie will allow charter schools to be authorized more quickly.  Assemblywoman Mila Jasey (D., Essex) said that the bill will show NJ to be a friendly place for charters to operate. 75 charter schools now operate in the state of New Jersey.  Currently only the state Department of Education can authorize new charters.  The proposed legislation would have authorization go through Rutgers University.

headline: New database details unpaid taxes in PA
abstract: In its latest effort to bring in every last dollar during the recession, the PA Department of Revenue has introduced an expanded online database that it hopes will shame tax delinquents into coming up with the money and getting the liens against them lifted. The amount of unpaid taxes ripe for collection is significant. The database lists 39,324 liens assessed since July 1, 2009, for $233 million in back taxes statewide

headline: Candidates seek seat for 111th
abstract: For the first time in a decade, the race for the 111th Legislative District will include a challenge from a Democratic opponent. Incumbent PA Representative Sandra Major, Republican-Bridgewater Township., is opposed in her re-election bid by Democrat Jim Knapp of Pleasant Mount, and Green Party candidate Jay Sweeney of Falls in the district that covers parts of Susquehanna, Wayne and Wyoming counties.

headline: Allow Pa. gas firms to bill for pipeline repairs
abstract: A gas pipeline explosion in San Bruno California has people in PA asking whether it could happen there. Much of the state's natural gas infrastructure consists of cast iron pipes, which are susceptible to corrosion. Therefore, as the author advocates, the PA General Assembly should approve a natural gas distribution system improvement that would allow gas companies to recoup the revenue needed to upgrade pipelines.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Gettysburg battles again over a casino plan
abstract: Local preservation groups are fighting to stop a proposal to put a resort casino in an aging conference center a half-mile south of the Civil War battlefield on the storied Emmitsburg Road. Casino developer David LeVan, a former Conrail chief executive who served on the Philadelphia school board, and his supporters maintain the resort is far enough from the battlefield that it won't be a threat. It is unclear when the final resort license will be awarded.

headline: Program seeks to inspire Pittsburgh middle schoolers
abstract: The Summer Dreamers Academy, paid for through the School District of Pittsburgh's cut of federal stimulus money, is a summer camp that will give middle schoolers the chance to participate in recreational activities. The program will cost $5.5 million and is meant to address literacy.

headline: County Council considers prevailing wage bill
abstract: Allegheny County Council introduced a third ordinance that would require employers of county-subsidized development sites to pay their employees a prevailing wage consistent with county averages. Pittsburgh City Council passed a prevailing wage measure which Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl questioned the legality of.

headline: Sinus trouble? Secondhand smoke may be to blame
abstract: According to a new study, secondhand smoke may be the cause of chronic sinusitis  in up to 40 percent of cases.

headline:
Obama defends policies
The president discusses the struggling economy and delivers a rebuttal to GOP criticism in a speech at Carnegie Mellon University
abstract: US President Barack Obama defended his economic policies at a speech at Carnegie Melon University. The president indicated that Republicans have been obstructing his policies rather than contributing towards them. The president lauded a growing economy since he entered office and called for cap-and-trade legislation, and the end of tax-cuts for the rich.

headline: Prosecutors throw DeWeese's words in his face at corruption hearing
abstract: Prosecutors in the Bonusgate case threw Rep. Bill DeWeese's own testimony at his face when confronted on the stand this week.  DeWeese admitted to witnessing other staffers do campaign work while on the clock for the state.  DeWeese said that it was all a part of the culture on Capitol Hill at the time.

headline: Lawmakers should foster growth
abstract: If the PA General Assembly has the ability find a funding solution to address the state’s aging transportation system when it regroups for the remaining weeks of its session. PA Transportation Secretary Allen Bieher recently convened a bipartisan meeting to outline two funding options that could potentially be implemented this fall and put into practice by as early as January.

headline: Spending stimulus money is key challenge in PA
abstract: According to state officials, recipients of the roughly $29 billion doled out for Pennsylvania stimulus projects were told to spend the money allocated to them. Mary Rucci, director of citizens' awareness at the Pennsylvania Stimulus Accountability Office in Harrisburg says there is a focus on spending the money quickly to jump start the economy. With more than $10.5 billion spent so far, the state appears to be on track to spend its share of the $787 billion stimulus package by 2014.

headline: Pa. House approves pension fix bill
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will soon be sent a bill intended to curb increasing pension costs. The House overwhelmingly passed the legislation, which accounts for the $4 billion spike by extending payments on unfunded pension liability over 30 years. Representative Jenn Mann said that if the bill was not passed that school districts would see property taxes increase in the next year.

headline: Penguins co-owner to help Philadelphia newspapers
abstract: Penguins co-owner Ron Burkle is stepping in to help a local Philadelphia ownership group retain control of that city's two major newspapers. Governor Ed Rendell personally asked Burkle to help the current owners retain control of the Inquirer and Daily News, which have large debts.

headline: State corruption trial could be a civics lesson
abstract: The trial to begin for former PA House Democratic Whip Mike Veon of giving out taxpayer-paid bonuses to caucus staff. The author states that the trial could be a look into the government's ethics ahead of the primary elections in May, especially the gubernatorial election. The article notes how PA Attorney General Tom Corbett has been accused of political maneuvering while conducting the corruption probe.

headline: Bucks GOP derides Murphy, health bill
abstract: Members of the Bucks County GOP to oppose US Representative Patrick Murphy and Democrat of the 8th District of Pennsylvania in the may primary are deriding the proposed federal healthcare reform bill as too costly, and are saying that the US House procedural vote to send the bill straight from the House to the President is unconstitutional. Former US Rep. Mike Fitzpatrick derided Murphy and US Rep. Nancy Pelosi.

headline: SCI-Waynesburg to reopen
abstract: The state Department of Corrections confirmed that the  State Correctional Institution at Waynesburg will reopen in mid-August. The 510-bed facility off Route 188 in Morgan Township will house male nonviolent offenders and employ 169 people.

headline: Upper Burrell group wants to get to bottom of Marcellus Shale
abstract: Upper Burrell residents are grouping together to hold informational meetings on the environmental and economic prospects for Marcellus Shale gas drilling in the area. The meetings will be open to the public and will include many groups. The group plans to get the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection to cooperate with the discussions.

headline: Second suit filed in Lower Merion spycam case
abstract: Jalil Hasan, a recent graduate of Lower Merion High School is the second student to step forward with a lawsuit regarding the school district's use of remote activated webcams.  Hasan says that the software used to spy was activated during his use of the machine.  The district is accused of snapping more than 1,000 pictures of Hasan.  His family learned of the behavior after they were contacted by an attorney for the school district.

headline: The problem of illegal labor: It drives down wages & distorts the market in many other ways, too
abstract: A few years ago, an analysis of 473 occupations found that native-born American workers comprise the majority in all but four of them plasterers and stucco masons, agricultural graders and sorters, personal appliance workers, and tailors and dressmakers. The way many employers fill low-wage, low-skilled jobs has changed significantly. Instead of placing want ads, more and more rely on informal immigration networks, such as asking their current immigrant workers to find other workers to fill openings.

headline: U.S. Senate candidates rake in 3rd-quarter cash
abstract: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Pat Toomey announced raising $3.8 million in the third quarter, while Democratic U.S. Representative Joseph Sestak, Democrat-7, of Edgmont, reported raising $3.2 million. Toomey campaign said in a release it had raised more than $14 million from more than 64,000 contributors since he announced his candidacy in April 2009. Sestak’s campaign noted he had raised more than $5 million since depleting funds in the May primary against incumbent U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter.

headline: Capital region businesses are strong despite Harrisburg's debt
abstract: The author is a commercial realtor in Harrisburg that feels that business owners have remained creative and resilient in the face of the capital city's fiscal woes. Business is doing well despite the city's public debt problem. The author cites recent awards won by the city, such as Forbes' No. 2 in America's Best Places to Raise a Family and 4th Most Equal Wage Distribution in the Nation.

headline: Paid leave: Landmark legislation still has holes to fill
abstract: According to a poll, 77 percent of Americans are in favor of businesses providing paid family and medical leave for workers. The author feels not enough is being done to address the gaps in the 1993 Family and Medical Leave Act. The act applies only to workplaces of 50 or more employees and provides those workers with up to 12 weeks of unpaid medical leave.

headline: Much more economic growth needed to cut jobless rate
abstract: The economy grew 5.7% in the last quarter of 2009 but it would need to grow by at least 5% for all of 2010 to decrease the unemployment rate by 1 percentage point. Economists say growth in 2010 will slow to 2% or 3%. The

headline: Inmate's mistaken release was not the only odd thing about the case
abstract: A clerical mistake by an employee of the Clerk of Quarter Sessions caused William Holloran to be released early from jail because his paperwork stated that he serve his two sentences concurrently instead of consecutively. Holloran is currently serving the rest of the time he owes. A Court of Common Pleas Court judge asked the PA Department of corrections to not give holloran credit for time served after the was released.

headline: Mine land cleanup in North Scranton to be complete soon
abstract: A $431,000 project to remake the former Leggett's Creek Colliery in North Scranton is expected to be completed in the next couple of months. The project, which was paid for with a grant from the Environmental Protection Agency is being overseen by Lackawanna County. Plans to create a residential development have been put on hold.

headline: New biography highlights many sides of Flood
abstract: A new biography about former Luzerne County Congressman Dan Flood depicts him as a congressman who worked hard for his constituents, fought communism world wide, and took gifts for political favors.

headline: New Fodder for War Critics
abstract: The leaking of thousands of confidential US documents is expected to provide war critics with new fodder to protest the US involvement in Afghanistan.  The documents shine light on killings of civilians as well as corruption in the US-backed Kabul government.  The release of the documents is expected to put added pressure on Obama to reevaluate the country's involvement with the war.

headline: Hearing reveals divisions over Gettysburg casino
abstract: After two days of impassioned testimony, the PA Gaming Control Board wrapped up a public hearing on whether to open a casino near the historic Gettysburg battlefield.

headline: Barletta confident it’s his time
abstract: Barletta, the Republican mayor of Hazleton said after talking to voters every day during his campaign, he is confident the election result in the 11th Congressional District will be different. Barletta is trying for the third time to unseat U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski, of Nanticoke, a 13-term Democrat. According to Barletta Kanjorski is out of touch with the district and its people.

headline: Penn State can become a leader in health and biotech innovation
abstract: The author reminds public officials at all levels of government to create policies that stimulate the creation of jobs in the Harrisburg region. The author advocates a number of policies at the federal and state level that deal with taxes and research. She believes that Penn State, the University of Pittsburg and the University of Pennsylvania can be the future of medical innovation in the US.

headline: Pa. board OKs table games at Meadows
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board approved a petition from Washington Trotting Association Inc., the operator of The Meadows Racetrack and Casino, permitting The Meadows to provide games such as poker, blackjack, craps, and roulette.

headline:
Asians tell of anguish over S. Phila. attacks
Grandmother says district mishandled case of beating victim Hao Luu, 17
abstract: The School District of Philadelphia's handling of attacks on Asian-American students in early December 2009 according to a grandmother of Hao Luu, a victim of the attack. Luu's family was not contacted by the administration and Luu was accused of gang activity and was ordered to transfer schools. The School Reform Commission of Philadelphia heard testimony from 19 people telling of the mishandling of disciplinary actions of the School District of Philadelphia.

headline: 119th Democrats find middle ground
abstract: Candidates for the Democratic state representative seat held by John Yudichak, gave their opening statements during a public forum at King's College. The Candidates sought to separate themselves from each other, all while making a push toward the middle, carrying messages of fiscal responsibility and sensible reform.

headline: Congress pushes electric vehicles through incentives bill
abstract: Legislation being introduced in both chambers of congress would provide for incentives for the purchasing of electric cars and maintaining a network conducive to electric cars. The two bills differ but essentially offer the same incentives. The House legislation would provide five $800 million grants to deployment communities, who would have to apply for the grant.

headline: 2 Drexel basketball players & friend surrender in robbery targeting coed
abstract: Jamie Harris and Kevin Phillip, two players on the Drexel University basketball team have been accused along with a third person of robbing a classmate by gunpoint on Wednesday.  The students have been placed on "interim suspension" pending the outcome of the case.

headline: Editorial: Setting the right tone
abstract: Philadelphia School Superintendent Arlene Ackerman told parents and students at South Philadelphia High that there would be zero tolerance for violence and that the school would have all the resources needed to ensure students' safety. The latest efforts come eight months after an ugly attack on dozens of mostly Asian students, and a finding by the Justice Department that the students' claims of abuse had merit.

headline: York Adams Academy could become 'model'
abstract: York Adams Academy, the county's only high school specifically designed for drop-outs, will be the site of a state Senate hearing on Friday. The academy accepts students from around the county who have left their home school district but still want to earn a high school diploma. The school has faced certification issues from the state Department of Education because there is no exact classification for it.

headline: Health care costs rising, and reform is cited
abstract: Congress has not hesitated to bash the federal health care reform. Employees at many companies are finding they will have new benefits such as extended coverage for young adults and coverage for children with pre-existing conditions at a low additional cost. The health care environment could change once again if Republicans gain a majority in the House of Representatives.

headline: Nesting pair of bald eagles confirmed in Crescent
abstract: The state Game Commission has confirmed Allegheny County's first nesting pair of American bald eagles. According to the commission, there are 174 known nesting sites in 48 Pennsylvania counties.

headline: Dubious record for jobless rate
abstract: The Lehigh Valley posted a 9.8% unemployment rate according to the PA Department of Labor and Industry, but the author suggests that the employment conditions may be a lot worse. The author says the unemployment rate would be 17% if it included all the people who want to work, including part-timers who want full-time work, according to the US Department of Labor.

headline: N.J. schools stunned by cuts
abstract: NJ Governor Chris Christie announced that he will cut aid to NJ schools by 5% of their total budgets, much higher than was predicted by NJ schools. The governor called on legislators to adopt new school worker and teacher union negotiation rules in order to keep school's labor costs down. He cited the New Jersey Education Association as one union to be targeted.

headline: Chester Downs makes case for Harrah’s table games
abstract: The state gaming control board held a hearing on the petition submitted by the Chester Downs and Marina LLC requesting authorization to set up table games at Harrah’s Chester Casino and Racetrack.

headline: Pennsylvania: Tax Revenue Falls Short
abstract: Pennsylvania's tax revenues were $125 million short in May leaving the state with a $1.2 billion deficit for the current budget year. PA Governor Rendell identified $700 million to $800 million in cuts and revenues to make up for the deficit.

headline: Story: Pa. tops in taxes from casino gambling
abstract: PA has collected more gambling revenue in the last year than any other state.  This includes gambling behemoth Nevada.  PA was first in revenue with $1.1 billion, Indiana second with $878 million and Nevada third with $831 million.  PA has just 9 casinos in operation, but takes 55% of slots revenue.  Nevada only takes 8 percent.

headline: New dean named for University of Pennsylvania’s School of Medicine
abstract: J. Larry Jameson, a prominent molecular endocrinologist and dean Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, today was named to become dean of the University of Pennsylvania’s School of Medicine and executive vice president of the Penn health system next year. Jameson will replace Penn’s Arthur Rubenstein on July 1, 2011. Rubenstein announced his retirement as dean and head of the health system earlier this year.

headline: Stimulus helped, more work ahead, Holden says
abstract: U.S. Representative Tim Holden said Wednesday in a meeting with The Patriot-News editorial board that the stimulus bill did a lot of good. But he said that Democrats have not done a good job of informing the public. State Senator Dave Argall, R-Schuylkill County, is challenging Holden in the November election.

headline: Officials break ground on corridor project
abstract: The $27 million Broad Street Corridor project had its ground-breaking ceremony. The project is a cooperative  effort of Hazleton, West Hasleton, and PennDOT. One of the first tasks of the project is utility pole relocation to ensure the safety of drivers along the road.

headline: Community Foundation forms merger with The Pittsburgh Foundation
abstract: In an effort to expand its ability to make grants and increase support for nonprofits in the county, The Community Foundation of Westmoreland County will merge with The Pittsburgh Foundation. Under the terms of the merger, the Community Foundation of Westmoreland County will operate as part of The Pittsburgh Foundation but will maintain its local board, staff, and Greensburg offices.

headline: Philly area's smaller banks not hurrying to repay TARP funds
abstract: Banks nationwide have been able to repay most of the federal money they received from the 2008/2009 bailout effort. Many banks in Philadelphia are reluctant to sell new shares at depressed prices to repay the government investment. Bank executives have stated that small-bank gains came at the expense of larger and troubled banks, rather than from pure economic growth.

headline:
State: PennDOT doesn't have to release Route 22 files
Agency won open records battle with Lehigh Valley Planning Commission
abstract: The PA Office of Open Records has backed the PA Department of Transportation's refusal to release information on a traffic-engineering study to the Lehigh Valley Planning Commission. The study concerned planning to extend Route 22 in the Lehigh valley from 4 to 6 lanes or improving the road.

headline:
Gay group honors senator
Eichelberger praised for resolving dispute
abstract: PA Senator John Eichelberger, who has introduced legislation to define marriage as between a man and a woman in the state constitution, is being given a 'spirit award' by a gay community leader whom he helped in a dispute with a national gay organization. John DeBartola of Keystone Alliance/Gay Newsletter gave him the award for helping in his dispute with Parents, Families and Friends of Gays and Lesbians, a national organization.

headline: PennDOT announces tentative work plans
abstract: The State Department of Transportation has announced tentative work plans. PennDOT suggests motorists should drive with caution throughout all work areas and be alert for signed work zones requiring the use of headlights.

headline: Monroe County Area Agency on Aging: Save on Medicare drug plan costs
abstract: Some Medicare beneficiaries are eligible to benefit for "Extra Help" subsidies to help pay for premiums, deductibles, and co-payments.

headline: State law-enforcement lite: Proposed ethics commission is an idea without enough substance
abstract: While the idea of a larger commission to go after ethics violations sounds good, it is largely unnecessary when understanding how the committee would be operated.  Such a committee would be shacked by the inability to prosecute offenses.  At the end of the day, one set of elected or appointed members would be responsible for making decisions on other elected officials.

headline: Onorato slams Corbett's opposition to drilling tax
abstract: PA Democratic gubernatorial candidate Dan Onorato alleged Wednesday that the opposition of his Republican rival, PA Attorney General Tom Corbett, to a severance tax on natural-gas drilling is evidence that Corbett was more interested in helping the industry than forcing it to pay for environmental problems.

headline: Allentown board OKs most of superintendent's plans
abstract: The Allentown School Board Education Committee signed off Thursday on Superintendent Gerald Zahorchak's five-year leadership and curriculum plans, except for one. The committee did not vote and did not comment on Zahorchak's plan, to remove four principals in exchange for millions of dollars in federal school improvement grants that mandate leadership, staff or governance changes as conditions for receiving the money. The committee's 8-0 approvals send Zahorchak's plans to the full board for adoption on October 28.

headline: Gambling revenue to mean tax rebate
abstract: Revenue from slots gambling will provide tax relief for homeowners, but not for state workers who are subject to layoffs due to a state deficit expected to reach $63 million for the fiscal year. Slots revenue provided $616.5 million for property tax relief in 2010.

headline: Hempfield teachers union agrees to health care 'escape clause'
abstract: A union representing teachers in the Hempfield Area School District has agreed to an "escape clause" that could allow the district to change health care providers, a move the union says would save $1.4 million.

headline: Officials: Latinos key to accurate city count
abstract: Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta is encouraging Hazleton residents to fill out the census as he believes that Hazelton has grew in population since the 2000 census and filling out the census is important for the Hazelton area to gain federal funds. Amilcar Arroyo, editor of a Hispanic newspaper in Hazleton is working to encourage Latinos to fill out the census and to quell their fears of revealing personal information.

headline: License suspension hinders offenders' drive to succeed
abstract: A drug offense in Pennsylvania suspends your driver's license when released from prison, making it difficult for ex-offenders to find work once released. PA Representative Jake Wheatley finds the policy counterproductive and has introduced legislation to let ex-inmates apply for a limited license once they have been released from jail.

headline: Inmate work program worthwhile for everyone involved
abstract: Pennsylvania's Inmate Community Work Program, permits outside agencies and nonprofit organizations to request the use of supervised inmate labor to work on community service projects. The organizations provide materials while the inmates provide the labor.

headline: Seasonal flu shot to include H1N1 vaccine
abstract: This fall's flu shot will include a vaccine for the H1N1 virus but those at the Erie County Department of Health wonder whether the vaccine will arrive in time to avoid the spread of the disease. They also have questioned whether the disease will be prevalent in Northwest Pennsylvania like it was last year.

headline: Senate Republicans block campaign-ad legislation
abstract: Not a single Republican was able to support the DISCLOSE act which would have forced more stringent disclosure requirements on corporations, unions, and other independent groups that finance ads for political campaigns.  Senate Democrats even made last minute changes to the bill to attract bipartisan support.

headline: A second, unrelated measles case in Philly suburb
abstract: The second case of measles in less than a month has been reported in Montgomery County, but U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) officials said Wednesday that an investigation had determined that the cases; both involving people who recently did relief work in southern African countries experiencing outbreaks were not connected. The CDC will then work with the PA Department of Health to track down passengers who sat in the same row and in two rows ahead and behind.

headline: Alternative teacher certification in PA could be school saver
abstract: Traditional educators view alternative certification with suspicion, as if customary collegiate philosophy and practice were the only answers to exemplary classroom instruction. Although traditional training involves writing lesson plans, it is with fictional students and often guided by professors who have not been in an elementary or secondary classroom for a decade or more. Extreme mentoring a more effective alternative, in includes immersing an educator into the classroom with a safety net, which includes co-planning and co-teaching with supportive mentors, is a key component for success.

headline: No money to burn: Firefighters' cancer bill would prove too costly
abstract: Author agrees with Governor Ed Rendell’s decision to veto HB 1231, a bill that would cover the cost of any cancer a firefighter may develop during his or her lifetime. The current law only protects firefighters if they develop lung cancer.

headline: Resource offers genealogy assistance, especially in researching black families
abstract: Riverbends Inc., a genealogical research firm, is offering free services under the condition that customers scan and post documentation that can be shared and researched against other databases. Unlike sites like Ancestry.com, Riverbends Inc. aims to help black people in particular, who often struggle to trace their families, with researching their ancestry.

headline: Proposed natural gas drilling site raises concern
abstract: Fox Township Supervisor Randy Gradizzi challenged the PA Department of Environmental Protection over the placement of a Marcellus Shale drill site that he said was too close to a drinking water source. Gradizzi said the PA DEP needs to take a closer look at drill sites.

headline: In the suburbs, incumbents, rivals give their (predictable) take
abstract: As the vote on healthcare approaches members of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation have voiced their support or opposition to the bill. Those voicing concern are US Representative Pat Meehan, PA Representative Bryan Lentz, 6th district Democratic candidate Doug Pike. Those in favor are US Rep. Joe Sestak and US Rep. Patrick Murphy.

headline: Families with tainted water reject driller's plan for treatment
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection has issued an order that gives Cabot Oil and Gas Corp. until May 15 to install treatment systems in 14 affected homes and submit a report proving that the systems reduce methane and any other contaminants in the water to safe levels.

headline: Toprani wooed for state AG run
abstract: Washington County District Attorney Steven Toprani has confirmed Tuesday he's been approached to run for state attorney general by the PA Republican Party. Toprani has not made a decision on whether or not he will run but has met with current PA Attorney General and gubernatorial candidate Tom Corbett.

headline: Philly school reorganization continues
abstract: Philadelphia School Superintendent Arlene Ackerman has made some major moves in her bid to reorganize the Philadelphia School District.  Just a month and a half before school begins, Ackerman has dismantled the regional division of schools and has made a number of personnel changes.  Even more changes are expected before school begins in September.

headline: New Jersey Transit seeks to add WiFi to rail lines, train stations
abstract: The New Jersey transit agency said Wednesday it was seeking a company to provide wireless broadband, or WiFi, Internet service for its 12 rail lines and 165 train stations.

headline: Hold on overtime expanded
abstract: Dispatchers and call-takers at the City of Harrisburg's 911 center and a handful of police officers in the Police Bureau's Technical Services division joined city firefighters this week in receiving IOU's for overtime worked. The holds have occurred because all money budgeted for overtime in the respective departments is spent, additional overtime can't be paid until budget transfers are approved. In all, about 100 of the city's 557 workers are affected.

headline: Fay-Penn to buy land in Upper Tyrone
abstract: Fay-Penn is negotiating to purchase 180 acres in Upper Tyrone and will be looking at using the acreage for a mix of residential use and an industrial business park. The paperwork related to the sale has not been finalized, but Fay-Penn Economic Development representatives are confident the sale will got through.

headline: More Raw Milk Permits Suspended in PA
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture has urged consumers to discard raw milk purchased from the Elmer Z. and Martha B. King farm in Aaronsburg, Centre County and from Cedar Hollow Far in Mill Hall, Clinton County. According to a press release from the PA Department of Agriculture, samples taken from the farms tested positively for Listeria monocytogenes and Campylobacter. No illnesses have been reported.

headline: Helping "Main Street": Pa housing trust fund legislation would open doors for most vulnerable
abstract: The author submits that the proposed National Housing Trust Fund would give Pennsylvania $35 million to set up a trust fund in Pennsylvania that would give money to low-income workers to buy homes. Bills in the PA Senate and PA House of Representatives have been introduced to set up a trust fund that would also support low-income senior citizens. A poll by the Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania shows support of the proposal.

headline: Commissioners want Munchak to resign
abstract: Lackawanna County Commissioners Corey O'Brien and Mike Washo have asked fellow commissioner A.J. Munchak to resign following an indictment him and former Lackawanna County Commissioner Robert  Cordaro received for racketeering, conspiracy, and honest services fraud. The commissioner and the former commissioner allegedly took kickbacks from area businesses.

headline: Arlen Spector switches parties
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Spector D-Pennsylvania defends his decision to switch parties, after being criticized for doing so to better position himself for the upcoming election. Spector explained that he changed parties because the Republican party changed its makeup. He points to the 200,000 people switched out of the republican party to vote for Hiliary Clinton or Barack Obama.

headline: Time to pass a budget Pa. can afford
abstract: PA Senator Bob Mensch states that PA Governor Rendell's proposed budget for 2010-2011 is bloated and will result in higher taxes. He said the state needs to stay within their means and adopt a conservative budget. He notes decreases in taxes for individuals and businesses as a way to ensure this.

headline: No word after lawyers meet in Lower Merion webcam case
abstract: Lawyers for the Lower Merion School District and one of the students suing the district over its webcam enabled laptops met with a federal judge Thursday but would not say if they were any closer to resolving the dispute.  The meeting lasted 75 minutes and followed a number of filings from both sides that suggest that the dispute is far from over.

headline: Nonunion hotels make Philly a tough sell to labor gatherings
abstract: Labor unions, which hold big multiple night membership meetings attended by thousands of delegates, are not booking their conventions at the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia, a loss of up to $30 million a year in delegate spending. Union's have a policy of refusing to stay in nonunion hotels which is the major reason no such events are held in Philadelphia. The two largest hotels closest to the Convention Center, the Philadelphia Marriott Downtown and the Loews Philadelphia, are nonunion.

headline: DEP takes soil, air, water samples from Jeannette glass plant site
abstract: Some residents and former workers at the former Jeannette Glass factory are worried that possible hazards at the site, a city landmark for more than a century, run deeper than its deteriorating buildings. Armed with search warrants, inspectors for the state Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) spent two days this week taking soil, air and water samples at the former glass factory property, looking for evidence of environmental violations. If property owner Abe Zion of New York is found to be in violation, he could be forced to clean up the site and ordered to pay fines, according to DEP officials.

headline: Gaming officials act mad as hatter
abstract: An audit released by state Auditor General Jack Wagner revealed the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board ran up expensive travel bills and awarded millions of dollars in contracts without public votes.

headline: Muncy Hospital’s renovations championed
abstract: The Muncy Valley Hospital held a community night open house allowing community members to see the facility’s newly renovated medical surgical unit.

headline:
Temporary rules for table games OK'd
Interim regulations will be in effect for two years to allow casinos to offer games quickly.
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board has approved temporary regulations for table games in Pennsylvania's casinos in order for the games to be available this summer. The regulations covered which games could be played, oversight of the games, and security in the casinos with the games. Revenue from the games is included in this year's budget and the temporary regulations will last two years.

headline:
Pennsylvania Tavern Owners Pushing for Small Games of Chance
Taverns across the Keystone State could soon have more than just food and drinks to offer customers
