abstract: The PA Tavern Association is lobbying the state legislature to allow small games of chance in Pennsylvania taverns. Tavern owners said the small games of chance would help them create jobs and stay in business while giving money to local organizations and to the state.

headline: Pennsylvania's primary election is just 14 days away
abstract: One of the most highly contested races is playing out in Pennsylvania's 19th congressional district which includes York and Adams counties and parts of Cumberland county. Representative Todd Platts -R and his challenger Mike Smeltzer are competing for the Republican nomination. Smeltzers campaign has raised questions over what would happen if Platts accepted an appointment in the Obama administration, which could lead to Governor Rendell affecting who would appear on the ballot.

headline: State reps honored by scouts
abstract: PA Reps. Russ Fairchild and Merle Phillips were awarded the Susquehanna Council, Boy Scouts of America 2010 Distinguished Citizen Award by scout leaders during a reception at the Charles B. Degenstein Campus Center on the campus of Susquehanna University. The two were honored for representing the interests of boy scouts in the legislative arena.

headline: Foxwoods gets extension in struggle to keep license
abstract: Foxwoods Casino is asking for another 3 months to plan their venture in South Philadelphia.  Their lawyers appeared before the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board but only ended up getting a 2 week extension.  The casino is considering turning over the project to another wealthier developer should that opportunity come along.

headline: Western Montgomery County career, tech center goes state of the art
abstract: Western Montgomery Career and Technology Center last week introduced a new state-of-the art gadget, putting the $27,000 computerized automobile wheel-alignment system through its paces. The center, in Limerick, is starting the school year after completing a $36.7 million renovation that included adding 50,000 square feet of space. Career and technical schools like Western Montgomery play a key role in the state's education system.

headline: Is an E-Z-only turnpike up ahead?
abstract: The turnpike is ready to study the idea of converting the toll road to a cashless collection system. If viable, an all-electronic system would eliminate the need for the turnpike's 615 toll collectors. Carl DeFebo, a turnpike spokesman. said 62 percent of the 520,000 drivers who travel the turnpike daily have E-ZPass transponders in their vehicles.

headline: $18.4M budget holds Armstrong County taxes steady
abstract: Commissioners adopted the final $18.4 million budget, keeping Armstrong County real estate taxes at their current rate of 15.5 mills.

headline: Road fund short $470M
abstract: Hearings to determine the financial impact on Pennsylvania in the wake of the federal government’s rejection of tolls on Interstate 80 have begun. Several officials, including state Department of Transportation Secretary Allen Biehler and Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission CFO Nick Grieshaber, are expected to testify.

headline: 10 Pennsylvania legislative staffers joined $100,000 club in 2009
abstract: Ten PA Legislative staffers joined the list of staffers making over $100,000 annually, making the number of people on the list 83. Two PA House Republican staffers made more than Governor Rendell. Tim Potts of Democracy Rising PA decried the legislature for giving salary increases while cutting vital services from the state budget.

headline: Sweetened-drink tax idea generates negative buzz
abstract: Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's proposal to tax sugary drinks in Pittsburgh at 2 cents per ounce is said to be an initiative to encourage a healthier lifestyle in the city. Opponents say it is just another way to tax to make up the $15 million pension fund gap the city faces. The Pennsylvania Beverage Association has opposed the tax which Mayor Ravenstahl says is copied from Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's proposal.

headline: Pennsylvania governor urging lawmakers to increase the transportation funds
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell announced in a session today that he wants at least $472 million a year in additional funding for roads, bridges, and mass transit. This statement comes after the federal government denied a plan to toll interstate 80.

headline: $500K grant marked for cyber learning in Beaver, Allegheny counties
abstract: A $500,000 federal grant will give the National Network of Digital Schools the ability to help a non-profit in Beaver County to help Beaver and Allegheny County schools explore creating their own cyber learning programs.

headline: Developer booted from Philly Family Court deal says courts, Parking Authority targeted him
abstract: Conshohocken developer Donald Pulver was booted from a $200 million project to build the new Philadelphia Family Court building after the Philadelphia Inquirer reported that he had a side deal to share development fees with another lawyer.  Pulver says that the Philadelphia Parking Authority and city courts are working together to target his involvement with the project.

headline: Editorial: Cleaning up one oil mess
abstract: In the wake of the deadly BP oil-rig disaster in the Gulf of Mexico and a fire that broke out on a nearby rig Thursday, it's fortunate that US President Barack Obama appears to be moving ahead quickly on his administration's pledge to "clean up the mess" at the Interior Department. A former federal prosecutor and Department of Justice inspector general, Michael R. Bromwich, was named in June to take over the Interior that oversees offshore drilling.

headline: Legislature takes step backward on open-records laws
abstract: Bills to amend the 2008 Right to Know Law are on the move in the state Capitol, just a few weeks before the November election and after a one-year lull in any work on open-records legislation. In the Senate, Bill 1469 won unanimous approval last week and moved to the House for review, which would exempt volunteer fire and rescue companies, significantly cut back on the records available from government contractors. House, Bill 1667 would eliminate public access to dates of birth and home addresses, vital identifiers which allow both the public and journalists to distinguish between persons with the same name.

headline: New PennDOT salt-storage sheds should be done soon
abstract: PennDOT decided to raze the tarp-covered salt-storage sheds after a study showed the structures might not withstand the combined stress of high winds and heavy snow. The two new salt-storage sheds for York County will be completed soon

headline: Jobless rate here drops to 8%
abstract: According to the state Department of Labor and Industry, the unemployment rate in Lancaster County dropped to 8 percent. Despite the drop, the rate remained 4.4 percentage points higher than it was at the beginning of the recession in December 2007.

headline: Green light given for design work on regional water system
abstract: Engineering firm Herbert, Rowland and Grubic Inc. has been given a green light by the Lycoming County Water and Sewer Authority to move forward on design work related to expanding the Halls Station Water System into a regional system. The authority approved an agreement with the firm that will allow it to begin designing water systems in the Fairfield Road corridor and Grey Fox Plaza.

headline: 4 school districts to go less than 180 days
abstract: The state Department of Education has given permission for four school districts -- Canon-McMillan, East Allegheny, Penn-Trafford and Philadelphia -- to hold classes for fewer than 180 days this year because of the snow. The state received 45 such requests after last month's snowstorm forced many districts to close for five days or more.

headline: Huge transportation funding deficit looming in Harrisburg.
abstract: Work is underway to find some way to close the gap in projected state revenue. There is debate among legislatures in Pennsylvania on how to make up the billions Pennsylvania has been spending on highways and bridges. One proposal is to charge every car that leaves or enters Pennsylvania one dollar and every truck five dollars to make up the difference.

headline: Mount Airy CEO: Casino 'in midst of a turnaround'
abstract: Despite poor revenue numbers by casinos that had been open for more than a year on Memorial Day, the state increased revenue on Memorial by $23 million but revenues were $157 million less in the month of May compared to last year. Mount Airy Casino owner George Toth said his casino is in the midst of a turnaround.

headline: Nutter, activists cheer immigration 'sanity' as judge rejects part of Ariz. Law
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter spoke before an excited crowd of 100 citizens and immigrants in the wake of a federal court decision that struck down the controversial Arizona immigration law.  Nutter relayed positive remarks about the role of immigration in the nation's history as well as the current state of immigrant relations.

headline: More Philadelphia-area health systems requiring employees to get flu shots
abstract: The hospitals in the Main Line Health system could persuade only about 60 percent of their staff to get flu shots each year even though it seemed obvious that the shots would reduce the odds that workers would get sick or spread the virus to vulnerable patients. This year Main Line Health Inc. is taking a much tougher stance, it is requiring employees and doctors to get the shot or get fired.

headline: Candidates tackle party politics, debate drilling tax
abstract: Democratic candidate for the Congressional 5th District in Pennsylvania Michael Pipe, left, and Congressman Glenn Thompson answer questions during the League of Women Voters' candidate forum on Wednesday. Candidates tackled questions about breaking up those partisan politics, which stall productive decision-and policymaking.

headline: State Sen. Jake Corman ponders run for U.S. Senate
abstract: Republican state senator Jake Corman is exploring the possibility of running for Pennsylvania’s U.S. Senate seat against Bob Casey Jr.

headline: 2 projects have job-creating potential
abstract: Two city projects with job-creation potential, including Moran Industries’ future rail-service complex, were reviewed positively by the city’s finance committee. The committee also endorsed awarding a contract for rail siding work at the site to a Maryland firm that was the lowest of five bidders with a bid of $183,647.

headline: Doherty's wife urges support for an Onorato/Doherty ticket
abstract: Donna Doherty, wife of Scranton Mayor Chris Doherty, sent an e-mail out to supporters urging them to vote for a ticket of her husband and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato as running mates in the 2010 gubernatorial election on the PA2010.com website. She encouraged those that the two would make a good ticket but did not specify which would be the governor candidate and which the lieutenant governor candidate.

headline: Gas companies eager to tap Marcellus Shale
abstract: Natural gas and energy companies are investing heavily in Pennsylvania's Marcellus Shale region in order to profit from the large pockets of natural gas tha lies beneath the shale. Some companies are buying out others or are moving their corporate headquarters to Pennsylvania to better take advantage of the energy resource.

headline: Incinerator debt came and went with no check from the authority
abstract: The city of Harrisburg recently was in negotiations to work out a long term plan to pay the city's Incinerator debt. Brian Hudson who was appointed by Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell to help advise the mayor and the city with their finances was apart of the negotiations.

headline: Gov. Rendell in on talks to prevent Sestak run
abstract: PA Governor Rendell disclosed that he had numerous conversations with US President Obama's Chief of Staff Rahm Emmanuel about keeping US Rep. Joe Sestak off the Democratic primary for Senate in Pennsylvania. Gov. Rendell dismissed Republican criticisms but said the White House should release any documents related to offering Rep. Sestak a job in the White House.

headline: Joe Sestak is a friend of Israel
abstract: This opinion piece seeks to respond to a series of ads calling into question Joe Sestak's commitment to Israel's security concerns.  The piece details Sestak's experience in dealing with Israel through his visits in his official capacity with the Navy, along with his stated positions on major pieces of US-Israel foreign policy.  The piece was written by Peter Joseph of the Israel Policy Forum.

headline: Ackerman cites excitement at Promise Academies
abstract: Hundreds of district students started their school year in one of Philadelphia Schools Superintendent Arlene Ackerman's six Promise Academies. As a bonus, parents and students are invited to attend an enrichment fair at the school today, during which students will choose to participate in programs including boxing, rowing, dress design and dance.

headline: PA lawmakers act to ease farm truck rules
abstract: Legislation relieving trucks weighing between 17,000 and 26,000 pounds bearing farm truck license plates or exemption stickers from stringent federal commercial standards has been approved as part of a transportation bill passed by the PA House and Senate and sent to Governor Ed Rendell. The exemptions were initially sidetracked by representatives of state agencies who were concerned they would impact funding from the federal government.

headline: Bucknell alum tapped by Corbett
abstract: Gov.-elect Tom Corbett has name Alan Walker, a Bucknell University alum and member of the school’s board of trustees, to be the state’s next secretary of the Department of Community and Economic Development.

headline: DEP to analyze air quality in area
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Protection is gathering samples to analyze air quality in areas near natural gas operations in Washington and Greene counties. The department's efforts, which will be conducted in four phases, with each phase lasting one week, are intended to isolate the source of odors that have prompted complaints from residents. Under the Air Pollution Control Act, any entity operating a source of odors may be fined up to $25,000.

headline: AG: Complaints, Money Recovered or Saved Up
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett announced that the PA Bureau of Consumer Protection received more consumer complaints in 2009 than in any other year. The bureau also saved or recovered over $32 million for consumers as a result of actions taken by the Attorney General. The most common complaint had to do with credit-related issues.

headline: Business tax structure favors select few in Pa.
abstract: The authors write that Pennsylvania's business tax structure is out of date and must be changed to include combined reporting. The author's suggest that it would result in lower businesses taxes for businesses owners because those businesses that currently use tax loopholes to avoid paying taxes. The article is written by PA Rep. David Levdansky and Rep. Mike Sturla.

headline: Third District primaries mostly drama-free
abstract: South Jersey's Third District will feature one of the nation's most volatile U.S. House races this fall as Democratic incumbent U.S. Rep. John Adler is likely to face Republican newcomer Jon Runyan. However neither plans to debate their primary opponents. Some question Runyan's strategy to not debate his primary opponent since his stance on policies is largely unknown.

headline: State budget solution always begins with taxes
abstract: The author states that PA Governor Rendell's budget proposal needs to be consistent with inflation. He says the governor's proposal is too high with a 4% increase. He says that the state will need to come up with increased taxes to cover its large spending plans.

headline: Tenure for all
abstract: The idea that tenure is central to the problems ailing public education is unreasonable according to this opinion piece.  The stereotype of tenured positions creating cushy, unproductive jobs for life has grown wildly out of proportion.  Even positions with tenure offer many ways to get your position terminated.  The department could be eliminated, the school could have financial problems, or one of a handful of rules could be broken.  The one type of conduct that tenure protects teachers from is being fired for having an opinion.  With the reduction in the amount of tenure-track faculty at universities we are going to see a shift in the type of education being provided to students.

headline: Ending DROP may be easier said than done
abstract: If the track record of states and cities across the country is any guide, Philadelphia Mayor Nutter faces significant legal hurdles in his effort to kill the city's Deferred Retirement Option Program pension benefit. In Philadelphia, the fear of losing DROP is so great that when Nutter asked Council to eliminate it for any employees not yet enrolled, he triggered a flood of 933 new applications. The program lets city employees collect a lump sum upon retirement in exchange for accepting a lower monthly lifetime benefit.

headline: Governor: Medical malpractice payouts dropping
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced Tuesday that medical malpractice fund payouts statewide have decreased by 61 percent since 2003, and that's good news for doctors who pay increasingly less for medical malpractice insurance. According to figures released by the governor's office, total malpractice payouts dropped from more than $341 million in 2000 to about $178 million last year. Physicians overall now pay 64 percent less on average for malpractice insurance than they did in 2002.

headline: High court reviewing magisterial court changes
abstract: A plan that would consolidate the magisterial district serving Dunmore and the city’s North Scranton and Green Ridge sections is under review by the state Supreme Court. The consolidation would reduce the number of district courts in Lackawanna county from 11 to 10.

headline: Senator: Casino offers jobs, development for region
abstract: Sen. John Wozniak responds to a column in which Publisher Robin L. Quillon expressed his anti-gaming views. Sen. Wozniak, while appreciative of Quillon’s passion, disagrees with his position. He believes casino development would be beneficial to the region.

headline: Pa. 611 to be dedicated as memorial to slain trooper
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation  is holding a dedication ceremony to commemorate the naming PA 611 between Main Street and Interstate 380 in Coolbaugh Township, Monroe County the Trooper Joshua D. Miller Memorial Highway. The state legislature passed the naming of the highway into law for State Trooper Joshua Miller who died in the line action.

headline: Council may end ban on workers' political activity
abstract: City Council's Law and Government Committee approved a bill that would ask voters to cede powers to change the city's home rule charter on political activities by council's workers to the council. This is an attempt to loosen up political activity restrictions on city workers, especially committee people.  The Nutter Administration said the restrictions may be too strict.

headline: Old-school campaigner
abstract: Pennsylvania State Auditor General Jack Wagner-Democrat is probably the most well known of the four Democratic candidates running for Governor, but he is a distant third in fund raising and is trailing in the polls. The biggest blow to his campaign was Governor Ed Rendell's financial backers to throw their money behind Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato-Democrat.

headline: SCI-Fayette guard arrested on drug smuggling charges
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Police Organized Crime Task Force has charged a prison guard at the State Correctional Institute-Fayetter prison of smuggling marijuana and a gun into the prison and selling the marijuana to inmates.

headline: Agency cuts road, bridge allocations drastically
abstract: The Southwestern Pennsylvania Commission, a 10-county regional planning agency, approved a plan to slash spending on roads and bridges by 32 percent over the next 4 years.  They say it comes as a result of funding shortages.  The American Society of Civil Engineers are disappointed to hear of the shortfall in funding.  They rated the state's infrastructure in May and gave the state a D+ rating.

headline: Little relief in sight for Philadelphia region's dry spell
abstract: The National Weather Service has posted a "red flag" fire danger warning for Wednesday afternoon into the evening, when the air over Philadelphia could mimic that of Las Vegas. It has been an extraordinarily warm six months since the snows melted. In the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast, 27 stations reported all-time record highs for the March 1-Aug. 31 period, according to the Northeast Regional Climate Center.

headline: Incinerator manager sues over missed payments
abstract: Covanta Harrisburg Inc., the company hired to run Harrisburg's incinerator is suing the city over what it claims is more than $1.9 million in missed loan payments. The lawsuit, filed Tuesday in Dauphin County Court, is the third lodged against the cash-strapped city in the last month as missed payments on the $288 million in debt tied to the incinerator continue to grow. On Friday, Mayor Linda Thompson asked the Rendell administration for distressed-municipality status for the city, a move Thompson said she hopes will help kick-start development of a long-term financial recovery plan.

headline: Lackawanna, Luzerne counties similar, should work together
abstract: Population estimates and demographic statistics released through the U.S. Census Bureau revealed the median age in Lackawanna and Luzerne counties is rising. The counties also experienced similar gains on both per capita and median household income, providing more evidence to support collaboration between the two bodies.

headline: Dozens volunteer at Vet Museum on Comcast Cares Day
abstract: More than 50 people turned up at the Pennsylvania Veterans Museum to volunteer as part of Comcast Cares Day. Volunteers worked throughout the day, painting, making repairs, and cleaning out a storage area that will be renovated to become a resource room for Delaware County Veterans.

headline: Not enough money for Great Lakes in Obama's budget, environmental groups say
abstract: President Barack Obama cut Great Lakes funding by 36% in his 2011 budget, resulting in a $175 million cut in funds to restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. Healing Our Waters-Great Lakes Coalition said that the cuts doesn't allow for the protection of the great lakes and that funding should be restored to that in recent years. The Brookings institute said investment in the great lakes will pay off economically.

headline: Alternate pension solution rejected by Pittsburgh officials
abstract: City officials along with the city's finance director said that shifting the city's parking garages into the city's lagging pension fund would be a poor decision. Opponents noted that the city's parking authority owes $105 million in debts.

headline: Tuned In: TV news: speed bumps on the way to accuracy
abstract: Due to the competitive nature of local TV news stories sometimes unfold in a way that makes you wonder to what lengths a news outlet will go to get a story first and how much accuracy matters. One example of this is when local station WPXI reported on a story about former Pittsburgh Steelers Santonio Holmes being escorted of a plane, when he had actually left on his own.

headline: Academy credited for better discipline
abstract: The Blended Schools Academy, Palmyra Area School District's new alternative education program, has helped reduce secondary discipline issues. In-school and out-of-school suspensions and detentions were cut in half in 2009-10, compared with the previous year. This was the first full year for the program, piloted in the second semester of the 2008-09 year to replace the IU-13 alternative education program, which closed.

headline: Former Gov. Ridge joins Marcellus Shale Coalition
abstract: The Marcellus Shale Coalition has hired a number of advisors from the administration of Gov Ed Rendell, but now have hired former Gov. Tom Ridge to act as a strategic advisor for the coalition.  It is unknown if his lobbying skills or political clout will be used in the forthcoming debate about taxing the natural gas industry.

headline: Michael Smerconish: The power of 9/11 pin money
abstract: Steven Singer, the man whose unique marketing campaign is ubiquitous on Philadelphia radio and billboards has become a fundraising superstar for his contributions to the construction of the Flight 93 National Memorial in Shanksville, PA. Singer through his fundraising efforts has raised over $100,000 for the memorial.

headline: Republicans, Democrats should revisit history to jump-start economy
abstract: We now know that the U.S. economy hit bottom 15 months ago and that the recession is over. Many argue that the recession was caused by financial deregulation which has enjoyed bipartisan support, starting with President Carter and continuing with President Reagan. Deregulation has been a major theme of U.S. policy since the early 1970s, and has continued.

headline: Revenue stop is big challenge for Pennsylvania budget
abstract: A deficit ranging from $3 billion to $4 billion is projected for the 2011-2012 budget, despite cost-cutting measures that have yielded savings for the state. According to a report from the National Conference of State Legislatures, while state revenues have begun to increase, the growth from those revenues is unlikely to be sufficient enough to replace expiring ARRA (American Recovery and Reinvestment Act) funds or cover projected increases in entitlement spending. Proposals to sell the state-owned liquor stores to private owners and revamp the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission are being discussed as revenue generators.

headline: GOP candidates make their cases for the 8th
abstract: Four Republican candidates for the 8th Congressional district criticized both the opposition and members of their own party during a forum sponsored by Republicans for Action. Each candidate had a 10-minute introductory speech and then was asked questions submitted by attendees in the crowd of about 150.

headline:
Some parents, students oppose drug testing
Say it runs counter to the principle that we are innocent until proven guilty.
abstract: Penn Manor High School implemented a drug testing policy in 2006 that parents, students, and members of the community have said are a violation of students' rights. Opponents have said that the school is overstepping its authority. These include the American Civil Liberities Union.

headline: Pa. Senate panel tables bill to ban gay marriage
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee voted 8-6 to table a bill that would amend Pennsylvania's constitution to ban gay marriage. The bill's main sponsor was PA Senator John Eichelberger.

headline: Penn students go to the dogs to take a bite out of study stress
abstract: "Canine Chillout," which is a pet-therapy study break held in Rodin College House at the University of Pennsylvania to help students get through the stress of finals. The event was hosted by VETPETS, a pet-visitation outreach program developed by Penn's School of Veterinary Medicine. All the dogs in the program belong to Penn Vet faculty, staff and students who volunteer to come to VETPETS events.

headline: Pennsylvania rail museum gets critical $5M
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's office will give $5 million to the Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania to preserve railroad artifacts. The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission the money will help connect the railroad's past to the present. The money will build a roundhouse to store the artifacts and the rest will go to building an interpretive exhibit about Pennsylvania's train history.

headline: Historical groups left in lurch by funding cuts
abstract: Sites of historical significance have until recently received regular appropriations from the state government, but the most recent budget passed has eliminated grants for historical sites entirely.  It is causing a lot of such sites across the state to have to consider their entire existence.  Many organizations have had to lay off employees in recent years and some will have to contemplate shutting down all together.

headline: Obama to stop in Philadelphia on barnstorming tour
abstract: President Barack Obama plans to hit the road for a series of campaign rallies beginning later this month to mobilize dispirited Democrats to vote in the Nov. 2 midterm elections, party officials said Thursday. Obama plans to stop in Philadelphia on Oct. 10 as a part of the tour.

headline: Drillers split on PA severance tax
abstract: PA House Democratic and Senate Republican leaders face a narrow window to negotiate a compromise severance tax bill on natural gas production as the legislative session winds down. The Marcellus Shale Coalition is united in their opposition to the House-approved bill to levy a significant severance tax rate at 39 cents per thousand cubic feet, of natural gas at the wellhead. However, the coalition is split when it comes to opposing any severance tax as a cost of doing business.

headline: Less trouble closer to home
abstract: Author questions the necessity of spending millions of dollars each year on sending members of the Pennsylvania Society to New York City for an annual dinner.

headline: Odd Man Out
abstract: Author profiles Anthony Williams, 11-year state senator for Philadelphia’s eighth district and democratic candidate for governor.

headline: Mine company's move to Greene a good sign
abstract: Shaft Drillers International, a West Virginia mine construction company, will be moving to Meadow Ridge Business Park in Greene County and bringing in 98 new jobs. SDI chose to move to Pennsylvania because the state offered them $2.1 million in construction and worker training funds to relocate, most under the Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program.

headline:
Caltagirone-led panel OKs bill to make teen sexting a misdemeanor
Proponents say current felony option is too severe for teenage offenders in state
abstract: PA Representative Thomas Caltagirone and the House Judiciary Committee approved a bill that would make "sexting," the use of taking nude pictures on a cell phone and transmitting them, a second-degree misdemeanor rather than a felony. The law is meant to give teenagers who "sext" less of a punishment with a higher likeliness of having the crime expunged from their record.

headline: Two more charged in Philadelphia driver's license scheme
abstract: Harold Palmer, 43 a PennDot a license examiner who accepted bribes from Philadelphia businessman  in return for issuing "hundreds" of driver's licenses to illegal immigrants and foreign residents Saman H. Salem, was charged by government prosecutors Thursday. Salem received about $4,000 from each client and in total received $1 million through the scheme.

headline: Analysis: Primaries yield no unifying theme
abstract: The 11 primaries for Senate and Governor across the US did not yield any uniform result as both insiders and outsiders won primaries. Democratic Senator Blanche Lincoln won the Arkansas Senate primary but party insiders like US Senator Arlen Specter lost primaries for US Senate.

headline: Casey to introduce bill to improve response to gas well accidents
abstract: After workers at a Clearfield County well explosion didn't call 911 for three hours after the incident to report it, regulators are letting companies know that they must do so right away in the future.  US Sen. Bob Casey is considering advancing legislation that would require new steps to be taken to respond to such accidents.  It would require drillers to keep certified rescue crews within 1 hour of the site and require them to contact emergency response teams within 15 minutes of an accident.

headline: In PA governor's race, candidates run from being seen as an 'insider'
abstract: Despite many years in politics and deep ties to his party's political establishment, each man is casting himself as the outsider candidate in the Nov. 2 election for Pennsylvania governor. Dan Onorato, 49, has been in elected office for 18 consecutive years, beginning as a Pittsburgh City Council member and Allegheny County controller before twice being elected as the Allegheny County executive, first in 2003. Corbett's political life goes back to the 1980s, when he was Western Pennsylvania coordinator for George H.W. Bush's 1988 presidential campaign.

headline: State Representative Smith owes benefits
abstract: For more than 70 years, the family of current PA State Representative Ken Smith (D-112) operated a successful restaurant in South Scranton. This week, two former employees of Ken Smith, alleged the legislator’s political aspirations began to spell the end for the storied eatery. The seven or eight employees who remained at Smith’s Restaurant until its end were denied unemployment as, his employees claim.

headline: DUI Court tackles problem as leaders seek solution for repeat offenders
abstract: Centre County court officials hope to expand the DUI Court program, which is designed to keep repeat offenders from re-entering the system. The District Attorney’s office is hoping to address the issue through educational prevention programs for 6th, 7th, and 8th graders, as well as high school students.

headline: Parents, relatives remain most likely abusers of children
abstract: According to an annual report released by the state Department of Public Welfare, about 81 percent of the substantiated 3,365 sexual assaults on children statewide in 2009 were committed by parents, family members, or someone living in the child’s home. Of the 1,647 physical abuses reported statewide, parents were the abuser 66 percent of the time, with 558 reports of abuse by the mother and 529 reports of abuse by the father.

headline: Court chooses in-house justice
abstract: The PA state Supreme Court ruled reached an administrative decision to extend medical benefits to same-sex domestic partners of court employees. The decision will apply to all 1,100 judges and 1,000 judicial staffers. The costs are unclear since the court is unsure how many employees will apply for benefits. Justice Seamus McCafferey said the issue was a civil rights issue.

headline: Man seeks answers about alleged mistreatment at Crawford jail
abstract: A representative from the Pennsylvania Prison Society confronted three commissioners from the Crawford County Prison Board about a report released by the warden of the Crawford County Correctional Facility about the medical treatment of four inmates. The representative said that the inmates were abused and had not received proper medical treatment.

headline: Recess coaches help kids play, and that helps them to learn
abstract: Joe Cokes who works as a "recess coach" for a youth-fitness advocacy group called Playworks, was at William Dick School in North Philadelphia teaching students the how to play nice during recess. Playworks teaches low-income students across the nation how to play games, and how to lead games and equip the students with leadership skills to solve conflicts on their own.

headline:
IUP chief decides to depart at end of June
Atwater takes job with professional college organization
abstract: President of Indiana University of Pennsylvania, Tony Atwater, has been resigned to join the Washington, D.C.-based American Association of State Colleges and Universities. Atwater received a vote of no confidence by the university's faculty in December 2009. The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education will pick an interim president.

headline: Planners oppose transfer of federal road funds by state
abstract: The Southwest Pennsylvania Commission which plans and distributes transportation funding for southwest PA has voted to block the state government from using its funds to pay for other state projects.  The last time this was done was in 2007.  It is not the type of thing that should be able to be used on a regular basis the commission held.

headline: DRPA clarifies ban on free tolls for workers
abstract: Delaware River Port Authority has closed a loophole that allowed employees to continue to get free bridge tolls even after a high-profile ban on the perk.

headline: 3 Pennsylvania agencies won't cut budgets, Gov. Rendell says
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature, the courts and the Office of Auditor General Jack Wagner are the only three state agencies that have not responded to requests by Governor Ed Rendell to cut their budgets by 1.9 percent.

headline: Nursing service reaches higher level with doctorate
abstract: About 120 schools nationwide offer a doctorate degree program endorsed by the American Association of Colleges of Nursing that looks at advancing the practice of nursing and developing the profession’s standing. A graduate of the program from Murrysville is profiled.

headline: Municipalities scramble to meet approaching tax collection changes
abstract: Unless Luzerne County municipalities and school districts begin sending representatives to tax collection meetings, they will lose out on more than $70 million in revenue.

headline: WJAC-TV News at Noon
abstract: Governor Rendell has proposed lowering the sales tax while expanding the list of items subject to the sales tax. Rendell has never passed a budget by the budget deadline. Gov. Rendell's budget proposal is $29 billion, a $1.1 billion increase from last year's budget.

headline: Annette John-Hall: More than black or white
abstract: The author states that the expansion of race categories available on the 2010 Census is a positive for multi-racial races as it gives them a chance to more accurately describe themselves to the federal government. She notes how few race choices were available for most of the previous Census takings.

headline: Camp Hill prison guard jailed after police say he gave pot, phones to inmates
abstract: Kevin Atkins a guard at the Correctional Institution at Camp Hill Cumberland County Prison was charged with drug and other offenses for allegedly supplying inmates with marijuana and cell phones. Atkins was suspended from his job after he turned himself in to authorities today and was placed in to Cumberland County Prison.

headline: Forget Arizona: Pa. bills on illegal construction workers are fair
abstract: Two bills introduced in the PA legislature will require construction companies to verify the legality and citizenship of their workers before they can bid on government contracts or else lose their licenses and certificates as private contractors. The author states that these are fair immigration laws.

headline: Megan's Law update to cost Pennsylvania $3 million
abstract: PA is facing losing $1 million in funds each year it isn't in compliance with Megan's Law.  A full update will cost the state at least $3 million.  Only three states are in complete compliance with the law, but the state is taking the task seriously and hopes to be in compliance soon.

headline: Murphy, Fitzpatrick squaring off in Bucks again
abstract: U.S. Rep. Patrick Murphy  Democrat from Bristol is running for a third term in a hazardous political environment against Republican Mike Fitzpatrick, an aggressive campaigner whom Murphy unseated in the 2006 congressional election by less than 1 percentage point. During his political hiatus, Fitzpatrick, 47, successfully battled colon cancer. Now, he wants his old job back, and GOP operatives in Washington think that he has a shot at reclaiming it.

headline: Committee reimburses state for moving Pennsylvania Worker statue
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said taxpayer money was never intended to pay to move The Pennsylvania Worker, sculpted by William F. Duffy, which sat on a landscaped circle inside the gate at the Second Street entrance to the residence.

headline: Shift seen on casino oversight
abstract: Rep. Curt Schroder, the likely chairman of the Gaming Oversight Committee, has called on the gaming board to postpone awarding Pennsylvania's resort casino license since terms expire next month for four members of the seven-member board. Schroder stated, "Waiting an additional month or two until new members are appointed and educated on each applicant will ensure confidence that the Board is making the best decision".

headline: Cost and corruption of Pennsylvania legislature brings call for reform
abstract: A legislative branch that ranks as the second most expensive in the nation and a scandal-plagued General Assembly has fed public cynicism about state government and prompted a host of candidates to campaign on changing the status quo, especially with primaries in the near future.

headline: NBC11 News: The Bay Area at 5AM
abstract: Governor Rendell has made plans for the late US Representative John Murtha. Gov. Rendell is trying to figure out how to hold a special election for Murtha's now empty seat.

headline: Consol makes $3.5B deal for gas exploration-production business
abstract: Consol Energy Inc. has purchased Dominion Resources Inc.'s Appalachian Basin natural gas exploration-production business for $3.5 billion, making the company the third largest owner in the Marcellus Shale region and the largest in the Appalachian Basin. The company plans on doubling its profits through natural gas production while also trying to buy back a former subsidiary company, CNX.

headline: House Republicans suggest Pennsylvania could save money by cutting fleet of state cars
abstract: Despite Gov. Ed Rendell's budget getting passed by the Pennsylvania House, Republicans offered ideas to balance next year’s Pennsylvania budget Wednesday at a news conference without increasing taxes. The plan offers three ways to help balance the budget which would include using rental cars on long distance trips by state employees, paying for goods and services electronically, and eliminate Medicaid eligibility errors.

headline: Competing forces lobby legislators on state budget
abstract: Those who want their taxes lowered and those who want more money for state services are once again clashing in Harrisburg over the state budget. Republicans would like to cap spending at $27.5 billion, less than last year's budget of $27.8 billion while Democrats would like to tax smokeless tobacco and Marcellus Shale gas drilling to provide for social services. PA Governor Rendell has proposed a budget of $29.1 billion.

headline: $5M PennVEST loan for Winfield sewage project denied
abstract: A sewage project for Winfield Township has been derailed as a result of a denied PennVEST loan.  It would have covered $5 million of the project.  It was denied funding because the project was not considered a high priority by "need and volume."  Although the sewage project was mandated by the Department of Environmental Protection, and PennVEST receives its money from the DEP, it is ironic that the project would not qualify for funding.

headline: Drought? This is a record wet period
abstract: On average, officially Philadelphia receives about 41 inches or rain annually this years total is at 30-plus inches and counting. In the 137 years of record-keeping, only 25 times has the city failed to get less than at least 85 percent of that total, or 35 inches.

headline: Sestak calls on Obama to assess war on al-Qaida
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Sestak said Monday that President Barack Obama needs to release a clear assessment on what kind of progress is being made, if any, against al-Qaida.

headline: 'White' finding to stand for nuke plant
abstract: A 'white' finding, signifying low-to-moderate safety concerns, issued to the Susquehanna nuclear power plant will stand, according to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

headline: Flags to lower to half-staff to honor civil rights leader
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell has ordered flags on Pennsylvania state facilities to half-staff in honor of late civil rights leader Dorothy Height. Height led the National Council of Negro Women for 40 years and has received two of the nation’s highest honors.

headline: KDKA Morning News on The CW - 7AM
abstract: Due to snowstorms Governor Rendell has ordered 6 highways closed, leaving only one highway artery out of Philadelphia open.

headline: Councilman on the hunt for junked, abandoned cars in city
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Bruce Kraus patrolled the street of his district with a list of 47 abandoned cars that have received complaints. Kraus also noted trash and graffiti in his district which he said would be ordered to be cleaned up.

headline: Courts with merit: Statewide reform also means appointing judges
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell has long backed the idea of the merit selection of judges, and in his final year in office Rendell is supporting bills in the Pennsylvania Legislature to reform the way judges are selected in the state. If passed Pennsylvania would no longer be one of only six states that elects all of its judges.

headline: Pittsburgh named 7th best place to raise a family
abstract: Forbes.com has ranked Pittsburgh the 7th ranked best place to raise a family. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl said he would like to strive for a higher ranking next year. The area was selected for their educational opportunities and affordability.

headline: Pennsylvania finalist for education grant
abstract: PA will find out in September whether it will receive a cut of the $3.4 billion allocated for education reform.  The "Race to the Top" program has advanced to the second round and PA and 17 other states and DC have made the cut.  Regardless of whether the state makes the cut, Education secretary Arne Duncan says that many states are headed in the right direction with new laws governing teacher evaluations.

headline: Police: Bad blood preceded Kraft plant killings
abstract: A 43-year-old woman was charged with murder today in the deaths of two coworkers during a shooting rampage that erupted Thursday night at Kraft Foods baking plant in Northeast Philadelphia shortly after she had been suspended from her job and sent home. Yvonne Hiller has been charged with killing LaTonya Brown, 36, and Tanya Wilson, 47, both of Philadelphia. Coworker Bryant Dalton, 39, was hit in the neck, and remains in critical condition at Jefferson University Hospital.

headline: Pat Toomey's Wall Street career given another twirl, this time by Mother Jones
abstract: Pat Toomey's Wall Street past is elaborated upon in a brand-new piece in Mother Jones by Nick Baumann. Toomey's Senate campaign office was asked to respond, but didn't, according to the author.

headline: No tax increase for city residents
abstract: City council approved final readings of an estimated $7.5 million general fund budget that projects no tax or fee increases for residents of Hazleton.

headline: Pension board boosts state's contribution rate
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Employees' Retirement System has approved a 5.64 percent increase in the composite employer contribution rate for the 2010-11 fiscal year. A change in the increase may occur if the legislature adopts Governor Rendell’s plan to cap the rate at 5 percent.

headline: Ch. 7 News at 4
abstract: Snowstorms in Clearfield County caused a 50 car pileup forcing Governor Rendell to shut down parts of I-71 and I-78.

headline: Government policies can support green initiatives
abstract: The author states that government on the federal, state and local level can support green initiatives through policy decisions. The author cited tax credits put forward by the federal American Recovery and Reinvestment Act and sustainability of downtown centers such as inner-city Pittsburgh. The author stated that private investment spurs industry but that the public sector can contribute with green-driven policy initiatives.

headline: Rothfus in the 4th: His run for Congress would be solely on the issues
abstract: Pennsylvania's 4th Congressional District which includes northern Allegheny County, all of Beaver and Lawrence counties and parts of Butler, Mercer and Westmoreland counties is currently held by two-term Democrat Jason Altmire. Altmire will be running unopposed in the primary but either Republican Mary Beth Buchanan or Keith Rothfus will be sure to offer a strong conservative alternative to Altmire.

headline:
Students must be ready to learn
Which means schools must address more of the problems they encounter at home
abstract: The author states that Pittsburgh Public Schools must do more to try to foster an encouraging educational environment in students' private lives in order to achieve more success in schools. The author also states that early-childhood education and intervention are key factors in achieving this.

headline: PennDOT to beef up reporting on bus drivers
abstract: The state Department of Transportation is expected to start reporting on whether a given driver has been involved in an accident that involved the loss of life or major property damage.  The information is expected to help employers keep dangerous drivers off the roads.  Currently, records only show whether a motorist was involved in a crash with any suspensions or citations.  The catalyst for the legislation was an incident with a Collegeville area bus driver who got into a fatal accident driving a school bus when he already had a fatal accident on his record dating back to 1999.

headline: Federal appeals court strikes down Hazleton's immigration ordinances
abstract: In a high-profile Pennsylvania case that helped spark the ongoing national debate over immigration policy, a federal appeals court ruled Thursday that the City of Hazleton has no right to punish businesses or landlords who hire or rent to illegal immigrants. The ruling, by a three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit in Philadelphia, upheld a 2007 lower-court decision prohibiting Hazleton from enforcing local immigration ordinances.

headline: WTAJ (CBS)Johnstown, PA DMA: 101
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has admitted defeat in his push to enact a severance tax on the marcellus shale natural gas drilling industry in Pennsylvania. Rendell says that the proposal won't pass this year, because the lawmakers refused to compromise on negotiations and turned their backs on the idea.

headline: Arlen Specter will have floor for last time on bill for Holocaust survivors
abstract: Author comments on outgoing Senator Arlen Specter and his introduction of Senate bill S.4033, which seeks to restore the right of Holocaust survivors and their descendants to proceed with lawsuits in U.S. courts to recover unpaid proceeds under Holocaust-era insurance policies.

headline: Tax amnesty staff bolstered due to heavy response
abstract: State officials are working to address the jammed phone lines due to the number of people seeking to take advantage of a new tax amnesty program. The initiative allows tax dodgers to pay off tax debts accrued through June 2009 with no penalty and half the normal interest.

headline: Raw deal: Insurance shouldn't be forced on sewer customers
abstract: A new $5 monthly service fee is being charged for water and sewer protection in Pittsburgh. The politically connected Utility Line Security of Forest Hills was contracted to do the repairs through Pittsburgh's Water and Sewer Authority but only after a non-transparent process that included an opt-out provision rather than a opt-in provision.

headline: State senator introduces marriage amendment
abstract: PA Senator John Eichelberger has introduced a bill that would amend the Pennsylvania constitution to define marriage as a union between a man and a woman.  The state already has a law defining marriage as a union between a man and a woman but Eichelberger wants that provision amended into the state constitution.

headline: A garden grows in Harrisburg
abstract: Today a bipartisan group of Pennsylvania lawmakers got down and dirty outside the state Capitol building breaking ground on the new Hunger Garden. Rep. John Myers D-Philadelphia., co-chairman of the legislative Hunger Caucus believes this show of support for community gardens will help bring awareness to the issue of the lack of healthy food options in urban areas.

headline: Retailers, restaurateurs gambling that they can lure customers without coupons
abstract: Pittsburgh retailers and restaurants relied on coupons and discounts during the recession to keep people coming into their businesses. Sensing an economic recovery, some of those businesses are now taking away their discounts and trying to lure customers in without them.

headline: Onorato, Corbett both back health insurance extension
abstract: 46,000 are expected to lose their health insurance unless the state can come up with funding to keep the Adult Basic program alive.  The program gets most of its money from a 5 year funding arrangement with local insurance providers.  The candidates for governor both support extending the program, but have differing approaches.

headline: Editorial: Castle's challenger
abstract: In Delaware, the race for the US Senate seat long held by Vice President Biden is up for grabs. The GOP-endorsed moderate contender is Mike Castle, the longtime congressman and former governor. Polls show him with a comfortable lead against Democrat Chris Coons in a general-election matchup.

newspaper: WPCW Pittsburgh (KDKA on The CW) CW
headline: KDKA Morning News on The CW - 7AM
abstract: Pennsylvania's unemployment rate fell for a second straight month as employers added more than 7000 jobs to their payroll. The state Department of Labor and Industry says unemployment crept downward by two tenths of a percentage points last month to 9%.

headline: Hilton Harrisburg celebrates 20th anniversary as general manager Joe Massaro says business is looking up
abstract: Q&A with Joe Massaro , the general manager of the Harrisburg Hilton.

headline: House panel approves bill on sex education in schools
abstract: A bill requiring Pennsylvania’s public schools to provide sex education to students narrowly passed the House Education Committee with an14-11 vote. Under the bill, parents would have the opportunity to withhold their children from the classes. The bill is on its way to the state House of Representatives for a vote.

headline: More state forestland up for gas leases
abstract: Governor Rendell has written into his state budget proposal a provision that would free up state-owned forest land for Marcellus Shale gas drilling leases. The plan is said to generate $180 million in its first year and $1.8 billion over five years. Conservationists in the legislature say the plan is an affront to the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources who work to maintain the lands.

headline: UPMC for You moves ahead with plans for co-payments for Medicaid patients
abstract: Medicaid enrollees in the UPMC for You health plan will start to pay a $1 to $3 co-payment for hospital and doctor visits, along with x-rays and other medical tests. Families USA and other opponents said that the co-pay may be too expensive for some low-income families. UPMC for You said it was necessary to institute a co-pay due to budget shortages.

headline: Success rate seen as low but significant
abstract: Officials said Berks County Treatment Court is working well despite the success rate of the program being at 33 percent. The program is designed to treat offenders who commit crimes as a result of a substance addiction, with the goal that that person will not commit a crime if they can solve their addiction. Susan K. Halbeisen, treatment court probation officer believes the program is working if even just one person is a success.

headline: As food prices rise, people cut back
abstract: Food prices all over the world are rising and aiding in the proliferation of hunger. Some countries blame dry weather and the price of oil while others blame government policies of manipulating currencies and creating inflationary economies.

headline: One dead after being trapped in shaft at Sewickley wastewater plant
abstract: John "Jack" Hogan III, 31, of Baden died after falling down a 30-foot shaft after being overcome by noxious fumes at the Sewickley Wastewater Treatment Plant.  A number of other workers went to rescue Hogan but were overcome by fumes as well.  They did not go in with breathing apparatuses.

headline: False goals for city schools
abstract: In 2010, more than 50 percent of the children in the Philadelphia School District met state standards in both reading and math. This is the eighth straight year in which the district has made gains in these subjects. Critics of city schools point out that there's still a long way to go before all children are reading and doing math at grade level.

headline: Action News 24 at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell believes Democrats are running from the things that they have done. Rendell himself is not running for re-election since he has already served two terms as Governor.

headline: Republican-leaning states will gain Congressional seats because of census results
abstract: Republican-leaning states will acquire a half dozen House seats due to findings from the Census Bureau that show the nation’s population growing more slowly than in past decades. Following each census, the nation must reapportion the House 435 districts to make them roughly equal in population. Pennsylvania will lose a House seat as a result of the reapportionment.

headline: State cops hold up delivery of newspapers
abstract: Philadelphia Daily News and Inquirer delivery drivers were forbidden to drive on the Schuylkill Expressway because of a state police code which denies non-essential drivers to drive on roads that governor has closed to the public. Delivery drivers carried a Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency directive that allows them to drive on the roads. The PA state police said the police code trumps the directive and the drivers cannot drive on the roads.

headline: Region's jobless rate rises to 8.1%
abstract: The Pittsburgh region's jobless rate rose by two-tenths of a percentage point in the first month of 2010. It is the highest unemployment rate for the region since 1986.

headline: Faisal Shahzad bought fireworks in Pa.
abstract: Video of alleged terror suspect Faisal Shahzad's March 8 visit to a northeast Pennsylvania fireworks store was turned over to federal authorities on Tuesday. The video reportedly shows Shahzad purchasing at least some of the 152 M-88 firecrackers recovered from his explosives-rigged SUV last weekend in New York's Times Square.

headline: Arkansas Senate runoff tops a busy election day
abstract: Numerous primaries for US Senate and Governor show California, Nevada, and Arkansas among those states in which major changes may happen. eBay executive Meg Whitman faces off for the Republican nomination for Governor while and a former Hewlett Packard CEO is up for the nomination to unseat US Senator Barbara Boxer. US Senator Blanche Lincoln of Arkansas is up against a heavy influx of labor money being used against her.

headline: Pittsburgh sewer backup problem disputed
abstract: Homeowners are getting fed up with backups caused by Pittsburgh Water and Sewer Authority's sewer lines.  Betsey and Keith Mary have had the floor of their newly renovated basement covered in untreated sewage because of backups plaguing their area.  PWSA claims that it isn't the authority's fault.

headline: O'Donnell gets boost from Palin
abstract: Sarah Palin on Thursday endorsed Christine O'Donnell's Senate bid in Delaware, hoping to give another tea party-backed candidate a final push to beat an establishment favorite. The endorsement could provide a major boost for O'Donnell, locked in a bitter primary against Representative Mike Castle but short on campaign cash.

headline: Morning Joe
abstract: Americans who have lost their jobs or had their hours cut, who are worried about sending their kids to college are scared, says PA Governor Ed Rendell. From a communications perspective, the important thing for the White House to do is to say to those people we get it, we understand what you're going through, and we're trying to address these issues.

headline: South Fayette adopts 2011 budget with no tax increase
abstract: South Fayette commissioners adopted an $11.9 million budget for 2011 that holds the property taxes at their current rate of 3.84 mills.

headline: No more Florida 'gun birds'
abstract: The police and the Philadelphia District Attorney's office are troubled by people who have been denied a concealed weapon carrying license in Pennsylvania who go to Florida to more easily obtain the license. The license is honored in PA because of a reciprocal arrangement among states to honor each other's gun laws. The author said the law should be changed and PA Attorney General Tom Corbett should revisit the reciprocal arrangement.

headline: Area unemployment hits double digits
abstract: For the first time in 17 years Somerset County's unemployment rate has reached 10%. The job losses are credited to the loss of manufacturing jobs and the closing of Gilmour Manufacturing in Somerset. The PA Department of Labor and Industry said all other industries besides manufacturing are holding their own in Somerset.

headline: Democrats launch attack ads as primary election nears
abstract: The top three Democratic candidates looking to succeed Pennsylvania Gov. Ed Rendell have launched attack ads two weeks before the primary. Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato is maintaining a 20 point lead over State Sen. Anthony Williams, D- Philadelphia, Montgomery County Commissioner Joe Hoeffel, and Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner.

headline: Nutter revamping program for hiring ex-offenders
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's program that gives companies that hire ex-offenders a tax credit has not hired one person and hasn't given out any tax  credits. The administration is now struggling to keep the program alive. Nutter is trying to make it more accessible to companies by not requiring them to provide tuition assistance, paying150% of minimum wage, and requiring inmates to give 5% of their paycheck back to the city.

headline: Not washing reusable shopping bags could lead to food poisioning
abstract: A new study by professors at the University of Arizona and Loma Linda University, in California shows that reusable shopping bags can carry harmful bacteria and cause food poisoning if unwashed.  Customers are encouraged to wash their reusable bags.

headline: Indiana County jobless rate unchanged in July
abstract: Indiana County's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 8.8 percent in July, according to the PA Department of Labor and Industry. July unemployment rates for all Pennsylvania counties ranged from 6.7 percent in Centre County to 14.0 percent in Cameron County.

headline: ABC27 News Daybreak at 6:00A
abstract: Hundreds of people gathered in Carlisle to see the unveiling of the 5,178 solar panels spread over 6.2 acres of Carlisle area school district land. The solar panels will generate 1-megawatt of energy, enough to power one-third of the district's energy needs. PA Governor Ed Rendell says the district will save $170,000 a year in energy costs, and receive $450,000/year in tax credits.

headline: Judge voids turnpike worker's claim he was fired for being a whistleblower
abstract: Donald Moyer, a fired Pennsylvania Turnpike toll collector, has lost a federal court fight to regain his job. A judge ruled that Moyer was unable to procure evidence to support his claims and found the Turnpike Commission didn’t violate Moyer’s rights regarding the firing.

headline: When residents pull together, street gets cleared
abstract: Members of one narrow street in Philadelphia have teamed up to clear their street of snow, moving it to the sidewalks. Lynn Landes, a member of the group has reached out to Philadelphia Streets Commissioner Clarena Tolson and members of city council to ensure that they would not be ticketed for not shoveling their sidewalks. Landes said shoveling the road was a safety measure.

headline: Time for clean slate: Harrisburg Authority primed for new leadership
abstract: The author hopes that with Harrisburg City Council's task to appoint three members to the Harrisburg Authority it will mean more transparency with the authority which is tasked with handling the $68 million in debt the city is in due to the city's trash incinerator.

headline: Hollywood Casino plans are under review in East Hanover Twp., Dauphin County
abstract: Penn National’s land development plans for the 44,000-square-foot addition at Hollywood Casino for table games and more slots were accepted for review by the East Hanover Twp., Dauphin County supervisors Tuesday night.

headline: John Baer: 'Ed World' is governed by cronyism, selective memory, blame-shifting
abstract: The author states that PA Governor Rendell has not been honest about saying he didn't know about his press aide Kevin Feeley's "legacy project" that used $30,000 of state money to pay for an emblem of Governor Rendell's time in office. He also criticizes the governors role in attempting to take US Rep. Joe Sestak off the ballot for US Senate.

headline: Pennsylvania universities chancellor gets contract extension, no raise
abstract: Chancellor John Cavanaugh had his contract renewed by a year with no salary increase.  He should be applauded for how he has run the state's university system during his tenure.  His salary will remain at $327,500 for the year.  Budgetary concerns were cited as to the lack of a pay raise.

headline: For sewer rate hike, opposition continues
abstract: Residents continued to protest Pennsylvania American Water Co.'s request to triple the average customer's sewer bill Tuesday at the last scheduled public input hearings on the matter. Pennsylvania American Water Co. has requested it be allowed to increase revenues by about $8.2 million after completing a new wastewater facility in South Coatesville at a cost of about $55 million

headline: Missing state artifacts already are showing up
abstract: During a news conference Thursday, PA Auditor General Jack Wagner said at least 1,800 historic artifacts were missing from state collections, but five hours later officials from the State Museum Commission said they had already located almost 300 of them and expected to find more. Mary Jane Miller, head of collections management, said auditors were working from lists she created between 1998 and 2008 to keep track of inventory that wasn't in its proper place.

headline: Activists remember the 101 homeless in Philly who died in 2010
abstract: People gathered at John F. Kennedy Plaza to observe Homeless Memorial Day and bring attention to the 101 people in Philadelphia who died while homeless in 2010.

headline: Editorial: Scrap this site
abstract: A scrap yard in south Philadelphia is set to move to Eddystone in Delaware County. The author said the city will lose 25 jobs as a result but the state will gain 200 in Delaware County . The author said the south Philadelphia site can then be used for something more pleasing to the eye for visitors.

headline:
Sermon on the (head) count
Nutter takes to five pulpits, shepherding flocks to help the city by filling out federal forms by April 1.
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter visited churches to encourage members of the congregations to fill out the census form. Mayor Nutter urged religious leaders from all religions and races to encourage those who fear the census to fill it out.

headline: No matter the tax, Philadelphia residents will pay the piper
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Nutter and City Council leaders have been discussing various compromises as the May 31 budget deadline is approaching. Proposals include a property-tax increase of just under 10 percent, a soda tax of a 1/2-cent per ounce and further cuts of at least $20 million. City Council prefers a property-tax hike and more cuts.

headline: City looking for citizens' helping hands
abstract: The City of Philadelphia has hired a new chief service officer with a $200,000 grant from the Rockefeller foundation. The service officer will help organize volunteer services across the city. The service officer, Catie Wolfgang, is not meant to take away service work, she said, but to supplement city workers.

headline: Cool it: 'Climategate' was unfounded, although climate scientists learned a valuable lesson
abstract: Climategate was a manufacture red hoax by right-wing activists deadset on discrediting the scientific consensus behind climate change and global warming.  No evidence was found to back up the claim that scientists had faked data to prove the existence of man-made climate change.

headline: State cites South Side fundraising firm
abstract: PA Bureau of Charitable Organizations authorities are alleging that Outreach Associates Inc., a Pittsburgh South Side fundraising company, broke the law dozens of times in recent years by hiring convicted criminals to solicit money for charities and by failing to file timely and complete financial reports. The Solicitation of Funds for Charitable Purposes Act forbids anyone convicted of any felony or a misdemeanor involving dishonesty from working as a professional solicitor.

headline: Corbett, Onorato keep debate civil
abstract: The candidates for Pennsylvania governor disagreed in a debate, televised live statewide Saturday night, about how the state should address funding for public education, pensions for state workers, and health-care reform. Amid a frenzied national election season when foes in some states have accused each other of lacking patriotism or even being fools, Republican Tom Corbett and Democrat Dan Onorato played nice. The debate was the first of two televised encounters between the candidates in three days.

headline: LCB has to put wine kiosks on hold
abstract: Technical problems have forced the Liquor Control Board to temporarily close wine kiosks in 30 supermarkets across the state.  According to LCB officials, the board will reopen all the kiosk machines once they have been fixed and tested by the developer.

headline: Pew poll: Nutter gets job OK from 53 percent in city - but only 43 percent of blacks give approval
abstract: A Pew poll has shown that Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's job approval rating is up to 53%. African Americans only support him 43% which Nutter said is due to the economic downturn's effect on that segment of the population. Hispanics supported him 55%. Residents also showed a 51% approval of casino's in the city.

headline: Incoming Drexel president has ambitious plans
abstract: Incoming President of Drexel University John A. Fry is profiled. Fry was a former executive at the University of Pennsylvania, and former president of Franklin and Marshall college. Fry wants to create closer ties with Penn, expand Drexel's network, keep tuition costs down, and get more students to live on campus.

headline: Obama nears decision on justice
abstract: President Obama interviewed federal judge Diane Wood of Chicago yesterday for the vacancy on the U.S. Supreme Court. Wood is the last of four candidates known to have had a face-to-face interview with Obama the others include Solicitor General Elena Kagan and federal appeals court judges Merrick Garland, who serves in the District of Columbia, and Sidney Thomas, who is based in Montana.

headline: EPA tightens sulfur dioxide emission rules
abstract: The US Environmental Protection Agency has lowered the amount of sulfur dioxide emissions that power plants and industry must regulate themselves by. The amount of SO2 allowed in the air is now 75 parts per billion over a one hour period, the current standard is 140. SO2 leads to asthma attacks and respiratory problems.

headline: Study in multiple counties will promote regional planning for transit services
abstract: CAT, Lebanon Transit, Rabbittransit in York and transit agencies in Berks, Adams and Lancaster are participating in a coordination study that seeks to build a more integrated regional transit system.  Businesses, riders and those in the community will be invited to be interviewed for input in the planning.

headline: School's back; Should it have been gone?
abstract: Summer vacation is an education tradition in this country, that's not the case in much of the rest of the world, and much of the rest of the world is ahead of the United States on the learning curve.

headline: Pot rules put many on edge
abstract: The New Jersey Department of Health and Senior Services' release this month of draft rules dictating who will have access to medical marijuana and how it is distributed might have been a moment to celebrate. The law that New Jersey legislators passed in January already was the most conservative among the 14 states that have approved distribution of medical marijuana. The proposed rules would make the program even stricter, dropping the number of state-approved distribution centers from a potential six statewide to four and limiting the drug's potency.

headline: Duck plan doesn't fly
abstract: Author suggests city officials take consideration of the public opposition to boat tours on the Schuylkill.  The city is currently accepting proposals for the tours.

headline: State public interest group urges support for high-speed trains
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Interest Research Group released has urged the federal government to start development on a high-speed rail network that would connect every major US city. PennPIRG praised President Barack Obama's $8 billion stimulus investment in high-speed rail development but said that it was not enough. Pennsylvania's share was used to better connect Philadelphia and Harrisburg, which drew criticism from US Senators Bob Casey and Arlen Specter.

headline: Project to get transplant organs from ER patients raises ethics questions
abstract: A federal project led by the Health Resources and Services Administration will conduct a pilot program to obtain organs from Emergency Room patients whose heart has stopped but brain continues to function. It is an effort to obtain more organs for organ transplants but opponents say it may sway doctors to let a patient die in order to gain an organ transplant. Current practice states that patients' organs can only be harvested after the brain has stopped.

headline: Rendell warns lawmakers to act on transportation
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell said in a speech to state lawmakers Tuesday that outlined different ways to fill in the gap in the states transportation budget, which Rendell says would be enough to repair and maintain the states transportation infrastructure.

headline:
Same-day surgery hygiene called lax
A U.S. study of centers found "surprising" problems in basic infection control.
abstract: According to an expert study, same-day surgery centers have continually breached sanitary standards, leading to infection of patients at outpatient centers. US Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius said that she would expand its hospital infection action plan to include ambulances.

headline: Fayette looks to become leader in energy efficiency
abstract: Barry Seneri, economic development manager with Fay-Penn Economic Development Council Inc., said that it is important that businesses in Fayette County look to make their businesses more eco-friendly.  Industry representatives were hosted at a summit regarding renewable energy at Penn State's Fayette campus.

headline: Slots won't change feelings on Gettysburg
abstract: There is a debate in Gettysburg over the proposed building of a casino, this time about a mile from the southern end of the 6,000-acre Gettysburg National Military Park. Supporters say casinos would not disrespect the sacrifice made by the 51,000 soldiers who were killed, wounded, captured or missing in the three-day Battle of Gettysburg in 1863, any more than all of the other commercial enterprises that sit right in the middle of hallowed ground.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Pension crisis looms
abstract: With a growing chunk of the city budget going to fund pensions, there will be fewer tax dollars to put police on the street, keep firehouses open, pick up trash, and provide other key services. Pension reform can't be put off any longer, Mayor Nutter, City Council members, and the city's municipal unions have to meet the challenge or risk the city's continued fiscal decline. The city's pension contribution from its general fund more than doubled in the last five years, and will rise again by nearly 50 percent in several more years.

headline: Teacher shakedown
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association, the state's largest teachers union, plans to raise annual dues for its 191,000 members by about 11 percent.

headline: Doherty being asked to run for Mellow seat, aide says
abstract: Scranton Mayor Chris Doherty has been urged by fellow Democrats to run for former PA State Senator Bob Mellow's seat. Scranton lies within Mellow's seat and Doherty's gubernatorial bid has lagged.

headline:
NJ Transit to cut 200 jobs, raise fares 25%
As gov. says, 'Money doesn't grow on trees'
abstract: New Jersey Transit's new executive director, Jim Weinstein, has made cost cutting measures to make up for New Jersey Transit's debt due to low-ridership and dwindling state aid. Weinstein will cut staff, rail and bus services, institute fare increases, and cut pension benefits and salaries.

headline: Pay raises = tax hikes
abstract: York County tax-payers are going to be seeing tax rate increases ranging from 2.47 percent in Southern to 4.23 percent in South Western districts. This tax increase is the result of the rise in costs of local school districts which is attributed to factors like increase pension costs.

headline: PhillyInc: Philadelphia lags as a "smart city"
abstract: A forum at the National Constitution Center hosted by IBM talked about "smarter cities" and named Philadelphia as a "skilled anchor," meaning they slow-growing, less diverse, but have a high educational attainment. The author notes how Philadelphia has an educated, young workforce but with little jobs to offer them.

headline: Group re-enacts Vietnam War in Military Museum woods
abstract: 10 re-enactors staged a battle of the Vietnam War in the Spring Creek foliage next to the Pennsylvania Military Museum for spectators on Saturday.  The annual event entitled "Vietnam Revisited" began in 2007 as a tribute to those who fought in Vietnam.

headline: Oil platform explodes off La. coast; crew rescued
abstract: An oil platform exploded and burned off the Louisiana coast Thursday, the second such disaster in the Gulf of Mexico in less than five months. This time, the Coast Guard said there was no leak, and no one was killed. The Coast Guard initially reported that an oil sheen a mile long and 100 feet wide had begun to spread from the site of the blast, about 200 miles west of the source of BP's massive spill.

headline: Pa.'s frustrating tax-refund process for Ponzi investors
abstract: Mark Feldman, a retired Havertown dentist who moved to Massachusetts last year, lost a $1.3 million investment in Bernard L. Madoff's Ponzi scheme.
