Feldman contends that he was put through an ordeal by Pennsylvania Department of Revenue officials over his request for a refund of taxes paid on Madoff income he never received. The state Department of Revenue did not respond directly to Feldman's accusations, because the department cannot discuss any individual taxpayer.

headline: Action News at 6:00
abstract: According to the labor department, unemployment rose in 21 states. Pennsylvania’s state rate declined two-tenths from 8.8 to 8.6% compared to the nationwide rate which rose to 9.8%.

headline: Rendell's $29 billion budget lifts 74 sales tax exemptions
abstract: Governor Rendell's budget for fiscal year 2010-11 would apply the sales tax to 74 previously exempt items and services while lowering the sales tax rate at 4%. Rendell's budget is $26.27 billion in state funds and $2.76 billion in stimulus funds. Through multiple revenue options Rendell plans to create a Stimulus Transition Reserve Fund that would create a fund to be tapped when stimulus funds run out.

headline: Blackjack 101: Students at NCC-Monroe learn fine art of table games
abstract: Students at Northampton Community College enrolled in a six-week blackjack dealing course to get ready for table games available at Mount Airy Casino Resort. NCC-Monroe is the first community college to do so.

headline: Ready to retire? There are a lot of unknowns
abstract: Earlier this year former Blue Cross claims administrator Dennis Phipps learned that his health insurance plan which was part of his retirement package, which had originally been a $66 monthly premium is now $368 a month. Phipps left the company in February 2008, as a part of an early trickle in what turned into a flood of hundreds of layoffs from the region's largest insurer.

headline:
Lincoln bucks tide in Arkansas
The incumbent survived a runoff. South Carolina, California, and Nevada also saw big primaries.
abstract: Many US Senate and gubernatorial elections showed that money from tea partiers, and an anti-establishment wave caused for difficult primaries for established politicians including US Senator Blanche Lincoln of Arkansas. Two women from California won Republican primaries also.

headline: Officials accused of crimes should not continue duties
abstract: The ongoing Orie case should spur lawmakers to change how we deal with those who have violated the public trust while serving in public office.  Janine Orie remains on paid suspension as her sister's aid while the trial continues.  Under no circumstances should that continue.  Those accused of violating the public trust should not be permitted to continue his or her job while charges are pending.

headline: Action needed
abstract: PA House and Senate members questioned the state transportation secretary about a proposal to raise $1 billion annually in new funding. Transportation Secretary Allen Biehler said the state could raise that sum by taxing oil company profits and increasing motorist fees. Governor Ed Rendell said the public supports upgrading the transportation network and cautioned lawmakers that inaction would only delay the inevitable and add to its cost.

headline: Corbett avoids final-round KO vs. Onorato
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato entered the final debate of the race for governor last night looking for a knockout punch to drop state Attorney General Tom Corbett. On the regulation of guns, Onorato repeated his complaints that Corbett as attorney general did not end the "Florida loophole" practice of allowing state residents to apply and receive permits to carry concealed weapons from the Sunshine State. Corbett said Florida's procedures are just as strict as those in Pennsylvania, adding that he does not see the need for any new state laws regulating guns.

headline: Chief Oil & Gas will see some Marcellus Shale properties
abstract: Chief Oil & Gas LLC and Radler 2000 Limited Partnership have agreed to sell certain natural gas properties in the Marcellus Shale, including acreage in Columbia County, to EXCO Holding PA for $459 million. Assets being sold include 15 producing wells, 11 wells waiting to be completed and approximately 50,000 net acres located primarily in Lycoming, Sullivan and Columbia counties.

headline:
Pause the Pa. gas rush
The state must deal with environmental questions before it allows more drilling.
abstract: An opinion piece written by PA State Representative Greg Vitali. He states that Governor Rendell's decision to lease state forestland in his proposed budget is premature because there are no studies as to the environmental impact of the drilling. Vitali has proposed a 5-year moratorium on leasing state lands for drilling until studies as to environmental effects are completed by the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: Program could save money transporting inmates in Blair County
abstract: The Blair County Prison Board is investigating a state-run program that would call on the PA Department of Correction to transport to State Correctional Institution Cresson any inmate who must be returned to Blair County from his home institution. The state would charge the county 16 cents per mile, which is said to be much less than the wear and tear on the county's vehicle and the wages of the two officers that must accompany.

headline: U.S. interest in Haiti isn't selfless
abstract: U.S. First Lady Michelle Obama's trip to Haiti last month added to the list of prominent Americans to have visited the earthquake torn country. The list also includes U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and former Presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush. Some say the U.S. interest is due to their interest in maintaining a stable government in Haiti.

headline: No overhaul this year for West Phila. High
abstract: West Philadelphia High School's scheduled turnaround will be delayed another year after the Philadelphia School Reform Commission and Philadelphia Schools Superintendent claimed that members of the school advisory council had worked for one of the organizations up for the bid to takeover the school. The superintendent said it was a conflict of interest and the council must be reconstituted.

headline: A pike perk? Workers get toll-free rides
abstract: Joe Brimmeier, Pennsylvania Turnpike CEO expects that 90% of his employees' usage of PennDOT EZ Passes is for business purposes only.  The Turnpike is under the microscope for its employee perks after other authorities were caught allowing employees to use its EZ Passes for personal use.  Brimmeier says that they will look into employees using business EZ Passes for personal use.

headline: Cumberland County woman dies after being burned in fire started by magnifying glass
abstract: A mentally disabled woman who set herself on fire with a magnifying glass has died at a Pennsylvania hospital. The Lehigh County coroner’s office says the 34-year-old woman died from her injuries today at a hospital in Allentown.

headline: In Pennsylvania's Eighth District, Murphy not overconfident about Fitzpatrick
abstract: U.S. Representative Patrick Murphy guarantees it when the polls close November 2, the two-term Democratic congressman from Bucks County plans to head to his house in Bristol Township. In 2007, Murphy had been quick to come out in support of Sen. Barack Obama's presidential bid. His alliance with party leaders has aided his ascent from obscure Iraq war veteran to Democratic National Convention speaker and party spokesman on certain legislative issues.

headline: News 8 at Noon
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is holding an indoor beach party in Philadelphia to thank his supporters. Rendell’s campaign is funding the event, which is expected to have several thousand people in attendance.

headline: Municipalities may need federal help after snow
abstract: Municipalities in Pennsylvania and New Jersey may need federal financial assistance to deal with large amount of money spent on snow removal in this winter's heavy storms. Municipalities are coming up with costs in order to submit them to federal approval for assistance. President Barack Obama declared parts of Pennsylvania a disaster area meaning that those parts are subject to federal relief funds.

headline: Charter Day big draw for museums
abstract: Charter Day, the day that celebrates King Charles II of England's granting of the land that would be Pennsylvania to William Penn, was celebrated with free admittance to state-owned museums in the Lancaster area. The museums included Ephrata Cloister, Landis Valley and the railroad museum.

headline: Rep. Patrick Murphy wins plum Appropriations slot
abstract: U.S. Rep. Patrick Murphy Democrat-Pennsylvania won assignment to the powerful House Appropriations Committee in a vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, replacing the late John P. Murtha also from Pennsylvania. Murphy said he will use the post to bring high-paying jobs to the Philadelphia area, and target wasteful spending.

headline: RoboCup teams worldwide strive to bend it like C3PO
abstract: Two teams from Pennsylvania universities will compete in the "RoboCup" in Singapore. The RoboCup is a competition between teams across the world who make robots to play 3 vs. 3 games of soccer. The University of Pennsylvania and Carnegie Melon University are the two teams that will compete.

headline: Wastewater tracking bill introduced
abstract: State Rep. Phyllis Mundy, D-Kingston is introducing a bill that will provide for the tracking of polluted waters that come from the process of drilling for natural gas.  The bill would seek to improve public confidence in the job the state is doing to regulate the amount of polluted water sent back into the state's waterways.

headline: Sleep's a distant dream for over-60 set
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh has received a $9.8 million grant from the National Institute on Aging to conduct a five-year study, to be called AgeWise, will recruit some 400 seniors to understand the causes of insomnia. The goal of the study is to better understand the biological causes of insomnia and then find the most effective non-pharmaceutical solutions for each cause.

headline: City seeks Pa. study of firefighting direction
abstract: Philadelphia city fire officials, faced with budget cutbacks, costly union contracts, and complaints about the Nutter administration's commitment to public safety, have asked the state to fund a first-ever study of the city's needs for a 21st-century Fire Department. Top administration officials asked the city's state-appointed overseer to study everything about providing fire safety, from deployment of fire companies to management structure and revenue. The move signaled a willingness by the Nutter administration to seek an independent review of any restructuring of the Fire Department.

headline: Mortgage applications fell last week
abstract: According to the Mortgage Bankers Association, the overall mortgage application index decreased 18.6 percent from the previous week as higher rates on fixed mortgages have discouraged borrowing.

headline: Rendell's budget boosts spending and broadens taxes
abstract: Governor Rendell's budget proposal broadens the application of the sales tax and increases overall spending by 4.1%. Rendell has increased funding of education and has proposed a severance tax on Marcellus shale extraction. The Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry and the Altria Group have said that the governor's budget hinders business in Pennsylvania.

headline: Where are the Harrisburg area's female leaders?
abstract: The article discusses CEO of Rite Aid Corp., Mary Sammons, and her stepping down from that post as emblematic of the absence of women leaders in central Pennsylvania. The article discusses the need for women to lead businesses and universities and battling sexism.

headline: Economy, education top issues as candidates debate
abstract: Nearly 100 people attended the forum for Pennsylvania's 12th Congressional District candidates Mark Critz, Tim Burns, Ryan Bucchianeri, William Russell and Ron Mackell, hosted by the Daily American, Somerset. Critz and Burns are facing off in a special election to fill the rest of the unexpired term of the late John Murtha, who died in February, all are also seeking the two-year term that begins in 2011.

headline: The Runyan-Adler slugfest begins
abstract: The race between Democratic-incumbent US Representative John Adler and Republican challenger John Runyan is proving to be a battle early on. Both sides have exchanged criticisms of the other while facing party complications. Runyan accused Adley of overly taxing and Rep. Adler accused Runyan of getting a farmland tax credit for raising four donkeys and harvesting timber on his property.

headline: DCNR head: State parks to stay open
abstract: State conservation officials expect that the budget cuts hitting the rest of the state government should not result in them having to close any of the state's 117 parks.  The department will rely on a combination of reduced services and cuts in hourly-wage jobs.

headline: Flight 93 memorial needs money to be finished
abstract: Calvin Wilson speaks about the Flight 93 Memorial and remembering 9/11 at a Wednesday news conference announcing Rocky Bleier's fundraiser at Heinz Field to benefit the memorial. As part of the fundraising effort for the project, former Steelers running back Rocky Bleier has organized a Forty for Forty dinner, featuring 40 Steelers alumni who will join the 40 families of those who lost loved ones aboard Flight 93.

headline: Rendell asks for counterproposal on gas tax plan
abstract: In a conference call with PA legislative Democratic and Republican leaders Tuesday, Governor Ed Rendell told them that if they did not like his compromise shale tax proposal, they should deliver to him a counterproposal by the end of the day. Just over a week ago, Senate Republicans delivered Rendell draft legislation that outlined their position on a tax. That proposal calls for a 1.5 percent tax on the market value of gas from wells producing more than 150,000 cubic feet of gas.

headline: ‘Route 30, Too!’ filming ends
abstract: Filming for “Route 30, Too” has wrapped. The film which is scheduled for release in 2012, filmed its last scenes at Mr. Ed’s, an elephant museum and peanut and candy emporium.

headline: Next 24 hours 'important' in city's efforts to clear streets
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl said that the next 24 hours in the city's cleanup are important to averting more hardship for city residents. Ravenstahl and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato have said that area roads are still treacherous and that city businesses should take travel into consideration for their workers. The city has employed outside help for snow removal.

headline: Contractors file suit against Montgomery County
abstract: Associated Builders & Contractors Inc. of Southeast Pennsylvania has filed Montgomery County over a provision that specifically requires that bidders for construction contracts be unionized. Opponents say the provision that passed in February by the Montgomery county commissioners is discriminatory.

headline: Taking credit: Pa. students can cut costs with college transfers
abstract: The Pennsylvania College Credit Transfer System, authorized and signed into law in 2006 came along just in time to give hard-pressed residents a less-expensive way to start their higher education. As a result of the law fewer students had to repeat courses taken at one school when they moved to another, which the state estimated saved them $35 million last year alone.

headline: Welcome America to get city services gratis
abstract: The City of Philadelphia's recently passed ordinance that places the financial burden on parade organizers for city services used for the event. The non-profit Welcome America, which organizes the Fourth of July Parade, has been exempt from paying the city for city services claiming that it was different in the sense that the parade represents the city.

headline: Cards in line for blackjack, poker school
abstract: Luzerne County Community College is partnering with a NY based consulting firm to open up a blackjack and poker dealing school this fall.  LCCC will offer the courses this fall ending on October 28.  The blackjack course runs 120 hours and the poker course runs 100 hours.  Steve Dahle, vice president of marketing at Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs in Plains Township, said the casino would definitely considering hiring from those who receive certificates from the program.

headline: Some visits to doctor are costing lots more
abstract: West Penn Allegheny Health System spokesman Dan Laurent said that the health system has fees for visits at facility-based medical practices, as allowed by Medicare. Last year, the Cleveland Clinic faced a storm of public criticism when it instituted facility fees at some of its outlying family health centers. One health center patient told the Cleveland Plain Dealer that her medical bill increased 63 percent as a result of the additional fee.

headline: Medical-data breach said to be major
abstract: A computer flash drive containing the names, addresses, and personal health information of 280,000 people is missing. The breach, which involves the records of Medicaid recipients, is the first such Medicaid data breach in Pennsylvania since at least 1997, according to the state's Department of Welfare, which has oversight.

headline: Speak out against gerrymandering
abstract: Author argues against gerrymandering and discusses the commissions in New Jersey and Pennsylvania and their partisan practices when redistricting.

headline: Rendell proposes equal funding to Penn State
abstract: Governor Rendell gave his budget address which gives the same amount of appropriations to Pennsylvania State University in 2010-2011 as it did in 2009-2010. The governor stressed the importance of passing the budget.

headline: Ban driver cell phones now
abstract: The author is encouraging state government to pass a ban on cell phones while driving like Pennsylvania cities like Philadelphia, Allentown, and Erie.

headline: Guess who lives in America's fifth most livable city? You do.
abstract: Harrisburg ranks fifth in a Forbes.com list of America's most livable cities, and Pittsburgh is first. According to Forbes.com the list is based on one aspect of cities livability which is the ability to go through the day-to-day business of life with the fewest difficulties.

headline: County rules on guns could be unconstitutional
abstract: A new rule at Lackawanna County parks says that the carrying of registered firearms is illegal. Local law enforcement believe the rule is too lenient and that police will not allow firearms at a public facility. Meanwhile, residents say the law pre-empts state laws by forbidding those with a concealed license to carry their gun. They say the rules are unconstitutional.

headline: Wound care center opening in Meyersdale
abstract: As many as 7 million people need special care to help treat persistent wounds.  Meyersdale Medical Center’s new Wound Healing Center will open on August 2 to help those with such wounds that won't go away on their own.  Experts says that wounds can heal if under the right care.  Some patients aren't aware that their wounds are in need of treatment and go on as if they are a part of their way of life.

headline: State College ranked no. 2 among best college towns
abstract: State College, PA was ranked the second best college town with a population of 250,000 or less by the American Institute for Economic Research. The rankings are based on data collected in 12 categories including cost of living, student diversity, how much research goes on, income and options for arts and entertainment.

headline: 'Don't rush' to apply to DROP, Tasco tells city workers
abstract: Philadelphia City Council yesterday urged city workers not to enroll in Deferred Retirement Option Plan (DROP) in haste. Since Mayor Nutter has called for the elimination of the controversial retirement perk, more than 1,200 workers have applied to the program. Council yesterday passed a resolution promising city workers that even if the DROP is eliminated, there will be a window for eligible workers to enroll.

headline: Larry Wise pleads not guilty in assault case
abstract: Larry Wise, a Burnham Borough councilman, is charged with three counts of involuntary deviate sexual intercourse and one count of sexual assault. He pleaded not guilty to the charges during a formal arraignment in the Mifflin County Court of Common Pleas. Wise is accused of having inappropriate sexual contact with a 16-year-old male.

headline: John Murtha, 1932-2010: A great American
abstract: US Representative John Murtha who represented the 12th district of Pennsylvania died at 77. He will be remembered as the first Vietnam veteran elected to congress.

headline: the costs that will increase to the states
abstract: States are concerned that they will have to pick up the costs of the expansion of Medicare and Medicaid that are likely to be enacted in the federal healthcare reform bill. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is among those who are concerned.

headline: N.J. Supreme Court nominee wins praise
abstract: Anne M. Patterson was nominated to the New Jersey Supreme Court on Monday by Gov. Christie, highlighting a 27-year legal career. Patterson a registered Republican is a partner in the Morristown firm of Riker, Danzig, Scherer, Hyland & Perretti, and has primarily represented business concerns in class actions and corporate litigation and appeals.

headline:
Sands casino could restart conference center
Sands still losing money, but hotel and tables will help.
abstract: The Sands Casino of Bethlehem has said construction on a planned conference center, hotel, and mall will continue after being sidelined during the 2008 recession. Sands will team up with Steel Ice Center to create a conference center for concerts and other events. The Sands has been offered to be bought but the offers were less than they paid for the casino.

headline: Area joblessness dips slightly to 10.2 percent, still Pa.'s highest
abstract: Joblessness among Scranton/Wilkes-Barre/Hazleton areas residents dropped slightly to 10.2%.  While it is unreasonable to expect that jobs will be gained as quickly as they were lost, there is room to be cautiously optimistic in these new numbers.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate Democratic nominee Joe Sestak says Washington needs to refocus on small businesses
abstract: Speaking before a gathering of machinists and members of various labor unions, PA Senate Democratic nominee Representative Joe Sestak, D-Delaware County, this morning portrayed himself as a defender of laborers and the manufacturing sector, and a long-time proponent of small business. Sestak highlighted the major economic differences between him and Republican opponent, former Rep. Pat Toomey, describing the former Lehigh Valley congressman as an advocate for Wall Street and large corporations that export jobs overseas at the cost of hometown jobs.

headline: Pat Meehan: Political career grew from work as a prosecutor
abstract: Patrick Meehan had been Delaware County district attorney less than a month when a multimillionaire sports patron shot and killed an Olympic wrestler in Newtown Square, then a few months later, a college student was abducted along the Blue Route, then killed and dumped in a lot in North Philadelphia. Winning convictions in those two cases bolstered Meehan's reputation as a law-and-order Republican, and led to his appointment as U.S. attorney for the eastern district of Pennsylvania in 2001. Now Meehan is running for an open seat in the Seventh Congressional District, one of the most closely watched races of the year.

headline: Experts: Big blunder usually serial killers' fatal flaw
abstract: Philadelphia Police are hoping that a flaw common to serial killer’s will result in the capture of the Kensington Strangler. The Philadelphia Police have enlisted the help of the FBI to compile a profile of the Kensington Strangler.

headline: Museums anticipate losing state funding
abstract: Pittsburgh area museums are expected to step up lobbying efforts after Governor Rendell proposed completely cutting funding to those attractions in his budget proposal. Museums such as the Carnegie Museum of Natural History and the Senator John Heinz Regional History Center will be cut resulting in a loss of jobs.

headline: president obama and congressional democrats are celebrating the passage of the historic health care legislation this morning
abstract: President Obama is expecting to receive a healthcare reform bill to sign into law after the US House of Representatives passed a healthcare reform bill that would extend healthcare to 32 million Americans.

headline: Rendell urges legislature to find transportation funds
abstract: On Tuesday Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell during a special session of the legislature urged them to raise enough money to fix the state's crumbling highways and bridges and underfunded mass transit agencies. According to Governor Rendell lawmakers need to find at least $472 million a year to replace anticipated funds blocked by a federal rejection of a state plan to place tolls on I-80.

headline: Happier, healthier    Weatherly Area Middle School students strive to be more active
abstract: Students of the Weatherly Area Middle School were applauded for becoming more and more active in the past year due to a grant from the Pennsylvania Department of Health to improve health and fitness activities in the school. Weatherly was one of 40 schools selected by the DOH through the federal Preventive Health and Health Services Block Grant. The Blue Cross of Northeast Pennsylvania also gave money to the cause.

headline: Sen. Casey introduces another bill on gas drilling safety
abstract: U.S. Sen. Bob Casey, D-Pa. is planning to introduce federal legislation that aims to make drilling sites safer.  He would require that drillers call 911 after accidents and that rescue vehicles be positioned to conveniently respond to accidents.

headline: High-tech equipment for city police constantly evolving
abstract: The Pittsburgh Police Department unveiled new waterproof citations at a Fire and Police Training Academy in East Liberty. The new tickets, which can be printed by patrol officers, are among several advances in technology that were displayed Tuesday by city officials.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Bets off on safety
abstract: Philadelphia's SugarHouse casino has been open only a matter of weeks, yet it has already lived down to expectations. Not only are there gamblers blowing the rent money among the customers spending an incredible $5 million a week, but there are also thieves to fear.

headline: Corbett's pick for chief of staff backs out
abstract: Governor-elect Tom Corbett's pick for chief of staff, Brian Nutt, announced he would be leaving his position and joining a political-consulting firm. A replacement has yet to be chosen.

headline: Mayor's brother gets boost when potential rival gets city job
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl appointed his campaign manager, Paul McKrell, as the city's first government relations manager after he dropped out of the race for former PA Representative Don Walko's seat against Adam Ravenstahl, the mayor's brother. The Ravenstahl's have been accused of quid-pro-quo in granting McKrell the job.

headline: The O'Reilly Factor
abstract: PA Governor Rendell discusses whether the recently passed healthcare legislation is a form of social welfare with Bill O'Reilly. O'Reilly said that the government will be giving away healthcare while Governor Rendell said only those on Medicare and Medicaid would have fully subsidized healthcare while low-income people would have to still pay a premium based on their income.

headline: Nursing homes site considered consumer friendly, but experts say visit in person, too
abstract: After a year and a half the reaction to the federal government's five-star rating is much the same as it was when the system was first introduced. The system allows consumers to view the rankings simply by going to the Medicare website and look for nursing homes under resource locator. Consumer groups applaud the system, while nursing home representatives say that the rankings can be misleading.

headline: Split seen on county merit selection option
abstract: Supporters of merit selection of judges said they would like to focus on state judges rather than local common pleas court judges. PA Governor Rendell said he would like a provision in the bill that would allow county residents to petition to put an option on the election ballot that would allow citizens to vote on whether they would like to vote for judges or not. PA Senator Jane Earll said getting such a provision in the bill would inhibit its passage

headline: Storm cleanup continues
abstract: At least 3 tornadoes touched down in Wayne County on Friday.  One twister carved a 15 mile path with winds as high as 125mph.  Residents were amazed by the damage the storms can cause.  No injuries were reported as a result of the storms.  Many trees were uprooted as well as some sparse property damage.

headline: Most East Stroudsburg schools making progress in state tests; problems persist
abstract: Five of East Stroudsburg's 10 schools made adequate yearly progress, which means that students passed state tests, known as the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment, at prescribed rates in two consecutive years. In math, 56 percent of students must pass the PSSA; in reading, 63 percent must do so, these performance thresholds will increase this year.

headline: With GOP fired up, Democrats ramp up the rallying
abstract: The midterm election campaign in Philadelphia and across the country has been defined by surveys showing Republican voters more fired up, intent on registering displeasure with President Obama and the Democratic Congress. So the elements of the Democratic coalition are going back to basics, with the national committee's Organizing for America army of volunteers, organized labor, the city machine, and black churches all trying to mobilize enthusiasm among the party base. President Obama, who drew 18,500 to a rally in Germantown this month, is returning to Philadelphia on Saturday, and Michelle Obama is to campaign in the city next Monday.

headline: The Wimps Who Stole Christmas
abstract: Author is disappointed with the decision by Mayor Nutter and others to postpone a Philadelphia Eagle’s game due to a snowstorm.

headline:
Pa. likely to steal Wheeling players
The two casinos in the Pittsburgh area plan to set up dozens of table games over the summer.
abstract: With the addition of table games to the state's casino's many Pittsburgh-area gamblers plan to stop going to their usual table-games gambling venues in Wheeling, WV and instead will go to nearby Pittsburgh casinos Rivers and Meadows. Many gamblers forego Rivers and Meadows in favor of those in Wheeling that offer table games.

headline: Carney: Health insurance law will benefit senior citizens
abstract: US Representative Chris Carney of Pennsylvania said that the new healthcare reform bill will benefit seniors  by helping to close the Medicare part D "doughnut" hole by providing a $250 rebate. It also provides for preventative care protections while better coordinating between physicians who care for the elderly.

headline: State House passes drilling moratorium on forest lands
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives passed House Bill 2235 on Tuesday, which would put a three-year halt to natural gas drilling in state forests.

headline: Rendell's tax ideas lead to economic stagnation
abstract: The author opines that PA Governor Rendell should cut public sector employment to support his budget, which he says spends too much. He notes that the private sector has made cutbacks during the recession while the public sector has grown. He says that the governor's plan to tax business will make it hard to fund the public sector because the companies will not be profitable to pay taxes.

headline: Authority forming to help park scheduling, funding
abstract: Rep. Ed Staback, D-115, Archbald has been involved in organizing regional cooperation in recreational activities after expressing concern about their scarcity.  Some communities in the Midvalley wish to combine forces to organize a true regional recreational authority to better organize and distribute funding for improvements.

headline: Lack of gas tax puts us in an odd state
abstract: Kevin Harley, gubernatorial campaign spokesman for Republican Tom Corbett, believes that the natural gas industry can be taxed out of existence in Pennsylvania. West Virginia has the same tax of roughly 5 percent that Governor Ed Rendell proposes, so drillers would find no break there. The state has issued permits for 3,800 Marcellus Shale gas wells and about 1,800 of them have been drilled.

headline: Rendell vetoes education bill over charter-school tax break
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell on Friday vetoed a comprehensive education bill that he said gave an unfair tax break to charter-school landlords a move that blindsided and outraged some legislators and advocates of the measure. The provision would have exempted nonprofit foundations that rent property to charter schools, and let them apply the tax break retroactively. But the governor's veto took down with it a wider law that included about 20 other initiatives among them, ones to combat student violence, make textbooks more affordable, and improve financial literacy.

headline: Phila. Homeowners facing foreclosure get holiday reprieve
abstract: Common Pleas Court President Judge Pamela Dembe ordered a 30-day moratorium on sheriff’s sales. The Philadelphia Unemployment Project, a grassroots advocate for unemployed and low-income workers, lobbied for the delay to allow a federal foreclosure-intervention program to take effect.

headline: 'Self-preservation' to dominate state budget process
abstract: Ahead of Governor Rendell's budget address legislators are expected to make their self-preservation as part of the legislature an issue in the budget process, said a spokesman for Pennsylvanians for Effective Government. Legislators are unlikely to support unpopular policies due to this year being an election year. The gap in the budget is $450 million.

headline: Jobless may get help with mortgages
abstract: The Obama administration may plans to overhaul its handling of the mortgage crisis by ordering and subsidizing lenders to decrease the amount of equity or their monthly mortgage payment to unemployed people who have defaulted on their mortgage payment. They also plan to ask lenders to cease payment of mortgage payments.

headline: I-80 tolling remains long-term option
abstract: The U.S. Federal Highway Administration's rejection last month of Pennsylvania's application to toll I-80 starting in 2011 has created a $470 million short-term gap for road and bridge projects, and long term funding needs are expected to be in the $2 billion range. At a special Pennsylvania legislative session Governor Ed Rendell told lawmakers they need to continue to pursue tolls on Interstate 80 and Interstate 95.

headline: Susquehanna Health ranks among elite
abstract: According to the 2010 Hospital Index, the Williamsport Regional Medical Center of Susquehanna Health has been named one of the top 100 hospitals in the country, ranking 26 out of 100 nationally.

headline: PA may get 70 percent of federal medic-aid funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell meet with PA Congressman this morning about what they will do if congress does not approve the full 850 million dollars in medic-aid money. If the state does not receive the full amount state layoffs would have to be made, up to 20 thousand people would be laid off to cover the costs.

headline: Three schools in area receive national honors
abstract: Cornell and South Fayette elementary schools as well as Wylandville Elementary in the Canon-McMillan School District were cited among 304 schools nationwide as National Blue Ribbon Schools by the US Department of Education.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Costly overtime
abstract: Philadelphia Sheriff John D. Green's has often been criticized for his two-decade operation of the elected office, and last year spent 23 percent of his payroll on time-and-a-half. Meanwhile, other city departments have been ratcheting back at the direction of Mayor Nutter. Green's excuse for the runaway overtime costs year in and year out is that his deputies, who transport criminal defendants and prisoners, are at the beck and call of the courts.

headline: Two approaches to drilling
abstract: Pennsylvania DEP instituted new drilling regulations earlier this year that it insisted were among the best in the country, and is still working on one more major set of changes concerning the construction of well sites.

headline: Pennsylvania Turnpike commissioner quits after admitting to 2 DUI convictions in turnpike vehicle
abstract: Pennsylvania Turnpike Commissioner Timothy Carson sent a letter to Governor Rendell announcing his resignation after he admitted to two driving while intoxicated incidents with a turnpike-issued vehicle.

headline: Clout: Cops had flash-mob news conference well covered
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter gets asked questions about why cops were taken off the streets to be a backdrop for a flash mob news conference. Pia Varma, Republican primary challenger to US Representative Bob Brady blames local GOP leaders of not competently gathering nomination signatures. Ralph Nader has asked PA Attorney General Tom Corbett to investigate Reed Smith LLP, the law firm that led the effort to get him removed from the 2004 Presidential ballot.

headline: Tolling Interstate 80 remained an option
abstract: Last month the U.S. Federal Highway Administration rejected Pennsylvania's application to toll I-80 starting in 2011 which created a $470 million short-term gap for road and bridge projects. Governor Ed Rendell during a special legislative session Tuesday told law makers the state would follow national regulations, but urged them to find other ways to raise money needed for the state's transportation system.

headline:
Area school districts hit hardest by budget crunches
Study shows districts in southeastern Pennsylvania are cutting staff, dipping into reserve funds at rates above state average
abstract: In 2010-2011 schools in southeastern Pennsylvania have been affected by the downturn in the economy. 51 percent of school districts in the state were surveyed, 69 percent were cutting staff to balance budgets, and 73 percent in southeast Pennsylvania were cutting budgets, according to a study by the Pennsylvania School Funding Campaign.

headline: Philadelphia's retirement plan is a financial drain
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter is advocating a deferred retirement option plan to pay city employee's retirement plans. With this plan a city worker picks a retirement date well in advance up to four years and in exchange for providing that notice, the city then begins paying the workers pension into an account, with interest. The worker then gets to collect that lump sum when they retire; all told this plan could cost the city $258 million in 11 years.

headline: Hotel tax exemption concerns local officials
abstract: PA laws governing the 6 percent state hotel tax and county hotel taxes say any person staying in a hotel room for more than 30 days is considered a "permanent resident" and exempt from the tax. Since almost 50 percent of rooms occupied in Wyoming County are falling under the "30-day rule," a large portion of which are gas drillers the exemption has come under scrutiny. The Department of Revenue estimates the exemption represents what could be about $1 million in revenue for the state.

headline: Perzel steps up efforts to keep House seat vs. Boyle
abstract: In December, PA Representative John Perzel, was charged with 82 counts of conspiracy, theft and conflict of interest as part of "Bonusgate," the scandal involving payments of state money to state workers for campaign work. Now Perzel is facing his first serious challenge in a decade, from Kevin Boyle, brother of PA Representative Brendan Boyle who has been hammering Perzel in television and print ads and calling for "honest leadership" in Harrisburg.

headline: District court offices could be cut
abstract: In an effort to offset a possible $17 million state deficit, the Pennsylvania judiciary has asked individual counties to consider closing some magisterial district court offices. Allegheny County, which has the largest number of courts in the state, could face the closure of 4 of its 48 offices.

headline: OPINION: Ed Rendell's sales-tax cut looks like a bait-and-switch
abstract: The author argues that Governor Rendell should have cut spending and restructured pension plans in order to cut the state's deficit. The cutting of the sales tax and lifting exemptions could mean that the next governor will simply raise the sales tax rate.

headline: More Doctors Giving Up Private Practices
abstract: Increasing amounts of doctors are leaving their private practice to join larger healthcare systems to make more money and to have more steady working hours. The new federal healthcare legislation actually steers doctors away from private practice. Some view it positively as giving patients access to more specialists and doctors than a private practice, but others see it as giving large healthcare systems a monopoly over healthcare thus being able to impose leverage on health insurance providers.

headline: Going green at graduation
abstract: Eco-conscious campuses have been trying to reduce the environmental impact of commencement ceremonies by using less electricity or printing programs on recycled paper. Now academic apparel companies are coming out with environmentally friendly products such as deposable gowns, that are made of recycled materials or can decompose safely in the soil.

headline:
Secondhand Smoke Linked to Mental Distress 
Risk of psychological troubles rises for exposed nonsmokers
abstract: A University College of London study showed that mental distress is linked to exposure to secondhand smoke. Previous research has shown that exposure to nicotine may alter moods in people by disrupting immune responses.

headline: Thousands of state layoffs have been avoided
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was counting on $850 million in Medicaid funding from the feds, but US senators voted to stop debate on the funding yesterday. It now goes to the full senate where it is expected to pass. If passed Pennsylvania should get about $600 million, which means some layoffs but nowhere near the 12,000 expected if the money had not come.

headline: Appeals court rejects ex-lawmaker's plea to overturn conviction
abstract: A federal appeals court on Thursday rejected the argument of a former PA Representative Max Homer found guilty in 1975 of extortion and perjury that his conviction should be overturned.

headline: PA cash surge grows as election nears
abstract: In the last week, Pennsylvania gubernatorial candidates Republican Tom Corbett and Democrat Dan Onorato have collected at least $7 million, according to daily reports filed with state election officials. Corbett has taken the lion's share, more than $5 million, buoyed in part by two million-dollar payments in three days from a national group, the Republican Governors Association, and $480,000 from the state GOP. The donations, disclosed in daily reports that each candidate must make, offer a stark reminder of Pennsylvania's no-limits campaign finance system.

headline: Cashless turnpike tolls eyed
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission has authorized a yearlong study on how the 545-mile highway network could switch to a “cashless” toll collection system, known as “All Electronic Tolling”. When the study is complete, a team chosen by the commission will prepare a report listing all available tolling options, general system requirements, estimated costs, traffic-and-revenue impacts and the implementation schedule involved with such a conversion.

headline: Anger at governor over SSI misplaced
abstract: Governor Rendell's press secretary Gary Tuma writes that the Altoona Mirror provided false info regarding cuts to state funding of the Supplemental Security Income in the state budget. He said PA Senator John Eichelberger voted for decreasing funding for SSI and against raising funding to SSI while the governor worked to gain adequate funding for SSI in state budget proposals.

headline: Nutter calls Sen. Williams ‘great public servant’
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and PA Representative Dwight Evans endorsed PA Senator Anthony Williams for PA Governor in the gubernatorial Democratic primary. Anthony Williams has endorsed the proliferation of charter schools and tax write-offs for companies that donate to privately run schools.

headline: Congressional candidates talk issues
abstract: Candidates for Pennsylvania's 10th Congressional District attended a forum sponsored by the Williamsport Tea Party, where the candidates shared their thoughts on many issues primarily dealing with government power. Republican candidates Thomas A. Marino, Malcolm Derk and David Madeira attended the forum in anticipation of the May 18 primary.

headline:
Manheim hearing draws a crowd
Delays discussion of facility for convicts
abstract: The Manheim Borough Zoning Hearing Board postponed their hearing on a plan to build a housing facility for state prisoners upon release from prison. The plan has drawn controversy and the State Department of Corrections said the state is planning on building a community corrections center in central Pennsylvania. The zone for the proposed plan is zoned industrial and does not recognize institutional uses.sr

headline: PA Governor Ed Rendell is in central Pennsylvania, talking transportation funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is calling on state lawmakers to come up with more money to improve roads in central PA and the rest of the state. Not all lawmakers are in support of the governor's plan. The governor is going to formally ask all the lawmakers to come back to Harrisburg on August 23rd, two weeks before the next legislative term.

headline: Commentary: Pat Toomey emphasizes being a 'former small business owner'
abstract: Pat Toomey the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate has lashed his electoral identity to the American men and women who create jobs through sweat and innovation in corner-shop operations such as dry cleaners and Italian ice stands.

headline: Green postpones retirement as Philadelphia sheriff to deal with audit
abstract: Philadelphia Sheriff John D. Green, scheduled to leave office at the end of the month, Wednesday postponed his retirement to work with City Controller Alan Butkovitz on a full-scale audit of his office and remove the "cloud" resulting from a blistering report from the Controller's Office. Butkovitz on Tuesday called for the forensic audit of the Sheriff's Office, saying that Green had failed to provide information on its $53 million in accounts, leaving the office open to fraud and abuse.

headline: Work hard, awards will come
abstract: The Franklin Learning Center, recently selected as a national Blue Ribbon School, is profiled for its accomplishments.

headline: Snow plow drivers work long hours with little thanks
abstract: Jim Blood, a public works employee from Hampden township, along with others, help clear the snow from Hampden roads. They often work long hours and make special trips to help people make vital trips.

headline: Stu Bykofsky: Most flash-mobbers were black, but was the incident racial?
abstract: The author asks whether the flash-mob attacks, which were coincidentally black on white crimes, were the result of race or socio-economic status. The author states that anti-social behavior stems from poor upbringings in poor, ethnic neighborhoods.

headline: Lousy school lunches fuel childhood obesity
abstract: Exercise and less soda has been the slogan of many of those claiming to be combating child-hood obesity. But the real problem is nutrition content of the lunches which are offered to students, this is an issue which has never been thoroughly discussed. With 31 million students who eat lunches in the United States a major step to combating childhood obesity is to address the lunches being offered.

headline: Pennsylvania Orders EOG Drilling Halt After Blowout (Update1)
abstract: EOG resources has been ordered by to stop natural gas drilling for as long as seven days  in Pennsylvania after a well in Clearfield County exploded, according to the Department Environmental Protection. The explosion spewed natural gas and 35,000 gallons of drilling fluid. There were no injuries and no fires.

headline: PA Governor Ed Rendell addresses what he calls a transportation funding crisis
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is saying the state can raise millions for public transportation by taxing oil companies for the gas they sell in Pennsylvania. Rendell also wants to hike the state's gas tax and up the fee to renew your driver's license and registration. However, critics oppose such measures to pay for local projects like helping the Pittsburgh Port Authority pay its bills.

headline: Fish and Boat Commission seeks severance tax funds
abstract: The Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission proposes to use $1.6 million from a severance tax to hire additional staff to monitor streams, review drilling permits and help natural gas drillers better design well sites to minimize impacts to fish, reptiles and other aquatic life. Governor Ed Rendell, who supports a tax, has estimated that it could generate $475 million annually by 2015.

headline: News Channel 8 This Morning
abstract: Iowa Governor Culver said despite trailing in the polls, he knows the democrats will pull through. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell who was at an event with Culver, said democrats were down in the dumps but now are enthusiastic and ready to win on November 2nd.

headline: Leadership turnover in nonprofits may energize region
abstract: Key nonprofits are experiencing vacancies in top leadership positions. The vacancies are thought to be a result of a suffering economy. Some of the more significant institutions experiencing vacancies include the Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh, the Andy Warhol Museum, the Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh, and the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership.

headline: Job growth must take hold for our economic recovery
abstract: Written by Bill George President of the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO. He praised the Obama administration and US Congressional Democrats of staving off a depression with the Troubled Assets Relief Program. He says that if it wasn't for the greed of wall street bankers more TARP money would be available to help state and local governments hold onto public sector jobs. He proposed policies like encouraging banks who receive excess TARP money to reinvest it into the local community.

headline:
Local tourism group touts 2009 success
Fishing tournament, G-20 summit top list of biggest events
abstract: The Forrest L. Wood fishing tournament and the G-20 summit were the two events held in Pittsburgh last year that produced the most revenue for the city. The G-20 summit was touted as a success by the tourism agency visitPittsburgh which said that all the good press about Pittsburgh gave the city brand exposure.

headline: Philadelphia's million-dollar condos
abstract: Million dollar condo sales in cities like New York and Paris are nothing new, but for Philadelphia this is a fairly recent phenomenon. Penthouse condos at the Residences at Two Liberty Place are now up to $30 million, and some condos in Rittenhouse Square are now in the million dollar range as well.

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell to address Harrisburg City Council committee about fiscal crisis
abstract: PA Governor Rendell will speak at an administrative committee meeting of the Harrisburg City Council to discuss city finances. Gov. Rendell has provided the city with two financial advisors. The city owes $68 million in 2010 and the Harrisburg Authority, which was disbanded two weeks prior, is in debt $288 million.

headline: New rules proposed by Delaware River Port Authority chief
abstract: New rules proposed Wednesday by the Delaware River Port Authority (DRPA) chairman John Matheussen  would make sweeping changes in the way the bi-state agency operates. This comes after demands from the New Jersey and Pennsylvania governors to make the DRPA more open and responsive. Among the proposed changes include putting an end to hiring relatives of executives and employees, and other changes to help eliminate corruption.

headline: Some Democratic legislators push for shale gas tax
abstract: PA House Democrats and several environmental groups today demanded that the Legislature meet an Oct. 1 deadline for enacting a new tax on the natural gas extracted from areas of Marcellus shale in Pennsylvania. Governor Ed Rendell favors a two-part tax, putting a 5 percent tax on the value of the gas that's extracted and sold, plus a levy of 4.7 cents per MCF, or 1,000 cubic feet of gas pumped out.

headline: State Senate should reconvene to pass gas tax
abstract: After taking a six-week summer recess the PA Senate returned to Harrisburg and rejected a fair tax on natural gas extraction that had been passed by the House. Senate Republicans subsequently refused to participate in a compromise effort led by Governor Ed Rendell. Millions of cubic feet of natural gas are being removed from beneath the commonwealth each day and sold.

headline: Fast Eddie's fudge factory: Get real
abstract: Author suggests that Governor Ed Rendell has chosen to use a more positive, yet less extensive federal audit of Medicare funding rather than a less positive, yet more extensive audit released by Auditor General Jack Wagner in order to suit his political purposes.

headline: Broad Street Market in Harrisburg remains closed despite extermination
abstract: The Broad Street Market in Harrisburg remained closed after a heavy snowstorm and a failed health inspection forced it to close down for extermination.

headline: States argue the feds can't force purchase of health insurance
abstract: Thirteen states' Attorney Generals have filed suit against the federal government for the mandate included in the healthcare reform bill that would require those without health insurance to buy health insurance. They say this is an overbroad interpretation of the to regulate commerce in several states. Legal ambiguities remain in regards to health insurance as a commodity.

headline: The special session: Get real
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell addressed a joint session of the Pennsylvania General Assembly today to discuss the urgent need for highway funding. This comes after Governor Rendell's attempt to toll Interstate 80 and skim millions off the top to pay for other transportation needs, which was rejected because it violates federal rules.

headline: Natural gas industry group defends drilling
abstract: Energy In Depth, a natural gas industry group, responded to derogatory claims as to the character of the natural gas industry after attorney Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a group of environmentalists went to Dimock, Pa to assess the impact of the natural gas industry. The group said the attorney and environmentalists did not see all sides of the impact of the natural gas industry on the town.

headline: State revokes license of center where man died
abstract: PA state officials Thursday revoked one of the licenses of the Bucks County facility where a severely autistic man died in a sweltering van. The PA Department of Public Welfare also banned Woods Services, the Langhorne residential care center, from accepting new clients until the department completes its investigation into the death of Bryan Nevins.

headline: Blair gets Liberty Medal for peacemaking efforts
abstract: Tony Blair, Britain's former prime minister, received this year's Liberty Medal in ceremonies last night at the National Constitution Center, honoring his success resolving the conflict in Northern Ireland and his ongoing pursuit of peace in the Middle East and Africa. Former President Bill Clinton, a longtime friend presented Blair with the award.

headline: Spring-Ford students help clean up Medal of Honor Grove
abstract: Nearly 20 student-athletes from Spring-Ford High School woke up bright and early Sunday morning to rake leaves and clean the monuments at the Medal of Honor Grove at the Freedoms Foundation of Valley Forge. After it was reported in July that the 52-acre Medal of Honor Grove was in poor condition, volunteers have flocked to clean it. The 52-acre grove is divided into one-acre plots for each state, as well as Puerto Rico and Washington, D.C.

headline: Business oversight board lists 186 actions
abstract: The Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs, which maintains 29 professional licensing boards, issued 186 disciplinary actions. A list of sanctions can be viewed online at www.dos.state.pa.us by clicking "Licensing" and then "Disciplinary Actions."

headline: Deficit as big as loophole
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget deficit could be attributed to the Delaware loophole. The loophole attracts 71% of the state's business and of the remaining businesses that do 79% pay under $10,000 per year. A bill to close the loophole projects the state could make $700 million. Companies complain that the state has too high of a Corporate Net Income tax rate at 9.9%.

headline: Lawmakers key to cities' future, Reading mayor, York ex-mayor say
abstract: The mayors of Reading and York spoke to a crowd at Alvernia University about the need for the state legislature to step in to help cities raise revenue to pay for pensions and other expenses. The two recommended a 1% sales tax option that would help local school districts, a consumer tax, an income tax for those who come into the city to work, a liquor tax, and pension reform.

headline: Herd of Republicans challenge Dahlkemper in pivotal 3rd District
abstract: U.S. Rep. Kathy Dahlkemper is the only freshman Democrat running for re-election in Pennsylvania this year. Kathy won her seat in 2008 and in the process unseated a seven-term Republican, but in a district that favored John McCain in 2008 for president Kathy will surely face a stiff challenge from one of the six Republican candidates. However of the six only former city Councilman Mike Kelly has ever held public office.

headline: $5 million from state boosts Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania
abstract: The Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania in Strasburg will begin work on a reconstruction project that will include multimedia exhibits of Pennsylvania's train history. This is all due to $5 million authorized to them by PA Governor Rendell.

headline: Ramsey beefs up Philadelphia police ethics strategies
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey announced plans Thursday to assign more officers to the department's Internal Affairs bureau, as the number of incidents of police misconduct continue to rise. Ramsey plans to enhance officer training in ethics issues, and create new ways for officers to report misconduct among their colleagues.

headline: Montco has West Nile virus case
abstract: After killing more than 1,000 people nationwide earlier in this decade, West Nile virus cases have declined. But health authorities in Pennsylvania and New Jersey have noticed a resurgence in infected mosquitoes this summer.

headline: Rendell halts natural gas drilling
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has carried out an executive order placing 1.5 million acres of state forest land off-limits for natural gas drilling, getting praise from environmental groups but sharp criticism from Senate Republican leader Joe Scarnati. The order bans any more drilling pads from being located in state forests, other than on the 700,000 acres of forest land already designated for gas drilling by the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. Scarnati said the high tax rate that Rendell and House Democrats want will hurt the industry just as it begins to bring hundreds of new jobs to PA.

headline: Lawmakers distressed by double absence
abstract: State Sen. Richard Codey is criticizing the Governor Chris Christie and Lt. Gov. Kim Guadagno for being absent during a snow storm that dumped two feet of snow on parts of the state. Christie and Guadagno were both on vacation at the time, leaving Senate President Stephen Sweeney to deal with problems that resulted from the snowfall.

headline:
DEP approves gas drilling wastewater treatment permit
TerrAqua will discharge treated water into West Branch of the Susquehanna River
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has granted a permit to TerrAqua to treat wastewater used for the fracking of Marcellus Shale Natural Gas wells and discharge it into the West Branch of the Susquehanna River. The operation will be built in Water Tower Square in Williamsport. The company will be subject to stricter DEP regulations to control sediments and contaminants going into the river.

headline: Beaver County airport gets funds for runway
abstract: The Beaver County Airport will receive $250,000 in state and federal funds for research and design into a new runway to be built with more state and federal funds yet to be determined. PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that $13.8 million will be going to Pennsylvania airports this year as part of a state program led by the PA Department of Transportation that collects revenue from the liquid fuels tax combined with matching funds from local governments.

headline: Environmental payoff: Allegheny County is once again fit for eagles
abstract: A new housing development in Crescent is drawing the attention of environmentalists because a nest, 4 feet in diameter, s believed to be home to a pair of bald eagles. The Pennsylvania Game Commission confirmed the existence of the first eagle's nest in Allegheny County in decades but only said that the nest is in the township of Crescent.

headline: Lawmakers: Verify legal status of Pennsylvania construction workers
abstract: State lawmakers urged passage of legislation that would verify the legal status of construction workers working under state-funded programs. The bill would require construction companies to confirm the legal status of their workers. PA Governor Rendell said he questions the reliability of the federal E-verify system and doesn't have a stance on the bills as of yet.

headline: Big government is not our enemy
abstract: Tea party supporters passionately complain that government is the enemy of freedom, they believe the more government grows, the more our liberty shrinks. In reality few of our government programs, even big government programs do anything to actually threaten anyone's freedoms. Nearly all of the common activities of the modern state are not inherently coercive or oppressive at all.

headline: Adler, Runyan reach for middle ground at forum
abstract: Freshman Democratic US Representative John Adler and Republican Jon Runyan both face a difficult challenge in the historically Republican New Jersey Third Congressional District, which two years ago made Adler its first Democratic congressman in decades but which swung for Republican Governor Chris Christie in 2009.

headline: Tax credits: Questions abound
abstract: The conservative Commonwealth Foundation says the credits increase the tax burden for all but their recipients. The liberal Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center says legislators increasingly dislike the credits' lack of control and accountability.

headline: Allegheny County Controller Flaherty to seek county exec job
abstract: County Controller Mark Patrick Flaherty plans to run for County Executive, regardless of whether fellow Democrat Onorato seeks a third term. Other potential candidates are awaiting Onorato’s decision. As many as five Republicans are considering a run in the May 17th primary, though according to GOP chairman Jim Roddey, they will most likely drop out if Onorato runs.

headline: Westmoreland County commissioner puts feelers out for Murtha seat
abstract: Westmoreland County Commissioner Tom Ceraso has announced he will begin to put together support for the late US Representative John Murtha's seat. Ceraso is a three-term Democrat from New Kensington.

headline:
War on teachers escalates
Frustrated at the state of public education, we are scapegoating an entire group.
abstract: The author states that America's teachers are being mislabeled as educators that fail their students. The author contends that other factors play a role in how students perform other than teacher performance. He notes the firing of 74 teachers at Central Falls High School in Rhode Island and the Obama administration's praise of the superintendent for such firings.

headline: Macey touting Maglev
abstract: Allegheny County Councilman Bob Macey, D-West Mifflin and Councilman Michael Finnerty, D-Scott Township are introducing a resolution calling attention to McKeesport-based Maglev Inc., which is largely ignored in a recent state report on high-speed rail transportation. This comes after Maglev Inc. was promised it would receive a $28 million grant from the Federal Railroad Administration.

headline: Pennsylvania to test high school graduation in as little as 2 years
abstract: The PA Department of Education is looking for schools to participate in a program by a Washington-based nonprofit that would allow high school students to graduate high school in 2 years. The National Center on Education and the Economy who would run the program will cost the state $40 million.

headline: Pittsburgh council president hospitalized
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council President Darlene Harris is in Allegheny General Hospital being treated for a stomach ailment.

headline: Philadelphia schools to get $96 million
abstract: The Philadelphia School District will receive an additional $96 million in federal funds over the next two years, which is the city's share of the $10 billion education jobs bill signed by President Barack Obama last month.

headline: Ravenstahl wants parking, pensions summit
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl said he'll expose City Council's plans to the withering light of day, signaling that he does not believe his $452 million garage- and meter-lease plan is buried. The mayor reversed his earlier resignation to the defeat of his plan, two years in the works, to lease the city's parking assets to winners of an auction in which J.P. Morgan Asset Management and LAZ Parking prevailed. The proposed lease garnered just one yes in a final council vote Tuesday that was followed Wednesday by a 7-1 tentative vote for the council plan to sell meters.

headline: Billboard's aim: Enliven controversial debate
abstract: A new billboard paid for by the Final Exit Network, which simply reads “Die with Dignity—the Final Human Right”, has been erected at the intersection of the Boulevard of the Allies and McDevitt place in Oakland. The Final Exit Network has posted similar billboards throughout the country. While they do not actively aid suicides, the group hopes to raise public awareness about the need for discussion surrounding right to die issues.

headline: Proposed state police fee would strain rural Wayne budgets
abstract: A proposed bill in the Pennsylvania legislature would require municipalities who use state police protection to compensate the state for those services. Local governments in Wayne County that rely on state police to either supplement their police force or depend on state police for their entire police force say the bill would put their already tight state budgets in the red.

headline: Women are moving forward, but there's still work to do in Pa.
abstract: The author states the need for women to have a larger role in federal politics and Pennsylvania state politics. The author states that just under 4% of congress are women and that Pennsylvania ranks fifth to last on women political participation among the states.

headline: Refusing DUI test is 'a big gamble'
abstract: Pennsylvania drivers who refuse blood or breath tests will not be allowed to drive for a year regardless of whether they were charged with driving under the influence. Drivers who are charged and convicted after refusing a test, face penalties that are much more severe because those who refuse are prosecuted as if they were driving with the highest blood alcohol content.

headline: governor ed rendell stopped in scranton this afternoon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell stopped in Scranton to promote the state's tax amnesty program, which only has 10 days left. The program is hoping to recoup the $2 billion the state is owed in back taxes.

headline: Pittsburgh Public Schools settle suit over girl's anorexia, taunting
abstract: A former student at Frick Middle School who claimed that teasing from fellow students about her weight and the administration's failure to halt the abuse led her to develop anorexia has agreed to settle her federal lawsuit. The girl who was not identified and her mother settled for $55,000, as well as the cost of mediation.

headline: Hard work will pay off, Obama tells Masterman students
abstract: President Barack Obama presented his back-to-school speech to about half of Masterman School's in Philadelphia 1,200 students in the auditorium of the magnet school, at 17th and Spring Garden streets. US Secretary of Education Arne Duncan, said one reason the top school was chosen for the president's address is the progress the Philadelphia School District has made.

headline: Governor hopefuls tell little about cuts
abstract: The final debate of the 2010 gubernatorial campaign presented a golden opportunity for Tom Corbett and Dan Onorato to say something meaningful about the deep cuts in state spending they have locked themselves into. Neither have outlined their plan for repairing the budget, which means they are keeping their plans secret or they have no plans for confronting a prospective budget deficit next year that both Democratic PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration and leaders of the Republican majority in the state Senate currently project at between $4 billion and $5 billion.

headline: Pitt chemistry professor at the forefront of a futuristic science
abstract: Alexander Star, a University of Pittsburgh chemistry professor, is one of few people making significant progress towards figuring out how nanotubes work. Nanotubes are naturally occurring, and increasingly manmade, microscopic tubes of carbon. The National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences named Dr. Star one of its eight Outstanding New Environmental Scientists for 2010. He was awarded a five-year, $2 million grant to help expand his lab and facilitate further research into the environmental impact of nanotubes.

headline: Pittsburgh schools criticized over charters
abstract: Randall Taylor, a former member of the Pittsburgh school board, criticized the Pittsburgh Public School's handling of a charter-school application.  Taylor claims that the school board rejected a charter-school application because they feared competition; he argues that a public discussion about the value of charter schools needs to be encouraged, and that all students deserve charter-school options.

headline: PMC's cancer center plans are on display
abstract: Pocono Medical Center's goal to build a cancer center by 2012 progressed one more step when architects at Erwin Cole unveiled plans for a 59,000 sq. ft. cancer center. The next step is to open up bids for contractors.

headline: 2-year state budgeting? Not a good idea says Dwight Evans
abstract: The author, PA Rep. Dwight Evans of Philadelphia, states that the suggestion of a biennial budget process for Pennsylvania would not better achieve the difficulties the state has had in recent years of passing a budget on time. Rep. Evans said a biennial budget would result in more drawn out and difficult budget discussions and less government oversight over government programs. Anticipating revenues and spending two years in advance would simply be too difficult.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate warns Pocono schools of funding shortfall
abstract: The worsening state budget for the current year threatens to curtail local school districts' spending plans for next year. The $1 billion gap in the revenue is more than double what was expected by the Pennsylvania state Senate. In a letter to the heads of the 500 state school districts, the senate told districts funding levels for school districts or any other entity in the Commonwealth in the 2010-11 state budget is not guaranteed.

headline: governor rendell did something he's never done last night
abstract: PA Governor Rendell spoke to Harrisburg City Council members about finances. He told them to avoid bankruptcy and lease, not sell the city's assets like parking garages. The city faces a $300 million debt, with a mismanaged garbage incinerator largely the problem.

headline: Small nonprofits could lose tax-exempt status
abstract: The Flight 427 Air Disaster Support League hasn't generated income, collected membership dues or solicited donations in nearly a decade. The nonprofit organization formed by family and friends of the 132 passengers and crew killed when a US Air jet crashed into a Beaver County hillside in 1994, used most of the money it collected in the first several years following the accident to purchase the eight-acre crash site in Hopewell and erect a memorial marker there.

headline: 'Dream big,' Obama tells Philadelphia students
abstract: President Obama delivered his back-to-school speech at Masterman School, the elite magnet at 17th and Spring Garden Streets which is the city's highest-performing school Tuesday. Masterman last week was named a 2010 National Blue Ribbon School. About 600 students and staff were chosen by lottery to listen to Obama's speech in person including Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's daughter Olivia.

headline: Control gas plans, South Fayette Township urged
abstract: Few people complained about the prospect of drilling for natural gas beneath South Fayette's rolling hills until word spread that Chesapeake Energy might plunge into land near the township's 2,000-student K-12 campus. More than 150 unhappy residents attended a township commissioners meeting this week, and a larger crowd is expected to protest a vote set for Monday on an ordinance that would govern drilling for natural gas in the town of 12,000 people.

headline: NE Pa. school board member's son alleges abuse
abstract: Court documents claim 50-year-old Robert Corcoran, a member of Wilkes-Barre’s board, punched his 13-year-old son in the face 11 times, breaking his front teeth. Corcoran has disputed the bulk of the allegations. Restraining orders were issued barring the Corcoran from contacting his son, and vice versa.

headline: Mourners recall former senator as 'a great man'
abstract: Mourners paid their respects to former state Senator Terry Punt.  Punt, a Waynesboro native, died of heart failure on December 28th; he served over 30 years in the state Legislature and was remembered as a man who always put the needs of others first.

headline: Valley View Business Park to add 26 tax-free sites
abstract: Valley View Business Park's addition of 26 new business sites called the Keystone Opportunity Zone will have their real-estate taxes abated by the Archbald, Jessup, and Valley View School Districts. An access road under construction by the PA Department of Transportation will provide access to the site and will be completed in June.

headline:
State's inmate numbers rising
That's in contrast to much of the rest of the nation, where the population fell for the first time since 1972.
abstract: The state of Pennsylvania's prison population grew by 4.3% in the past year while the nation's decreased by 0.4%. The rise in the PA prison population stems from the lengthening of crime sentencing policies and the failure of the judicial system to handle all of the cases brought before them, often resulting in people staying in jail while awaiting trial. The reasons for a national trend downward is that other states have adopted alternatives to jail and probation with therapy and rehabilitation. The PA Department of Corrections acknowledged the problem.

headline: House approves compromise drill moratorium
abstract: An amendment that provides for state studies of the environmental and socio-economic impact of Marcellus Shale drilling occurring on leased forest lands was passed by the Pennsylvania House of Representatives.

headline: Loopholes Grow in Bill to Offset Ruling on Campaigns
abstract: A bill in the US House of Representatives that is supported by Democrats would require disclosure on part on campaign contributions of corporations that buy television campaign commercial time. The Democrats reached a deal with the NRA which would exclude them from the law. The bill now faces Republican opposition in the House and likely in the Senate.

headline: Obamacare brings coverage to high-risk residents
abstract: Thanks to the new US health care legislation as many as 3,500 Pennsylvanians who have been denied medical coverage or found it prohibitively expensive because of illness soon may be able to purchase it. The state on Wednesday began accepting applications for the PA Fair Care program, which will provide health insurance coverage to high-risk residents who have been without it for at least six months and have a pre-existing medical condition.

headline: Christie wants public employees to work longer and pay more for health care
abstract: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie is calling for public employees to work longer, contribute more to their pensions, and pay more for health care, as part of a plan to rein in the state's costs. The gap between the predicted liabilities for New Jersey's public employee pension funds and current assets is an estimated $46 billion, a figure many experts believe falls far short of describing the state's true liabilities. Under the governor's proposal, the state would roll back a 9 percent increase in pension benefits granted to employees in 2001.

headline: Grant targets area bioscience
abstract: A $60,000 federal grant announced Monday will be used to study the region’s bioscience industry sector. U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski and Austin J. Burke, secretary of the PA Department of Community and Economic Development, announced the grant to help create an eight-county regional economic development strategic plan.

headline: KDKA Morning News
abstract: Govenor Ed Rendell issued a moratorium banning any further leasing of state forest land for natural gas drilling. The Jefferson Hills Borough Council is in the process of developing an ordinance to regulate Marcellus shale drilling.

headline: U.S. mining deaths fall to record low
abstract: In 2009, the number of miners killed in the United States fell to 34--the fewest since officials began keeping records a century ago.  Last year, two miners were killed in Pennsylvania.

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell's budget proposal would tax more services, sweets, supplies
abstract: Governor Rendell's budget proposal will lift sales tax exemptions on 74 products and services.
