The governor plans to raise revenue through the sales tax expansion to gap the $5.6 billion budget gap expected to appear next year. The budget gap is attributed to state pension payments and the end of federal stimulus money. The article lists the 74 sales tax exemptions being lifted.

headline: Harrisburg Schools: All parties need to devise unified school plan
abstract: The author calls for a forum on the state of Harrisburg School District that would include the state legislature, the Harrisburg appointed Board of Control for HSD, and the Harrisburg School Board. The author cites PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola with potentially being a player in the turnaround of Harrisburg School District, which ranks near last out of the state's 500 school districts in test scores.

headline: Specter, Kanjorski seek funds to expand Innovation Center
abstract: During a tour of the Innovation Center Monday, U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter and U.S. Rep. Paul E. Kanjorski said they would try to obtain $2.4 million in federal funds to build to a new facility to accommodate expansion. Projections say the project would provide support to more than 33 new start-up companies and has the potential to create about 205 new jobs and more than $35 million in wages in the first 10 years it is completed.

headline: Council drive-by: Let the Citizen Police Review Board do its job
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council voted to urge Pittsburgh's Citizen Review Police Board to ease the requesting of arrest reports to be used in an investigation of police conduct during the G20 summit. A Common Please Court Judge ordered the reports to be handed over to independent board for review. The author states that those who are trying to keep the reports from the board should be held in contempt of court.

headline: Pitt receives grant to study elderly falls
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh Graduate School of Public Health has received a $1.5 million grant from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to compare and evaluate two programs to prevent falls by elderly people,

headline: Pennsylvania gubernatorial candidates advocate school-vouchers bill at forum
abstract: Republican Tom Corbett and Democrat Dan Onorato, the two candidates for Pennsylvania governor said Tuesday they generally support a bill that would permit low-income students in failing public schools to obtain vouchers they could use for attendance at another public school or private school. This represents a major shift in the education debate since the last election for governor in 2006, when school choice was not a top issue.

headline: Eachus, Toohil slug it out in oddly conceived debate
abstract: In what will likely be the only debate between the candidates vying to represent the 116th Legislative District before the Nov. 2 election, Democratic incumbent Todd Eachus and Republican challenger Tarah Toohil squared off Wednesday on issues including jobs, health care and ethics, agreeing only that jobs were the most important issue. Both candidates suggested questions to debate moderator Sam Lesante, president of Hazleton-based Sam-Son Productions, prior to the debate and took turns answering the questions chosen by Lesante.

headline: MSNBC News Live
abstract: In an interview with MSNBC, Governor Ed Rendell criticized fellow Democrats for not speaking out about their legislative accomplishments, such as the passage of the health care law. Rendell also spoke about his time as chairman of the DNC.

headline: Amish eye loophole in health care proposals
abstract: The Pennsylvania Amish community is hopeful that they will be exempted from the individual mandate to purchase health-insurance coverage; the individual mandate is a feature of the health-care legislation currently under consideration in Congress.  According to representatives from the PA Department of Insurance, there is a religious exemption in the current legislation, and this exemption would apply to groups who believe--as do the Amish--that it is the duty of religious groups to provide for one another when they are sick.

headline: Forest City schools receive money for engineering curriculum
abstract: Forest City High School and Lakeland High School received donations from Lockheed Martin to start teaching engineering courses in high school. The program is called Project Lead the Way and includes courses focused on science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

headline: As obesity increases, so does challenge to EMS
abstract: The increase in obesity rates among adults in children in recent years has placed financial challenges on Emergency Medical Services teams and personnel as EMS crews attempt to outfit ambulances and equipment with enough  sustainability to care for obese patients. Retrofitting an ambulance, for example, may cost between $20,000 and $40,000, according to the PA Bureau of Emergency Medical Services.

headline: Ackerman gets $65,000 performance bonus
abstract: Philadelphia Schools Superintendent Arlene Ackerman has been awarded a $65,000 performance bonus, and official said Monday. Ackerman who was put in charge of the nation's eighth largest in June 2008, was awarded the bonus for exceeding all 21 benchmarks set out by the School Reform Commission.

headline: Artsfest was a big success and so was $5 fee
abstract: Support for the PA Council on the Arts has sank from $14.5 million last year to $9.5 million this year. At the Patriot News Artsfest they charged $5 for admission, which some people complained about. The fee was added due to decreased numbers in charitable donations also.

headline: U.S. Attorney nominee gets Senate judiciary approval
abstract: The US Senate Judiciary Committee this morning unanimously approved the nomination of David J. Hickton to be U.S. Attorney of Western Pennsylvania, moving the nomination to the Senate floor. Hickton who was nominated by US President Barack Obama to a four year term, could be confirmed by the full Senate as early as tonight.

headline: John Baer: Catch phrases often hide the truth in political ads
abstract: Campaign season is filled with political ads: Candidates offer themselves as saviors and portray opponents as leading us down the road to perdition. Ads in the U.S. Senate race, between Republican Pat Toomey and Democrat US Representative Joe Sestak for example, paint candidates as Wall Street patsies beholden to the evils of greed.

headline: Gas drilling helping airport attract passengers
abstract: Gas drilling in the Marcellus Shale formation has brought new passengers to the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport, filling the parking garage with energy company representatives' Texas and Oklahoma license plates, airport officials said at a meeting of the bi-county board of commissioners Thursday. Since June, about 20,000 passengers per month have flown through the airport. In the first nine months of 2010, just more than 160,000 people have flown through the airport, 1,300 more than for the same period in 2009.

headline: BBC World News America
abstract: The BBC’s website has full coverage of all the races, including the house and senate.

headline: Plans for Sparrowville Heritage Park in Old Forge to move forward in 2010
abstract: The Old Forge Coal Mine Group is raising money to develop the Sparrowville Heritage Park.  The park would help preserve the region's coal-mining history and would contain a restored mine car and mine tunnel.

headline: Gov’s Office Confirms: Rendell may single-handedly lease more state forest for drilling
abstract: Governor Rendell's office confirmed that the Governor plans to direct the director of the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources to lease more state forest land to Marcellus Shale natural gas drilling. Conservationists and environmentalists in the legislature say the governor promised to not open any more land in the 2010-2011 budget, which the governor's office said there was a two-year deal to lease land as part of the 2009-2010 budget agreement.

headline: Atlanta still the world's busiest airport, but Chicago is slipping
abstract: Atlanta International Airport is still ranked as the airport with the most traffic yearly but airports in Chicago and Los Angeles have lost passenger traffic in the past year while being surpassed by China's Beijing Capital Airport after Beijing's hosting of the Summer Olympics.

headline: Mistakes, little oversight cited for Philadelphia. VA prostate cancer treatment
abstract: University of Pennsylvania who performed prostate cancer procedures at the Philadelphia VA Medical Center from February 2002 to June 2008 made several mistakes during the six year period, and gave incorrect doses of radiation to 97 of 114 patients.  This according to a report done by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Inspector General's Office.

headline: Casinos prepping for the inevitable cheaters
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board has hired consultants to help them deal with cheating customers expected to come through the states casino's once table games opens up.

headline: In our five-county area, 29 percent of the bridges are rated structurally deficient
abstract: Over 76 bridges are considered to have serious deficiencies in the five-county Pittsburgh area, no rehabilitation or replacement projects are planned due to a lack of funds. PA Governor Ed Rendell will visiting Pittsburgh and other sites in Western Pennsylvania this week, as a part of his statewide tour to call attention to the funding shortfall and urge the Legislature to address it at a special session later this month.

headline: Christie to announce plan to fix $46 billion shortfall in public pension system
abstract: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie is expected to unveil his proposal to reform the public employee pension and health-care system this week. The governor has made clear that workers should expect cuts, which may include a rollback of a 9 percent pension increase granted in 2001. The official estimate of the state's public employee pension fund shortfall is $45.8 billion as of June 30, 2009, or more than $5,200 for every man, woman, and child.

headline: Challenger blasts Rep. Smith's tax woes
abstract: The Republican candidate for the 112th Legislative District seat blasted the Democratic incumbent, state Rep. Ken Smith, for failure to pay the tax obligations of the employees of his former restaurant. The longtime Smith's Restaurant in South Scranton was foreclosed on this summer after a series of financial woes. Since then, Mr. Smith, 49, of Dunmore, also has acknowledged he had not paid several payroll taxes for his employees, including unemployment compensation and personal income tax.

headline: Eyewitness News at 4:30am
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell opposed plans for a bike path in Ocean City, New Jersey. Gov. Rendell fears the bike paths will destroy the wetlands, which he says make New Jersey a special place. A group called Friends of the Wetland are trying to persuade city officials to abandon the plan.

headline: Kanjorski among top candidate spenders
abstract: According to data compiled by the Federal Election Commission (FEC), spending by House and Senate candidates declined in 2008; campaign contributions also declined in 2008.  Also, several local politicians made the FEC's top 50 list for various categories; the categories listed are top spenders, highest debts owed and most cash-on-hand.

headline: Obama proposal targets insurance-rate increases
abstract: The Obama administration said it would call for new government power to protect against health insurance rate increases in its healthcare proposal. The legislation would give US Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius the power to curb rate increases and would also create a Health Insurance Rate Authority to monitor increases. Congress is also preparing for the president's healthcare summit.

headline: Make tax system more equitable for all Pa. families
abstract: The author, of the Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center, states that Pennsylvania is a state with a regressive tax structure that should be changed. They proposed a graduated earned income tax, with a higher tax on unearned income, closing the corporate tax loophole, and ceasing to give tax exemptions on certain items.

headline: Remnant of the recession: Frugality grips consumers
abstract: The new AP Economy Survey which asked 44 leading economists whether the recession created a new frugality among consumers that will outlive the recession, two thirds said yes. Experts credit this new sense of frugality to the fact that consumers lost so much household wealth that they have become much more cautious about their spending, this means the economic rebound will be sluggish.

headline: Deadly crash by state police officer involved alcohol
abstract: Cpl. John Quigg Jr. was reported to have a blood alcohol content three times the legal limit when he drove into head-on traffic on the Schuylkill Expressway killing himself and injuring another driver. Quigg was expected to go to court for another alcohol related driving incident before he perished.

headline: Hatchet job: A political report mischaracterizes the T extension
abstract: US Republican Senators John McCain and Tom Coburn are advocating against the recently signed $862 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. The senators support an economic report that claims, "after eighteen months since the law's passage, millions of jobs are still gone and the economy is as uncertain as ever."

headline: JCB reform bill sensible
abstract: The Luzerne County's juvenile justice scandal has challenged the credibility of the court system not only through Luzerne County but at the PA Supreme Court blithely level as well. A subsequent investigation by a specially created agency, the Interbranch Commission on Juvenile Justice, clearly exposed the failures of key components of the Luzerne County system and of the state Supreme Court's apparatus for judicial discipline the Judicial Conduct Board.

headline: Racing, casino project bought
abstract: A new company owns the proposed Valley View Downs harness-racing track and casino project, which began in Beaver County early this decade and bounced to Lawrence County before becoming bogged down in bankruptcy. American Harness Tracks LLC, which lists an address as 241 Fourth Ave., Downtown, bought the project with a winning bid of $5.6 million, Centaur Gaming of Indianapolis said Friday. Centaur was forced to sell after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2009.

headline: Jansing and Co.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is asked to comment on the senate race between republican Pat Toomey and Democrat Joe Sestak. Rendell says democrats have done a poor job reminding voters of what they’ve accomplished.

headline: Nutter to focus on increasing college admissions
abstract: In an effort to help more Philadelphia residents attend college, Mayor Michael nutter plans to open a "PhillyGoes2College" office in City Hall.  The office will help residents with college aid forms, applications, SAT prep and essay writing.  Additionally, the mayor will seek 1,000 fully-funded college scholarships for city students.

headline:
Winter Classic: Is hockey in PNC Park's future?
Penguins-Capitals matchup would be a hit at PNC Park
abstract: Pittsburgh Pirates Team President Frank Coonelly has been in discussions with the NHL to bring the Winter Classic to Pittsburgh in 2011. The matchup would be between the Penguins and the Washington Capitals if Cooney gets his way.

headline: Joint effort: The city and county must take bigger steps
abstract: The author states that City of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County are taking too long to consolidate the two local governments into one entity. The author applauds the decision to share a software platform but notes that the city wouldn't have to come up with more taxes if they consolidated the county and city governments.

headline: Outsiders join in 12th district House race
abstract: With polls proclaiming a virtual dead heat just two weeks before the election, the two front-runners in the race for Pennsylvania's 12th Congressional District. Republican Tim Burns of Eighty Four, announced Monday that U.S. Sen. Scott Brown of Massachusetts will campaign with him May 14 in Washington, Pa. Democrat Mark Critz of Johnstown will be joined by West Virginia Gov. Joe Manchin at an event today in Washington, PA.

headline: Operation Broken Dreams nabs mortgage scammers
abstract: The Justice Department said they have made more than 500 arrests since March as part of their national effort to crackdown on mortgage fraud. The operation, called Operation Broken Dreams, involved 1,215 criminal defendants in cases that uncovered $2.3 billion in losses, according to Attorney General Eric Holder.

headline: Grand jury indicts former lobbyist
abstract: A federal grand jury Thursday indicted ex-lobbyist Paul Magliocchetti on charges that he funneled hundreds of thousands of illegal campaign donations to a number of House members whom he relied for millions in defense earmarks for his clients. This follows allegations of influence peddling and "pay to play" politics in the Capitol that enveloped a group of powerful House members, including the late US Representative John P. Murtha, D-Johnstown.

headline: Allegheny Energy jobs to be preserved in Westmoreland
abstract: FirstEnergy Corp. has made a five-year commitment to keep 600 or more jobs in Westmoreland County as part of its proposed merger with Greensburg-based Allegheny Energy. The agreement signed by both companies and 18 parties who objected to the merger establishes a minimum requirement of jobs in Westmoreland County over the next five years.

headline: Face the Nation
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is asked to comment on what appeared to be a surge in republican support in the weeks leading up to the election.

headline: Fayette approves across-the-board raises for workers
abstract: On Monday, the Fayette County Salary Board approved 1,000 dollar pay raises for all of the county's nonunion employees.

headline:
The stimulus: One year later
Pennsylvania is on track to receive more than $26 billion from the recovery act
abstract: Governor Rendell lauded the now year-old federal stimulus package saying it has created jobs for the commonwealth. Pennsylvania will receive $26 billion in funds from the package. 362 infrastructure projects have been started totaling $800 million. Republican Governor candidate and PA Attorney General Tom Corbett said the plan has done little to alleviate unemployment. Money is also being used for homelessness, and workforce investment.

headline: What the health-care overhaul would do
abstract: A health economist from the University of Pennsylvania and a professor of law and public health explain the changes to the insurance industry should the federal healthcare reform bill be passed.

headline: Drilling companies eye sites near water sources
abstract: Pennsylvania American Water Co. spokesman Terry Maenza said the company is having dialogue with the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection and will do water testing to ensure the quality of the Huntsville Reservoir, which is near the companies planned natural gas drilling site. The Huntsville and Ceasetown reservoirs, serve approximately 100,000 Pennsylvania.

headline: Stu Bykofsky: Parking Authority scoots into parking-zone confusion
abstract: Philadelphia Parking Authority officials were uninformed about the guidelines as to where scooters can park in the city, resulting in numerous fines where parkers thought they were legally parked. It is revealed that the rules changed for scooter parking without many people knowing. The author states that the PPA created motorcycle meter spots but never let people effectively know.

headline: State lawmakers receptive to idea of expanded ethics panel
abstract: A bipartisan group of PA state legislators last week proposed forming a Public Integrity Commission, which would become a statewide law enforcement agency investigating allegations of unethical behavior in all branches of Pennsylvania government. The proposal is a response to 29 cases of confirmed and alleged public corruption at the local, state and federal levels since mid-2008. PA Attorney General Tom Corbett sees this as a positive step.

headline: Allegheny Energy profits surge on higher power usage, rate increase
abstract: Allegheny Energy Inc. said today its higher net income for the third quarter of $115.1 million, or 68 cents a share, was the result of an increase in customer usage and a rate increase in West Virginia.

headline: SportsCenter
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell called the decision to postpone the Sunday night game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Minnesota Vikings a "joke".

headline: Phila. officer to be stripped of badge for killing unarmed man
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey announced that Frank Tepper, the off-duty police officer who shot and killed an unarmed man last November, will be stripped of his badge.  Tepper may also face criminal charges, as District Attorney R. Seth Williams plans to review the case file to see if further actions should be taken.

headline: CPAC straw poll: 2 percent support Santorum as GOP candidate in '12
abstract: A poll taken of members of the Conservative Political Action Conference said that 2% supported former US Senator Rick Santorum for the Republican Presidential Candidate in 2012.  Santorum attacked the Obama administration's policies on national security and the economy.

headline: Stu Bykofsky: Health care and a surprise for Dad
abstract: The author talks about how the American Association of Retired Persons alienated it's members during the federal healthcare reform debate, causing conservatives to join the American Seniors Association and liberals to join the Alliance for Retired Americans.

headline: Park decision heads to Senate
abstract: On Friday, the Crossing Legacy Foundation, the Coryell's Ferry Militia and other re-enactor groups  displayed an oversized check for $1 million made out to the Pennsylvania Museum Commission. This was in response to the Pennsylvania House on Tuesday voting to approve a bill that would transfer 137 acres of Washington Crossing Historic Park to a private entity.

headline: Editorial: Misleading labels
abstract: The US Food and Drug Administration has banned cigarette companies from labeling light or low-tar cigarettes as such. The cigarette companies now have now relabeled the cigarettes by color-coding them which the author and some believe is still promoting the message that some cigarettes are less of a health risk than others. The author states that the FDA needs to keep one step ahead of the tobacco industry's attempts to sell cigarettes.

headline: Disabilities can be overcome when it comes to casting ballot
abstract: Three Rivers Center for Independent Living in Pittsburgh, is one of more than 300 agencies countywide required to offer voter registration opportunities to clients. The National Voter Registration Act of 1993 requires public assistance agencies to provide voter registration forms when someone applies for services, re-applies or changes an address.

newspaper: CNN - National Programming (Cable News Network) Cable
headline: More patients turning to ER for acute care
abstract: Dr. Stephen Pitts, lead author of the report: Where Americans Get Acute Care, says patients have observed the fact that primary care physicians just don't have time for unscheduled visits, and sometimes the emergency room is the only option. The study released by the American College of Emergency Physicians, says even acute problems can become potentially serious, so getting timely care is crucial. The report analyzed more than 380,000 medical records between 2001 and 2004, and compared where people went to be treated for everything from chest pains to sinus problems.

headline: Mortgage foreclosures continue to rise in region
abstract: Third-quarter foreclosures in the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre/Hazleton metropolitan area jumped 12.8 percent over the same 2009 period, according to RealtyTrac, a Los Angeles-area business that compiles foreclosure statistics. The advance, though, represents a retreat from the first half of the year, when regional foreclosure filings jumped 74 percent, according to RealtyTrac. Statewide, foreclosure filings increased more than 18 percent for the quarter, although Pennsylvania ranked 33rd in activity.

headline: News Channel 4 at 5pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has made plans to speak at a fundraiser in Omaha, benefitting the Nebraska Democratic Party.

headline: Comitta becomes borough's 1st female mayor
abstract: On Monday, Carolyn Comitta was sworn in as mayor of the West Chester Borough.  Comitta will serve as the Borough's 58th mayor and pledges to help make West Chester safe, clean and green.

headline: Jury in Mike Veon trial issues mixed verdict, convicts Veon of 14 of 59 counts
abstract: Former PA Representative Mike Veon was convicted on 14 of the 59 counts he faced as part of the "bonusgate" scandal. His aide Annamarie Peretta-Rosepink was convicted of 5 counts; Brett Cott was guilty of 3 counts, while the fourth defendant, Steve Keefer, was acquitted of all counts.

headline: State budget deficit tops $1 billion
abstract: The projected deficit for the fiscal year 2009-2010 stood at $720 million a month ago, now the projected deficit has risen to $1 billion. The announcement was made Monday by Pennsylvania Senator Jake Corman, R-Center, chairman of the Senate Appropriations Committee. Governor Ed Rendell had proposed spending $29.1 billion in fiscal 2010-11, but to do so would require serious tax increases.

headline: Charters get nice surprise: Renewal, expansion Oks
abstract: The School Reform Commission voted to approve the expansion of a number of charter schools and to renew the charters that were expected to end at the end of the school year. This comes after the commission said it would delay its vote to August but action by the Pennsylvania Coalition of Public Charter Schools made phone calls complaining that schools and parents could not prepare for the school year if the commission waited until August to make the decision.

headline: Pennsylvania budget hole hinges on Medicaid funding
abstract: PA state legislative leaders and PA Governor Ed Rendell are awaiting a US Senate vote that will determine how much states get in extra Medicaid money. The $28 billion state budget passed on June 30 is dependent on $850 million in Medicaid money. Rendell has said thousands of state and local officials might be laid off to balance the budget if that federal money does not come through.

headline: Panel considers regional pipeline control
abstract: The PA House Consumer Affairs Committee will take testimony on a measure to create an interstate compact involving Pennsylvania and one or two other states with authority to approve or reject applications to expand pipeline to accommodate development of Marcellus Shale gas deposits. The proposed Mid-Atlantic Area Natural Gas Interstate Compact would be run by a council of respective state officials, state lawmakers, conservation district officials, local officials and business and housing industry representatives.

headline: Auditor: Pa. missing 1,800 historic artifacts
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner says more than 1,800 items from the state's collection of historic artifacts are missing and likely lost forever because of mishandling or theft.

headline: Excerpts from Pa. government transition reports
abstract: The Rendell administration has provided Gov.-elect Tom Corbett a small sampling from the state government agency transition reports. The reports include information on administration, transportation, agriculture, banking, budget, and community and economic development, and other topics.

headline: Pennsylvania tax revenue down more than $2 billion
abstract: According to a U.S. Census Bureau Report, Pennsylvania state tax revenue has decreased since last year.  The decrease in revenue is the result of Pennsylvania residents earning and spending less.

headline: Troopers Association says staffing could be problem in state
abstract: The state may be short of the adequate number of state troopers on duty because of an abnormal number of retirements, a small class of newly graduated cadets, and no funding in the 2009-2010 state budget for hiring new cadets. The Pennsylvania State Troopers Association said that Governor Rendell's allocation of $5.1 million in 2010-2011 for trooper hiring is not sufficient.

headline: Mayor chats up Harrisburg on options for raising taxes
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl met with members of the state house of representatives to come up with proposals to shore up Pittsburgh's "legacy" problems and pension fund. The city needs a one-time lump sum of $200 million along with $15 million in recurring revenue. The city has proposed a 2-cent per ounce soda tax, a rise in city services fee, and a raise in the payroll preparation tax for non-profits.

headline: Private investors needed to help fund transportation improvements, Pennsylvania officials say
abstract: After the federal government rejected a plan to toll Interstate 80 last month, Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell called on state lawmakers to hold a special session on financing transportation needs. In order to fill the $472 million hole in the 2010-2011 budget, ideas are circulating through the capital such as leasing the turnpike or other state roads to a private company.

headline: Chester County kennel where Biden bought dog found not guilty of violations
abstract: The Chester County Kennel where Vice President Joe Biden bought his dog was found not guilty of a third dog law violation. The owners said they were unfairly targeted by state regulators ever since Biden bought his dog from them. The PA Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement said they were waiting for the conclusion of the hearing to see whether or not to take future action against the kennel owners.

headline: Traders' faith in market revives
abstract: The stock market began August with a huge rally after reports from around the world revived investors' faith in the global recovery. The first day of the month brought a stream of news that reassured investors who have worried about a slowing of economic growth in the United States, China and Europe. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 208 points Monday to its highest close in three months.

headline: PA Senate Race: Sestak vs. Toomey
abstract: Earmarks have suddenly become a banner issue in the Pennsylvania US Senate race between US Representative Joseph Sestak, D-Edgemont, and former US Representative Pat Toomey-R, of Zionsville. The US House of Representatives has put a moratorium on earmark requests that would go to for-profit companies in the next fiscal year. Disclosure requirements for earmarks have only recently been instituted.

headline: Approval of electricity contracts gives boroughs more options
abstract: PA legislators unanimously approved a bill allowing boroughs to participate in power supply and electricity generation projects, according to state Senator Mike Brubaker, R-Lititz. Amendments to Senate Bill 168 legislation intended to secure affordable and reliable energy for consumers were voted on last week by the Senate and will take effect pending Governor Ed Rendell’s approval. Under a take-or-pay contract, a buyer or borough would agree to pay some fixed amount even if that product is not provided.

headline: Christie administration blames Corzine on charters
abstract: The Christie administration is attributing the failure to win a federal grant for charter school start-ups to a weak and understaffed state charter operation it says it inherited from Gov. Corzine. Democratic leaders criticized Gov. Christie after the state’s failed bid for $14 million in education funds was made public by The Inquirer. According to state officials, the state plans on reapplying for the grant.

headline: Suburban hospitals forced to be competitive
abstract: The proliferation of advanced specialty medical care is putting pressure on suburban hospitals to expand and add profitable services and the latest technologies.  This growing demand has caused some suburban hospitals to forge alliances with larger academic hospitals.

headline: Seatbelt use in Pa. below other states
abstract: Pennsylvania has a seatbelt use rate of 85.1%, lower than states that have primary seatbelt laws.  The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety said that campaigns to encourage seatbelt use are effective but should be more aggressive.

headline: Area seniors find resources to help them stay active
abstract: Senior citizens are offered many activities to keep their mind and body in good condition through local nonmedical home assistance providers that assist seniors in mind and body exercises.

headline: Ed Rendell rarely slows down, as our Dennis Owens learned this week
abstract: Dennis Owens of WHTM (ABC) was granted behind the scenes access to follow Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell on his day to day activities, over the span of a week.

headline: Philadelphia's top teacher again from Bodine High School
abstract: A teacher for the Bodine High School for International Affairs has won the Ruth Wright Hayre Teacher of the Year award for the third year in a row. Technology and Business teacher Aaron Greberman won the award this year. The award is given out by the School District of Philadelphia.

headline: Brewing to resume in Latrobe
abstract: City Brewing Co. will temporarily resume operations today at its Latrobe, PA plant, where production was halted earlier this week as a result of complaints of a foul odor. Officials from the PA Department of Environmental Protection requested the company halt production Tuesday night as a result of the odor.

headline: Trustees, insurer sue Harrisburg Authority, city over incinerator debt
abstract: TD Bank, a trustee on the 2007 bonds on the Harrisburg incinerator, is suing in Dauphin County court to try to force the Harrisburg city treasurer to forward nearly $35 million for a debt payment due Dec. 15.

headline: For governor, Dan Onorato
abstract: Pennsylvania's next governor will have to deal with a systemic budget deficit, a feckless state Legislature, a poisonous political environment, unresolved funding for roads and transit due to the failure of the Interstate 80 toll plan, a ticking public pension time bomb, and a host of other issues amid a struggling economy. The Times-Tribune editorial board endorses Democrat Dan Onorato, chief executive of Allegheny County, to take on those daunting issues.

headline: Put wine on shelves
abstract: Author suggests the state allow supermarkets to carry wine on their shelves due to the failure of state-run kiosks. The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board was recently forced to shut down wine vending kiosks in 30 supermarkets across the state due to mechanical and technological problems.

headline: SEA approves construction of Maz statue at PNC Park
abstract: The City-Allegheny County Sports & Exhibition Authority board passed the building of a statue of Bill Mazeroski outside of PNC Park in Pittsburgh. The Pirates will be responsible for building and maintaining the statue.

headline: Gas drilling watchdog process clearly in place
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection called out the natural gas industry for a foamy discharged found in water in Cummings Township which Pennsylvania General Energy called a reaction from a soap used to purify water. The author states that environmental regulatory oversight is ample and that the state should not bulk up their environmental oversight in order to not strangulate the industry.

headline: Governor Rendell says the state government is leasing more public forest land
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell said that a petroleum company will pay Pennsylvania 120 million dollars for the right to drill on 33 thousand acres of forest land. As a result the Governor says he will be supporting legislation to temporarily halt additional leasing of land for gas drilling.

headline:
Obama: 'Reckless' BP to pay
He sought to reassure the nation while offering few new specifics. A U.S. panel, meanwhile, says more oil is leaking than earlier thought.
abstract: US President Obama has said that he will make British Petroleum pay for damages to the Gulf of Mexico that happened as a result of oil that has been spilling into the waters there. A government panel of scientists said that the spill was spilling more than previously thought. President Obama also urged Americans to adopt his energy and climate-change legislation.

headline: Western Pennsylvania political powers long in a family way
abstract: PA Senator Jay Costa's decision to seek the Senate Democrats' top leadership post next year highlights the political clout clustered in a few Western Pennsylvania bloodlines. Most of the powerful families are Democrats, since the party that has dominated regional politics for decades.

headline: Work force: Pennsylvania should keep Industry Partnerships
abstract: A Pennsylvania program, backed by business and labor called Industry Partnerships helps industries identify their training needs and communicate that to education partners. They, in turn, develop and deliver the training, creating job applicants who show up ready to work with the desired skills. The idea began under Governor Richard Schweiker and came to fruition under Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Holden for Congress: He strives to look for practical solutions
abstract: U.S. Representative Tim Holden has held his seat since 2002 when the Republican-controlled state Legislature gerrymandered his district in expectation he would lose to George Gekas, the long-serving Republican congressman from Harrisburg. State Senator Dave Argall, his challenger, for the 17th Congressional District, is a smart and worthy opponent. He has served in the state House and Senate and been involved in key issues, including recently chairing a committee looking at ways to cut state spending.

headline: State police report: More killed, injured in 2010 holiday crashes
abstract: According to the Pennsylvania State Police, more people were killed and injured in crashes over the 2010 four-day holiday travel period than in 2009.

headline: Census Bureau officials talk to Pennsylvania legislators
abstract: In order to get the most complete and comprehensive count possible, the U.S. Census Bureau is partnering with several organizations and institutions in Pennsylvania.  Census Bureau officials met with members of the state Republican and Democratic House policy committees on Monday.

headline: Pa. candidates for governor asked about ex-inmate programs
abstract: An ex-inmate group called X-Offenders for Community Empowerment asked a panel of PA gubernatorial candidates what they would do to ensure that jobs and counseling were available to those coming out of jail. Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato, Montgomery County Commissioner Joe Hoeffel, State Auditor General Jack Wagner, and PA State Representative Sam Rohrer were in attendance.

headline: PV poetry reader is the state's best
abstract: Pleasant Valley High School senior Angela Goldberg won the state level competition of the 2010 Poetry Out Loud competition for her reciting of three poems. She will now compete in Washington, D.C. for the national title.

headline: Two sitting senators may fail to get their party's nomination
abstract: When interviewed today making rounds at Philadelphia area diners Joe Sestak said U.S. Senator Arlen Spector D-Pennsylvania should be respected for his service to his state and country, but after switching parties just before an election because he couldn't win a Republican primary cannot be trusted.

headline: Pa. budget vote pulled as House members disagree on gas tax
abstract: Efforts to adopt a state budget were stalled after a $320 million tax proposal by House Democrats was sent back to the Appropriations committee. The package included a tax on Marcellus shale extracts. The Marcellus Shale Coalition opposes a tax on the extracts by saying it would cause drillers to go elsewhere. Members of the Democratic delegation have differing views on where gas tax revenues should be allocated.

headline: Gas drillers pile up rule violations
abstract: In the last 2 1/2 years, drilling companies were cited for 1,435 violations, 952 of which were considered most likely to harm the environment, according to a report by the Pennsylvania Land Trust. Nearly half of the violations were related to improper erosion and sedimentation plans and improper construction of wastewater impoundments that contain fracking water.

headline: A group mobilizes for a City Council race
abstract: Anthony Coghill, 43, didn't feel he needed help from Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and his allies to win a 2009 council race in the city's South Hills. But as he faced a three-way Democratic primary that also included Patrick Reilly and Natalia Rudiak, he decided he may need some help with fundraising. The support he got provides a window into the political operations of part of an informal business network that has been deeply involved in the region's governance.

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell: Less aggressive agendas for Corbett, Onorato mean they could be successful at reforming state government
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said gubernatorial candidates Dan Onorato and Tom Corbett might have "the political capital" to convince lawmakers to go along with government reforms that have previously failed, because the men don't have the kind of aggressive policy agenda Rendell had when he took office in 2003.

headline: Harveys Lake OKs budget with millage hike
abstract: Harveys Lake council unanimously approved the borough’s $1,334,267 budget which will raise the millage rate from .604 to .704. Also included in the budget is a $50 fee for a curbside garbage and recycling program.

headline: Compromise emerging on table games as layoffs loom
abstract: Spokespersons for the PA Senate and House say that a bill allowing poker, blackjack, roulette and other table games at Pennsylvania's slot machine casinos could be sent to a joint House-Senate conference committee today.  Governor Rendell has said that failure to pass gaming legislation would result in 1,000 state layoffs.

headline: A $128 million allocation will expand area's broadband Internet access for schools, public safety facilities
abstract: The Keystone Initiative for Network Based Education and Research received $99 million to develop a 1,700-mile fiber optic network across Pennsylvania. $28.7 million will be used to connect more isolated, mountainous regions of Pennsylvania. US Senators Arlen Specter and Bob Casey announced the funding which was allocated by the US Department of Commerce.

headline: Ex-lawmaker's wife sentenced regarding Beaver nonprofit
abstract: Wife of former PA Senator Gerald LaValle, Darla LaValle, was sentenced with four years of probation after she pleaded no contest as part of a plea deal for charges that she gave herself an excess salary and failed to pay benefits to two employees while she ran a nonprofit in Beaver County. The nonprofit was called Voluntary Action Center of Beaver County.

headline: Sestak trails Toomey by two points in a potential matchup
abstract: Looking towards the upcoming primary election those inside democratic circles are split on who they would support to give them the best chance to win U.S. Senator Arlen Specter's D-Pennsylvania's seat. The president has not formally thrown his support for either Specter or his opponent in the primary Joe Sestak.

headline: Rudiak aims to boost public input on projects
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilwoman Natalia Rudiak introduced a bill called the "Neighborhoods First Capital Budget Reform Act" which would require the city to re-establish a six-year capital plan. The bill states that the mayor and city council would hold meetings twice a year to get input on capital projects. It would also stop "hidden money" from lying in unused capital project accounts.

headline: Road paint drying up
abstract: Contractors and municipalities are having trouble completing road painting projects thanks to a national shortage of the special paint used to mark highways and roadways. Doug Dolinar, general manager of Souderton-based Guidemark Inc., one of the state's largest traffic-marking companies, says a shortage of these supplies can have serious consequences. PA Department of Transportation receives 80 percent of the supplies and independent contractors are left with the rest.

headline: Market costs, not just fares
abstract: Lehigh Valley, Philadelphia and Newark airports all draw significant numbers of travelers from the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton area. Thousands of those travelers every year drive past the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport on Interstate 81 and the Pennsylvania Turnpike, en route to the other airports.

headline: Gov. Rendell will slap moratorium on new Marcellus Shale gas drilling on state land
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell sought to restart talks over a natural gas extraction tax Monday, a day before he was poised to issue an executive order banning any further leasing of state forest land for Marcellus Shale drilling. Rendell said Monday he wants Republicans who control the state Senate to resume negotiations over a prospective tax on the drilling.

headline: Fox 29 News at 11am
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell fueled controversy after a phone interview with Fox29 in which he called the decision to postpone the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Minnesota Viking a “joke”. The game was postponed due to snow.

headline: D.A.'s pick for top detective oversaw 'Tainted' unit
abstract: Christopher M. Werner, a former Philadelphia police captain, was named the chief of county detectives yesterday.  District Attorney Seth Williams' appointment of Werner is controversial, as Werner is at the center of an FBI corruption investigation.  After a close review of Werner's personal file, however, District Attorney Williams said there is nothing that prevents Werner from being the best person for the job.

headline: Jesse Jackson addresses student violence in Phila.
abstract: The Reverend Jesse Jackson visited students to talk about school violence in Philadelphia. He said that a focus on education was a means to stopping school violence. He also encouraged parents and faith-based organizations to get involved with the city's youth. Philadelphia Schools Superintendent Arlene Ackerman was also in attendance.

headline: Meadows' dealer hopefuls to be schooled on technique
abstract: Managers of the Meadows Racetrack and Casinos are training dealers ahead of the enactment of legalized table games. The dealer classes are free and each student that graduates will receive a certificate from the Community College of Beaver County.

headline: Privacy concerns worry some users of Facebook
abstract: The internet has been flooded with stories this week about people who have or are planning to leave the world's largest social networking site Facebook. The reason is that user privacy has been incrementally decreased over the past five years, causing many people to get fed up with the site.

headline: As Others See It: Obamacare will force the U.S. to steal doctors from countries that desperately need them
abstract: An author in Foreign Policy magazine wrote that the health care reform act will cause doctors to move to America from other countries that need doctors. The author states that US President Barack Obama's plan would move doctors overseas to reach the rising demand to cover an extra 32 million people.

headline: Can Tom Corbett keep his no-tax pledge?
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett has taken significant criticism for his pledge to not raise taxes if elected governor. Corbett's chief critic is Allegheny County executive Dan Onorato, who hasn’t ruled out raising taxes to fill a budget gap expected to be as high as $5 billion next year. PA Senate Republican Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi does not believe that Corbett will be able to keep his pledge.

headline: Urban issues put on table
abstract: U.S. Senate candidate Joe Sestak and Dave Argall, a Republican state senator challenging U.S. Representative Tim Holden in the 17th House District, appeared at the fifth Blueprint for Prosperity forum Tuesday at the Midtown Scholar Bookstore in Harrisburg to address election issues. Representatives of state gubernatorial candidates Tom Corbett and Dan Onorato also spoke on state issues. Earlier forums have tackled economics, education and crime.

newspaper: FNC - National Programming (Fox News Channel) Cable
headline: Happening Now
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell considers the decision to postpone a game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Minnesota Vikings a mistake, since mass transit options were available during the inclement weather.

headline: Bill gives casinos all of the cards
abstract: Senate Bill 711, which would allow the state's slots parlors to offer table games, is likely to pass this week.  The bill goes far beyond legalizing blackjack and poker, however, and gives casinos the tools and power they need create larger pools of addicted gamblers.  If this legislation passes, Philadelphians should place blame on their local representatives.

headline: Carlisle lawyer Stephen Bloom to run for 199th House District seat
abstract: Stephen Bloom, a North Middleton Township attorney and a Republican announced he will run for the 199th state House District seat being vacated by PA State Representative Will Gabig.

headline: City's computer network is in line for a makeover
abstract: The city of Philadelphia will invest $120 million over six years to revamp and centralize the city's Information Technology system. Allan Frank, Chief Technology Officer of Philadelphia, will be the leader of the process which is meant to save the city money by being more efficient and using less paper.

headline: Some find Pennsylvania's tax amnesty ads too scary
abstract: Critics say Pennsylvania's TV and radio campaign offering amnesty to the state's tax "scofflaws" is over the edge. However the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue says it had no choice but to get tough with the people and businesses that owe it millions of dollars. The amnesty program which began last month and will run until June 18 hopes $190 million in back taxes.

headline:
Unemployment rate up despite new jobs
State's economy added 19,500 jobs in May
abstract: Despite Pennsylvania adding 19,500 new jobs in May the unemployment rate rose .1% to 9.1%. PA Gov. Rendell said the state has added 76,200 jobs in the last 3 months, the most of any state besides Texas. According to the PA Department of Labor and Industry report said that jobs that produce goods decreased while more people worked for the government which was attributed to the hiring of census workers.

headline: Culture Fest set to open on Friday
abstract: Dauphin County will host its annual free, open-air festival celebrating cultural diversity from 5 to 10 p.m. Friday in downtown Harrisburg.

headline: Activists ask council to ban gas drilling in Pittsburgh
abstract: Worried that Marcellus shale drilling could contaminate water sources and contribute to poor air quality in the city, environmental activists filled Pittsburgh City Council chambers last night to voice their concern. About 120 people attended a public hearing held at the request of a petition by city residents. The hearing followed a half-hour protest on the steps of the City-County Building, Downtown.

headline: Counties get $20k grant to start autism center
abstract: The PA Department of Community and Economic Development has agreed to front a one-time grant to help build the infrastructure for the Autism Information Resource Center, said Lackawanna county Director of Human Services Teresa Osborne. Lackawanna County Commissioners approved a plan to use a $20,000 state grant to create an eight-county "clearinghouse" for resources related to autism.

headline: WBRZ News 2 Louisiana at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the country has become a “nation of wusses” after the NFL’s decision to postpone a game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Minnesota Vikings.

headline: Meehan gets a jump on campaign-finance report
abstract: Patrick L. Meehan says he has raised 790,000 dollars since his candidacy announcement on September 14th.  Meehan, a former U.S. Attorney, is a Republican candidate for Congress in the Western Suburbs.

headline: Bonusgate trial witness says campaign work was common in Rep. Mike Veon's office
abstract: Karen Steiner Blanar, a staffer for former PA State Representative Mike Veon, testified in the public corruption trial of Veon and three of her former co-workers on the staff. She said that she sent out mailings, and went over opponents' nominating petitions, and that working on campaigns was a normal part of her day as a legislative staffer.

headline: Gov. Christie signs pension cuts into law
abstract: NJ Governor Chris Christie signed into law three bills that would save $8 billion over 15 years. The bills cut pension increases to state workers by 9%, will mandate contributions of 1.5% to health benefits, and would cap payouts for unused sick time at $15,000. The bill only applies to new hires.

headline: Climate bill lacks support of GOP
abstract: U.S. Senator Kerry, D-Mass., and U.S. Senator Joe Lieberman, I-Conn in a last-ditch attempt sought to gain republican support to pass the American Power Act which the two co-wrote. The act which puts a price on carbon and creates a tightly regulated cap-and-trade market in which about 7,500 manufacturers and utility companies swap the right to pollute, fell through when talks with Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C. reached an endpoint.

headline: Pa. bill pushes to end gun permit 'loophole'
abstract: PA Rep. Bryan Lentz of Delaware County has introduced a bill to be heard in front of the PA House Judiciary Committee that would bar Pennsylvania citizens from obtaining concealed gun licenses from other states. Lentz said that people who were being denied licenses in Pennsylvania were still obtaining them from other states like Florida. Discussions are being held with the National Rifle Association.

headline: All quiet on the Harrisburg front
abstract: Harrisburg, PA Mayor Linda Thompson and City Council  are facing a financial crisis and have yet to produce a viable plan.

headline: Natural gas stations in Western Pennsylvania's future
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) awarded Equitable Gas a $700,000 grant to build a public natural gas refueling station by the end of March at a yet-to-be-determined location in Western PA. The grants aim to stimulate interest in natural gas vehicles, which officials say put out fewer emissions than gasoline-powered vehicles and are cheaper to fill up.

headline: Republican candidate for U.S. Senate Pat Toomey promises to end bailouts
abstract: If elected, Republican Pat Toomey vowed to put an end to budget deficits and taxpayer-funded bailouts of industries and promised to vote against proposals such as cap and trade, which he said would cripple the state’s coal and natural gas industries.

headline: WHP CBS 21 Morning News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's office says he plans to issue clemency orders today for three convicted killers. All three were found guilty in separate slayings during the 1970s.

headline: Free vaccine on offer at end of week
abstract: A spokesperson for the PA Department of Health said that everyone, not just those in high-risk groups, should get vaccinated for the H1N1 virus.  On Friday and Saturday, the Department of Health will offer free vaccinations at several locations throughout the state.

headline:
Finance report shows city has $8.6M surplus
But surpluses get smaller every year
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh posted a net surplus of $8.6 million in 2009, lower than the $31 million surplus in 2008. The city says they are trying to mitigate or reverse the effects of the recession on their surpluses. The city saved money by reducing spending on fringe benefits and salaries, but lost revenue through cancelled state funding and reduced tax collections.

headline:
Corbett pits Pa. against health plan
Republicans across the country are gathering forces and launching efforts to nullify the legislation
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett is posed to file suit against the Obama Administration over the constitutionality of the federal healthcare reform act which is pending passage in the US Senate after passing the US House of Representatives. Corbett is unsure of how the legal challenge will look like but the challenge will come in the form of alleging that the law oversteps its powers over interstate commerce in the commerce clause and that it infringes on states' rights not left to the federal government.

headline: Sestak gains against Toomey in possible Nov. matchup
abstract: U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak, who has narrowed the gap against Sen. Arlen Specter in the Pennsylvania Democratic Senate primary, is gaining against likely Republican candidate Pat Toomey, a poll released this morning shows. Mr. Sestak trails Mr. Toomey, 42 to 40 percent, compared to a 42 to 34 percent lead Mr. Toomey held in an April 8.

headline: Disagreements delay proposed Marcellus Shale gas tax
abstract: Disagreements over how to tax Marcellus Shale extracts has stalled the passage of a bill in the PA legislature that would tax the natural resource. There have been many propositions like taxing at a  percentage the value of gas that comes from a wellhead while taxing  per thousand cubic feet of gas extracted. Legislators also differ on how gas tax revenues should be spent. The gas industry is against the tax while environmental groups support a tax.

headline: West Perry board drops the ball
abstract: The West Perry School Board voted this week to make all fall sports coaches "volunteers," however school rules require a paid supervisor of any volunteers. As a result with less than two weeks to go until fall sports are supposed to begin practicing, West Perry effectively has no coaches and no fall sports teams.

headline: Severance-tax pitfalls
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Legislature have decided to levy a tax on Marcellus shale gas production in an effort to close deficits in the budget that was passed at the deadline in late June. Development of the Marcellus shale formation is in its infancy, a tax at this point would discourage continued development.

headline: Mayor's parking plan shot down
abstract: After months of impassioned debate, Pittsburgh City Council rejected Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's $452 million parking lease plan with little comment Tuesday and spent part of the afternoon discussing an alternative pension bailout designed to keep parking garages and meters under public management. Officials said the alternative plan would allow for more modest parking rates than Mr. Ravenstahl proposed, concentrate all city-related parking assets in the hands of the city parking authority and provide money to upgrade parking garages and meters.

headline: Census sampling turns up many quirks
abstract: A survey of Census estimates by the American Community Survey may contain large margins of error. The estimates made by the survey are drawn from small samples and only serve as big picture indicators. The American Community Survey was created to replace the old long-form questionnaire that one-sixth of households filled out for the decennial census

headline: More aid available for heat program
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that those qualifying for Pennsylvania's Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) will receive 100 dollars more than anticipated.  The governor said that more monies could become available for assistance if Congress releases contingency funds for the program; there was a 55 million dollar reduction in federal funding for state LIHEAP programs this year.

headline: State Internet projects win $130 million in funding
abstract: The federal Broadband Technology Opportunities Program announced that it will allocate $130 million to Pennsylvania's Pennsylvania Research and Education Network to provide broadband access statewide. The commonwealth will be better connected to serve schools, health care networks, libraries and state and local governments. The program will move 1,000 jobs to Pennsylvania.

headline:
Pittsburghers, Legislators Weigh In On New Health Care Legislation
Pittsburgh Residents Weigh In On Health Care Reform
abstract: Pittsburgh residents reveal their reaction to the recently passed federal healthcare reform legislation. Pittsburgh area congressman US Rep. Mike Doyle and US Rep. Kathy Dahlkemper voted yes on the legislation while Rep. Jason Altmire and Rep. Tim Murphy voted against the bill.

headline: Presidents change, but not the senator
abstract: Pennsylvania airwaves are filled with a new Specter ad amid a suddenly tight Democratic primary fight between Specter and another Delaware County Democratic congressman, Joe Sestak. Specter is tying himself to the liberal President Obama just as tightly as he once did to the conservative Reagan in 1986 when he was running for just his second term as a U.S. Senator.

headline:
Pa. Small Business Person of the Year Kevin Stecko career suits him to a T
Employs 28 at his $2.6 million T-shirt facility in Mount Pleasant Township
abstract: Kevin Stecko was named Pennsylvania Small Business Person of the Year for his T-shirt business that runs off a website called 80stees.com. Stecko was invited to the Rose Garden at the White House to meet with President Obama because of his successes. Stecko's website has made $10 million in the past two years.

headline: Computer upgrade challenged
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue relies on some computer systems that were installed in 1975. These systems handle the flow of money from different taxes into state government. Revenue Secretary C. Daniel Hassell worries the systems are living on borrowed time and could crash.

headline: Do your research before choosing a caregiver
abstract: As the baby boomer generation ages and nears the age of 65, their family members are facing the prospect of how to care for mom and dad. In order to protect consumers using the services of home care agencies and registries, the PA Department of Health requires, as of January of this year, that the businesses be licensed and that, by Dec. 12, 2011, all direct care workers employed or roistered by the agencies meet state-mandated competency requirements.

headline: Bankruptcy support heats city hearing
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson has asked for Harrisburg to receive help from a state-appointed coordinator as it tries to deal with a looming spike in debt-service payments tied to the Harrisburg incinerator, and a simultaneous deficit in the current-year operating budget. Thompson's interim chief of staff and finance director, Robert Kroboth, noted the city only has about $330,000 cash on hand but faces a $1.2 million payroll due next week.

headline: Americans will rise to the occasion
abstract: Author approves of Governor-elect Tom Corbett’s plans to sell off state liquor stores and not raise taxes or fees on gas drilling. He is optimistic that the American people will overcome the challenges facing them despite what may occur in Washington or in-state.

headline: Cash grants for help with home heating to increase
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that those qualifying for Pennsylvania's Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) will receive 100 dollars more than anticipated.  The governor said that more monies could become available for assistance if Congress releases contingency funds for the program; there was a 55 million dollar reduction in federal funding for state LIHEAP programs this year

headline: My first year in Harrisburg: Party labels and most 'friends' don't mean much in the capital of Pennsylvania
abstract: PA State Representative Jim Christiana commented on his first year as a state representative in Harrisburg. He said the spirit of corruption in Harrisburg is prevalent and that political friendships are merely conditional.

headline: Officials decry cuts in gun-crimes task force
abstract: PA Senator Anthony Williams and Philadelphia law enforcement have called for the reinstatement of $2 million in state funds to the Philadelphia Gun Violence Task Force which worked to reduce gun crime in Philadelphia. The task force was fully funded at $5 million in the 2009-2010 budget, but was cut by $2 million in the 2010-2011 budget negotiations.

headline: Oil spill is a warning
abstract: Since the blowout at a BP deep-drilling rig on April 20 in the Gulf Coast, more than four million gallons of oil has spilled. As a result the Obama administration has wisely postponed public hearings on its misguided proposal to lift a moratorium on drilling along the East Coast. The plan would have allowed drilling in the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Virginia, just 100 miles from New Jersey.

headline: Editorial: Wheel of fortune
abstract: the author says that the revolving door policy  for the PA Gaming Control Board doesn't apply to lawyers who used to work for the board. The author cites Frank Donaghue, former counsel for the board, who now works for a law firm that represents casino interests. He is exempt because he doesn't work for a casino, he just represents them.

headline: Casinos pay off for state, but gamblers with addictions must remain priority
abstract: Many opposed PA's original gaming bill, passed in 2004, that authorized 14 slots parlors. One issue with the state's decision to legalize gambling, was the question if it was right for the government to seemingly prey on people’s weaknesses to balance the state budget. The concern today is about ensuring that gaming revenues remain in PA, and that communities remain protected.

headline: Transportation bill unveiled
abstract: A bill to generate $1.3 billion annually in new transportation revenue was introduced Tuesday by PA House of Representatives Appropriations Chairman Dwight Evans, D-Philadelphia. The measure would levy a new 8 percent tax on oil company profits, increase the existing state oil company franchise tax by 6.5 cents per gallon and hike a number of motor vehicle fees.

headline: Representative race focuses on jobs, drilling tax
abstract: PA Representative Adam Ravenstahl, D-Perry North, will need to defeat two challengers to get his first break from campaigning in nearly a year. Ravenstahl in May won the Democratic primary and a special election to fill the remainder of Don Walko's term after Walko resigned to become an Allegheny County Common Pleas Court judge.

headline: 'Most Wanted' gets public to help round up fugitives
abstract: The Sun-Gazette partnered with Lycoming County law enforcement to publish a "Most Wanted" fugitive list. The men and women featured in the insert committed a variety dangerous crimes and failed to show up for probation or court appearances.

headline: Energy costs reduced in Pennsylvania-owned buildings
abstract: A spokesperson for the PA Department of General Services said that the Rendell administration's goal of cutting energy costs in state-owned buildings by 20 percent has been met.  This reduction in energy consumption is saving taxpayers an estimated 2.4 million dollars a year.

headline: Judge asked to delay drilling in Allegheny National Forest
abstract: The US Forest Service has told Federal Judge Sean McLaughlin to overturn his ruling that lifted a ban on oil and gas drilling in the Allegheny Forest. The ban was a deal reached from a litigation settlement with environmentalists.

headline: AG Corbett says jurors convicted Veon on most serious charges
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett said that the 14 counts that former PA Representative Mike Veon was convicted of were the most serious of the charges against him. Veon faces up to 73 years in prison for directing state workers to campaign on state time. Veon was acquitted of using $22,000 in taxpayer money to cater basketball games among fellow House Democrats.

headline: More accountability needed over state fleet of vehicles
abstract: According to a report issued in 2009 by Auditor General Jack Wagner highlighted that the Department of General Services must exert greater control over its management of the Pennsylvania's fleet of vehicles. The 16,600 vehicles, are used by elected officials, state agencies, commissions and public employees to carry out official duties on behalf of the state government.

headline: Senate advances bill to develop searchable website of state finances
abstract: The NJ state Senate approved the Transparency in Government Act, which would require the NJ state treasurer and NJ state technology officer to make available online the state's financial actions dating back to 2000. The bill is meant to make state financial decisions more transparent. The bill now moves to the NJ Assembly.

headline: It's potent. It's dangerous. It's legal.
abstract: Sold as herbal incense under names such as K2, Spice, Genie and Wicked, a synthetic marijuana is banned in eight states, but is currently illegal in Pennsylvania.

headline: Bill Clinton stumps for Onorato in Philadelphia
abstract: Appearing in Montgomery County for US Senate candidate Joe Sestak and west Philadelphia for gubernatorial hopeful Dan Onorato, former President Bill Clinton put the consequences of a Democratic defeat on Nov. 2 in the starkest of terms. Observers have said that Democratic lethargy could cancel out the party's massive voter registration edge, giving Republicans, who are seemingly more energized this campaign season, the opening they need to retake Congress.

headline: PNC profits double
abstract: PNC, Pittsburgh's biggest bank and the fifth largest deposit bank in the country, said this morning it earned $1.1 billion, or $2.07 per share, up from $559 million, or $1, in the third quarter last year. Excluding a 62 cents-per-share gain on the sale of the global investment servicing unit to Bank of New York Mellon and integration costs of 11 cents, net income in the most recent period would have been $837 million, or $1.56 per share, PNC said.

headline: Monroeville budget keeps tax rate, in-house dispatch
abstract: Monroeville's $27.99 million budget maintains the property tax rate and keeps the emergency dispatch center, which the council sought to eliminate. The budget includes an increase in the business privilege tax, resulting in about $1 million for the municipality.

headline: DCED secretary appoints four firms to handle Harrisburg's plan under Act 47
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development  has chosen who will assist in developing and implementing a recovery plan for Harrisburg. The Novak Consulting Group got the offer. Harrisburg became the 20th municipality active in the Act 47 program after a declaration of financial distress was made.

headline: Winning lottery ticket sold in Shippensburg
abstract: A winning million-dollar lottery ticket was sold at a Shippensburg convenience store.

headline: Gaming Control Board fines Meadows Racetrack & Casino
abstract: State gaming regulators have fined The Meadows Racetrack & Casino for incidents  in which three gamblers allegedly conspired to win more than $400,000 in false jackpots. The PA Gaming Control Board said the casino had internal control violations that led to the improper payout of the false jackpots. All three men have been charged also.

headline: Attorney General Tom Corbett says 'justice has been served' in Bonusgate verdict
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett said that justice has been served in the convictions of former PA Representative Mike Veon, his aide Annamarie Peretta-Rosepink, and Brett Cott. He said the most important conviction was the charge of conspiracy. The three were part of the "bonusgate" scandal which accused PA House Democrats of giving state-paid bonuses to legislative staffers for campaign work.

headline: Trib honors Westmoreland students' contributions
abstract: Emily Gabriel 18, a senior at Greensburg Salem High School who has volunteered for organizations such as the Clelian Heights School for Exceptional Children, and Special Olympics was one of 10 gold medal winners recognized in the Trib Total Media's 2010 Outstanding Young Citizen program.

headline: School of Future: High on tech, low on basics?
abstract: Philadelphia's High School of the Future, a high school with curriculum that is based on technology has received complaints from students and parents that the school has not adequately prepared them for college. They say the high-tech curriculum did not provide them with the educational balance that other students at other schools got. However, many students got accepted to numerous colleges.

headline: Camp stresses social skills for kids with autism
abstract: Students in the Bristol Township School District who have been diagnosed with an autism disorder used part of their summer vacation to develop their interpersonal skills. These students spent the past six weeks at a social skills camp at Benjamin Franklin Freshman Academy, developing vital social skills. Currently, there are 976 school-age students with autism diagnosis throughout Bucks County.

headline: Underage drinking rule changes
abstract: PA Senator Jake Corman, R-Bellefonte, proposed a three-bill package Friday that would increase maximum fines to $1,000 for underage drinking and public drunkenness. The proposal also would allow municipalities with college campuses to tack on an additional $100 fee to be applied to alcohol-abuse-prevention programs. Currently, fines are $300 for public drunkenness and first-time underage drinking citations, while repeat underage drinking offenders are subject to $500 fines.

headline: Toomey targets Sestak's dog ad
abstract: Republican Pat Toomey on Monday took aim at Democrat Joe Sestak's dog, Bella, to outline his opponent's record of voting for bailouts. In the ad, Sestak compares cleaning up his dog's droppings as similar to cleaning up the mess left over by the Bush Administration and Toomey's time in Congress. Toomey said the ad was just another "last-ditch effort" on the part of his opponent to run away from his record of voting "for every bailout that has come down the pike," and to pin the blame on others.

headline: Conservancy preserves 113 acres in Bedford
abstract: The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy announced the purchase of a 113-acre parcel of land along Lake Erie for a major permanent conservation project. The project, a partnership with private landowners, is a parcel connected to a large forested area that encompasses more than 9.500 acres and is home to a multitude of native birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, plants and trees.

headline: Officials: Web rumors about gun legislation are false
abstract: Rumors are circulating about two pieces of legislation that would restrict gun ownership and Second-Amendment rights.  One bill would require individuals to report all guns that they own to the Internal Revenue Service, and the other would add additional requirements for gun ownership.  U.S. Representative John Murtha said that these rumors are completely false; a National Rifle Association spokesperson agreed with Murtha's statement.

headline: Murtha House seat likely to disappear
abstract: Late US Representative John Murtha's seat in western Pennsylvania is expected to be the house seat that is projected to be removed after district realignment after the 2010 Census. Pennsylvania has seen a decline in population increases over the decade and is a state that may lose a seat. The upcoming election will play a large role in district realignment in 2012.

headline: Game Commission Releases 2009-10 Deer Estimates
abstract: The PA Game commission has released a report on the deer harvest for the 2009-2010 hunting season. Overall, hunting harvests are down for antler and antlerless deer. The PA Bureau of Wildlife Management is currently working to develop 2010 antlerless deer license allocation recommendations.

headline: Rivals tussle in Murtha's shadow
abstract: As the campaign for Pennsylvania's 12th Congressional District that was held by the late John Murtha heats up, supporters of both candidates like to invoke Murtha's name. Supporters of Democratic candidate Mark Critz's cite his ties to Murtha as his aide for more than a decade as a good thing. While Republican businessman Tim Burns supporters cite those ties as a hindrance since they believe Critz would only perpetuate the Democratic machine.

headline: Housing complex for veterans nears completion
abstract: A housing complex for war veterans and their families nears completion in Southwest Philadelphia. The veterans will have access to the Robert Brady Sr. Veterans Center where veterans can get access to services in the community and hold events.

headline: Democrats should rewrite, measure, and try once more
abstract: The US Senate failed to pass the Disclose Act, which would have imposed disclosure requirements on corporations, unions and other groups that finance ads for political campaigns, exempted the National Rifle Association and other nonprofit groups with more than 500,000 members. The act died when Democrats in the Senate last week were unable to get the 60 votes needed to end debate on the bill and move to a vote on passage.

headline: Fire museum to ring tribute to 9/11 victims
abstract: Although no members of the Pennsylvania National Fire Museum died in the terrorist attacks in New York City nine years ago this Saturday, its members feel a strong connection to the 343 New York City firefighters who did. Museum officials this weekend will sponsor two events in remembrance of Sept. 11, 2001: a tolling of the bell at 8:47 a.m. Saturday at the museum, and a Remembering 9/11 Service at 2 p.m. Sunday at the Riverfront Park firefighter's monument at Front and Verbeke streets.

headline: Pittsburgh council kills parking plan despite firefighters, police pleas
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council this morning voted 7-1 to kill Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's parking-lease proposal, leaving officials with the choice of implementing an alternative plan or allowing the state to take over the city's ailing pension funds. Ravenstahl said yesterday he instructed his staff to begin preparing for the state takeover of the pension funds, after council rejected his plan to prop up the pension funds with money from leasing parking garages and spots.

headline: State aid to business in doubt
abstract: The elimination or reduction of funding from the state's Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program may cause development projects in to slow or come to a halt. Governor-elect Tom Corbett has said the state cannot continue to borrow and spend at its current rate.

headline: Pittsburgh's legal advice costly
abstract: The Philadelphia law firm Cozen O'Connor charged the city of Pittsburgh 34,000 dollars in legal fees to review legislation, conduct research, and draft legal opinions relating to Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's proposed college-student-tuition tax.
