Mayor Ravenstahl proposed a 1 percent tuition tax to generate 15 million dollars for the city's municipal pension system; Cozen O'Connor determined the tax was legal.

headline: Price of heritage: A tight budget should still spend on preservation
abstract: The author urges Congress to fully fund federal preservation grant programs like Save America's Treasures and Preserve America in the federal budget. The Obama administration has proposed cutting the programs. The author says the preservation programs are vital economic and cultural institutions that are not costly.

headline: Meehan & Lentz spar over campaign improprieties in 7th District race
abstract: Republican Pat Meehan and Democrat PA Representative Bryan Lentz, both running for the 7th congressional district seat have sparred over Meehan's nominating petitions and the Radnor Democratic party chairman's use of his state e-mail address. Lentz accused Meehan of forging a name on his nomination petition and Meehan has accused the Radnor Democratic party chairman of using his Disciplinary Board of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania e-mail address to solicit supporters to a Lentz fundraising event.

headline: Views differ on whether Mellon Arena should survive
abstract: Residents of Pittsburgh's Hill District attended a meeting at Ebenezer Baptist Church Thursday evening to discuss the future of Mellon Arena and the 28-acre site owned by the city-county Sports & Exhibition Authority. Supporters of tearing down the Mellon arena say it needs to go to make room for housing and other amenities the Hill District has long needed.

headline:
Obama: Gulf will get back to normal
He called the region's seafood safe, and the White House said BP appeared ready to set up a compensation fund.
abstract: US President Obama, at a speech in Theodore, Ala., said that seafood from the Gulf of Mexico is safe to eat and that he is working on setting up a compensatory fund with BP. Meanwhile, a congressional committee released a report that showed that BP cut corners on safety in order to save on costs on the well weeks before the explosion. BP says they are making progress on stopping the flow of oil from the ruptured well.

headline: Rendell: Legislators should get back to work and fix our roads
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell at a press conference Wednesday asked Pennsylvanians to tell their legislators to go back to Harrisburg this month and find a way to pay for underfunded roads, bridges and public transit. Rendell is trying to lobby the General Assembly to raise taxes on gas at the pump, oil companies and motor-vehicle registration to pay for the estimated $1.7 billion needed to pay for vital transportation projects.

headline: Colleges buy 'cheap' land; use to be determined later
abstract: Colleges and universities are buying up chunks of land at bargain prices, sometimes without a clear idea how they will be used. The schools are banking on future growth to make their purchases good investments in the interim, many are leasing the properties they are not using until they need them.

headline: Pat Toomey's Wall Street career given another twirl, this time by Mother Jones
abstract: Pat Toomey's Wall Street past is elaborated upon in a brand-new piece in Mother Jones by Nick Baumann. Toomey's Senate campaign office was asked to respond, but didn't, according to the author.

headline: Specter's farewell: The long-serving senator sounds a warning
abstract: Arlen Specter made what is likely his last formal speech to the U.S. Senate. In his speech, Specter addressed a number of the nation's most severe problems.

headline: MLK Day to focus on Girard College
abstract: Yesterday, Ken Salaam, a civil-rights activist who for years protested the whites-only admissions policy at Philadelphia's Girard College, was honored for his social-justice work.  Girard College's whites-only policy sparked protests in 1965; the policy was eventually ended in 1968 when the U.S. Supreme Court upheld a lower-court ruling that required the college to admit black students.

headline: Cyber schools called 'disservice' to students
abstract: Southmoreland Superintendent John Halfhill said cyber schools drain public school districts' budgets with no positive results. He said the charter schools in Westmoreland County add costs of $8 million and the majority of them do not perform up to Adequate Yearly Progress standards in reading and math. He said he is looking into the amount of money the charter school spend on advertising.

headline: Gas driller seeks permits for Wayne County wells
abstract: Houston-based Newfield Exploration Co. and Hess Corp have teamed up to lease 140,000 acres of land in Wayne and Susquehanna counties. The two corporations plan to drill assessment wells this summer in order to test how much the wells will produce. The assessment wells differ from normal gas wells and are not regulated by the Delaware River Basin Commission, which regulates water resources in the region.

headline: Pennsylvania state Rep. Ron Buxton fights for his political life
abstract: State Rep. Ron Buxton, D-Harrisburg in his fight for re-election is being criticized by his challengers for his perceived lack of leadership to not knowing his constituents to fat government contracts for his son. Buxton is seeking a 10th term in the House against Democrat Karl Singleton who he outlasted in 2008 by just 176 votes.

headline: Keystone Gardens: Deep-rooted sources of food, pride
abstract: The PA Horticultural Society provides services to long-lasting, large community gardens that they designate as Keystone Gardens. The society gives them counseling and support so they can be sustainable over the long term.

headline: Rendell calls for legislative action on transportation funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell urged state lawmakers to find a solution to the state’s transportation funding crisis this year. In May, the PA Transportation Advisory Commission issued a report that estimated Pennsylvania is short $3.5 billion a year in making investments that will keep highways, bridges and transit in a state of good repair.

headline: Downtown Hilton owners file for bankruptcy
abstract: Shubh Hotels Pittsburgh filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Pittsburgh, estimating $50 million to $100 million in liabilities and 100 to 199 creditors.

headline: Economy continues to drag down Easton's revenues
abstract: Real estate tax revenue for the City of Easton appears in line with projections, and is ahead of amounts collected by this time last year, according to financial numbers through Sept. 30. The business privilege tax has exceeded expectations, mostly because of the city's auditing of yearly tax returns. the city's earned income tax continues to struggle as unemployment plagues the workforce. In addition, revenue from the admissions tax, local services tax and building permits all lag behind collections for the same period last year.

headline: Pa losing congressional seats, but will remain pivotal
abstract: The first wave of Census data revealed Pennsylvania is growing considerably slower, especially in comparison to places such as Texas and the Southwest. Politicians in Harrisburg will have to determine how to re-divide the state into new congressional districts with one fewer seat. With a Republican controlled governorship, the seat most likely targeted will be Democratic.

headline: The last six months of table talk
abstract: This article provides a legislative and political history of movement to legalize table games in Pennsylvania.  The author notes that, over the course of just six months, legalization of table games has gone from an inchoate notion to a budget-passing imperative pushed by Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Bucks, Montco among state's healthiest
abstract: According to County Health Rankings reports, Bucks and Montgomery counties are among the most healthy counties in Pennsylvania. The report measured deaths under 75, low birth weights and people reported in poor mental and physical health. The healthier areas were located in affluent suburbs of central and southeastern Pennsylvania while the most unhealthy were located in poorer areas of northeastern and northwestern Pennsylvania.

headline: Philadelphia Targets Certain Neighborhoods Threatening to Teeter into Decay
abstract: The City of Philadelphia and partnering organizations have released a report, "Protecting Philadelphia's Backbone: A Strategy for Vital Neighborhoods," which discusses proposals to revitalize neighborhoods that are blighted.

headline: Gulf catastrophe should push us beyond petroleum
abstract: Despite the devastation of the BP oil spill off the Gulf Coast of Mexico, President Obama continues to claim that we must push forward with more offshore drilling. The spill does offer America the chance to take serious steps to moving beyond oil dependence and towards energy security.

headline: In Oval Office Speech, Obama Calls for New Focus on Energy Policy
abstract: US President Obama urged the country to end its addiction to foreign oil in a televised address from the oval office. The statements come as a government estimate states that 60,000 barrels of oil a day are spilling from the oil well that exploded in the Gulf of Mexico. Estimates continue to increase as to how many barrels are spilling daily. The president will meet with BP, the owner of the exploded well, to seek a resolution to the spill and compensate those affected.

headline: PA may be forced to lay off 12,500
abstract: According to PA Governor Ed Rendell state and local governments would be forced to lay off a combined 12,500 public employees, including teachers, police officers and firefighters, if the US Congress does not send the state more recession-related aid. The Pennsylvania budget relies on $850 million in federal stimulus aid, and if passed the bill would provide $600 million to the state.

headline: State Police: Nine killed, 271 injured in Labor Day driving period crashes
abstract: Nine people died and 271 others were injured in 754 crashes investigated by the Pennsylvania State Police during the four-day Labor Day holiday driving period, Commissioner Frank E. Pawlowski said today.

headline: Pocono Medical Center breaks ground for $38 million cancer center
abstract: Pocono Medical Center's Dale and Frances Hughes Cancer Center expansion will increase space devoted to caring for cancer patients by nearly 50,000 square feet at the East Stroudsburg hospital. The new center, which will continue to be named after business leaders and philanthropists Dale and Frances Hughes, will be across from the hospital's main entrance and connected to the home base by a bridge. The cancer center will increase services that are much needed in the Poconos.

headline: Harrisburg meeting to address business opportunities for women- and minority-owned contracting businesses
abstract: Rev. Earl Harris is holding a “Where Do We Go From Here,” meeting at St. Paul’s Baptist Church on North 17th Street in Harrisburg to discuss minority- and women-owned businesses opportunities. The meeting is open to the public.

headline: Pa. House Gives Final OK for Casino Table Games
abstract: On Wednesday, the state House of Representatives approved a bill that legalizes table games.  Governor Ed Rendell has indicated that he will sign the legislation.

headline: Hiring of appraiser of city assets draws complaints
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson did not get a purchase order from the city controller before contracting appraisal work to a former business partner and campaign supporter. The controller said the office can withhold payment or audit from the firm, RSR Realtors, until the mayor gets submits the contract for a purchase order. Some Harrisburg City Council members are upset about the mayor's lack of transparency in handing over the contract.

headline: Census: More people arrive than leave for first time in almost 20 years
abstract: More people moved into the Pittsburgh metro area last year, more than those who left. It’s the first time the area has seen a positive population change since 1991. The data comes from Census Bureau estimates and takes into consideration Allegheny, Armstrong, Beaver, Butler, Fayette, Washington and Westmoreland counties.

headline: An almost good day
abstract: Philadelphia City Council held hearings on a couple of bills yesterday, which includes a proposal to require lobbyists to register with the city and to disclose their activities. The other bill would lift a longstanding ban on political activity by city employees.

headline: Commentary: State budget battle lacks usual clamor
abstract: The author states that verbal jibes between the governor and the legislature has calmed this year. The author says that there is little political will by Democrats to pass his budget or his education proposals. The author claims the governor may be looking ahead to stepping out of office at the end of his term.

headline: Effectiveness of solitary confinement discussed at hearing
abstract: A public hearing on the effectiveness of solitary confinement in state prisons was held at the Borough Hall Monday in Yeadon, PA. The hearing  was held by Representative. Ronald Waters, D-191, of Philadelphia, Thomas Caltagirone, D-127, of Berks County, and Vanessa Lowery Brown, D-190, of Philadelphia County. The hearing was held to see what kind of policy changes need to be made in order to make solitary confinement more humane.

headline: 3-in-1 flu shots advised for all ages
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department will begin offering the 2010-11, three-in-one flu vaccinations on Oct. 18. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention states on its web- site that "yearly flu vaccination should begin in September or as soon as vaccine is available and continue throughout the influenza season, into December, January and beyond." This year the flu shot will protect against H1N1, or the so-called "swine flu" of 2009, plus an H3N2 virus and an influenza B virus.

headline: Lawmakers are 'gutless' for not banning drivers from using cell phones
abstract: Lawmakers in Harrisburg need to do the responsible thing and pass a ban on using cell phones while driving.

headline: Chesapeake Bay, Marcellus Shale. Living in Harmony?
abstract: Author is upset with the lack of scientific data and information in a report released by The Chesapeake Bay Foundation regarding the environmental impact of drilling wells in the Marcellus Shale formation

headline: Seven plead guilty in Bonusgate
abstract: The first seven guilty pleas were secured yesterday in the Bonus gate corruption investigation.  Seven former House Democratic staffers pleaded guilty to diverting several million dollars of taxpayer money to legislative employees for political campaign work.  For the last three years, PA Attorney General Tom Corbett has investigated the use of public funds to pay legislative staffers for campaign work.

headline: On the hook: Unscrupulous tow operators must be reined in
abstract: The author discusses how towing companies in Pittsburgh often do not know or ignore city towing regulations regarding storage fees and towing rates. He noted Pittsburgh City Councilman Doug Shields and PA State Representative Anthony DeLuca of introducing bills to combat unscrupulous tow operating procedures.

headline: Sharp debate makes health care top voter issue in new poll
abstract: According to a poll by Franklin and Marshall college, healthcare and the economy will be the two main issues in the US Senate primary among Democrats US Senator Arlen Specter, US Representative Joe Sestak, former US Rep. Pat Toomey and Peg Luksik. The poll also shows that more people had not heard of the "bonusgate" scandal than had heard of it, and that many residents are in favor of a tax on smokeless tobacco and cigars.

headline: Deficit raises budget questions
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate Appropriations Committee has estimated the state deficit could hit $1.5 billion by year’s end on June 30 making the task of passing a budget very difficult. Governor Ed Rendell has urged the Legislature to approve a combination of spending cuts, new taxes and revenue transfers to balance the budget and avoid some of the issues the state went through last year.

headline: Stimulus Bond Program Has Unforeseen Costs
abstract: Building America Bonds which allow for states and cities to sell bonds at a high commission price while the federal government pays 35 percent of the interest costs has saved some cities and states billions of dollars but have unforeseen costs. The costs are that they have high commissions and that they are priced cheaply, which could result in investors to turn quick profits if the prices rise but raising interest rates for taxpayers.

headline: Zoners approve drilling more gas wells in Lake, Fairmount townships
abstract: After four hours of testimony Tuesday night, the Luzerne County Zoning Hearing Board approved the drilling of 10 more natural gas wells and the construction of another compressor station in the county. More than 20 people testified, most of them opposing Encana Oil & Gas (USA)’s request for temporary use permits and special exceptions for five wells in Fairmount Township and five other wells.

headline: Firm’s reports on protesters rankle Rendell
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell apologized Tuesday to groups whose peaceful protests or events, from an animal rights demonstration to a gay and lesbian festival, were the subject of regular anti-terrorism bulletins being distributed by his homeland security director. The bulletins listed demonstrations by anti-war groups, deportation protesters in Philadelphia, mountaintop removal mining protesters in West Virginia and an animal rights protest at a Montgomery County rodeo.

headline: Corbett has (largely) stayed on message
abstract: A weeks-long controversy over Tom Corbett's remarks that some of the state's unemployed preferring the dole to work, the two-term attorney general has offered a resonant if predictable message that works. Corbett's Democratic rival, Dan Onorato, the elected county executive of Allegheny County, has struggled to fashion a more compelling narrative. Corbett has hammered on themes that have aided other Republican candidates this year "lower taxes and less spending," while also delivering a Pennsylvania-specific message about cleaning up the Legislature, via the Bonusgate public corruption probe.

headline: Harrisburg-area insurer cuts mental health benefits
abstract: Susquehanna Twp.-based health insurer, Capital Blue Cross, will drop “behavioral health” benefits for about 9,000 people who have individual health insurance policies. According to Capital’s senior director for individual products, eliminating the benefits reduces what would have otherwise been a 20 percent increase to 10 percent.

headline: Gasoline prices expected to continue climbing
abstract: Gasoline prices are expected to steadily increase in 2010.  Experts say that weather and financial-flow issues are responsible for the anticipated price increases.

headline: Pennsylvania traffic fatalities at record low
abstract: Fatalities on Pennsylvania highways fell to its lowest number in 2009 since reporting began. PA Secretary of Transportation Allen Biehler noted the department's safety measures such as driver education and improved infrastructure development should be credited with helping decrease the fatalities.

headline: Area legislators split on tougher fines for secrecy
abstract: All legislators were not in favor of a law that would allow state agencies to hold closed meeting on issues secret issues such as security while also increasing the fine for violating the Open Meetings Law from $100 to $1,000. The Pennsylvania Newspaper Publishers Association and the Pennsylvania Township Supervisors Association oppose the measure while PA Representative Garth Everett and PA Rep. Rick Mirabito supported it.

headline: State employees won't be impacted by any budget-impasse related furloughs, Gov. Ed Rendell says
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell said this week that there will not be any budget-impasse related furloughs this year. This is good news for state employees, since they will not have to face the potential situation of having one or multiple pay days withheld from their paycheck. After the Rendell administration furloughed about 25,000 employees in 2007, the state Supreme Court ruled that state employees paychecks can’t be withheld if they put in their time.

headline: DEP seeks new drilling safety laws
abstract: PA Department of Environmental Protection Secretary John Hangar said that the agency needs to have more authority to deny oil and gas companies well permits in the Marcellus Shale region. He said this authority should be strengthened through a bill passed through the state legislature. Right now the DEP only has regulatory authority.

headline: Real 'stimulus' comes from tough decisions
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says layoffs of 12,500 public employees, including teachers, police officers and firefighters are coming if  the US Congress does not pass a $26 billion bill to extend federal stimulus aid to states and schools. Pennsylvania's budget is dependent on $850 million that the state hopes to receive from the stimulus bill.

headline: 9 schools in county qualify for Pa. ‘making-progress’ list
abstract: Luzerne County saw 45 of 63 schools make PA state-mandated goals for achieving Adequate Yearly Progress (AYP) on math and reading test results in the 2009-10 school year, a success rate of about 72 percent. Schools must meet a variety of goals to make AYP: minimum attendance rates for non-high schools, minimum graduation rates for high schools, minimum test participation rates, and minimum percentages of students scoring proficient or better in the standardized math and reading tests given in grades three through eight and 11.

headline: School board rejects Martin Tower tax plan
abstract: The Bethlehem Area School Board on Monday rejected a controversial plan to use tax dollars to help developers turn the Martin Tower property into a residential community. The 6-3 vote means developers will not be getting a tax-increment financing, or TIF, district. The plan would have guaranteed them $9.5 million in public money toward their $223 million project of 230 apartments, some office space, and up to 285 townhouses at the vacant site of Bethlehem Steel's former corporate headquarters.

headline: Budget session ends with tax hike
abstract: Hatfield Township commissioners passed a $10.5 million 2011 budget that will increase taxes about $79 for most residents. Homeowners assessed at the township average of $148,465 will pay $316 in township taxes in the coming year. Millage will rise from 2.54 mills to 4.035, an increase of more than 55 percent.

headline: Need a job? Casinos may hire up to 1,500 more
abstract: Sean A. Sullivan, vice president and manager of The Meadows Casino Resort, says that the legalization of table games could generate more revenue for the state and create as many as 1,500 more casino jobs across Pennsylvania.  Last night, the state House approved the introduction of table games to certain establishments.

headline: Parking-space etiquette: Chair-ish is the word
abstract: Residents of Philadelphia have begun placing plastic chairs as parking spot savers after the snowstorms of February. The practice is to keep people from taking parking spaces that require hard work to dig out. The act is illegal since the street is public property but Philadelphia police have not enforced the law out of respect for people's hard work.

headline: Despite House Approval, Pa. Budget Faces Long Battle
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget passed the PA House 100 days before the June 30 deadline, but may face opposition in the PA Senate. The budget is $29 billion and has no new broad-based taxes. Many legislators would like to avoid a budget stalemate that would cause the budget to be passed pass the deadline like it did the previous 7 years.

headline: Sen. Scarnati concerned with paroling criminals to Brockway
abstract: Pennsylvania state Sen. Joe Scarnati, R-Brockway, expressed concern with the increased movement of released criminals to the Brockway area.

headline: Commentary: Sestak, Onorato get big say in replacing Democratic chairman
abstract: With the resignation of PA state Democratic party chairman T.J. Rooney, Democratic candidates Dan Onorato and Joe Sestak have a large say in who will be temporary chairman until the party picks a new chair. The author states that the two candidates had a big say at a recent party meeting but both deferred the choice to the state party electorate.

headline: Website sheds light on transportation crisis
abstract: PA Department of Transportation's website is now providing online video to help citizens feel they are in the driver's seat navigating many of the most urgent road and bridge projects in the state. PA Governor Ed Rendell and Lawmakers are looking into ways to fill the $470 million-a-year revenue gap created when federal officials rejected Pennsylvania's application to toll Interstate 80.

headline: Explorer 9 part of push for faster, better Web
abstract: Microsoft will offer a test version of its next browser, Internet Explorer 9, in San Francisco today. This next generation of browsers represented by IE9 promises to accelerate the Web from still photo to film. While the majority of Web users, 60 percent, are still on Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox has leapt to 23 percent and Google Chrome had 8 percent of the market as of August, according to the browser tracker Net Market Share.

headline: Budget pledges, vagueness aren't good enough
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate race features solid candidates who offer a stark contrast in political philosophies, and Democrats had a shot at nominating someone who fell almost exactly in between. The Lehigh Valley's three local congressional candidates voters as more able than usual, despite what they're saying about each other. PA's gubernatorial race makes some wonder how we ended up with such a dismal choice.

headline: Rendell appoints Snyder to board
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell appointed Greene County Commissioner Pam Snyder to the Port of Pittsburgh Commission board. Snyder will replace former Greene County Commissioner Dave Coder, who resigned earlier in the year to take a position with U.S. Rep. Mark S. Critz.

headline: Local representative split on table games
abstract: Somerset County officials disagree on the legalization of table games.  On Wednesday, state representative Frank Burns voted for a measure that would legalize table games, while Representative Carl Metzgar voted against the legislation.  Representative Burns defended his vote, arguing that it was part of a larger state budget agreement.

headline: Peregrine falcons are nesting in Harrisburg, and people are tweeting about it this year
abstract: A pair of Peregrine falcons continue to nest on the Rachel Carson building in Harrisburg, which has a live feed of the pair which people have begun tweeting about. Peregrine falcons are starting to breed again after being poisoned with a contaminant in the 1960s which killed some of them off.

headline: People Are Living Longer and Healthier: Now What?
abstract: People are living longer in the developed world while the effects of aging like dementia and heart disease remain. This questions how humans in the developed world will approach life in the next century. It also will affect policy decisions when it comes to social welfare and caring for the elderly.

headline: Senators, Rachael Ray, first lady push for children's nutrition programs
abstract: First Lady Michelle Obama and celebrity chef Rachael Ray both held events Tuesday to call for federal action on child obesity, which brought much needed star power to the issue said Sen. Bob Casey Jr. D-Pennsylvania. Casey believes the First Lady and Rachel Ray's involvement bring both credibility and notoriety to the issue which the U.S. Congress cannot do on their own.

headline: Drilling wastewater rule gets vital Pa. approval
abstract: The Pennsylvania Independent Regulatory Review Commission voted to approve a proposal by PA Governor Ed Rendell that would prevent briny wastewater from natural gas drilling sites from polluting the drinking water and waterways of the state. The rule would require wastewater treatment facilities to get state approval for any water treated over a specified amount allowed.

headline: Berlin considers wind power options
abstract: Borough council members and American Municipal Power representatives fielded questions from the public regarding a three-turbine wind generation project in Brothersvalley Township on Wednesday. Borough Secretary Kerry Claycomb said the project, which could begin in 2011 could cost anywhere from $10 million to $12 million.

headline: Experts see better education, jobs as keys to fighting poverty in Reading
abstract: Reading PA's manufacturing base is a shadow of its former self, and as a result, the poverty rate has skyrocketed. To combat the problem, social services agencies and the state government pour millions of dollars into Reading for a temporary lifeline.

headline: Mr. Gingrich goes to Harrisburg
abstract: Former U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Tuesday that he'll decide by March whether to jump into an increasingly crowded field of Republican challengers to President Barack Obama in 2012. Gingrich has been hinting since mid-summer of a presidential run. His political groups, including American Solutions for Winning the Future, raised nearly $4 million through September, Politico has reported.

headline: Restaurants are back on the menu
abstract: A recent survey by the National Restaurant Association declared the restaurant industry at its healthiest since 2007, citing a broad survey that quizzed 400 operators on sales, traffic, labor and capital costs. The industry is experiencing its second month of overall growth and has seen a 4 percent increase in sales from the previous year.

headline: PennDOT condemns 5 properties for Rt. 61 work
abstract: As part of its plans for a major redesign of Route 61, state Department of Transportation Officials filed a declaration of taking for five Schuykill County properties on Wednesday.  The purpose of the filing is to acquire property for transportation purposes.

headline: Alle-Kiski Valley legislators not buying expanded sales tax
abstract: Allegheny and Kiski area PA state legislators are not in agreement with Governor Rendell's lifting of sales tax exemptions while lowering the sales tax from 6% to 4%. PA State Senator Jane Orie, PA Representative Darryl Metcalfe and others said the sales tax proposal would hurt middle class people by increasing the amount they pay for items and services.

headline:
Program helps newly released Berks prison inmates find, pay for place to live
Those with no housing options but a good work history are accepted. Money for the program is from the economic stimulus package.
abstract: Inmates in Berks county released from prison can benefit from a program funded by federal stimulus money and ran by the non-profit Berks Connections and Pretrial Services. The program gives released inmates a place to live while subsidizing rent. The program only accepts those who have a good work history and have a willingness to work.

headline: Get rid of BRT
abstract: Tuesday's referendum to disband Philadelphia's long-mismanaged Board of Revision of Taxes, gave Philadelphians a chance to cast a vote for a City Hall reform that directly affects their pocketbooks. For decades the seven-member board and staff of 160 were given the task of determining property tax rates in the city. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter supported the measure and encouraged residents to do the same.

headline:
Brain drain forecast for Pennsylvania
Pa. projected to have more educated workers than jobs, unlike rest of U.S.
abstract: The Georgetown University Center on Education and the Workforce found in a study that Pennsylvania may face a "brain drain" once the economy recovers as they predicted in 2015. By then most other states will see more jobs that require a post-secondary education than qualified workers. Pennsylvania is the exception where the state is on track to have more post-secondary graduates than jobs that require those skills.

headline: Pennsylvania casinos ease tax burden
abstract: Local citizens are urging elected leaders to put casino money toward tax relief instead of a community college or the other big-ticket items that casino revenue has financed in Erie County. Pennsylvania, with a 55 percent tax rate, collected $1.080 billion in taxes from its nine casinos in 2009 which has helped to ease the tax burden on localities.

headline: Healthcare reform faces low participation in high-risk pools
abstract: States across the country are reporting lower than expected participation in the high-risk pools for people with pre-existing conditions, raising concerns that a lack of public engagement could affect the Federal Healthcare reform law's success and that of health reform more generally. Some observers blame high healthcare costs and the angry political rhetoric ahead of the midterm elections for obscuring the law's benefits.

headline: Adler-Runyan race most competitive in N.J. this Election Day
abstract: A number of Congressional races will be voted Tuesday. Local races will also be determined. Freshman Democrat John Adler will face Republican Jon Runyan in the Third Congressional District, which is located in South Jersey. This is proving to be among the most competitive races in the state.

headline: Gamblers hit jackpot as Parx East opens
abstract: Parx Casino officials held a grand opening for their Parx East facility just off Street Road in Bensalem. The facility includes 45 poker tables, more blackjack, roulette and other live table games, bringing the total of live table games to 152 at the complex.

headline: Size of LIHEAP cash grants to increase this year; but fewer people will be eligible to see them
abstract: Due to federal-funding cuts, fewer Pennsylvanians will qualify for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, which helps state residents pay home heating bills and resolve emergency situations.  Those who do qualify for the program will, however, receive larger cash grants this year; Governor Rendell announced the cash-grant increase this week.

headline: Sheetz rallies for beer sales
abstract: Employees of Sheetz gas stations protested against Pennsylvania Liquor laws that prevent the sell of beer at grocery stores and gas stations. The Supreme Court overturned the rights of one Sheetz in Altoona to sell beer on the basis of a liquor code interpretation. A bill has been put forward by PA State Senator John Rafferty that would allow sales of beer in grocery stores and would freeze the amount of liquor licenses.  Many restaurant and merchant groups gave their opinion of the matter.

headline: Stetler to judge: Dismiss charges, investigate Corbett
abstract: The Dauphin County Court judge hearing the case of former Democratic PA Representatives Stephen Stetler and Brett Feese has agreed to hear Stetler's argument that PA Attorney General Tom Corbett had committed some of the same acts as those state representatives that he is prosecuting. Stetler claims that Corbett used the "bonusgate" investigation for political reasons. Corbett has denied the claims.

headline: Health-care costs to rise by 1% for grown kids
abstract: One of the earliest benefits of President Barack Obama's new health-care law is that young adults can stay on their parents' health insurance until they turn 26. As a result of this new provision Health insurance premiums will increase nearly 1 percent higher for employer plans, the government said in an estimate released yesterday.

headline: McKeesport Mayor heartbroken by out-of-control violence
abstract: McKeesport Mayor James Brewster is disheartened by the number of murders that have been happening in McKeesport during his time as mayor. The community offers social service and outreach programs to keep residents out of a life of crime.

headline: Hole in state budget looming larger
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is meeting with state legislative leaders to discuss the potential $850 million hole in the new state budget. Whether or not PA will receive Medicaid funding through the extension of a federal stimulus program known as FMAP is still hanging as a summer recess for Congress nears. The aid extension to the states is in President Barack Obama's federal budget request, but Democratic leaders are trying to acquire the necessary votes to pass the funding.

headline: Casino revenues up slightly, over a year ago
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board reported today that slot machines produced gross revenue of $196,635,849 in August of this year and $108,121,631 in tax revenue. That compares to $186,936,232 in gross revenue and $102,789,443 in tax revenue during August 2009.

headline: Corbett wins: New governor likely to follow Christie example
abstract: Former Attorney General Tom Corbett has become Pennsylvania's new Governor. When asked how he would proceed, he said that he would look across the river to New Jersey Governor Chris Cirstie for guidance. Fixing the budget is a main concern as well as dealing with the Marcellus shale taxation issue.

headline: Pittsburgh police officer charged with homicide by vehicle
abstract: Pittsburgh police charged Adam Lewis with vehicular homicide in a motorcycle crash that killed the officer's female passenger. Lewis, who was off-duty at the time of the accident, faces 10 charges including homicide by vehicle while drunken driving, involuntary manslaughter and reckless driving.

headline: City schools contract with PFT nearing deadline
abstract: By Wednesday, the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and the school district must agree to collaborate on sweeping changes for Philadelphia schools.  These changes must be agreed upon if the Philadelphia Schools District is to be eligible for the federal government's 4.35 billion dollar Race to the Top program.  If the district qualifies for the program, it could receive as much as 8 million dollars in grants; the grants would be used to implement changes that school superintendent Arlene Ackerman has proposed.

headline: Lawmaker's larger-than-life persona recalled
abstract: Members of Congress and former US President Bill Clinton attended the late US Representative John Murtha's funeral. US Rep. Nancy Pelosi talked of Murtha's appreciation of his constituents and his being the first veteran of the Vietnam war to serve in congress.

headline: Water problem gets closer look from DEP, EPA
abstract: The contamination of a water well in Hickory is being examined the federal Environmental Protection Agency, the PA Department of Environmental Protection, and Range Resources Inc., the owner of a gas well near the infected water well. An independent firm found traces of chemicals in the water which Range Resources said they did not find in previous tests.

headline: 16,900 arrested for DUI, a record
abstract: Pennsylvania State Police reported Tuesday that they made a record 16,900 drunken driving arrests (DUI) last year, making it 8 consecutive years they have made a record breaking number of DUI arrests. During the same period alcohol-related crash fatalities dropped to 141, a decline of 14 percent.

headline: Up to 17 years sought for Veon in State probe
abstract: Prosecutors are pursuing a 12- to 17-year sentence for former Pa House Democratic Whip Mike Veon for his conviction on 14 counts of conviction for paying legislative staffers with staff money for campaign efforts, illegal fundraising and other political activities.

headline: 1,700 cyclists take the big ride in Philadelphia
abstract: 1,700 bicyclists tackled the Italian-style Gran Fondo Sunday morning on their way from the Art Museum to the hills of Montgomery County and the quaintest reaches of Chester County. The Philadelphia event was based on Italian treks that attract masses of cyclists. The local ride, with three routes of different lengths, was the third such event in the United States; the first two were in San Diego.

headline: Marcellus Shale not all doom and gloom
abstract: The best news that has happened again to our region and economy in many years has been the discovery of the Marcellus gas shale formation. The Pennsylvania Legislature is presently drooling over the prospect of passing a gas severance tax. The recent emergence of the anti-drilling coalition continues to discourage this discovery.

headline: GOP takes full control of Pennsylvania Statehouse
abstract: The voters swept many incumbents out of the PA state legislature on voting day. Among those replaced were House majority leader Todd Eachus and former House GOP leader John M. Perzel, who ran with the added burden of criminal charges. With Tom Corbett becoming the new Governor, and the House joining the Senate as Republican controlled, legislation will for the most part be driven by Republicans.

headline: County employees will soon clock in
abstract: Luzerne County commissioners approved the purchase of a time clock system, requiring mandatory compliance from employees. The system will be used to generate payroll and will be purchased with capital funds previously borrowed through bonds.

headline: Gerlach drops out of race for GOP nomination for Pennsylvania governor
abstract: On Thursday, representative Jim Gerlach quit the race for Pennsylvania governor.  Gerlach will no longer be seeking the state GOP nomination--making Attorney General Tom Corbett the GOP frontrunner.

headline: Freshman Republican makes reelection bid to U.S. House official
abstract: Freshmen US Representative Glenn Thompson announced that he will seek a second term in congress. He commented that he was in favor of healthcare reform, pro-business legislation, and against pay increases in congress.

headline:
PennDOT to get new county facility
Work on PennDOT's new county maintenance facility is expected to wrap up sometime next year
abstract: Construction has begun on a new Cumberland County maintenance garage and office building for the local PennDOT contingent. The building is expected to be done next year and will cost $5.7 million.

headline: Polls: Specter, Sestak race too close to call
abstract: A poll of Democratic voters released Wednesday morning show challenger U.S. Representative Joe Sestak D-Pennsylvania has closed the gap with fifth-term incumbent U.S. Senator Arlen Specter D-Pennsylvania in the race for Specter's senate seat. The poll gives Specter a 44 percent to 42 percent edge over Sestak.

headline:
State Senate proposal would require extra vote to raise property taxes
School board would need 6 not majority of 5; no hearings yet scheduled
abstract: A bill introduced by PA state Senator John Rafferty would make local school boards achieve a two-thirds ruling not a majority ruling in order to raise property taxes. Opponents of the law say it is counter to the democratic process to make property tax rulings require more than a majority.

headline: Philadelphia fire union criticizes city timeline, policies in fatal fire
abstract: Firefighters union leaders Monday challenged the City of Philadelphia's timeline in the fire death of a 12-year-old boy Saturday night, and continued to assail old and new city policies that they say slowed the department's response. Union general president Harold A. Schaitberger sent a letter to Mayor Michael Nutter asking him to address this issue.

headline: Pennsylvania capital, Harrisburg, skips payment, may move closer to bankruptcy
abstract: The city of Harrisburg has said that it will not make a $3.3 million municipal bond payment due in two weeks, a decision that could move the Pennsylvania capital closer to bankruptcy. Harrisburg Mayor Linda D. Thompson has adamantly opposed declaring bankruptcy, while the move has been advocated by the city controller and a growing bloc on the City Council.

headline: New Pa. GOP leaders eye a fee on natural gas instead of a tax
abstract: Although many Republicans have expressed support for a tax on Marcellus Shale, Governor Tom Corbett has reassured his detractors that he will stand firm on his no-tax pledge. He has, however, mentioned an openness to discussing local impact fees on the industry. Another goal of the incoming administration and the new Republican majority is to cut spending in areas such as the Department of Public Welfare.

headline: Synthetic marijuana critics propose banning it
abstract: The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration is placing an emergency ban on the five main chemicals used to produce synthetic marijuana. The ban will include a year of study to determine whether the ingredients should be permanently controlled. In Pennsylvania, lawmakers unhappy with the speed of the process, are proposing a state band on the five main ingredients.

headline: Upper St. Clair man to challenge U.S. Rep. Tim Murphy
abstract: Dan Connolly, a Democrat from Upper St. Clair, announced his plans to run against U.S. Representative Tim Murphy this year.  Citing Murphy's votes against President Obama's stimulus package and health-care proposals, Connolly argued that Murphy has voted against middle-class interests time and time again.

headline: Stimulus funds going to slashed programs
abstract: More than $3.5 billion in federal stimulus funds are going to projects that are being cut in US President Obama's federal budget. Citizens Against Government Waste called the situation inconsistent. The White House defended by saying that the stimulus money went to those programs because they were not mandated in the annual spending plan.

headline: McGuigan knocked off state representative ballot
abstract: Scranton School Director Kathleen McGuigan will be pulled off the Democratic primary ticket for the 113th legislative district of Pennsylvania. McGuigan's nomination petition was challenged by PA Representative Kevin Murphy and Scranton resident Joseph Pilchesky. Commonwealth Court ruled that 30 of McGuigan's signatures were invalid, leaving her two short of the 300 signatures needed to be put on the ballot. McGuigan plans to start a write-in campaign.

headline: Specter features Obama in ad as Sestak advances
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter D-Pennsylvania having lost his once comfortable lead in the U.S. Senate Democratic primary over challenger U.S. Representative Joe Sestak D-Pennsylvania, is hoping his ad which features an endorsement from President Barack Obama will help his cause. This counters Sestak's footage of President George W. Bush endorsing Specter  in the 2004 Republican primary.

headline: Gas industry is benefitting local airport
abstract: The Marcellus Gas industry continues to benefit the Williamsport Regional Airport. The most recent report comes from the airport leasing 1,200 square feet of office space to a global energy company. The airport has also leased land to gas companies, and has seen an increase in passenger commercial flights and private jet flights arriving into its airport. Also, through a federal Transportation Investment Generating Economic Recovery grant the Joint Rail Authority will see expanded rail siding on its railways that cater to the natural gas industry.

headline: Finally, Delaware River Port Authority reform might take its toll
abstract: Governor's Ed Rendell of PA and Christie of New Jersey are calling for reforms to open the Delaware River Port Authority's (DRPA) dealings and reduce political pull in decisions and hiring. DRPA chairman John Estey has already stopped free E-ZPass and car allowances for employees, and is asking for audits and a ban on handing jobs to relatives.

headline: Sestak camp airs first TV ad
abstract: US Senate candidate Joe Sestak began airing his first television ad Tuesday attacking his opponent Pat Toomey for comments made in 2007 about eliminating taxes on corporations. Meanwhile a new poll Tuesday found Republican Pat Toomey leading Sestak by 10 points.

headline: Pa. allows Verizon to quit distributing residential phone books
abstract: The delivery of phone books, which began in 1903, will soon come to an end in New York, New Jersey, Delaware, Florida and  Pennsylvania. Verizon petitioned the PA Public Utility Commission for the change, which was unanimously granted. This environmentally friendly move by Verizon will not completely end phone book printing, as customers may request a phone book by calling a toll free number.

headline: Rendell: NFL's decision to postpone Eagles game "a joke"
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell expressed his anger and disappointment on various media outlets over the decision to postpone the Philadelphia Eagles and Minnesota Vikings game due to weather concerns.

headline: Palmyra Area School Board prepares to award contracts for new school
abstract: The Palmyra Area School Board will vote to award 17 million dollars worth of construction contracts for the district's fourth elementary school.  The school is expected to cost 3 million dollars less than anticipated; the contracts await final approval by the state departments of transportation and education.

headline: Pittsburgh's snowfall for February keeps piling up
abstract: Snowfalls in the Pittsburgh area for February have created problems for snow removal. The snowfalls have set records in Pittsburgh.

headline: PPL plan frustrates residents
abstract: Residents to be affected by the planned building of a PPL Electric Utilities power substation and power line near Dalmatia expressed frustration at the proposal. The PPL states that the project is needed to reduce the number of power outages and the length of the outages. Residents opposed to the plan said that it would cause the value of their property to decrease.

headline: A late entry, Williams has a pool of backers
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Anthony Williams D-Philadelphia was such a late entry in the May 18 Democratic primary for Governor that political players wondered how he could hope to win. Williams has received millions of dollars in support, from those like him who support using public money for private-school tuition vouchers as one way to reform education in the state.

headline: End discount
abstract: The author states that the state should do away with the vendor discount given to retailers who collect sales tax at the point of sale. Under the act, a retailer can collect 1% of their sales tax total back. The tax was originally for retailers to cover the costs of collecting the tax but with the computer age the tax is calculated easily. The state, the author says, could use the money to plug the deficit.

headline: Critics cite delays in G-20 inquiry
abstract: Pittsburgh officials' are attempting to restrict a Citizen Police Review Board inquiry and deny discovery requests in court cases. The result is a coordinated effort to withhold details of police conduct during the G-20 summit last September, attorneys involved in the cases said. Witold Walczak, legal director for the American Civil Liberties Union of Pennsylvania believes there was a real effort to obstruct any investigation into what happened at the summit.

headline: For sewer rate hike, opposition continues
abstract: Parksburg residents continued to protest Pennsylvania American Water Co.'s request to triple the average customer's sewer bill Tuesday at the last scheduled public input hearings on the matter. All of the testimony, including service issues, is considered relevant, according to attorneys from the Office of Trial Staff at the PA Public Utility Commission and from the PA Office of Consumer Advocate. The company has requested it be allowed to increase revenues by about $8.2 million after completing a new wastewater facility in South Coatesville at a cost of about $55 million.

headline: Researchers find another piece to the AIDS puzzle
abstract: AIDS researchers have recently discovered why certain people can contract the AIDS virus but remain healthy without treatment. The about 1 in 300 people in this category, called "controllers," have an enhanced ability to signal danger so that "killer" T-cells can keep the AIDS virus in check. One man, Robert Massie, has lived with the virus for over 15 years and has dedicated his self to the very scientific research that has led to these findings.

headline: New Year events are casualties of the economy, burned-out volunteers and weather.
abstract: Carlisle has been forced to forgo many of its New Year events due to lack of sponsors and volunteers.

headline: Poor neighborhoods pay higher property taxes, city councilman says
abstract: Pittsburgh city Councilman Ricky Burgess said that property reassessment will not lead to shield homeowners in poorer neighborhoods from paying more than their fair share of real estate taxes. Homes in wealthier areas, like Squirrel Hill, are assessed well below fair market value. Burgess' chief of staff said that when property taxes are raised, the problem is exacerbated.

headline: Gas firms pay $18 million to drill Pennsylvania game lands
abstract: The Pennsylvania Board of Game Commissioners accepted over $18 million from gas drilling companies who were drilling into the Marcellus Shale beneath state-owned game land. The deal between the two parties also prohibits surface disturbances on state land by drilling companies, a provision that protects hunting on game land.

headline: Senate Mulls Bills To Keep Kids Off Casino Property
abstract: A woman was charged with child endangerment after she her child was found outside of Rivers Casino while her mother was inside playing blackjack. A bill in the Senate would impose fines on anyone who leaves a child under the age of 14 alone in an automobile on casino property.

headline: Perzel plea highlights how power corrupts
abstract: Former state PA House Speaker John Perzel has admitted under oath that he is guilty of public corruption. He and others, as part of the Bonusgate scandal that has rocked the state capitol, have misused taxpayer money for their campaign purposes. Perzel will get jail time and lose his pension.

headline: John Baer: Poetry in commotion as Pennsylvania crafts budget
abstract: The legislature's budget process is compared to a poem, given its resemblance to a battle.

headline: Audit: Property board values in error
abstract: The State Tax Equalization Board had a 65 percent error rate in a sample reviewed by state auditors. Errors in the board’s figures, which are used to calculate state funding for school districts and for other local government funding streams, may have resulted in  unnecessary tax increases for districts and municipalities that received less money than they were owed, and in other cases may have received more money than they were entitled to. The board has said it is conducting an internal evaluation of the problems.

headline: County workers’ leftovers: $138,757
abstract: Luzerne County government workers are allowed to build up sick days and receive cash for them. Three of the county's 11 unions have the right to cash in unused vacation days annually. These unions are detectives, court-appointed professionals and court-appointed support staff.

headline: PA's high court names a reapportionment chairman
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court made a decision on the fifth and final member of the Legislative Reapportionment Commission. Two Republicans and two Democrats from the PA General Assembly, who were already members of the Commission, were unable to agree on the fifth member, who also acts as the chairman. The Supreme Court of PA, under Constitutional guidelines, stepped in and chose senior judge Stephen J. McEwen, Jr as the fifth member.

headline: Southwestern Township Officials Will Hold Anti-Impact Fee Meeting Tuesday
abstract: Local officials are not satisfied with the PA General Assembly's plan to impose an impact fee on natural gas drillers. What bothers them are the new limitations on local governments. The bill cracks down on local authorities' abilities to zone and regulate drilling. Municipalities would not have the authority to bar hydraulic fracturing in residential zones.

headline: Senator seeks new tax from nonprofits
abstract: PA Senator Wayne Fontana will introduce legislation that would require major universities to pay real estate taxes on their property holdings. His reasoning is that a larger tax burden is placed on citizens when universities buy land that goes off the tax rolls. Similar bills have been mentioned that would eliminate certain health care provider's tax exemptions.

headline: Senator Baker: Monroe needs to be heard in redistricting
abstract: The commission charged with redrawing state Senate and House boundaries for the next 10 years should hold a public hearing in Monroe County, where many residents believe they were shortchanged in the process in 2001, state Senator Lisa Baker says.

headline: Campaign chores took 'whole days'
abstract: A former staffer for Sen. Jane Orie told an Allegheny County jury that she knocked on doors, wrote thank-you notes, kept lists of political donors and ordered food for political fundraisers, all while on state time. The testimony contrasted with statements made by Orie’s attorney, claiming campaign work was only done on compensatory time. Jane Orie is charged with theft and conflict of interest.

headline: Outgoing governor draws praise from Mayor Leighton
abstract: Ed Rendell spent over an hour on the phone with reporters to talk about his eight years as Governor of PA. He said that he is comfortable with the regulations in place regarding the natural gas industry, and the recovery that the state is making economically. Rendell also predicted that the Eagles would defeat the Green Bay Packers the upcoming weekend.

headline: Tax relief from slots play to lower 2011-12 school property tax bills by an average of $200
abstract: Homeowners in Pennsylvania will see a reduced rate of their school property tax this coming year thanks to casino tax revenue. The amount of tax relief per individual depends on the school district, but on average $200 should be saved per person.

headline: State Sen. Orie Testifies During Hearing
abstract: In her corruption trial, Jane Orie said that she would like keep William Costopoulos as her lawyer. In her first corruption trial it was shown that certain documents submitted were forged. The prosecution thought that the lawyer might have had something to do with this. Orie has waived her right to challenge any rulings based on effectiveness of counsel issues.

headline: New West Philadelphia High opens to much fanfare
abstract: A number of dignitaries gathered a new Philadelphia public school to encourage the students to take advantage of the opportunities in front of them. PA Senator Vincent Hughes and Paula McKinney, president of the West alumni association, gave talks.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 4
abstract: The Governor Tom Corbett administration is making recommendations for the Marcellus Shale Commission to protect drinking water from the harmful effects of natural gas drilling.

headline: As health plan for working poor struggles, state legislators seek ways to save it
abstract: With adultBasic, a low-cost adult insurance program, about to run out of money, three state senators have voiced support for legislation calling for reaching into legislative leader accounts to keep the program running. State Sen. Michael Stack, D-Philadelphia, the bill’s primary sponsor, called the accounts’ nearly $189 million surplus excessive. Gov. Tom Corbett has previously indicated he plans to let the program expire when the money does, offering other options, including a program called Special Care, provided by the state’s Blue Crosses.

headline: Pittsburgh mentors, money fuel education
abstract: Pittsburgh police officer Tamara Davis loves to volunteer her time to kids in the Pittsburgh School Districts. She does this through a mentoring program, which eventually leads to a $40,000 scholarship over four years, which can be spent at any college or trade school in PA. The United Way of Allegheny County sponsors a similar program.

headline: Congressional Democrats issue caution on fracking
abstract: A Democratic congressional report showed Pennsylvania had the sixth-highest volume of dangerous chemicals used in the process of hydraulic fracturing, a mechanism used to extract natural gas from the Marcellus Shale formation, in the entire United States.

headline: Expanded hours for beer sales
abstract: A bill allowing the sale of beer for more hours on Sundays passed the PA House and Senate. One beer distributor says that the new law will help him compete with delis.

headline: Who's who of Marcellus Shale gas industry meeting in Philly.
abstract: Many prominent gas drillers will meet to discuss the shale gas boom. Opponents are planning a rival event to spotlight what they consider environmental and public health concerns. Current Governor Tom Corbett as well as former PA Governors Ed Rendell and Tom Ridge will speak. PA Environmental Secretary John Hanger will moderate a panel on getting conservation groups and industry to work together.

headline: GOP puts Barletta, Fitzpatrick on protected list
abstract: The campaign arm for congressional Republicans named 10 of its own to an incumbent protection program, including Lou Barletta, Mike Fitzpatrick, and Patrick Meehan, three Pennsylvania freshmen elected in districts won by Barack Obama in 2008.

headline: Greater flexibility proposed for happy hour time
abstract: A bill removing the restriction keeping restaurants from holding no more than two hours of happy hour per day is heading to the house floor. The proposed legislation would keep the 14-hours-per week restriction, but would allow owners to configure the hours per day to their liking. The bill would also permit restaurants with liquor licenses to sell wine to go and to serve spirits at catered functions off the premises. Despite unanimous approval from the House Liquor Control Committee, supporters of the bill expect opposition from groups and individuals concerned about oversight, drunken driving and underage drinking.

headline: Police: Bank robbers tossed loot from car window in York County
abstract: Sade Long, 21, and Eric Watkins, 30, face robbery charges after robbing a bank and then tossing the money out the window during a high speed pursuit. Bail is set at $250,000 for Watkins and $150,000 for Long. The duo were involved in three other robberies, the police said.

headline: Legislators consider allowing legal notices on websites
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate is drawing concern over a bill proposed that is designed to allow school districts to post legal notices on their websites, rather than in the local newspapers. The Pennsylvania Newspaper Association is lobbying to get the bill thrown out, while proponents say it saves school districts money.

headline: NJ sports betting bill advances.
abstract: A new law in NJ is close to gaining approval. The law would allow New Jersey residents to bet on sports games from their home computers or smartphones. NJ Governor Cristie expressed his support for the measure.

headline: Utah firm plans Antis hydroelectric plant
abstract: A Utah company is looking to construct a hydroelectric power plant in Antis Township. The company recently sent a permit application to the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. There are major environmental concerns, including trout, Heritage land, and wildlife conservation and recreation.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 5
abstract: Despite some restored funding to public education via the state House's version of the budget bill, the Sto-Rox school district still faces a loss of funding.

headline: Feds' transportation dollars will be tight
abstract: Despite the Obama administration’s promise to seek another $53 billion over the next 6 years to build high-speed rail projects, House Republicans have made plans to scale back federal spending across the board. The main source of funding for transportation projects, the gasoline tax, has not kept up with demand from states looking to build or repair bridges and highways. Federal stimulus money for such projects is also expected to run out, meaning Congress will face much difficulty in drawing up a multiyear surface transportation package.

headline: Police: Traffic stop leads to seizure of more than 3 pounds of pot
abstract: After Emanuel G. Alicea went the wrong way on a one way street, police pulled him over and found that he was in possession of a large quantity of marijuana. He told police about a motel he was staying where more drugs could be found. Alicea was arraigned at the county's Central Booking Unit on various drug charges, driving with a suspended license and failing to obey traffic-control signals.

headline: Water trouble puts brakes on Harrisburg
abstract: Trouble with a water main near the state Capitol building in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania sent home 16,000 state employees at midday. The water main was accidently ruptured by a contractor, and the Capitol building along with some local restaurants were closed while workers fixed the issue.

headline: Corbett signs Adam Walsh bill into law
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has signed the Adam Walsh bill into law. This act imposes tougher penalties on convicted sex offenders. It also closes loopholes in Meghan's law. Part of the plan is to create a centralized internet database that will help states communicate better.

headline: Bad legislation
abstract: The PA House of Representatives has approved a measure that would allow the Republican majority's plan that would require that every voter show photo ID. Republicans say this will curb voter fraud, while Democrats claim that fraud is not a big problem. Some think that the measure will dissuade the poor and elderly from voting.

headline: Privacy of state tax credits guarded
abstract: Businesses getting tax credits in some state programs remain shielded from public disclosure, but Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner  says taxpayers should know how much these businesses are saving, given that the credits detract from public money.

headline: Open space: More than just a pretty place
abstract: With expected growth of 393,000 people and 241,000 jobs in southeastern Pennsylvania by 2035, the authors share their views on the importance of conserving open land. Pennsylvania’s Growing Greener initiative, which provides support to conserve the 167,000 acres of land that would be subject to development over the period, is facing considerable loss of funding. The authors support government funding of the initiative.

headline: Cuomo Outlines Fiscal Fix
abstract: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo said that he is poised to guide the state out of its fiscal nightmare. He has shown some what he terms an "emergency" fiscal agenda. He borrows policy ideas from Wisconsin and the US Presidential administration of Barack Obama. He is drafting a plan to consolidate and shrink the number of agencies, authorities and commissions by 20%.

headline: Corbett missed chance to cut legislators' perks
abstract: Instead of cutting the benefits and advantages of being an elected official, Governor Tom Corbett of Pennsylvania has cut spending on education, an issue that has some in the public concerned.

headline: Local GOP leaders not surprised at Santorum's departure
abstract: Former PA Senator Rick Santorum has quit his campaign for president, a move that has not caught PA Republican party leaders by surprise. Mr. Santorum has been trailing in the PA primary polls to Mitt Romney as well as the general election polls to President Obama. The decision to suspend the Santorum campaign comes two weeks shy of the PA primary.

headline: U.S. needs balanced budget amendment
abstract: Rob Gleason, former Republican Party of Pennsylvania chairman, writes about his feelings on a balanced budget amendment. He states that if America does not begin to live within its means, it will lose the economic foundation upon which the country rests. He states that we will lose the American dream.

headline: In Pennsylvania, most teachers rejected Gov. Corbett's urging of pay freezes in face of budget cuts
abstract: Teachers in nearly four out of five school districts ignored PA Governor Tom Corbett's request for a voluntary pay freeze. It seems that more teachers were laid off in those districts that refused to freeze. A PA School Boards Association survey found that 140 of the states roughly 500 districts imposed a pay freeze.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: PA Senate panel to address abortion clinic oversight.
abstract: A state Senate committee will be holding a public hearing in Philadelphia to address concerns about state and local government oversight of abortion clinics.

headline: Counties try to coordinate public transportation for senior citizens, disabled people
abstract: Thousands of seniors and those with special needs face difficulty traveling due to uncoordinated transportation service systems in various counties. A study done by the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation warned that demand for special needs transportation in Pennsylvania is growing faster than funding. The study cautioned against fare hikes, which research has shown results in seniors and others’ discontinued use of transportation services and calls for change at the state level.

headline: NJ’s Anti-Bullying Update Signed Into Law
abstract: New Jersey Representative Diane Allen pushed for a very strict anti-bullying law, which may now be the toughest in the country. The new law requires school districts across the state to make programs addressing bullying and calls on colleges to address bullying in their codes of conduct.

headline:
Corbett names Intergovernmental
Cooperation Authority member
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Corbett has announced a member of the Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority, a state-appointed authority which oversees city finances. Ann Dugan was the appointee, founder of the Institute for Entrepreneurial Excellence at the University of Pittsburgh.

headline: New congressional map wins final approval
abstract: The PA House voted 136-61 to send Republican drafted congressional redistricting to PA Governor Tom Corbett for signing. The bill groups Scranton, Wilkes-Barre, Pittston and Pottsville in the 17th congressional district in PA.

headline: City gets state grants to spruce up facades, build garage
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has agreed to release project grants originally awarded by former PA Governor Ed Rendell. The grants will be used to transform rundown buildings in downtown Pittsburg. A spokesperson for Mayor Luke Ravenstahl discussed how the city plans to use the grants.

headline: Washington County given five weeks to start reassessment
abstract: Washington County President Judge Debbie O'Dell Seneca gave county officials five weeks to reach a deal with a private firm to manage property reassessment.

headline: New state sprinkler law: Shower of safety or just all wet?
abstract: Supporters and opponents alike argue the pros and cons of a new state rule requiring sprinkler systems in single-family homes. Supporters point to the lives saved by such fire suppression systems, while opponents said the added protection is miniscule and warned of the effects a government mandate may have on those living in rural areas without public water supplies.

headline: Parents want crossing guard where student was seriously hurt
abstract: Some Wilson School District parents are urging Spring Township supervisors to post a crossing guard at the Spring Township intersection. This comes after a 12 year old student was struck there, nearly ending the child's life. The PA Department of Transportation will review the request for a crossing guard.

headline: Shuster discusses federal spending, 219
abstract: United States Representative Bill Shuster from western Pennsylvania spoke on several government-related financial issues, and how those issues were affecting his constituents. He touched on the budget proposal by the Republicans and dispelled rumors that it would cut certain social programs.

headline: State House creates task force to investigate child sex abuse cases
abstract: The Penn State child sexual abuse scandal has inspired PA lawmakers to create a taskforce to combat such abuse. Lawmakers said this was created in direct response to the Sandusky case.

headline: District reviewing whether Ackerman's comments violate buyout deal
abstract: The Philadelphia School District's legal office is looking into whether Arlene C. Ackerman has violated her $905,000 separation agreement. She disparaged chief financial officer Michael Mansch in talking about the districts massive budget hole on the radio. Her separation agreement states that she may not make public statements or disseminate private or public information.

headline: May revenue collection pads PA surplus amid battle over budget cuts.
abstract: The tax revenue collected during May 2011 increased the projected surplus as the PA budget process nears completion, with contention surrounding planned spending cuts.

headline: Judge refuses ethics expert testimony
abstract: Common Pleas Court Judge Jeffrey Manning ruled denied the prosecution the chance to provide expert testimony from state Ethics Commission official, John Contino, in the trial of state Sen. Jane Orie. Orie is charged with 10 separate counts, including theft of services, conspiracy, and violating state ethics law.

headline: March 15 special election timeline
abstract: Applications for absentee ballots available from Berks County Election Services; third-party candidates begin circulating nominating petitions. The rest of the article lists certain voter deadlines, such as when a special Senatorial election takes place.

headline: Pa. should bolster abortion clinic oversight
abstract: In trying to increase safety and sanitation in abortion clinics, the PA State Health Committee recently passed a bill that would require just that. Abortion facilities would have to follow the same health standards as any other health care facility, a measure some hope will save lives.

headline: Proposed restrictions would shut most abortion clinics in the state
abstract: Several years ago Planned Parenthood of Western Pennsylvania purchased a historic building in Pittsburgh for abortion procedures. A new piece of legislation could require such facilities to comply with ambulatory surgical center standards, which would leave this particular Planned Parenthood in violation of the law.

headline: Perzel pension peril?
abstract: Former PA House of Representatives Speaker John Perzel pleaded guilty to eight counts of conflict of interest and theft as part of the Bonusgate scandal. He also said goodbye to his close to $90,000 pension. A spokesman for the PA Attorney General's Office thinks that this is justified.

headline: State bill does what federal laws should do
abstract: The author asserts that measures against illegal immigration being taken by the State Senate should be introduced on the federal level

headline: Raise stakes for boaters
abstract: Author supports stricter penalties for those operating boats under the influence of drugs or alcohol. Boating’s status as a recreational activity often results in less pervasive enforcement than on land.

headline: Gas boom exacerbating parking problems in Towanda
abstract: The gas boom has brought a number of new faces to Towanda. Unfortunately the new workers take up many parking spots, which hurts local businesses. Towanda Borough Council President Mark Christini said the entire parking situation in the borough's downtown will be reviewed by Towanda officials, with a goal of helping downtown businesses.

headline: Corbett budget cuts foundation
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget proposal that would cut education spending has drawn responses that question his judgment. With the ever globalizing economy, America's youth and young adults need to be educated to compete with other countries, this author explains.

headline: Redistricting will bring a big change to Armstrong County
abstract: Years of conflict in the PA House and Senate characterize the debate over Marcellus Shale regulations. Now a rare joint House and Senate Conference Committee is tasked with drawing up a local impact fee, and updating safety, environmental and zoning regulations. The committee will consist of two members from both Houses' majorities and one from both Houses' minorities.

headline: GAS BOOMING
abstract: The United States Geological Survey has increased its estimates of recoverable natural gas found in Marcellus Shale to 40 times the original amount--84 trillion cubic feet. John Christiansen, director of public affairs for Anadarko sees the industry as a positive force in the communities it is present in. He cited job growth in certain towns.

headline: In Pennsylvania capital, former spokesman fights powers he once promoted
abstract: The author describes Stephen Drachlers transformation from a spokesman for a state House leader to a spiritual leader and critic of the political system.

headline: Happy hour bill approved by Pennsylvania House panel
abstract: The House Liquor Control Committee approved a measure allowing bars and restaurants to hold as many hours of happy hour each day as long as the total does not exceed 14 hours per week. The current law permits two hours of happy hour per day up to the 14-hour-per-week limit. The measure will go to the full House for consideration.

headline: Test your house for tightness
abstract: Rich Dexter is part of the Home Energy Hero company. He uses infrared cameras to show where heat leaks from the home. His work can help save some up to 20 percent on home heating costs.

headline: Shale drilling sets up potential regulatory war
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency will most likely face a regulatory war over the environmental standards of Marcellus Shale drilling. While the PA DEP holds most of the regulatory power, the EPA acts as an overseer, a struggle for power that may appear in the future.

headline: Redistricting will bring a big change to Armstrong County
abstract: The PA Senate approved the Republican-drawn US House district map. Armstrong County will see a big change. There will be one congressman for the entire county. The districts of PA US Congressmen Altmire and Critz will be combined into one district.

headline: State parks must stay so
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is very enthusiastic about opening state land to natural gas drillers. Former PA Governor Ed Rendell issued a moratorium on further leasing of state forests. This was based a study that showed that no further leasing could occur without environmental harm. However, the Commonwealth Foundation has shown New York City's partnership with Central Park Conservancy has been beneficial.

headline: Barletta touts proposed legislation targeting ‘sanctuary cities’
abstract: U.S. Representative Lou Barletta has presented legislation that would hold municipalities responsible for enforcing illegal immigration laws by withholding funding from those who willfully choose not to.
