headline: Gerrymandering around the corner?
abstract:
The author wants improvements in the way state
legislative and U.S. congressional districts are drawn .The job of redrawing districts is left to a redistricting commission made up of the state Senate and House majority and minority leaders and a fifth member they agree upon. The author criticizes the lack of public input in the process.

headline: Health care program facing money crunch
abstract: Pennsylvania Insurance Department Press Secretary Rosanne Placey has said that more than 1,700 Delaware County residents who rely on adultBasic will be without health care coverage in February. There is a possibility that funding could offset this situation.

headline: Law would aid seniors who fall behind on property taxes
abstract: An ordinance proposition in Allegheny County, PA, looks to help senior citizens who were unable to pay their property taxes get back on track, before their homes were put up for auction. The current ordinance allows the sheriff or the public school district to auction off properties that missed on tax payments; the changes would make the selling through a licensed real estate agent, instead of the local government.

headline: Liquor privatization
abstract: The state may privatize liquor sales in the state. This would mean the end to of the state owned system run by the Liquor Control Board. Selling licenses could generate a great deal in windfall state revenue.

headline: Department of Public Welfare official's behavior over parking space is 'intolerable,' Rep. Ronald Waters says
abstract: Philip Abromats former deputy secretary of the Office of Income Maintenance within the PA Department of Welfare berated a black Harrisburg pastor for parking in his reserved space. PA Representative Ronald Waters and other PA Legislative Black Caucus members want to the department to explain their disciplinary policy for employees who act unprofessionally toward the public.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  12PM NEWS
abstract: A trial is underway dealing with violations of regulations on the gaming industry.

headline: State Senate honors O'Pake
abstract: The state Senate honored the late Sen. Michael A. O'Pake on Tuesday with a tribute by his colleagues on the floor of the Senate chamber.

headline: Erie man accused of placing cushion over infant's face headed to trial
abstract: Christopher Morschhauser will be heading to court over assault charges. He is accused of holding a sofa cushion over his crying son's face. Erie 6th Ward District Judge Dominick DiPaolo ordered that he stand trial on charges of aggravated assault, simple assault, recklessly endangerment and endangering the welfare of children. Morschhauser remains free on unsecured bond.

headline: Battlefield expansion bill reintroduced
abstract: Pending the passage of a federal bill, more than $700,000 in aid could be headed to the Borough of Gettysburg for improvements to its National Park. The train station in which President Abraham Lincoln gave his Gettysburg Address is the first on the list to receive improvements.

headline: Marcellus Shale opponents continue to give misinformation
abstract: The author thinks environmentalists' dismissal of House Bill 1950, a bill designed by PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Scale Commission, is radical. He thinks that their "free pass" rhetoric is misinformation, especially radio spots that claim that "many companies don't pay any taxes."

headline: Former state House Speaker Perzel and former aide to enter guilty pleas
abstract: Former PA Speaker of the House Perzel will soon face charges of wide-ranging public corruption as part of the Bonusgate trials. He is seen as the ringleader, accused of attempting to purchase millions of dollars worth of software that would give Republicans a competitive edge in elections. He wanted to use tax payer money. Former PA lawmaker Mike Veon has been sentenced to prison.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 5
abstract: Duquesne School District officials claim that the district will no longer be able to operate under the proposed state budget, though a state education official says the district will remain open in the absence of an alternative plan for the students.

headline: Harrisburg solicitor resigns, cites 'philosophical differences' with mayor
abstract: Harrisburg City Solicitor Phil Harper has resigned his post. Jason Hess has been named the acting city solicitor.

headline: Our view: Erie's high homicide rate shocks community
abstract: 15 or more people were homicide victims in Erie County in 2010. These are the highest recorded numbers since the 1960s. There was no pattern in the murders, but the root causes were poverty and the economy. The rest of the article tries to answer why a number of killings may have happened.

headline: Sprinkler repeal lauded by Everett
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed a law that repealed a mandate that required all newly constructed homes to built with a sprinkler system. Proponents of the measure said it would save new homeowners money, while also giving them the choice to install the fire deterrent device or not.

headline: GOP-made congressional map squeaks past PA Senate.
abstract: The new US House district maps have been narrowly approved by the state Senate. They push Democratic-leaning voters into districts where they are unlikely to defeat Republicans. PA Senate State Government Committee Chairman McIllhinney says that the plan is not perfect but is the best that the committee could do.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Could a board do worse?
abstract: PA Senator Mike Stack has suggested that the Philadelphia School Reform Commission be replaced with an elected board of education. Stacks bill would allow city voters to elect a nine-member board in a nonpartisan election. The mayor would be vested with the power to choose superintendents. This comes after the SRC's poor performance.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  6PM NEWS
abstract: Amidst the debate over how to use the Pennsylvania's projected surplus for 2011, the House Speaker has not ruled out spending it.

headline: Yogi Bear will protect your picnic
abstract: Author expresses frustration with the state Gaming Control Board and Former State Rep. Keith McCall.

headline: Montco set to get settlement funds
abstract: State Attorney General and Governor Elect Tom Corbett said his office will wire $8.4 million to government agencies throughout the state that were victimized in an alleged national bond bid-rigging scheme by the Bank of America. Montgomery County will receive about $2 million, however the county treasurer said that the county may need to route much of the money to the federal Internal Revenue Service, because of escrow and bond violations at the county level.

headline:
Guest Column: Corbett’s budget plan
will do great damage
abstract: The budget proposal by PA Governor Tom Corbett has drawn fire from some across the aisle. Opponents of the measure contend that it disproportionally affects different members of society, including the poor, inner-city members, while taking away basic insurance programs for them as well.

headline: Lehigh Valley Gerrymandering: You can't get there from here
abstract: The author is very upset with the gerrymandering that is evident in the Republican's new redistricting plan. He comments on one district that has been stretched across five counties to accommodate PA US Congressmen Dent and Barletta.

headline: Pa. wine kiosks get scathing review
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner has stated that the wine kiosks have cost the state about $1.5 million and alienated consumers. A strikingly high number or kiosks malfunction and that they rarely meet the sale threshold set by the PA Liquor Control Board. Wagner's report derided the PLCB.

headline: KYW-CBS  Philadelphia, PA  Eyewitness News
abstract: While large, Governor Tom Corbett's proposed cuts to education are not final.

headline: Corbett signs his first death warrants.
abstract: Tom Corbett has signed his first execution warrants as Pennsylvania's Governor for convicted murderers Dennis C. Reed and Aquil Bond.

headline: Yeager announces run for commissioner
abstract: Richard Yeager is the former chairman of the Greene County Republican Party. He ran against Bill DeWeese last fall for the 50th Legislative District seat. He will run for Greene County commissioner on the GOP ticket, and believes his business background makes him a suitable candidate to reform the county government.

headline: School nurse job isn't just band-aids anymore
abstract: The PA House measure that looks to lower qualification for school nurses is drawing complaints from some in the medical community. Certified school nurses have been attributed to the decrease in unexcused absences in the state's schools, yet the new law would allow for nurses who are not certified to work in schools, making the job more demandable.

headline: PA lawmakers try to wrap up, tie ribbons on bills.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett scrambled at the end of the year to finish up some important legislation. One issue on the to do list is a bill that creates taxpayer-paid vouchers to subsidize private school tuition for children of lower-income families. Democrats call the bill a gift to catholic schools.

headline: Bridges are boon for Montour Trail, but barriers to completion remain
abstract: Plans to build a bridge at the Routes 50-980 intersection cannot proceed until the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation moves ahead with realigning the intersection. A representative of the Montour Trail Council told the PA Transportation commission that he is eager to see the project completed so that bicyclists can be accommodated.

headline: Local Politicians React To Bin Laden’s Death
abstract: The reactions of various nearby-Philadelphia and Pennsylvania politicians to Osama Bin Laden's death are listed.

headline: Bitter bill: Republicans vote against better health coverage
abstract: Author wants the House to reject House Bill 42, which would shield Pennsylvania from the national Affordable Care Act. The author claims failure to implement the provisions of the federal reform will leave 1.3 million Pennsylvanians who already are uninsured without coverage.

headline: Franklintown seeks inquiry into borough's finances
abstract: Former secretary-treasurer Deb Walker collected about twice what she should have earned in 2009. Franklintown Borough Council authorized its solicitor on to contact the York County district attorney to probe the borough’s finances under Walker. Council President Dick Blouch said that accounting systems are being revamped in light of this situation.

headline:
Shippensburg parents, students stage mock bake sale at
Pennsylvania Capitol to protest education cuts
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget plan to cut spending towards the education sector resulted in a demonstration by parents from the Shippensburg School District, who held a bake sale in protest of the cuts in the Capitol Rotunda in Harrisburg.

headline: Corbett: Hybrid alcohol sales in Pennsylvania 'not privatization'
abstract: Pa Governor Tom Corbett is calling a bill drafted by the Liquor Control Board "not privatization," which he is after. The plan would retain the LCB and allow state stores to continue selling liquor and wine. Grocery stores would be able to buy wine and beer, said chairman of the board Taylor, a Philadelphia based state representative.

headline: Trial for ex-speaker Perzel, other defendants moves back two weeks
abstract: Dauphin County Judge Richard Lewis has moved the trial of former PA House Speaker John Perzel and five co-defendants. Perzel faces more than 80 counts of theft, conflict of interest, conspiracy and obstruction of justice. He is accused of using state tax money to boost Republican campaigns.

headline: Feds Go Back To Court To Seek Longer Sentence For Vince Fumo
abstract: A federal appeals court in Philadelphia has promised to expedite a ruling on a request to re-sentence former Pennsylvania state senator Vincent Fumo, a request by prosecutors to give him more jail time given the lack of reasoning for his quickly-reduced sentence.

headline: DCCC talks business
abstract: About 80 business leaders, members of the Delaware County Chamber of Commerce, met to discuss Governor Tom Corbett’s soon to be unveiled budget, as well as the possible privatization of liquor sales and Pennsylvania’s business climate.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Kan Tastykake be saved?
abstract: The author is dreaded to hear that Tastkake Co. may need to merge with another company or sell itself. He remembers beloved Philadelphia institutions like Wanamaker, Buten, Budd, Lit and Schmidt. The author suggests ways that the company might stay afloat, such as opening up a Tastykake Café.

headline: Quest for more table games - which could cut tax revenue
abstract: SugarHouse Casino in Philadelphia has requested the PA Gaming Control Board to allow more table games to be placed on their floor. Although SugarHouse has the fewest number of table games among all PA casino's, its revenue is in the top five. The casino is also asking to keep more of the revenue accrued from table games, instead of increasing tax rates, a request some gaming opponents see as unjustifiable.

headline: State Reapportionment
abstract: The Republican congressional reapportionment plan will soon be considered by the state Senate. Experts think that two democratic districts will be consolidated.

headline: State of emergency declared in PA
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has toured some of the worst damaged areas of PA after hurricane Irene swept through the area. He has asked US President Barack Obama to declare a state of emergency for the state.

headline: 6 state reps on fall ballot for local posts
abstract: Four Democratic congressmen and two Republican congressmen won primaries for seats in local governments.

headline: Nutter balks at no-bid contract to firm to fix Sheriff's Office computers
abstract: Pamela Pryor Dembe, president judge of the First Judicial District, circulated a draft agreement that named Lexington Technology Auditing Inc. of Conshohocken to prop up the Sheriff’s Office's nonfunctioning computer system in time for a March sheriff's sale, at a cost of about $650,000. The Nutter Administration and City Controller Alan Butkovitz have objected to the proposal noting the company has already received $110,000 in no bid contracts over the last  five months. Mayor Nutter’s approval is required.

headline: Perkiomen Valley teachers reject proposed pact
abstract: Teachers in Montgomery County's Perkiomen Valley School District overwhelmingly rejected a fact-finder's proposed contract settlement. In fact-finding, a neutral party takes each side's latest proposal and suggests a settlement. The proposal has not yet been made public. The 440-member Perkiomen Valley Education Association voted 308-9 to reject the proposal.

headline: Pittsburgh council moves to repeal ordinance banning leaflets
abstract: The Pittsburgh city council is expected to repeal an ordinance barring citizens from placing any form of literature on vehicles without owners' permission. The repeal of the ordinance is settling a federal lawsuit brought on by two Pittsburgh residences who believed their First Amendment rights were being infringed.

headline: Gas pipeline safety bill gets PA Senate's OK.
abstract: PA State senators approved legislation allowing Pennsylvania utility inspectors to enforce federal safety rules concerning gas pipelines. PA is one of two states that does not enforce the rules. Lines built in the most rural areas would remain uninspected by the state government, although they could be subject to various local and federal regulations.

headline: Budget cuts threaten medical aid program
abstract: The Cambria County Community Action Partnership may need to cut its transportation program for medical assistance clients, because of state cuts in funding. This program helps to transport hundreds to methadone clinics. The allocation was reduced by 24 percent for the 2010-11 fiscal year.

headline: Grand Jury issues report on Gaming Control Board
abstract: The author offers some details of a 102-page grand jury report on the Gaming Control Board.

headline: Rendell, wife separating
abstract: Former Gov. Ed Rendell and U.S. Circuit Judge Marjorie O. Rendell, are separating after 40 years of marriage. The news came in an brief email which stated the split is amicable. The couple has one son.

headline: How to save Tastykake
abstract: It is especially troubling to Pennsylvanians that Tasty Baking Co. is having financial difficulties, especially since taxpayers provided $32 million in low-interest loans to help the company relocate to the Navy Yard in South Philadelphia. The author makes satiric comments, suggesting that Philadelphia School Districts force kids to consume Tastykakes for lunch, and that Governor Elect Tom Corbett should not push to privatize liquor stores, but instead should have them switch to selling alcohol-soaked Krimpets.

headline: Pittsburgh-area jobless rate dips under 7 percent
abstract: The Pittsburgh area unemployment rate fell for this month, bringing it a whole percentage lower than the PA average of 7.8 percent, the PA Department of Labor said. The numbers are promising for the region, but the economy, according to labor economists, is not at full strength; a problem that could be keeping Pittsburgh from obtaining its economic frontier.

headline: Local expert presses single U.S. child-abuse reporting law
abstract: In a US Senate Subcommittee on Children and Families hearing, Anthony Mannarino, director of the Center for Traumatic Stress in Children and Adolescents at Allegheny General Hospital, said that the federal government should set national standards for reporting suspected child abuse. He also suggested increasing funding for investigating claims.

headline: Marcellus shale: Healthy questions
abstract: The US Geological Survey now estimates undiscovered Marcellus Shale reserves at about 84 trillion cubic feet, which is much lower than the US Energy Information Administration's 410 trillion cubic feet estimate. Drillers may have overstated the long-term productivity of gas.

headline: Still Assessing Storm Damage, Extension Sought
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has asked the Federal Emergency Management Agency, FEMA, to extend its May 24 deadline for Pennsylvania to request a major disaster declaration for damage from recent severe storms to allow more time to assess damage.

headline: Vogel pushes to reduce Legislature
abstract:
State Sen. Elder Vogel Jr. has reintroduced legislation that would slash the size of the
Legislature by 40 percent and save an estimated $117.5 million. Under the legislation, the Senate would be reduced from 50 to 30 seats and the House would be cut from 203 to 121 seats. Since the reduction measure would amend the state Constitution, it will have to pass the Legislature in back to back sessions before going to a statewide referendum.

headline: 19 House Dems vote to oust Pelosi
abstract: 19 House Democrats did not vote for Nanci Pelosi for speaker of the 112th Congress, which shows discontent within the new caucus. The number of defections was the highest since 1997 when nine Republicans voted against then-Speaker Newt Gingrich, R-Georgia. The GOP has vowed to repeal US President Obama's health-care law when debates begin again next week.

headline: State legislator renews effort to purge illegal workers
abstract: A PA state Representative urged Governor Tom Corbett to implement a federal system, eVerify, to certify that all public agencies and private companies are hiring legal residents. The eVerify system is currently used by the US Department of Homeland Security, its purpose is to stop illegal entry into the United States. Several states have already implemented the measure.

headline: Pennsylvania Republicans unveil a congressional map to Democratic disgust
abstract: PA Republicans unveiled their new congressional district map, which consolidates two democratic districts. Critics were quick to attack the plan. Republicans hope to make the map into law soon.

headline: Legislation to label homes used as meth labs
abstract: A PA State Representative from the Lehigh County want to enact legislation that would require all homes that have been used to produce meth to be labeled as such, so that future buyers can know what they are getting themselves in to.

headline: Howard, Wagner Win Controller Nominations
abstract: Chelsea Wagner received the Democratic nomination for Allegheny County Controller in a three-person race, while her Republican opponent Bob Howard was unopposed in the Republican primary.

headline: Consider students who would remain
abstract: Author opposes taxpayer-funded tuition vouchers that send students to private schools while leaving others behind. The author claims taking children out of public schools does no decrease cost and that there are no measures in place to make sure money given to the school is spent wisely or track the success or voucher students.

headline: Half of Pennsylvania voters lose faith in Obama, poll finds
abstract: A statewide poll conducted for the Tribune-Review found that 50 percent of Pennsylvania voters disapprove of the job US President Barack Obama is doing. Many of those polled indentified job creation, federal spending, and reducing the national deficit to be the most important issues. Obama will soon announce cabinet changes.

headline: House of Representatives
abstract: One resident offers concern over the size and scope of the PA legislature, as well as its way of operation.

headline: UPDATED: New PA congressional map rife with gerrymandering
abstract: The new maps drawn up by the state Republicans for future congressional districts have been released. PA State Representative McIllhinney said all the changes were necessary because the state lost a seat. The district's of two democratic incumbents, PA US Representative Critz and Altmire, will be combined. Republicans are happy because they get to keep the 12 representatives they elected, while democrats are upset they are losing one of the 7 they elected.

headline: Pension board backs council bailout
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl got all members of the Pittsburgh pension board to agree to stand behind city council's pension bailout plan. This is to avoid a state takeover. If the PA Public Employee Retirement Commission disagrees with the pension board, then the pension fund falls to state takeover, which could force the city to tax and cut services.

headline: Democrats Bash GOP Budget Plan
abstract: A group of state and local Democrats criticized the House Republican budget proposal , saying it cuts too deeply into education spending.

headline: Our kids: Do state lawmakers care about them? Lack of legislation raises questions
abstract: Author claims lack of legislation and loopholes in Megan’s Law have left children vulnerable to out-of-state sexual predators. As the law stands, those sentenced to a lifetime of sex offender registration do not have to register with authorities. The author also voices frustration for the lack of progress following the “cash for kids” scandal and the failure to pass a bill mandating legal counsel for juvenile defendants.

headline: Bank to reimburse victims of scam
abstract: The PA Attorney General/PA Governor Elect, Tom Corbett, has said that thirty Pennsylvania school districts, local governments and authorities victimized in a national investment scam will receive a combined $8.4 million this week from a legal settlement. The Department of Justice and Bank of America were involved in an alleged bid-rigging scheme on municipal investments.

headline: Gov. Corbett works to enhance business climate
abstract: Two city Chamber of Commerce leaders in PA addressed the Governor's budget proposal and how it helps businesses across the state in this opinion piece. The new budget cuts spending and adds no taxes, while PA and the rest of the nation faces a poor economy. These proposals are meant to strengthen a weakened business climate in the state.

headline: Dodgers of codgers: Pa. pols evading poor elderly drivers
abstract: The authors decries typical elderly driving performance. The author cites some of the worst accidents caused by negligent or simply confused or impaired elderly. PA Governor Tom Corbett has signed legislation that has affected the youth. One bill limits the number of people that teens can have in the car. PA has the third oldest population in the nation.

headline: Hearing in Neshaminy blasts teacher strikes
abstract: The PA House Education Committee said that it needed to prohibit teacher strikes in order to ensure that children get the education that they deserve. House Bill 1369 would ban teacher strikes and school lockouts, and fine teachers who strike. PA Representative Rock said that 37 other states ban strikes and that PA was the strike capital of the nation.

headline: Impact Fee Legislation Still Not Introduced
abstract: State lawmakers are still waiting for an impact fee bill from Senate President Pro Tem Joe Scarnati.

headline: Transportation funding faces uncertain future in Congress
abstract: Public and private-sector transportation leaders are pressing Congress to get moving on a long-term funding bill, saying the nation's economic recovery is being harmed by layoffs and business losses. The previous funding law for highways, bridges and transit, called SAFETEA-LU, expired in September 2009. Congress has passed six short-term extensions since then, the latest of which expires March 4. According to the American Public Transportation Association, one-third of the companies it surveyed said they would shift their focus to other industries is a long-term funding measure is not passed. With Congress currently looking to cut as much from the budget and with little public support for a raise in the gasoline tax which provides funds for transportation, the passage of a long-term measure seems unlikely.

headline: Lessons from Europe: Washington must focus on the U.S. economy
abstract: It may be useful for the United States and Europe to "compare notes" regarding the way they dealt with and are dealing with the economic crisis. The European Union poured billions into stimulus programs, which ends up creating inflation, which ultimately benefits the rich. The Federal Reserve needs to make sure to correctly adjust after the stimulus, so as not to have them have the same effect as the tax cuts for the rich.

headline: Marcellus shale jobs booming
abstract: The Marcellus Shale natural gas industry in western PA has the jobs market swelling with new opportunities. Local colleges are offering training programs for skilled positions, while jobs from technical and financial support, to field work are available as well. Estimations say Shale development could last for 50 years, bringing many jobs and opportunities with it.

headline: West Virginia mulling new rules for gas drillers
abstract: West Virginia Lawmakers are seeking public input in its decisions to regulate the natural gas industry. Permit fees, well construction stipulations and other concerns are currently being discussed in a hearing.

headline: Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Corbett takes to the outdoors
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett just kicked off a kayak tour, which will take him through portions of the state. He hopes to draw tourism to the state's waterways. This is similar to the annual bike tours by former PA Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: Vote On Tuition Vouchers Delayed After Corbett’s Comments
abstract: It appears that, over the objections of Governor Corbett, legislative action on a school tuition voucher bill may be pushed back until fall.

headline: Landowners unite to deal with drilling companies
abstract: Members of the Loretto Landowners Group attended a community meeting at Our Lady of Loretto Community Hall to discuss negotiations with gas companies for the right to drill for natural gas underneath their property, which stands at around 35,000 acres in Cambria County. Groups such as this have become a major force in the industry. By educating their members about Marcellus shale, the groups have yielded higher payments and more environmental controls for landowners than they would have gotten as individuals. The groups aim to educate landowners in hopes that they understand what exactly is at stake for them when companies approach them with offers.

headline: Poconos man arrested in burglary, arson cases
abstract: Jacob Thompson was spotted by Poconos Mountain Regional police at the scene of a house fire and has been arrested on suspicion of arson in that fire and suspicion of a house burglary from the day before. Thompson is suspected of stealing firearms from the first home.

headline: Pennsylvania undercut pensions, study finds
abstract: Pennsylvania failed to meet its pension benchmark by a larger margin than any other state, a study by the Pew Center for the States indicated. The state paid only 31% of the money needed into the pension system, while the national average is 78%. The drop in investments arising from the weak economy is said to be the driving force of this problem.

headline: Apple pulls down driver's license app at Sen. Casey's request
abstract: US PA Senator Bob Casey urged Apple.inc to pull its app that helps one in creating a driver's license from any state in the country. Apple heeded the request, because of the security threat the app posed.

headline: Gov. Corbett begins two-day kayaking trip to promote tourism
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett just kicked off a kayak tour, which will take him through portions of the Pennsylvania. He hopes to draw tourism to the state's waterways to stimulate economic activity and generate more tax revenue.

headline: Pa. House Passes Junior Driver And Distracted Driving Bills
abstract: A junior driver bill passed by the House contains provisions that make it a primary offense for drivers and passengers under age 18 not to wear a seat belt and puts limits on the number of minor passengers in a car driven by a junior driver.

headline: Corbett funding plan for schools worries educators
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett has made a move to replace $337.8 million in state education dollars with federal education funds. The move means nearly $1 billion of this year's state education budget is supported by federal funding that may not be available in the future.

headline: Five festivals set for SteelStacks site
abstract: Five festivals celebrating music from Latin to blues will take place in the newly constructed PNC Plaza, which lies in the shadow Bethlehem Steel blast furnaces. Other projects include a visitors center, outdoor concert pavilion with lawn seating and other amenities. The Mayor of Bethlehem John Callahan spoke very highly of these projects, and their ability to weather the bad economy.

headline: CAPA states its case with pride to Obama
abstract: Six different high schools from across the nation are vying for President Obama to speak at their graduation. The schools, one being from Pittsburgh, are participating in the White House Commencement Challenge, where students create a video showing why their school achieves academic and social excellence. President Obama then, from the list of finalists, chooses one in which to speak for graduation.

headline: U.S. House redistricting maps delayed
abstract: The PA joint state House and Senate Government committee will soon meet to finalize the redistricting map. This map will show the changes to congressional districts in PA, effective January 2013. The map will account for a one seat reduction that is the result of stagnant population growth in the state.

headline: Superintendent buyouts to be audited
abstract: PA Representative Doug Reichelly welcomes an audit on the exit deal of former Allentown Superintendent. The new superintendent is promising to turn over all information to state auditors.

headline: ACLU of Pennsylvania Opposes Voter ID Bill
abstract: A house bill opposed by the American Civil Liberties Union that would require voters to show government issued photo identification when they go to vote waits for consideration by the state House of Representatives after committee debate.

headline: Legislature looks at school choice
abstract: The Chairman of the Senate Education Committee will lead a hearing on his bill to establish the Opportunity Scholarship and Educational Improvement Tax Credit Act.The proposal would increase funding from $75 million to $100 million for an existing program that gives tax breaks to businesses that finance tuition scholarships for children in lower-income families as well as offer families making no more than 130 percent of the federal poverty guidelines.

headline: Talk Philly
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell lost his temper while the cameras were on. In an interview with 60 Minutes, Rendell talks about the state's aggressive work to build casinos for revenue. When challenged on the issue of the negative aspects of gambling, Rendell became very defensive.

headline: Gun in hand is best border protection, NRA chief contends
abstract: National Rife Association vice president Wayne LaPierre argued that a personal gun is the best protection against border violence between Texas and Mexico. Under the US Constitution, border protection is a federal issue, but LaPierre stated the federal government was not performing its duty, leaving issues into citizens' hands.

headline: For-profit colleges should be held accountable, too
abstract: In 2011, 34 states cut funding to K-12 schools and most, including PA, cut spending to public colleges and universities. Over the last decade enrollment in private, for-profit schools has rapidly expanded. Studies by the US Department of  Education and US Senate's Health Education, Labor and Pensions Committee show reveal concerning statistics and dubious business practices.

headline: PA residents wary of Marcellus Shale drilling ask EPA for help
abstract: Officials from the US Environmental Protection Agency, the US Fish and Wildlife Service, the Centers for Disease and Control Prevention, and the PA Department of Environmental Protection, met with residents in Susquehanna County to discuss regulation of the natural gas industry. Residents discussed water contamination, air pollution and health problems brought that they blame on the natural gas industry.

headline: No limits for gifts to PA lawmakers
abstract: The author discusses the lack of limits for gifts to Pennsylvania officials.

headline: Vitali seeking tax on natural gas drilling
abstract:
State Rep. Greg Vitali plans to introduce legislation that would put a tax on natural gas extraction in the Marcellus Shale region. According to a release, revenues from Vitali’s proposal would go to the state’s general fund, local governments and environmental issues. Opponents of taxing gas extraction claim it would be job-killing and drive developers to other
states in the region.

headline: Bernanke: We are 4 to 5 years from normal employment
abstract: Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke is optimistic about the future of the US economy, but still thinks we need the $600 billion bond-buying program because unemployment will be high for another five years. The service sector is growing at it fastest pace in four years and consumers are spending more freely. A payroll tax cut is likely to boost this spending further.

headline: Budget lessons
abstract: A public forum led by PA legislators, members of the academic and college student communities, discussed the proposed $2 billion budget cut to state education spending. The speakers talked about the harm these cuts could create, and how consolidating the 501 school districts within PA could change the economic climate for state schools.

headline: PennDOT says it's open to study on the use of recycled slate waste
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transpiration has conducted research on recycled slate waste and is open to legislation requesting further research into the matter. The PA House requested that the department conduct research into the use of recycled slate in projects dealing with highway construction, concrete aggregate and drain fields, and skid-resistance aggregate.

headline: Education chief slams 101 schools
abstract: The PA Secretary of Education announced $66 million in School Improvement Grants to 26 of the state's lowest-performing schools recently. He talked a lot about money that was not given away because of school's not applying for grants. Pittsburgh Public Schools was awarded about $14 million.

headline: Senate GOP wants to spend, not save, surplus money
abstract: Some state Senate Republicans may prefer to use surplus money to restore cuts, rather than the put it in the reserve fund proposed.

headline: Obama pushes energy initiative, touts Penn State work.
abstract:
In a speech before 3,000 people at Penn State University, President Obama focused on proposals to promote energy-efficient buildings and touted Penn State's research in the field. The State College trip was the third in a series of visits to energy-related enterprises in as many weeks.
The President also used the speech to promote his view that the pursuit of technological innovations would create more jobs in the future.

headline: Police: Pa. man got boy to steal pills from father
abstract: Christopher Grimm, 20, allegedly used Facebook to get a 12-year-old boy to steal painkillers from his father and give them to him. He is in the Washington County Jail unable to post bond on criminal solicitation and other charges filed Wednesday. He faces a preliminary hearing in five days.

headline: Help struggling students
abstract: A PA Senate bill looks to help struggling families send their children to private schools. The Opportunity Scholarship and Educational Improvement Tax Credit Act, would give businesses tax credits to donate money towards scholarship funds within private schools. Members of both parties are backing this plan.

headline: Amend open records act to include state-related schools
abstract: Penn State officials cite an exemption in the Right-to-Know Law in their denial of requests for information concerning a 1998 investigation of Jerry Sandusky. The author feels that Penn State, Temple, Lincoln and the University of Pittsburgh should all be subject to the law, because they receive substantial funds from the state.

headline: Harrisburg Mayor sends City Council warning about fiscal plan vote
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson said that even if counsel votes down her fiscal recovery plan, she will go to PA Governor Tom Corbett to implement her plan. The state has agreed to give money to the city to pay for fire protection. Thompson's plan still includes the commuter tax.

headline: Unions rally against budget
abstract: Members from groups including the PSEA, SEIU and AFSME gathered on the Capitol steps to protest Governor Tom Corbett’s $27.3 billion budget, with much of the protest focused on the more than $1 billion the Republican wants to cut from education spending.

headline: Civic Arena auctions provide nice bonus for Penguins, sports authority
abstract: Two online auctions involving Civic Arena and Penguins memorabilia generated $80,515 in revenue for the Penguins and the Allegheny County Sports & Exhibition Authority, bringing the total money collected from the three auctions to $180,515. AssetNation, which handled the auctions, received a 10 percent commission on each sale. The SEA may use its share to help fund the demolition of the arena if the building isn't designated a city historic structure, while the Penguins plan to use their share to support youth hockey.

headline: Firefight ends: W-B gives thousands in back pay, pension to firefighters
abstract: Some firefighters in Wilkes-Barre are going to receive part of a $1 million settlement between the union and the city over a 2008 arbitration award.

headline: No-tax pledge follows Corbett in first 100 days
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has not backed down from his promise of no new taxes. His pledge is sparking debate in the state General Assembly and across the citizenry however, where some believe the Marcellus Shale drilling companies should be paying some form of "impact" tax in order to scale back on the proposed cuts to education in his budget plan.

headline: Corbett expected to sign expansion of beer sales on Sunday
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is expected to sign legislation that would extend hours that beer distributors can sell beer.

headline: Pa. auditor general wants to know who gave to Ackerman's buyout fund
abstract: The Philadelphia School District cut about 2,700 jobs to overcome a $629 million budget gap. They are now looking to buyout Superintendent Arlene Ackerman. Auditor General Jack Wagner is looking to make this deal more transparent to the public because it is their tax money. He is also asking the PA General Assembly to enact legislation to reduce or eliminate buying out contracts.

headline: Family resource center closing
abstract: State funding for community-based family resource centers throughout Pennsylvania was cut from the state House budget, but may be restored.

headline: Corbett names picks for veterans, aging departments
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has chosen director of the Bucks County Area Agency on Aging ,Brian Duke, to lead the Department of Aging. Gov. Corbett also named retired National Guard Commander, Wesley Craig, as the head of the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs. Their nominations are subject to Senate confirmation.

headline: The Harsh Reality Of The Falling Unemployment Rate
abstract: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that unemployment dropped from 9.8% to 9.4% in December, which is the biggest one-month drop since 1998. The most jobs came from jobs in the hospitality and health care sectors of the economy. The federal bond buying program should have acted to suppress the yield on a  10-year Treasury, however the opposite effect took place.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Featherman better for GOP
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer endorses John Featherman in the Republican primary for Philadelphia mayor. In a city where Republicans are outnumbered 6-1 to Democrats, Mr. Featherman is a candidate that wants to change the political climate in the city, and is most capable of holding Mayor Michael Nutter accountable in the upcoming election.

headline: Group concerned about insurance legislation
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Access Network is concerned with Senate Bill 1336 and House Bill 1983, because they will require all health insurers to get the PA Insurance Departments stamp of approval for large rate hikes. The plans will also do little to lessen insurance costs and little to allow consumers to challenges increases in these costs.

headline: Supreme Court justice sympathetic to Nealon
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Max Baer said that Lackawanna County Judge Terrence R. Nealon is a good judge despite the mistake he made in a 2004 voting district consolidation case. Nealon admitted that it was unethical to rally Democrats to oppose a voting district consolidation plan made by Republicans.

headline: Wissahickon acts to oppose state legislation
abstract: The Wissahickon School Board has adopted a resolution stating its opposition to both Senate Bill 911 and House Bill 1326, which would affect the maximum rate at which a school district can tax, and exceptions to the limit.

headline: Dover Area's second case of ethnic intimidation attracts concern
abstract: A second incident involving ethnic intimidation in the Dover Area School District has State Rep. Ronald Waters concerned about the school district’s commitment to keeping such acts from occurring. Dana Baker, assistant superintendent for Dover Area School District, said the incident is still under investigation by the school district.

headline: Luzerne County municipalities awarded PennDOT grant funding
abstract: Kingston Township will receive $300,000 from the PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT) to complete a 2-mile multi-use trail between the Borough of Luzerne and the village of Trucksville. The grants are one of 41 "Smart Transportation" projects, as part of the PA Community Transportation Initiative (PCTI). PennDOT received 238 applications from cities, boroughs, townships and other transportation and advocacy groups for funding.

headline: Document release adds paper to 'birther' fire
abstract: President Obama released a copy of his birth certificate, hoping to alleviate rumors and theories that he was never born in the United States, instead in Kenya where his father is from. The document showed he was born in a Honolulu, Hawaii hospital. In order to be elected as President, that person must have been born in the USA, sparking debate when the President originally declined to release the document.

headline: PA’s congressional maps will be made public Monday
abstract: The PA Legislative Reapportionment Commission will soon release it reapportionment map to the PA House and Senate for approval. PA Senator McIllhinney, chairman of the State Government Committee authored an empty bill with the intention of amending it next week, so as to speed up the political process.

headline: Mullery looking for tougher penalties for those who steal grave markers
abstract: PA Representative Mullery is looking for stiffer penalties for those who steal grave markers and sell them for scrap. He has noticed that this crime has happened all across the state and wants to do something about it.

headline: Sick-day pay may be on the way
abstract: Legislation that would require Philadelphia employers to provide paid sick days to their workers progressed in City Council.

headline: Obama taking energy message to Penn State today
abstract: In his visit to Penn State University, President Obama will propose a package of initiatives, including tax and regulatory changes, designed to promote energy efficiency in commercial buildings that account for roughly a fifth of all of the nation's energy consumption. The President will also tour several campus laboratories devoted to energy research.

headline: EPA sues owner of Homer City power plant
abstract: The US Environmental Protection Agency and Department of Justice recently filed a lawsuit against EME Homer City Generation alleging nearly seven years of pollution control violations. The US District Court said that the company made a number of required changes, but without hiring the best employees and without using the best technology.

headline: Scarnati unveils plan for natural gas drilling fees
abstract: PA Senate Pro Tempore Joe Scarnati introduced legislation that would levy an impact fee on Marcellus Shale natural gas drillers. Senator Scarnati said his plan falls into the Governor's guidelines, which were no new taxes on gas drillers and no collected revenue from drilling to go towards balancing the state budget. Scarnati's plan would place fee revenue in the hands of local governments.

headline: Film on gerrymandering shown
abstract: The new redistricting plan under consideration greatly benefits republicans. Democrats will lose a seat, as two democratic districts would be consolidated under the new plan. The state lost a congressional seat because of low population growth.

headline: Synthetic marijuana ban
abstract: The ban on synthetic marijuana and bath salts will officially go into affect soon. PA Governor Tom Corbett will sign the bill.

headline: Gov.'s cuts could cost Monroe County homeless shelter
abstract: Monroe County's Salvation Army could lose up to $30,000 next year under Governor Tom Corbett's proposed budget cuts.

headline: Harhut replacement could fall to governor
abstract: A provision in the state Constitution could prevent Lackawanna County, which is expected to have an opening for a new judge in 2012, from holding an election for this year.

headline: Truly tough habit to break Area 2nd worst for smoking
abstract: An internet group called the Daily Beast has ranked Scranton as the metropolitan area as second nationally for smoking. According to their study, 23.5 percent of adults smoke an average of 16.8 cigarettes each day. More than 60 percent of these smokers have tried to quit. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention ranked PA 40th overall for number of smokers.

headline: Surplus issue driven by far more than just money
abstract: Amid massive education cuts discussed in PA Governor Tom Corbett's new budget plan, the General Assembly is keeping millions in surplus dollars hidden. The surplus money is used as a safety net against budget problems and stalemates, but while one of the largest state legislators continues to operate, school funding is being cut dramatically.

headline: Sharper focus reveals depth of housing problem
abstract: The housing shortage that is accompanying the drilling boom of Marcellus Shale is affecting many local residents. Some who were not struggling two years ago now are. There simply aren’t enough low to middle priced rental housing available, a study conducted by Drs. Bonita Kolb and Jonathan Williamson of Lycoming College shows.

headline: Problems with staffing at Carlisle hospital
abstract: null

headline: Protesters see 'bind' in urged state cuts
abstract: Those protesting cuts to programs for disabled citizens contest that they will be under much pressure without them.

headline: Let's try this again: Ed Rendell joins bank to work on infrastructure deals
abstract: Investment bank Greenhill & Co. (GHL) has hired Ed Rendell as a senior advisor focused on "public-private partnerships, infrastructure projects and advising governments on a wide range of financial matters."

headline: At Obama White House, Back to the Future
abstract: US President Barack Obama has introduced new Chief of Staff William M. Daley to his office in the East Room of the White House. Obama also nominated Gene B. Sperling to head the National Economic Council. Many prominent figures of the Presidential Administration of Bill Clinton have joined Obama's administration.

headline: Group admits errors in energy tax report
abstract: The Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center, who was responsible for  report dealing with Marcellus Shale drilling companies and their dealings with state tax policy, has rescinded some information published in their report. The information dealt with the gas companies' tax rate when labeled as a limited liability company. The Department of Revenue was blamed for flawed mathematical data.

headline: Pa. prison officials dismissed complaints about abuse
abstract: Parents of an inmate held at the State Correctional Institution Pittsburgh complained to the Department of Corrections that their son was being sexually abused in the facility. PA Representative Deasy has made efforts to secure the safety of the inmate, but they have been denied by the department.

headline: In defense of Ackerman
abstract: PA Senator Anthony Hardy Williams defending Philadelphia School District Superintendent Arlene Ackerman: She has improved the district more than any other person before her. She is being undercut by petty politics. Williams cites statistics to show how she improved students' performance.

headline: Bethel Park outlines proposed program, staffing cuts for schools
abstract: The Bethel Park school board is preparing for cuts to their funding, delaying their budget vote pending the state budget's final passage.

headline: Lawmakers can make roads safer, save lives and money
abstract: Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety has given Pennsylvania a red light designation for what they consider to be weak safe-driving laws. Pennsylvania was faulted for not having or having inadequate versions of various laws, including a primary-enforcement seat belt law, which would allow police to stop drivers for seat belt infractions. The paper suggests that the  Legislature make simple, effective changes to state laws.

headline: Spring City man charged with attempted murder waives preliminary hearing
abstract: Juan Timothy Ruiz, 23, has waived his preliminary hearing in Spring City County court. He is being charged with attempted murder after allegedly slashing the throat of a family friend at a child's birthday party. District Judge Thomas A. Palladino’s presided over the hearing.

headline: Phila. school advocates take aim at aid cuts
abstract: Philadelphia's school district and teachers are facing budget cuts on the heels of PA Governor Tom Corbett's new spending plan. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter, among others, are lobbying extensively to roll back some of the proposed cuts in order to save art and music programs as well as jobs in the school district.

headline: For Sandusky's accusers, a chance to face him.
abstract: Ex-Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky will face the testimony of at least 6 young men in his grand jury sexual abuse trial. This boy also met Sandusky through the training camp Second Mile in 1977. The court is trying to keep the identities of the witnesses hidden from the public.

headline: Coin drops: economic boon or major safety hazard?
abstract: Coin drops, such as those often held by fire departments to raise funding for new equipment, are illegal under state law. Police ignore this law. A state police officer said that it is up to comps to act on any violation of the vehicle code. He said it is all about safety. If he sees a violation at a busy intersection, he may act.

headline: Plan for train from Westmoreland to Pittsburgh moves along
abstract: A commuter train project from northern Westmoreland County to Pittsburgh is expected to be approved.

headline: Santorum returns to South Carolina as he mulls a possible presidential run
abstract: Former Pennsylvania Sen. Rick Santorum will be returning to South Carolina on the heels of a possible presidential run. Santorum will speak at Tea Party events in Myrtle Beach and Charleston. It his ninth visit to the state.

headline: House plans test vote Friday on health care repeal
abstract: The Republicans are now in charge of the US House of Representatives, and they began by holding a symbolic debate to repeal US President Barack Obama's health care package. Democratic leaders in the Senate say they will block repeal. The big issues of the health care debate will likely be brought back to voters for the 2012 presidential election.

headline: Under pressure, Easton Area teachers up the ante
abstract: The Easton Area School District teachers union in PA has allowed their rate of pay to decrease in order to close a budget gap, something they were not willing to do originally. After being pressured by the school board, the teachers union agreed to open up its original contract and initiate some sort of pay freeze. The agreement stalled a board vote on the discussion of laying off over 150 teachers.

headline: Carbon monoxide monitors
abstract: A couple in Lancaster County was saved by carbon monoxide monitor that alerted them to high levels of the gas in their home. The gas is odorless and colorless. If the family had continued to sleep throughout the night, the gas leaking from their furnace could have killed them.

headline: OPINION: Pennsylvania should preserve Sunday hunting ban
abstract: Since 1873 PA has prohibited hunting on Sundays. This is an old "blue law." The author feels that the peace and quite on the latter half of the weekend that this law brings is worth it. The author says this with due respect to hunters and the PA Game Commission. PA Senator Emrick said that he has received concerns from hunters who would like to keep the law as it is as not to alienate farmers and other land owners who allow them to hunt.

headline: Veon trial delayed again
abstract: The trial of former state Representative Mike Veon has been delayed for a fourth time due to a scheduling conflict with defense attorney Dan Raynak.

headline: An Eagles-Steelers Super Bowl would be nuts
abstract: Former PA Governor Ed Rendell discusses he desire to witness a Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers Super Bowl during his time as Governor.

headline: Tyrone receives $516,324 grant
abstract: Tyrone Borough will continue its streetscape project with help from a half-million-dollar grant from the Pennsylvania Community Transportation Initiative. The funding will be used to improve sidewalks, curbs and replace streetlights. Johnstown also received state money to improve the entrance to the central business district.

headline: Second GOP candidate expected for attorney general.
abstract: David Freed of Cumberland County is poised to join the race for PA Attorney General. PA Senator Rafferty said he is seeking the Republican nomination. PA Governor Tom Corbett appointed Republican Linda Kelly to the position after he left it to become governor last year.

headline: Heat for drilling impact comments
abstract: PA Representative Sturla said that he was concerned with the social problems associated with drilling companies moving into PA. He cited an increase in STDs brought by transient workers that would affect the "womanfolk." He said that he did not mean to offend women by his remark, and is not sorry for touching on this real problem.

headline: Public notices to stay in newspapers after online proposal falters
abstract: A bill moving all local government notifications online and out of newspapers has been shelved.

headline: January's state tax collections show continued signs of recovery
abstract: Despite increases in collections of all three of Pennsylvania’s major taxes, House Appropriations Committee Chairman Bill Adolph cautioned against any hope that major spending cuts can be avoided. The state is facing an anticipated $4 billion to $5 billion budget deficit next year.

headline: Mine work proceeds though DEP permit status is in question
abstract: AMD Reclamation Incorporated is now drilling boreholes into a Perry Township mine. Environmental groups as well as the federal Office of Surface mining have raised questions over the permitting process. This concern comes after the PA Department of Environmental Protection revoked a revision to AMD's post-mining permit for the same project.

headline: State awards grant to Allentown affordable housing project that was killed by hockey arena
abstract: Allentown received a $2.25 million grant from the state's Redevelopment  Assistance Capital Program. Officials wanted to build an affordable housing complex on 700 block of Seventh Street. This location, however, is the cite for a new hockey arena. The plans for the hockey arena have been scrapped.

headline: 'Womenfolk' flap diverts the focus on gas drilling
abstract: PA Representative Mike Sturla, House Democratic Policy chairman, reacted negatively to the money pouring into the state from gas drillers, claiming that the drillers brought STDs with them, infecting the "womenfolk."  The author feels that the gas industry should pay a severance tax, and that comments like Sturla's hurt rather than help this cause.

headline: PA Senate OKs bill to preserve jobless benefits.
abstract: The state Senate  approved a bill to preserve 13 weeks of extended unemployment benefits for 135,000 jobless Pennsylvanians.

headline: Crawford County farmer nominated as agriculture secretary
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has chosen Crawford County Dairy Farmer, George Greig, to be the new secretary of agriculture. The nomination is subject to Senate confirmation.

headline: Counterdrug training center program may be curtailed due to federal budget cuts
abstract: Due to cuts to the 2011 federal budget, the Northeast Counterdrug Training Center at Fort Indiantown Gap expects to lay off 60 active duty National Guard. US Representative Tim Holden said that he is trying to gain approval for a stopgap measure to secure funding for the soldiers. Without the funding the training center will temporarily cease operations in February.

headline: Heal our health care system: UPMC must negotiate a contract with Highmark
abstract: Ken Melani, CEO of Highmark, and Jeffrey Romoff, CEO of UPMC, praised tiered networks that force providers to compete on cost and quality of health care. Experts believe this is a key way to control health care costs outside of government rate-setting. PA State Representative Dan Frankel introduced legislation that would require binding arbitration between Highmark and UPMC to cover certain hospitals.

headline: Officer honored
abstract: Over 200 officers from around PA gathered to honor a fallen law enforcement officer, Officer Lasso.

headline: Commentary: Harrisburg, Dauphin County division grows
abstract: The author discusses local government elections in Dauphin County, specifically changes state Senator Jeffrey Piccola wants to see made to local government structure.

headline: State urged to tax online purchases
abstract: Chris Rants, head of the Main Street Fairness Coalition, urged the House Appropriations Committee to join other states working to collect revenue from online retailers. Rants argues states are losing revenue and businesses face unfair competition from their out of state, online competitors. Under the collection system, states will determine rates and decide which items to exempt.

headline: Man accused of strangling his fiancée waives preliminary hearing
abstract: Gary Alan, 27, waived his preliminary hearing in Cumberland County court today. He is being charged with criminal homicide in the strangling death of his fiancée. The couple had no history of domestic violence incidents to which police had responded before the slaying.

headline: Harrisburg receiver gets public hearing
abstract: During a public hearing David Unkavich, who was picked by PA Governor Tom Corbett to solve Harrisburg's debt crisis, was questioned by Judge Mark Schwartz. The judge will soon announce whether he has approved the receivership.

headline: Political candidates get funny on purpose at Improve
abstract: Candidates' Comedy Night 2011 in Pittsburgh was a huge success, raising over $30,000 for children services in Allegheny County. Mr. Bicket, who is running for judge of the Court of Common Pleas, was in attendance. 350 people attended and the show featured candidates for political office doing three- to five-minute comedy bits. Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato was the headliner.

headline: CREW sues non-profit over Barletta ad and others
abstract: The congressional watchdog group Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington asked federal officials to investigate the legality of a nonprofit's spending on congressional campaigns last fall, including a television commercial that asked for help for Republican candidate Lou Barletta.

headline: Obama to slash community action programs
abstract: Community action agencies, which are nonprofits that help low-income Americans with such needs as job training, housing, energy assistance and child care, may see cuts in funding, leaving many organizers worries about the future of their communities.  These agencies receive a significant portion of their funding from an annual $700 million federal grant, which is in jeopardy as the federal government looks to decrease spending.

headline: Snow tapering off for morning commute; another dusting possible overnight
abstract: The Harrisburg area could see a few more light flurries this morning, but the 'clipper' system that brought a blanket of snowfall has passed through the region, according to Accuweather forecasts. A light dusting is expected next week. Many mid-state schools have delayed classes.

headline: City debt frustration boils over at Harrisburg Hope forum
abstract: City Council Attorney Mark Schwartz, PA Senator Piccola and Dauphin County Commissioner Michael Pries attended a event hosted by Harrisburg Hope at Harrisburg's Midtown Scholar bookstore. The commuter sales tax was discussed as well as the state take over of the city's finances.

headline: Sturla apologizes for remarks
abstract: PA Representative Sturla recently remarked that Republicans were downplaying the impacts of gas drilling. He said that gas drillers were bringing STDs into the state. He made an official apology for the remark.

headline: TXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  6PM News
abstract: Citizens protested Governor Tom Corbett's policies at Albright College's Commencement

headline: Castor weighs in on Hoeffel's decision
abstract: Democrat Joseph M. Hoeffel III’s decision to not run for re-election leaves Republican Bruce L. Castor as the only Montgomery County commissioner seeking re-election.

headline: 40 bank robbers jailed in 2010, officials say
abstract: A bank-robbery coordinator for the FBI's Philadelphia Division said that 13 of the 40 bank robbers jailed in 2011 were caught with the help of readers of the Daily News. The FBI solves about 20 to 85 percent of bank robbery cases each year, with a conviction rate close to 100 percent.

headline: LCB 'progress': Another joke
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board's (PA LCB) program that ships alcohol orders via the internet is in violation of a 6-year-old U.S. Supreme Court ruling--the PA LCB treats in state and out-of-state wineries differently. The author derides the LCB and then proposes that the state system privatize and take advantage of the estimated $1.6 billion in license sales.

headline: Plan for I-70/I-79 interchange receives $3 million federal boost
abstract: The US Department of Transportation has recently announced a $3 million dollar grant to reconstruct the Interstate 79-Interstate 70 interchange in South Strabane. In June the Federal Highway Administration invited states to apply for federal funding from 14 grant programs. The PA Department of Transportation will soon open bids for the construction.

headline: A penny saved or a penny burned
abstract: The author contests that more of the surplus should be directed towards savings, rather than being budgeted into other areas.

headline: Senate bill reforms judicial conduct board
abstract: A state senator has introduced legislation altering the way the Judicial Conduct Board handles complaints. The measure would require the board to make the decision on whether a complaint against a judge should be acted upon and stipulates that the board must continue its own investigation of a judicial complaint even in the face of a grand jury or law enforcement investigation into the same conduct.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Wanted: A new sheriff?
abstract: The author thinks that the senate should scrutinize PA Governor Ed Rendell's nominee to fill the Philadelphia Sheriff position. His nominee, Barbara Deeley, worked for former Philadelphia Sheriff John D. Green. The Committee of Seventy has urged the city to find an outsider, because they feel that Deeley acted unethically in her former position.

headline: Governor Corbett says school administrator evaluations should be revamped
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett says that both teachers and administrators should be evaluated as a result of education reforms that he would like to enact. He doesn't trust the strength of the current system of evaluating school employees.

headline: Ackerman goes back to work and says she’s staying
abstract: It is rumored that Arlene C. Ackerman is on the way out as Philadelphia School District's superintendent. She recently met with the Philadelphia Black Caucus and discussed her desire to stay on the job. Under Ackerman test scores have risen every year, as they had for the six years before she arrived in Philadelphia. Soon she will award schools that have reached benchmarks set by the federal No Child Left Behind Act.

headline: Excluding the elderly
abstract: The author predicts the effects of legislation that would move local public notices online from the newspaper on the elderly, and asserts that the bill must fail.

headline: Lawmakers revisit hand-held cell phone ban for drivers
abstract: One week after Pennsylvania received a failing grade for driving safety legislation from a national safe driving advocacy group, Pennsylvania lawmakers have reintroduced a proposal in the state House that would ban hand-held cell phone use and texting for all drivers and impose stricter rules for those under the age of 18.  A violation of the proposed law would be considered a primary offense, meaning police could stop a person for that violation alone. Supporters of making the violations secondary offenses claim policing them as primary offenses would be impossible because there isn't enough manpower.

headline: Pittsburgh's U.S. Steel Tower may be bought
abstract: US Steel Tower in Pittsburgh may be sold as its majority owners work to restructure its debt. Five Mile Capital is trying to seize control of the 64-story building through an auction. According to the Allegheny County website, the site is worth $175 million. Generally, tenants aren't impacted when a building changes hands.

headline: Presidential presence
abstract: US President Barack Obama visited the Wilkes Barre region to talk about his efforts to push Congress to extend one-year payroll tax cuts. He told school students that the tax “will be paid for by asking our wealthiest citizens to pay their fair share.” PA US Senator Bob Casey is on board with the plan.

headline: Pa. had most domestic animal rabies cases
abstract: Erin Moore of the PA Department of Agriculture has issued warning about rabies attacks. The number of human cases in PA has not increased in recent years, the number of domestic animal cases in the state is the highest in the country.

headline: Survey shows potential for rising PA school cuts.
abstract: A growing number of Pennsylvania's school districts appear to be considering layoffs and eliminating programs such as summer school and full-day kindergarten and raising taxes by more than the rate of inflation to help address significant cutbacks in state aid that are nearly certain, according to a survey

headline: Battle over PA House rules fails to materialize
abstract:
A potential showdown over legislative rules in the PA
House of Representatives did not occur, as Republicans opted not to go ahead with their threats to cut one Democrat from each legislative committee and change internal rules to make it easier
to kill amendments they do not support.

headline: Rendell regrets OK of '05 pay raise for lawmakers
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is about to leave office. His one regret is signing the 2005 legislative pay raises. He opposed the pay raise one year earlier but gave into the raise after legislators threatened to not approve of his agenda. Voters were outraged over pay raises for judges and  employees of the executive branch, which the court later repealed.

headline: Corbett-Appointed Harrisburg Advisor Left NYC Job After Assault Arrest
abstract: An advisor for the law firm that the Corbett administration hired to handle the Harrisburg takeover recently resigned from a post as New York City deputy mayor due to a domestic violence incident with his wife. Charges were never filed in the incident.

headline: Pa. Department of Health faults Carlisle Regional Medical Center's long emergency-room waits
abstract: The PA Department of Health checked to see if emergency room care at Carlisle Regional Medical Center was adequate. This means that patients are receiving "prompt evaluation and treatment." The hospital is not doing this, and according to the health department, a study in July showed that patients were still not getting proper treatment.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  6PM NEWS
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett was released from the hospital after back surgery.

headline: 'Jihad Jane' Pleads Guilty in Terrorism Plot
abstract: A PA woman accused of conspiring to wage jihad against a Swedish cartoonist changed her plea to guilty. Colleen R. LaRose, 47 pleaded guilty in US district court in Philadelphia. She worked obsessively on her computer to recruit people to wage a violent jihad in Europe and South Asia. LaRose has a sixth-grade education.

headline: Acting superintendent gets job in Kutztown
abstract: Nicholas Lazo has been part of the Kutztown School District for the last 32 years. The school board gave him unanimous support to become the superintendent of the district.

headline: Expert says Harrisburg takeover will likely trump bankruptcy
abstract: Bill Brandt is the President and CEO of Development Specialists, Inc., and has been keeping an eye on the Harrisburg debt crisis. He says that a state takeover of the municipality will likely trump the city's bankruptcy filing.

headline: Former state House Speaker John Perzel opts for lump-sum pension
abstract: Philadelphia Superintendent Ackerman thinks that Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter wants her to leave her position.

headline: Legal ad bill draws debate
abstract: There is a debate over whether or not local governments should be allowed to post public legal notices on their own websites rather than in newspapers.

headline: Two local wine kiosks reopen
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board is gradually restarting the high-tech dispensing machines across the state. Wine kiosks in the Wegmans in Allentown and Nazareth are back in service. There was a system wide shutdown because of certain malfunctioning machines.

headline: New talk of liquor store privatization
abstract: House Majority Leader Mike Turzai has gotten behind privatizing liquor sales in PA for the upcoming fiscal year, which includes a $5 billion deficit. Turzai wants to sell licenses for 750 retail and 100 wholesale locations throughout the state, which he said could generate about $1.7 billion in immediate revenues, as well as annual sales tax revenues of $350 million. PA is one of few states that still has state control over liquor sales.

headline: Governor Tom Corbett says he's disappointed in how Penn State has handled the Jerry Sandusky case
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett says that for two years he has been holding back voicing his disappointment in how Penn State handled the sexual abuse allegations against Jerry Sandusky. He oversaw the investigation as state Attorney General until he became governor.

headline: Former state House Speaker John Perzel opts for lump-sum pension
abstract: Former PA House Speaker John M. Perzel will soon face trial in the "Bonusgate" public corruption scandal. He took a retirement payout of $203,936 after being defeated last November. A spokesman for Rock the Capital has said that Perzel will get to keep whatever money he has thus far cashed out. Former attorney general and now PA Governor Tom Corbett brought the charges against him.

headline: Not everyone would get notices under proposed laws
abstract: New legislation would move local government notifications online and out of newspapers, which some feel compromises the citizens' right to know.

headline: County to receive $47,683 to cover missing tax revenue
abstract: Wilkes-Barre will receive close to $50,000 from a bonding company to cover missing tax revenue from Lake Township. Lake Township Tax Collector Donna Kocher failed to turn over this money between 2006 and 2009. There was no evidence of theft. The money went missing because of sloppy bookkeeping.

headline: Sholley installed as Union-Snyder president judge
abstract: President Judge Harold F. Woelfel Jr. of Union-Snyder has stepped down. His replacement is Michael H. Sholley, who has experience as an associate judge. This position allowed him to be responsible for his own case load without administrative duties. Sholley's pay will bump and his responsibilities will now include overseeing the probation and domestic relations departments and five district courts.

headline: Discussion of Penn State scandal
abstract: The Penn State sexual abuse scandal is discussed.

headline: Downsizing the legislature could yield many benefits
abstract: Common Cause and the League of Women Voters have criticized the PA General Assembly for failing to reduce the size of the legislature. Many other states have done so and PA seems like a state that needs a reduction. The article discusses other forms of legislative reform, such as term limits, and citizen legislatures.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 11
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett was released from the hospital after back surgery.

headline: White House Wants to Cut Pet Project of Late Rep. Murtha
abstract: PA Representative John Murtha died one year ago. He is credited with creating the National Drug Intelligence Center in Johnstown, PA. The White House wants to see it go. Conservatives argue that it is a waste of taxpayers money, because it never delivered the desired result--an analysis of drug networks. US Congressman Bob Casey suggested that the center change its concentration.

headline: Obama hopes Republicans will help with 'delivering jobs'
abstract: US President Obama said that he hopes that the new congress, which includes many new Republicans, will help him deliver jobs to the American people. He did not comment on upcoming battle over his health care bill. He said that "there's gonna be politics" but he is confident that both sides work together to deliver jobs for the 21st century.

headline: Strategic plan in the works for aging and disabled support programs
abstract: The state Department of Aging is crafting a 4 year plan to tackle the issue of providing services to seniors and people with disabilities in the midst of dwindling state funds. The biggest current hurdle to creating programs is finding reliable funding. The Department of Aging is looking to encourage more philanthropy and local partnerships to ensure seniors and the disabled have access to necessary programs.

headline: Big, new pipelines on tap for PA, Marcellus Shale.
abstract: Most new interstate natural-gas pipeline projects proposed to federal agency regulators involves PA. The projects already generate many jobs for steel mills, welders and so forth, but are also raising concerns about air and water pollution as well as eminent domain issues. PA Representative Mirabito is concerned about the environmental impact of a proposed pipeline that would run through Lycoming.

headline: WTXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  5PM News
abstract: Chesapeake Energy was given A $1 million fine for drilling violations that led to fires and contamination of private water supplies.

headline: New Cumberland man facing charges in false carjacking report
abstract: Timothy Watson told Harrisburg police that he was robbed of his vehicle at knifepoint by two men that jumped into his car as he was driving into the city. The police found that he was making a false report. He allowed a man to take the car to go get drugs, but he never returned. He is being charged with making a false report, but the police are in search of his car.

headline: People's politician Michael A. O'Pake remembered
abstract: PA Senator O'Pake died on November 22. 2010 following complications of open heart surgery. He served in the PA State Legislature for 42 years. This article includes a multitude of citizens' accounts of the lawmaker. One of them comes from a student of Gov. Mifflin High School who got to visit the senator in his Harrisburg office.

headline: States struggle to recover revenues
