abstract: While the broader economy recovers, state governments are still having difficulty getting back on their feet. A combination of reduced federal support, exploding entitlement costs and slowly growing tax revenue is spelling disaster for many budgets. The result is fewer programs for the vulnerable and higher taxes.

headline: Forced pooling for Marcellus Shale gas is nothing more than greed
abstract: The author calls "forced pooling" the heist of the century. This process, outlined in the Conservation Pooling Act (sponsored by PA Representatives Gergely and Everett), allows gas companies to access minerals against the wishes of property owners so that gas companies and neighbors can profit from what lays underneath your home. The author makes an argument calling into question the constitutionality of this.

headline: Masquerading need to privatize
abstract: The author asserts that the sale of liquor should be privatized.

headline: the Crawford County Conservation District, and the Great Lakes Regional Water Board.
abstract: Lower Paxton Township police responded to a 911 call that had no one on the line. The police tried to arrest a man in ski mask at the scene. He escaped out of a back window. The cops gave up chase after the man began to shoot at them. The man in the mask was trying to get the owner of the apartment to give him money.

headline: State tries out intensive parole program in Berks
abstract: Dellray Scheuren recently graduated from Berks County Court as part of a state pilot program to prevent offenders from committing new crimes. She has been stealing since she was a child, but she thinks that she is cured. 46 percent of state prisoners re-offend within three years of being released. The PA Board of Probation and Parole determines who is eligible for the program.

headline: Sen. Jeffrey Piccola says if voucher bill isn't passed in 2 weeks, it might get ignored in an election year
abstract: Sen. Jeffrey Piccola, R-Dauphin County is retiring at the end of his term and he is warning colleagues that it may be now or never for the school voucher bill. He argues that the bill may be too controversial to be tackled in an election year. There are conflicting reports as to what is expected to happen to the legislation.

headline: Pennsylvania attorney general has high-profile cases to prosecute
abstract: Linda L. Kelly has been installed as PA Governor Tom Corbett's successor as attorney general. She will keep with tradition and not run for a full four-year term in 2012, as she was midterm appointee to a state row office. In her time though, she hopes to wrap up the "Bonusgate" scandal.

headline: There will be new faces on Council
abstract: The 2011 Philadelphia City Council election brought the most new council members in an election since 1991.

headline: About 7,650 homes and businesses are without electricity.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has chosen George Greig to head the Pennsylvania Farm Bureau. This agency is charged with protecting and promoting agriculture and related industries and providing inspection services. Greig has also worked with the USDA Farm Service Agency Pennsylvania State Committee, the Crawford County Conservation District, and the Great Lakes Regional Water Board.

headline: Reform on Capitol agenda in 2011
abstract: As the new year begins, the PA State Legislature should take time to reflect on what it wants to do in the future, the author says. They should take time to figure out how to stay out of trouble, as many legislators face federal, state or county criminal indictments. The new Republican majorities have already expressed various reforms, such as PA Representative Sam Smith, who suggested a reduction of the size of the 203-member House.

headline: Port Authority braces for another slash to service
abstract: Unless Gov. Tom Corbett acts to plug a gap in transportation funding, transit in Pittsburgh is going to get a lot more difficult to use. Port Authority Transit officials say they will cut service by another 35% next fall. Service was recently cut that resulted in thousands of stranded riders and overcrowded buses.

headline: DeWeese right
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett, as former attorney general, filed corruption charges in late 2009 against PA Representative Bill DeWeese. DeWeese is now trying to tie similar theft-of-services charges to the governor's administration. A state trooper picked up the wife of a high ranking official from a police processing center after she got a DUI, and transported her home.

headline: Santorum: McCain doesn't understand interrogation.
abstract: Former Senator Rick Santorum stated that John McCain is mistaken in saying that waterboarding and other harsh interrogations did not lead

headline: National Weather Service cancels ice storm warning
abstract: The National Weather Service has canceled the ice storm warning for the Lehigh Valley. The service expects precipitation to taper off into scattered showers. Although the worst may be over, 10,000 homes are left without electricity. Many roads are icy still.

headline: Commissioners have full agenda for final year
abstract: In 2012, a home-rule government featuring 11 part-time council members and a manager will govern Luzerne county. The property tax rate will remain at 5.215 mills. Left to do in 2011 for the Luzerne County Commissioners is implementing a new time-management and payroll system with biometric time clocks for county employees.

headline: U.S. starts investigating Penn State's responses
abstract: The U.S. Department of Education has begun its probe into whether Penn State University officials broke federal law when they failed to properly notify authorities of child sexual abuse allegations. A team of four investigators have arrived on the campus to examine the evidence in the case.

headline: Turzai and Conti testify at liquor sale hearing
abstract: PA Representative Turzai is pushing House Bill 11, a privatization measure for state liquor sales. A representative from the Liquor Control Board thinks that the initiative is misguided. The new system would help to generate budget revenue. A union leader for workers of the LCB testified on their behalf.

headline: Fitzgerald, Raja win for county executive
abstract: Former Democratic county council President Rich Fitzgerald and D. Raja, a Republican Mt. Lebanon commissioner, won their respective primary elections for Allegheny County's Chief Executive.

headline: Kurowski to run for judge in Washington County
abstract: Washington County attorney Charles Kurowski is seeking the Democratic and Republican nominations for Common Pleas judge. He noted that he has experience in the US Supreme Court. The seat was left open after the death of Judge Mark Mascara. Three others are running for the post.

headline: $25M bridge project to hit the road
abstract: East Hempfield officials recently said that the intersection at Route 283 and State Road (Route 722) will be completed soon. The construction included two bridges, with a combined cost of about $25 million. McCormick Taylor received a bid for the final design of the project from the PA Transportation Department.

headline: DN Editorial: Schools out: District's plans should reach public
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is praised for its community outreach when it comes to school closures. The district has lost 25 of its students in the last decade, so it has a lot of experience in dealing with managing declining enrollment and allocating resources.

headline: Corbett's kayak trip
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett shed his suit and tie and began a 3 day kayak trip. The trip is to promote state tourism and natural recourses. He will talk about the natural gas industry, a very controversial topic.

headline: House Republicans' proposal would restore some education money
abstract: A budget developed by House Republicans would restore some of Governor Tom Corbett's cuts to education.

headline: US judge dismisses lawsuit against Bush wiretap program
abstract: A federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit that tried to hold the government accountable for a secret, warrantless wire tap conducted four years after the 9/11 attacks. Judge Vaughn Walker said that the Center for Constitutional Rights (CCR) did not have the necessary legal standing to bring such a suit. CCR wanted to show US President George Bush's actions were unconstitutional.

headline: Fox 29 News at 11AM
abstract: PA Representative Mike Vereb joins us today to talk about some of the issues at hand in PA from selling off the state run liquor stores, to pension reform. Vereb thinks that PA Governor Ed Rendell needs to enjoy his last few weeks in office and lay off the Republican agenda. Vereb commented that he is committed to job growth, the fair share act, and tort reform.

headline: Corbett’s picked for Harrisburg receiver getting mixed reaction
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is moving forward with plans to help Harrisburg recover from its crippling debt crisis.

headline: Former Pa. judge gets 28 years in 'kids for cash' case
abstract: US District Judge Edwin M. Kosik has handed former Luzerne County Court Judge Mark A. Ciavarella Jr. 28 years, the longest federal prison sentence ever given in a US political corruption case. He is guilty of having engineered a for profit sentencing scheme with a private juvenile detention center.

headline: Buckling up
abstract: The State House passed a bill that includes a number of provisions aimed at enhancing safety for junior drivers, including an increase number of supervised driving hours for learners, and limiting the number of teenage passengers in a junior driver's car.

headline: 2 commissioners spar over promotions
abstract: The Berks County commissioners sparred over employment issues. One board member objected to promoting employees into high-level positions and raising their salaries without searching for candidates with better qualifications. Commissioner Mark C. Scott said that taxpayers deserve to know the qualifications of employees that make six figures. Commissioner Christian Y. Leinbach disagreed with Scott, saying that he would not keep his mouth shut just because it is an election year.

headline: Howard Dean endorses Daley for chief of staff, rips White House
abstract: Former Vermont Governor Howard Dean said that William Dean would make a fine new chief of staff for the US President, Barack Obama. Dean has made clear that he will not run against the President in 2012 and it would be foolish for another person to do so. He also said that Obama should tread lightly on Social Security, Medicare, defense spending and taxes--four things that drive the deficit.

headline: State Sen. Gene Yaw alone on taking a 3 percent pay hike
abstract: Sen. Gene Yaw, R-23 of Williamsport is one of the few lawmakers that will accept his annual cost-of-living adjustment. He says that it is simply "part of the compensation for the job." He also says that he donates far more than that to charity every year. PA has the second highest legislative salaries in the nation.

headline: Auditor general: LIHEAP still being abused
abstract: A 2007 audit by the Office of Auditor General found criminal abuse in the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP). According to Auditor General Jack Wagner, the PA Department of Public Welfare oversight of this program has not improved. Pennsylvanians are guilty of using the social security numbers of the deceased to get assistance.

headline: House GOP plan for school funding ignores 'fairness'
abstract: The article criticizes the House Republicans' disregard for the fairness formula and their across-the-board cuts to public education.

headline: Philadelphia papers start charging for online version
abstract: It is cheaper to read the Philadelphia and the Daily News online. PA Governor Ed Rendell is joining the Daily News as a columnist. The price hike comes in response to tough economic times.

headline: Del. police say murder victim seemed confused on video
abstract: A prominent national defense expert was found recently in a downtown Wilmington landfill. John Wheeler, a Vietnam War veteran who served in the administrations of three Republican presidents and helped get the Vietnam War Memorial built, was seen in an office building as late as 8:30 p.m. days before. Witnesses said he appeared dazed and confused.

headline: New charges for PSU coach?
abstract: Critics are asking the attorney general's office why it took so long for their investigation into Jerry Sandusky's alleged child molestation to be brought to a grand jury. PA Gov. Tom Corbett was attorney general at the time of the investigation.

headline: Mayor wants Corbett, legislature to step up to the plate
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson says that if the city does not accept her plan to fix the municipal fiscal crisis, the results may be disastrous. She is waiting for PA Governor Tom Corbett to return her phone calls, as she is looking to the Governor for help.

headline: Editorial: LCB's new tune
abstract: The author asserts that expanding the state's liquor distribution will make its control over liquor sales even more ineffective.

headline: Bill to ease concussions is bogus
abstract: The NHL required helmets after someone died a few decades ago. It seems that there are more head injuries with helmets than without, though. Some think this is because helmets provide a false sense of security.

headline: Linden Street Bridge trench collapse victims were 'inseparable,' father says
abstract: A Chester County construction worker who survived a trench collapse that killed his co-worker and best friend while working under the Linden Street Bridge in Allentown remains hospitalized. The friends played middle school football and attended church together.

headline: Lawmaker introduces plan to eliminate property taxes in PA
abstract: State Rep. Jim Cox R-Berks County wants to expand the state's sales and income taxes in order to eliminate local property taxes.

headline: NY Gov. Cuomo says state considering commercial casinos.
abstract: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo has said that the state is seriously considering gaming as a revenue source. This comes after the state cut spending on health care and education to fend off deficits. Donald Trump, who has donated considerable funds to Cuomo over the years, would like to build casinos.

headline: Corbett factor, Marcellus shape Allegheny County executive race.
abstract: The opinion of Governor Tom Corbett and the debate around natural gas drilling are affecting the attitudes of the voters choosing nominees for Allegheny County Executive

headline: Winter fuels rise in asthma cases
abstract: Asthma is fueled by cool, dry air. That is why doctors at Jameson Hospital are seeing an increase in the number of asthma cases during the winter season. Extremes in weather are usually problematic for anyone with a repertory condition, said one doctor.

headline: Search for Suspect in Lewisburg Robbery Spree
abstract: Lewisburg Police think that John Pittman is to blame for four attempted robberies in one part of Union County. Police say Pittman has a criminal history. The public is asked to help find this man; police have released a photo. Pittman does not have an automobile and may be on foot or riding with someone else.

headline: Mistake on the lakes: The U.S. House bows to the shipping industry
abstract: A budget bill that passed the US House last week contains a provision that could harm our waterways. The bill would strip state regulations that ensure that ballast water from ships is free of invasive species. These species have been credited with serious ecological disruption.

headline: Rep. seeks probe of incident with state official's wife
abstract: PA Representative Bill DeWeese is calling on state officials to look into why a commonwealth employee used a commonwealth vehicle to pick up the wife of a high-ranking government official. PA Governor Tom Corbett, while attorney general, caught DeWeese and several other staffers in a corruption case that is still underway.

headline: Group opposes state fund cuts to nonprofits
abstract: The Greater Pittsburgh Nonprofit Partnership launched a statewide campaign to combat budget cuts to nonprofit organizations.

headline: Nazareth, Portland, Bethlehem downtowns are losing businesses
abstract: There is no more walking traffic in Nazereth. This has caused Marisa Balzafiore and many other small business owners to close shop. She owned a boutique on South Main Street. Nazareth Council President Daniel Chiavaroli said that this is the worst that he has ever seen the city.

headline: Tastykake maker: Financial issues could force sale
abstract: A new Tastykake production facility failed to produce projected savings. This could force the companies sale or merger, said the company's President Charles Pizzi. Tastykake has hired an outside financial advisor to examine the options ranging form refinancing its debt to sale of company. The company has also said the bankruptcy of A&P, Super Fresh and Pathmark have contributed to its financial dilemma.

headline: Death of former state Rep. Linda Bebko-Jones
abstract: Former state Rep. Linda Bebko-Jones, a Democrat from Erie died in Sunday at UPMC Hamot.

headline: Wearing their emotions to hearing
abstract: Former Luzerne County Judge Mark Ciavarella soon faces sentencing for handing out harsh sentences to teens in an elaborate money making scheme. The presiding judge won't allow juvenile testimony, so parents are wearing shirts displaying pictures of their children. US District Judge Edwin Kosik was afraid the testimony would turn into a circus.

headline: PMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  FOX43 MORNING NEWS
abstract: A Pennsylvania representative is developing legislation that would make bullying a crime .

headline: Allentown now offers domestic partner benefits
abstract: Allentown Mayor Ed Pawlowski has signed a bill granting benefits to same-sex partners of city employees. The city council unanimously approved the measure last week. The new law extends medical benefits to domestic partners of city workers. The ordinance was written by Columbia Law School's Sexuality and Gender Law Clinic.

headline: PUC gets 10 petitions opposing new NW Pa. code
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission says 10 groups have filed petitions opposing a plan to change the telephone area code of northwestern counties from 814 to 582. Phone customers in Erie, Crawford, Warren, Venango, Forest, Clarion, Jefferson, Elk and McKean counties would have the new code. Certain businessmen are opposed to the plan.

headline: GOP PA electoral vote plan might be out of steam.
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett has backed off a bill that would change the way PA allocates its electoral votes in presidential elections. Corbett says that he still supports the bill but sees no need to push for its implementation at this point.

headline: Some legislators reluctant to move quickly on state store sale
abstract: null

headline: Editorial: Improving education
abstract: The author discusses distribution of state funding for education and its effect on school choice.

headline: Officials optimistic site of center to be Georges Twp.
abstract: County commission Chairman of Fayette County Vincent Zapotosky thinks that the US Army Reserve Center should be built in the Fayette Business Park parcel. According to the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) 2011 report, this is the preferred location. This location has the least environmental impact. Zapotosky was aided by US Representative Bill Shuster.

headline: Rifle range shooting case moving forward to trial
abstract: Raymond Peake III has been charged with murder and the trial is moving forward. Peake's trial was complicated because his first attorney was not certified to handle capital cases in PA. Peake, 64, faces eight charges, including criminal homicide, robbery and aggravated assault, stemming from the death of Getgen, an attorney from Enola.

headline: Crow's Run: Yet another effort
abstract: Proponents of the Crow's Run Expressway project are facing an uphill battle to the tune of $60 million. Supporters say that truck traffic has greatly increased on local roads, but PennDOT says the money simply isn't in the budget. Local politicians are working to form a group that will be devoted to obtaining funding for the project.

headline: Gas driller opposes pipeline rules, asks landowners to raise concerns
abstract: The US Army Corps of Engineers have updated requirements affecting natural gas pipelines in PA. Chesapeake Energy has called on leaseholders to protest the new rules which they call "unnecessary, time consuming and redundant." A spokesman from the PA Environmental Protection Agency said the new regulations will streamline the permitting process.

headline: WTXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: Cuts to public education may likely lead to cutting kindergarten from full day to half-day.

headline: Central Pa. a 'corridor of human trafficking,' says lawmaker
abstract: A recent CBS 21 News exclusive shows federal agents raiding a Dauphin County home looking for human trafficking. PA State Senator Daylin Leach has written legislation that provides for a hotline to help solve the problem. Leach said that other states with the law have already seen it make a difference. The law would also expunge prostitution charges from trafficked persons.

headline: Corbett Names New Chief Of Staff.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has appointed his friend William F. Ward of Pittsburgh to his administration's chief of staff. Ward was a federal prosecutor who served with Corbett when he was the US Attorney for the Western District. Ward has also served on the Board of Probation and Parole, where he oversaw more than 1,000 employees in 54 offices across the state; he was also Corbett's First Deputy Attorney General in the PA Attorney General's Office.

headline: What took Corbett so long to build case?
abstract: The makings of the PSU sexual abuse investigation are examined.

headline: Commission maps out transportation funding
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Transportation Funding  Advisory Commission is tasked with finding about $2.5 billion to help the state meet infrastructure funding needs. A commission created in 2007 was created to do the same thing, by permitting the PA Turnpike Commission to raise tolls. The federal government nixed this and tolled I-80, however.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  5PM NEWS
abstract: Tuition voucher bills

headline: NEW – Police make an arrest in Benscreek bank robbery
abstract: Police arrested an Upper Yoder Township man in connection with a holdup this morning at First Commonwealth Bank in the Benscreek area. Additional details will be provided in tomorrow's Tribune Democrat.

headline: State launches tractor safety initiative
abstract: A statewide program launched recently will pay Pennsylvania farmers to put roll bars and seatbelts on their tractors. There were 58 farm-related deaths from tractor rollovers in Pennsylvania from 2000 through 2008, among the five highest death tolls in the country, according to Penn State. Many farmers in Lancaster County have older tractors without rollover bars and seat belts.

headline: Money a major obstacle to improving school lunches
abstract: Schools should be able to do more when it comes to the eating choices of its students during lunch. While stronger federal regulations were defeated by a Congress aligned with food industry lobbyists, schools should be doing what they can to encourage healthy eating while catering to their finicky eaters.

headline: Federal debt deal's impact on Pennsylvania murky
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is happy that PA didn't spend the $800 million in unexpected taxes last year, because the state may need it. Obama agreed to cut $2.4 trillion from the deficit and states may get stuck with the bill. There will likely be less money for mass transit and Medicaid.

headline: Everett likes House Republican budget
abstract: State Representative Garth Everett expressed his approval of the proposed Republican House state budget, specifically the re-allocation of education funds and lack of tax hikes.

headline: Financial crisis was 'avoidable,' inquiry finds
abstract: According to the Federal Reserve, the financial crisis was avoidable. It happened, though, because of widespread government failures, corporate mismanagement and extreme risk taking on Wall Street. Additionally, regulators allowed risky mortgage lending.

headline: Water woes concern locals
abstract: The Associated Press found that PA could not account for the disposal of about one-fifth of the 6 million barrels of wastewater produced over a 12-month period by shale drillers. Dr. Thomas Jiunta, president of the GDAC, said that he has complained about the lack of oversight on Marcellus Shale since it began drilling seven years ago. He feels that there should be a moratorium on drilling until the environmental hazards are better assessed.

headline: Penn State image damaged; what can university do?
abstract: A number of public relations experts are interviewed for their thoughts on what Penn State University can do to recover from the university's crushing sexual abuse scandal. Suggestions such as transparency and honesty, along with suspending Joe Paterno's sizable pension are discussed.

headline: Battling prison infection
abstract: Many people have contracting Merca in a PA prison. PA Representative Boscola has suggested using latex paint, which kills the disease. The prison has been sued a number of times because of this problem.

headline: WTXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: Commentators discuss the effects of natural gas drilling and the proper amount of regulation for gas drillers.

headline: Water Gap man admits possessing child porn
abstract: John Greene, 58, has pleaded guilty to possession of child pornography. According to the US Attorney's Office for the Middle District of PA, he used his computer to download child pornography between 2006 and 2010. The investigation was carried out by the FBI and local police authorities.

headline: Renewable energy industry shows surprising clout
abstract: Ohio’s renewable portfolio standard requires that 25 percent of Ohio’s energy come from renewable sources by 2025, and that half of that renewable portion be created in-state. Governor John Kasich said he might try to eliminate this mandate. Seth Kaplan of the Conservation Law Foundation stresses the number of jobs that the green economy has already made and the number that it will continue to make. This comes even though cap-and-trade is off the table in congress.

headline: She helped parents find strength in numbers
abstract: Sylvia Simms says that the Philadelphia School District retaliated against her for founding an advocacy group that targets the district for reform. Her access to overtime as a bus attendant for the district was cut off, along with her ability to work in the schools.

headline: EPA asked to test drilling chemicals
abstract: PA environmental groups joined groups from other states to ask the federal regulators to require natural gas drillers to perform testing and disclose information on the safety of the chemicals used in hydraulic fracturing. The petition was filed by the environmental law firm Earthjustice and requests the US Environmental Protection Agency to adopt rules that would require disclosure.

headline: Tighter restrictions on shale wells urged
abstract: Two environmental organizations have proposed 50 changes to Pennsylvania's Oil and Gas Act aimed at tightening environmental controls, increasing public review and taking into account the cumulative effects of Marcellus Shale gas development.

headline: Dozen Attend York Meeting With Guns
abstract: The law allows guns to be carried at council meetings in York. A large group protested a councilwoman's request to ban guns at council meetings by bringing their firearms. Many of those who brought guns were part of the Tea and Libertarian parties.

headline: Republicans seek to bleed Obama's health reform
abstract: Republicans armed with greater strength in numbers after the November election have their sights set on upsetting US President Barack Obama's healthcare reforms. Republicans have portrayed the changes to the healthcare system as a costly extension of government control over people's lives. Democrats plan to emphasize popular aspects of the law like mandatory coverage of children with pre-existing conditions and stress that the law's repeal would only add to the budget deficit.

headline: Trial in forged petition signatures case
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Robert Daniel Lavelle stands accused of forging petitions during a drive for the re-election of state Rep. Jake Wheatley.

headline: Harrisburg mayor's recovery plan slammed by lawmakers
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson will soon get a public hearing regarding her plan to lift Harrisburg out of debt and forgo state intervention. Council will soon vote on a plan.

headline: House-passed school-choice bill considered 'DOA' 5/11/2011
abstract: A bill passed by state House expanding a state tax-credit program for school choice, which many lawmakers consider a viable alternative to tuition vouchers, will be killed in the Senate, according to Senator Jeffrey Piccola.

headline: K2 synthetic marijuana banned on Lebanon Valley College campus
abstract: Lebanon Valley College has instituted a ban on synthetic marijuana. This comes after three students were sickened by the drug. The substance not only causes a marijuana like high, but also has dangerous health effects including racing heart, skyrocketing blood pressure and high anxiety/paranoia.

headline: Utility says lead levels in water corrected
abstract: Elevated lead levels that temporarily occurred in water delivered to some customers of West View Water Authority have been corrected. A spokesman from the Allegheny County Health Department said that there were never levels high enough to pose a health risk. The lead levels occurred because of the addition of chloramines to the treatment process, which is approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

headline: Mixed views
abstract: Not a single local lawmaker was in support of a bill that is likely to be the most impactful legislation ever in the region. Lawmakers agree that an impact fee is needed to help municipalities cover the expenses caused by the new natural gas industry, but disagree over the wording. The government should be focused on extracting as much money from the industry as possible because they will leave once the resource runs out.

headline: Perry County bus mom: Incident shows law modification is needed
abstract: All charges have been dropped against Tara Keener who entered a bus to help her child who had fallen ill. Under PA statute it is a misdemeanor of the third degree to enter a school bus without prior authorization.

headline: House GOP puts stamp on budget
abstract: The House republicans proposed their changes to the state budget, restoring some of Governor Tom Corbett's cuts, especially those to education, and making some of their own.

headline: Residents press Dallas Twp. supervisors over gas compressor plan
abstract: The Dallas Township Zoning Hearing Board will soon decide whether or not to allow Chief Gathering LLC to build a natural gas compressor station. The station would be 1,345 feet from the Dallas School District campus. The decision will never come into the hands of the township supervisors; it is entirely the domain of the zoning hearing board.

headline: A better map: Redistricting should be about fair representation
abstract: Pennsylvania will lose one of its 19 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives in time for the 2012 elections, because of new census data indicating that PA population is not growing at pace with the national average. PA is one of eight states where this is happening. Legislative redistricting will take place but the high court has the final authority to draw a map. When the 112th Congress takes office, Pennsylvania's House delegation will consist of 12 Republicans and seven Democrats.

headline: Washington lawmaker wants hearings into Penn State, Citadel sex scandals
abstract: Federal lawmakers are beginning to ask questions about the recent spate of sexual abuse scandals at major universities.

headline: Promise Academies strafed by budget woes
abstract: The chief business officer for the Philadelphia School Reform Commission has revealed more cuts to the district. He is looking to close a $35 million budget gap. In doing so he cut out Superintendent Arlene Ackerman's Promise Academies.

headline: WHTM-ABC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  5PM News
abstract: The Steel-High State Championship girls Basketball team was honored in the State Capitol.

headline: State urged to tax online purchases
abstract: Shoppers who buy from out-of-state retailers cost Pennsylvania about $706 million a year in sales taxes. Former Iowa House Speaker Christopher has urged the House Appropriations Committee to join other states that are working to collect revenue form online retailers. Brick-and-mortar business face unfair competition from out-of-state businesses that don’t charge sales tax.

headline: Harmar supervisors reach tentative accord on police contract
abstract: The Harmar supervisors reached a tentative agreement with township police over a new contract recently. In other news: Supervisor Michael Hillery was unanimously appointed Supervisor chairman for 2011. At the last supervisor meeting, the supervisors amended a zoning ordinance to make concrete recycling operations a permitted use in I-1 industrial zones.

headline: Gas industry concerns, issues raised at Coalition forum
abstract: A forum sponsored by the Lycoming County Health Improvement Coalition put residents in touch with lawmakers and the heads of various gas drilling companies to discuss the impact the industry is having on the community. Residents report an increase in poverty and crime as a result of the increased population brought by the new industry.

headline: National health care reform carries threat of bureaucracy
abstract: New bureaucracy to facilitate the purchase of health care insurance plans is looking very expensive. A few state government have opted to leave the expense to the federal government. PA Governor Tom Corbett's Office of Health Care Reform estimates that 1.3 to 2.1 million people in the state will purchase health insurance through an exchange, which would mean $45 million to $75 million in oversight.

headline: WHTM-ABC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  7PM News
abstract: House Democrats have criticized the Republican budget plan, citing cuts to welfare programs

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: Health-reform law has had some setbacks
abstract: US President Barack Obama's health care reform package has been declared unconstitutional in Florida federal court. This will set the stage for a heated US Supreme Court battle. Vinson, the Florida Federal Judge thinks that the mandate for all to purchase health insurance is unconstitutional. It is noted that the dissenting opinions come from Republican judges.

headline: Two men arrested for months-old Lower Paxton Township robbery and attempted robbery
abstract: Lower Paxton Township police have charged two men with burglary and attempted burglary of an occupied home. Furniture and electronics were taken from the first home and were found in the homes of Richard L. Workman and Luis Colon. Lower Paxton Township Police say Swatara Township Police provided information that resulted in the arrests and recovery of the items.

headline: Congressman seeks hearing on Penn State, Citadel.
abstract: California Rep. George Miller, the top Democrat on the House Education Committee called for a hearing on the recent sex abuse scandals at Penn State University and The Citadel. The hearing will determine whether changes are needed to federal law to help prevent these types of crimes.

headline: DePasquale Senior Fair
abstract: PA Representative Depasquale will host a senior fair in his district. Seniors will be able to learn more about state government services available to them.

headline: Palin's restraining order for PA man extended.
abstract: A restraining order against a 19-year-old Pennsylvania man accused of stalking Sarah Palin has been extended for six months, following testimony from the 2008 Republican vice presidential nominee that she feared for the safety of herself, her family and friends.

headline: PennDOT prepares for icy road conditions during evening rush
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) is anticipating icy conditions later today. The snow should start falling sometime after rush hour traffic. A spokesperson from PennDOT said that salting would take place overnight.

headline: East Hanover Township supervisors create manager position
abstract: East Hanover Township (Dauphin County), voted to create the position of township manager following a public hearing on the issue. The township budget has grown from $3 million to $7.8 million over the last five years. Supervisor David Marshall said that the increasing size and scope of the projects under way in the township need more attention than the supervisors and existing clerical staff can currently muster.

headline: Pa. House, Senate approve drilling bills
abstract: The PA House voted 107-76 to approve the controversial bill that would allow the state to impose fees on the rapidly growing natural gas business. A similar bill passed the state Senate two days earlier. Supporters say the bill will help the environment while stimulating the local economy.

headline: Ex-LCB chief: Sell the state stores
abstract: The push to privatize liquor sales in PA is gaining force. Its former chairman, Jonathan Newman has come out to say that the government monopoly is "inherently wrong." He cited inventory mismanagement. The Liquor Control Board was created after prohibition to make the purchase of alcohol expensive and inconvenient.

headline: Pa. panel eyes change to help military
abstract: A state House committee held a hearing on a bill that seeks to exempt deployed active duty military personnel or National Guard members from the 60-day marriage license validity time period.

headline: Former state Rep. O'Brien has died
abstract: Former PA Representative Bernard O'Brien has passed away. He was instrumental in securing funding to rebuild in Wilkes-Barre after a 1972 flood. He also helped to get the Cross Valley Expressway underway. He served 9 consecutive terms in the 121st District. He was at one time the Mayor of Wilkes-Barre.

headline: Goodbye, Governor? Hardly a chance
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is making waves, although he has only two weeks left in office. He can be found on numerous television shows talking politics. This comes after calling America "a nation of wussies." There are rumors that he will join the Obama administration in some function, but right now it appears that he is going for a full-time media job. Philadelphian's are already used to him offering post-game analysis after Eagles games.

headline: Corbett facing some fire for grant to Second Mile charity
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is facing criticism for a grant that was given to accused child rapist Jerry Sandusky's Second Mile charity.

headline: 'Model legislation' questioned
abstract: The left-leaning advocacy group Keystone Progress has accused PA Republicans of "turning the keys of state over to interests whose priorities don't match up with the average taxpayer." The American Legislative Exchange Council, which drafts legislation on conservative issues to which lawmakers can attach their names, gets funding from Exxon-Mobil and the Koch Foundation.

headline: Ag programs may get reprieve
abstract: There is consideration regarding the placement of some agricultural programs in higher education under the operation of the Department of Agriculture, to spare them from looming cuts to the higher education system.

headline: State requires sprinkler systems
abstract: The PA legislature has changed the Uniform Construction Code (UCC) to include a requirement that all new homes be built with fire sprinklers installed. The sprinklers are far less powerful than commercial sprinklers, and are intended mainly to prevent flashover. Data from the National Institute of Standards and Technology are used to reason the case for these sprinklers.

headline: Second man arraigned in 2007 Bethlehem killing at Diamond
abstract: A man charged in a 2007 killing outside a west Bethlehem bar was recently arraigned on homicide charges in Lehigh County Court. The victim, Debra Robberson, was robbed and then shot, which she died from. Her father said he believes she was targeted and killed because she was gay.

headline: DePasquale calls for outside, independent investigator in Penn State case
abstract: State Rep Eugene DePasquale, D-York, is calling for an independent investigation to get to the bottom of the Penn State sexual abuse scandal.

headline: Restrict how campaign funds are spent
abstract: US Representative Kanjorski's actions have people concerned about federal election law. After he lost his bid for a 14th term, his campaign finance committee started paying higher rents to its landlord for office space and document storage. The landlords are Kanjorski and his brother.

headline: Idea of moving legal ads from print to websites stirs debate
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers are considering legislation that move mandated public notices and legal advertisements from newspapers to government websites, amidst debate over the cost and practicality of the reform.

headline: Jobless rate continues its drop in December
abstract: According to the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, jobless numbers increased in the state and nation. However unemployment for the Juniata Valley decreased over the Christmas season. The rate dropped from 7.9 percent to 7.5 percent in December.

headline: Dollar General on a growth spurt
abstract: Cost-conscious shoppers and a soft retail real estate market have fueled rapid expansions for such discount retailers as Dollar General, Family Dollar and Dollar Tree. Dollar General recently announced that it will hire 6,000 people to fill positions in 625 new stores planned for construction in 2011. The firm has not announced where the new store locations will be.

headline: Area soot linked to 1,300 deaths
abstract: 1,300 deaths could be prevented in the Pittsburgh area annually if only for stronger federal air quality regulations. The Pittsburgh area ranked sixth in the nation for such deaths. Stronger federal regulations have been met with resistance by GOP governors like PA Gov. Tom Corbett.

headline: Allegheny County health chief moves to limit jail suicides
abstract: Allegheny County health director Bruce Dixon has proposed a five point plan to reduce the rate of suicide in prison. One idea is to provide inmates with tear-resistant gowns. Dr. Dixon also suggested improvements in guard training, inmate screening and lock down policies.

headline: Rally targets state budget cuts
abstract: Workers rallied at the River Common Amphitheater against state budget cuts they fear are a threat to public education, health care and the environment.

headline: District releases list of possible cuts
abstract: Juniata County School District needs to balance its budget. It is therefore making cuts to full-day kindergarten, tutoring, athletics, staff and class size. This comes also in anticipation of losing funding from the state and from federal stimulus money. The tentative budget includes a tax increase of 12.04 mills.

headline: Airport hangar project ready for liftoff
abstract: Hangars that often accommodate the small twin-engine aircraft of business owners will be built in Somerset County Airport. The project, at an estimated cost of $660,000 will be funded in part through state and federal taxes on jet fuel, airline tickets, freight waybills and international departure fees. The rest will be covered by the county. The county commissioners pursued a grant for the construction in 2008, but the county was unable to match the funds at the time.

headline: Switching Port Authority buses to natural gas boosted
abstract: The U.S. Department of Transportation will give the Port Authority of Allegheny County a $3.1 million grant to build a natural gas fueling station. The transit authority hopes to use natural gas powered buses in the near future. They are billed as being a boon to the environment and less costly than diesel buses.

headline: Philadelphia lawyer's fraud case shines light on troubled city program
abstract: Mike D. Jones borrowed about $150,000 from a city program five years ago to expand his new Philadelphia law practice. He has been charged with fraud by federal prosecutors who say much of the money went to pay personal expenses. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter shut down Philadelphia Commercial Development Corp. which was connected to this man through friends.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate takes action to confirm Gov. Tom Corbett's cabinet picks
abstract: Confirmation hearings were scheduled for four of Governor Tom Corbett's nominations, after the confirmation of seven others.

headline: Mundy reintroduces juvenile court legislation
abstract: PA Representative Phyllis Mundy has introduced legislation that would allow the Juvenile Court Judges Commission to analyze court cases and trends in the system in response to the Luzerne County kids-for-cash scandal. The commission would use its analysis to make recommendations for improving the system. The bill is stalled in the Senate.

headline: Officials celebrate groundbreaking for two 'flex' buildings at Navy Yard
abstract: Mayor of Philadelphia Michael Nutter, along with 2 members of Congress, were present at a groundbreaking ceremony for two buildings that totaled little more than 100,000 square feet. Such a small undertaking usually does not attract such high ranking officials, but this is the biggest project since May 2009. The buildings will be unique to Philadelphia's commercial real estate stock.

headline: Municipalities pleased with amendment to Pa. drilling bill
abstract: State senators representing Luzerne County were split on the wording of a new bill that municipalities say would restore some authority over Marcellus Shale development to them. The bill would allow municipalities to set their own drilling regulations as long as they are in line with zoning law for other types of industry.

headline: Commuter tax: If it's enacted, Harrisburg residents will be the ones who are taken for a ride
abstract: Many feel that it would be unfair for the citizens of Harrisburg alone to shoulder the $310 million debt crisis. This is because the city's debt is tied to bond deals on a faulty trash incinerator. The newspaper along with many citizens feel that Mayor Linda Thompson should have been negotiating with various creditors to solve the problem. Harrisburg residents don't think they should be punished through the commuter tax.

headline: Pippy defends overseas trips
abstract: State Senator John Pippy of Moon Township defended two overseas trips he took in 2010 that were highlighted in an Associated Press report on state legislators’ recently filed ethics reports.

headline: Illinois governor signs civil unions bill
abstract: Illinois Governor Pat Quinn recently signed landmark legislation that grants rights to gay and lesbian couples. They will have many of the same rights as their married counterparts. The new law allows gays and lesbians to get civil unions as a way to get many of the same rights given to heterosexual couples when they marry.

headline: Freshmen Bring Business Resumes
abstract: Congress will soon see 87 new Republican lawmakers sworn in. Many of them are novice politicians with significant experience in industries they will now help regulate. US Representative Michael Grimm will regulate Wall Street after working there. Representative Steve Fincher will bring his knowledge of farming to his post on the Agricultural Committee. Representative Bill Flores, who spent decades in the oil industry, will now oversee drilling in the Gulf of Mexico.

headline: DN Editorial: The race to legislate in Penn State scandal
abstract: The avalanche of new bills designed to tackle issues brought about by the Penn State sexual abuse scandal calls for a more organized and steady approach. While bills calling for stronger reporting requirements are definitely needed right away, other proposals can be more thoroughly examined.

headline: A tax by any other name is still a tax
abstract: Despite PA Governor Tom Corbett's promise to not raise taxes, he is considering a few new ways to raise revenue. One includes increasing the amount paid for auto registration and driver's licenses. Another deals with uncapping the state gasoline tax threshold. When Corbett took office he commissioned a group to generate ideas for raising transportation funds.

headline: Is it halftime for kindergarten? Youngest students could lose most under proposed state budget cuts
abstract: There exists a possibility that kindergarten programs will need to be cut to half-day due to the anticipated state budget cuts, specifically programs in the Clairton School District, despite the opinions of school officials and advocates for effective early childhood education.

headline: Healthwise first lady has Girl Scout role, too
abstract: Michelle Obama, first lady to US President Barack Obama, has made fighting childhood obesity her number one priority. She is the honorary national president of Girl Scouts of the USA, which sells many cookies. Some think that the dual roles are contradictory.

headline: Are Americans Wusses or Just Fond of Trash Talk?
abstract: US President Barack Obama was recently lambasted for killing a house fly with his hands. PA Governor Ed Rendell has called us a "nation of wussies," which raised a lot of eye brows. He now understands why this comment stung so much. In an interview Rendell recounts US history: "Our country was founded by risk-takers, an army of farmers and shopkeepers who knew they would be hung if they lost. We have lost our boldness."

headline: Former Centre County DA says Sandusky case referred because of 'indirect' tie.
abstract: Former Centre County District Attorney Michael Madeira said that he referred a report of child sexual abuse by former Penn State assistant coach Jerry Sandusky in 2009 to state prosecutors due to a conflict of interest. He had an "indirect connection" to the Sandusky family.

headline: Politicians expected to attend fair
abstract: It is county fair season, and as is tradition, politicians will be sure to show and take part in the festivities. PA Representative Fred Keller plans to do that this week. Tom Corbett went to the same fair that Keller will attend before he became PA Governor.

headline: WTXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: [14:48]   Preview Clip Protesters: Big business not carrying their load

headline: Report: Florida kids allegedly killed by mom lived in Carlisle area while dad attended War College
abstract: Julie Schenecker of Florida is accused of killing her children. Investigators think that she was under the influence of drugs. Neither Schenecker nor her husband, an army intelligence officer, had a criminal background.

headline: Jury to get case of Pa. judge charged with assault
abstract: Gerald Liberace, a Delaware County senior magisterial district judge in Haverford Township is accused of inappropriate contact with a teenage girl more than six years ago. Jurors are expected to begin deliberations soon. Jurors will listen to a taped conversation where Liberace is heard to say that he meant nothing sexual, even if some of his actions were inappropriate.

headline: End of the line for NDIC?
abstract: A new federal spending bill has $20 million dedicated to the closing of the Johnstown National Drug Intelligence Center. Members of the PA congressional delegation say they will work to protect the jobs the NDIC provides the region.

headline: Berks doctor taking another run for Gerlach's seat
abstract: The congressional redistricting process will conclude in 2012. US Representative Jim Gerlach has held the 6th district for 5 consecutive 2 year terms, while Manan Trivedi has his sights set on taking that seat away. Berks will likely become a greater part of this district, an area Trivedi is familiar with.

headline: Pennsylvania House approves plan to give restaurants, bars more flexibility for happy hours
abstract: The state House approved a plan that would give restaurants, bars and hotels more flexibility in setting happy hours, allowing establishments to distribute time out of the 14-hour-per-week happy hour limit however they want, as well as allow customers to buy up to three bottles of unopened wine from a restaurant to take home.

headline: Motorcycle event will come to Pennsylvania Farm Show Complex in April
abstract: PA has the fourth highest number of motorcyclists in the country. The 2011 Sturgis Road Show will stop by the Harrisburg Farm Show this year.

headline: Ed-speak: Wussies is one thing, but Rendell should keep casino opinion to himself
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell made clear his opinions on who should receive the state casino license. He thinks that the PA Gaming Board should not award the license to Mason-Dixon Resort and Casino, because he "wouldn't put one close to a battlefield." This is a questionable statement because his previous law firm, Ballard Spahr,  represents another casino that wants the license. Also, Rendell made no such comment about a casino built near historic Valley Forge, which was represented by Ballard Spahr.

headline: Gun madness: Some felons can be dangerous but still armed
abstract: The New York Times recently reported that thousands of felons are able to get their right to own a firearm reinstated without much oversight. While this used to be rare, effective lobbying from the National Rifle Association has caused rules to be relaxed in many states.

headline: Pa. ruling on assessment math could threaten Philly's real-estate income
abstract: New state property assessments in Philadelphia could cost the city a lot in tax appeals. The common value ratio for assessing property, however, has dropped from 32 to 18 percent. This could mean a flood of litigation, which would compromise city revenues. The Nutter administration is trying to shift to a system that would use actual values, thereby nullifying the common level ratio system.

headline: Corbett urges 'caution' after bin Laden killing
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett urged Pennsylvanians to be cautious in the wake of al-Qaida leader Osama bin Laden's death, given possible threat of retaliation from other al-Qaida leaders.

headline: Commentary: SEC in Harrisburg should be just the start of widespread probe of city's surreal debt
abstract: The Harrisburg 2009 audit has not been completed and filed. The US  Securities and Exchange Commission is coming to investigate. Bill Cluck of the Harrisburg Authority said that the agency should start by looking at the incinerator debt. The last mayor, Stephen R. Reed promised to fix the problem, but ended creating more debt.

headline: Chance of snow forecast for Harrisburg area
abstract: The National Weather Service in State College has said that the Poconos could see snow all day next Friday. Weather.com is forecasting around 1 to 3 inches of snow for the Harrisburg region in the next 48 hours. This could coincide with the opening day of the PA State Farm Show.

headline: Youth concussion law includes new requirements for coaches, trainers
abstract: The student-athlete safety bill aimed at stopping in the increase in head injuries will require that coaches and trainers adopt new methods and take new precautions to ensure safety.

headline: City leaders try to 'reach a consensus' on Harrisburg recovery plan
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson will present her city fiscal recovery plan in an attempt to persuade counsel members not to allow the state to take over. Her proposal was described as similar to that of the state's Act 47 team, which entails selling the incinerator and parking garages. One of the members derided the commuter tax.

headline: Pa. Revenue Department offers view of Marcellus Shale tax payments
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue released its report on how much natural-gas drilling companies have paid in taxes, amidst disagreements regarding a tax on natural gas drillings.

headline: We've had enough with property taxes
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett should eliminate property taxes, thinks the author. He thinks that the tax gives license to municipalities to spend recklessly. He cites Londonderry Township, where property taxes rose by 180 percent recently.

headline: Commercial real estate in Harrisburg area looking to bounce back in 2011
abstract: The AMC Colonial Commons 9 in Lower Paxton is already looking to re-lease. Developers are looking to build a massive commercial shopping complex in Swatara Township. Sewage and transportation plans have been approved to make this become a reality. However, the plans will not get off the ground unless the Central Dauphin School District and the township can agree to use a real estate tax payment called tax-increment financing to help fund those upgrades.

headline: Governor wants legislation soon that would require those witnessing abuse to call police
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is calling for the legislature to send him a bill that would require those who witness abuse to contact authorities.

headline: Court decision says Vienna Treaty doesn't apply to state prosecutors
abstract: Humberto Leal, responsible for the murder of a 16 year old, and his attorney tried to invoke the 1963 U.N.-enforced Vienna Treaty, which would require the US to tell foreign nationals of their right to foreign consulates. The US Supreme court found that state prosecutors were not bound by this.

headline: Political Prose: Facebook war and drilling bore
abstract: The author discusses a lawsuit brought against State Representative Jesse White by Robinson Township/Washington County Democratic committeeman Ray Bish, who sued White for defamation and invasion of privacy. The second part of the article criticizes Governor Tom Corbett's policy on natural gas drilling and education.

headline: Accused sex offender wants mentally disabled victim evaluated
abstract: Shawn Charles Stankina, 30 has been accused of sexually assaulting a 19-year-old mentally disabled man. He is challenging this and has asked a Montgomery County judge to grant a defense psychologist to evaluate whether or not the man was able to consent to sex.

headline: Tom Corbett has a fracking problem
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was not especially "green" during his tenure as Philadelphia's mayor, but as Governor he has a strong track record of being a advocate for alternative energy. Rendell could have done more to tax and regulate the natural gas industry, argues the author. Governor Elect Tom Corbett has pledged some new oversight of Marcellus Shale but nothing significant. His efforts will likely be too little.

headline: EDITORIAL: Curb outrageous pensions in public higher education
abstract: The state needs to get the costs of outrageous pensions under control. The Patriot News of Harrisburg found that Jerry Sandusky received a lump-sum payment of $148,271 from the Pennsylvania State Employees’ Retirement System when he retired in 1999. He receives monthly payments totaling $58,898 a year. Costs such as these should not be imposed on students paying ever higher tuition.

headline: Marcellus commission leaves door open on impact fee, pooling
abstract: The former secretary of the PA Environmental Protection Agency said that the recommendations from PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale Advisory Commission are non-controversial and useful. However, impact fees and forced pooling are likely to get a lot of attention. Both environmental groups and right wing Senate Republicans have derided impact fees.

headline: Time for Ringmaster Corbett to begin his budget circus
abstract: The author discusses the looming requirement for new Pennsylvania leaders to make begin work on passing a timely budget in the midst of disagreements on Gas drilling taxes and use of a possible surplus, even among those in leadership positions.

headline: County suspends loan program through the development authority
abstract: Northumberland County commissioners will no longer make loans via the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding. This is because the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) failed to submit substantial documentation. This decision by the commissioners is in accordance with the PA Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED).

headline: City extends deadline for real-estate tax payments
abstract: The Pittsburgh finance department is being lenient to its taxpayers. A resolution was passed to extend the postmark cutoff for 2010 to January 3, 2011. The original deadline was December 31, 2010, but the finance department felt that the holiday weekend may have tripped up some taxpayers. Paying taxes late results in a 10 percent penalty.

headline: Voter ID legislation faces opposition in Congress
abstract: U.S. Rep. Keith Ellison, D-Minn has sponsored legislation that would stop bills in 27 states including PA that seek to require photo identification to vote. Ellison and other voters' rights advocates contend that the legislation is set up to make it difficult for poor and minority voters to cast a ballot.

headline: Reflexively pro-privatization
abstract: This is an editorial that comments on other editorials covering the effort to privatize liquor sales. He talks of the changing nature of PA Representative Mike Turzai's legislative proposals to make the change, which the author believes cannot improve upon PA Liquor Control Board. According to the author, the new plan would generate 20 to 30 percent in new taxes, and would not result in lower prices.

headline: Marge Madness: Tartaglione defies criticism
abstract: Marge Tartaglione is a 78 year old Philadelphia Democratic ward leader. She recently underwent surgery and has a daughter that is being forced to resign as her aide because of illegal politicking. Her daughter's husband is in federal prison for bribery. She is running for her 10th term.

headline: Laubach gets 5-10 years in state facility
abstract: Ralph R. Laubach, 66, has been charged with repeatedly sexually abusing a female juvenile. He has pleaded guilty to five counts each of aggravated assault and indecent assault. He will have to register under Megan's Law for the rest of his life, said Juniata County District Attorney Cory Snook.

headline: State College firm buys businesses in Bradford County
abstract: Glenn O. Hawbaker Inc., of State College, purchased assets of a family business in Bradford County and is expanding its operations there. He purchased businesses dealing with coal, construction and quarrying. The quarries provide construction materials in the region. Some facilities provide the PA Department of Transportation with materials.  Hawbaker hopes to expand the businesses and employee more people.

headline: Pa. lawmakers scramble to draft child-sex-abuse bills
abstract: Lawmakers are scrambling to write legislation to address the vulnerabilities in the state's reporting system for child abuse. Sen. Kim Ward (R., Westmoreland) has put forth a bill that would require anybody receiving a college paycheck to report child abuse. Current law applies to K-12 schools and ambiguously to colleges in the state.

headline: Pennsylvania Budget Signed Minutes Before Deadline
abstract: For the first time in nine years the PA General Assembly had a finished budget in place before the start of the new fiscal year. He only signed the bill 3 minutes before the deadline, because he insisted on companion bills; one complicates raising property taxes for school districts. His budget makes significant cuts to education.

headline: The Marcellus Boom: Title/deed researchers jam some county row offices
abstract: Contractors hired by gas companies to research mineral and land deeds are sometimes elbow-to-elbow in Butler County. Butler Recorder of Deeds Michelle Mustello had to place a 31-person limit on the deed room, because of the potential hazard overcrowding has created. One company offered to pay rent to use space in the building and wants to donate microfilm viewing machines.

headline: State designates Sunday ‘Ronald Reagan Day’
abstract: State legislators have designated Feb. 6, 2011, as “Ronald Reagan Day” in PA. This is the date of what would be this former US President's 100th birthday. PA Representative Steve Barrar says that Ronald Reagan is one of our greatest modern presidents. Many other PA Representatives give similar praise.

headline: Jim Burn says he won't run for Allegheny County executive, controller
abstract: Jim Burn was elected Democratic Party chairman last year. He recently said that he would not run for Allegheny County executive or county controller. Some thought that he should run if County Executive Dan Onorato did not seek a third term. Burn's concentration is on working to set the stage for a democratic rebound after the widespread losses during last year's congressional election season.

headline: Corbett discusses Penn State scandal on Meet the Press
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is interviewed on NBC's weekly public affairs show, Meet the Press.

headline: Corbett accomplishes some priorities with budget
abstract: A pollster says that spending cuts are evidence that PA Governor Corbett's administration is committed to smaller government. Corbett's polling ratings are below normal for a first year governor. Corbett had legislative victories in lawsuit abuse reform and limitations on school districts' ability to bypass voters when raising property taxes.

headline: Corbett looking for education accountability
abstract: The public education system in PA will change markedly while PA Governor Tom Corbett is office. He encouraged teachers to take a one year pay freeze due to the budget. He also thinks voters should have more authority to veto local tax increases. PA Education Secretary Andy Tomalis said he is working to institute merit pay.

headline: Shale work not risk to air quality, says study
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection recently released the results of a study into Marcellus Shale natural gas operations and their effect on air quality. The study showed detected methane, ethane, propane and butane, but not in concentrations that could present a health risk. The results are now being evaluated.

headline: W.Hazleton OKs budget with property tax increase
abstract: Property owners in West Hazleton will be paying more in taxes next year, while wage earners will be paying less. The borough council adopted a new spending plan which includes a 0.6-mill increase on property taxes. However, the $1.9 million budget also includes a decrease in earned income tax (EIT), said a spokesman from the PA Economy League. The property tax increase will replenish the $115,000 loss the borough will experience from the decreased EIT.

headline: Corbett encourages additional potential victims to contact police
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is calling on other victims of the Penn State child sex abuse scandal to come forward to seek justice.

headline: Bald Eagle Rebounds in PA
abstract: In 1983 there were 3 bald eagle nests in PA. A record 203 have been counted in 50 of PA's counties this year. A PA Gaming Control Board spokesman said that the board will monitor the population with hopes of removing eagles from the threatened species list. Much of the rise in sightings is attributed to repopulation efforts conducted by the US Fish and Wildlife Service.

headline: State Sen. Kim Ward seeks limits on methadone treatment
abstract: A state audit shows that methadone treatment services cost taxpayers about $80 million a year. PA Senator Kim Ward will introduce legislation to limit these services. The bills would limit Medicaid payments for methadone treatment and transportation to such treatment. The state budget crisis inspired her to make cuts here.

headline: Report says fly ash sites leak chromium into water
abstract: According to Earthjustice and two other environmental groups, two southwestern PA fly ash disposal sites are contaminated. They found unsafe hexavalent chromium levels in groundwater near a landfill. The report released calls for tighter federal regulations on chromium. The report came out on the eve of scheduled Senate testimony by US Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lisa Jackson about the public health concerns of contaminated drinking water.

headline: 2 rookies ready to represent region
abstract: The 112th Congress is more Republican than its predecessor. US Congressmen Lou Barletta and Tom Marino are newly elected Republicans from the Northeast of PA. The budget deficit is a policy priority for both of these rookie representatives.

headline: Texting ban a big step, but lawmakers should do more
abstract: Lawmakers are applauded for banning text messaging while driving, but more must be done to make the roads safer. Studies show that operating a cell phone while driving can cause a level of impaired driving that is equivalent to a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent.

headline: Lawmakers could push shale tax or fee in the fall
abstract: Polls show that most PA residents support a fee or tax on natural gas drillers. A good-government advocate thinks that lawmakers will pass a shale tax just in time for election season next year. A spokesman from Democracy Rising PA thinks that the tax is inevitable when he looks at the collections the tax drives in other states. Many think that lawmakers will have to answer to constituents come next election season.

headline: IDs would help to thwart voter fraud, group argues
abstract: The House State Government Committee recently held a hearing on a bill that would require voters to show identification cards when they cast ballots. This is to combat voter fraud. However SeniorLAW thinks this would place undue hardships on seniors trying to vote. PA Representatives Daryl Metcalfe and Angel Cruz both have bills that would make the requirement.

headline: The Justice Department has a way to go on ending prison rape
abstract: The author is surprised that US Senators Edward Kennedy and Jeff Sessions agreed to cosponsor the Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA). The act was adopted in 2003 but has not come along as far as it should have by now. The author decries the lagging implementation of the bill, and demands that these standards also be adopted for immigration detention centers.

headline: Rookie congressmen to take office Wednesday
abstract: Newly elected US Congressman Tom Marino from PA will represent the 10th District, including parts of Lackawanna and Luzerne counties. Marino said that he is looking to cut spending, but is not sure where yet. He believes that encouraging business in the districts is contingent upon cutting federal taxes. He advocates the safe development of Marcellus Shale.

headline: Corbett addresses PSU crisis at bill signing ceremony
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett made brief remarks about the ongoing child sexual abuse scandal at Penn State University.

headline: Liquor Store Privatization Gains Support
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Turzai is expected to restart his push to privatize state liquor sales this week, with an endorsement from PA Governor Tom Corbett. The sale of liquor licenses could generate for the state anywhere from $200 million to $2 billion in revenue. Turzai would also change how liquor is taxed. The Independent State Store Union opposes the plan.

headline: East Penn finds $700,000 to slice from budget
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget, which calls for sweeping cuts to education, reduces by $2 million subsidies to East Penn School District. The district is looking to cut another $700,000 from their budget to compensate for the cuts. Superintendent Thomas Seidenberger recently made suggestions of areas to cut back, such as technology and capital projects.

headline: Lawsuit proposed to force Legislature to fix property assessments
abstract: Allegheny County Council members are considering two controversial property reassessment approaches. Council President Rich Fitzgerald is asking his colleagues to back a lawsuit which would declare the state's assessment broken and order the legislature to fix it. One council member is crafting legislation that would stop municipalities and school districts from collecting windfall real estate taxes if assessed values were to rise overall.

headline: Law would protect landowners
abstract: Currently the law allows a drilling company with a lease agreement with the subsurface mineral rights to move onto a property with little or no interaction with the surface landowner. This issue is very relevant as drilling companies buy up mineral rights to harvest natural gas from Marcellus Shale. US Senator from PA Richard Kasunic is pushing a bill that would require such notification and require gas producers to inform landowners of their intended operations so that they can evaluate property impact.

headline: Twice enough in Fumo case
abstract: U.S. District Judge Ronald L. Buckwalter of Philadelphia added 6 months to Vince Fumo's sentence instead of the 15 years sought by the prosecution. The prosecution is advised to stop appealing on the basis of the steep increase in restitution that was ordered and the fact that the judge thought the prosecution overcharged Fumo.

headline: Liquor Store Privatization To Take Center Stage This Week
abstract: The privatization of state liquor sales is a big issue in PA. A spokesperson for PA Representative Pileggi said that many issues that will confront the PA General Assembly this fall involve deadlines, though. For instance Congressional redistricting. Hopefully the liquor store issue will be resolved by the end of the year.

headline: Moves afoot to restart talks on Port Authority cuts
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato showed willingness to restart talks on contract givebacks that could allow the Port Authority to restore 15 percent of service that was eliminated this week. Commuters must now deal with jam-packed buses and rail cars. Union officials have said that Onorato must back away from his demand that they accept one of the two cost-cutting proposals he gave them.

headline: Meet some key Corbett cabinet picks: Ron Tomalis, Secretary of Education
abstract: Ron Tomalis was the executive deputy secretary of education under former PA Governor Tom Ridge. He is the new state education secretary under PA Governor Tom Corbett. In the former post, he butt heads often with PA education organizations, such as the PA School Board Association, and the PA Education Association. Tomalis has experience implementing the federal No Child Left Behind Act.

headline: State collects $191M more than expected in December
abstract: Pennsylvania Gov. Ed Rendell says the state collected $191.2 million more than expected in revenue in December 2010. Collections in every major tax category surpassed expectations. Rendell said that Governor Elect Tom Corbett will still have very tough decisions to make due to rising costs related to corrections, pensions and Medicaid.

headline: Corbett signs texting while driving ban
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett has signed a bill banning the practice of texting messaging behind the wheel.

headline: PA budget eliminates walking around money while giving agencies more power
abstract: Some PA State Democrats feel that the new budget eliminates their discretionary spending and limits their oversight over how certain state agencies can use their funding. The budget includes no walking-around-money. PA Representative Josh Shapiro thinks that this disrupts the system of the checks and balances.

headline: Stimulus spending can be tough to track
abstract: Recently US President Barack Obama and Vice President Joe Biden announced the Recovery Accountability and Transparency Board, which is intended to "foster greater accountability and transparency" in stimulus fund expenditure. One can use this tool at Recovery.gov. The board, however, cannot tell federal agencies issuing contracts with stimulus money what to report.

headline: Allegheny council committee seeks answers on Boyce ski lift
abstract: The ski lift at Boyce Park left 33 people suspended in the air for more than an hour. A committee of Allegheny County Council members wants to hear from maintenance crews to get a clear picture of the problem in an attempt to restore public trust in the mountain company. The success of the mountain is important because of the tax revenue that it brings to the community.

headline: The hair, the beard. Is that Vince Fumo?
abstract: A Philadelphia courtroom was treated to a glimpse of the effect of prison on former state Sen. Vince Fumo. Since being incarcerated 26 months ago he has gained 10 pounds and looked disheveled in court. His lawyers were asking for a lenient sentence based on Fumo's age and medical condition.

headline: January Toll Increase On Pa. Turnpike Is For Cash Customers Only
abstract: PA Turnpike tolls will increase, and the full burden will be felt by those paying cash. E-Zpass customers will not see an increase. A PA Turnpike Commission spokesman explained that this is a move to drive more E-Zpass enrollment.

headline: political briefs
abstract:
PA Representative Tarah Toohil has been appointed to the
House Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Crime and Corrections for the 2011-12 legislative session. Toohil will work on issues related to the states crime code and the PA Department of Corrections.

headline: Endowments at colleges, universities reflect start of recovery
abstract: According to the National Association of College and University Business Officials, the endowments of several of PA's major colleges and universities has increased since the recession. The University of Pittsburgh has an endowment close to $2 billion, the 28th highest in the country.

headline: Campaign rhetoric is about to meet Pennsylvania budget reality
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will leave PA with a number of budget problems. The national recession has had a huge impact on tax revenues. PA has lost federal stimulus funding of $2.7 billion. Also, PA has used a $1 billion one-time expenditure. This all conspires to create a $4.5 billion budget hole, which Governor Elect Tom Corbett is expected to fix. He plans to do this through cuts alone.

headline: Rep. Kevin Boyle calls for law change over Penn State arrests.
abstract: Philadelphia Democratic Rep. Kevin Boyle wants the law on reporting known instances of abuse strengthened so that instances of abuse like those at Penn State University can't happen again.

headline: Driver survey will help PennDot shape safety messages
