abstract: The PA Department of Transportation is asking motorists to take an online driver safety survey. The results will shape the department's safety messages. The survey also wants to see how often people are flouting the law.

headline: Liquor sale study to guide new bill
abstract: PA Representative Mike Turzai said that a study into the privatization of liquor stores commissioned by PA Governor Tom Corbett will help shape legislation into the selling of state-owned liquor stores. Corbett mentioned this move in his inaugural address. The governor is also interested in the revenue yield of the sale for the budget's sake. The Liquor Control Board currently operates 650 retail stores.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Reasserting the right to high-quality schools
abstract: The author relates school choice vouchers to the civil rights era integration reforms. He notes that the public school system varies widely in quality. He thinks that many Philadelphia kids should have an opportunity to try another school. The bill dealing with vouchers at the moment would enhance the Educational Improvement Tax Credit program.

headline: Computers That See You and Keep Watch Over You
abstract: A series of articles examining the advances in artificial intelligence and robotics and their potential impact on society: Prison guards are now being assisted by smart video technology, which can pinpoint when and where potential disturbances between inmates are occurring. Some computers can read a man's face to determine his heart rate. Others can remind doctors to wash their hands before surgery.

headline: Senate bill gives tax credit for property renovation
abstract: A bill introduced by Sen. Lloyd Smucker a Republican from West Lampeter Township would give $10 million annually to commercial renovation projects in historic districts. The legislation would make the state much more attractive to the types of developers willing to revitalize historic structures. Lisa Riggs, executive director of the James Street Improvement District says developers can easily go to nearby states which have programs like Smucker's.

headline: USW workers say no to Allegheny Ludlum pact
abstract: United Steelworkers union members at Allegheny Ludlum voted down a proposed four-year contract. They gathered before the USW headquarters to protest what they called a five time increase in their medical insurance costs. USW officials said the proposed contract included wage increases and other benefits.

headline: Casey could be GOP target next year
abstract: The Republicans have enjoyed victories both at the state and national electoral levels. Now they are eying the 2012 presidential election. US Senator Bob Casey from PA will run for re-election at the same time US  President Barack Obama runs for reelection. Republicans want to strap Bob Casey to unpopular things Obama has done.

headline: In Pa. House, it's calm before another storm
abstract: The debate on the House floor seemed to show that the Democrats and Republicans had made amends. They debated civilly over bills protecting whistleblowers, and making PA government more transparent. Nonetheless, there was commotion after the Republicans tried to make it harder for Democrats to amend bills.

headline: Fox 29 News at 11AM
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell held a press conference in Philadelphia. He discussed budget related matters. PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett will take office this month.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Should Pa. expand vouchers?
abstract: The state Senate has approved a plan that would allow parents of students in failing schools to use taxpayer dollars to send their child to private school. The plan has not received much support in the House, but it should be dropped all together in favor of more adequately funding the public school system. Most PA residents oppose the voucher program as a bad idea for public education.

headline: Blue Cross asks to make changes to insurance plan
abstract: Blue Cross of Northeastern PA has filed to make changes to its insurance plan giving subscribers more control over monthly premiums. If approved by the PA Insurance Department, the change would affect about 300 people.

headline: Allegheny County inmate settlements could go to children
abstract: Common Pleas Judge Kathryn Hens-Greco, administrative judge of the Allegheny County courts' family division, ordered the freezing of any settlement payments to former inmates who are overdue on child support. The county agreed to pay $3 million to settle a class-action lawsuit filed by people who were strip-searched upon being jailed for minor offenses.

headline: Snow gridlock traps commuters for up to 13 hours
abstract: Buses, cars and people were left stranded in the snow. One man, Denise Borders, spent 13 hours on the parkway without a bathroom, without food, and without sleep.

headline: Leaving a legacy
abstract: US Senator from PA, Arlen Spectar, will leave the Senate after 30 years of service. Spectar began his political life as a Democrat, but spent four decades as a Republican. He believes, like John F. Kennedy, that parties sometimes demand to much of the individual. In 2009 he provided a key vote for President Barack Obama's economic stimulus package. He was the only congressional Republican facing re-election in 2010 to do so.

headline: Protesters march to governor’s Philadelphia office
abstract: Occupy Philadelphia protesters marched to the city's state government offices where Governor Tom Corbett has an office.

headline: Three-year deal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's administration has signed off on the sale of a state building at Broad and Spring Garden to builder Bart Blatstein Tower Associates. A weak market worked to Blatstein's advantage in striking the final price. The sale resulted in $840,000 for the city in property-transfer tax. Blatstein wants to build 150 apartments.

headline: Pennsylvania: Drinking water shows normal levels of radioactivity
abstract: According to PA Governor Tom Corbett, tests performed on public drinking-water supplies throughout Pennsylvania found no elevated levels of radioactivity. This comes after fears that fallout from Japan's damaged nuclear plants would reach the US. Some western states have detected traces of radiation, according to the federal Environmental Protection Agency.

headline: Paid to pontificate
abstract: Former PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a contract with NBC to offer his analysis of the 2012 presidential race. This comes a week after he left office. Rendell made frequent appearances on MSNBC during last year's mid-term elections. The terms of his deal have not been disclosed.

headline: Sex-offender law must be fixed now
abstract: A loophole in the state's Megan's Law has made it impossible for law enforcement to arrest sex offenders who avoid registering under Megan's Law. The loophole covers the homeless and those who move from other states. Local district attorney offices report they have had to drop cases against accused sex offenders because of this loophole.

headline: Leaving Market
abstract: Janney Montgomery Scott, the Philadelphia brokerage and investment bank, is leasing the Three Logan Tower. PA Governor Tom Corbett signed a $10 million taxpayer-funded matching grant to help the bank move. The grant had been previously approved by the PA General Assembly under PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Corbett: 'We've got to find a balance'
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett said that he wants a newly formed commission on Marcellus Shale natural gas drilling to come up with an equitable, locally-levied impact fee for communities affected by natural gas. He said this at a meeting of county commissioners.

headline: Young children know what they like to eat -- but it could be full of fat, salt and sugar
abstract: Researchers from the University of Oregon and the University of Wisconsin designed two studies looking at food preferences, which show that children are able to express food preferences and product awareness at a young age. A study author said that this should be a public policy message that "we need to start earlier" to help kids make healthy choices.

headline: Cuomo pushes for property tax cap, ethics reform early in administration
abstract: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo wants to push through a property tax cap and an ethics reform as he steps into office. He thinks that New Yorkers can't afford the "never-ending tax increases" that outpace the economy and salaries. A tax cap is popular among voters, as New York is one of the most heavily taxed states in the country.

headline: Governor set to sign safety in youth sports law
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is expected to sign a new law regulating youth sports programs.  The new safety regulations are a long time coming according to some groups.

headline: PhillyDeals: Philadelphia-area post offices targeted for possible closing
abstract: The US Postal Service has many conflicting demands to meet. It must deliver declining amounts of mail to very hard to reach places. Thousands of post offices are set to close because of the ubiquity of email and the rise of private delivery companies.

headline: In visit to The Progress ... Scarnati speaks on gas drilling, health care, more
abstract: PA Senator Joseph Scarnati III visited Clearfield recently and stopped by the Clearfield County Economic Development Corporation office. The first thing that was discussed was the cuts to education in PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget. He also talked about smaller schools and said that he believed the decisions rest with localities.

headline: Breast cancer drug may slow lung cancer's march
abstract: The breast cancer drug tamoxifen may stall the progression of non-small cell lung cancer in those who take it after breast cancer treatment, a new study has found. The drug shows statically significant results showing that taking the drug can reduce the chance of death after having breast cancer.

headline: Obama aide: Debt limit fight could be "catastrophic"
abstract: A Spokesman from the White House Council of Economic Advisers has warned of catastrophic consequences that will result if Republicans follow through on threats to reject an increase in the nation's borrowing limit. The US Treasury Department has estimated that the limit will be reached during the first or second quarter of FY 2011. US President Barack Obama has said that the debt ceiling is "nothing to toy with."

headline: Thursday's jury deliberations produce no verdict in PA's government corruption trial.
abstract: Former state Rep. Brett Feese and his former aide, Jill Seaman are charged with a scheme to spend millions in taxpayer dollars to hire consultants and use state employees to develop high tech campaign tools.

headline: LVIA delays hiring management firm
abstract: The Lehigh–Northampton Airport is ready to hire a Dulles, Virginia, company to run the airport. The company will get paid roughly $330,000 a year, but executive compensation is still disputed.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Why we need a Safe School Advocate. Fast.
abstract: The author feels that the state needs an Office of the Safe School Advocate. The office was closed in violation of the law that created it in 2002. PA Representatives John Taylor and Bill Keller want to reinstate it. The author brings the issue up because her child was severely mistreated by a teacher.

headline: Snow set to arrive Wednesday
abstract: There was a snowstorm last Friday and it looks like it will rain or snow in the Lehigh Valley. A winter storm watch is in effect for the area. The snow should begin on Wednesday, with a 90% chance of precipitation. Meteorologists are expecting 3 to 5 inches of accumulation.

headline: Coming soon: Nightmare on area streets
abstract: The High Street bridge over Manatawny Creek will be closed for 18 months and will be replaced by the PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT). The closure of this bridge will result in a bottleneck of the Hanover Street Bridge, so PennDOT is diverting some traffic to South Hanover Street.

headline: Consolidation of districts concerns Frazier
abstract: Frazier School Board and administration are continuing to show signs of concern regarding state Rep Tim Mahoney's plan to consolidate school districts in Fayette County into one. Acting Superintendent Kenneth Meadows said he would support a study that looks into both cost savings and the effect the consolidation would have on education in the county.

headline: U.S. Rep. Kelly leans toward backing revamped Boehner debt plan
abstract: US Congressman Kelly of Butler, PA, says that he will not support US House Speaker Boehner's spending plan. This plan would help the federal government avoid a default. US President Barack Obama is struggling to find a compromise on the debt limit. Senate Democrats feel that the Republicans plan will leave the country on shaky economic footing.

headline: Privatizing treatment of mentally ill opposed
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has proposed changes to the Department of Public Welfare that concern some. He wants to contract out operation of the forensic psychiatric units at Torrance and Norristown state hospitals. The measure should cut $3 million and cut 400 state positions. In 2007 the plan was abandoned after the PA State Correction Officers Association opposed it.

headline: Rendell silver nicked; chef accused of taking cutlery, tea set, autographed football
abstract: Michael D. Yancy, a chef at the Governor's mansion for nine years, has been charged with receiving stolen property. He sold purloined silver cutlery to a pawn shop and various valuable items from the Governor's mansion, including a signed football that belonged to former PA Governor Ed Rendell. Current PA Governor Tom Corbett offered no comment on the arrest.

headline: Powerful legislators hail from Western Pa. House, Senate leaders are Jefferson Co. natives
abstract: Both the PA House and the PA Senate leaders are native to rural Jefferson County in west-central Pennsylvania. PA Representative Sam Smith has led the Republicans in the House for the last four years and should have more influence now that the House is controlled by Republicans. PA Representative Joe Scarnati originally ran as an independent and won; he later switched to the GOP.

headline: PA joblessness rate triggers extended benefits
abstract: Some unemployed people in PA now qualify for up to 7 more weeks of unemployment benefits because of the state's rising unemployment rate. The additional weeks of payments are available to those who have exhausted regular state unemployment as well as federal emergency unemployment.

headline: Cameras won't make schools safe
abstract: The president of the Philadelphia school police union says that cameras recently installed to Philadelphia schools have not made the schools any safer. A comprehensive program of restorative practices was instituted in 2008 by the PA Department of Education, which helped to significantly reduce school violence. The author wonders why the camera money was not spent for such programming.

headline: Lawmakers Consider Privatization of Liquor Stores
abstract: Legislators in Harrisburg are debating whether liquor stores should be privately owned. On March 8th, Governor Tom Corbett said that he would be forming a panel to study the issue of privatization. PA Representative Kevin Murphy, who serves on the House Liquor Control Committee, thinks this is something the state has got right.

headline: Letters: Casino vote means loss of city jobs and revenue
abstract: The author takes issue with the editorial "A good call on Foxwoods." He is frustrated that the Foxwoods casino could not comply with reasonable requirements of the PA Gaming Control Board. He is especially frustrated that this happened during a time when Philadelphia needs job growth, and is suffering from budget shortfalls. Philadelphia missed out on a lot of tax revenue.

headline: Metcalfe pushes anti-immigrant package
abstract: Daryl Metcalfe of Butler County has unveiled a package of controversial bills that seek to control the effect of immigration in PA.

headline: A pain in the gas
abstract: The author feels that PA Governor Tom Corbett deserves at least some applause for creating the Marcellus Shale Commission, although it has heavy representation from the gas industry. The report evidently shows this bias, but is a starting point for coming to grips with the huge impacts that drillers have had on the state.

headline: At PSU, budget message finally is getting through
abstract: Penn State and many other schools in the state were raising tuition rates by greater the rate of inflation and benefiting from very favorable funding treatment in state budgets. PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget will mean a departure from this system.

headline: Conflict over Corbett nominee's claims for health policy
abstract: Gary Alexander, a nominee for PA Governor Tom Corbett's cabinet, has released statements that are not substantiated by officials in Rhode Island. Alexander said that while working in Rhode Island for Governor Don Carcieri, there were changes made to the federal Medicaid program that saved the state $100 million. No one in Rhode Island knows how he came up with that number.

headline: Task force wants funding for libraries put before voters
abstract: Court Judge Frank Lucchino, chairman of the Carnegie Library's Public Private Task Force, has suggested that the issue of closing Pittsburgh area library branches should be put to a vote. This comes after the public showed great opposition to the closing of Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh. Voters would decide how to fund libraries.

headline: Castille says Family Court probe stays private
abstract: A firm hired by Supreme Court Chief Justice Ronald D. Castille is now being sued for fraud and legal malpractice after it has spent $780,540 of public money with nothing to show for it.

headline: Commentary: Window is closing on Harrisburg's debt plan
abstract: PA Senator Piccola authored legislation that blocked the City of Harrisburg from filing for chapter 9 bankruptcy. Harrisburg Mary Linda Thompson is looking to file an Act 47 plan, a means of helping this fiscally distressed city. When the PA General Assembly reconvenes in the fall, they will vote on a three member board to oversee Harrisburg's Act 47 plan.

headline: Ex-offenders hope Philadelphia passes 'ban the box' bill this week
abstract: Donna Redd Miller, councilwoman in Philadelphia, supports the "ban the box" measure, which disallows employers to ask about criminal history on the first interview. This could help qualified people get jobs but some are afraid of the law. Cities across the country have adopted similar measures. Community Legal Services and the National Employment Law Project favor the measure.

headline: EDITORIAL: State GOP goes nuclear
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has promised to restore honor to Harrisburg. What transpired recently in the House Rules Committee is no indication that this sentiment is being taken to heart by the legislature. Republicans voted to reduce the number of Democrats on every House committee and overturn the minority party's ability to have amendments considered on the house floor. Democrats responded with outrage.

headline: Evening News: Occupy Erie’s plans for the New Year
abstract: Occupy Erie has reached its 78th day and they show no signs of slowing. This new year they intend to demonstrate in Perry Square.

headline: Romney's faith no big deal in Pa.
abstract: Voters are asked about their views on GOP presidential candidate Mitt Romney's faith as a Mormon. 80 percent of PA residents polled say that his faith won't affect their vote. Many voters are unfamiliar with Mormonism and are curious about depictions of their lifestyle in popular culture.

headline: Focusing on benefits of gas industry
abstract: PA State Senator Yaw says that most residents do not realize the impact Marcellus Shale has on the area. He stated that most PA residents do not live where Marcellus Shale drilling occurs and could take place. He thinks that a severance tax is not fair and that local impacts differ from borough to borough, and that therefore impact fees should be assessed at the county level.

headline: Where's the shared sacrifice from Pennsylvania's most powerful people?
abstract: Pa Governor Tom Corbett and other lawmakers are urging unions and teachers to make sacrifices in order to save taxpayer money. Corbett wants to cut salaries and benefits for public workers. The article shows what kind of perks that the governor and other executives get.

headline: Cheers & Jeers: 'Jersey Shore' tactics at capitol, more bad news for Hbg
abstract: This is an article commenting on various happenings in the PA statehouse. The author thinks that the shouting match that erupted between PA Representatives Mike Turzai and Frank Dermody was infantile. She also says "good riddance" to Aramark Incorporated, a Philadelphia based company pulling out of the contract to run the cafeteria in the state capitol.

headline: Section of Lower Northeast sees money erosion
abstract: According to the US Census Bureau, the rate of poverty in the Lower Northeast of Philadelphia is up 110 percent since 1999. Sociologists and community-development officials attribute at least 6 factors to the rise in poverty, which include issues of race, age, and the change in jobs available to people from said region. The director of the Mayor's Office of Multicultural Affairs says that the influx of Latinos into the region is part of a "natural migratory phenomenon."

headline: Passage of Safety in Youth Sports act earns plenty of applause
abstract: The Safety in Youth Sports Act was unanimously approved by the state Senate and it heads to the desk of PA Gov. Tom Corbett who is expected to sign the bill. Parents and students are happy that the bill has received support. Lawmakers were spurred into action by an increase in head injuries by student athletes.

headline: Causer announces 9th annual Senior Citizens Expo
abstract: PA Representative Causer will host the Ninth Annual Senior Citizens Expo at the University of Pittsburgh. This is an opportunity for senior citizens and family members to learn about the programs available to them. Information about health care, insurance, nutrition, exercise, fire safety, financial planning, fraud protection, government services, hunting/fishing and personal safety will be available.

headline: Pennsylvania judges court sunny locales
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Ronald Castille told judges and justices not to go to locations like Las Croabas, Puerto Rico or Key West on the states dime to attend law conferences. This is mainly because of the state deficit of $4 billion. Castille will testify before the Senate Appropriations Committee in a hearing on court finances.

headline: Dauphin County Drug Court participants show discipline, courage
abstract: 23 people have graduated from the Dauphin County Drug Court. Daniel McGovern is the most recent graduate of the court. He said that he did it not only for himself but for his son. County Judge Richard A. Lewis, who presides over drug court, has commented on the courage that all of the graduates have shown throughout their cleansing.

headline: Marino, Thompson agree more spending cuts needed
abstract: Two U.S. House members from the northern PA region both did their part in passing the budget measure to cut nearly $40 billion in federal spending. The vote allowed the government to move on without a shutdown. The focus now moves to the 2012 Republican spending plan, which promises to cut as well.

headline: House passes texting while driving ban
abstract: The PA House passed legislation banning the practice of sending text messages while behind the wheel.

headline: Court OKs DNA test for anyone arrested
abstract: A federal appeals court decision found that law enforcement can take and test DNA samples from people who are arrested but not yet convicted. DNA testing may overtake fingerprinting as the universal identifier of the accused. The American Civil Liberties Union filed a brief in the case, arguing against pre-conviction DNA sampling.

headline: Does Pa.'s $300M diversion skirt the law?
abstract: In PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget proposal, he seeks to direct future tobacco settlement payments into the general fund. Some think this is illegal. The money would not be used for its original intent--public health--said one Democracy Rising spokesperson. Corbett blames former PA Governor Ed Rendell for setting the precedent for tapping the fund.

headline: Proposal for Harrisburg halfway house at 6th and Maclay streets draws neighbors' opposition
abstract: A development firm wants to open a halfway house in Harrisburg for female offenders newly released from prison. The PA Department of Corrections operates halfway houses for women in Philadelphia an Pittsburgh but does not have a female-only facility in its Central Region. The Nativity School and local YMCA are strongly opposed to the development.

headline: State Police take over PA's Homeland Security division
abstract: PA's Homeland Security office was once under the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency. It is now under the control of the state police. Officials say that this move will help different emergency response offices communicate better.

headline: Mon River bridge to carry Musial's moniker
abstract: State Route 1077 over the Monongahela River in Washington and Westmoreland counties will be named for St. Louis Cardinals star Stan "The Man" Musial. He is a native of Denora. State Sen. Tim Solobay, D-Canonsburg sponsored the legislation to get the road named after the baseball star.

headline: State stores sale divides GOP
abstract: PA Representative Petri said that he is "not sold" on House Majority Leader Turzai's bill to sell the state liquor stores. Petri is worried about the impact on restaurants and beer distributors in the event that other retailers are allowed to sell liquor and wine. The bill imposes a new tax structure, which includes allowing private wholesalers to sell liquor and wine.

headline: A legal drug even a head shop owner won't sell because "It's too hard-core."
abstract: A new drug, methylenedioxypyrovalerone (MDPV), is sweeping the nation. It can sometimes lead to a very aggressive high, which lands many in the hospital. PA Representative Tina Pickett is moving to write legislation banning the substance. PA Senator Larry Farnese is also advocating a bill. The federal Drug Enforcement Agency has labeled it a "drug of concern."

headline: Factory and spending data support strong growth tone
abstract: Factory activity in the Midwest hit a 22-1/2 year high in January. Another report shows that consumer spending ended 2010 on firmer footing. The prices for US government debt fell. A report from the US Commerce Department showed that spending, which accounts for 70 percent of US economic activity, increased by 0.7 percent in December.

headline: Rendell employer gets state contract
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's administration has hired a New York-based investment banking firm, Greenhill & Co. to help the state determine which areas of state government should be privatized. Former PA Governor Ed Rendell is a part-time advisor to this company. Rendell is not involved in the project. Corbett grapples now with a $4.2 billion deficit.

headline: Tougher driving laws make sense for teens
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett recently signed Lacey's Law which limits the amount of passengers allowed in the vehicle of a teenager. It also calls for more stringent training requirements. Teen drivers are four times more likely to have an accident than older drivers.

headline: Congress divided on debt plans.
abstract: US House Republicans and Democrats have both issued proposals to raise the nation's $14.3 trillion borrowing limit. The proposals did not seem substantively different. Congress has a week to solve this problem and US president Barack Obama has said that, "We are left with a stalemate." The president said it would be bad for his re-election campaign to adopt a short term fix to the problem.

headline: Health care 'debate' more like 'theater'
abstract: This is a clarification to an article released by the same newspaper. It corrects and article that states that there was a hearing in the Capitol held by the health subcommittee on US President Barack Obama's health care law. This is not true. There was no debate. PA Governor Tom Corbett simply declared the law illegal. The author concedes that the Affordable Care Act has problems.

headline: State Senate plans Monday vote on property tax cap measure
abstract: The Republican controlled New York Senate will soon vote on Governor Andrew Cuomo's proposal to limit annual property tax increases to 2 percent or the rate of inflation. If this passes the Senate then the pressure would be on the Democrat led Assembly. The measure has overwhelming voter approval, but the United Teachers union opposes the bill because it would "unfairly cripple school districts."

headline: Lawmaker COLA.
abstract: The Lawmaker's Cost of Living Adjustment or COLA, is causing a stir. Representative's Vance and Grell will send their pay bumps back to the Treasury. PA Governor Tom Corbett's salary jumps about $6,000, but he says he'll give it to charity.

headline: Sen. Greenleaf to seek a national stage with presidential ballot spot
abstract: Republican State Sen. Stewart J. Greenleaf will be on the New Hampshire presidential primary ballot, but the lawmaker says he is not running for president. Instead, he is running to try to turn the spotlight on issues like the national debt and government spending.

headline: Public interest detour
abstract: The author thinks that it is wrong that a Commonwealth Court decision denies access to records of PA Turnpike Commission employees' free E-Zpass rides on the toll road. The Patriot News of Harrisburg sought the records but could not get them.

headline: Turf luck
abstract: The Eastern York school board has voted to reserve the right to seek an exception to exceed its state-mandated cap of 1.8 percent. This comes in response to uncertainty regarding PA Governor Tom Corbett's new budget. The author questions why the school still wants to build an artificial turf field that will cost close to $1 million.

headline: Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Corbett talks about family members buried in Burns Hill Cemetery, Waynesboro
abstract: In 2008 someone vandalized gravestones at Burns Hill Cemetery. Current PA Governor Tom Corbett went to visit the site, but not for professional reasons. He went to make sure that his parent's graves were still intact. The rest of the article gives a biography of Corbett, including his election, and his family.

headline: Will liquor store sale bill get vote?
abstract: PA Representative Turzai is in favor of privatizing liquor sales in PA. The move could earn the state about $1.5 billion for the state budget.

headline: Philadelphia would lose, Chester County would gain under state redistricting plan
abstract: A tentative plan by a legislative commission charged with redrawing the House and Senate districts would have Philadelphia lose a seat while Chester County gains one. The plan was approved 3-2 along party lines. The process is described as being explicitly partisan. The plan would ultimately move the 169th District from Philadelphia to York County. The existing district in Philadelphia would be absorbed by surrounding districts.

headline: Pittsburgh schools could let go more than 100 on Wednesday
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public School districts are preparing to furlough up to 38 teachers and layoff or furlough as many as 68 other employees. The school board is expected to vote on the job cuts soon. This is a phenomenon seen across the state as districts cope with cuts in state funding and lost federal stimulus aid, as well as other impacts of the economic downturn.

headline: Mayor warns city council of revenue shortfall
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl sees holes in the 2011 budget. He expects budget cuts or service reductions to follow. The budget was based on increased revenues from the parking authority.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has tapped an assistant US Attorney to replace him as attorney general. Linda Kelly, the chosen attorney, is a federal prosecutor from western PA. Her appointment must be confirmed by the state Senate. Corbett also talked about the $4 billion deficit.

headline: Committee formed to replace Paterno
abstract: Penn State University has put together a committee to find a replacement for their embattled football program. Joe Paterno, the former coach, was fired in the midst of the sexual abuse scandal that has engulfed the university.

headline: Bill Targets ‘Internet Sweepstakes Cafes’ In Pennsylvania
abstract: Chester County Republican Curt Schroder, chairman of the House Gaming Oversight Committee, has approved a bill that would shut down gambling operations that operate under a perceived loophole in the state's sweepstakes law.

headline: In-home help program for needy faces cutback
abstract: The United Cerebral Palsy/Community Living and Support Services (UCP/CLASS) in Pittsburg suffered severe budget cuts, which means less service to the needy. The program was cut by 14 percent by the state's most recent budget. A spokesperson from the Department of Public Welfare has said that the department is working with providers and advocates to do more with less.

headline: Education reformer decries state cuts
abstract: Geoffry Canada, from Harlem Children's Zone, thinks that children should not be unfairly penalized for the financial crisis with budget cuts to education. He was in Pittsburgh to discuss PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget. President Barack Obama applauded Canada for his education reform efforts last year.

headline: WTAJ News This Morning
abstract: School leaders have been warned of a funding gap that they may face in the near future. The acting secretary of education has said that PA Governor Tom Corbett has replaced $300 million of state education money with federal funding from edujobs, which can only be used once. When this and other stimulus money runs out, either property taxes will rise, or huge cuts will be made to students and teachers.

headline: Funeral services Wednesday for former state Rep. Bebko-Jones
abstract: The funeral for former state Rep. Bebko-Jones will be held Wednesday.

headline: Vouchers or support for public schools?
abstract: The benefits of public schooling and vouchers are discussed.

headline: Environment is key element in new report about drilling
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale Advisory Commission has released its 137 page report, which includes 96 separate recommendations. The bulk of the recommendations are found in the Public Health, Safety & Environmental Protection sections. The report states that the PA Department of Environmental Protection should be able to impose civil fines on drillers.

headline: Red-light cameras stalled in PA
abstract: The article is the answering of a question asked by a reader of the Morning Call: She asks why we are not doing more for red light enforcement. The National Motorists Association sees cameras as a Big Brother way of generating tax revenue. PA Representative Dominic Pileggi has sponsored a bill that would allow for red light cameras in certain municipalities.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: Many local governments are having trouble paying for snow removal. State tax revenues do not start coming in until  late march and April. Many townships have asked the Governor to release liquid fuel tax revenues to pay for snow removal.

headline: Corbett seems ‘concerned’ about high tuition costs
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is said to be concerned with rising tuition costs and is looking for ways to cut costs.

headline: Former teachers union president Kevin Deely aims to unseat Simmons in 131st District
abstract: The former head of the teachers union at the Easton Area School District plans to challenge Republican Justin Simmons for his House seat in the 131st Legislative District.

headline: Governor Corbett declares fiscal emergency in Harrisburg
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett has declared a fiscal emergency in Harrisburg and is ready to appoint a financial adviser for the city. The governor recently signed legislation giving him this authority.

headline: Marcellus panel recommends impact fee
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale Commission recently released recommendations that include requiring drillers to pay an impact fee but ruled out a new state tax on extracting natural gas. The report from the panel is intended to guide the legislature to regulate the shale industry, while balancing the need to generate revenue and promote drilling.

headline: Legislators nervous about basic ed cuts
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's proposed $1 billion cut to public education has Republican lawmakers looking for ways to ease the blow to school districts. PA Representative Mike Fleck said that declining revenues. Larger budgets and no more federal stimulus money has left the state with few options. One Republican talked of willingness to adopt a reasonable severance tax on natural gas drillers to meet revenue shortfalls.

headline: WETM Morning News on WIVT
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will name George Greig of Crawford County to head the agricultural department. Greig has served on PA's farm bureau's state board for the past six years. He has also been involved in agricultural leadership at the national, county, and local levels.

headline: Clinics are key to health care, Pennsylvania state senator says
abstract: Sen. Ted Erickson, R-Delaware County held hearings underscoring the urgency to address a large uninsured population that continues to grow because of the jobless rate. PA has roughly 260 clinics, many of which receiving federal funding. They are the safety net for the nearly 1.3 million uninsured PA residents.

headline: Philadelphia GOP puts its hope on City Commissioners race
abstract: The tattered state of the Philadelphia GOP is examined. The party has decayed nearly to the point of irrelevancy according to some experts. Today, Democrats outnumber Republicans by more than 6-1.

headline: Status quo? Try nonpro
abstract: Former PA Representative John Kennedy was despised by fellow legislators for his anti-career-politician-stance. He imposed a term limit on himself, leaving the legislature after 8 years of service. The 2005 pay raises that legislators granted themselves prompted him to chair Citizens Alliance of PA, which works to change the legislature.

headline: Tough budget cuts start at home for Pocono lawmakers
abstract: The $4 billion deficit has PA state legislators from the Pocono region preaching about shared sacrifice. The piece lists many legislators and what they are doing to cut costs. For instance, PA Senator Lisa Boscola is refusing to accept the hike in legislators' pensions.

headline: Santorum in no hurry to make presidential decision
abstract: Former PA Senator Rick Santorum said that he would not decide whether or not to seek the Republican nomination until the summer, because no other potential candidates seem to be in a rush to make the announcement. He said that delaying an announcement allows lesser known candidates to make key alliances with activists.

headline: Not everyone agrees with Corbett education plan
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's school reform proposals are discussed.

headline: Governor Corbett and other leaders have expressed support for privatization
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett continues to express support for privatizing the state's wine and liquor sales.

headline: President of Marcellus Shale coalition would support 'reasonable' impact fee
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale Coalition suggests that an impact fee on the natural gas industry would be appropriate. However, the commission has not suggested how much the fees should be.

headline: Shuster speaks with Rockwood sophomores
abstract: Rockwood Area High School was visited by US Representative Bill Shuster. He talked about the economy, the environment and the federal deficit. He fielded questions. Michele Beener, director of organizational development for Somerset Hospital, facilitated the event.

headline: Harrisburg teen robbed on his way home from library
abstract: A 13-year-old boy in uptown Harrisburg was robbed by two older teens. They stole his iPod. One of the assailants was wearing a face mask. The police found him and he is now facing robbery charges and conspiracy charges in juvenile court.

headline: Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Corbett rolls out school reform package
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett laid out his education reform proposal today in York. It calls for a school choice program for students in the state's worst schools, tax credits for scholarships and expansion of charter schools. The programs were quickly denounced by the Pennsylvania State Education Association who called for the governor to restore funding to public schools instead.

headline: School vouchers Q&A: Pennsylvania Senate Bill 1 is awaiting House action
abstract: Sen. Jeffrey Piccola, R-Dauphin County, and Sen. Anthony Williams, D-Philadelphia, the architects of the PA school voucher program answer questions about how their legislation would be enacted if passed. Eligibility, income requirements, and fraud prevention are discussed.

headline: Break open state’s alcohol monopoly
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Mike Turzai is releasing a plan to privatize liquor sales. He promises that the sale will provide a steady flow of tax revenue for the state. The union that represents liquor store clerks has come out in opposition because of job losses. A truncated PA Liquor Control Board would remain to handle licensing, enforce laws and conduct educational activities.

headline: Harrisburg residents don't seem to mind increased security at city hall
abstract: Visitors to Harrisburg’s City Government Center must now pass through a metal detector upon entering. A spokeswomen for Mayor Linda Thompson says that these steps are part of a long-term plan of hers to respond to threats towards her.

headline: Santarsiero eager to start second term
abstract: According to PA Representative Steve Santarsiero, the next legislative term is about job growth, fighting for education reform and environmental protection. He has been appointed to the environmental resources and energy, local government, state government and transportation committees. He thinks that once the economy rebounds, the state should cut corporation taxes to give businesses an incentive to come to PA.

headline: Heed workers, not bosses, Obama urged
abstract: President Obama visited Pittsburgh today where he met with his Council on Jobs and Competitiveness.  Local activists were concerned that the council was made up of companies that shipped jobs overseas.  86,000 people became eligible for a program that helps workers whose jobs have been outsourced.

headline: Corbett says he still favors the privatization of liquor and wine sales in Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett says that he would still like to move ahead with his plan to privatize the state's liquor system.  Currently all wine and liquor sales are done through state-run stores.

headline: State jobless rate rose to 7.6 percent in June
abstract: The PA Department of Labor and Industry has reported that the unemployment rate has rose to 7.6 percent in June, a 0.2 percent increase from May. The rate is, however, still 1.1 percentage points lower than the 8.7 percent rate a year ago (when adjusted for seasonal hiring factors). The labor force (those looking for work) also declined.

headline: Philadelphia City Council is where job growth goes to die
abstract: The author thinks that it is an insult that City Council's Darrell Clarke wants to add the "Jobs Commission" on the May primary ballot. This would be the third committee in eight years created by Philadelphia to look into the job climate. There was a Tax Reform Commission in 2003 and a Mayor's Taskforce on Tax Policy and Economic Competitiveness in 2009.

headline: One Nation, Indivisible
abstract: The author feels that the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit flouted Supreme Court law when it struck down affirmative action at the University of Texas Law School. Last week the law school developed a plan that takes race into account. The author feels that admission procedures at most universities are good at increasing minority enrollment, but some high schools don’t prepare students to meet the standards of more demanding majors.

headline: Takeover bill could become law by mid-October
abstract: The legislation created by Senators Grell and Piccola to take over the finances of Harrisburg could become law within the next few weeks. The goal is to take over, but return power as quickly as possible to the elected officials. Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson wants to impose a commuter tax.

headline: News at 10
abstract: Stores are being given the chance to eliminate any newly-banned substance from their shelves before they are prosecuted.

headline: Legislators seek meeting with UPMC, Highmark
abstract: A bipartisan group wants to meet with UPMC and Highmark to discuss an ongoing contract dispute. Hearings will be held by the House Insurance Committee and the Senate Banking and Insurance Committee to seek legislative remedies to the contract dispute between the two healthcare providers.

headline: PSU can set a national example
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is asking Penn State to stop crying poverty. American universities spend about twice as much per student. Penn State tuition rose from $6,852 in 2000-01 to $15,250 this year, growth far above inflation, according to US Department of Education data. During this same period, the school increased its expenditure on administration by more than $66 million.

headline: First month of winter has been snowiest in N.J. in 62 years
abstract: A New Jersey climatologist is calling this the whitest winter in the state in the last 62 years. Snowfall is above average... With more snow come more winter blues. A psychologist talks about the sometimes depressing effects that winter can have on people. In winter there are fewer hours of sunlight.

headline: Land deal of 1880s in center court over shale rights
abstract: A Northern Pennsylvania court will reconsider an 1880s land deal in dispute. The parties involved are contesting who owns the valuable Marcellus Shale gas below the property. The old agreement states that the seller of the land shall be entitled to half of the minerals and petroleum oils. There is no mention of gas. The result of this case will set an important precedent.

headline: Transit spending boost urged
abstract: State Auditor General Jack Wagner called for an immediate boost in transportation funding the state. He warned that decaying infrastructure threatens the economy and public safety. PA Gov Tom Corbett on the other hand seems to be in no rush to push for such funding.

headline: Piccola says commuter tax for Harrisburg not an option
abstract: The commuter tax is not an option in Harrisburg after city council rejected the Act 47 plan. PA Representative Piccola wants PA Governor Tom Corbett to withhold state funding for the state capitol. Piccola thinks that Harrisburg's rejection was a move to force a bailout, and he thinks that the state should pass legislation to require a management board to force the implementation of Act 47.

headline: Senators sympathetic to colleges' plight
abstract: Dustin Saksek said that he is unsure whether he will attend Bloomberg next year because of PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget, which means steep cuts to the State System of Higher Education. During a meeting with the Senate Appropriations Committee, Republicans and Democrats both expressed their discomfiture with the new budget.

headline: Reward offered for robbers who smashed elderly women's car windows
abstract: Two elderly women were stopped in the 200 block of Pleasant Acres Road in Springettsbury Township by a robber. He smashed in the windows of the cars and stole purses. York County Crime Stoppers has an award for information that will help solve the robbery.

headline: Pennsylvania counties to receive federal disaster aid
abstract: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has announced that federal aid is available for those in PA affected by Tropical Storm Lee. US President Barack Obama has ordered this action.

headline: Last-minute state grant saves center
abstract: The Salisbury Area Family Center reopened after receiving a $500,000 grant by the state. The center serves 1,100 families a year.

headline: Shale jobs windfall debated
abstract: Two Penn State professors estimate that Marcellus Shale activity could generate up to $12.8 billion in economic activity in 2011 and support 156,000 jobs. The availability of cheap natural gas has saved Pennsylvania's $633 million in 2010 and should generate more than $1.2 billion in state and local taxes in 2011.

headline: Process begins to redraw legislative districts
abstract:
The Legislative Reapportionment Commission, made up of Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, Senate Democratic Leader Jay
Costa, House Majority Leader Mike Turzai and House Democratic leader Frank Dermody, will have to redraw the state's 203 House districts and 50 Senate districts. If they cannot agree by May 4th, then the PA Supreme Court is left with the final redrawing.

headline: Harrisburg exhausts 1/3 of its overtime budget for snow removal
abstract: The last storm may be the most expensive of the season. The Harrisburg's budget has been drained by overtime pay for snow removal. Public works asked the city council for $75,000 for overtime pay to clear the streets, but only received $50,000. One third of that money is already used. Mayor of Harrisburg Linda Thompson has promised that reallocations will be made to secure the streets.

headline: Underemployment dogs Pa. workers
abstract: The Keystone Research Center recently reported that while pa is hovering around the average of 8% , the real number of people who have been unemployed is a much higher percentage of the workforce. The numbers tell an even sadder story when we look at the number or people who have moved to part time work form full time work.

headline: How much is Pennsylvania's death penalty costing taxpayers?
abstract: An in depth look at the state of the death penalty in Pennsylvania including its history and most recent application. The cost of death row inmates far exceeds that of ordinary prisoners, due to security and the lengthy appeals process. Most people executed by the state waved their right to appeal.

headline: Analysis: Relationships make legislative politics work
abstract: Oklahoma Senator Tom Coburn is optimistic that a federal budget deal can be struck with US President Barack Obama. The federal government must reach this deadline by August 1. in order to not default. Coburn and Obama differ politically but have a strong friendship, similar to that between former US President Reagan and then Democratic Speaker of the House Tip O'Neill.

headline: Rendell approves of some Christie, Corbett cuts
abstract: Former PA Governor Ed Rendell said that he approves of some of the cost-cutting measures taken by PA Governor Tom Corbett and New Jersey Governor Chris Christie. Rendell said that public-worker benefits are not supportable in their current state.

headline: 2-hour delay, unscheduled leave for federal workers
abstract: Federal agencies in the Washington area are open Thursday with a two-hour delayed arrival. Workers were allowed to leave work early due to inclement weather on Wednesday. Follow the Capital Weather Gang for new developments.

headline: Baker briefs on redistricting
abstract: PA Senator Lisa Baker told a group of senior citizens recently that she may be losing around 19,000 constituents after the legislative redistricting is completed. She, along with PA Representative Yudichak, will host an expo for the area's senior citizens, which will feature information on the services available to PA's older residents.

headline: Sunday hunting controversy
abstract: A study commissioned by the state Legislature found that the state could add $804 million to the state's economy if they legalized Sunday hunting. Some hunters say they buy licenses in other states so they can go hunting there one day a week. State Rep. Thomas R. Caltagirone, a Reading Democrat, is listed as a co-sponsor of the bill.

headline: 131st Transportation Company grieves soldiers' deaths as mission carries on
abstract: For six months, the Williamstown-based 131st Transportation Company, 213th Area Support Group of the Pennsylvania National Guard, didn’t suffer a single injury. This group protects Afghans hauling supplies. Sergeants Brian Mowery, Edward Koehler, and Staff Sergeant Kenneth VanGiesen recently perished and will be awarded posthumous purple hearts.

headline: State school bills hailed as relief
abstract: 18 bills sponsored by the Republican and Democratic chairmen of the Senate Education Committee would lift requirements that cost districts money and offer greater freedom in hiring and laying off employees. This may help PA school districts to cut costs. Some of these measures are consistent with PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget.

headline: Baby steps toward reform
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's reform package represents only baby steps towards the sweeping reforms that he promised during his campaign. The PA House will join the Senate in having to pay 1 percent of their salaries for their top-end health coverage. The author feels that the governor should have also addressed issues like redistricting reform, and campaign contribution caps.

headline: Rep. meets with residents of adult homes
abstract: US Congressman Mike Kelly recently visited a home for people with disabilities. He praised the facility and said that it was a model care facility.

headline: Fewer rules, not vouchers, needed to improve schools
abstract: Don Bell, superintendent of the Northern Lebanon School District, says that throwing state money into private schools via vouchers only continues the issues that plague public schools. Instead of more money from more centralized government, the solution is fewer rules and more local control.

headline: Commission reports on how state can raise transportation money
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett commissioned the Transportation Funding Advisory to generate funds to repair deficient roads and bridges across the state. Under this plan vehicle registration fees to the PA Department of Transportation would increase. However, the amount of time between registration would increase. The advisory also suggests removing the cap on the oil company franchise tax.

headline: Lawmakers press LCB officials: Why not privatize state stores?
abstract: The Senate Appropriations Committee tried not to dwell on the potential privatization of the PA Liquor Control Board during a recent meeting. However the very large issue was impossible to ignore. The two sides argued over whether the move would make the LCB more consumer friendly and whether this will increase access to alcohol by minors. PA Governor Tom Corbett says the state needs the $2 billion from the sale to fix the budget.

headline: Erdman to take job with Corbett
abstract: Northumberland County Controller Chuck Erdman will resign. He will switch to a position with PA Governor Tom Corbett's administration. He commented on the $4 billion deficit and hopes that his talents will be put to use to solve the problem. Northumberland County Commissioners Vinny Clausi and Frank Sawicki are sad to see Erdman go.

headline: Flags at half staff for Philly victim of Afghan copter crash; services Thursday
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett ordered flags in the Capitol complex and at commonwealth facilities to fly at half-staff. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter also gave an order for Philadelphia. This comes after Petty Officer 1st Class Michael Strange died while serving in Afghanistan.

headline: Corbett likely to declare fiscal emergency for Harrisburg this week
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is going forward with the plan to rescue the City of Harrisburg from its financial chaos. With new authority to takeover the state's capital city, the impact of such action is discussed.

headline: Transportation recommendations could cost people more cash
abstract: PA must generate about $3.5 billion a year to service old roads and bridges. The Transportation Funding Advisory Commission is considering raising fees, increasing fines for speeding and ending a cap on the tax for wholesale fuel prices.

headline: With census in, congressional redistricting on the way
abstract: Erik Arneson, communications and policy director for Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, said that the logical place to cut a congressman is from western PA, as eastern PA has seen most of the population growth in the last decade. In is uncertain what the new districts served on by US Congressmen Lou Barletta and Tom Marino will look like.

headline: Rep. Baker handling clinic, welfare bills
abstract: PA Representative Matt Baker has new responsibilities, which include developing health legislation. He has plans to regulate abortion clinics and make the welfare system more accountable. He is writing a bill that will give clear and concise authority to the PA Department of Health to inspect and regulate abortion clinics, which comes after a grand jury found that a Philadelphia doctor used scissors to "kill viable babies."

headline: Study: Economy hurting children
abstract: A study from the Kids Count Data Book shows that PA children are bearing the brunt of the weak economy. PA scored lower than other states in the following categories: low birth weight babies, infant mortality, percent in poverty, and percent in a single parent home. Much of the data was gathered from the US Census Bureau.

headline: New law targets ‘fractured system’
abstract: A new law will standardize the way earned income tax is calculated, collected and paid in January. The new law should allow the state to recover an additional $100 million in uncollected taxes. The new system replaces a highly criticized, byzantine system with too many rules.

headline: Penn State York students happy with 2.9 percent tuition hike
abstract: Penn state University students gathered at the Capitol to protest PA Governor Tom Corbett's cuts to education funding. The recently released budget cut funding by 19 percent. Penn state raised its satellite campus tuition by about $175 a semester, less of hike than many expected.

headline: Two GOP governors plan to spare film tax credits
abstract: Republican Governors Rick Snyder of Michigan and Tom Corbett of Pennsylvania have said that they will spare the their respective Film Tax Credit programs. A tax expert from Center on Budget and Policy Priorities says that this will not pay off.

headline: 2nd woman charged with bilking closed Pa. thrift
abstract: Elexa Manos-Becton, of Coraopolis, was indicted on bank fraud, money laundering and other charges for allegedly taking about $908,000 from Dwelling House Savings and Loan. She used an online Paypal account to make overdraft transactions. Federal regulators closed down Dwelling House because it could not absorb the $3 million in internet fraud losses.

headline: Rep. Ron Buxton opposes Harrisburg commuter tax, legislation to prevent city from imposing taxes
abstract: PA Representative Buxton is against Harrisburg officials adopting a commuter tax in a fiscal recovery plan Mayor Linda Thompson has created. This is not because he supports legislation by Republicans to block the city from imposing new taxes; he believes the tax will adversely affect Harrisburg residents.

headline: Blair could be Marcellus Shale hub
abstract: Blair County may have the opportunity to be a major hub for the state's burgeoning natural gas drilling industry in spite of the county only having a narrow strip of the coveted resource. Investment in the region is booming. Gardner Davis of Wayne, Pa., announced plans to build a $15 million plant in Tipton that will aid the drilling industry.

headline: How Hershey charity director fees rose to half a million
abstract: Leroy S. Zimmerman was appointed to a board that managed the assets of the Hershey charity for disadvantaged youth, which paid about $35,000. By 2010 he was earning about $500,000 and was serving on three other fee paying Hershey boards. Then Attorney General Tom Corbett ordered a probe after the Hershey charity made a suspicious purchase.

headline: Poorer school districts have most to lose in governor's budget proposal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget means steep budget cuts to schools across the state. However what the cuts mean to individual districts depends much on their wealth. Some districts rely on the state for up to 70 percent of their funding, while other districts only 25 percent. A review by The Sunday Times and an analysis by the Education Law Center concluded that the governor's proposed cuts fall hardest on districts with the greatest student poverty.

headline: EMT supervisor admits stealing $127K from Honey Brook ambulance company
abstract: A former official of the Honey Brook Fire Company's ambulance division admitted to stealing more than $127,000 in donations to the company. Christopher Aaron Yocum will spend 23 months in Chester County Prison on charges of theft by unlawful taking and criminal conspiracy. A shorter sentence was originally decided by Senior Judge Ronald Nagle but he threw it out for the longer one.

headline: Commission recommends modest impact fee
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale Commission has said that a modest, competitive, impact fee on the natural gas industry is appropriate. PA is the only major gas producing state without a severance tax. Investment and production in the gas field is growing faster than expected.

headline: 6PM News
abstract: Banks and numerous other agencies in the state are lobbying governor Corbett to put aside funding for adult protection services in the upcoming budget

headline: Transportation commission votes for raised fees
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Transportation Funding Commission suggested increasing vehicle and driver registration fees and raising taxes on oil companies to fund the repair and construction of roads and bridges across the Commonwealth. The commission will vote on suggestions and then hand in a report to Corbett.

headline: End the monopoly - support school choice
abstract: The author has kids that go to good public schools. She reasons why she should nonetheless care about the fate of the 91 failing schools in Philadelphia. In 2002, Philadelphia schools were taken over by the state and are now funded by state taxes in addition to local taxes. Under Rendell there was an increase in spending with a decrease in results. She advocates Senate Bill 1, which concerns school choice.

headline: 3 from Pennsylvania to join First Lady during State of the Union address
abstract: West Philadelphia High School junior Brandon Ford and Brandon and Julie Fisher of Berlin-based Center Rock Incorporated have been invited to see US President Barack Obama give his State of the Union address. The highshcooler was originally invited to see the president months before but he forgot his ID. Center Rock Incorporated was invited for their role in helping to rescue 33 Chilean miners. Others who helped US Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords were invited.

headline: After switching from Peco, one customer sees the danger of a variable rate
abstract: Energy consumers who signed up for a variable rate that would fluctuate depending on market conditions saw a massive increase in their energy bills. One provider said that the increase was due to an "unusual" wholesale price spike. Residents in PA are used to regulated utility prices, but are able to buy electricity in a competitive market.

headline: Sen. Casey reports nearly $4 million in war chest
abstract: U.S. Sen. Bob Casey Jr. has nearly $4 million in funds ready for his reelection campaign. Competing for the Republican nomination are Chester County entrepreneur Steve Welch, Washington County businessman Tim Burns, Harrisburg attorney Marc Scaringi, Bucks County veterans’ advocate David Christian, Bedford County pharmacist John Daniel Kensinger III, Armstrong County coal industry veteran Tom Smith, and Tioga County retired Army Col. John Vernon.

headline: DN Editorial: Shale Commission…or shill commission?
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Jim Cawley is part of PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale Commission which voted last week on a number of recommendations. The recommendations will include forced pooling, an impact fee, and tighter regulation for violators of regulations of the PA Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: New law hosed
abstract: The PA House approved the repeal of the requirement that builders equip new homes with fire-sprinkler systems. The author is upset that the very pro-business PA Governor Tom Corbett will not repeal this repeal. Home buyers who pay more for a home with sprinklers will see an immediate drop in their property insurance rates. Volunteer fire fighters like the bill law because it will ensure less fires and therefore less danger to their lives.

headline: Pennsylvania searches for new firm to operate Capitol Cafeteria
abstract: Philadelphia based Aramark Incorporated is looking to leave the Capitol Cafeteria because it does not find it to be profitable. The company recently informed the PA Department of General Services of its plans to leave, giving PA ample time to find a new company to fill the spot. The contract does not end until 2012 but allows either the state or the Company to end the pact for financial reasons.

headline: Corbett's drilling panel set to wrap up work
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale advisory panel will soon meet for the last time. The 30-member group will debate dozens of recommendations. The panel's main duty is to suggest ways for the state to best capitalize on the economic potential of the gas boom while containing environmental problems.

headline: ‘Stories’ compel lawmakers to help
abstract: The stories of local residents affected by recent flooding disasters compelled state Rep. Eddie Day Pashinski to act to help these residents. Pashinski D-Wilkes-Barre, and state Reps. Phyllis Mundy, D-Kingston, Gerald Mullery, D-Newport Twp., and Mike Carroll, D-Avoca, have proposed four bills that could bring relief to thousands of residents affected by recent flooding.

headline: 600 tell lawmakers they need good jobs
abstract: Terry Miale was laid off in 2001 as a result of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. She wants to let PA Congressmen Doyle and Casey know that her district needs good jobs. She calls on Washington to stop playing political games and bring jobs to PA.

headline:
State Lawmakers Working Up Sweat At
Taxpayers' Expense
abstract: The House of Representatives bought two new Precor exercise bikes for the lawmakers' private health club. They are worth more than $5,192. PA Representative Jim Marshall said that he didn’t think the equipment was necessary. Tim Potts of Democracy Rising Pennsylvania said that is was aw ridiculous waste of tax dollars.

headline: Locals march for life
abstract: About 180 Altoona area residents participated in the March for Life rally in Washington DC. This march is in opposition to the 1973 US Supreme Court ruling Roe v. Wade, which legalized abortion. US Representative Eric Cantor of Virginia addressed the crowd. US House Republicans recently released bills which would toughen restrictions on taxpayers funding of abortions.

headline: Monica Yant Kinney: Who killed Pa.'s foreclosure-rescue program?
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget will end the Homeowners' Emergency Mortgage Assistance Program (HEMAP), a program that has brought the state national acclaim. The Wallstreet Journal and the Federal Reserve bank raved that this program encouraged personal accountability. PA State Representative Taylor said that "no-new-taxes" pledges are fun until you see the real-life ramifications.

headline: Marcellus Shale Youth Jobs Forum recruit high school students for industry jobs
abstract: State Rep. Brandon Neuman, D-North Strabane is looking to encourage local youth to train to take the jobs becoming abundant in the region's gas drilling industry. Many of the jobs are going to people from the South due to the lack of qualified local applicants. While the work is long and difficult, the average salary of $76,000 is appealing to many high school graduates.

headline: PSU tuition rising by ‘fair’ amount
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget meant a cut of $68 million to Pennsylvania State University's state allocation. To make up for the loss, spending was reduced and tuition was raised by 4.9 percent. That translates to roughly $700  tuition hike for a year.

headline: Friendly Sons of St. Patrick toast holiday with governor, former Irish PM
abstract: Pa Governor Tom Corbett attended a dinner in the 106th District. There were boos and catcalls in the audience as he defended his agenda. One voice called out: "Tax the gas companies!" He talked of the steep budget cuts to education and social programs.

headline: Fixing Rendell’s tax, borrow and spend mess
abstract: The tax, borrow and spend agenda of PA Governor Rendell  and some PA General Assembly members has not left PA on the path of prosperity. Also, the US Census Bureau showed stagnant population growth in PA and so there in one less congressional seat. Rendell increased the states operating budget by $21 million, leaving his successor with $5 billion in debt.

headline: Local Democratic lawmakers blast state budget as helping rich and hurting poor
abstract: The 2011-12 state budget is $27.2 billion. Democrats in the PA House are calling it detrimental to education and human services, while Republicans, such as PA Governor Tom Corbett and PA Representative Mike Reese, are calling it fiscally responsible. This budget will result in layoffs in the PA Department of Environmental Protection and does not include a tax natural gas extraction.

headline: Corbett moves toward Harrisburg takeover.
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is taking steps to takeover the finances of the City of Harrisburg. In defiance of the governor, Harrisburg City Council has filed for bankruptcy protection. The city continues to seek a way to limit the state's authority.

headline: Cheating also reflects poorly on testing
abstract: Steven Levitt and Stephen Dubner, authors of "Freakonomics" (2005), found that teachers boosted their students standardized test results. Many schools started offering financial incentives for teachers whose students scored higher than previous years; this came after the national No Child Left Behind program pointed to inadequacies in public education. The PA Department of Education detected possible cheating in PA.

headline: Montco legislator addresses board on state budget cuts
abstract: School districts in Montgomery County are facing budget cuts. PA Representative Todd Stevens met with four area superintendents to discuss subsidies. Stevens said that PA Governor Tom Corbett's plan to reduce social security reimbursements to school districts will hit the 151st Legislative District harder than others.

headline: 6,000 had no power on season's coldest day
abstract: More than 6,000 PPL customers were without power Monday, which was one of the coldest days of the season. Some outages lasted around 87 minutes. Many schools had to close.

headline: Pittsburgh School District Considers Closing More Schools
abstract: Pittsburgh Public Schools Superintendent Linda Lane has outlined the process to determine recommendations for school closings and realignment for the 2012-13 school year in response to state budget cuts.

headline: State House, Senate pass takeover law
abstract: The PA legislature has passed a bill that authorizes the takeover of the state's capital city, Harrisburg.

headline: Midstate district attorney considers Pennsylvania attorney general run in 2012
abstract: Cumberland County’s David Freed and Dauphin County’s Edward M. Marsico Jr. may both run for the statewide position of attorney general. However, it seems that only Freed will go on to run. Marsico has stated that he is comfortable in his current position, while Freed recently attended a dinner with top Republican officials and floated the idea, receiving a positive response.

headline: City schools may slash capital spending
abstract: Pittsburgh Schools Superintendent Linda Lane thinks that the city could reduce its debt service by cutting $45 million in capital projects. The biggest project that is being delayed is the renovation of Pittsburgh Arlington PreK-8.

headline: Warrior Run responds to bullying incident
abstract: Dr. John Kurelja, superintendent of Warrior Run School District, said that he and his administration are taking serious steps to respond to a bullying incident that took place in December. The school board will initiate the Positive Behavior Plan. The school website will be updated to reflect the changes.

headline: Whole Foods in McCandless to sell beer and wine
abstract: The Whole Foods grocery store expected to open in the Wexford Plaza late in 2011 will be the first in Western Pennsylvania to sell alcohol following  a public hearing on transferring a liquor license to the Perry Highway store. Town Council is expected to approve the transfer on July 5.

headline: Study says casino-funded PA grant program to end for fire, rescue and ambulance companies.
abstract: Unless lawmakers reauthorize the program, millions in funding for Pennsylvania fire, rescue and ambulance companies will expire. More than 2,700 companies have benefited from the grants. The state fire commissioner says that if the program is not reauthorized by February, it may not be in time.

headline: Delozier wants to update Small Games of Chance law
abstract: PA Representative Delozier wants to allow nonprofits to use small games to cover operating expenses. A spokeswomen for the PA Tavern Association states that this hurts small businesses. PA Governor Tom Corbett thinks that the small games law should be updated but he does not support allowing the games at for-profit bars and restaurants.

headline: Plan to reduce transit funds is DOA
abstract: The Port Authority in Allegheny county planned service cuts. Allegheny County Council proposed to cut funding to the authority. Under Home Rule Charter, however, the county budget cannot be amended unless the county executive approves. County Executive Dan Onorato has not approved, stating that the cuts would result in further cuts.

headline: Admitted drug dealer gets five years in prison
abstract: Joseph R. Paige IV, 23, admitted to having conspired to sell cocaine in Milton, PA. He was sentenced by US District Judge John E. Jones III to five years in prison. This term will run consecutive to a 2- to 4- year Philadelphia drug case.

headline: Legislature approves expanded 'happy hour' bill
abstract: The general assembly approved a bill that would allow bars to offer happy-hour specials up to four hours per day, not to exceed 14 hours per week. Current law limits happy hours to two hours per day.

headline: Dr. Sordoni honored for contributions
abstract: Dr. Susan Fort Sordoni, the founder of the Volunteers in Medicine clinic on Pennsylvania Avenue in Wilkes-Barre, was honored for her contributions to society. She along with eight other women received awards at the governor's residence in Harrisburg.

headline: DN Editorial: Harrisburg dickers over liquor privatization
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Mike Turzai has proposed a plan to privatize PA liquor stores, stripping the PA Liquor Control Board of this authority. PA Governor Tom Corbett has argued that privatization will give consumers more choice. Many worry that the 5,000 state workers who staff the state liquor operations would lose their jobs, but Turzai said that his proposal includes tax credits to hire these workers.

headline: Ackerman bonus disturbingly generous, auditor general says
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner has come out against the cash strapped Philadelphia School System. A contract for Superintendent Arlene C. Ackerman includes lucrative bonuses. Recently School Reform Commission Chairman Robert L. Archie praised Ackerman for leading the district to "tremendous academic strides."

headline: Tuesday Morning Coffee: The Revolution Is Just A Tee-Shirt Away.
abstract: Former Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell has been named a NBC News political analyst. He has been a frequent guest on NBC News broadcasts. He says that he is excited to start the new job, as the country faces "critical challenges."

headline: WPXI-NBC  Pittsburgh, PA  Ch. 11 News
abstract: 26 positions will be cut from the Gateway School District in response to budget cuts to education.

headline: Group homes for disabled told to expect slashed budget
abstract: The state Department of Public Welfare has informed providers of mental health services of a 6 percent cut in funding for group homes. DPW officials have identified wasteful expenditures in some private homes that house about 16,000 PA residents total. The wait list for such housing also numbers 16,000.

headline: Rep. Mike Kelly sells interests in oil and gas companies
abstract: PA Representative Mike Kelly told the Sharron Herald that he sold his stock in Phillips Resources and T.W. Phillips. Critics said that the stock was a conflict of interest because the representative supports federal subsidies for the oil and gas industry.

headline:
F&M poll: Pa. rates Corbett
Majorities oppose education cuts, tax policy
abstract: A statewide Franklin and Marshall College poll found that a majority of Pennsylvanians are confident that PA Governor Tom Corbett can handle the budget problem. Nonetheless, many disagree with him on important policy, like his refusal to tax natural gas extraction and his proposed spending cuts to public schools.

headline: Reducing the deficit and growing the economy will be the hot topics in 2011
abstract: US President Barack Obama recently debated with Republican leaders over how to deal with the deficit and expand the economy. This will likely set the terms for the 2012 elections. US Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell said that he and his fellow Republicans would do all in their power to stop spending increases. Obama talked with Organizing for America about job creation.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 5
abstract: Legislation has been proposed that would ban teacher strikes in Pennsylvania.

headline: The legislation for a state takeover of Harrisburg could wind up on governor Corbett's desk this week
abstract: Legislation authorizing the state takeover of its troubled capital city is poised to clear both chambers of the PA legislature this week.  A bill could be ready for the governor's signature soon.

headline: Corbett blames teacher layoffs on school districts
