abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is blaming teacher layoffs on school districts, not on budget cuts he made to the state budget. He said that school districts should have budgeted more conservatively. He also stated that school districts should have more wisely spent federal stimulus money.

headline: Teachers must 'do our part,' union chief says
abstract: James Testerman of the PA State Education Association has sent a letter to local affiliates to discuss a one year pay freeze and other cost saving measures with their school boards. He thinks that we should take seriously PA Governor Tom Corbett's call for the freeze, but still keep the welfare of students in mind. Many shot back saying that legislators are not taking a pay freeze.

headline: State Senators' school voucher proposal draws critics, supporters
abstract: PA Senators Jeffrey Piccola and Anthony Williams recently announced plans to propose legislation that would offer vouchers to allow low-income students to attend a different public or private school. PA Governor Tom Corbett talked favorably of school vouchers in his inaugural address. The Pennsylvania School Boards Association, which opposed vouchers under former PA Governor Tom Ridge, has come out again against the system.

headline: WTXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: Teachers are expressing their discontent with Governor Tom Corbett's proposed budget, which cuts funding to public schools.

headline: Bridges in Pittsburgh labeled the worst
abstract: A study by Transportation for America, a coalition of groups seeking reform of national transportation policy, Pittsburgh has the highest percentage of structurally deficient bridges in the U.S. The report said that 70,000 bridges were structurally deficient in the US. The Federal Highway Administration says it would cost $70.9 billion to eliminate the maintenance backlog.

headline: Turzai estimates $2 billion in revenues from liquor store selloff
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Mike Turzai is working to privatize liquor and wine sales. The state would close over 600 liquor stores and auction over 1200 licenses. Turzai estimates that the plan could generate over $2 billion in revenue for the state.

headline: Dismantling law a slap in the face
abstract: PA Representative Jim Cox has sponsored a resolution to study the 2008 puppy mill bill. The author is very upset with the PA legislature, citing is lack of dedication the projects many legislators campaigned on, like property tax elimination and reducing the size of the legislature.

headline: Cohen: Health-care 'myths' actually lies
abstract: The author defends US President Barack Obama's health care reform. He thinks that it is not a government takeover. The "Death Panels" that Alaska Governor Sarah Palin talks about are a "damned lie." What was deemed death panels by the opposition were in fact end-of-life counseling for the elderly.

headline: Corbett's budget hits those trying to get by the hardest
abstract: The author discusses her plight as a nontraditional undergraduate students, specifically her financial difficulties and the threat posed by a budget cut to higher education.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate passes Harrisburg takeover bill with a 37-13 vote
abstract: Legislation approving the takeover of the City of Harrisburg passed the Senate and heads to the House. Meanwhile, Harrisburg City Council has filed for bankruptcy in spite of the state government disputing the eligibility of such a filing.

headline: Local delegation frustrated, too
abstract: US President Barack Obama has been negotiating a deal behind closed doors with the leaders of both parties to raise the nation's $14.3 trillion borrowing limit. Republicans won't accept a deal that includes more tax revenues; Democrats won't agree to cuts in Social Security and Medicare. Presidential candidate Michele Bachmann of Minnesota has said that she will not vote to raise the debt limit under any circumstance.

headline: Commentary: Future appears to be at least partly nuclear
abstract: PA is a the second largest generator of nuclear power in the US. It is also the home of two of the world's largest natural gas plays. The reactor meltdown in Japan after the tsunamis has roused fears of the energy source once again in PA. US Senator from PA Bob Casey is monitoring the situation in Japan and is making sure we prepared for similar problems. US President Barack Obama believes that nuclear energy can help us move away from fossil fuels.

headline: GOP Forum On Special Election Candidate
abstract: PA Senator Mike O'Pake has passed away and has left open a seat. The Berks County GOP recently hosted a forum so the public could meet those vying for the Republican nomination. Those in attendance commented that it will be tough to decide between the six men that are running for the spot.

headline: Arguments made of straw
abstract: The author calls out what he believes are paradoxes in the day's politics: US President Barack Obama can ask GE to help reform the corporate tax structure when they do not pay taxes. PA Governor Tom Corbett can claim that gas drillers will leave the state if a severance tax is imposed. Alaskan Governor Sarah Palin is considered a serious candidate for President, etc.

headline: Harrisburg finance takeover bill poised to pass
abstract: The bill that authorizes the state to take over the troubled finances of the City of Harrisburg is expected to pass.  City leaders share their concerns.

headline: DN Editorial: Different democracies at work in Act 1
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett says that he is not responsible for teacher layoffs that will result from his budget cuts to education. The author thinks that this is an unfair assessment to make because his budget also included a law making it harder for districts to raise taxes. More tax hikes will have to go before voters.

headline: Corbett's turnpike appointment sends wrong signal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett said that the culture of favoritism had to end when he got elected. His actions seem to oppose this sentiment; he recently gave a family friend a job running the PA Turnpike, earning close to $200,000 a year. To be fair though, Roger Nutt, the friend, has over 30 year experience working for the New Jersey Turnpike Authority.

headline: Ex-Erie man faces arraignment on charges in 2004 shooting
abstract: Craig C. Carroll, 31, has been taken into custody by the Erie police. He is charged with a 2004 shooting on the city's east side. He was arrested in Georgia in 2007 on unrelated charges and had been serving a prison sentence there since.

headline: Toomey authors balanced budget bill
abstract: Newly elected US Senator from PA Pat Toomey is a big voice on budget reform. Today the senator will lead his first US Capitol news conference to introduce a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution. This is a melding of two bills introduced by US Senators Rand Paul and Olympia Snowe. The heritage Foundation and other groups showed support for the legislation.

headline: PA House OKs HIV tests for sex-assault defendants.
abstract: The state House voted 197-to-1 to require defendants in sexual assault cases get tested for HIV. Allegheny County Republican Rep. Mark Mustio sponsored the bill and says that it will ensure PA will receive full grant funding through the federal Violence Against Women Act.

headline: Liquor store workers union wary of privatization plan
abstract: Opponents to the privatization of liquor sales in PA worry that many of the 5,000 workers employed by state-owned liquor stores will lose their jobs. PA House Majority Leader Mike Turzai disagrees, stating that these workers will be an asset to retail store owners, as they know the product. United Food and Commercial Workers Local 1776 has blasted the proposal.

headline: Obama Urges Pa. Lawmakers To Save Education
abstract: US President Barack Obama said that he understands the budget dilemma that PA faces and how it could hurt public schools. He commented that the country is trouble both at the state and the federal level. He is urging Congress to fix the No Child Left Behind Act.

headline: Shell expanding in Haynesville Shale
abstract: Shell Exploration and Production Corporation is building an office complex near Mansfield. It will service its work in the Haynesville Shale natural gas field in northwestern Louisiana. Shell has stake in more than 340,000 acres in the Haynesville Shale area.

headline: Ground broken for turnpike interchange in Chesco
abstract: Ground was broken in Chester County as the all-electronic interchange linking the Pennsylvania Turnpike and Route 29 is ready to open. The new system should reduce congestion. The project was funded by tolls.

headline: Infinity Charter School in Penbrook has a perfect record in meeting the yearly academic performance targets
abstract: Infinity Charter School in Penbrook was the only charter school in the state to have all of its students score at or above grade level on the state’s reading and math exams last spring. Only three other schools in the state had its students show such proficiency. Some of the controversy surrounding charter schools and their effect on the public school population are examined.

headline: Privatization bill introduced
abstract: PA Representative Turzai has introduced legislation to privatize the sale of liquor in PA. The bill has much support from Republicans but very little from Democrats. PA Representative Evans thinks that even the Republican controlled House will not pass the bill. PA Governor Tom Corbett is not endorsing this proposal but is in support of privatization.

headline: Berks Democrat elected to succeed O'Pake in state Senate
abstract: Democrat Judy Schwank, a former Berks County commissioner, won a special election to succeed the late Michael O'Pake as PA Senator from the 11th District. Schwank ran on lower property taxes and more protections for farms.

headline: Giffords able to stand up as she readies for rehab (video)
abstract: US Representative Gabrielle Giffords, who survived a bullet wound to the brain, will soon undergo extensive mental and physical rehabilitation. This is based on new research that shows that starting therapy sooner is better.

headline: New DEP pick says he will 'apply the law'
abstract: Michael Krancer was lauded by mine workers for a sensitive decision he made despite the PA Department of Environmental Protection. Some are now skeptical of the judge as he leads the DEP under PA Governor Tom Corbett who has taken significant campaign contributions from the natural gas industry and opposes a severance tax.

headline: Act 47 could cost city 10 police positions
abstract: Act 47, a state initiative aimed at financially distressed municipalities, may cause Reading's police force to cut 10 officers in 2012. The department already has nearly 50 fewer officers than in 2009. City Council is struggling to find money in the budget to help the police department.

headline: Democratic Policy Committee examines budget impacts
abstract: School districts have to scramble to make due after PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget cut education. PA Representative Sturla is traveling around the state to see what schools are doing to cope, and thinks that the Governor should use tax surplus to fund education. Corbett fired back, stating that school districts have a duty to responsibly budget.

headline: Obama seeks to rewrite 'No Child' law
abstract: US President Barack Obama is urging Congress to rewrite the No Child Left Behind Act. This is in line with his campaign for an overhaul of public education. Lawmakers are likely to include other issues like merit pay and public vouchers for students to attend private school. The White House describes talks by the House and Senate to be productive.

headline: Schuylkill rep named to 4 House committees
abstract: PA Representative Neal Goodman has been appointed to serve on the House Labor and Industry, Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness, Professional Licensure and Gaming Oversight committees for the 2011-12 legislative session. Goodman will remain the chairman of the Northeast Delegation.

headline: Gas industry buying time and influence
abstract: Last year the gas industry gave more than $3.4 million to state elections. PA Governor Tom Corbett, and PA Senators Jake Corman and Joe Scarnati were among the highest recipients. Until 2002 the gas wells paid property taxes but the PA Supreme Court found that assessment of oil and gas wells was not clearly defined in the statutes. Citizens pay more in property taxes because of the industry.

headline: Legislative panel gives nod to red light cameras
abstract: A bill that would allow Pittsburgh and other large cities to install red-light cameras won approval from the state Senate Appropriations Committee. It passed with a 21-5 vote, however it faces an uncertain future in the House. State Sen. Jim Ferlo, D-Highland Park, denounced the measure as "nothing more than a revenue-generating activity. It has nothing to do with public safety," he said.

headline: Authority awards sidewalk contract
abstract: The Uniontown Redevelopment Authority has awarded Parkside Contracting of South Park a roughly $30,000 contract to construct 1,000 feet of sidewalks on Maple Street.

headline: State budget fight headed to local communities
abstract: The budget debate will become relevant to local communities in ways that it has not in years. PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget will seek wage and benefits concessions from school district and state government employees and cut state aid to higher education. He also seeks salary rollbacks and high health care contributions in upcoming contract negotiations with unions representing state employees.

headline: State's 46th Governor Faces Deficit In Billions
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett faces a $3 to $5 million deficit. His inaugural speech did not address the deficit but stayed true to his campaign promises of limited government, fiscal responsibility and no new taxes. Lieutenant Governor Jim Cawley was sworn in today; he left his Bucks County board of commissioners position to take the job.

headline: Temple fears a future with less funding
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's proposed budget would cut Temple University's state funding from $172 million to $80 million. Temple's senior vice president said that the school will need to raise tuition, cut jobs and make program cuts to make up for the loss. Temple has encouraged students to ask their elected officials to speak out against the cuts.

headline: Join forces on flood plans
abstract: Duryea residents recently took to their borough council to criticize the response to recent flooding that ruined hundreds of homes. Going forward, planning for these disasters should be done at a wider scale, involving more levels of government.

headline: Racetrack license transfer approved
abstract: The PA Harness Racing Commission transferred the last harness-racing license to Pittsburgh-based American Harness Tracks. The facility has 60 days to provide a management agreement and obtain proof of at least $150 million in financing for the project. Receiving and keeping this license would allow the company to apply with the state Gaming Control Board for the more lucrative casino license.

headline: Economic shockwaves to reach Pennsylvania
abstract: The earthquakes that devastated Japan will affect the business in PA. More than 200 companies do business there, exporting more than $1.7 billion in goods each year. According to the Allegheny Conference on Community Development, damage from tsunami might have more of an impact on contracts than on investments by companies.

headline: Obama to visit Penn State
abstract: US President Barack Obama will meet with leaders from Penn State University to discuss the university's Energy Innovation Hub. This is part of his agenda to promote clean energy, innovation and jobs, as outlined in his State of the Union speech. Penn State received $129 million from the US Department of Energy to create the Energy Innovation Hub at the Philadelphia Navy Yard.

headline: Pa. high court OKs King of Prussia casino
abstract: The Valley Forge Convention Center can now include 600 slot machines and 50 tables games. This comes after the PA Supreme Court ruled that the venue fit the definition of an established resort hotel under the state's gaming law. The court ruled 3-2 in favor of the PA Gaming Control Board's decision.

headline: Electoral college change proposal
abstract: Controversial changes are being proposed regarding how PA distributes its electoral votes in presidential elections.

headline: State representative asks for school "Whistle-blower Hotline" on tests
abstract: PA State Representative McGeehan called on the state education secretary to create a confidential, statewide "Whistle-blower Hotline." The idea is to encourage school staffers to report testing irregularities. McGeehan met with Philadelphia School District teachers to discuss the hotline. Some said that they feared penalization from the district for coming forward.

headline: Commentary: Real March Madness is schools' PSSA tests
abstract: Students will take the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment tests in March. The test is in part used to measure how well teachers are doing their jobs. Results also go to the federal government under the No Child Left Behind Act to see if students are achieving their "Adequate Yearly Progress.” Some worry the tests affect intellectual curiosity.

headline: Man arrested for fighting in Frackville is illegal immigrant
abstract: A West Mahanoy Township man charged with trying to stab a borough man in the stomach with a box cutter Friday is an illegal immigrant from Honduras. Flores-Laines has been charged with two counts each of aggravated assault and simple assault and one count each of possession of prohibited offensive weapons, reckless endangerment and harassment, police said. District Judge Elizabeth Romig will schedule his preliminary hearing.

headline: What Corbett's budget is full of
abstract: The author is not satisfied with PA Governor Tom Corbett's new budget: The new budget is full of recriminations. Corbett claims that former PA Governor Ed Rendell misused federal stimulus money. Corbett claims that the deficit is the result of too much spending. He is wrong; the recession caused tax revenues to sink.

headline: Irene is costliest storm in Peco's recent history
abstract: Hurricane Irene, which knocked out more than 30 percent of Peco's customers, is officially the costliest storm in Peco's recent history. It cost the Philadelphia utility $45 million. Spokespeople for other utilities say they are still tabulating the final cost of the August storm.

headline: Turzai plan would double liquor retailers
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Mike Turzai will introduce his plan to privatize liquor and wine sales. This could effectively double the number of liquor stores in PA, as the bill would mean the closure of 609 state-owned stores and the auction of 1,250 licenses. Turzai said that the plan would include tax incentives to stores that hire former state workers under the PA Liquor Control Board.

headline: Letters: Nonprofits are partners; help them help the state
abstract: A statement from the Jill Michal, President and CEO of United Way of Southeastern Pennsylvania: Governor Tom Corbett's budget of no new taxes is asking us to build a "new Pennsylvania." We still need to remember those in the safety net. The real job of non profits is to ensure the social structure is equipped to support and prepare workers.

headline: Early care means good teeth in small children
abstract: About half of all Head Start students in Schuylkill County need dental care. Child Development Incorporated has focused on educating new parents about dental health at an early age. Head Start provides grants to local, public, and private and non-profit agencies to provide comprehensive child care for disadvantaged children.

headline: PA Senate OKs second bill to widen self-defense law.
abstract: The Senate is revisiting castle doctrine, reviewing a bill that would expand a person's right to use deadly force against an attacker outside the home. A similar bill passed under PA Governor Ed Rendell, but he vetoed, fearing that the bill would lead to more violence.

headline: What was he thinking?
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is criticized for his lack of media access. He was recently in the area, however the press was not informed of a key visit at the Greene County Fairgrounds. Corbett delivered a speech about issues such as gas drilling, education and the state budget.

headline: Mann supports stronger penalties
abstract: Terry Collopy has admitted to murder. She is sentenced to 20 to 40 years in prison.

headline: Team 4: State Lawmakers Sitting Comfy In Expensive Seats
abstract: Budget hearings recently began in Harrisburg. Legislators decided on how to cut the $4 billion dollar deficit while sitting on $1000 chairs, said a spokesperson from Democracy Rising. House Republicans ordered the chairs for the majority caucus room. PA Representative Richard Stevenson, the Republican Caucus Administrator, bought other expensive chairs (using tax payer money) that could be found online for half the price.

headline: Wis. GOP, Dem parties wager with Pa. counterparts
abstract: The Wisconsin Republican party has made a wager regarding the superbowl with the PA legislature. They have put up two pounds of 10-year-old cheddar, six pounds of bratwurst and one case of Sprecher Root Beer, while PA has put up four orders of Pamela's Pancakes, four Primanti Brothers sandwiches and one case of Iron City beer.

headline: Vouchers put spotlight on education
abstract: PA Representative Jeff Piccola and Senator Anthony Williams have proposed a bill that would fund school vouchers. This means public money for kids to attend private schools. This will help kids in localities that do not have the tax base to provide the level of funding that more well-to-do districts have. PA Governor Ed Rendell made similar strides but not through vouchers.

headline: Military veteran will have seat on PA Civil Service Commission
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett has signed into law a measure that creates a permanent spot on the state Civil Service Commission for a veteran. The body oversees the hiring of state employees. Veterans are supposed to have an advantage in being hired for state employment.

headline: DN Editorial: Measuring the value of summer school
abstract: The South Eastern Transportation Authority recently briefed US Congressmen Casey and Fattah, and Peter Rogoff, head of the Federal Transportation Administration. The briefing dealt with the state of the transportation system in PA. This was an attempt to lobby for more federal funding, as $4.2 billion are needed to restore the system. A reduction in state funding has stalled many efforts.

headline: Certain tort reforms overdue in Pennsylvania
abstract: A survey from the PA Chamber of Business and Industry finds that the business environment could be improved by tort reform. The legislature failed to pass a law similar to the current "fair share act" under former PA Governor Ed Rendell, because he vetoed it. Also in 2002 under former PA Governor Mark Schweiker, the legislation was batted down because of technicalities in its passage of the legislature.

headline: Minority opinions face new struggle
abstract: Republicans and Democrats are waging a big battle in the PA House Rules Committee. The Republicans sent a bill to the House that would allow the majority to table any amendment made by the minority without discussion. Committee Majority Chairman Mike Turzai shut down discussion in the last Rules Committee meeting after accusing Democrats of obstructionism.

headline: Why Scott Walker must win
abstract: The author criticizes the "anti-democratic methods" that US President Obama's "union allies" are using in Wisconsin to fight cuts to government workers' pay and pension. Some demonstrators carried placards with crosshairs over the face of Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker. He thinks that government workers should have to pay their fair share for pension and health care costs.

headline: Vouchers, charter schools top Governor Corbett's education reform plan
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett wants to put a state commission in charge of overseeing charter schools in the state. He wants control to be taken out of the hands of local school districts. He also advises opponents that his voucher plan does not neglect local public schools because the money to fund the charters comes from the state, not local property taxes.

headline: DN Editorial: Measuring the value of summer school
abstract: A power shift within the PA legislature and executive seemed to mean less would be attention paid to Philadelphia. PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget confirms this. School districts will surely suffer, but the city itself needs to look into how money is being spent. A summer school program shows that taxpayer money may have been unwisely spent.

headline: Fund used to fill gaps in social service budgets will be cut under Gov. Tom Corbett's proposed budget
abstract: This year $16,400 from the PA Human Service Development Fund helped a Harrisburg emergency shelter to extend its service. If PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget is passed, that money and other similar programs will disappear. Counties use such money to fill gaps in their service budgets. Dauphin County Commissioner George Hartwick III thinks this goes against some of what Corbett has proposed.

headline: Municipalities set to adopt stormwater ordinance
abstract: Lycoming County will soon implement the Stormwater Management Plan. The plan is designed to reduce flooding and erosion and increase water quality in county watersheds. State laws requires municipalities to adopt an ordinance implementing the plan by March 16, 2011.

headline: State to hold hearing on Armstrong renovation projects
abstract: State Education Department officials have announced that they will hold a public hearing on the Armstrong School District's $80 million school renovation projects. The announcement comes on the heels of a letter sent to acting education secretary Ronald Tomalis by two state senators and a state representative, asking that the department further review the proposed projects before approving financial reimbursement to the district.

headline: Officials At Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board Want To Restore Their Image
abstract: William Ryan, chairman of Pennsylvania’s Gaming Control Board says his board has an image problem. Ryan supports efforts to move the gaming board’s Bureau of Investigations and Enforcement to the authority of the attorney general.

headline: Looking ahead to state AG's race
abstract: Kathleen Kane and PA Representative Patrick Murphy have launched campaigns for the statewide office of attorney general. No republicans have so far launched campaigns. PA Governor Tom Corbett served as attorney general before becoming governor.

headline: More schools likely to fall short of state achievement standards
abstract: PA students will soon take the Pennsylvania System of Student Assessment. The number of school districts failing to meet tougher math and reading scores is likely to rise. State officials wield considerable power under federal law to make drastic changes if standards are not met. US Education Secretary Arne Duncan told Congress that up to 82 percent of schools could fail to meet the adequate yearly progress.

headline: state police troopers injured in crash
abstract: Troopers Alex Grote and Donald Beynon were responding to an in-progress domestic incident when they struck a pick-up truck. The truck failed to yield the right of way. The officers are being treated for minor injuries; the truck driver was uninjured.

headline: Law to ban bath salts headed to House today
abstract: Legislation that would ban specific types of bath salts could be headed to the House Judiciary Committee  for consideration. The legislation, now broken up into three separate bills to ban synthetic marijuana, bath salts and salvia, are sponsored by state Reps. Jennifer Man, D-132, Jerry A. Stern, R-80, and RoseMarie Swanger, R-102. If passed, Pennsylvania would become the 18th state to ban the substances.

headline: House debates prevailing wage for public works projects
abstract: Opponents say that a plan by the House Republicans would result in lower pay for construction workers. Current law sets a minimum wage that government in PA must pay to workers involved in public works projects. Supporters of the law say that it kills jobs.

headline: Reflective signs required by 2018, but cities, boroughs stuck with bill
abstract: The federal government instituted unfunded mandates on improving nighttime visibility of street signs. Municipalities have until 2015 to replace warning and regulatory signs and until 2018 to replace guidance and street-name signs. The larger letters and brighter signs are intended to help an aging population drive safely. Carbondale, PA, Mayor Justin Taylor says that such a replacement will cost up to $60,000, money not in the budget.

headline: Corbett's chainsaw budget cutting is irresponsible
abstract: The author thinks that majority of those who voted for PA Governor Tom Corbett liked the sound of no new taxes. But now people want no new taxes without budget cuts. The author states that this is unrealistic. The author thinks that Corbett is irresponsible and it is unfair that his business "cronies" are getting a "free pass." Governor of Wisconsin Scott Walker got the public-sector unions to agree to some pretty painful cuts.

headline: Pittsburgh puts entertainment technology on center stage
abstract: The Pittsburgh Film Office designed Pittsburgh Entertainment Technology Project  to introduce innovative companies to the film boom that has swept southeastern PA. The idea is to help a variety of different technologies interact with one another. The film industry has pumped some $560 million into the region since the film office opened in 1990 and the tax incentive program for the film industry began in 2007.

headline: Rendell and Santorum, a study in contrasts
abstract: Article discusses the personalities and political ideologies of both Ed Rendell and Rick Santorum and the media’s reaction to their often controversial remarks on both political and social issues.

headline: Pa. Progressive Summit To Be Held In Philadelphia This Winter
abstract: The Pennsylvania Progressive Summit is expected to hold its winter gathering in Philadelphia this year. Jonathan Saidel, a member of its board of directors, says the summit will focus on key public policy issues. Last year's summit was in Pittsburgh where the Rev. Jesse Jackson delivered the keynote address.

headline: Governor’s first-inning scorecard
abstract: The article weighs the good and bad of PA Governor Tom Corbett's first budget. Budget cuts returned state universities to pre-stimulus levels and made major cuts to corporate welfare programs. The budget did not make cuts deep enough to address deficits in unemployment compensation and pensions. The budget does little to reduce PA's onerous tax burden--the 10th highest nationwide.

headline: Push to drug test welfare recipients renewed
abstract: PA Senator Richard Alloway is sponsoring a bill that would require those seeking PA cash assistance to agree to random drug tests. The bill would amend the Public Welfare Code to deny benefits to individuals who do pass state funded drug tests. Andy Hoover, a legislative director with the American civil liberties Union of PA says the bill is misguided and unconstitutional.

headline: Pittsburgh Teacher Academy to begin with smaller class than anticipated
abstract: The Pittsburgh Teacher Academy Residency will begin with smaller numbers than expected. Superintendent Linda Lane filed for federal money for the school and only received about half of the $30 million she requested. The smaller grant means that fewer teachers can be in residency. A spokesperson from the Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers said that the academy is important for the professional development of teachers.

headline: Kongsberg donates to Flight 93 memorial
abstract: Kongsberg Defense Corp., which builds tripod-mounted guns for the military, donated $30,000 toward construction of the Flight 93 National Memorial.

headline: Corbett expected to reveal Marcellus Shale drilling policy package
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is expected to announce a plan to charge a fee on natural gas drillers that would go to the local areas most affected by the drilling activity. The fee is expected to generate $200 million a year according to Senate President Pro Temp Joe Scarnati. They hope to pass the bill by the end of the session.

headline: Turzai initiatives debate over state store privatization
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Mike Turzai initiated talks on legislation that would privatize state liquor stores. Many attempts have been made to do this, but none have ever been adopted.

headline: Giving up booze
abstract: The author is supportive of PA Governor Tom Corbett's push to get the state out of the liquor business. He thinks it will be difficult to find a solution that protects taxpayers. The Liquor Control Board is state run business. State House Majority Leader Mike Turzai says that selling the liquor licenses could bring in close to $2 billion to fix the budget.

headline: County Recorder of Deeds field gets even bigger
abstract: Former Hempfield Area school board member Maria DiPiazza has joined the Westmoreland County recorder of deeds race. There are now four competitors looking to unseat incumbent Tom Murphy. Murphy owes the federal government about $71,000 in unpaid taxes.

headline: More than 7,000 customers in N.J. are without power
abstract: Ice is snapping tree limbs and thereby bringing down power lines in New Jersey. About 7,650 homes and businesses are without electricity. Crews are working to fix the situation but their job is hampered continually by icy roads.

headline: Corbett wants to change teacher evaluation system
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's school reform proposals are discussed.

headline: Nonunionized Pennsylvania government workers upset over paycheck imbalances
abstract: Since the recession began nonunion and management state employee wages have been frozen. As gas prices rise, utility bills rise and groceries cost more, many hope that PA Governor Tom Corbett will give them a raise. Although the 2010-11 fiscal year ended with a $780 million surplus, his administration has no plans for raises.

headline: Santorum could be unlikely Iowa force
abstract: Although US Senator Rick Santorum lost a reelection bid by 18 percent in 2006, he could still wield a lot of influence in the 2012 presidential election. The article talks about the various circumstances that could lead to Santorum winning the vote in Iowa. Former US Congressman Bob Dole and former US President George Bush managed to capture Iowa.

headline: Public-private transportation deals sought for state's roads
abstract: PA Representative Rick Geist says that public private partnerships are a good idea for PA. These partnerships could be the answer as many roads are in disrepair and PA Governor Tom Corbett has vowed not raise any new taxes. A policy analyst from the House Transportation Committee's Republican caucus says that partnerships could offset 10 to 15 percent of the transportation funding crisis.

headline: Donchez announces re-election bid for Bethlehem council
abstract: Bethlehem City Councilman, Robert Donchez, has always supported the zoning that paved the way for the redevelopment of Bethlehem Steel. He announced that he will run for a fifth term. He thinks that we need to keep a closer eye on city finance. Last year the city spent $6 million in capitol expenses on day-to-day expenses when the cash flow got tight.

headline: Healthy separation: State gaming investigators deserve independence
abstract: State Rep. Mike Vereb, a Republican from Montgomery County has proposed a way for the state Gaming Control Board to get itself out of an arrangement that is compromising the credibility of the board.  The plan would take enforcement of background checks on license applicants, employees and vendors out of the Gaming Control Board's hands and give that responsibility to the state attorney general's office. This would eliminate the chance for another compromising scandal.

headline: Pennsylvania eliminates motorcycle sales 'blue law'
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed legislation eliminating the "blue law." That law prevented the sale of motorcycles on Sunday.

headline: Groups say facilities wrongly discharging drilling wastewater
abstract: Clean Water Action and Three Rivers Waterkeeper recently filed an intent to sue against McKeesport and Franklin, claiming that the sewage treatment plants are in violation of the federal Clean Water Act. The facilities were dumping Marcellus shale wastewater into the Monongahela River and did not have federal permits. Clean Water Action was very critical of the PA Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: School choice gains widespread momentum
abstract: Alberta C. Wilson, who heads Faith First Educational Assistance Corporation, recently held an event in favor of school choice. PA Governor Tom Corbett is behind such measures. School choice would allow many low-income children to transfer to schools of their choice with publically funded scholarships or vouchers. PA has proposed expanding the Educational Improvement Tax Credit like some other states.

headline: Erie man charged with firing shots outside fast-food restaurant
abstract: David G. Taylor is accused of firing two shots in the drive-through lane at a McDonald's Restaurant in Erie County. He was arrested on charges of terroristic threats, reckless endangerment and other charges. He is being held in the Erie County Prison on $50,000 bond following his arraignment before Erie 6th Ward District Judge Dominick DiPaolo.

headline: Legislators say they didn’t know ‘no-tax pledge’ was career-long commitment
abstract: Legislators discuss the implications of a no-tax campaign pledge they signed.

headline: Districts face tough choices with referendum changes
abstract: Luzerne County Treatment Court recently graduated 13 people after they completed a one-year program. The former drug addicts had their records expunged after graduation. PA Representative Day was present. Luzerne County Judges Lewis Wetzel and Joseph Carmody oversee the program.

headline: Grand jury probe into Philly GOP committee election started
abstract: District Attorney Seth Williams has launched a grand jury investigation. He sees irregularities in the last elections for Republican committeemen. Curtis Douglas, a deputy district attorney, is in charge of the investigation. A number of signatures on ballots collected by the committeemen were fake.

headline: Please Touch Museum feeling pain from debt load
abstract: The new Please Touch Museum is struggling now that it has moved to its Fairmount location. The museum came about $20 million shy of its $80 million fundraising goal. This happened partly because the resale value of their old facility was lower than expected, said the Philadelphia Authority for Industrial Development. Leaders of the museum say that it is important that the museum be upheld because it teaches children about art.

headline: Revenue growth won't fill shortfall
abstract: Kenneth Gailey, who worked for the PA Department of Transportation for 16 years, does not think that raising taxes is the solution for fixing the $ 4 billion deficit. He thinks instead that the state should eliminate high-end salaries and make government more efficient. PA Representative Joe Markosek said that it is not right that PA faces a mounting deficit despite a boost in the economy and a boost in tax collections.

headline: Ads target GOP state senators
abstract: Citizens Alliance of Pennsylvania has begun airing ads targeting GOP Sens. Pat Vance of Camp Hill and Gene Yaw of Williamsport. The conservative group paints the senators as liberals and accuses them of siding with "left-wing special-interest groups." Vance and Yaw believe the ads are tied to their views against school choice.

headline: Districts face tough choices with referendum changes
abstract: PA Act 1 of 2006 set an annual limit on tax hikes that school districts could enact without voter approval, but the act also included 10 exceptions districts could apply to the state for, and exceptions were rarely denied. PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget makes deep cuts to education, eliminates 7 of these exceptions and makes it easier for districts to control spending.

headline: Area collegians face less aid thanks to state’s budget cuts
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget proposal could mean trouble for schools and colleges. Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance program, a needs-based grant, will drop from a maximum of $3,541 to $3,056. The article lists how much money a number of Luzerne area schools will lose due to the budget cuts.

headline: Police investigate break-ins at two Perry County churches
abstract: There have been attempted burglaries at United Christian Church of Duncannon and God’s Missionary Church of Duncannon. The burglar could not get into the first church. The burglar got into the second church and was seen fleeing the scene by a witness.

headline: The real face of casino gambling in Pennsylvania
abstract: Former Jenkintown's mayor, Mike O'Neill, blew his life savings at the casinos after they opened in PA. He then became a tax collector, and blew about a quarter million of tax payers dollars gambling. He will spend about 2 years in jail for that offense. Casino's have already pumped about $4 billion into state coffers during the recession.

headline: Harrisburg city officials take on takeover bill sponsor, Rep. Grell
abstract: Officials from the City of Harrisburg discuss their view of the action being taken by the state government to resolve the city's financial crisis.

headline: Locals petition for Pa. to enact 'Caylee's Law'
abstract: An online petition called "Caylee's Law" has gone viral on many petition gathering websites online. The law seeks to make it a federal offense for a parent to neglect to notify the police of a child gone missing in a timely manner. It would also require a parent to report the death of a child to law enforcement within an hour after said child's death. PA State Representative Vereb is in support of such measures.

headline: It's reality check time for Corbett budget
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett said that he was proposing a "reality based budget." In order to live up to his campaign promise of no new taxes, he must make drastic cuts to public schools and universities. School boards will have to raise higher school property taxes to compensate.

headline: Carlisle police investigating attempted arson
abstract: A woman told police that someone threw a lit kerosene jug against her back door. The fire went out before there was any damage. Anyone with information should call the Carlisle police.

headline: Fayette County may help indigent defendants
abstract: Criminals in Fayette County may no longer need to pay for alternative sentencing programs because it is cheaper for the county to pay for it and thereby reduce jail time expenses to the county. It costs $48 a day to house an inmate, but only $14 a day to stay in the Intermediate Punishment Program. Sheriff Gary Brownfield thinks that anyone who has the county pay the fees should work for the local government in exchange.

headline: Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education to seek a 2.1 percent increase in state funding for 2012-13
abstract: The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education approved a state appropriation request of $421.4 million, a 2.1 percent increase, the smallest such request ever made by the system.  The State System will still need to raise tuition to cover a gap of at least $23 million.

headline: Pa. needs to go on a diet
abstract: PA ranks 19th among the most obese states in the country. The eighth annual "F as in Fat" report by the Trust for America's Health shows that 28.5 percent of Adults in PA are obese. Researchers have been able to identify a diabetes belt across the US, which includes many PA counties. With some success, PA has tried to stop obesity from starting in schools.

headline: February tax collections give mixed economic signals
abstract: PA Representative Bill Adolph said that state tax collections sent a mixed signal. He said that PA General Fund collections are 1.6 percent above estimates for the year to date. However, February collections are slightly below expected.

headline: Misconceptions linger about Gettysburg casino
abstract: Many anonymous letters sent to the Gaming Control Board show that there is a misinformation campaign going on. Some say that casino's should not be built on the battlefield. In truth, nothing is being built; the new casino would be placed within an already existing structure that has functioned as a resort for the last four decades.

headline: NY Senate fighting again, over lt. gov., chairs
abstract: The New York State Senate is now debating whether a lieutenant governor can break tie votes. Republicans now in power of the Senate have proposed to prevent Democratic Lieutenant Governor Robert Duffy form exercising what has long been a constitutional power. If the change passes, Democrats are prepared for a legal battle.

headline: AT&T takeover bid is bad for everyone
abstract: The proposed merger of AT&T and T-Mobile may result in higher prices and fewer options for consumers according to lawsuits filed by multiple state attorney generals. PA Attorney General Linda Kelly and six other AGs joined the lawsuit in a bipartisan effort to block the merger.

headline: Area school districts adjust to leaner times
abstract: School officials say that they are frustrated by the severe cuts in state subsidies to public education proposed in PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget. The Keystone Oaks District, which reduced its budget from $4.8 million to $4.5 million, has offered an early retirement plan to cope with the cuts.

headline: Budget fallout: Weed and Seed faces end of funding
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett proposed budget will cut funding from the Weed and Seed program. This is part of his effort to close the $4 billion funding gap. While a US Attorney in Pittsburgh, Corbett championed this program. PA Senator Robert Freeman said that the cuts would jeopardize works in progress.

headline: 2-4 inches of snow in the forecast for Harrisburg region
abstract: A winter weather advisory has been issued for the Harrisburg area, including Dauphin, Cumberland, Perry, York and Lebanon counties. Check the PA Department of Transportation's 511 site for travel advisories and view traffic cameras on PennLive.com. Rush hour traffic should prove challenging.

headline: Carlisle man flown to hospital after stabbing
abstract: Jamal Carter, 28, stabbed a 20 year old Carlisle man. The police responded to a possible domestic abuse incident and found the man bleeding on a stoop. Carter has been charged with aggravated assault, burglary, criminal trespass and simple assault. There is no bail for safety of the victim.

headline: School Reform Commission to get new chairman
abstract: The body that controls the Philadelphia School District will be getting new leadership.

headline: Ohio exploring idea of privatizing turnpike
abstract: Ohio may, unlike PA, lease its turnpike to a private operator. Ohio Governor John Kasich thinks that the idea could generate $3.2 billion for the state, $1 billion of which would go for highway, rail and harbor improvement projects. PA Governor Tom Corbett ruled this out in PA.

headline: Budget hurts, but gas drillers feel no pain
abstract: The author criticizes PA Governor Tom Corbett for cutting $1 billion from colleges and public schools, while not imposing a severance tax on natural gas. The governor is trying to govern without money by keeping his campaign promise of no new taxes.

headline: Praise given three newest grads of Dauphin County Drug Court
abstract: So far 23 men and women have graduated from the Dauphin County Drug Court. Programs like this have been springing up around the country. They allow offenders to try to reform without going to prison. Judge Richard A. Lewis said that completion of this course is milestone in their lives.

headline: State tuition voucher proposal on path fraught with questions
abstract: Charter schools were allowed by state law in 1997, and since then change has taken place. For example, tax credits for businesses contributing to scholarship funds largely for nonpublic school students have emerged. A bill sponsored by PA Representatives Jeffrey Piccola and Anthony Williams would allow poorly performing public schools to switch to other public or private schools, and receive taxpayer funded vouchers to pay their tuition. US Education Secretary Arne Duncan has strongly encouraged states to become more hospitable to charter schools.

headline: Turzai gains support for liquor privatization
abstract: House Majority Leader Mike Turzai is attracting support from the Senate for the plan to privatize the state's liquor system. GOP Sens. Pat Browne of Lehigh County and Bob Mensch of Montgomery County joined Turzai in the Lehigh Valley to speak in support of the plan. The legislators believe the PA Liquor Control Board should focus its efforts on control and enforcement of alcohol laws.

headline: PLCB reports record sales in 2010-11.
abstract: 2011 was a banner year for liquor sales in Pennsylvania. The PA Liquor Control Board reported a record $2 billion in sales. This report drew flak from the Commonwealth Foundation, a group supporting PA Governor Tom Corbett's attempts at selling the liquor licenses off.

headline: Lt. governor's office gets 75 percent bump
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is raising the allocation to the lieutenant Governor's office by 75 percent, from $490,000 to $867,000. Catherine Baker Knoll, former lieutenant governor under former PA Governor Ed Rendell, died in office in 2008. The office was filled by PA Representative Joe Scarnati. Then the office was in dormancy somewhat and the new funds are needed to "revamp operations," said Corbett.

headline: Pennsylvania should end the death penalty
abstract: One of PA Governor Ed Rendell's last actions in office was to urge the legislature to fix or repeal the death sentence. He thinks that the death penalty is a good deterrent to crime, but only when executions are brought out within a reasonable time after the crime is committed. He also thinks that the lengthy appeals process costs the taxpayers too much money.

headline: Corbett to hold open house at Governor's Residence
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett  and his wife, Susan, have announced that they plan to hold an open house at the Residence at 2035 N. Second St., Harrisburg. Lieutenant Jim Cawley will also be present. Security measures will be in place. No cameras, backpacks, or large totes or purses, and everything else will be subject to search.

headline: PhillyDeals: IBC establishing a nonprofit foundation to aid health-related programs
abstract: Independence Blue Cross is funding a new non-profit that will steer services to the poor and create incentives to innovate in the field of health care. The Independence foundation, to be headed by Independence Blue Cross executive Lorina Marshall-Blake will be funded initially with $10 million.  The health insurer says that the foundation will offer "roughly the same level of giving" as their yearly grants to various nursing-student programs.

headline: Despite budget, Cambria fears exist
abstract: The PA 2011-12 budget was on time this year. Cambria County Commissioners have fears that the new budget will negatively affect state mandated human services provided at the local level. Last year a cash crunch closed the county's Family Resource Center. A United Way executive that operates this facility said that the budget is only half of what it was last year.

headline: Jack Orie, brother of state senator, faces contempt charges
abstract: The brother of PA Senator Jane Orie will appear before Common Pleas Judge Jeffery A. Manning. He is held in contempt of the court for violating a court order not to talk about his sister's corruption trial. The US Secret Service will examine evidence that led to a mistrial in the corruption case.

headline: Pa. State Democratic Chairman Jim Burn calls on House Majority Leader Mike Turzai to step down
abstract: PA Democratic Committee Chairman Jim Burn is calling on House Majority Leader Mike Turzai to step down from his leadership post. Burn said that Turzai prevented debate during a Rules Committee meeting when Democrats made objections to some of the rules that Republicans wanted to make. One rule dealt with reducing the number of Democrats on each committee.

headline: Marcellus Shale gas rush prompts legislative battles
abstract: A Penn State professor recently held a webinar on the progress PA has made in regulating the natural gas industry, but he was disappointed by lawmakers not passing a severance tax. Somerset Conservation District Manager Len Lichvar also expressed his disappointment. He credited the PA Department of Environmental Protection for increasing drilling permit fees. PA Governor Tom Corbett is very opposed to new taxes.

headline: Corbett says education policy next on his agenda.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is setting his sights on improving education in the state.  Other agenda items such as transportation funding have been put on the shelf.  Corbett is also engaged in negotiations with the PA legislature regarding abortion clinics.

headline: Few in area clamor for Sunday hunting
abstract: The PA Game Commission's call for lawmakers to lift the ban on Sunday hunting appears to be drawing little local support, despite hunting's popularity in the Cambria-Somerset region. PA State Senator Wozniak said he is leaning towards lifting the ban. He thinks that some people's fear of overcrowding on this day is an overreaction.

headline: Governor's budget nixes WAMs
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has proposed a eliminating a number of line items from the budget. One measure would cutting legislators' discretionary spending. Proponents of WAMs say that these funds help jumpstart local projects, while opponents say that they are a waste of taxpayers money. PA Senator Richard Alloway thinks that this is fair because cuts should be spread out and no one should be spared.

headline: Middletown might not save as much as expected by turning communications center over to Dauphin County, officials say
abstract: Middletown has turned its communications center duties over to Dauphin County to save money, but borough council members say that this may not save as much as intended. The borough will need to pay out unemployment benefits to laid-off workers.

headline: Fallout felt from airlift of Haitian orphans
abstract: In the wake of the Haiti earthquake disaster, PA Governor Rendell and US Representative Jason Altmire led an airlift of 54 orphans to the US. One of them, Rocky, joined a family in Aspen, Colorado. Rendell has been unapologetic as some considered this gesture political grandstanding. It took nearly a year for the government of Haiti to agree to this plan.

headline: Concussion bill advances
abstract: A bill put forth by Sen. Pat Browne, R-Lehigh to regulate treatment and reporting requirements for student-athletes has passed both chambers of the PA legislature. The bill is in response to a rise in serious head injuries in the country. Among other things, the bill requires the state Departments of Health and Education to make information available regarding the risks of head injuries on their websites.

headline: State budget: Pain now to avoid disaster
abstract: PA State Representative Mirabito has called PA Governor Tom Corbett's non-tax-raising budget detrimental to human services and public education. PA State Representative Baker has called it one of the hardest budget to pass. The $27.2 billion budget represents a 3 percent cut from last year; the cuts are intended to offset the$4 billion budget deficit.

headline: Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission's bookstore to close, will sell online
abstract: The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission announced today that it is closing the PA State Bookstore in Harrisburg. One can still buy books online at www.PABookstore.com.

headline: Harsco plans to revitalize, add jobs in Harrisburg, Camp Hill
abstract: Industrial services and engineered products company Harsco Corporation said that it will restore its Harrisburg Steel operating site. This will create 20 new jobs. The company plans to invest more than $2 million dollars.

headline: Lifts fixed at county ski slopes near Pittsburgh
abstract: Over the weekend some skiers at Boyce Park in Pittsburgh were stranded in a ski lift, but the repair has been made. State regulators have inspected and repaired the lifts so they are safe for operation.

headline: Marcellus shale opportunities, taxes
abstract: The controversy surrounding the state's natural gas industry is discussed.

headline: State AG: More than 1,000 suspicious contests, lotteries in 2010
abstract: A spokesman for the PA Attorney General said that there were over 1000 reported cases of suspicious contests and lotteries. Many of the scams ask for fictitious taxes. Other schemes involve fooling the elderly, where a scammer calls someone elderly, posing as a grandchild to ask for a money wire to get bailed out of jail in a foreign country.

headline: Corbett's tough decisions could lead to rough time for education and taxpayers
abstract: The author feels that PA Governor Tom Corbett did not evenly "dole out the pain." He is doing a good job of not raising new taxes. Education and the environment took a big hits. The author does support privatization of liquor stores and derides former PA Governor Ed Rendell for making cuts to the Educational Improvement Tax Credit program.

headline: Harrisburg police searching for armed robbers
abstract: Three men held up a man walking near South 21st and Berryhill streets in Harrisburg PA. The 34-year-old man was held at gunpoint and he gave up his wallet. He returned home, cancelled his credit card, then called the police.

headline: New Laws Govern Guns, Web, Banks
abstract: A slew of new federal and local laws ring in the new year, dealing with topics from health care and finance to texting, guns and smoking. Some of the most far reaching laws include new taxes on drug makers and lower prescription costs to seniors. Some states adopted legislation to combat cyberbullying.

headline: DN Editorial: Concerns about Guv's privatization council
abstract: While PA Gov Tom Corbett explores privatizing various state enterprises, the Philadelphia Daily News wonders when the state will get stronger ethics laws. The paper points to the fact that the governor's privatization council is made up mostly of supporters to his campaign.

headline: Corbett to sign budget
abstract: The PA House and Senate are both Republican controlled. Some thought that the 2011-12 budget would be signed on time. However, the governor did not sign it and asked for a separate property tax bill. State universities across the state had to raise tuition in order to deal with the loss of millions in cuts.

headline: Corbett budget proposal slashes education funding, with program cuts and teacher layoffs likely
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett proposed cutting more than $1 billion in funding for public schools. This move could trigger tax increases, program cuts and teacher layoffs throughout the state. The shortfall in the Philadelphia School District could be greater than $600,000.

headline: The 'secret' tapes: The Patriot-News tells the 'real story' of the infamous House meeting on reform
abstract: This article details a heated argument in the PA House Rules Committee over reforming the legislature. Chairman Turzei blocks any attempts by Democrats to discuss the reform plans. He just wants to get through the roll call.

headline: Governor unveils Marcellus impact fee plan
abstract: In response to mounting protests, PA Governor Tom Corbett has announced a plan that would collect a fee from natural gas drillers that would compensate local areas for damage caused to the environment.

headline: Throop seeks ban on Marcellus waste as landfill cover
abstract: The Throop Borough Council has asked state regulators to stop allowing Keystone Sanitary Landfill to accept Marcellus Shale drilling waste, which has been happening since 2009. The PA Department of Environmental Protection has allowed this to happen, but Throop wants to provide the agency with environmental safety information that it believes would compel a ban on such dumpings.

headline: Lawmakers differ dramatically on budget proposal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's new budget includes many cuts to clear the deficit. PA Representative Jaret Gibbons said that the cuts were drastic and disproportionate. He also said that the tax burden would be passed back to local governments.

headline: Show you're a leader, Gov. Corbett
abstract: Former PA Attorney General and newly elected PA Governor Tom Corbett has made government reform his number one issue. About three years ago PA Representatives Rob Kauffman and Todd Rock proposed a piece of legislation that would reduce the size of the legislature, but it was quashed by the Speaker's Reform Commission.

headline: Orie's lawyer can avoid stand, stay on case, judge says
abstract: PA State Senator Orie's lawyer will be allowed to stay on the case for Orie's second corruption trial, an Allegheny County Common Pleas judge ruled. Prosecutors wanted to call the lawyer as a witness against Orie to ask him where he got forged documents, which he introduced as evidence in her first trial.

headline: Lackawanna and Luzerne would get little from Corbett drilling fee
abstract: Officials in Lackawanna and Luzerne Counties are upset that PA Gov Tom Corbett's plan to allow local government to collect fees from natural gas drillers only include those towns most acutely affected by the drilling. State Sen. John Yudichak, D-14, Nanticoke explained that NE PA roads are being worn down by the sharp increase in truck traffic.

headline: School funding as expected, or better
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget calls for over $1 billion in cuts to education. Many school officials are relieved that the cuts to their budgets are less than anticipated. Districts in Fayette and Westmoreland counties may need to raise taxes, cut positions and cut programs to make up for the loss in state funding.

headline: Fitzpatrick defends record on cuts
abstract: Heritage Action released data ranking votes on 21 amendments to US House Bill 1. Many of these amendments were cuts, and the Philadelphia delegation received lower percentages. US Congressmen Mike Fitzpatrick and Charlie Dent find fault with the data because they fail to account for votes on amendments that sought to shift spending proposed by US President Barack Obama.

headline: Search warrants called 'vague'
abstract: The Allegheny County Common Pleas Court judge who will preside over the trial of PA Senator Jane Orie has denied a motion to suppress evidence in the case. The Ories are charged with misusing the senator's legislative offices and staff to help another sister, state Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin, in her election campaign in 2009.

headline: Township opposes state regulation of drilling
abstract: Officials in Washington County are against state legislation that strips local townships, boroughs and cities of control over Marcellus Shale development. The PA House and Senate passed a bill that would set uniform standards on drilling regulation. If localities do not accept certain model ordinances, then they cannot share money from local impact fees. PA Governor Tom Corbett supports heightened state control.

headline: Two proposals seek to change how Pennsylvania allocates its electoral votes
abstract: Dueling plans that seek to change the way PA appropriates its electoral votes have been put forth by Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi and political heavyweights Tom Golisano and Fred Thompson.  Pileggi's plan would replace the current winner-take-all system with one that awards Electoral College votes by congressional district.  Golisano and Thompson propose to award PA's electoral votes to the  national popular vote winner.

headline: Pa. legislature remains stalwart against same-sex marriage
abstract: The New York legislature recently approved same-sex marriage. A spokesman from Equality Pennsylvania does not think that same-sex marriage will be legal in PA anytime soon. PA State Senator Metcalfe has introduced a bill that more firmly bans same-sex marriage. Many believe that the US Supreme Court will resolve the issue for all of the states.

headline: Rep. Brady brokered pols' agreement
abstract: Philadelphia Councilman Frank DiCicco was unsure whether he would win a fifth term. Mark Squilla wondered if he could win his spot. US Representative Bob Brady called the two together and brokered a deal. DiCicco will drop out and support Squilla. Also in the race is a man representing the Local 98 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers.

headline: Gaming chief: Wait to auction Foxwoods license
abstract: The head of the Pennsylvania Gaming Control board said that it would be unwise to auction off the revoked license of the Foxwoods Casino. The issue will be debated in court for years to come and may even see the PA Supreme Court. Others think that the license should be bid off because there simply is not demand enough for two casinos in Philadelphia.

headline: Corbett pushes ‘choice’ at taxpayer expense
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett pushes a bill that would allow the state to authorize taxpayer dollars to go to private schools.

headline: Corbett unveils Marcellus shale fee
abstract: In response to mounting protests, PA Governor Tom Corbett has announced a plan that would collect a fee from natural gas drillers that would compensate local areas for damage caused to the environment.

headline: Transportation Commission working toward suggestions
abstract: The Transportation Funding Advisory Commission is working to deal with a gap in funding and its effect on projects.

headline: State tests on river water find low amounts of radiation
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection said that tests of drinking water downstream from a Marcellus Shale drilling site showed no signs of dangerous levels of radioactivity. The president of the PA Independent Oil and Gas Association said that he is not surprised by the results. PA Representative Tim Murphy says that the DEP should take the lead on regulating the industry.

headline: PennDOT, State Police say complaint sparked Barbera probe
abstract: Gary Barbera's Chryslerland dealership in Northeast Philadelphia has been audited by the state police and the PA Department of Transportation. Both agencies received a customer complaint. The details of the audit cannot be released at the moment but a PennDOT spokesperson has said that the audit is not "random." Barbera is serving three years probation after pleading guilty in federal court to filing false tax returns.

headline: Lawmaker wants to end automatic COLAs for legislators
abstract: A Crawford County House member put forth a bill that would end automatic cost of living adjustments for legislators in the PA General Assembly.

headline: Dauphin County commissioners unveil solar farm
abstract: The Dauphin County commissioners unveiled a new 1-megawatt solar farm. The farm is on 5 acres of municipal-owned land in Middle Paxton and West Hanover townships.

headline: A last push to save the Tobacco Settlement Fund
abstract: With final state budget negotiations set to kick off next week, health care advocates are making one last pitch to save Pennsylvania’s $339 million dollar Tobacco Settlement Fund, which has been providing funding for medical research, health care programs and prescription drug plans since 2001.

headline: Ronald Tomalis' nomination as Pa. education secretary wins Senate panel approval
abstract: The Senate Education Committee voted unanimously for Ronald Tomalis to become the PA Education Secretary. He supports school choice but not the current legislation. He stated that PA Governor Tom Corbett would hold discussions on the legislation in the future.

headline: With crime nearby, Temple plans to hire more police & other security staff
abstract: Carl Bittenbender, executive director of Campus Safety Services at Temple University in Northern Philadelphia, said that new officers would be hired to patrol the campus. Temple is also hiring Philadelphia Police Department to increase patrols in neighborhoods adjacent to the campus. This comes after a number of on campus robberies.

headline: Texting while driving ban awaits governor’s signature
abstract: The legislation banning the practice of text messaging behind the wheel has passed both houses and awaits the governor's signature.

headline: State Rep. Vereb’s teen heart bill passes House unanimously
abstract: State Rep. Mike Vereb (R-150th of Montgomery County) is the sponsor of a bill passed by the state House that protects student athletes from sudden cardiac arrest.  Sudden cardiac arrest is the leading cause of death among young athletes.  The bill was passed unanimously and now heads to the Senate.

headline: Philadelphia City Council Pass Sick Leave And DROP Bills
abstract: Philadelphia city council passed a bill requiring employers to offer paid sick days, and reformed the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP).

headline: Governor’s new budget due today
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will unveil his budget today. PA Representative Gerald Mullery said that House Republicans voted House Bill 915 out of the Appropriations Committee. This reduces funding for basic education by $400 million. Senator Lisa Baker expects Corbett to stick to his campaign promise of no new taxes.

headline: Gov. Corbett: His arrival marks an era of fiscal restraint
abstract: During PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett's inaugural address, he invoked PA's need for fiscal discipline repeatedly. The low-key ceremony showed his commitment to austerity. He talked of his intentions to increase transparency, reform the legislature and provide a regulatory climate favorable for the growth of industry.

headline: Work begins on Harrisburg financial recovery plan
abstract: Repairing the finances of the City of Harrisburg in the wake of its recent state takeover take center stage in the region.

headline: Former Perzel aide testifies public, political work mixed.
abstract: William Tomaselli, former House Speaker John Perzel's "special projects coordinator" from 1998 to 2006

headline: Pa. Lawmakers Working To Preserve Federal Unemployment Benefits
abstract: With a deadline looming, state lawmakers are still trying to agree on legislation that would preserve federal unemployment benefits for thousands of Pennsylvanians.

headline: Pa. budget showdown: Waging middle-class warfare
abstract: The author states that he is not anti-corporate. He thinks, however, that PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget is using the deficit as a way to "further disempower" the middle class. He cites PA Governor Tom Ridges willingness to fund adultBasic. He also gets angry at Corbett for not taxing the gas industry. He talks about union's willingness to make concessions.

headline: Craver attorneys say Commonwealth can't prove homicide or torture, ask for dismissal of York County case
abstract: Nathaniel Craver, a 7-year-old boy from Caroll Township, is dead. His parents contend that they had nothing to do with the boys demise, and cite his tendency to self-mutilate as the cause of his death. There is no evidence linking the parents to the blunt force trauma that the child experienced. The Commonwealth Court has stated that the parents nonetheless did not take the time to get the child the help it needed.

headline: Corbett signs the state takeover bill
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has signed the bill passed by the legislature that authorizes the state to takeover the City of Harrisburg.  Harrisburg's finances were thrown into chaos after the purchase of a trash incinerator.

headline: Governor's approval ratings high, but protests continue
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is in the midst of an onslaught of protests against his approach in regulating the state's booming natural gas industry.  Overall, however, the governor enjoys strong approval ratings statewide.

headline: Pa. Senate Passes Juvenile Court Reforms In Response To ‘Kids For Cash’ Scandal
abstract: A package of reform bills resulting from the “Kids For Cash” scandal, in which juveniles were given harsh sentences and sent to private detention centers for profit, has passed the Pennsylvania Senate.

headline: Area lawmakers at odds over gas drilling
abstract: Former Governor of New York David Paterson signed into law a moratorium on gas drilling in his state. Lawmakers from New York sent US Representative Glenn Thompson a letter urging him to urge PA to hold discussions over the environmental impact of drilling. The US Environmental Protection Agency has shown concern about hydro-fracking.

headline: Court hearing on Harrisburg incinerator debt lawsuit delayed until March
abstract: A judge ordered a two-month delay that could alter the trial concerning the Harrisburg incinerator debt. The lawsuit comes from a city couple that wants to see the city pay the incinerator debt before paying any other bills, and they have the backing of county commissioners. City officials say that paying this debt could interfere with the city's status under the Act 47 distressed municipality process.

headline: Grell says takeover legislation will ensure public health and safety
abstract: PA Rep Glen Grell speaks about the impact of the legislation authorizing the takeover of the City of Harrisburg.

headline: Krancer: EPA is rushing bay cleanup regulations
abstract: State Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Michael Krancer says that the federal EPA is imposing costly regulations on the state and that it should verify the scientific validity of the models used to drive the decision to enact new regulations.

headline: Rick Santorum Joins Race For Republican Presidential Nomination
abstract: Former two-term US senator Rick Santorum began his campaign for the presidency in Somerset County, Pa.

headline: Wagner: Resume adultBasic funding
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner thinks that the state should resume funding adultBasic. He thinks that PA Governor Tom Corbett should return to getting money through a 1998 settlement with cigarette manufacturers. PA Governor Ed Rendell diverted this money toward purposes not included in the original 2001 law.

headline: Commentary: Tom Corbett to usher in striking changes as Pennsylvania's governor
abstract: The transition from former PA Governor Ed Rendell to PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett will be drastic. Rendell loved the spotlight, whereas Corbett is known to simply say "no comment." Rendell is known as a tax-and-spend liberal, while Corbett is for governmental downsizing. This change is happening in the face of a $5 billion deficit. Relations with unions will likely change drastically as well.

headline: Perzel says "we all crossed the line”
abstract: At a corruption trial Former House speaker John Perzel testified that "we all crossed the line” regarding improper campaign activities.

headline: DN Editorial: Dem Party courtship of judicial candidates a stickup?
abstract: The antics of the Philadelphia Democratic Party are used to support the case for merit selection of judges.  The paper uses the instance of Democratic Party treasurer Frank Oliver and Democratic Party chair Bob Brady inviting judges running for retention to a $10,000 breakfast in exchange for the party's support.

headline: $27.15 B Budget Sent to Corbett
abstract: The Pennsylvania state House approved the 2011-2012 budget with a little more than 24 hours to spare. Republicans are praising the spending plan for holding the line on taxes but democrats say the GOP decision to not tax shale gas extraction or use more of the budget surplus made the budget more painful than it needed to be.

headline: This state budget will be different: The work is all done
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget is unusual for three reasons. First, the details are heavily guarded. Second, his first budget should be taken seriously. PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget were usually just a step towards a final product. Third, balancing a budget with projected deficits around $4 billion without raising taxes will mean big cuts, perhaps the biggest that PA has ever seen.

headline: New round in gun law debate (video)
abstract: US Senator Frank Lautenberg intends on writing legislation that would prohibit the manufacture of high volume magazines for semiautomatic firearm. This comes after the attempted assassination of US Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords. The ban on such magazines expired in 2004 and many advocacy groups would like to see it reinstated.

headline: Corbett expected to sign bill fining minors not properly buckled up
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is expected to sign a road safety bill that will give police greater power to pull over and write tickets for minors improperly restrained in automobiles.

headline: Panel tackles casino grand jury report
abstract: The PA House will take up the overhaul of the state Gaming Control Board this week. The overhaul has been deemed necessary by a grand jury in Allegheny County. The grand jury found instances of conduct that put state casino licensing practices in a harsh light. A number of House members are putting forth bills that seek to establish standards for transparency and to help reduce corruption.

headline: Tentative Deals With 2 State Workers' Unions
abstract: The Corbett administration is emphasizing what the commonwealth will save if the tentative labor contract agreements with Pennsylvania’s two largest public worker unions are finalized. The deals are with the Pennsylvania chapters of the American Federation of State County and Municipal Employees and the Service Employees International Union.

headline: Massive cuts expected in Corbett's first budget
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will soon unveil his first state budget to the PA legislature. Corbett is expected to stick to his campaign promise by not raising any taxes. This will certainly translate into billions in cuts. The current budget it $28 billion, helped by $2.6 billion in federal stimulus dollars.

headline: As Corbett is sworn in, Republicans pledge to follow through on promises to cut state spending
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett was signed in recently and both houses are controlled by Republicans. Therefore many local legislators feel that Republicans have a mandate to make PA fiscally disciplined. Cutting spending and passing balanced, on-time budgets are at the top of the legislative list, Corbett said.
