headline: Pass the jobs plan: Washington must put Americans back to work
abstract: President Barack Obama will be visiting Pittsburgh today to talk about job creation. Results are unlikely, however, due to the efforts of the GOP to block any action that could improve the unemployment rate. Washington is urged to save the politics for a time when fewer families are suffering.

headline: Bill would impose new limits on teen drivers
abstract: A new teen safety bill could change what new drivers under the age of 18 are aloud to do. The bill would prohibit teen drivers to transport more than one other person under the age of 18 during the first 6 months of having a license. The new rule would not apply when an adult is present.

headline: Orie Gets Day in Different Court
abstract: Pennsylvania's high court says state senator Janie Orie of McCandless should be allowed to argue that a new trial on public corruption charges would constitute double jeopardy.

headline: Voucher plan worthy of legislative support
abstract: The author is concerned about education in PA and the future of the country. In 2002, the Philadelphia schools were taken over by the state and are now funded by state and local taxes. Under PA Governor Ed Rendell, spending on education increased 40 percent, but there was a decrease in results. She advocates Senate Bill 1, which provides for school vouchers to children in low-income families.

headline: Obama Courts Business Support
abstract: President Barack Obama has ordered government agencies to review hundreds of federal regulations to ensure that they are not hampering small business. This measure is intended to garner the support of employers and anticipate Republican attacks. The IUS Small Business Administration said that federal regulations cost small business an average of $10,585 a worker, compared with $7,755 an employee for large companies.

headline: Auditor General says state stores should stay in state hands
abstract: Auditor General Jack Wagner is not in favor of the PA House proposal to privatize liquor and wine sales. He thinks that the proposal is not in the best interest of PA. He also stated that the Liquor Control Board is one of the few profit making parts of state government.

headline: New restrictions for teen drivers
abstract: New driving legislation allow teen drivers under the age of 18 to have only one other passenger under the age of 18. It would also increase the hours of experience needed to get a learner's permit. The bill has passed the house and is awaiting Tom Corbett's signature.

headline: Think Tank Disputes Shale Jobs Numbers
abstract: Reports published by the Marcellus Shale Coalition and other pro shale industry groups in April touted the creation of 48,000 new jobs in Pennsylvania thanks to the growing shale industry, now, the left-leaning Keystone Research Group says the number is “vastly overstated.”

headline: State rep. pushes bill: Government has no business selling booze in Pa.
abstract: PA Representative Mike Turzai wants to put wholesale and retail sale of wines and spirits in the hands of the private sector. One proposal would auction 750 retail store licenses and would also auction the inventories of current state stores. The sale of the licenses would result in $2 billion to the state. Turzai wants to get rid of the "Emergency Tax" and work for a gallonage tax.

headline:
Governors sound inaugural note
Citizens Voice
abstract: Tom Corbett will soon be inaugurated as PA's 46th Governor. He will take an oath and give a speech. A common theme of past speeches has been restoring PA to its glory days as an economic powerhouse. The economy was a main part of Corbett's gubernatorial campaign.

headline: CCBC loses $500,000 from state, $250,000 from Cal U
abstract: The Republican-backed budget will cut about $500,000 in state funding to Community College of Beaver County. The cut equates to 2.5 percent of the college's operating budget. Legislators managed to restore some of the funding cut by PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget.

headline: Fraud is on Corbett's mind
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is concerned about false damage claims after the state was rocked by natural disaster. He says that the state needs to balance getting aid quickly to victims and protecting tax dollars from fraud.

headline: State Workers Protest
abstract: A few dozen state workers gathered outside of Governor Tom Corbett's Pittsburgh office to protest cuts too the Department of Public Welfare

headline: A Tax Cut May Carve Into the Budgets of 19 States
abstract: US President Obama's signing of federal tax cuts could have unintended consequences. A provision allowing businesses to deduct the full value of new equipment purchases from their taxes through 2011, along with the extending of (US President) Bush-era tax rates, will put more pressure on state budgets. States may be able to avoid some of the negative consequences by decoupling their state and federal tax laws.

headline: FBI: Powder no danger at Pa. federal building
abstract: A letter containing white powder inside a federal building in Philadelphia is not harmful. Police closed the street outside the building but no evacuations were needed. The letter was addressed to a name similar to a federal judge.

headline: Ackerman backers say she is being bypassed
abstract: PA Senator Williams blasted the state-run Philadelphia School Reform Commission for issuing directives to Superintendent Arlene Ackerman's staff without her consent. He said that he would work to abolish SRC. Williams believes that Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter is working to find a replacement for Ackerman.

headline: PA bill could break Harrisburg council-mayor stalemate
abstract: PA Representative Grell is upset the city of Harrisburg rejected a taxpayer funded economic plan. He is working on legislation that would allow PA Governor Tom Corbett to appoint a committee to fix the city's problems.

headline: Clinic Legislation Moves Forward
abstract: A bill changing the way Pennsylvania’s abortion clinics are regulated has cleared the Senate on a 38-12 vote. The legislation reclassifies abortion clinics as ambulatory surgical facilities, which supporters will provide stricter oversight.

headline: Chamber of Commerce
abstract: US Senator from PA Bob Casey thinks that the federal government is not doing enough for childhood learning programs. He is behind the Supporting State Systems of Early Learning Act, which would establish a an Early Learning Challenge Fund to help states to support low-income children under the age of 5. The PA Early Learning Investment Commission thinks this is a sound investment.

headline: Monday Morning Coffee: A Quick Fill Up.
abstract: The Farm Show begins this week in Harrisburg PA. There are tons of attractions like milkshakes and pulled pork sandwiches. You can even find alligator jerky.

headline: For motorists, cameras raise a red flag
abstract: The state may be looking to hand out more fines to generate transportation funding needs. The PA General Assembly may act upon recommendations made by PA Governor Tom Corbett's Transportation Funding Advisory Commission. The Federal Highway Administration says that red light cameras, which the commission may end up using, are used in more than 540 US communities.

headline: Bush praises Corbett, says he respects Obama
abstract: The PA Chamber of Business and Industry met in the Hershey lodge recently. Former US President George W. Bush praised PA Governor Tom Corbett for balancing the budget while not raising taxes. He said that he respects and supports Barack Obama. He did not endorse any candidates for the 2012 presidential election.

headline: Warrendale Gas Co. Bought by Exxon
abstract: ExxonMobil has bought regional natural gas drillers Philips Resources and TWP in a $1.7 billion deal.

headline: U.S. Chamber gives Pa. 'poor' rating for employment policies
abstract: The US Chamber of Commerce rated PA as one of the most burdensome states in the country for employers. The Chamber said that PA's biggest shortcomings are its high level of private sector union penetration, high number of employment related lawsuits and a prevailing wage requirement for state contracted work. PA Governor Tom Corbett is looking to sign right-to-work legislation, but the AFL-CIO is vowed to fight it.

headline: PSU student found dead in off-campus apartment
abstract: A Penn State University student has found a dead body inside of his off-campus apartment. The body of the unidentified 22-year old man was found after the student returned from holiday break. An autopsy is planned and the death does not seem suspicious, say investigators.

headline: Despite concerns, Barletta, Marino approve legislation
abstract: US Republican Congressmen Barletta and Marino have both voted in favor of debt ceiling deal approved Monday by the US House. The deal between US President Barack Obama and congressional leaders passed with 66 Republicans voting against it and Democrats splitting, 95-95. US Senator Toomey said that he would oppose the deal.

headline: Money will allow Delaware River-deepening project to continue
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett announced funding today for a Delaware River dredging project. The project must be completed so the Philadelphia ports can handle larger ships, stated Corbett. The dredging is also necessary to stay competitive with New York and Baltimore ports. The project will likely have environmental ramifications.

headline: Is Santorum’s Monday Announcement Key?
abstract: The importance of Rick Santorum's announcement of his Southwestern Pennsylvania presidential campaign is discussed.

headline: Wagner proposes restoring adultBasic with tobacco fund
abstract: Auditor General Jack Wagner has a plan to fix adultBasic. Wagner thinks that the program should return to its original funding source, the tobacco settlement fund. Wagner said that PA Governor Ed Rendell redirected $1.3 billion for health related causes to cover budget holes. PA Governor Tom Corbett discontinued the plan because it ran out of money, but he courted the federal government for help.

headline: Corbett Names Sec. Of State, Revenue Secretary.
abstract: PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett's transition teamed announced that Chester County Commissioner Carol Aichele will run the Department of State. George White has been named as the administration's chief information officer. These nominees are subject to Senate confirmation.

headline: Somerset County funding turning lanes into new business park
abstract: A state-mandated road improvement to Route 31 will cost Somerset County about $1.4 million. The PA Department of Transportation requires the upgrade as part of a high occupancy permit. County Commissioner Jim Marker said that this improvement will make the county "much more business friendly."

headline: FEMA centers helping flood victims
abstract: A Federal Emergency Management Administration official has said that already $5 million in assistance has been handed out to people affected by recent flooding. He stated that one can even get help for income tax relief.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: State representative Jennifer Mann has contested that the projected surplus should be spent restoring funding to programs who had theirs cut in passed budgets.

headline: Fox News halts contract with Santorum for now
abstract: Fox News suspended its contract with US Senator from PA Rick Santorum as he prepares for a possible presidential run. He recently spoke at the Conservative Political Action Conference.

headline: Penn Twp. is first here to go solar
abstract: Penn Township is the first township in Lancaster County to go solar, said a proud David Kratzer Jr.--a township manager. The project was funded mainly through federal stimulus money and rebates from PPL. The system is expected to produce more than 76,000 kilowatt-hours a year for the township buildings.

headline: Pennsylvania issues a measles warning
abstract: The PA Department of Health is urging anyone with measles-like symptoms who has not been fully vaccinated to contact their medical provider. Measles is approaching its highest levels in recent years in PA and the US.

headline: Mayor urges Harrisburg council to move forward before takeover
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson is calling on city counsel to move ahead on lingering financial issues. The city does not have money to pay its bills. There is threat that the state will take over the city after the council turn down a recovery plan created by state officials. Thompson spoke of the incompetency of certain councilmen.

headline: WHTM-ABC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  7PM News
abstract: State Representative Glen Grell supports an act that would limit the city of Harrisburg's ability to declare bankruptcy.

headline: Mistrial declared in Orie case
abstract: Judge Jeffrey A. Manning declared a mistrial in the corruption case against PA Senator Jane Orie after finding that her defense had submitted forged evidence. The Senator is accused of using state-paid staffers in campaigns for herself and her judge sister, state Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie.

headline: Council votes to purchase cruiser, protective gear
abstract: The Dallas Borough Council authorized the purchase of 10 Tasers, 10 power magazines, a dataport interface, 50 Taser air cartridges and 10 practice targets for the police department. A Borough Manager defended the expenditure citing old, worn equipment.

headline: Governor signs budget that hurts people
abstract: The speaker calls PA Governor Corbett someone who is either insane or someone who just hates people. She thinks his budget will hurt the poor and education. Corbett has signed a bill "that basically makes it OK to shoot anyone anywhere for self defense." He also signed a bill that extends happy hour.

headline: State Senate Democrats outline budget priorities
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senate Democrats announced their main budget priorities, outlining the direction they see state spending going. At a news conference in Philadelphia, the legislators proposed a tax on Marcellus Shale drillers that would enable restoration of cuts to education, among other measures.

headline: State surplus may be needed for flood recovery
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett says that the states $700 million state surplus will be used to help those affected by the recent flooding. Federal money only cover about half of the damage. Before the flooding he was urged by many to use the money to cover budget cuts.

headline: WHTM-ABC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM News
abstract: House majority leader Stan Saylor has said that there will not be a vote on natural gas drilling until at least fall 2011.

headline: ARENA PLAN UNVEILED
abstract: Mayor of Bethlehem Ed  Pawlowsk has unveiled a plan for a new Allentown Entertainment District. Pawlowski said that they will use a $300,000 PA Department of Transportation grant to develop a master plan. PA Senator Pat Browne and Representative Jennifer Mann spearheaded a plan to establish a special taxing district to fund the project.

headline: Water-main break near Washington, D.C., closes part of I-95
abstract: A water line break iced over a major commuter highway in one of Washington's Maryland suburbs. Cars where the break occurred were inundated with water and store fronts were shattered by the rushing water. Because of the break, thousands of customers on Central Avenue experienced low water pressure.

headline: When the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers isn't up to the job
abstract: The author criticizes Philadelphia Federation of Teachers for placing the interest of teachers above those of students.

headline: School vouchers bill hits snag in Senate
abstract: After many expected the Senate bill on school vouchers in Pennsylvania to pass fairly easy, a plan to give tax money to low income families who want to send their children to private school, Governor Corbett interceded forcing the Senate to wait until his administration fully backs the plan to vote. Republican leaders are looking for ways to remedy this situation as well as fend of detractors who say the bill costs too much.

headline: What kind of drilling fee would Corbett impose?
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett wants to impose an impact fee that would be used to cover road and bridge damage in counties hosting the natural gas industry.

headline: Anti-lien statute doesn't apply, court rules
abstract: A federal appeals court ruled that a federal law preventing Pennsylvania from placing liens against the properties of living Medicaid beneficiaries doesn't hinder the state from collecting medical costs from money that beneficiaries receive from lawsuits.

headline: Pa. bill targets human smuggling
abstract: PA Representative Rob Kauffman has joined other state lawmakers to introduce 14 bills dealing with illegal immigration. Kauffman thinks that "the feds" have shirked their responsibly. One bill would put a strict fine on smuggling humans. The American Civil Liberties Union has attacked some of the legislation as unconstitutional.

headline: Pennsylvania seeks federal help for people who need health insurance
abstract: More than 40,000 people in the adultBasic program are expected to lose their state-subsidized insurance in about a month. PA Governor Tom Corbett is therefore asking the federal government for looser rules detailing who can join the PA Fair Care program. Currently Fair Care requires new enrollees to have already been without coverage for at least six months.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  6PM NEWS
abstract: There is opposition to a bill that would restrict the city of Harrisburg's ability to declare bankruptcy.

headline: Ending the cruelty
abstract: A bill banning live pigeon and turkey shoots has been introduced in the Pennsylvania state House. Pennsylvania remains the final state that allows such actions, and Republicans and Democrats alike in the House and Senate look to work together to end the practice.

headline: Corbett proclamation impacts murder case
abstract: Statements made by PA Governor Tom Corbett and the news media could influence the trial of a woman who allegedly killed her children. Few people have not heard of the Coleman case, and her attorney is fearful that the jury will have to many preconceived notions.

headline: WTXF-FOX  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: null

headline: Casey pushes for testing of water sources
abstract: Marcellus Shale drilling has continued in PA. US Senator Bob Casey has called on state and federal environmental regulators to increase testing of public drinking water supplies for radioactive contamination. The PA Department of Environmental protection and the Pittsburgh Water and Sewer Authority said that they will take samples and report their findings.

headline: Are politicians 'bought'?
abstract: The author says that he is amazed when he hears people saying that large contributions from interest groups are attempts to "buy" candidates. This is because legislators have already made up their minds on how they will vote before they receive money.

headline: Christiana unveils voucher bill
abstract: Students from low-income families who attend poor-performing schools would qualify for vouchers to change districts for 2012-13 under legislation introduced by state Representative Jim Christiana.

headline:
Lawmaker asks colleague: What if I blew
your brains out?
abstract: Among the debates over the castle doctrine legislation that passed overwhelmingly in the Pennsylvania House expanding PA citizen's self-defense rights, two state Representatives exchanged some words that broke what some say was "reasoned civility." The argument involved a situation where a person felt threatened and used deadly force upon another.

headline: Harrisburg council votes against mayor's recovery plan again; Corbett says he'll sign takeover bill
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett said that he will sign any legislation allowing the state to take over Harrisburg. This comes after the city counsel refused two of the states economic recovery plans.

headline: Area’s delegation in Harrisburg divides on issues linked to Pa. budget
abstract: State officials from the Harrisburg area were divided along party lines on issues related to the state budget.

headline: $300 million goes uncollected from online retailers
abstract: The author stands up for small businesses that face competition from online retailers that escape sales taxes: Americans expect that tax laws are followed. It is fair that a company be held responsible for taxes, but what difference does it make if that service is online or offline, they ask? The technology is there in online commerce to collect taxes at the point of sale.

headline: Corbett: Plan for change upcoming
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has recently been sworn in as PA's 46th governor. He hopes to fulfill a few campaign promises, like reducing or eliminated legislators' "walking around money." He wants to also reduce legislative surplus and require documentation for the legislative per diem payments.

headline: WCAU-NBC  Philadelphia, PA  11PM News
abstract: The state Senate has approved a bill banning the use of drugs called bath salts, as well as types of synthetic marijuana.

headline: Conklin: District needs 2 offices
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Scott Conklin is asking for the state to build another district office, his third. Conklin represents a large area in central PA that features many different demographics, including college students and families. Another district office would act to lessen some constituent's driving distance as well as enabling staff and himself to address specific problems within the area with more precision.

headline: Gov. Corbett statement could impact trial
abstract: Tanisha Coleman is accused of starving her child to death. She wants an out of town trial because her attorney believes statements made by PA Governor Tom Corbett in the aftermath will negatively affect the jury.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM NEWS
abstract: The budget bill passed by the state Senate still features cuts to education.

headline: Senate panel OKs Pa. school-voucher bill
abstract: The Senate Education Committee voted in favor of a bill that would phase in a voucher program for low-income students over three years. The bill would also expand the Educational Improvement Tax Credit. Low-income families will be defined using federal guidelines. PA Governor Tom Corbett supports school choice, but has yet to endorse this legislation. The bill would also expand the Educational Improvement Tax Credit.

headline: Son of man charged with child rape faces similar charges
abstract: Robert D'Ginto Jr., 21, was charged Friday with four counts each of involuntary deviate sexual intercourse, aggravated indecent assault and indecent assault, and one count of simple assault. He has been sent to Lehigh County Prison on $1 million bail. He gave the victims drugs, cell phones, and cash for sex.

headline: Rep. Kanjorski to be honored for serving consumers
abstract: Former U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski is scheduled to receive an award from the Consumer Federation of America for his lifetime service to consumers.

headline:
Commentary: GOP's crowded field presents
a problem for President Obama in 2012
abstract: Pennsylvania's electoral college votes will most likely come with a little more difficult to President Obama in 2012 as compared to 2008. A crowded Republican field all vying for the presidency have become more popular to Pennsylvania citizens thanks to low approval ratings in the state for the President, according to Public Policy Polling.

headline: Corbett orders quick response for flood victims
abstract: PA Governor Corbett has ordered that those under him do all they can to help those affected by flooding. He is directing homeowners to file damages with their local governments. The state has applied for under water federal funding.

headline: WSEE-CBS  Erie, PA  Late Night News
abstract: The $27 billion state budget is expected to pass before the deadline.

headline: State considers teacher layoff bill
abstract: The PA General Assembly is considering bills that would permit schools to lay off teachers for economic reasons. This negotiating tool will help school districts deal with tough teachers unions. PA Representative Paul Clymer said that this will help schools to balance their budgets and control taxes.

headline: Governor Corbett Proclaims 'Pennsylvania School Choice Week'
abstract: In an address concerning school choice, PA Governor Tom Corbett said that this reform transcends ideology and political party affiliation. He said that research shows that giving kids and parents a choice boosts performance. National School Choice week is a collaborative effort by more than 150 organizations to raise awareness about educational choice and many other issues, among them being tax credit scholarships.

headline: PA House approves ban on 'bath salts,' fake pot.
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed a bill adding more synthetic drugs, including  Salvia Divinorum, Salvinorin A, Divinorin A, synthetic marijuana, and synthetic cocaine or heroin to the list of Schedule I controlled substances.

headline: Two Susquehanna Valley Locations In Running
abstract: The final casino license is being sought after by four different locations from across the state. One location is near Gettysburg, sparking debate about its proximity to the battlefields. The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board will meet in Harrisburg to announce the winner.

headline: Corbett updates flood impact in Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is urging PA citizens not to drive over bridges during high water events. "Don't drown, turn around" is his motto.

headline: Debate on gas drillers' impact fee put off
abstract: A debate over the details of a possible impact fee on natural gas drillers has been halted after Governor Tom Corbett threatened to veto and budget bill that included at tax on natural gas drillers.

headline: Causer to close state Megan's Law loopholes
abstract: The PA General Assembly has adopted many reforms to Megan's Law this week. Representative Martin Causer voted to fix the loopholes. Causer said that recent court cases have prompted the need to fix this problem.

headline: Analysis: Legislature takes the lead with reform agenda
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett relied heavily on his promise to change state governance during his election. However, some of his measures are unlikely to pass despite having a Republican majority in both houses. Corbett suggested replacing per-diems throughout state government with reimbursements for expenses backed up by receipts and making legislators pay for some of their healthcare costs.

headline: Casey brings sobering drug, violence news
abstract: U.S. Senator Robert Casey revealed that a report by the National Drug Intelligence Center indicates gang members in the greater Williamsport area are increasingly carrying armed weapons to peddle illegal drugs supplied through the Philadelphia market.

headline: Vote on school vouchers delayed pending changes
abstract: Expected approval by the Pennsylvania Senate of the school choice bill, a measure allowing for tax dollars to go towards a private school vouchers system, was halted because of proposed changes. Opponents of the measure in the Senate claim it is too costly while proponents argue parents should hold a choice in where they can afford to send their children.

headline: Corbett speaks to energy executives at Marcellus Shale conference
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is a strong supporter of the natural gas industry. The Marcellus Shale Coalition will host Corbett to speak to executives at a conference. He opposes an impact fee because he believes it will cost jobs.

headline: Gushers highlight potential of Pennsylvania's Marcellus Shale gas field
abstract: Two uncontrolled releases of natural gas in Susquehanna county have served to demonstrate the potential of gas drilling in PA.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: No way to run the government
abstract: PA US Congressmen Mike Fitzpatrick, Pat Meehan and Jim Gerlach all voted against cleaner air standards in the House. In another effort to cut spending, Republicans also tried to block the Environmental Protection Agency from limiting emissions of greenhouse gases from coal-fired power plants. The Democrat-led US Senate has taken a stand against these "ideologically driven cutbacks."

headline: Public's help doubles arrests by Berks sheriff's deputies
abstract: Sheriff Eric Weaknecht has made it his mission to catch a fugitive responsible for a 2005 homicide in Berks County. He shot his estranged wife after she exited the bank where she worked. Investigators believe that Torres is in the Dominican Republic. Weaknecht has been able to make more arrests because of money provided by the federal government for overtime.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM NEWS
abstract: Domestic Abuse Shelters are pleading for less of their funding to be cut, as it will be under the budget bill passed in the state House.

headline:
Hundreds of schoolchildren descend on Capitol
to push for passage of a school choice bill
abstract: A few hundred school-aged children descended upon the state Capitol to push legislators to pass a school choice bill. The measure would allow tax dollars to go towards a private school voucher system. Both the Governor and Lieutenant Governor urged the children to let their voices be heard as the legislation faces its toughest test in the House.

headline: Synthetic drug ban now in effect
abstract: Synthetic drugs, like bath salts, are now illegal to sell and distribute. A law banning the substances was signed by PA Governor Tom Corbett in June and it is now taking affect.

headline: Corbett's state bio tosses Waste Management job down the memory hole
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett's background as an attorney and spokesman for Waste Management Inc. has been left out of his official state bio.

headline: Act 47 panel rejects city's financial system proposal
abstract: The Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority ordered Pittsburgh to move forward with a comprehensive financial management system. Part of this includes a city-county partnership. Mayor of Pittsburgh Luke Ravenstahl was ordered to submit legislation authorizing this within 10 days. Part of the system is supposed to be funded with the proceeds from the sale of the Municipal Courts Building to the state.

headline: Corbett off to bad start (1/24/11)
abstract: The author already does not like PA Governor Tom Corbett because he had a lavish inauguration despite the state of the economy. The author wants to see a Governor like Chris Christie of New Jersey, who stood up to "out-of-touch" unions, and did not have an elaborate celebration.

headline: Kelly sworn in as AG
abstract: Linda Kelly took the oath of office for her position as Attorney General, after a unanimous Senate confirmation vote.

headline:
Pennsylvania House approves expansion of Castle
Doctrine related to lethal force in self-defense
abstract: Pennsylvania state House members approved a measure that expands a person's right to use lethal force in the situation of self-defense. The proposal would allow the use of lethal force outside of a person's home, if he or she feels their life is in danger.

headline: Corbett gives briefing on flooding
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett says that this is not a time to panic but a time to prepare. He reiterated how important it is not to drive when it rains so hard. The PA Emergency Management Agency is working hard to service people affected.

headline: No raises appear to be in the cards for management and non-union employees in Pa. state workforce
abstract: Non-union state workers and management employees will not likely see raises in 2012, along with state union workers.

headline: Corbett announces Delaware River Port
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has appointed himself and five others to the Delaware River Port Authority. This PA contingent also includes PA treasurer Robert McCord and PA auditor general Jack Wagner. The authority owns and operates four Philadelphia-area bridges and the PATCO high-speed rail line between the city and Camden, New Jersey.

headline: Traffic congestion costs region $3.3B in lost work hours
abstract: A study from the Texas Transportation Institute at Texas A&M University shows that when the economy improves, traffic congestion worsens. Philadelphia was ranked 7th of 35 in terms of congestion, where $3.3 billion in lost work hours result from congestion. Derrick Stokes, deputy director at the Transportation Management Association of Chester County, says that we need to be smarter commuters.

headline: Mobile phone companies back 814 'overlay' plan
abstract: Wireless phone companies back an alternative to a state Public Utility Commission plan that would have split the vast territory covered by the 814 area code in Pennsylvania into two area codes.

headline: Drug tests for welfare recipients worth a try
abstract: A new piece of legislation in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives aims to require drug testing for every welfare recipient within the state. Some question whether the issue can withstand PA Constitutional guidelines, while others contend that drug testing in the workplace is a regular occurrence, and should be in these instances as well.

headline: Military service of state police honored
abstract: null

headline: Greene County lawmaker wants his case heard in home county
abstract: State Representative Bill DeWeese wants to move his trial on theft charges from Harrisburg to Greene County, his home. DeWeese is accused of using state funds for his election campaign.

headline: State to offer plan to ease Middle Road traffic
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation will soon hold a meeting in Hanover Township to discuss the South Valley Parkway project. PA Senator John Yudichak and PA Representative Gerald Mullery said that they may attend. 80 percent of the project will be paid for by the federal government.

headline: Bellan named new Ross police chief
abstract: The County Commissioners said that Lieutenant Robert Bellan passed all of the Civil Service Commission tests, and so will become Ross's new police chief. Former police chief Ralph Freedman will retire February 1st.

headline: Fayette County to be site for new Army Reserve center
abstract: A new Army Reserve center will be built on 20-acres of land in Fayette County.

headline: Survey says professors' raises don't keep pace with inflation
abstract: Professors on college campuses will be receiving a pay raise which falls below the rate of inflation for the second consecutive year. In a survey produced by the American Association of University Professors, the recent recession played a roll in the pay discrepancies between the top earning professors and the others.

headline: Waters holds hearing on cemetery laws
abstract: PA Representative Waters held a hearing to discuss new regulations and oversight for cemeteries.

newspaper: WPGH Pittsburgh (Channel 11 News on FOX 53) FOX
headline: PGH-FOX  Pittsburgh, PA  10 PM News
abstract: null

headline: Orie denies dictating political work on the taxpayer dime
abstract: Jane Orie tried to refute 12 days of testimony in her corruption trial, explaining to an Allegheny County jury that she did not in fact order staffers to do campaign work on state time. Her attorney brought 61 character witnesses to comment on the integrity of Jane Orie.

headline: Plan would cover those on adultBasic
abstract: AdultBasic is expected to run out of money in about a month. PA Governor Tom Corbett has a plan for PA's 41,000 low-income adultBasic health insurance customers, which would shift these people over to the federally funded, state-run PA Fair Care program. Federal law would need to be changed to make this possible and so Corbett is asking US President Barack Obama for assistance.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  12PM NEWS
abstract: Funding will be restored for a counterdrug training center at Fort Indiantown Gap in the latest budget draft.

headline: An unhappy gas drilling coincidence
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett and a group of state lawmakers announced their plan to spend almost $48 million in state money to help boost the market for natural gas. Convincing local governments and businesses to change their vehicles to natural gas, and building natural gas fueling stations were among the details in the plan.

headline: Lawmaker reminds residents of home mortgage assistance
abstract: Representative Mark Cohen is urging affected residents to apply for financial relief after Hurricane Irene. The last PA budget slashed funding for the Emergency Homeowner's assistance fund, however, $96 million is available for a short period of time.

headline: Senate vote expected as Pennsylvania budget unfolds
abstract: The Senate is expected to vote today on a $27.15 billion state budget that does not restore any of the funding for commonwealth universities cut under Governor Tom Corbett's budget.

headline: Teen driving bill unveiled in state House
abstract: PA Representative Kathy will introduce another version of her teen driving bill. The legislation would expand training requirements before a teenager could take a test for his or her license. For instance, behind the wheel training would increase from 50 to 65 hours. Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety cited PA as a poor performing state when it comes to auto safety laws.

headline: West Philly High student to sit with Michelle Obama at State of the Union speech
abstract: Four members of the West Philly Hybrid X Team, which got national attention for performing exceptionally well in a fuel-efficiency contest were invited to see US President Barack Obama in the White House. One student forgot his ID and was not allowed. However, he later received another an invitation to see the White House to meet Michelle Obama and US Secretary of Education Arne Duncan.

headline: WHTM-ABC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  9AM News
abstract: The clip provides an unfavorable opinion regarding a pay raise for state officials amidst pay cuts for many commonwealth employees.

headline:
Substance abuse ban; ‘shutdown’ get
local votes
abstract: Several issues, ranging from school board matters to substance abuse issues were voted on by locally elected officials and federal officials from the area.

headline: Perzel statement expresses regret
abstract: Former House Speaker Perzel has pleaded guilty in his criminal trial as part of the Bonusgate corruption scandal. He wanted to spend millions of dollars to help GOP legislators get reelected.

headline: Retirement community group stirs political pot
abstract: Parents and supervisors of Earl Township and residents of Garden Spot Village retirement community are in disagreement over cuts to the local budget and the raising of taxes in the retirement community, specifically as it applies to lay-offs within the school district. There is also controversy surrounding the local political system

headline: Congressman: Spending problem more serious than thought
abstract: Freshman Congressman Lou Barletta did not realize the severity of Washington’s spending problem until spending hours trying to get representatives to agree on funding levels and making more than 700 amendments to a temporary spending bill.

headline: Former U.S. prosecutor to lead audit of sheriff's books
abstract: City Controller Alan Butkovitz has contracted Deloitte Financial Advisory Services to audit the Philadelphia Sheriff's Office. Former federal organized-crime prosecutor Louis Pichini, will head the forensic accounting team. After John Green resigned as Sherriff last year, former PA Governor Ed Rendell named Barbara Deeley as acting sheriff.

headline: Long, winding road
abstract: The article discusses the 1,000-mile jog around Pennsylvania being undertaken by Paul J. Mathison to raise awareness of the need for an honest legislative redistricting process in the wake of the 2010 census.

headline: Poll shows Pennsylvanians favor accountability standards for school vouchers
abstract: A poll of several hundred Pennsylvanians showed that a vast majority of them favor different forms of accountability standards for school vouchers and private schools. This polling happens on the heels of a new school choice bill making its way through the state Senate.

headline: Hornaman hosts seniors
abstract: State Representative Hornaman will host a senior fair at the Tom Ridge Environmental Center. Sixty vendors will attend, providing literature and advice to the elderly.

newspaper: WPGH Pittsburgh (Channel 11 News on FOX 53) FOX
headline: WPGH-FOX  Pittsburgh, PA  10 PM News
abstract: null

headline: Abolition of insurance stokes fears
abstract: State funding for the state’s AdultBasic program will soon run out leaving 42,000 low-income Pennsylvanians uninsured. Members of the Pennsylvania Health Access Network, a health advocacy organization, said members have organized a candlelight vigil outside the governor’s mansion in an effort to persuade Gov. Corbett to save program.

headline: Radical restructuring for 18 chronically failing Phila. Schools
abstract: Superintendent Arlene Ackerman said that the Philadelphia School District will make radical changes to 18 chronically failing schools. Ten schools will receive a cash injection of at least $1 million each and another eight will be given to charter organizations. This is made possible, despite the budget deficit, by a planning grant from the US Department of Education.

headline: DEP continues review of citations
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection is continues to review citations given to natural gas drillers in violation of regulations, amidst confusion regarding the issuing of violations notices being contingent upon approval of agency leaders.

headline: Pa. House passes 'Fair Share' act
abstract: The state House of Representatives has passed a bill that changes the process in which damages are awarded in civil lawsuits. Known as the Fair Share Act, it would require judgments to be made based on the degree of responsibility occurring in the civil suit. Opponents argue it would give less compensation to victims, while proponents contend it will increase competitiveness in PA's economy.

headline: Hurricane Irene's impact
abstract: Hurricane Irene has affected 29 counties in PA. Affected residents can seek financial assistance through the Federal Emergency Management Administration.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 11
abstract: Democratic congressmen are holding their opinion that natural gas drillers should pay a severance tax on natural gas.

headline: Commentary: Gov. Tom Corbett might fight more for natural gas drillers than against unions
abstract: Author comments on Governor Tom Corbett’s willingness to open Pennsylvania to natural gas drillers while refusing to back a tax on natural gas extraction.

headline: U.S. Steel posts 8th consecutive loss
abstract: U.S. Steel Corp. said that it lost $249 million in the final quarter of last year. That marks the 8th consecutive loss and the future does not look brighter. The losses, however, were not as big as previous quarters. The steel industry should benefit from a 5 to 10 percent increase in automotive production.

headline: Surcharge on gas drillers won't halt business in state
abstract: The author feels that PA Governor Tom Corbett's opposition to the severance tax on Marcellus Shale is specious, especially considering the budget crisis. The author thinks that the governor's position that imposing a tax will scare away business makes no sense, because PA is the only state with no tax. Where would the industry go where it would not be taxed, he asks?

headline: Greene County company gets clean energy grants
abstract: Two Pennsylvania state legislators announced over $90,000 in clean energy grants for several mine water treatment facilities. The Commonwealth Financing Authority awarded the grants, which will be used to install in-line turbines in the treatment plants.

headline: Sen. Orie Waives Preliminary Hearing
abstract: PA State Senator Jane Orie waived her preliminary hearing and went straight to trial. Orie has been charged with 16 counts of forgery, perjury and tampering or fabricating evidence. Judge Jeffery Manning declared a mistrial in the original case.

headline: Tort reform measure gains ground
abstract: The state House on Sunday advanced legislation that would change the way damages are awarded in civil lawsuits.

headline: Let's keep school voucher debate civil
abstract: The public debate over school vouchers in Pennsylvania has become vitriolic. Opponents of tuition vouchers have been compared to former Alabama governor and segregationist George Wallace, who stood in the schoolhouse door in 1963 opposing the civil rights movement. The author, who grew up in Alabama during the Civil Rights Movement finds the rhetoric from school voucher proponents extremely insulting.

headline: Flight plan: Now's the time to book Pittsburgh-to-Paris
abstract: Delta Air Line's nonstop trips between Paris and Pittsburgh International Airport will be under scrutiny by the carrier. This comes after the post-911 downsizing of air service in Pittsburgh. The non-stop flights to Europe were back with subsidies from the Allegheny Conference on Community Development, but now the same authority wants to see people buying tickets.

headline: Public enemy No. 1? Teachers deserve better, so do taxpayers
abstract: The author talks about the public opinion of school teachers over the years: We once looked up to teachers. They endure so much. Now they are the public enemy. James Testerman, head of the PA State Education Association, encouraged teachers to accept a one year pay freeze.

headline: Obama decides to engage in debt fight
abstract: President Obama will present his debt-reduction plan soon. The President is expected to solidify his stance that the wealthiest Americans cannot receive a tax break while turning Medicare into a private program, as the Republican plan suggests.

headline: Nutter Appoints Former Staffer Wendell Pritchett to SRC Seat
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter is moving quickly to fill the seats of the School Reform Commission. Nutter wants to appoint a former staffer. PA Governor Corbett’s nomination of Pedro Ramos is awaiting confirmation by the Pennsylvania state senate.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM NEWS
abstract: The debate over a potential fee for natural gas drillers could possibly impede a deal on passage of the state budget

headline: Be glad Pennsylvania doesn't sell pants and shirts
abstract: Author contends that the state’s stranglehold on the sale of alcohol is as absurd as having to buy clothing from state-run clothing stores.

headline: Pa. woman charged for conducting fake raffle to benefit family adoption fund
abstract: Lynette Karen Shedden, 41, of Canton has been charged with theft by deception as a third-degree felony. She set up a fake raffle to benefit a Columbia Cross Roads family's adoption fund. She never paid the family and kept the money for herself.

headline: Lay off the double standard
abstract: PA Senators, including Jeffrey Piccola, Mike Waugh and Lloyd Smucker, have introduced legislation designed to ease the burden of state mandates on districts. This comes after the financial squeeze that public schools will face became apparent in PA Governor Tom Corbett's budget. Currently districts cannot lay off a teacher because of financial difficulties.

headline: State may limit drilling byproduct from being spread on farms
abstract: Pennsylvania may limit the usage of sewage sludge as fertilizer on farms. After a recent New York Times article highlighted the possibility of radioactive material present in Marcellus Shale drilling wastewater, the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection is looking to regulate the transfer of sludge created from Marcellus waste from sewage plants.

headline: 3-On Your Side: FEMA Help For Hurricane Victims
abstract: Citizens from Philadelphia, Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, Northampton, and Lehigh counties are eligible for financial help from the Federal Emergency Management Agency. Residents can use the funding to purchase housing, home repairs, medical and dental services, clothing and other items and services.

headline: WBRE-NBC  Wilkes Barre-Scranton, PA  28 NEWS AT 6
abstract: A bill has been passed in the General Assembly that restricts the city of Harrisburg's ability to file for bankruptcy.

headline: Pennsylvanians didn't vote for dirtier air
abstract: The Authors comment on H.R. 1 which they claim threatens the health of Pennsylvania’s children, elderly citizens and other vulnerable populations by blocking the Environmental Protection Agency from enforcing the Clean Air Act and cleaning up dangerous carbon dioxide pollution from coal-fired power plants and oil refineries.

headline: Good Day at 6
abstract: Camden's police chief said that criminals would now have it easy despite the budget cuts to the department. The city is receiving help from the state police and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

headline: DeWeese pressing Corbett to reverse canceling prison
abstract: PA Representative Bill DeWeese is pleading PA Governor Tom Corbett to go back on his decision to cancel the construction of a state prison in German Township. As state attorney general Corbett filed charges against DeWeese for allegedly having employees do campaign work on state time. Deweese is looking into the PA Department of Corrections records concerning the cancelation.

headline:
School boards would need more votes
for tax hikes under Rafferty bill
abstract: A bill sponsored primarily by Pennsylvania state Senator John Rafferty requiring a two-thirds majority vote by a school board in order to raise property taxes has moved its way out of committee. The bill, which is one step closer to becoming a law, will replace the existing statute that only allows property taxes to be raised to a state-imposed index based on inflation.

headline: Former Pa. House Speaker Perzel Enters His Guilty Pleas
abstract: Former Pennsylvania  House speaker John Perzel could face up to 24 years in jail on his eight public corruption charges. He was at the center of a scheme to spend millions of taxpayer money on computer technology for the benefit of GOP political campaigns. Perzel is expected to forfeit his state pension.

headline: John Baer: Reforms in new state budget? Don't hold your breath
abstract: John Baer contests that there is a lack of government reform in the state budget.

headline: Coalition to lobby Harrisburg, seeking to spare Philly schools from funding cuts
abstract: The "Our Students, Our Philly, Our Future" coalition is hoping to protect funding for the Philadelphia School District which will face a $400 million shortfall by the end of the following year.

headline: Public servant warns youth of dangers of technology
abstract: Craig S. LeCadre, who works for the PA attorney general's office said at a public presentation titled "Cyberbullying: Sticks and Stones," that cyberbullying can be a greater threat than some may realize. With the advent of new technology, the insults and threats become instantaneous, more widespread, and semi-permanent.

headline: Health care leaders back lawsuit reform legislation
abstract: The Fair Share Act is currently being debated in the PA House. The bill seeks to reform tort law by making it so people who are only 1 percent liable cannot be held 100 percent liable for something. This is gaining support from business leaders and health care agencies, like the Wyoming Valley Health Care System. PA Governor Tom Corbett said he would sign the bill.

headline: Self-defense rights plan faces hurdle in state House
abstract: A bill expanding the "castle doctrine" in the state of Pennsylvania could be delayed for a few weeks while the House and Senate work out details. Instead of approving a Senate-passed version, the House decided to pass its very own version, which happened to be identical to that of the Senate's. The delay is not expected to change the final outcome, a signed law expanding self-defense rights to Pennsylvanians.

headline: Senator Casey pushes for improved protection of troops during visit to Pakistan
abstract: PA Senator Casey wants US soldiers to be better protected form roadside bombs in the Middle East. He will soon make his third trip to the region to meet with Pakistani officials. Casey is Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee on Near Eastern and South and Central Asian Affairs.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM NEWS
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett said that he would sign a Senate bill that would restrict the city of Harrisburg's ability to file for bankruptcy.

headline: Corbett names Powelson as PUC chairman.
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett named Commissioner Robert Powelson as the new chairman of Pennsylvania's Public Utility Commission. Powelson replaces former Chairman James Cawley, who had been appointed chairman by Democratic Gov. Ed Rendell in 2008.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will soon unveil a reform plan. One reform would require legislators to cover some of their own health care costs. The plan also calls for an online database that would allow taxpayers to search state spending. Another proposal would reduce legislators' "walking around money."

headline: Both sides in LCB debate state their case to senators
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett and the PA Liquor Control Board are fighting over whether to privatize or modernize. The one time sale of liquor licenses could mean $2 billion in revenue. Joe Conti, a former PA Senator and current executive director of the LCB, thinks that modernizing the LCB makes more sense.

headline: State legislative staff draws fire as easy way to cut
abstract: Pennsylvania's state legislator was ranked as second in total spending, while employing 1 out of every 11 state legislative workers in the entire United States, a study performed by the National Conference of State Legislatures concluded. With the state in an unsavory financial situation and with the increase in government corruption charges in the past few years, the PA legislator is looking like an entity that could be shrunk.

headline: Voter survey shows opposition to electoral college proposal
abstract: A poll conducted by Quinnipiac University shows that most Pennsylvanians are not on board with the proposal to change the way that PA allocates its electoral votes. Under the PA Senate's plan votes would be dolled out based which party won a congressional district. Eliminating the winner-takes-all model seems to be motivated along party lines.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: Steve Santarsiero asserts that there is a need for some type of payment by gas drillers to the government to be built into the state budget.

headline: Hospital infections still a problem in Pennsylvania
abstract: A drop in health care-associated infections across the state reflects a renewed focus among hospital officials and policymakers to identify causes of preventable infections and implement strategies to reduce them. Though 1.2 percent of patients admitted to PA hospitals contracted at least one infection during their stay, many health care associated infections are unavoidable, meaning a zero percent infection rate is not realistic.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett welcomed hundreds to the Governor's Residence in Harrisburg yesterday. He showed off his first floor office and said that he would be doing a lot of work there. He wants to put the finishing touches on his reform package which he is expected to detail soon.

headline: West Mifflin Area school district cuts 52 jobs
abstract: The West Mifflin Area school board recently approved cutting 52 jobs and several programs due to severe budget constraints. Before PA Governor Tom Corbett came into office, the district faced a #3.1 million deficit. His new budget would cut another $1.2 million.

headline: Redistricting Battle Under Way, With Lobbyists and Lawyers
abstract: With the redistricting process underway in all states and at the federal level, some elected officials are hiring their own lobbyists. With Republicans gaining a big victory in many state legislators, many believe new district maps will be heavily favored toward Republican interests, forcing Democrats to take up the fight to save their districts and jobs.

headline: House likely to look at changes for Harrisburg takeover
abstract: PA Representative Grell is in support of legislation that would allow for the state takeover of Harrisburg. There is provision in the PA constitution that states that an appointed board cannot do what elected officials are supposed to do. However, the board will be run through the governor's office. Harrisburg’s City Council has refused plans suggested by state advisors.

headline: Pa. Senate approves concussions legislation
abstract: Legislation that would impose new treatment and reporting requirements for student-athletes who suffer concussions is expected to get a hearing before a key state House committee.

headline: Orie's lawyer grills witness about politicking, immunity deal
abstract: Sen. Jane Orie's lawyer questioned the senator's former chief of staff, Jamie Pavlot, over what she told prosecutors about politicking in the office and the immunity deal she got in return. Orie is accused of using Pavlot and other employees to work on her campaigns as well as those of her sister, state Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin.

headline: WTAJ News at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett thinks that liquor sales should be taken out of the government's hands. The government should instead sell wholesale and retail licenses in an effort to solve budget woes. Union leaders think that too many state jobs would be lost this way.

headline: While rooting out corruption, city's inspector general recovered or saved $9.1 million in 2010
abstract: In 2005 the US Department of Defense sent Philadelphia nearly $3.4 million in city wage taxes covering federal employees who work in the city. Inspector General Amy Kurland discovered them. Kurland's office recovered $9.1 million in taxpayer money over the last year. She believes that they have shown that they can work independent of the District Attorney.

headline: Gas article hot topic at meeting in Tioga County
abstract: An article written in the New York Times related to spillage from the Marcellus Shale drilling process made its way into a Richmond Township (PA) supervisors meeting. The Times article stated natural gas wastewater had spread onto township roads and threatened to seep into the water supply. Concerned residents questioned the supervisor, Chuck Neal about the issue.

headline: President Obama visits Flight 93 National Memorial on 9/11
abstract: US President Barack Obama and more than four thousand people gathered at the Flight 93 National Memorial. Local members of US Congress Bill Shuster and Mark Critz, as well as former PA Governor Tom Ridge and current PA Governor Tom Corbett gave speeches.

headline: Happy faces over happy hour
abstract: The general assembly approved a bill that would allow bars to offer happy-hour specials up to four hours per day, not to exceed 14 hours per week. Current law limits happy hours to two hours per day.

headline: Wisconsin offers good example of why unions are needed
abstract: The author, a union employee for nearly 40 years, opines on the Wisconsin governor’s demands that unions relinquish their collective bargaining rights, and points to the positive working conditions brought about through collective bargaining over the years as a reason to support unions.

headline: DN Editorial: Why Philly should care about Camden
abstract: The author feels that Philadelphia should keep an eye on its struggling neighbor Camden. This comes after New Jersey Governor made cuts to the appropriation to this city, and a budget deficit that forced the mayor to cut services like police and fire. The author posits that Philadelphia's health relies on the health of the neighboring regions. A professor at Drexel University has proposed that Philadelphia and Camden merge municipal services to save money.

headline: Nutter's challenge makes Street's day
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter recently challenged T. Milton Street's eligibility to run for mayor  in the Democratic primary election. Street spent the 26 months in federal prison for not paying his taxes. Nutter claims that to run for mayor, one must be a resident of Philadelphia for the last three years. The prison was in another state. There is a list of other challenges in the city and in PA.

headline: Philly unwraps campaign against STDs
abstract: Mayor of Philadelphia Michael Nutter launched a new campaign against sexually transmitted diseases, the Freedom Condom. With HIV cases among teens in the city up 40 percent over the last three years, public health officials saw a need to jump-start a new effort against the diseases. With young people in mind, the city has planned over 100 distribution centers for the free condom.

headline: Charter school reform on PA legislature's agenda
abstract: The PA Senate Education Committee is considering legislation that would provide more oversight for the states charter and cyber schools. Senator Piccola wants to create a statewide committee that would analyze and regulate funding. The bill would also make it easier for schools to be converted into charter facilities.

headline: Nominee for Philadelphia school commission got high rate for district legal work
abstract: Until Governor Corbett nominated him to serve on the Philadelphia School Reform Commission last week, Pedro Ramos was billing $325 an hour as an outside attorney for the School District - one of the highest rates the district pays lawyers.

headline: Meehan addresses ConocoPhillips workers in Marcus Hook
abstract: U.S. Rep. Patrick Meehan met with ConocoPhillips employees to discuss new Environmental Protection Agency regulations that will require about 6 million businesses nationwide to follow permit requirements under the Clean Air Act. According to Meehan, the EPA has determined that greenhouse gases are pollutants and claims the new regulations will adversely affect local refineries.

headline: Housing and Safety
abstract: Williamsport Mayor Gabriel J. Campana says that the "local economic residential tax abatement" or LERTA is a comprehensive plan for housing. The plan is intended to encourage private development in the area of market-rate housing through a five-year tax exemption of real estate taxes and other abatements. 12 housing developers have expressed interest.

headline: State releases results under new way to calculate graduation rates
abstract: New graduation rates released by the state show that some schools graduate all of their students, while others graduate only 1 in 4. The figures are not final and are based on the four-year cohort graduation rate mandated by the federal government. PA Education Secretary Ronald Tomalis mentioned that improved methodology in collecting figures may account for changes in figures.

headline: Corbett wants to roll back pay increase for unionized state employees
abstract: The Corbett Administration is proposing a 4 percent pay cut and health benefit changes in a new contract being negotiated with the PA government's largest worker's union. In order to achieve significant cuts to the state budget, the Governor voiced his concern with the planned pay increase for unionized employees, especially since non-unionized employees are experiencing a pay freeze.

headline: Charges of partisan politics surround Electoral College reform proposal
abstract: State Republicans want to change how PA allocates its 20 Electoral votes. Delaware County Senator Daylin Leach says that the plan is not partisan, however many disagree. The plan would favor Republicans in the next presidential election, in light of the state control of congressional seats at the moment.

headline: WCAU-NBC  Philadelphia, PA  11PM News
abstract: State Representative Tim Hennessy has introduced a bill that would back background checks mandatory for hires by ambulance companies.

headline: Police Dept. needs better screening of recruits, more accountability for all officers
abstract:
The author comments on the news that the Philadelphia Police Department may be getting approval to hire a new class of recruits, despite having 13 of its members arrested and other currently under investigation of the FBI. The author suggests an increase in funding of the Police Advisory Commission, the agency enlisted to provide outside oversight of the police department.
?

headline: Middletown Borough Council OKs Penn State Harrisburg student liaison
abstract: Penn State Harrisburg student Marcellus Taylor has become Middletown Borough Council’s first college liaison. Many council members objected to the appointment, though. Some thought that it was unconstitutional. It was agreed, however, that the non-voting student liaison position is not prohibited by the state constitution.

headline: Lawsuit seeks adultBasic renewal
abstract: Several recipients of the adultBasic program want Commonwealth Court to order PA Governor Tom Corbett and the legislature to provide new funding for the program. They say that the Corbett administration is violating state law requiring the use of annual state payments from tobacco companies to maintain adultBasic. State Auditor General Jack Wagner thinks the funding should return.

headline: Corbett asked to rescind DEP policy on drilling violations
abstract: A group of 42 separate organizations sent a letter to Governor Corbett requesting he rescind the Department of Environment Protection's new provision requiring appointee-approval of all violations stemming from gas drilling. The organizations argued that requiring bureaucratic approval for all violations would create delays and put risk on natural resources, an overall inefficient way of running government.

headline: SRBC calls on Congress to restore funds for flood forecast system
abstract: The Susquehanna River Basin Commission is urging US Congress to restore funding to the Susquehanna Flood Forecast and Warning System. The commission and as well as the PA Department of Environmental Protection funded the program last year. Commission spokesmen think that this is jeopardizing resident's safety.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  5PM News
abstract: State Representative Daryl Metcalfe opposes a bill that would provide grants for attendance in state colleges to the children of illegal immigrants.

headline: Chamber takes MinSec concerns to governor
abstract: In a letter to Gov. Tom Corbett, the Greater Hazleton Chamber of Commerce expressed its concerns about MinSec Companies' community corrections facility in downtown Hazleton. Some of the concerns regarded residents and former residents of the facility that have been involved in a number of high-profile crimes in the area. According to the board chairman of the chamber, citizens are frightened by the knowledge of convicted criminals in the area and are concerned about their effect on local businesses. The facility’s location in the heart of downtown Hazleton was also discussed.

headline: Central Dauphin East twirler performs at Capital One Bowl
abstract: Sarah Milletics, a junior and a Central Dauphin East High School twirler, was selected to perform at the Capital One Bowl in Orlando, Florida. She has been a baton and ribbon twirler since the sixth grade. She and her squad will have to give up Christmas back home in order to perform.

headline: Jurors begin deliberations on Orie
abstract: PA Senator Jane Orie faces 10 charges of ordering state-paid staff to do political work on state time. Her older sister Janine Orie faces two charges of ordering the senator's staffers to do campaign chores for Melvin. If convicted of this felony, Orie could loose her pension.

headline: Casinos statement bill gains support
abstract: A bill in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives that would require casinos to send statements to individuals on their win-loss count is collecting momentum. The bill moved out of committee with a 14-11 vote. The bill is dubbed as a "consumer protection" issue, while opponents see no proof that these statements would actually curb gambling addiction.

headline: PA Turnpike Commission negotiating with union workers
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission has said that it is unlikely that the Teamsters union will strike as it did in 2004. That strike forced the turnpike to collect a flat toll fee from motorists for a week. If there is a walk out then the turnpike will use non-union workers.

headline: Legislator's bill proposes to fix a nonexistent problem
abstract: It is asserted that an proposed amendment to the Right-To-Know act that would hide the identity of 9-1-1 callers is unnecessary, as there does not seem to be any fear of dialing 9-1-1.

headline: Give up surplus, protect workers
abstract: Author is urging lawmakers to use the state’s operating surplus to fund the AdultBasic program, a health insurance plan for low income workers. The Corbett administration will be terminating the program, leaving nearly 500,000 workers uninsured.

headline: Morris announces primary run
abstract: County Commissioner Charles Morris announced that he will seek the Democratic nomination for county commissioner in the May 17 primary. If elected, Morris said, he will address gas well drilling and housing. He wants to strike a balance between the growth of the industry, job opportunities, and respect for the environment.

headline: Schools' success, failure online
abstract: The PA Department of Education recently released the findings of the Pennsylvania Value-Added Assessment System. This system looks at how students scored on PSSA tests and then compares how they score on future tests with how they should have scored on future tests. Some of the highest scoring schools did not receive distinction because they did not exceed expected results.

headline: Obama pushes energy policies at PA plant.
abstract: President Barack Obama paid a visit to Gamesa Technology Corporation in Fairless Hills, Pennsylvania, to campaign for energy policies. The plant which specializes in wind turbines used for power generation, employs 800 people. The President used this backdrop to accentuate his promise on energy independence within the nation.

headline: Everett wants to change regulations that promote flooding
abstract: PA Senator Everett is urging PA Governor Tom Corbett to establish a relief fund specifically for victims of natural disasters. Everett has met with at a joint hearing of the Senate and House Affairs and Emergency Preparedness committees. He has plans to the meet with the PA Department of Environmental Protection. Money could be drawn from the Johnson Flood Tax fund.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  10PM News
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett is expected to sign a bill widening the right to use deadly force inside one's home.

headline: Franklin County looking for jail warden; John Wetzel's state prison nomination headed to Senate
abstract: Franklin County Officials are looking for someone to fill John Wetzel’s position as jail warden. More than 30 people have applied for the position. A replacement is expected to be hired by April 1. Governor Tom Corbett nominated Wetzel to be secretary of the state prison system. The state Senate will hold hearings on all of Corbett’s cabinet nominees and vote on their confirmations in the upcoming weeks.

headline: Switch to Pro-Abortion Governor Allowed Abortionist Horror
abstract: PA boasts one of the strongest pro-life laws in the country. The editorialist argues that the transition from pro-life PA Governor Bob Casey Sr. to "pro-choice" PA Governor Tom Ridge set the stage for abortion violations to take place. Before Ridge took office, the PA Department of Health inspected Kermit Gosnell's abortion clinic, finding problems. But with Ridge the inspections stopped altogether, resulting in departmental deficiencies.

headline: Getting in through the back door
abstract:
Expansion of tax credit program for businesses that donate to private and parochial
schools known as 'back-door vouchers,' will play a key role in the debate over school choice in Pennsylvania. if school-choice backers get their way, the decade-old initiative formally known as the Educational Improvement Tax Credit will get a significant infusion of money. The funding hike is a key component of legislation that would allow low-income parents in failing school districts to use taxpayer-funded vouchers to send their children to the school of their choice.

headline: Agency unlikely to allow drilling
abstract: The state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has no immediate plans to lease state owned lands to be used for natural-gas drilling purposes. It is up to the state whether or not to lease public lands such as state parks for drilling, and although they chose not to at the Black Moshannon State Park, the land area around the park will most likely see drilling occur in the near future.

headline: Mortgage assistance a success in state
abstract: The Emergency Homeowners' Loan Program has had success in PA, according to state Senator Bob Casey. This is a $1 billion federal program to help homeowners avoid foreclosure. The Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency received $105 million under the federal program. About $9 million is used for advertising and administration.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  5PM News
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett is expected to sign a bill widening the right to use deadly force inside one's home.

headline: PennDOT accepting summer employment applications
abstract: PennDOT is accepting applications for 2011 summer employment for students. To qualify for the program, which runs from May through August, candidates must be full-time college students enrolled in any degree program and must be in good academic standing.

headline: Plant closing will have ripple effect
abstract: Fleetwood Folding Trailers will have a ripple effect on other businesses in the area. Somerset County Chamber of Commerce Executive Director Ron Aldom said that "anytime a company closes the loss of jobs has an impact on other businesses." Somerset County Commissioner Pamela Tokar-Ickes said that this will also have an impact on taxing bodies.

headline: Fatal crash on I-81 near Harrisburg puts spotlight on distracted driving
abstract: A five-vehicle chain reaction crash that killed one and injured three on Interstate 81 has brought attention to the deadly consequences of distracted driving. According to the U.S. Department of Transportation, nearly 5,500 people died and half a million were injured in 2009 in crashes caused by inattentive driving.

headline: DN Editorial: Happy Ramsey's staying, but we'll hold the halo
abstract: The head of the Philadelphia police force, Charles Ramsey, has decided to continue his work in Philadelphia instead of taking an offer from the city of Chicago for the same position. Ramsey received a $60,000 raise in order to continue his work.

headline: Poll: Voters don't favor electoral change
abstract: PA Republican legislators want to change how PA awards its 20 Electoral College votes. It currently is a winner-takes-all approach. The new plan would strip PA of its swing state status. A majority of citizens oppose the plan, according to a Quinnipiac University poll.

headline: Costa leaves pension board
abstract: State Senator Jay Costa has stepped down from the Public Employee Retirement Commission amidst allegations of financial improprieties related to the receipt of $25,000 by a law firm Costa is a shareholder in from city Controller Michael Lamb.

headline: Pennsylvania lawmakers renew push for gas-drilling tax
abstract: With a looming Pennsylvania budget deficit estimated at more than $4 billion, some local Democratic state lawmakers sought to inject renewed interest in taxing natural-gas drilling. Although a similar effort failed last year despite better political odds, Democrats hope the tax will gain favor as the Republican-controlled legislature considers budget cuts in an effort to preserve Gov. Corbett's pledge not to raise taxes. In a recent poll, 62 percent of Pennsylvanians said they supported a tax on natural gas drilling. Pennsylvania is the only one of the top 15 natural-gas-producing states that does not tax gas extraction.

headline: Bill would make vouchers available to low-income students
abstract: State Senators Anthony Williams, and Jeffrey Piccola will soon offer Senate Bill 1, their plan for school vouchers. They called it "the civil rights movement of the century." The bill calls for a new state agency, the Educational Choice Board. Public school districts could be hurt if the bill passes, as the cost of vouchers is still being determined.

headline: Rendell inspires grant backlash in Pa.
abstract: With a looming state deficit and a swelling debt load, Gov. Ed Rendell’s Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program is facing renewed scrutiny. Critics of the program, which shelled out $2 billion for building projects, compared the grants to earmarks. Gov. Corbett has frozen at least 50 applications of projects already in the pipeline and House Majority Leader Mike Turzai has vowed to block any bills proposing new grants. State Auditor Jack Wagner has launched an investigation into oversight of the funding for the projects.

headline: Ex-lawmaker LaGrotta set to plead in drug case.
abstract: Former state legislator Frank LaGrotta has been charged with altering prescriptions for an anti-anxiety drug. He is scheduled to enter a guilty or no contest plea. Mr. LaGrotta was still on probation for conflict of interest charges when the drug charges were filed.

headline: Pa. extends deadline for disaster-related food stamps
abstract: PA Department of Public Welfare officials have extended the deadline to apply for disaster-related food stamps. Originally applications were being processed at disaster recovery centers set up by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, but now the state can process them in district offices.

headline: Cordaro and Munchak found guilty
abstract: A federal jury found Lackawanna County Commissioner A.J. Munchak and former Commissioner Robert C. Cordaro guilty of taking and extorting bribes.

headline: New Kensington leaders make pitch for federal help
abstract:
Rep. Mark Critz, joined New Kensington Mayor Tom Guzzo and several business owners at Buffalo Bill's
Roadhouse for an informal discussion on the city's economic outlook. Critz, who serves on the House's small business committee,  wanted feedback on how the federal government can improve the economy. Mayor Tom Guzzo voiced his concern over possible cuts to the federal Community Development Block Grant
program, from which New Kensington annually receives several hundred thousand dollars that are used toward
