redevelopment efforts. Critz promised do his best to represent the needs of the city and the region.

headline: Helsel facing life in jail
abstract: David Allen Helsel was convicted 10 years ago of two child rape charges. He now faces life in jail after a Blair County jury convicted him of a third sexual offense. The last incident happened behind the Prospect Park baseball field.

headline: Gaming investigations topic of hearing
abstract: The House Gaming Oversight Committee is holding a public hearing today on legislation to transfer the Bureau of Investigations and Enforcement to the state attorney general's office. A group of Republican lawmakers have sought to transfer power from the BIE since the height of the controversy in 2008-2009 surrounding the since-dropped perjury case against Dunmore businessman Louis A. DeNaples, the builder of Mount Airy Casino Resort in Monroe County.

headline: Corbett: What did you expect?
abstract: Some Pennsylvanians show frustration and anger at the Governor's office to expected cuts his budget will place on education and the library system. While Governor Corbett cuts from education, his opponents say, he refuses to tax the drilling companies that are tapping into the Marcellus Shale. Although cuts were inevitable, the Governor's naysayers issue a warning about the drastic effects it could have on the education system in the future.

headline: People with guns kill: And states should decide who gets to own a gun
abstract: The National Rifle Association is backing US HR 822, the National Right to Carry Reciprocity Act. This act would force states like PA to follow other states' permit to carry concealed gun laws, even if those laws are more lax. US Congressmen Bob Casey and Pat Toomey will likely back the bill.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM NEWS
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett is expected to sign a bill widening the right to use deadly force inside one's home.

headline: Nonprofit groups criticize proposed city billboard restrictions
abstract: A host of nonprofit groups criticized proposed legislation that would change the “dwell time” of ads on electronic billboards from 6 seconds to 60 seconds. During a public hearing before the city planning commission, speakers whose organizations benefit from the free advertising said the change would severely affect the ability of Lamar Advertising to offer free space to nonprofits and other groups that use the billboards to promote awareness, raise money and even track down criminals.

headline: MCA approves hiring freeze, with additional cuts expected
abstract: Mount Carmel school district has done some belt-tightening, due to increased spending and less revenue. The school board voted unanimously to implement a hiring freeze. The school had to deny a request made by a coach to attend a clinic, but the board member later came out and made a donation so the coach could attend.

headline: Dauphin County Chief Clerk Chad Saylor takes job with Lieutenant Governor Cawley
abstract: Dauphin County Chief Clerk Chad Saylor is leaving his post to become deputy chief of staff and communications director for newly seated Lt. Gov. Jim Cawley.

headline: Seven House GOP bills tout natural gas
abstract: Republican state lawmakers revealed their bill package that would work to encourage businesses, transportation organizations, and others to buy natural gas to power their systems. The measure would offer almost $50 million in tax credits, loans and grants to help pay for the cost of new natural gas engines and fueling stations to these certain businesses.

headline: EPA asked to improve air standards at Marcellus Shale wells
abstract: The US Environmental Protection Agency held a public hearing about Marcellus Shale in the Lawrence Convention Center. Outside demonstrators urged for swift environmental protections, including water and emissions standards. One person living near the a production site testified, talking of the negative affects the industry has had on her community.

headline: WPMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  10PM News
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has set the spending limit for any budget to be considered at $27.3 billion, requiring controversial cuts to public education and welfare.

headline: State government moves toward more openness
abstract: The state House recently passed legislation to create a website publishing revenues and expenses of various state agencies.

headline: Diocese plans to keep schools open, raise tuition
abstract: The Diocese of Scranton is pushing to stabilize its school system. In order to avoid further school closings, the diocese is looking to increase tuition, emphasize advertising, and loud Catholic values. The schools' retention rate is very high (94 percent), but enrollment has steadily declined over the years (now at 74 percent).

headline: Reading turns to iPads to cut costs
abstract: In an effort to save costs, members of Reading's city government will begin using iPads to view agendas and documents at their meetings, instead of reading printed copies, which cost the distressed municipality $700 annually to print.

headline: Firms get praise for women on boards
abstract: State Treasurer Rob McCord recognized five public companies in Pittsburgh for their women representation in the boardroom. Studies have shown companies with women on their board of directors have yielded higher returns to their shareholders, compelling the Treasury Department to recognize those companies who did just that.

headline: Bush: No misgivings about banking bailout
abstract: Former US President George W. Bush has stated that he regrets nothing about the $700 billion bailout to the banking industry in 2008. He thinks it saved the country from another depression, he said at a PA Chamber of Business and Industry annual dinner. Bush lost the PA to US Senator John Kerry during his 2004 reelection campaign.

headline: Limit gas fee talks to drilling communities
abstract: The state Legislature is preparing to debate the particulars of a gas impact fee on companies that have begun operating in Pennsylvania to take advantage of the state's Marcellus Shale gas deposits.

headline: Casino license vote won't likely come this month
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board won’t likely award the state’s last casino license at its meeting. The board, which first planned to make a decision by early January, was gridlocked. Four sites are vying for the license, which allows up to 600 slots and 50 table games

headline: Pennsylvania should proceed with caution when it comes to privatizing its infrastructure
abstract: Local governments across the state are cash strapped and the state needs to fix its infrastructure. Many have considered the benefits of public-private partnerships. PA needs to address transportation but still keep the public interest in mind. Pittsburgh's City Council rejected a proposal to privatize the city's parking system.

headline: PennDOT reduces road speeds to 45 mph due to icy conditions
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has reduced speeds to 45 mph on several roads in the mid-state due to icy conditions this morning. If you plan on traveling despite the weather, PennDOT recommends that you bring emergency food, water, blanket, small shovel and warm clothes.

headline: Blue Dog Democrats less blue than after November's election
abstract: The once-forgotten sect of the Democratic party in Washington, the Blue Dogs, best known for their pro-business approach to policy, have reemerged as critical players in Washington politics. With a divided Washington and with their party as the minority in the House, the Blue Dogs have been able to yield more influence because of their moderate approach to what some say is a radical legislature.

headline: Natural gas impact fee in works
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett and PA Senator Joe Scarnati are working to complete an impact fee on natural gas drilling. Scarnati mentioned that environmental safety standards for protecting water supplies are included. A spokeswoman for the Marcellus Shale Coalition said that an impact fee must be competitive.

headline: Corbett: Budget will pass if spending holds
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett re-affirmed his assertion that the congressional budget will pass if his cuts are sustained and no fees are placed on gas drillers.

headline: Proposal made to save state health program
abstract:
Senate Democrats offered a plan they say would save the adultBasic
health insurance program for the working poor by asking the state, insurers and those covered to contribute. The plan will require $25 million from the state and ask insurers to contribute $25 million. According to the Democrats, premiums would go up an unspecified amount-enough to produce $4 million. A plan set up by Republican Gov. Tom Corbett before he took office arranged for insurers to provide the adultBasic recipients with the Special Care program, which will cost $80 to $190 per month and involves no tax dollars. Democrats say Corbett’s plan not only costs more, but also reduces coverage.

headline: Legislature takes steps toward Corbett reform plan
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett spent his first day in office and met with senior staff to discuss PA's problems. In an address to a joint session of the General Assembly, Corbett will discuss "walking around money." He wants to establish a searchable online database for all legislative spending, which is something he advanced during his campaign.

headline: Maria Donatucci wins special election
abstract: Maria Donatucci, widow of former PA Representative Robert Donatucci, won a special election to end her late husbands term. If voters approve of her service, she will run for another term in 2012, she said. Donatucci died six days after being elected.

headline:
State legislators fail to select chairman
for reapportionment
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislative Reapportionment Commission was unable to come to a consensus on the fifth and final member of their Commission by the given deadline. The fifth member, who serves as the chairman, must not be employed by a government agency or entity. It is now up to the state Supreme Court to choose the fifth member.

headline: First GOP trial opens in PA corruption scandal.
abstract: Former Republican PA Speaker of the House Perzel, along with former Representative Preski and various legislative aids, are guilty of using millions of taxpayer money to buy massive computer databases of information about state voters. Judge Richard Lewis thinks the trial will last about two weeks.

headline: Westerly winds blow pollution into New Jersey
abstract: New Jersey is pushing Pennsylvania and it's energy suppliers to work harder to enforce emission standards in Philadelphia in response to the pollution blown into southern New Jersey.

headline: State Rep. Martin Causer appointed to House Appropriations Committee
abstract: State Rep. Martin Causer has been appointed to House Appropriations Committee, giving the lawmaker greater standing in the development of the state budget. As a member of the committee, Causer will participate in a series of hearings with officials from every major state agency and department in order to determine their budgetary needs.

headline: MCCC holds college affordability program for families
abstract: Montgomery County Community College is hosting a free financial-information program, "Making College Affordable." PA Treasurer Rob McCord will help facilitate the event, and offer "tax-smart ways to invest in those you love." There will also be a discussion of the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) and financial aid process.

headline: Obama coming to State College
abstract: US President Barack Obama will soon visit Penn State main campus to talk about future investments in research and development. He will talk about green and clean energy. The US Department of Energy will make this part of PA an Energy Innovation Hub. US Representative from PA Glenn Thompson welcomed the president, stating that he agrees with some of his views on the new energy economy.

headline: UPJ students protest funding cuts
abstract: Students from the University of Pittsburgh-Johnstown met with lawmakers in Harrisburg to discuss Governor Corbett's proposed cut to higher education funding. The cuts would hurt state related institutes like UPJ, and the students met with their legislators to make their concerns heard. The event was organized by University administrators and student-government leaders.

headline: Put assistance on the fast track
abstract: Hurricane Irene and Tropical Storm Lee have ravaged 29 counties in PA. Five Senators from Delaware County, including Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, have crafted seven pieces of legislation aimed at providing financial assistance to certain storm victims, including tax breaks. PA Senator Wozniak thinks funds should be drawn from the Johnson Flood Tax.

headline: WCAU-NBC  Philadelphia, PA  Live @ Issue
abstract: State representative Jim Roebuck lends his opinions on the state budget debate, specifically its effect on education services for people with Autism and other disabilities.

headline: Congress' attack on music
abstract: The author is opposed to Congress’ proposal to eliminate funding for public media and suggests cuts to funding would deal a blow to American arts and culture.

headline: 70,000 empty seats in Philadelphia School District classrooms
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is looking at a $430 million budget shortfall. The fact that the number of empty seats in classrooms is greater than thought adds to this dilemma. The district has already begun to consolidate schools, close some of the its 284 schools and offer space to charter schools. Superintendent Arlene C. Ackerman ordered staff to immediately restrict non-urgent spending.

headline: Scranton police unveil new crime-fighting software
abstract: Scranton police have used a new piece of technology to deputize all the city's residents. The new crime-mapping system involves tracking and an anonymous tip tool. The system will allow citizens to look at crimes in terms of location, nature and time as far back as 2003.

headline: Monroe County's hopes for a senator face gauntlet
abstract: A redistricting committee has yet to decide whether to grant Monroe County its own senate seat based on the growing population there. The four-member redistricting committee has yet to find the fifth and final member, one who is not working under a government entity, and until they do so, are unable to grant the county its very own seat.

headline: Curriculum revised to meet demand in shale industry
abstract: According to the Department of Community and Economic Development, 23,000 new jobs have been created by the Marcellus Shale gas drilling industry. Nine career and technical education centers in PA have revised their curriculum to accommodate the demand of drilling professionals, according to the PA School Boards Association.

headline: Benefit extension important
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett signed compromise legislation that will allow 45,000 residents to continue to receive 13 weeks of extended unemployment benefits up to a total of 86 weeks.

headline: Customer disservice: The PWSA should have pursued an investigation
abstract: After executive director Michael Kenney resigned in December in the midst of what was supposed to be a review of an authority contract with a private vendor and his involvement in the matter, the Pittsburgh Water and Sewer Authority failed to address concerns about the matter in a report that contained only recommendations for new ethics guidelines. Councilman Bill Peduto and Councilman Doug Shields have asked the state attorney general to look into the warranty line program. Peduto’s original demand for the release of all investigative materials related to the contract was rebuffed.

headline: Police seek help in finding missing western NY man
abstract: A 74 year old man from Olean, New York, has disappeared. The man is suffering from the early stages of Alzheimer's disease. Frederic Seamans was last seen leaving a local business driving a 2010 Dodge Dakota.

headline: Saylor bill would dedicate part of Route 462 to honor Korean War vets
abstract: The state House of Representatives successfully passed a bill that would designate a section of roadway in York County as the "Korean War Veterans Memorial Highway." Rep. Stan Saylor moved the bill to change to public's perception of what some call the "forgotten war." The bill now moves to the Senate.

headline: Judges merit selection bill worth a look
abstract: PA State legislators have introduced legislation that calls for merit based selection for PA appellate court judges. The legislation creates a 15-member, citizen-based Appellate Court Nominating Commission. Voters would decide every 10 years whether the judge should stay on the bench.

headline: Evaluating teachers more complicated than yes or no
abstract: The author lends his support to Education Secretary Ron Tomalis's assertion that the states evaluation system for teachers is ineffective, given that they are not useful in displaying what is actually achieve in classrooms.

headline: City and state team up for shipbuilding projects at the Navy Yard
abstract: The Commonwealth and Aker Philadelphia Shipyard Inc. plan to construct two oil tankers at the Navy Yard over the next two years, with the state investing $42 million for the existing capital assets of the Aker Philadelphia Shipyard. The city has agreed to temporarily defer $8 million in tax settlement payments due from APSI, which purchased the Shipyard's assets over the last decade. The project is expected to create 1,000 jobs.

headline: Backing change in GOP
abstract: Rob Gleason, a Johnstown businessman that heads the Pennsylvania and Cambria County GOP, wants to see a change of leadership within the Republican party. He is dissatisfied with the leadership of Michael Steele and supports Reince Priebus of Wisconsin for the next leader of the Republican Nation Committee. Gleason is already looking towards the next US Senate and US Presidential races.

headline: Failure in the air: The state could be doing more to curb tobacco use
abstract: PA was one of 40 states slammed by the American Lung Association last week for failing to adequately fund tobacco prevention programs. PA was singled out for failing to tax smokeless tobacco products. Before the budget cuts the programs aimed at curbing smoking seemed to be working, according to the PA Health Department. The association thinks that PA legislators can do more.

headline: Pennsylvania drivers could be taxes on miles traveled, not gas usage
abstract: State Representative Rick Geist revealed a proposal to study a potential vehicle mileage tax. Currently, gas taxes are collected by the amount of gas bought, but with the emergence of more fuel efficient cars, many lawmakers are afraid revenue will decrease dramatically.

headline: Spin overtaking facts in Marcellus Shale debate.
abstract: Scientists say that advocates on both sides of the Marcellus Shale issue spinning every shred of research to fit their views. Marcellus Shale advocates claim that drilling never presents a problem, while the other side is certain that every well drilled will result in environmental catastrophe. Both sides are quoting a Duke University study that tells a mixed story.

headline: Two Democratic state Senators talk state budget
abstract: State Senator Jay Costa and Senator Rich Kasunic recently outlined the caucus solution for combating all of the budget cuts Governor Tom Corbett is proposing.

headline: Newspapers sue for records in abortion case
abstract: A group of Pennsylvania newspapers has asked the state Supreme Court to allow the public access to court records in a case concerning a minor's right to have an abortion. Records in the case are sealed under a provision of the state Abortion Control Act intended to provide privacy for those who seek permission to have an abortion under the law. The newspapers argue the Supreme Court's decision on whether a lower court should have more closely examined the basis for the county judge's decision when the judge denied the minor’s request to have an abortion, will be a matter of importance to the public and the public is entitled to know the legal reasoning behind it.

headline: Gas Drilling Company Hiring PA Workers
abstract: One gas company in the Wilkes-Barre area wants to hire more local workers to replace its original workforce from Texas. The company, Pumpco, says that they have about 30 positions to fill. Pumpco is looking for drivers, equipment operators and mechanics.

headline: Harrisburg police capture Steelton fatal-shooting suspect
abstract: Steelton Mayor Thomas Acri has said that Kermit Pittman, 18, has been arrested for the murder of the owner of Gino's Mini-Market in Steelton. Surveillance and physical evidence show that Pittman is the gunman. Pittman is awaiting arraignment Tuesday night in Dauphin County Night Court on charges of homicide, robbery, two counts of aggravated assault and reckless endangerment.

headline:
Harborcreek Township becomes Six Mile
Creek Park's owner
abstract: Harborcreek Township has just acquired the deed of the 450-acre Six Mile Creek Park from the Erie County government. The process took almost two years, culminating in the state legislature's approval.

headline: State approves new loan for arena project
abstract: The Allentown Commercial and Industrial Development Authority took out about $18 million in loans for property acquisition and demolition projects intended for the planned hockey arena. The PA Department of Community and Economic Development was required to approve the loans under the Economic Development Financing Law.

headline: KYW-CBS  Philadelphia, PA  Eyewitness News
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett is expected to sign bill outlawing the synthetic drugs "bath salts" and salvia, among others.

headline: Influence-peddling hurdles party lines
abstract: The Author, a columnist for the Gazette, addresses accusations of having a partisan agenda after he singled out state Senate Pro Tem Joe Scarnati in a column about expensive perks Scarnati received at a time when the Legislature is being lobbied about Marcellus Shale natural gas issues. The author claims the  point of the column was to decry what amounts to legalized bribery in Harrisburg and the susceptibility of amoral elected officials to campaign contributions from the natural gas industry.

headline: POTUS 08
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell speaking with the Brookings Institute: He mentions that he is co-chair on the America's Future nonprofit with Mayor Bloomberg from New York and Governor of California Arnold Schwarzenegger. For him it is a labor of love, because they do not get paid. Rendell will soon leave the office of PA Governor.

headline: Gilman to announce run for judge
abstract: The race is open for the Washington County judge position. Attorney Gary Gilman said that he would run in the primary election for the judicial seat left open by Mark Mascara, who passed away last summer.

headline: Pa. court may have to act on reapportionment
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court may have to intervene to select a fifth and final member of the panel dedicated to redrawing of PA's legislative districts. There are currently two Republicans and two Democrats on the panel which has yet to decide on the fifth member, who must not be employed by any government agency.

headline: Barletta ‘raging’ over loan rate
abstract: US Representative Lou Barletta is begging the US Small Business Administration to lower interest rates to flood affected businesses so the region does not lose even more jobs. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has been flooded with applications for relief since US President Barack Obama signed a declaration of disaster.

headline: PA State Rep. Vereb introduces Sudden Cardiac Arrest Prevention Act
abstract: State Representative Mike Vereb delivered a bill to the House floor that aims to prevent sudden cardiac arrest in student athletes by calling for the removal of student athletes exhibiting signs of the onset of Sudden Cardiac Arrest from athletic activity.

headline: Orie's lawyer might subpoena Zappala
abstract:
Senator Jane Orie’s attorney wants prosecutors to stipulate that Allegheny County District Attorney Stephen A Zappala, Jr. does not hire professional fundraisers for his own election
Bids and if prosecutors refuse, promises to seek to subpoena Zappala and force him to testify in Orie’s upcoming corruption trial. Orie, who was charged by Zappala, is accused of using her state-funded staff to work on her campaign and the campaign of her sister, Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin.

headline: Facebook teams with agencies for AMBER Alert pages
abstract: Increased reports of missing children has prompted the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children and the US Department of Justice to team up with Facebook to create AMBER Alert pages, which will help in the search for missing children. Each state will have its own page. Similar pages have been created in four Canadian provinces already.

headline: More training planned at Lackawanna County Prison
abstract: The PA Department of Corrections (DOC) cited the Lackawanna County Prison with a number of deficiencies. The lack of staff training was among them. New training is intended to show the staff how to remove  aggressive inmates, and how to minimize the chances of harming such inmates.

headline:
2 more defendants sentenced in Pa.
corruption case
abstract: A married couple who was charged with multiple crimes stemming from the PA General Assembly corruption scandal have received their sentencing. Both received reduced charges because of their cooperation in testifying against other defendants involved in the corruption case.

headline: School districts struggling with the cost of communication
abstract: Public relations specialists in Western PA schools have more and more job responsibilities as time goes on. If the school is not a strong believer in public relations, then these professionals risk losing their jobs. Many districts are dumping PR because of recent budget cuts at the state level.

headline: WTAE-ABC  Pittsburgh, PA  Ch. 4 Action News At 6
abstract: Approval has been granted for a statue honoring former state Representative John Murtha.

headline: Toomey wants borrowing tied to cuts
abstract: Senator Pat Toomey is the architect of a 13-line bill that prioritizes spending by using the steady stream of tax revenues to pay its debt obligations before any other government spending as a way of ensuring the United States does not default if the $14.3 trillion debt limit is hit. Those opposed to the plan, claim that it would force dramatic cuts across federal agencies. Toomey says he would not oppose raising the debt limit under the condition that it's tied to other reforms, like a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

headline: Exodus to Columbia County mulled
abstract: Several municipalities may break away from Luzerne County to join Columbia County. Luzerne County Commissioner Chairwoman Maryanne Petrilla wants to speak with disgruntled citizens and a citizens' watchdog group before any formal steps are taken. County Commissioner Stephen A. Urban said state legislators gave citizens the right to join another county, and he won’t attempt “to stop them.”

headline: Obama's State of the Union proposals will test whether parties can work together
abstract: US President Barack Obama will surely face opposition from both parties as he makes his State of the Union address. The only measure that the two parties have agreed upon, was to keep the tax cuts in place for most Americans. US House Speaker John A. Boehner thinks any education reform package should include private school vouchers.

headline: Rubbing more salt in Labor's wounds
abstract: The state of Maine is mulling over an effort to remove a mural depicting some of the state and country's leaders of the labor movement. The mural is explained to be "one-sided" proponents, while opponents of the removal see it as only another attack on labor interests.

headline: Pa. Governor's Residence reopens for public tours after being evacuated during recent flood
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett, along with his precious antiques, had to flee the governor's mansion because of floods caused by Tropical Storm Lee. He returned a week later.

headline: Pennsylvania poised to enact bill to preserve federal jobless benefits
abstract: Pennsylvania's Senate is expected to pass a bill that would allow 45,000 jobless residents to continue to receive 13 weeks of federally funded unemployment benefits.

headline: Philly SRC hears dire warning on school funding
abstract: City public school students, already lagging in academic achievement, are in danger of slipping further due to potential $500 billion budget on top of an already $40 million shortfall that could lead to larger classes, layoffs, cuts to school budgets, and a deeply slashed central office. The district must adopt a 2011-12 budget by the end of May.

headline: Mayor of tiny Pa. town charged with 'numbers'
abstract: Herbert Vargo Jr., the mayor of Fayette City, says that he has been falsely accused of taking "numbers" bets in a newsstand he owns. However, state police found Vargo's records of winners and payoffs and a large amount of money in a lockbox under his bed. Vargo faces preliminary arraignment on the gambling charges Feb. 17 and a preliminary hearing Feb. 25.

headline: Jeffrey Yocum seeks re-election as Lebanon County coroner
abstract: Dr. Jeffrey Yocum is seeking a fifth term as Lebanon County coroner. He has practiced medicine their since 1983. Yocum is member of a number of medical associations and is a diplomat of the American Board of Addiction Medicine.

headline: Pa. House OKs bath salts chemicals ban
abstract: The state House of Representatives voted unanimously to ban chemicals found in "bath salts" and other substances that were used to mimic the effects of cocaine and methamphetamine. These substances were sold mainly in tobacco shops and hemp stores, and after a recent string of crime related directly to the substances, the House moved quickly to pass the bill.

headline: State wants to broaden insurance oversight
abstract: PA received funding from the US Department of Health and Human Services to contract with experts to review rate increases, train staff, buy technology, and make health insurance information more accessible. The state is working on legislation that will grant the PA Department of Insurance review authority.

headline: 'Bath salts' ban sent to Corbett for enactment
abstract: A bill that would ban the sale of a legal drug known as "bath salts" is heading to Governor Tom Corbett's desk for approval after unanimous passage by the state Senate.

headline: Onorato to veto council's 'sweatshop' resolution
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato says he will veto county council's resolution that brands a Rankin steel company a "sweatshop" and ineligible for future county contracts based on provisions of the county's 2007 anti-sweatshop ordinance. If Democratic council members remain unanimous in their vote, they would have enough votes to override a veto. A spokeswoman for Onorato said he would provide more detail on his decision in a veto letter.

headline: Tioga County, Pa., mobile home park owner faces $10,000 fine
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has fined the owner of the Dear Mobile Home Park in Lawrence Township, Tioga County, $10,000 for illegally dumping and burning solid waste on his property. This is the owners third violation since 1996. The money will be paid in $1,000 installments as part of the Solid Waste Abatement Fund, which helps to finance cleanups across the state.

headline: A humble soldier: Maj. Dick Winters epitomized military's everyday heroes
abstract: The HBO miniseries "Band of Brothers" depicts Major Dick Winters as a hero during World War II, but he is too modest to ever stake that claim. The article describes Winter's life after the war. The author reminds the reader of the courage and the valor of the men and women currently fighting wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

headline: Obama re-election launches with email, website
abstract: President Barack Obama announced his re-election bid, urging his followers who propelled him to victory in 2008 to do the same in 2012. After announcing formally, the President is now in the process of filing with the Federal Election Committee which will then allow him to begin the massive fundraising campaign many see him planning.

headline: DN Editorial: Electoral college change would make us disappear
abstract: PA Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi wants to change electoral college laws. In a plan endorsed by PA Governor Tom Corbett, he proposes replacing the winner takes all system, with a system that would reward one vote to the winner of each congressional district. The author feels that this is less democratic considering the redistricting that has happened.

headline: Seasonal per diem hike kicks in for Harrisburg
abstract: A summertime boost in per diem rates by the federal government is drawing criticism from state Representative Sid Michaels Kavulich, who claims that an increase in the lodging rate for June through August can affect what some state lawmakers collect while on business in Harrisburg.

headline: Mellow is focus of feds’ probe, court says
abstract:
Former state Sen. Robert Mellow is the focus of a federal probe into alleged extortion, money laundering and fraud, according
to the dismissal of his appeal for the return of the evidence taken from his home and office. The exact nature of the investigation was disclosed in an opinion issued Wednesday by a three-member panel of the 3rd U.S.Circuit Court of Appeals. The court also noted that Mellow, who retired last year after serving 40 years in office, is the target of a grand jury sitting in Scranton.

headline: The repeal question: House Republicans owe Americans a few answers
abstract: Republicans can either work in the US House to fight the health care bill, or join Democrats in bipartisan fashion to fix and improve the legislation in the wake of Gabrielle Giffords shooting. Even if the Senate were to approve the repeal, the president would veto that. Republicans feel that the bill violates the constitution.

headline: Shelley not seeking re-election in 2012
abstract: Three-term Juniata County Commissioner Dale Shelley will not seek re-election in 2012. He has cited that age and family are reasons for retirement. Shelly talks about his accomplishments in the position. He was proud that he was able to add field officers to the county assessment office. These employees helped to keep property taxes in line.

headline: Nobody did the math on teacher cuts
abstract: Anger over Governor Tom Corbett's proposed education budget cuts has spilled over into school board meetings, as was the case in Allentown. In order to fix the problem of less funding, the Allentown School Board has proposed a new blueprint to their scholastic approach, a plan that would cut 247 teaching jobs. The plan has caused an uproar throughout the community.

headline: Casino revenue study warns of competition from other states, cannibalization from within
abstract: PA is set on using gambling money for property tax relief. To achieve this goal, the state may be better off creating casinos in Reading, York, or Altoona, according to a new economic analysis by state Treasurer Rob McCord. The logic is that concentrating casinos means less revenue, spreading, more.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  6PM News
abstract: Full day kindergarten remains threatened even after the latest budget plan restores some funding to its operation.

headline: Campaign office separate, ex-Orie staffer says
abstract: Former Staffer Joseph Smith said State Sen. Jane Orie used no public funds to pay for a campaign office complete with supplies and computers during a cross-examination by Orie's lawyers on the fifth day of her corruption trial. Orie is accused of using Smith and other taxpayer-funded staffers on her re-election campaigns, as well as those of her sister, Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin. Jane Orie faces 10 felony charges, including theft and conflict of interest.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Keep an eye on casinos
abstract: In attempt to boost Atlantic City's struggling casinos, Governor or New Jersey Christie deregulated. He has shifted oversight over the state's 11 casinos from the Casino Control Commission to the Division of Gaming Enforcement, which is part of the Attorney General's Office. It will now be left to the casinos to count their revenues and give the state a fair share.

headline: Pa. man crashes into ambulance carrying daughter
abstract: A Pennsylvania man rushing home after his daughter suffered a seizure struck the ambulance carrying the girl, injuring several people. The girl wasn't hurt in the crash but the man, along with the EMT driver had to be sent to the hospital.

headline: Why do politicians blame teachers and students for their busted budgets?
abstract: Governor Corbett's proposed $1.5 billion cut in education funding is drawing a lot of angry replies throughout the commonwealth. There is no one the cut will hurt more than the student and the parent, the opposition points out, while at the same time the governor refuses to tax gas drillers.

headline: State senators cross aisles for flood aid
abstract: PA Senators Blake, Baker, Yudichak, Gordner and Yaw have introduced a series of bills that will provide aid for those who have been affected by natural disasters. The bills will fix roads and bridges and allow local governments to lower victim's taxes when their property is damaged. The PA Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committees will meet to discuss funding.

headline: WPXI-NBC  Pittsburgh, PA  Ch. 11 News
abstract: Former state Representative Frank LaGrotta was taken to the hospital after fainting during his sentencing.

headline: Kevin Murphy: Selling liquor stores won't benefit state
abstract: State Rep. Kevin Murphy is opposed to  privatizing state liquor stores and as a member of the House Liquor Control Committee, promises to fight to push back the proposal. Murphy claims the proposal to sell appears is shortsighted and reckless and does not generate any real recurring revenue for the state in the long run.

headline: Should the state decide if mother knows best?
abstract: The author mentions a number of cases where parents' negligence led to the death of their children. She blames certain religious beliefs that stop young children from getting proper care from easily curable, but fatal conditions. She derides parents who allow their children to overeat and engage in risky behavior. She talks about what she believes the proper role of the government should be in the lives of children.

headline: Heated rhetoric: Did the war of words create a political climate that fueled the Giffords shooting?
abstract: Both liberal and conservative US Congressmen are outraged at the violence against left leaning members of Congress. The country wants swift justice for Jared Loughner, who is being charged with the attempted assassination of a member of Congress, two counts of killing federal employees and further charges relating to the murder of a 9-year-old girl. After recovering, US Representative Giffords joined the 112th Congress in the reading of the constitution; she read the first amendment.

headline: Examining state fleet a good start
abstract: Commonwealth One, a 41 foot bus used by governors past and present, is finally being auctioned off. The bus cost taxpayers up to $66 thousand dollars to maintain. Governor Corbett at a news conference announced the end to the bus, comparing it to how the state has been run over the years, inefficiently and outdated.

headline: PA House GOP corruption trial could last eight weeks.
abstract: The corruption trial for three former Republican aides will soon commence. The staffers and their lawyers are now choosing a jury. The staffers include Brian Preski, who worked for PA House Speaker Perzel, former Representative Feese and a former Feese aid. House Speaker Sam Smith may serve as a defense witness.

headline: LaGrotta back home, sentencing on for Wednesday
abstract: Former state Representative Frank LaGrotta has been released from a hospital and should appear in Lawrence County Court so a judge can complete his sentencing on drug charges.

headline: Philadelphia Sheriff's Office targeted by federal grand jury probe
abstract: A federal grand jury is investigating the real estate operations of the Philadelphia Sheriff's Office following recent upheaval over management and accounting practices under former Sheriff John Green. The U.S. Attorney's Office issued subpoenas for records on the sale of foreclosed properties after the Sheriff's Office was unable to document nearly $53 million in assets for an audit last year by City Controller Alan Butkovitz.

headline: Pennsylvania Turnpike reduces speed limits on section because of snow
abstract: Travel restrictions are in place on parts of the Pennsylvania Turnpike because of gusting winds and drifting snow. Commercial vehicles are being restricted to the right lane on that stretch. The PA Department of Transportation said that conditions are improving in Eastern PA.

headline: Movie critic's heirs say state Sen. Jeffrey Piccola has conflict of interest in estate case
abstract: Sharon Johnson left no will and her estate is still unresolved eight years later. Some of those involved in the settlement feel that the attorney and PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola has a conflict of interest in the case because he represents some people who have contested agreements with other clients of his. President Judge Todd A. Hoover has a hearing scheduled for the Dauphin County court.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Let inspectors do their job
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has granted even more leniency to the gas drilling industry, in the view of this editorial, by forcing the Department of Environmental Protection to approve all violations cited by their inspectors in the field. The measure slows down the process of government and enforcement, and the governor's office needs to allow the inspectors to perform their duty.

headline: No need to make English official
abstract: PA Representative Perry wants to make English the official language of the commonwealth of PA. The bill would also reduce funding for English-as-Second-Language programs. Similar bills have been passed in other states.

headline: Few attend hearing on Pennsylvania's congressional redistricting
abstract: There was a small attendance at a public hearing dealing with congressional redistricting, despite controversy surrounding the topic.

headline: Five films, including 'Batman' sequel, might shoot in Pittsburgh
abstract: Five films including, “The Dark Knight Rises” the third installment in the revived franchise, could be shooting in Pittsburgh, bringing much needed attention to the local film industry. The five feature films are scouting locations in the area for projects set to film during the spring and summer. Many movie studios are waiting to see if the tax credit survives Governor Corbett’s budget cuts, which is a major determining factor in whether they continue to choose the area for filming.

headline: Palmyra amnesty program reduces delinquent sewer, trash accounts
abstract: The recent amnesty program for Palmyra residents who are delinquent on their sewer and trash bills will result in about $30,000 for the borough and save residents about $7,000. Residents who paid by December 3 avoided penalty fees. The borough filed liens on the top accounts still delinquent after December 3. The city have $146,000 in delinquent sewer bills.

headline: Sentinel View: Sparking everlasting change
abstract: Representative Stephen Bloom agreed with angry citizens at a Carlisle town hall meeting on the topic of state legislature size. Pennsylvania is currently second among all states in legislature size and Rep. Bloom was adamant in the importance of pressure and persistence from the voting public in order to get real reform accomplished and the size of the legislature shrunk.

headline: Hearings eyed for Blue Cross
abstract: Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania is asking the PA Department of Insurance for a roughly 5% rate increase for its Special Care policy. It is also asking for permission to charge a $25 co-pay for diagnostic services. Special Care is a plan for low-income individuals who cannot afford enough to pay for Medicare. PA Governor Tom Corbett suggests that low income people use Special Care.

headline: Corbett approval found to founder
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett is experiencing low approval ratings five months into his term, but not exceptionally low compared to other governors in states dealing with budget issues.

headline: 40,000 new jobs? 100,000 new residents? Plan says it could happen
abstract: According to a draft released by the City Planning Commission, Philadelphia is poised for dramatic growth over the next 25 years and could attract upwards of 100,000 residents and create 40,000 jobs. The plan looks at physical development, transportation, land use, public utilities, public facilities, and parks and recreation, with the intent of making recommendations on how to facilitate that growth.

headline: Allentown police charge Marine on leave in rape of girl, 12
abstract: Franklin A. Burgos, 19, has been charged with rape of a child, rape by forcible compulsion, two counts of involuntary deviate sexual intercourse, two counts of aggravated indecent assault, sexual assault and indecent assault. This marine was arraigned by Senior Judge John Dugan and is now behind bars; bail it set at $200,000.

headline: Drug Court, frequent 'raids' making positive impact
abstract: One hundred and nine people have entered Northumberland County's Drug Court program since its inception in 2005. 40 people have graduated so far and the rest remain involved. Of the 40 graduates, only five have been rearrested for drug violations. The drug court costs about $5 to $6 dollars a day per individual, while housing that same person in jail costs about $50 a day.

headline: Nation's jobless rate declines slightly
abstract: The federal Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that jobs in the U.S. rose by over 200,000. The rise was aided by professional and business services stemming from the tax season. Local governments cut 15,000 jobs, mostly in education.

headline: Stop trying to suppress state's vote
abstract: The Republicans control both PA state chambers and they are experts at gaming the system for their own political advantage. The first act they took was to require voters to present identification at polling places, a measure that will likely affect the poor and minorities. PA State Senator Pileggi wants now to change how the state awards electoral votes.

headline: Unsustainable state pension system must be changed
abstract: It is asserted that the projected payouts for the state pension plan will be unpayable given the lack of contribution to the plans from state employees.

headline: Abortion clinic scandal fallout costs 6 jobs
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett announced that six state employees responsible for overseeing a Philadelphia abortion clinic where two women died have resigned or been fired. The Governor also unveiled tougher standards for clinics nationwide during his announcement. Under the new standards, more than 20 clinics will get annual and random unannounced inspections by the Health Department unit that inspects hospitals and outpatient surgery facilities.

headline: Kasunic, Wozniak to chair committees
abstract: PA Senator Richard Kasunic was appointed Democratic chairman of the Game and Fisheries Committee and PA Senator John Wozniak was appointed party chairman of the finance and transportation committees. PA Senate Democratic Leader Jay Costa made these announcements. The Senate is slated to return to session on Jan. 18.

headline: West Reading mayor vetoes '11 budget, wants more spending cuts
abstract: Reading Mayor Shane J. Keller has vetoed the borough's 2011 budget. He thinks that the council needs to do a better job of finding items to cut. Another problem with the budget was that it included revenue assumptions, which included an amount from Reading Hospital that it would pay the borough in lieu of taxes. The property tax rate will increase to 7.35 mills.

headline:
Saccone expects spending to hold at
$27.3 billion mark
abstract: State Representative Rick Saccone said state spending should stay at the proposed mark set by the governor's budget proposal. With the governor's opposition to Marcellus Shale taxation and his commitment to shrink the size of government, Rep. Saccone explained that the public sector, especially education, must work with less money in their budgets.

headline: Legislation protects student-athletes
abstract: PA Senator Pat Browne has sponsored the Youth Sports Safety Act, which establishes standards for dealing with concussions and traumatic brain injuries. Similar legislation has been passed by Representative Neuman. The PA Orthopedic Society is urging swift enactment.

headline: WPMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  10PM News
abstract: Operators of non-profit social clubs are calling for legislation that would allow them to keep more money from the sale of small games of chance in order to stay open.

headline: State senators hear liquor store privatization arguments
abstract:
Senators on the Law and Justice Committee heard testimony on the experience of other states that have liberalized liquor
Laws.  House Majority Leader Mike Turzai, R-Allegheny, is working on a privatization plan he says would bring $2 billion in one-time revenue into Pennsylvania by selling wholesale and retail liquor licenses. Newly elected Gov. Tom Corbett supports the idea and says he remains committed to privatization and is monitoring discussions on the topic in the Legislature.

headline: Barletta's first votes on budget cuts, health care
abstract: Freshman US Representative Lou Barletta has already developed a clear voting record. He voted to cut the House of Representatives budget by 5 percent and voted in favor of a rule that will allow the House to move ahead with a health care repeal vote next week. Senate Democrats have promised to override any attempt to repeal the health care bill.

headline: Cyber-school payments strain Elco's budget
abstract: The Elco School Districts 2011-12 budget deficit could be as high as $1.7 million. Charter schools costing close to $1 million, increasing electric charges and health-care costs, and stagnant tax revenue contribute to this problem. Superintendent Richard Nilsen said that raising taxes does not seem like a good idea in these economic times. A district resident filed for a special-education settlement agreement in the Lebanon County Court of Common Pleas, which ruled in his favor.

headline: DA calls on retailers to halt 'bath salt' sales
abstract: Luzerne County District Attorney Jackie Musto Carroll took the first step in stopping the sales of "bath salts" by calling on retailers to discontinue selling the item. This move is only a preliminary measure, for most in the region believe a state ban is imminent. "Bath salts" is a hallucinogenic controlled substance that has been the primary cause for some high-profile crimes occurring in the region.

headline: Uniontown approves special exception for Healthy Start
abstract: The Uniontown zoning hearing board has approved an exemption to allow Healthy Start to buy a house in the city and renovate it into office buildings. Healthy Start bought the home in 2004 but was unable to go ahead with the renovation because of the zoning ordinances on social service agencies. Healthy Start receives federal funding.

headline: Local officials welcome ban on texting while driving
abstract: The state Senate passed, a measure that makes texting while driving a primary offense, and hand-held cellphone use a secondary offense.

headline: Is banning gifts too much to ask?
abstract: Author believes legislators should not be permitted to accept gifts from special interest groups.

headline: Holden talks about Arizona shootings
abstract: US Representative Tim Holden discussed his concern for US Representative Gabrielle Giffords after she was shot by Jared Loughner. Holden could not understand why Giffords would be the target of such a brutal attack. Giffords has been mentioned as a possible Senate candidate in 2012 and a gubernatorial prospect in 2014.

headline: Money for gas well 911 training wanes
abstract: Without more state funding, volunteer fire companies in Pennsylvania that also serve as first responders to incidents and emergencies at Marcellus Shale gas wells could see their training programs cut. The programs are used to train local responders who often cannot afford to pay on their own and teach emergency procedures dealing with well blowouts to broken limbs.

headline: Health law to spur hospital, doctor networks
abstract: New health care rules set up by the Obama administration following the healthcare law will force hospitals and insurers to create accountable care organizations, or ACOs. These ACOs are networks of doctors and insurers who coordinate care for Medicare patients. Their purpose is to spurn affordable and quality care for the elderly, a move that could save as much as $960 million dollars in government spending over the next 3 years.

headline: PA jobless rate jumps in August to 8.2 percent.
abstract: The PA Department of Labor and Industry said that unemployment jumped in August as the national economy slowed. The state civilian labor force is about 6.3 million people. About half a million people in the state are looking for jobs. A spokesman for the Keystone Research Center said that manufacturing was one of the healthiest sectors.

headline: Practice what you preach, Gov.
abstract: Governor Corbett is criticized for using four newly purchased state vehicles after proposing a cut of 17,000 vehicles during his campaign.

headline: Health reform empowers states
abstract: Author Kathleen Sebelius, U.S. secretary of health and human services, describes the importance of The Affordable Care Act and assures readers that the act provides states with the flexibility to tailor their plans according to their specific health care needs.

headline: LPNs vanishing from hospital settings
abstract: Missy Moore, president of the National Federation of Licensed Practical Nurses notes a trend in the health care profession. Many hospitals are getting rid of licensed practical nursing jobs. Nurses work more in long-term care facilities, private clinics and physician’s offices. Despite this, experts say the future looks good for the profession, as the federal health care reform takes effect.

headline: Casey: Voluntary fracking chemical registry 'not enough'
abstract: A registry process created to allow energy companies to disclose the chemicals they use in the shale hydraulic fracturing process has worked, but some are calling for more regulation. Hydraulic fracturing has been the main extraction method at Marcellus Shale well sites. U.S. Senator from Pennsylvania Bob Casey has called for more government oversight on the issue because not all companies are obligated to share their information on the chemicals used.

headline: Keeping up with repairs
abstract: A report done by Transportation for America, a coalition of 500 organizations centered around improving federal transportation policy, has indicated that Pennsylvania's bridges are among the worst in the nation in terms of condition. With the down economy, funding all the necessary projects has become difficult, but PA as a whole has attempted to address the long list of construction- deficient bridges.

headline: County to reassess Pittsburgh values first
abstract: Pittsburgh property owners will be the first to new assessments to their real estate. This will save the city and its schools about $2 million in short-term borrowing costs. School officials said that they would need to borrow about $60 million if their property=tax were held up because of missing assessment numbers.

headline: Teens and tanning: Parental permission, not ban is enough
abstract: It is suggested that parental permission to tan should be made a contingency for teenagers' patronage of tanning salons, as opposed to an outright ban on their attendance.

headline: Congress ready to cut budget
abstract: President Barack Obama released his $3.7 trillion budget proposal for the fiscal year, which Republicans argue is too timid on spending cuts and deficit reduction. The House has yet to decide on a continuing resolution to fund the government from May to October.

headline: Jubelirer disputes claims of threats toward Rendell
abstract: PA Senator Robert C. Jubelirer has called claims made by PA Governor Ed Rendell "ludicrous and disingenuous." Rendell said that the Republicans forced him to sign the pay raise by threatening to block his agenda if he did not. According to Jubelirer the pair had a heated discussion but were pals the next day, and that Rendell said the heated discussions were nothing compared to what former mayor of Philadelphia John Street used to scream at him.

headline:
Democrats say they’ve been excluded
from whistleblower website
abstract: Pennsylvania House Democrats are upset over their inability to help regulate and oversee a state website that allows for people to report government waste or wrongdoing within the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board. The public is unable to view the website, but it used to uncover injustices within the gaming industry, from citizens to workers within casinos.

headline: Top-level approval of drilling under fire
abstract: State legislators are putting the Corbett administration under fire for certain procedures put in place dealing with enforcement procedures. These procedures require top political appointees inside the Department of Environmental Protection to approve of all Marcellus Shale drilling enforcement actions. The PA DEP issued a clarification memo stating that the procedural change was only temporary. Opponents of the measure argue that centralized enforcement will lead to less oversight all together.

headline: Flood crisis a reminder of importance of local government
abstract: Much praise has gone to local fire and rescue squads. We must look to the future, however, and think of how we can make it better. Citizens should vote on Election Day. Who you choose can affect how well you are taken care of when disaster strikes.

headline: Animas Corp. holds party for 125th anniversary of Johnson & Johnson
abstract: Animas Corp. opened up its Lawrence Drive headquarters for a tour and a party, to celebrate the 125th anniversary of their parent company, Johnson & Johnson.

headline: Rizzo not expected to get GOP endorsement
abstract: Incumbent Frank Rizzo is not expected to be among the five candidates endorsed for City Council by Republican Ward leaders. Rizzo’s exclusion from a list of recommended candidates by a committee of GOP leaders is due to fallout from his participation in the city’s controversial Deferred Retirement Option Plan (DROP). Though the committee’s endorsement carries much sway, many observers question whether the lack of an endorsement could keep Rizzo off the ballot due to name recognition.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Timoney Knox lawyer Harper to run for Montco commissioner
abstract: Kate Harper, a partner at Fort Washington law firm Timoney Knox and a state representative, said she plans to run for Montgomery County Commissioner this year. This is because the man currently in this spot, James R. Matthews announced that his is looking for a job in the incoming administration of Governor Elect Tom Corbett. Party leaders think that he has little chance because Matthews has turned his back on the Republican Party and is currently under investigation.

headline: McGeehan shouldn't be face of ouster movement
abstract: Pennsylvania state House member Michael McGeehan is lobbying for Philadelphia school district Superintendent Arlene Ackerman to be fired. McGeehan is not the first person calling for the termination of the Superintendent, but McGeehan has in the past made racial comments, and those such comments have changed his qualification to comment on the issue of Ms. Ackerman, some say.

headline: Erickson proposes tax on natural gas drilling
abstract: State Senators Ted Erickson and John Yudichak recently put forward a bill that would place a tax on all natural gas extracted from the Marcellus Shale region. The tax would generate more than $406 million by the year 2016, according to Senator Yudichak's office. The funds from the taxation would be split into three different areas, all going towards environmental issues dealing with the Shale drilling procedures.

headline: Seven regional 'disaster recovery centers' open in PA.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has announced the creation of seven "disaster recovery centers" across the commonwealth in response to Tropical Storm Lee. Before visiting a center people need to file a claim with their insurance provider and request aid from the Federal Emergency Management Administration.

headline: Rendell, Schwartz: Weiner must go
abstract: Former PA Governor Ed Rendell and Representative Allison Schwartz have both called for the resignation of Representative Anthony Weiner following a scandal during which he sent lewd photos of himself women he met on the internet.

headline: Witness: Staffers pretended to be Jane Orie in campaign calls
abstract: In her testimony before an Allegheny County jury, retired staffer Christine Bahr claimed that staff members for state Sen. Jane Orie made campaign phone calls during the workday and were directed to impersonate the senator on the phone.

headline: WETM Noon News on WIVT
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell lashed out at a reporter who asked him about the effect of legalized slot-machine gambling on gambling addicts. Rendell said that "simpletons" and "idiots" do this and that people will gamble regardless of the state's role. Rendell is no stranger to controversy, as his "nation of wussies" comment shows.

headline: Budget solution offered by state Dems
abstract: Pennsylvania state Democrats have unveiled their budget proposal for the fiscal year 2012. At a Philadelphia news conference, Democratic leaders proposed taxing Marcellus Shale gas extraction and restoring funding to the adultBasic program, a health insurance program for low income citizens. Governor Corbett's budget proposal calls for a 50% cut from higher education spending, something Democrats say can be alleviated by taxing Shale well production.

headline: Change is coming at glacial speed
abstract: The Speaker of the House of Pennsylvania, Sam Smith, has introduced a bill that would eliminate 50 seats in the House, cutting the member number from 203 to 153. The bill has a number of co-sponsors, but in order to pass, requires a constitutional amendment. A bill requiring as much attention and change as this could take up to ten years to take true form.

headline: Pa. judge declares key part of Obama's health plan unconstitutional
abstract: A federal judge ruled that parts of US President Obama's health-care legislation are unconstitutional. The judge found a problem with the government requiring every individual to purchase insurance. US District Judge Christopher C. Conner said that this does not fall within in the federal governments power to regulate commerce.

headline: Cambria defense firm wins contracts
abstract: Cambria County defense firm JWF Defense Systems has been awarded contracts for the some of the manufacturing related to a remote-operated weapons system.

headline: Freebies for lawmakers
abstract: Pennsylvania Senate president pro tempore Joe Scarnati enjoyed an all expenses paid trip to Super Bowl XLV in Texas. Consol Energy Inc., a major player in the gas-drilling industry covered all of Scarnati’s expenses.

headline: Canonsburg expected to OK $1M for street repairs
abstract: Canonsburg Borough Council is expected to approve spending of about $1 million to repair streets at its legislative meeting today. The funding comes from the federal Community Development Block Grant funds. Borough manager Terry Hazlett said that the borough got really great deals on the streets.

headline: Corbett wins initial victory in healthcare suit.
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett won a key victory in a healthcare suit brought on by members of the former adultBasic insurance plan, a form of health coverage subsidized by state government for low income workers. The Commonwealth Court of PA denied a motion to hold government funds originally appropriated for the adultBasic program. AdultBasic was shut down by the Corbett administration after failing to be economically sustainable, and members of adultBasic sued to resurrect the program.

headline: Pa. Gov Signs Tougher Abortion Clinic Rules
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will sign a bill that will implement new abortion clinic standards. The initiative came after grotesque conditions were uncovered at a Philadelphia location. Clinics can be subject to unannounced inspection. Both opponents and supporters are up in arms over the legislation.

headline: Pennsylvania's political clout on the line
abstract: Legislation sponsored by PA Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi and PA Governor Tom Corbett would scrap the current winner-take-all system of electoral college votes. This could erode the states political clout. Former PA Governor Ed Rendell thinks that this would lead presidential candidates to spend less time campaigning in the state.

headline: WTAE-ABC  Pittsburgh, PA  Ch. 4 Action News At Noon
abstract: Former state Representative Frank LaGrotta was sentenced for charges relating to forged prescriptions for the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

headline: School districts bracing for end of stimulus funds
abstract: Thanks in part to the economic stimulus money in the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, most PA school districts were able to weather the recession. With money no longer available by the end of the calendar year and possible reductions in state education funding, many fear the progress made in education will be halted. This story was compiled by education writer Eleanor Chute from stories produced by a national reporting project undertaken by 36 news outlets in 27 states, including the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette and the Philadelphia Inquirer.

headline: Public-private partnerships offer promising future
abstract: The author feels that Pennsylvania must take a hard look at transportation funding now that tolling I-80 is off the table. He talks about Public-Private Partnerships and how they can reduce costs to taxpayers and deliver a higher level of service. Local governments around the country have employed this model, and their financial backers often include union pension funds. PA Representative Rick Geist has crafted legislation to this effect.

headline: Cumberland County site developer won't appeal casino-license decision
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board awarded its final casino license to a Fayette County site. The decision ended the hopes of several other locations who were vying for the license, including RV World in Cumberland County. RV World was hoping to be a recreational vehicle-themed casino resort in Hampden Township.

headline: Corbett signs new abortion clinic rules into law.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will sign a law tightening regulations on abortion facilities. Abortion clinic operators fear that the new costs will put them out of business. Costs will depend on how the PA Department of Health decides to apply the new restrictions.

headline: Proposed change would let Pennsylvanians get test results from labs
abstract: The US Health and Human Services Administration has announced the passage of a new federal law that will allow patients to get test results directly from laboratories instead of waiting for them from a doctor. The logic is that if patients are more involved and aware of their situation, they will make better healthcare choices.

headline: Army Reserve Center in Forks Township should honor fallen Emmaus soldier, say Charlie Dent, Bob Casey
abstract: U.S. Rep. Charlie Dent and U.S. Sen. Bob Casey say an Army Reserve center in Forks Township should be named for Emmaus woman Ashley Lynn Moyer, a Sergeant killed in Iraq.

headline: Chuck Ardo talks about working for Mayor Linda Thompson
abstract: Chuck Ardo, the former spokesman for Mayor Linda Thompson, spoke with The Patriot-News Editorial Board about his decision to resign from his post as well as Mayor Thompson’s job as Mayor.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: The Philadelphia Department of Human Services, Quasir Alexander & me
abstract: The author feels that the PA Department of Human Services (DHS) is under capable leadership but that the child-protection agency has a very long way to go. He recounts his traumatic experience with the agency as a child, and explains how the death of Quasire Alexander could have been avoided through the actions of this agency. He calls upon Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter to push for improvements.

headline:
Ariz. Legislature OKs presidential
'birther' bill
abstract: The Arizona state legislator passed a bill that would require all Presidential candidates to show proof of birth within the United States in order to be on the state election ballot. The measure is waiting for a signature from Arizona Governor Jan Brewer to become law. Opponents of the bill say it is about opposition to President Obama, who some believe was not born in the United States. Proponents say the measure deals with election integrity.

headline: ANALYSIS: Fall session lacked big victories for Corbett, GOP
abstract: Pennsylvania state representatives received an automatic pay increase on December 1. 2011. The author feels that residents are being shortchanged, because despite paying for a full time legislature, few issues were actually tackled. PA Governor Tom Corbett would not budge on education, while House Majority Leader Mike Turzai fought to privatize liquor sales.

headline: Pennsylvania National Guard aids flood cleanup efforts
abstract: Tropical Storm Irene devastated some homes in the Middletown area. A detachment of the PA National Guard was dispatched to secure the area so that homes would not be looted. There has been some looting and the guard captured one looter.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 6
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilwoman Theresa Smith has introduced a bill that would limit how close dancers could come to patrons at strip clubs and set further guidelines for where such clubs can operate.

headline: More Pennsylvania, New Jersey suburbanites using food stamps
abstract: Food stamps are becoming readily commonplace, most surprisingly in middle-class and affluent suburban communities. Places such as Collegeville, where the median household income is more than 104,000, have seen significant increases in SNAP usage. Layoffs in the pharmaceutical and mortgage-finance industries may be partly to blame for the increases. The average monthly SNAP benefit for an individual in Pennsylvania is $123; in New Jersey, it's $125. The two states recently increased eligibility to current levels from 130 percent of poverty last year, after a Temple University study.

headline: Colorado D.A. offers Philadelphia help in Kensington strangler case
abstract: Denver District Attorney Mitchell Morrissey says he wants to help Philadelphia police catch the Kensington strangler using a new forensics technology known as familial DNA. Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams, as well as Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey, Fraternal Order of Police president John J. McNesby, and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter have all been contacted and will likely work with the Federal Bureau of investigation to try to solve this cold case.

headline: Galloway calling for open records review
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representative John Galloway has called on state House and Senate members to conduct a full review of the PA Office of Open Records and the accuracy of its website information. The reason behind the review stems from a project completed by the Associated Press and the Bucks County Courier Times that collected salary and benefit information of state legislators.

headline: We need the space: Land preservation should be a priority
abstract: Over the past few decades, Harrisburg has grown increasingly suburban. The city's Open Space Committee is now taking efforts to preserve the area's natural beauty. The purpose of the committee is to prioritize targets for preservation, to help the city approach the state and federal government for funding.

headline: Board of health: UPMC's directors are the ones to call on Highmark
abstract: The service agreement between Highmark and the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center will soon expire. This could leave many Highmark customers without access to UPMC doctors and facilities, unless they buy a new brand of insurance. PA Senator Wayne Fontana is trying to pressure the health care provider to resume talks with the insurer. Pittsburgh County Councilman Ed Kress wants to revoke UPMC's property tax exemption if Highmark is not upheld.

headline: Mortgage protections in danger
abstract: The author expresses his concern over the possibility that a mortgage assistance program may lose funding under the 2011 budget plan.

headline: State senator: Tax equalization board must be more accountable
abstract:
State Sen. John Gordner will be introducing a bill that would increase
State Tax Equalization Board members from three to five, hold hearings at municipality or school district requests, and review findings that show property values changing by 10 percent or more compared with previous years. STEB, which balances disparities in property values for school districts determining budgets, has made widespread assessment mistakes, brining the state agency into the spotlight.

headline: Convention bureau chief's Philly roots go deep
abstract: Jack Ferguson, who has spent four decades in the hospitality industry, is head of the Convention and Visitors Bureau in Philadelphia. Ferguson talks about his pride in the history of the city and the expansion of the Convention Center. Philadelphia Mayor Nutter expresses his admiration for the dedication that Ferguson has for improving the city.

headline: OUR VIEW: School boards need to tighten their belts amid big funding cuts
abstract: Many local concerns have arisen over Governor Corbett's proposed cut of $500 million to the education budget. Even though the cuts seem severe, school boards must still work on measures that ensure financial frugality and efficiency, in order to keep their schools running effectively.

headline: Illuminating plight of the homeless
abstract: 93 homeless have died in Wyoming Valley over the last few years. They were recently honored in a ceremony set up by REACH, an advocacy group for the homeless. PA State Senator Lisa Baker attended.

headline: Toomey: Debt panel should tackle entitlements
abstract: Pat Toomey, the freshman US Senator form PA, is one of the 12 federal lawmakers tasked with cutting over $1.5 trillion in spending over the next decade. Toomey stated that his colleagues need to tackle big-ticket issues like Social Security and Medicare. He is a proponent of federal entitlement reform.

headline: Pa. Education Secretary: School districts can't blame charters
abstract: Department of Education Secretary Ronald Tomalis has refuted claims by public school officials that funding for charter schools place their schools under financial stress.

headline: Regional caucus may help focus attention
abstract: Author praises a group of GOP lawmakers for creating the Southcentral Pennsylvania Caucus. The author believes legislative caucuses offer a great way for lawmakers with common interests to increase a region's influence and address issues that apply across the borders of legislative districts.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Cursing isn't always a crime
abstract: The US Supreme Court has said that cursing is protected speech, providing it's not threatening. Police officers in Philadelphia are given special training so that they can draw this line. The author feels that the average Philadelphian needs to put up with a lot of "ear pollution," and advocates a public awareness campaign by the Eastern State Public Transportation Authority aimed at encouraging better etiquette on its vehicles.

headline: A line can take funny twists in redistricting
abstract: Redistricting in Pennsylvania and throughout the United States is underway and along with it, gerrymandering. Gerrymandering is the process in which legislative districts are drawn to include a demographic most suitable to vote for a certain candidate. This editorial takes a look at the history and the present day facts of gerrymandering, and how it affects elections.

headline: Bucks Congressman in middle of payroll tax cut arguments
abstract: Bucks County Republican Congressman Mike Fitzpatrick, while standing in for Congressman John Boehner as Speaker of the US House of Representatives, walked off the floor after Democrat Steny Hoyer brought up a bill to extend tax cuts. Fitzpatrick stated that Steny's action went against a bipartisan agreement to not bring up "unanimous consent" agreements without consulting both parties' leadership.

headline: Pennsylvania's state workers facing unsettled work schedule in light of forecasted flooding
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has stated that he will confer with officials who watch rainfall and flooding forecast when deciding whether state workers will report to the capitol tomorrow for work. A spokesman for the General Services Administration building said the federal courthouse in Harrisburg will be open as usual.

headline: Goldsworthy bows out; Denisco chosen
abstract: West Pittston Mayor Bill Goldsworthy resigned from office during a council meeting to accept a position as deputy director of Governor Tom Corbett’s Northeast Regional office. Anthony Denisco was appointed to replace him.

headline: Santorum says U.S. 'belongs to God.'
abstract: Former Sen. Rick Santorum told attendees at the Conservative Political Action Conference that "America belongs to God" and  urged them not give up their opposition to abortion, gay rights, or President Obama. Santorum is considering a possible White House run.

headline: Transportation weighs on Western Pennsylvania
abstract: A poll shows that Allegheny County residents are more concerned about transportation issues than residents elsewhere in the state. Jim Roddey, who has been tapped for PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett's transition transportation committee said that the problem was serious. The PA Department of Transportation said that about 22 percent of roads and 30 percent of bridges in the area are deficient.
