headline: Montco senator eyes transportation woes
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator John Rafferty, chairman of the Transportation Committee, answered questions dealing with traffic and road congestion at a speaking engagement in Delaware County. Rafferty commented more state money was needed to fix the traffic problems in the region, an area that generates up to 70 percent of total state tolls.

headline: PA first to use special hologram on driver's licenses
abstract: A new hologram will soon appear on all new PA driver's licenses. The PA Department of Transportation says that it is the first state in the country to use black-and-white holograms. The holograms are meant to combat fake IDs. A spokesman for the Liquor Control Board said that this is one of many steps that the state needs to take to outpace counterfeiters.

headline: ACM awarded $1.5 million grant for new building
abstract: PA State Senator Richard Kasunic confirmed the release of a grant the to Somerset campus of the Allegany College of Maryland. This is a long-awaited $1.5 million state redevelopment grant to construct an addition. Somerset County Chamber of Commerce Executive Director Ron Aldom thinks this will greatly improve the economy.

headline: Firms that hire illegal immigrants could lose Allegheny County business
abstract: Allegheny County would be able to break any contracts it has with companies that hire illegal aliens under an ordinance now being considered by county council.

headline: Rally to call for Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson to quit
abstract: Some of Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson’s most ardent critics are holding a rally calling for Thompson to resign. The rally comes on the heels of Thompson’s former spokesman, Chuck Ardo’s criticisms of her management style.

headline: Commentary: Corbett misses opportunity to chip away education's fortress
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Corbett voiced his concern over a school voucher bill, a measure allowing tax dollars to go towards private education for low income families, after it had already passed the Senate and looked to be on course for his desk. Lobbying seems to have played a role in his concern over the current bill, comments the editor.

headline: Strengthen our workforce: get more GED sites
abstract: In this letter, a member of PA Governor Tom Corbett's Advisory Commission on Postsecondary Education speaks extensively on the overwhelming need for more GED testing facilities. More than 1 million adults in PA did not graduate high school, and the GED test is a way in which they can access the high school degree. By having better access to testing facilities for potential GED test-takers, the workforce within PA would be strengthened, the author writes.

headline: Wilting in the drought
abstract: The excessive heat and lack of rainfall in the central PA region has created issues in the state's agricultural sector. Milk production has decreased along with crop yield, causing higher prices for farmers and consumers.

headline: Plowed under: Federal farm bill languishing
abstract: The federal farm bill expired Sept. 30 and is worth about $284 billion over five years. It includes subsidies for a wide range of federal programs. Congress is tackling larger budget issues which have delayed consideration of this legislation.

headline: Analysis: Rick Santorum's last stand
abstract: Former US Senator Rick Santorum from PA has seen his once substantial lead in PA over Mitt Romney in the primary race for president shrink over the past few weeks. Mr. Romney has secured a large spending edge over Mr. Santorum, and although the Santorum campaign has won some key battleground states in the past months, his once surging campaign seems to be on the decline. PA is poised to be the make or break point for the Santorum campaign.

headline: Big project targets acid discharge in Adams Twp.
abstract: An acid-mine problem in Cambria County, PA, has caused federal and state officials to approve a $15 million project aimed at treating the contaminated water flowing down the Little Conemaugh River in Adams Township.

headline: Blame is laid at Harrisburg’s feet
abstract: Dave Davare, former director of research services at the Pennsylvania School Boards Association held an information session about school tax funding. His research dates back to the 1980s.

headline: Rep. Thomas joins marchers in Philadelphia
abstract: PA state Representative Curtis Thomas from Philadelphia urged members of his district to stop the recent surge in violence in a rally held in North Philadelphia. Members of the community joined along side Rep. Thomas to help increase crime awareness among adults, teenagers, and children alike.

headline: Ticket $ changes just fine
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed into law a measure that would reduce the revenue generated to state municipalities from traffic citations. PA municipalities are now required to reach a threshold of hours-per-week of police protection in order to receive half of the fine revenues resulting from traffic stops.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: What's Corbett trying to hide?
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer wants to know why PA Gov. Tom Corbett is trying to skirt the state's open-records law. Corbett has made a regular habit of declaring his daily schedule off limits to the press. Associated Press reporter Mark Scolforo filed a request in February 2011 to see the governor's schedule and e-mails. Corbett's lawyers responded that they were exempt from the state's 2008 Right-to-Know Law.

headline: Kotik in the 45th: Democrats should stay with an experienced rep
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette endorses Democrat Nick Kotik for the 45th Legislative District, a seat he has held for five terms. Although he resides in the minority party, Mr. Kotik has proven his ability to reach across the aisle and work with Republicans in Marcellus Shale and public transportation legislation, among others.

headline: American Atheists state director to desecrate Quran if state House doesn't drop "Year of Religious Diversity" resolution
abstract: The director of the PA chapter of American Atheists will vandalize the Quran if the state House of Representatives decides to pass a resolution celebrating religious diversity within the state. The move to desecrate the Muslim holy book has sparked controversy in the state as well as abroad.

headline: Holiday event held at Governor’s Mansion
abstract: The governor and family hosted holiday festivities at the Governor's Mansion.

headline: The film tax credit works, and Western Pennsylvania is a winner
abstract: The PA General Assembly along with Governors Corbett and Rendell have succeeded in making the film tax credit work in PA. Pittsburgh especially, as well as other parts of the commonwealth have seen an increase in film activity that has resulted in almost $2 billion in economic activity and 3,000 jobs stemming from the film industry.

headline: Casey rolling in cash
abstract: Sitting US Senator Bob Casey from PA is leading his challenger, Republican Tom Smith, by a three-to-one margin in campaign financing, following Mr. Casey's biggest fundraising quarter of the campaign season.

headline: Prison could lose $642,000 with loss of state inmates
abstract: Centre County Administrator Tim Boyde is trying to find ways to make up the revenue the county will lose when dozens of state inmates are forced to move from the Centre County Correctional Facility due to overcrowding.

headline: Governor’s role in Joe Paterno firing at issue
abstract: A gag order has been placed on several public officials, including PA Governor Tom Corbett, pertaining to the Penn State University sex abuse scandal. ESPN The Magazine published an article that implicated the Governor as a major player in the firing of PSU head football coach Joe Paterno, an accusation Gov. Corbett is unable to answer to.

headline: GOP to choose candidate to run against Petrarca
abstract: After presumed Republican state House candidate John Palaika dropped out of the election, the state Republican party has set up a public meeting to choose their candidate for the 55th state House district.

headline: Elimination of jury commissioners on the table
abstract: Pennsylvania counties face a Dec. 31 deadline to decide whether to keep or eliminate jury commissioners. Centre County may follow a statewide trend and eliminate its two jury commissioner positions.

headline: Corbett's office responds to Freind column
abstract: The office of PA Governor Tom Corbett issued a reply to a scathing letter written by one PA citizen. The letter addressed issues pertaining to the child sex-abuse scandal involving Penn State University employee Jerry Sandusky while Gov. Corbett was the acting state Attorney General.

headline: Corbett cuts ribbon on new Turnpike interchange
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett cut the ribbon on the new Turnpike interchange at PA state route 23.

headline: Court to hear appeal of shale drilling law
abstract: Appeals were heard in the PA Commonwealth Court regarding the constitutionality of the state's natural gas drilling law. Local government officials from western PA made their case on why the law's measures on zoning rules and chemical confidentiality fall outside the purview of the state's constitution.

headline: Community nonprofit tax credit is experiment
abstract: The new PA state budget includes a tax credit provision that could incentivize businesses to financially assist nonprofit agencies who work with the mentally disabled. The tax credit was created to replace a 10 percent cut in spending to community based programs in the current budget plan.

headline: Casey argues for more heating funding
abstract: US Sen. Bob Casey (D-PA) announced support for a plan that will provide $4.7 billion in heating assistance for low-income households. The federal program, called the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP has been cut in recent years to just $3.5 billion in funding.

headline: Parents contact Boyle about safety of CSX tracks
abstract: Safety issues have risen concerning railroad tracks that are found close to a little league baseball field outside of Philadelphia, PA. State Rep. Brendan Boyle, as well as local parents have called on the train operating company, CSX, to build a fence to ensure the safety of the children who play on the field.

headline: Obama portrayed as enemy of success by Romney
abstract: Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney accused President Obama's lack of business experience as a main factor behind the sputtering US economy. While speaking in Westmoreland County, PA, Mr. Romney also blamed failed liberal policies to have caused unemployment and not progress. PA Governor Tom Corbett introduced the candidate to the audience.

headline: State Treasurer McCord wants to review Lottery contract
abstract: State Treasurer Rob McCord says a contract with the firm that runs the United Kingdom's National Lottery may be in jeopardy if the governor expands the games without legislative approval.

headline: Pennsylvania budget cuts, policy changes are ravaging services, disability advocates say
abstract: The recent PA budget cuts proposed by the Corbett administration have left some service providers in the state without essential resources needed to continue operation. Service providers for the intellectually disabled have had to lay off workers and dismantle programs because of the shortage in government aid, leaving advocates for the disabled upset and disgruntled.

headline: Romney To Make 2 Campaign Stops In Area
abstract: Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney is scheduled to make two stops in PA where he hopes to win a state that has gone Democratic since 1998. Mr. Romney plans to focus on the slow-moving economy and how the President's policies have hurt the PA middle class.

headline: Special prosecutor should investigate Harrisburg's debt debacle, state senators say
abstract: State Sen. Michael Folmer (R-Lebanon) said he introduced legislation Wednesday calling for the appointment of a special prosecutor to probe financial transactions by the city of Harrisburg.

headline: Campaign 2012: 37th District Senate candidates debate in Peters
abstract: Three candidates for the PA 37th Senatorial District seat squared off in a public debate in Peters Township in the western part of the state. The incumbent, Senator John Pippy is not seeking reelection, leaving the race open to a state Rep., Mark Mustio; a nurse, Sue Means; and a Pittsburgh-area software company owner, D. Raja. The three took jabs at each other, while also focusing on the public transportation problem in western PA, among other topics.

headline: Mulling possible funding sources for child abuse triage centers
abstract: Facilities within the state that help victims of child abuse could receive a large boost in funding, according to PA state Representative Julie Harhart. The increase in reported child abuse has spawned the movement from more concentrated funding towards these facilities.

headline: Federal government will run PA’s healthcare exchange
abstract: The Corbett administration has refused to cooperate with the Affordable Care Act thus far and the federal government will be forced to provide the infrastructure to sign up the thousands of Pennsylvanians who will use the new plan to get coverage.

headline: Corbett blames school boards for tax increases.
abstract: In his monthly radio appearance, PA Governor Tom Corbett told Pennsylvanians to appeal to their local school board if they are disgruntled with the financial operations of their public schools. After the state cut millions of dollars of aid to state public schools, opponents of the cuts blamed the Corbett administration for cutting what is an essential service for children and the youth within the state.

headline: Aiming to make restaurant ‘BYOW’ policies obsolete
abstract: PA state Representative Dan Moul has introduced a legislative measure that would make it easier for restaurants to sell wine to their customers. The plan would allow for wine-only licenses, a contrast to the current regulation requiring all wine-selling restaurants to hold full liquor licenses.

headline: School employee with conviction can keep job, court rules
abstract: The Allegheny Intermediate Unit cannot be forced to fire a longtime employee even though a new state law places a ban on school employment for people convicted of certain crimes. AIU executive director Linda Hippert called the employee in question "exemplary" and is pleased with the court's ruling.

headline: State flag to fly at half staff through Saturday for fallen firefighters
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett announced that flags of the state will fly at half-staff following the death of two firefighters in the state.

headline: Philly election official details examples of voter fraud
abstract: A Philadelphia city government commission in charge of investigating potential voter irregularities reported that such irregularities have occurred over the past decade in the city. The report was backed by PA Governor Tom Corbett as proof for new state legislation requiring the use of personal identification at voting booths. The irregularities came about by both mistake and fraud, the commission found.

headline: State voter ID law is far from resolved
abstract: The recent injunction that allowed voters to vote without showing identification covered only the last election. Witold Walczak, legal director of the American Civil Liberties Union of Pennsylvania is working with others to further delay implementation of the law.

headline: 39th House District: Levdansky for the Dems, D'Alessandro for the GOP
abstract: An election in western PA for the 39th House District is heating up as the primary looms. In a district where Republicans are outnumbered two-to-one, Shauna D'Allessandro is facing incumbent Rick Saccone in the Republican primary. The Democratic primary has a former House member, David Levdansky, facing Rob Rhoderick, a candidate who ran for the seat but lost six years before.

headline: Ex-NE Pa. lawmaker appeals pension forfeiture
abstract: Former PA representative Robert Mellow is appealing the decision of the State Employees' Retirement System to stop payment of his yearly pension, following his guilty plea to corruption charges. Mr. Mellow pleaded guilty to misuse of state-paid employees and faces up to five years in prison.

headline: Corbett promises fund plan for transit and roads
abstract: Transportation Secretary Barry Schoch said a detailed transportation funding plan would be released early next year. It will include a list of projects that would move forward if the plan gains approval. The governor's Transportation Funding Advisory Commission is considering a tax on gasoline wholesalers.

headline: Mellow’s guilty plea relocated to Scranton
abstract: Former PA state Senator Robert Mellow's guilty plea hearing has been relocated to Scranton instead of Philadelphia by a U.S. District judge. Senator Mellow is being tried for conspiracy after he and members of his staff used state time to perform campaign work.

headline: New welfare restrictions target booze, tattoos
abstract: Several state legislatures including Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, and Arizona have been pushing for more restrictions and oversight of welfare programs. Proponents of the measures say some welfare recipients are abusing the program, requiring reforms that would disallow tax-payer money for tattoos, liquor, or other vices.

headline: Corbett scheduled to attend upcoming crime summit
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett will attend an upcoming summit meant to address rising crime in Berks County.

headline: Humane Society: PA egg farm 'deplorable.
abstract: An undercover probe by the Humane Society of the United States of PA egg farm giant, Kreider Farms, has many animal-health advocates outraged. Conditions in which the chickens were living were found to be "intolerable" by the Society, while Kreider Farms called the accusations a misrepresentation of their overall farming operation.

headline: Partisan politics in play in photo ID law debate
abstract: Democrats in the PA General Assembly accused Republicans, notably the House Majority Leader, of politicizing the voter identification issue after the Majority Leader suggested it could allow Republican presidential nominee Mitt Romney to win the state. The voter ID law was formed to stop voter fraud, an issue Democrats say disenfranchises certain minority voters.

headline: Corbett correct to keep pushing for liquor privatization
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett is determined to win approval for his plan to privatize the state liquor system. He hopes to show others how much revenue is lost by residents buying alcohol in neighboring states.

headline: State candidates ponder, should government be involved in health care?
abstract: Several state officials from PA were questioned on their views of the Affordable Care Act, the bill passed into law by Congress concerning health care and health insurance. The Act is facing immense pressure from opponents who say the mandate to purchase health insurance is unconstitutional. Proponents of the measure see it as a rational step to combat high prices for health care.

headline: Corman: 'People need to relax,' state officials shouldn't cut PSU funds without more facts
abstract: Some PA state lawmakers are unlikely to support funding cuts to Penn State University following the Jerry Sandusky child-abuse case and the Freeh report. Some state legislators have brought up the issue of cutting state funds to the University, something Senator Jake Corman calls "knee-jerk."

headline: Governor missing in action?
abstract: null

headline: Rohrer hopes to take pickup truck full of votes out of Lancaster County
abstract: Former state Representative Sam Rohrer is running in the Republican primary for U.S. Senate and is logging significant time in Lancaster County. Although his 2010 run for PA Governor was stopped short in the primary against Tom Corbett, Lancaster was one of only two counties that Mr. Rohrer won in votes. He is hoping the county will again vote in his favor.

headline: Gov. Tom Corbett discusses Penn State football, Paterno statue, ongoing criminal investigation
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett addressed several issues surrounding former Penn State University employee Jerry Sandusky and the criminal trial that found him guilty of child sex-abuse. Speaking in Harrisburg, Gov. Corbett answered questions about his involvement in the investigation as Attorney General as well as his opinions on the FBI's Freeh report.

headline: Green-energy mandates will hit PA’s poorest hardest
abstract: A new study by the Beacon Hill Institute at Suffolk University, a free-market think tank, says that a state mandate that requires electric providers to use so-called green energy will drive up costs for consumers in PA.

headline: School spending: The exemption ruse
abstract: Although PA has on the books restrictions and regulations on school districts raising local property taxes, the PA Department of Education has recently approved 199 districts hiking property taxes, an action many are finding "outrageous."

headline: Corbett did not tell Penn State trustees of investigation.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett did not warn his fellow Penn State University trustees of the ongoing Jerry Sandusky child-abuse investigation while also leading the investigation as the state's Attorney General. The FBI's independent investigation, the Freeh report, criticized the University's trustees, including Gov. Corbett, for covering up the Sandusky incident and failing to probe further into the matter.

headline: Dems nominate former Lebo commissioner for House vacancy
abstract: Former Mt. Lebanon Commissioner Dan Miller is running for the state House seat recently vacated by Matt Smith. Smith was recently elected to state Senate.

headline: Rick Santorum Looks For Win In Pa.
abstract: Although the Republican primary for president seems to be shifting in former Governor Mitt Romney's favor, PA's own Rick Santorum is still looking optimistic at his chances for a win in PA's primary come April 24. Mr. Santorum and his campaign are working hard in his home state, a primary that could be the fate of his entire campaign.

headline: Federal transportation funding leaves burden to state
abstract: A federal transportation program has appropriated almost $2 billion for PA state infrastructure improvements, a figure that still falls below the $3.5 billion in unmet transportation needs a state commission estimated in 2011. The state legislature is now in charge of bridging the funding gap, or finding alternatives to the infrastructure funding issue.

headline: Some legislators oppose Scranton's commuter tax
abstract: Rep. Sid Michaels Kavulich (D Taylor), said a commuter tax in Scranton would be akin to "taxation without representation." Other senators have stated their opposition to the new tax.

headline: Former Governors Share Their ‘Straightforward’ View Of The Republican Race
abstract: Two former Governor's of neighboring states, New Jersey and Pennsylvania, took jabs at the current Republican presidential race. Democratic Governors Ed Rendell and Christine Todd Whitman offered their perspectives on what they see as a sloppy and "shameful" race between several Republican hopefuls.

headline: Taxpayers charge that Easton Area School Board broke law, request transparency
abstract: The Easton, PA school board has been under scrutiny by some citizens after eliminating the jobs of over twenty people behind closed doors. A group of nine people signed a petition against the school board's actions, calling them unlawful. However, under the PA Sunshine Act, school boards are not required to publically discuss possible job terminations.

headline: Pa. ranks just after Texas in shale jobs
abstract: Pennsylvania's oil and gas workforce accounts for about 8 percent of all natural gas industry jobs in the nation. Development in this sector added $1.2 billion in state and local revenue in 2012. The study was funded by the American Petroleum Institute and America's Natural Gas Alliance among others.

headline: PA Republican Party Executive Director Discusses Santorum’s Decision
abstract: PA Republican Party Director Mike Barley discussed the decision of former PA Senator Rick Santorum to drop out of the presidential race as well as the overall process being taken by the Republican party to dismantle the Obama administration and his reelection campaign come November, 2012.

headline: Countywide initiative to fight blight could get under way
abstract: Housing issues in Altoona, PA has some considering the possibility of a commission created to combat abandoned properties and blighted houses using federal grant funds. Several neighboring counties have already began the process.

headline: Ex-Gov. Tom Ridge on gun control: 'It's a little more complicated than just bans and background checks'
abstract: Former PA Gov. Tom Ridge threw his support behind more protective gun control laws as people around the country react to a recent mass shooting at a Connecticut elementary school.

headline: Democratic race for PA Attorney General nomination heats up
abstract: The race for PA Attorney General is heating up in the Democratic primary. Lackawanna County, PA, prosecutor Kathleen Kane faces former U.S. House member Patrick Murphy. Both candidates have picked up key endorsements while the race remains close leading up to the April 24 primary date.

headline: Turnpike rates rising in 2013
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission approved a rate increase for all drivers paying cash on the state road beginning in 2013. The rate increase will generate the revenue necessary to complete their funding obligations, one Commission official stated.

headline: Corbett says mental illness the issue in Connecticut tragedy.
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett believes the answer to the recent spate of mass shootings is better funding for those dealing with mental illness.

headline: PA Lawmaker Proposes Two Year Moratorium on Deep Injection Wells
abstract: PA state Representative Bud George has introduced legislation that would stop the construction of Marcellus Shale natural gas wells for two years. The wells dispose of fracking water, a solution some environmentalists see as dangerous to water wells. Earthquakes have also been attributed to the fracking process.

headline: Recent rain did little to ease Western Pennsylvania dry spell, experts say
abstract: The region of western Pennsylvania is suffering through damaging dry spells that have depleted the river-water supplies and damaged crop growth. Rainfall in the area is over two inches below normal yearly levels, requiring the PA Department of Environmental Protection to issue a drought watch for 15 western PA counties.

headline: Corbett to honor victims in Connecticut school shooting.
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is holding a moment of silence in honor of a recent school shooting in Connecticut.

headline: 20-year incumbent to face challenge in November
abstract: 20-year Republican state representativeTim Hennessey will face a challenge from Democratic Spring City councilman Michael Hays in November.

headline: Corbett says no tax money should be spent on fine.
abstract: The fines levied by the NCAA on Penn State University following the Jerry Sandusky child-sex abuse trial should not be paid with taxpayer dollars, PA Governor Tom Corbett said. PSU's football team was given heavy sanctions, including fines of up to $60 million by the collegiate athletic association, following the conviction of Mr. Sandusky.

headline: State System chancellor resigns to take job in D.C.
abstract: John Cavanaugh, chancellor of the State System of Higher Education, is resigning to join the DC based Consortium of Universities of the Washington Metropolitan Area, a group that advocates for 14 institutions. In accordance with the system's succession plan executive vice chancellor Peter Garland will serve as acting chancellor.

headline: Slow drumbeat for transportation funding
abstract: Richard Geist, the veteran chairman of the House Transportation Committee added his voice Monday to a slow drumbeat of calls for legislative action to generate billions of dollars in new state transportation money.

headline: Corbett flaunts W.Pa. recreation
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett, along with other state officials, kayaked almost eight miles down the Conemaugh River in western PA. Gov. Corbett afterward boasted of the region's beauty, while explaining how important the preservation of natural resources is to his administration.

headline: $720M sale of Equitable Gas to Peoples Gas to form state’s largest gas utility
abstract: Peoples Natural Gas Co. will become the state's largest gas utility if regulators approve a $720 million deal to allow the company to acquire Equitable Gas Co. from Downtown-based EQT Corp.

headline: Transit ridership rises, thanks to young commuters and high gas prices
abstract: High gas prices and the changing habits of young people are driving a shift toward mass transit that could influence budget battles in Washington and state capitals.

headline: Protesters, courts, feds all get their say on PA’s new voter ID law
abstract: The controversial PA voter ID law brought many dissenters to the PA State Capitol to protest the passage of the law. The voter ID measure, which would require all registered voters to show some form of ID at the polls, is under review by the US Justice Department for its constitutionality, while some interest groups and Democratic legislators call the bill disenfranchising to minority voters.

headline: Corbett says banning assault weapons not the answer
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett comes out against calls to ban assault weapons.

headline: WPMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  FOX43 News at 11PM
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has expressed discontent over an ESPN article that suggests he played a key role in firing Joe Paterno.

headline: 271 Pittsburgh school workers await layoff vote
abstract: The Pittsburgh, PA, Public Schools board is expected to layoff over 270 professional employees in a vote tonight. The layoff, resulting from a lack of funding, is the largest since the school board's creation, a fact the board itself and the teachers' union is calling "sad."

headline: Allentown arena authority left to monitor its own spending
abstract: The oversight of hundreds of millions in state funds to redevelop downtown Allentown will fall almost entirely to the Allentown Neighborhood Improvement Zone Development Authority. The authority is a nine-member board appointed locally.

headline: Libertarians bringing in big names
abstract: The Libertarian Party of Pennsylvania will hold its state convention in the city this week featuring Gary Johnson, the party’s candidate for president, and Rupert Boneham, voted the fan favorite on the TV show “Survivor Pearl Islands.”

headline: Two charged in Gibbons robbery to face trial
abstract: The two men responsible for robbing PA state Representative Jaret Gibbons will face trial in Dauphin County. Rep. Gibbons, along with two aides were robbed and gunpoint. The perpetrators were arrested shortly after the incident.

headline: Op-ed: Gov. Corbett must lead the way on gun control
abstract: PA Gov. Corbett is called upon to end his support of the NRA and call for tougher gun laws in response to a recent shooting at an elementary school in Connecticut.

headline: Republicans Joe Eisenhauer, Tom Hawk challenge State Rep. RoseMarie Swanger for 102nd District seat
abstract: State Representative RoseMarie Swanger faces two GOP primary challengers in her bid for a fourth term in the 102nd state House District, based in Lebanon County. The two challengers are Joe Eisenhauer, 33, of Swatara Twp., a land and economic development consultant and lobbyist for Delta Development Group; and Tom Hawk, 65, a South Lebanon Twp. Resident who worked 33 years for the state Labor and Industry Department’s job training program.

headline: Melvin’s bench peer not required to testify
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Max Baer will not have to testify in the corruption trial of fellow Justice Jane Orie Melvin, after being subpoenaed by Orie Melvin's attorney. Justice Orie Melvin faces trial on charges related campaign work performed by her judicial staff.

headline: Penn State and NCAA at odds over fate of fines
abstract: PA lawmakers want $3 million per year in child-abuse prevention funds to be spent within Pennsylvania only. The NCAA levied these fines against Penn State University and intends on spending the money nationally.

headline: Residents question safety, oversight at meeting about natural gas compressor station explosion
abstract: State regulators and natural gas company officials faced nearly two hours of questions from residents about safety, air pollution and eroded public confidence during a briefing at Montrose Area High School about a recent natural gas compressor station explosion.

headline: Expired licenses muddle voter ID numbers
abstract: New data has emerged showing almost 1.6 million registered voters in Pennsylvania could be without proper identification following the passage of the voter ID law. The new law requires all voters to show proper identification at the voting booth. Opponents point to the data and the ID law as a form of suppression against the individual's voting rights.

headline: 2012 headlines dominated by partisan politics, tragedy
abstract: A review of the stories that made headlines in Pittsburgh in 2012.

headline: Veon sentencing pushed back to May.
abstract: The sentencing of former Pennsylvania state House Democratic whip Mike Veon for his second corruption conviction is being postponed.

headline: Several area schools on low-achieving list
abstract: Several secondary and elementary schools in central Pennsylvania were labeled as under-achieving by the state Department of Education, making several of their students eligible for a new tax credit program. The program allows low and moderate-income students from under-achieving schools to attend participating public and private schools in the area.

headline: Governor says 911th critical for U.S. defense
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett says that the 911th Airlift Wing is critical for US defense and urged its saving.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  CBS21 News at 11PM
abstract: Mitt Romney avoided social issues during a campaign stop in Lancaster County.

headline: Corbett says Penn State students bear 'brunt' of NCAA sanctions.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett commented on the sanctions placed on Penn State University and its football program by the National Collegiate Athletic Association. The sanctions, which range from $60 million in fines to loss of bowl-eligibility for four years, were placed on the University following the child-sex abuse trial and conviction of school employee Jerry Sandusky.

headline: So-called "elves" contemplate the "Scrooge Christmas" outlined by Obama
abstract: President Barack Obama visited the K'NEX plant in Hatfield, Montgomery County calling workers there “Santa’s extra elves.” He was there to encourage Congress to pass his plan extending tax cuts for most wage earners.

headline: Grassroots group seeks tax reform
abstract: About 50 people gathered on Wednesday to learn more about local tax rates at the Fairchance Fire Hall. The Fayette County Homeowners Action Committee seeks grassroots change to temper the tide of high taxes.

headline: State court knocks out key piece of gas drilling law
abstract: The PA Commonwealth Court struck down a provisional of the state's oil and gas drilling law, allowing municipalities within the state more zoning power over gas-well sights. The oil and gas law originally gave the state power over municipalities to accept gas-drilling operations, something the PA court found unconstitutional.

headline: Inquirer and Daily News headed for online paywall
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News and Inquirer are expected to start charging users for access to the newspaper's content.

headline: Campaign 2012/North: Three from GOP in 37th District primary
abstract: Three Republican candidates with similar opinions but vastly different backgrounds are seeking the 37th state Senate District seat of John Pippy from Moon, who is not seeking re-election.

headline: Professor says voter ID law will help GOP
abstract: The new PA voter ID law could potentially effect the presidential election outcome within the state, a professor in charge of studying the issue said. Most notably, the Republican party has the most to gain from the controversial law, which requires all registered voters to show proper identification at the voting booth.

headline: To fill skills gap, Corbett official suggests changing the status of those with skills
abstract: Secretary Alan Walker, head of the state’s Department of Economic and Community Development is looking for ways to train workers the skills needed to take the jobs that are in demand.

headline: It's about time
abstract: The author praises the proposal of a bill that would limit the school districts ability to levy property taxes.

headline: Red light cameras ... hey, not so fast!
abstract: Red- light cameras are an important factor of motorist safety, but the power can be abused by states seeking increased traffic-ticket revenue, this AAA executive writes. Giving examples from Philadelphia and New Jersey, the writer questions the motives behind PA's red-light camera expansion.

headline: Schools reviewing policies after Newtown shootings
abstract: After the recent school shooting in Connecticut state Department of Education officials here in the state sent a notice to all school districts to be aware of any suspicious behavior.

headline: Medicare saves $202 million in year with bids
abstract: A Medicare program piloted in Pittsburgh and eight other cities saved the government $202 million on medical equipment in its first year and will expand next year, federal officials said in a report.

headline: Watchdog calls for Penn State changes
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner called on the state legislature to take away school board-voting rights from Penn State University's president and Governor Tom Corbett following the scandal surrounding former University employee Jerry Sandusky. Sandusky was found guilty of child-sex abuse.

headline: Growing turnpike debt worrisome
abstract: The PA General Assembly passed and Gov. Ed Rendell signed into law Act 44 of 2007, a trasportation funding bill that requires annual payments of up to $1 billlion from the PA Turnpike Commission to the state. The money was to be raised by existing polls as well as turning I-80 into a toll road. The Federal government did not follow through on I-80 and the Commission became saddled with debt. Many are worried that the PA turnpikes toll increases will become too much for drivers and they might resort to using secondary roads causing congestion and accidents.

headline: Airport allocates state aid
abstract: Fayette County Airport Authority members decided to allocate the remaining $25,000 of a $200,000 grant from the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development to purchase equipment, upgrade its computer system and replace a roof.

headline: GUEST COLUMN: Repeal Voter ID law if it survives in court
abstract: PA State Representative Babette Josephs remarks on the rally to take place at the state Capitol to protest the new voter ID law. Rep. Josephs is currently working on legislation to repeal the law, which she finds to deprive the vote of thousands of people, mainly minorities.

headline: Noise from natural gas station startles neighbors
abstract: A natural gas dehydration station in Monroe Township had an emergency shutdown. PVR Partners who run the station explained the shutdown was due to a loose wire on one of the fire detectors triggering the emergency shutodwn and resulted in the large noise that neighbors heard. The station was part of a pipeline system that is brings natural gas from wells in northern Wyoming county area to the tranco interstate pipeline in Dallas Township, PA.

headline: Harrisburg ponders laws, not cash, to aid cities
abstract: PA State Senator Jane Earll wants to improve Act 111 of the 2011-12 legislative session. This bill is intended to help fiscally distressed cities like Scranton, but Earll thinks that its arbitration awards process and the inability to collect property taxes from land owned by charitable organizations to be "cost-drivers." Earll wants to change collective bargaining rights for city employees, and public charity law in order to help distressed cities.

headline: Revenue secretary visits Somerset
abstract: Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue Daniel Meuser said discussed the Department of Welfare's budget at the Somerset County Chamber of Commerce Eggs & Issues meeting at the Somerset Country Club.

headline: County jobless rate jumps in advance of PBS data
abstract: The unemployment rate of Somerset County, PA, rose a small percentage to 8.6 percent, the PA Department of Labor and Industry reported. The small jump in the rate puts Somerset County above the state and national unemployment rates, in part because of the layoff of 225 employees by a regional coal company.

headline: Governor, top brass see off combat unit at Fort Indiantown Gap
abstract: 1,500 members of the 55th Heavy Brigade Combat Team were honored at a parade field at Fort Indiantown Gap. Gov. Corbett, Maj. Gen. Wesley E. Craig, and PA's adjutant general were in attendence. The 55th Brigade is sending about half of its soldiers for three months of training at Camp Shelby, Miss., before they are deployed to Kuwait for nine months. Gov. Corbett is a former National Guardsman.

headline: Transparency part of true 'oversight'
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection identified a faulty gas well drilled by Cabot Oil and Gas Corporation, which caused methane to infiltrate at least three nearby wells. This was not reported to the public, however, until the Times Tribune asked about violations. The DEP violated its own policy. During this same time it signed off on Cabot's decision to stop delivering drinking water to some Susquehanna residents.

headline: What the L's going on? Jewel Williams foes crying foul
abstract: Chris Brennan describes the campaigns of Jewell and Jewel Williams for Philadelphia City Government.

headline: Air Force veteran testifies Pa. voter ID law could prevent him from casting ballot
abstract: Testifying in Commonwealth Court, an Air Force veteran said the new PA voter ID law could prevent him from voting because of his lack of a drivers' license. The law would require all registered voters to show proper identification at the polling place, but is being challenged in state court over its constitutional validity.

headline: Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett lauds Legislature for finding a funding source for state police cadet training
abstract: On September 1, 2012 a new law was enacted that forces larger municipalities covered by PA state police to give up their share of the traffic-fine revenue and divert that money to the training of new troopers. Gov. Corbett remarked that the new law will provide millions of dollars annually for new training programs without a tax increase.

headline: Small group insurance rates now to get state review
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has signed Act 133, which protects employees from sharp increases in group insurance rates. The bill subjects such rate hikes to review by the state's insurance department.

headline: State wants to export more Duquesne pupils
abstract: Seventh- and eighth-grade students from the Duquesne School District could attend either West Mifflin Area or East Allegheny schools if a plan approved Thursday by the state board of control overseeing the district is accepted by state Education Secretary Ron Tomalis.

headline: Witnesses, including chief clerk, describe Orie Melvin's campaign demands
abstract: A top aid to PA Supreme Court Justice Jane Orie Melvin, among other staffers, testified in the corruption trial against the Justice. Orie Melvin is charged with using her state-paid resources in her election campaigns.

headline: 'Convenience 2020' plan would put liquor stores closer to markets
abstract: State House Majority leader Mike Turzai, R-Allegheny has been pushing for the privatization of the state's wine and liquor sales. Out of this year's legislative hearings came a proposal dubbed "Convenience 2020", an eight-year initiative. The PA Liquor Control Board wants to move some of its stores next to supermarkerts and team up with grocery stores where beer is sold. The LCB has placed wine and spirits outlets inside three supermarkets in western PA to test the initiative.

headline: Loan to Russian steel-maker canceled
abstract: The Russian steel company Severstal will not receive a $730 million federal loan as expected. The US Department of Energy stopped the company's plan to develop a high-strength automotive steel with the loan. PA US Senator Pat Toomey worked against the plan, stating that we should put US companies like US Steel first.

headline: Clout: Other players in city casino game?
abstract: Another casino may be built in Philadelphia.

headline: Health advocates note approaching deadlines for state insurance exchange
abstract: Some health-related interest groups are worried over the state's handling of the federal Affordable Care Act. Deadlines for implementing  key features of the measure are approaching, with little movement from the state government to implement them.

headline: District court dismisses lawsuit challenging "Year of the Bible"
abstract: U.S. District Judge Christopher Conner granted the PA House Republicans' motion to dismiss the lawsuit from the Freedom From Religion Foundation claiming he was bound by legislative immunity. The athiest group had challenged the legislature's resolution declaring 2012 the "Year of the Bible". Conner issued a strong rebuke of the Republican's legislature's action saying that this case pushed the "Establishment Clause envelope behind the safety glass of legislative immunity". He said that the resolution was at its worst, premeditated pandering designed to provide a reelection sound bite for use by members of the General Assembly.

headline: Should Democrats dump Obama? Specter says yes, maybe no
abstract: The author asks the reader whether US President Obama should choose Hillary Rodham Clinton to be his running mate instead of current US Vice President Joe Biden. Former US Senator Arlen Specter asked this question, but suggested that perhaps Obama be the one who should go.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  10PM NEWS
abstract: Cuts to the budget of the Allentown school district has led to lay-offs and half-day kindergarten.

headline: Top Pa. elections official admits not knowing voter ID law
abstract: The PA Secretary of the Commonwealth, an important state election official, acknowledged the fact that she was unfamiliar with the new voter ID law. The Secretary conceded her lack of knowledge to attorneys challenging the measure, which would require all voters to present a valid form of identification.

headline: Redrawn 12th District draws outside interest
abstract: The election in the 12th District of Western PA is between U.S. Rep Mark Critz D-Johnstown and Republican challanger Keith Rothfus, a lawyer from Sewickley. Critz is campaigning for his fourth election in two and half years since former Rep. John Murtha died in 2010. Rothfus is running for the second time after narrowly losing to Rep. Jason Altmire in 2010. The 12th district was drawn so that it would be difficult for a Democrat to win, John McCain received more votes than Barak Obama in 2008. Outside money is also a factor with the National Republican Congressional Committee and others supporting Rothfus. It looks to be a tight race.

headline: Targeting (another) Orie: State of Corruption?
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin is the target of an Allegheny County grand jury investigation. In 2009 Janine Melvin, a relative, was charged with politicking on the taxpayers dollar. In 2010 her sister Senator Jane Orie was charged with public corruption as well.

headline: Holden can’t hang on to seat
abstract: Matt Cartwright, a 50-year-old attorney from Moosic, defeated 20-year incumbent U.S. Representative Tim Holden, according to unofficial Democratic primary results for the 17th Congressional District

headline: Pennsylvania Lottery sees record year in sales
abstract: The 2011-2012 fiscal year was the most profitable year in the history of the Pennsylvania Lottery. Net revenue increased by almost 9 percent over the previous high mark, in 2005-2006.

headline: Court sets voter-ID law aside for November elections
abstract: Judge Robert E. Simpson Jr. upheld the voter-ID-law but blocked it from taking full effect in the Nov. 6, 2012 election. There will be a soft roll out in the April primary in which voters will be asked but not required for identification. Critics of the law were happy with the decision but worried about future implementation of the law. They are also worried about voter confusion if the state continues its aggressive education campaign on the voter-ID law. In his ruling Judge Simpson said that he did not have a problem with asking voters for identification but that voter's might not be able to obtain the necessary ID in time after casting a provisional ballot and would result in voter disenfranchisement.

headline: 5PM News: Asset test for food stamp recipients?
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has signed legislation that will implement asset testing for food stamp recipients. Those with a certain amount of assets will no longer be eligible for food stamps.

headline: DeWeese to serve up to 5 years for Bonusgate
abstract: Former House Democratic leader Bill DeWeese was sentenced today to 2-1/2 to 5 years in prison for theft and other political corruption charges stemming from the wide-ranging Bonusgate investigation in the Capitol.

headline: New Southeastern Vets Center facility opens
abstract: A new facility at the Southeastern Veterans Center has been built to house veterans suffering from dementia and other related illnesses. PA Governor Tom Corbett was the keynote speaker at the opening of the facility, which serves veterans in Chester and Montgomery counties.

headline: 'Everyone should have an ID anyway': Linglestown woman trudges through the rain to get her state ID
abstract: A local woman from Linglestown, Bonnie Koppenheffer, made a trip to Harrisburg to secure her state photo ID just in case it is needed for the upcoming election. Governor Tom Corbett answered questions on the voter-ID-law. Many voters who attempt to get their photo-ID's have complained about long waits at DMV's in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: GOP poll shows support for Fee
abstract: Mindy Fee recently beat out Stephen Black in a straw poll taken by committee members in the 37th Legislative District. PA Representative Tom Creighton is retiring. This district was recently redrawn.

headline: Rally to protest Pa. immigration bills
abstract: As the U.S. Supreme Court hears arguments Wednesday on Arizona's controversial immigration law, local advocate group Juntos are organizing a bus trip to Harrisburg to protest the package of bills championed by state Representative Daryl Metcalfe, an ardent foe of illegal immigration.

headline: Professor testifies voter fraud rare
abstract: A Rutgers University professor testified in the PA voter ID law hearings, stating voter fraud rarely happened. The testimony in the Commonwealth Court was part of an effort to delay the implementation of the law until after the 2012 elections. The PA voter ID law would require all voters to present some form of state-allowed ID at the voting booths.

headline: Pa. voter ID ruling was reprieve, but laws still lacking
abstract: Even with Commonwealth Court Judge Robert Simpson's ruling that put an end to the implemenation of the voter-ID-law this upcoming election, PA is still among five states with the most stringent voter requirements. According to analysis from the National Conference of State legislatures, PA is the most populous state that has not legalized voting measures other states have adopted such as online voter registration or election-day registraion, early voting and no-excuse absentee balloting. Republicans and Gov. Corbett were disapointed with Judge Simpson's ruling.

headline: Justice Joan Orie Melvin urged to depart in probe
abstract: The call for Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie to step down from the bench has grown more complicated. Her presence gave Republicans a 4-3 advantage. The PA Legislature's redistricting plan has been appealed and some feel like her absence would result in an unprecedented tie. Some political scientists feel that this would not necessarily be the outcome depending on the merits of the case.

headline: Sen. Pat Vance wins party nomination
abstract: State Sen. Pat Vance fought off her first Republican challenger in decades to secure a primary election win. The win all but ensures she will retain her seat representing the 31st district since there is no Democrat in the race.

headline: Luzerne doctor sues over bans in new fracking law
abstract: A northeastern PA doctor has sued the state of Pennsylvania in relation to confidentiality requirements in the natural gas drilling law. The law does not require gas-drilling companies to disclose chemicals used in the fracking method, concerning some doctors on the health risks related to those chemicals.

headline: Allegheny County left with animal control void
abstract: Triangle Pet Control Services, an animal control company and kennel provider in McKees Rocks that serves dozens of Allegheny County municipalities has been suspended for violating state dog law by failing to maintain records and sanitary conditions. The owner of the kennel pleaded guilty last month to violations whch included "excess feces in kennel".

headline: 5PM News: PSEA says invest during recession, not cut
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association says that Governor Tom Corbett needs to invest in education during a recession and not cut funding. They also suggested seeking revenue from the taxation of Marcellus Shale.

headline: Critics: PA failing to enforce puppy mill law
abstract: The state office that regulates Pennsylvania's dog-breeding industry is running out of money, has been slow to enforce new regulations meant to improve the lives of tens of thousands of kennel dogs, and faces charges that it's once again going easy on operators of so-called "puppy mills."

headline: 2 Delco DPW caseworkers charged with theft of funds
abstract: Two PA Department of Public Welfare employees have been charged with stealing around $300,000 from state funds. The two schemes, which were done separately, involved fake accounts where state assistance money was then wired. PA Attorney General Linda Kelly expects more arrests to occur in the case.

headline: Temporary Voter Relief in Pennsylvania
abstract: Judge Robert Simpson provided temporary relief to the democratic process in PA by ruling that voters would be able to cast ballots in the next election without identifcation cards. Judge Simpson noted that there wasn't enough time before the Nov. 6 election to ensure no one would be disenfranchised by the law but he had no problem with voters needing to provide identification in the future. He also refused to stop election officials from asking for ID cards at the polls which could lead to voter confusion.

headline: Chester Upland teachers do more than educate
abstract: The author decries the reckless spending cuts to Pennsylvania schools seen in last years budget. He then applauds the teachers from Chester Upland who have stayed on the job despite the district's inability to pay their salaries. The author's faith in public education has been renewed.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  CBS21 News at 11PM
abstract: Business owner Tom Smith won the Republican nomination to face Bob Casey in PA's Senate race

headline: Size of voter ID budget debated
abstract: The $1 million budget for the implementation of the PA voter ID law has come under debate in the PA General Assembly. With differing estimates on the exact number of registered voters without proper identification, several interest groups and Democratic lawmakers see the appropriation as lacking.

headline: Huge income gap between Tom Smith and Bob Casey in past years
abstract: PA Senate canditate Republican Tom Smith and incumbent Democratic Senator Bob Casey are extremely mismatched in terms of personal finances. Smith has a total income of almost $22 million in 2010 after he sold his major coal-mining business according to federal tax returns he has released to the Inquirer. Currently Smith has a much smalller income but he still receives returns form mines near his home in western PA. Casey is paid $174,000 yearly in Senate salary and reported $171,000 in total income last year. Smith proposes a single flat-rate tax to be paid by all Americans. Casey has said that the tax code needs to be made simpler and fairer.

headline: York County businessman announces bid for state Sen. Jeffrey Piccola's Senate seat
abstract: Businessman Steve Johnson announced his candidacy Monday for the Republican nomination for the 15th PA State Senate District. Don O’Shell announced he was running for the same nomination. He is the York County Clerk of Courts. A number of other candidates are running for the seat.

headline: Voter trends, labor support enabled Critz to oust Altmire
abstract: Timothy McNulty describes the race between Jason Altmire and Mark Critz for U.S. Representative.

headline: School review shows conflicts
abstract: The Pennsylvania School Boards Association released a statement calling new student achievement standards within the state as "conflicting." The PSBA found that a quarter of state schools labeled under achieving by the state in 2011-2012, actually met 2010-2011 state achievement standards. The conflict has to come to pass in part because of a new business tax credit that incentives businesses to invest in under-performing schools.

headline: Keep pushing for more flood relief
abstract: Lycoming County has recently received $13 million in flood recovery funding for Hurricane Irene and Tropical Storm Lee. The funding will go toward the $52 million in storm damage that this district suffered. About half of the funding will go to replacing a bridge.

headline: Campaign 2012: 45th District / Kotik prevails in challenge
abstract: Nick Kotik, D-Robinson, who a few months ago feared his job was being eliminated because of redistricting, was elated Tuesday night that he won the Democratic nomination for the 45th District.

headline: In politics, irony isn't all that it's cracked up to be
abstract: In this letter, the writer examines wayward politics in PA today. He emphasizes a visit to an oil site by the PA Governor and the "flip-flopping" of Democratic state Senator.

headline: State Parks Director John Norbeck stepping down; advocates fear drillers at the gate
abstract: The head of PA State Parks, John Norbeck is stepping down. Under his tenure PA state parks won national awards for being the best managed park system in the US. Environmentalists fear that Norbeck's departure could be a sign that the Corbett administration is preparing to open the parks for natural gas drilling. Last month Paulette Viola from Citizens Advisory Council resigned after claiming that changes under the Corbett administration made it impossible for the council to function effectively and independently. A spokesperson for Gov. Corbett has denied any connection between Norbeck's resignation and natural resource development on state land and the current moratorium for additional leases of state land.

headline: 6PM News: Governor helps kick off MLK Day of Service
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett and Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson were both at a convention on Martin Luther King day to encourage others to devote themselves to service. Children were encouraged to participate.

headline: State, local governments need to plug in
abstract: The author calls for state and local governments to utilize technology to increase govenrment efficiency.

headline: Republican Rep. Vulakovich, Democrat primary challenger Brown vie for Orie seat.
abstract: Two candidates are running to fill the vacant seat of PA state Senator Jane Orie after Orie stepped down due to corruption charges.

headline: Measure to return police helicopter to airport fails
abstract: A state police aviation unit will not be returning to the Williamsport Regional airport due to a PA State House vote that rejected State Rep. Rick Mirabito's bid. Mirabito has said he will continue to fight to return the helicopter which has been relocated to Hazelton.

headline: John Baer: Imagine, representatives truly representing
abstract: The author describes an idea to get PA politicians to do what voters want. It comes from Majority Party PA, a political action committee. They want to utilize public-integrity polling, which would record voter's views on a number of key issues. Politicians could pledge to uphold the findings of the polling and it would be up to voters to hold them accountable.

headline: In rare move, Pennsylvania Supreme Court orders live broadcast of redistricting hearing
abstract: The PA Supreme Court has allowed the hearings on the state legislative redistricting plans to be broadcasted on television. For only the second time in the Supreme Court's history will their proceedings be viewed live, the first being a previous redistricting hearing.

headline: Considering implications of judge's suggested narrow injunction
abstract: Legal experts believe that the injunction of the voter-ID-law that now requires those without proper ID to vote provisionally, could prove chaotic. An attorney in the Republican national lawyers Association said that counting provisional ballots is not an easy job and lawyers will be present to monitor the counting of ballots.

headline: Corbett coddles the rich and gas companies while making life more difficult for the poor
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is behind a plan to enact a food stamp asset test. Under the plan people under 60 with more than $2,000 in savings or other assets and individuals over 60 with $3,250 or more would lose aid. The author feels that the administration does not care about the elderly and the poor. The PA Department of Public Welfare recently received an award from the federal government for the efficient administration of the food stamp program.

headline: Former Harrisburg Receiver David Unkovic hires lawyer, enters appearance in Commonwealth Court
abstract: Former Harrisburg Receiver David Unkovic has acquired an attorney and filed an entry of appearance in Commonwealth Court, but no hearing calling Unkovic to testify has been set. Unkovic abruptly resigned March 30, saying in a handwritten resignation letter to the court that he found himself "in an untenable position in the political and ethical crosswinds," and that he could no longer achieve a solution. Two days before he quit, Unkovic called an impromptu press conference asking for a federal and state investigation of the city's incinerator retrofit project that all but bankrupted Harrisburg.

headline: Scranton Council pursues hedge fund financing
abstract: The Scranton, PA, City Council is in the beginning stages of borrowing close to $20 million from a hedge fund in order to cover massive budget shortfalls for the upcoming fiscal year. The action has come after months of failed planning to create a sustainable map to bridge the budget gap. Several hedge fund firms are vying for the financial position, including funds from Harrisburg and Wall Street.

headline: Property tax elimination plan needs re-tooling, says IFO
abstract: Rep. Jim Cox (R-Berks) has a plan to phase out school property taxes and raise higher tax rates on personal income and purchases. A report by PA Independent Fiscal Office believes that schools woud lose between one and two billion dollars under the plan. Cox has responded that there just needs to be an increase in the personal income tax (PIT) to fill any gap possibly from 3.07% to 4.01%. The IFO report finds that this PIT increase and state sales tax increase would relieve 37% from retired homewoners taxes and raise 10% on working renters.

headline: Should pet euthanasia be by guns?
abstract: The PA General Assembly is set to vote on a Senate Bill 1329 requires that dogs and cats by euthanized by means of barbiturates, but leaves the door open for the shooting of dogs and cats. This has some animal rights advocates up in arms. The author does not feel that animals have rights commensurate with human rights and that killing an animal with a well-aimed bullet can be just as humane.

newspaper: WPGH Pittsburgh (Channel 11 News on FOX 53) FOX
headline: WPGH-FOX  Pittsburgh, PA  10 PM News
abstract: A ceremony was held for students killed in a Somerset County bus crash.

headline: Vulakovich wins Senate seat
abstract: Republican state Representative Randy Vulakovich won the vacated 40th district Senate seat of Jane Orie in a special election. Former Senator Orie was convicted of corruption charges stemming from election work done on state time and stepped down.

headline: John Baer: House Democrats use Sandusky to pursue meaningless swipe at Corbett
abstract: The columnist believes that the Democratic caucus is using the Sandusky case to attack Gov. Corbett. He says they are pusing a meaningless nonbinding House Resolution that calls upon the U.S. attorney general to appoint a special counsel to investigate Gov. Corbett's handling of the Sandusky case.

headline: Dredging doubts grow deeper
abstract: Congress has declared a moratorium on earmarks in order to make sure that projects were based on merit instead of political muscle. As part of this Congress' independent investigative arm, the Government Accountability Office has questioned the economic benefit of the deepening of the Delaware River.

headline: McGinnis: Debate decision cost Geist
abstract: John McGinnis said he couldn't wait to debate with incumbent Rick Geist during their campaign for the Republican nomination for the State House. To his disappointment, Geist declined to engage. The author suggests that this hurt Geist's campaign.

headline: PA high court fast tracks juvenile lifer appeals.
abstract: Pennsylvania's Supreme Court has begun to hear appeals from state inmates pertaining to the US Supreme Court ruling that mandatory life sentences without parole is unconstitutional for juveniles. Currently there are 373 people in state correction facilities who fall under this ruling.

headline: Education funding: Charter school reforms are a must
abstract: Today in PA, about 6% or 105,000 students recieve their education through charter schooling. However the charter school system needs reform. There needs to be an independent authorizer that approves charter schools and moniters the closing of low-performing schools which is currently done by public schools. There needs to be a continuation of studies on equitibiltiy issues, such as special education. State Auditor General Jack Wagner has recommended that the state could save millions of dollars by setting different rates of funding for brick-and-mortar schools and another for Internet-based cyber charters and limiting the payment to the national average.

headline: FOX29 NEWS AT 10: Drunk driving case heads back to court
abstract: PA Representative Sharell Parker's court case is heading back to court because it was uncovered that Parker and the judge were friends on each others Facebook accounts. The judge should have recused himself because of the potential conflict of interest.

headline: Port Authority Board Approves Cuts To Service
abstract: The Port Authority Board of Directors today voted to cut routes and raise fares once again. The cuts are part of an effort to balance a budget with a $64 million hole.

headline: Jim Foster can run against U.S. Rep. Chaka Fattah, Commonwealth Court rules
abstract: The PA Commonwealth Court ruled in favor of a Philadelphia man looking to challenge US Representative Chaka Fatta as an independent. Although the man in question, Jim Foster, is unable to run as an independent per state election guidelines, he may be able to run under the Independent Party.

headline: Pa. Turnpike CEO quitting due to health reasons
abstract: Roger Nutt, chief executve officer of the PA Turkpike Commission is leaving his post due to health issues. During Nutt's one-year tenure his accomplishments included updating the comission's process for contracting professional services and expanding its capital improvements program. Nutt is the father of Gov. Tom Corbett's campaign manager and political advisor, Brian Nutt. Nutt had 28 years of service in New Jersey Transportation agencies. The PA Turnpike Commission has faced a state grand jury investigation since 2009 regarding its employment and procurement practices, it also has a growing debt burden.

headline: Money from state approved for Chester-Upland
abstract: PA Senator Pileggi is asking PA Governor Tom Corbett to give money to Chester-Upland, a struggling school district. Many teachers are staying on the job although the district cannot afford to pay for them.

headline: Pa. Auditor General Renews Call For Repair of State’s Rotting Infrastructure
abstract: Pennsylvania auditor general Jack Wagner made a stop under one of Philadelphia’s more heavily traveled bridges to demonstrate the sad state that thousands of bridges across the state are now in.

headline: Public meetings on cracker plant scheduled
abstract: A ethane cracker plant planned to be built in Beaver County, PA, by Shell Oil Company will be the focus of a public discussion in Potter Township. The exact operations performed at the proposed plant will be discussed, as well as will be the environmental and economical impacts to the county and township.

headline: House Majority Leader Eric Cantor campaigns for Republican Scott Perry
abstract: U.S. House Majority leader Eric Cantor has been campaigning for GOP House canditates all over the country including for PA GOP challengers Keith Rothfus in the 12th congressional district and Scott Perry in the 19th congressional district. Cantor praised Gov. Romney's first presidential debate performance and was confident that Rep. Paul would succeed in his upcoming debate with Vice President Biden. Cantor chided the President for fomenting partisan disagreement in Washington and reiterated his position agaisnt any new tax increases in this tough economy.

headline: Altmire breaks with party on debt vote
abstract: PA US Congressman Jason Altmire voted with the Republicans on a resolution against increasing the US debt ceiling. Democratic National Committee Chairwoman Debbie Wasserman Schultz called this resolution a "political stunt." House Minority Whip Steny Hoyer said that this is just a ploy by Republicans to show that they are opposed to the debt ceiling although it is ensured in previous legislation.

headline: Santorum Hints At Romney Endorsement
abstract: Former Republican presidential candidate Rick Santorum says he expects to endorse Mitt Romney. Santorum says that he believes Romney is “the right guy” to challenge President Barack Obama. Still, he’s stopping short of an official endorsement of his former rival.

headline: 2 Pennsylvanians have West Nile virus, DEP says
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection confirmed the second case of the West Nile Virus in the state. The second occurrence happened in Franklin County where a woman was hospitalized from contracting meningitis due to the virus. Higher numbers of mosquitos carrying the virus have been confirmed in the state for this year, most likely due to the milder winter.

headline: Judge rules Libertarians can stay on PA ballot.
abstract: A PA commonwealth judge has allowed for the Libertarian party to stay on the PA ballot. Canditates for President and three statewide offices are now on the ballot. The judge confirmed that the Libertarians had collected 20,740 valid signatures or 129 more than the law requires for third-party canditates running state-wide. A review of the signatures had invalidated over 50%. The Green Party also had the same signature requirement but suceeded in getting its canditates on the ballot without any challenges.

headline: Marcellus Shale well safety bill heads to governor's desk
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett will soon see a bill sponsored by PA Senator Lisa Baker, which requires operators of new and existing wells to provide sophisticated citing information to emergency responders and develop response plans to deal with accidents and spills. Baker said that the PA Department of Environmental Protection will be directed to write regulations on an emergency basis to implement the bill.

headline: SPECIAL REPORT: Pennsylvania’s New Voter ID Card Law
abstract: Pennsylvania’s new voter ID law requires that, beginning in November of 2012, all voters present a photo ID every time they vote.

headline: Stilp seeks Barletta debates
abstract: Democratic candidate for the 11th US Congressional District Gene Stilp has challenged Republican incumbent Lou Barletta to a series of debates in each county the 11th District lies. The two have yet to confirm on a date or location of the first debate.

headline: Marcellus shale driller settles with Beaver landowners
abstract: Chesapeake Energy Corp. and eighteen Beaver County landowners settled two lawsuits over the company's development of Marcellus shale gas wells on their properties. The landowners claimed the company didn’t have valid mineral leases to the gas beneath their properties and the company sued to gain access to the properties so they could begin drilling.

headline: Pa. casinos' gaming revenue jumps to $3B
abstract: Casinos are now a $3 billion industry in PA. Not only has there been an increase in the number of places to play games, but the types of games have increased and the number of people who regularly play is higher.

headline: Romney In Philly To Address Tri-State Tax Day Tea Summit
abstract: Presumed Republican Presidential Nominee Mitt Romney was in Philadelphia Monday night to address the Tri-State Tax Day Tea Summit held at the Franklin Institute.

headline: Gov. Corbett hears it from all sides on Sandusky investigation
abstract: Sources from the PA government, the press, and interest groups have questioned the actions of PA Governor Tom Corbett pertaining to the Jerry Sandusky child sex-abuse scandal. Those sources fear politics or lack of resources led then-Attorney General Corbett in reacting properly to the issue.

headline: Officials, transportation leaders stress the need for more funding
abstract: Bridges in Lackawanna County are extremely structurally deficient at a rate of 21 percent of bridges which is 13 percent higher than the national average. 223 out of 415 segment-miles of roads are in poor condition according to the International Roughness Index. Local elected officials and transportation leaders joined together to press the need for Gov. Corbett to include funding options recommended by the state Transportation Advisory committee into next year's budget. Recommendations from a 69-page report include uncapping the Oil Company Franchise Tax over five years and increase vehicle and drive fees to match inflation-rate 3 percent going forward which combined would save close to $2 billion annualy.

headline: 6PM News: Lawmaker wants to expand voters’ voice on debt issues
abstract: A bill from PA State Representative Simmons has gained House approval. The lawmaker wants to expand voters' voice on debt issues. He wants a ballot measure for citizens to decided whether they want a debt increase.

headline: PA taxpayers could pitch in $30 million in Delaware County refinery deal.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett announced his administration's decision to commit a grant to Delta Air Lines in their attempt to buy an oil refinery in Delaware County, PA. The taxpayer-paid grant is worth up to $30 million and requires Delta to keep a certain amount of full-time workers at the refinery while also investing a considerable amount into the acquisition itself.

headline: 'EITC 2.0' hurts public schools
abstract: In this opinion piece, the writer is critical of the PA legislature's new business tax credit plan, formed to help children in underachieving public schools afford private education. The tax credit program is priced at $50 million, while public schools across the state have been forced to make dangerous cuts to their operating budget this past year.

headline: PA tattoo parlor health dangers cited by state auditor general
abstract: Out of the ten most populous states, PA is the only one to not regulate licensing for tatoo parlors. Practictioners in the state are not required to have training or certifications and their establishments are not inspected for health and safety. State Auditor Jack Wagner has released a report that says regulation is essential for preventing health risks such as Hepatitis C.

headline: GOP Senate candidates debate issues
abstract: At a debate sponsored by a conservative organization in Doylestown, attended by PA Representative Sam Rohrer and a number of other politically involved people, the future was discussed. If the five people in attendance had their way in the US Senate, several federal departments would close, a flat tax would replace the current income tax, the Affordable Care Act and the Patriot Act would be repealed, and steps would be taken to end abortion.

headline: Probe of gaming regulation reaches Valley View Downs project
abstract: A Pittsburgh, PA, grand jury examining issues with state regulation of the gaming industry has uncovered some contractual discrepancies between racetrack ownerships and horseman's groups.

headline: Federal officials tour flooding sites in Wyoming County
abstract: Officials from the US Department of Agriculture's Natural Resource Conservation Service visited areas in central PA damaged heavily by Tropical Storm Lee and Hurricane Irene. While surveying the damage, the federal officials visited with storm victims who expressed gratitude for the resources given to the area following the storm and massive floodings.

headline: Go big on transportation
abstract: The PA Turnpike Comission is $7 billion in debt after spending on highway projects. They believed that a new toll on Interstate 80 would bring in billion's of revenue but this idea was rejected by federal regulators three times. With the resignation of Turnpike Chief Executie Roger Nutt the PA Legislature should consolidate the Turnpike Commission and PennDOT into one department. Gov. Corbett should also decide on which recommendatinos he will implement from the advisory board which would increase costs on motorists for registration, licenses and fuel. Gov. Corbett needs to make transportation a priority in his next budget.

headline: Penn State trustees hope to address alumni concerns.
