abstract: The Penn State board of trustees has not met since Jerry Sandusky was charged with the sex abuse scandal and Hall of Fame coach Joe Paterno was ousted. They have recently met and wish to put all of this behind them. The trustees are hoping to make changes in their governance and administration to create transparency.

headline: Revenue from sales tax comes in under Pennsylvania's estimate
abstract: Revenue for a new tax inserted in PA has fallen below its original estimation. Taxpayers in PA are expected to report and pay taxes on items bought online or through catalogs. The collected amount from the tax was close to $2 million below the original estimate.

headline: Pennsylvania's online shoppers soon will have to pay sales tax
abstract: No longer will online purchases be exempt from state sales tax in PA following legislation passed in the PA General Assembly. It is estimated the state loses out on close to $400 million in tax revenue without enforcement of the internet sales tax.

headline: End of oversight to offer lift
abstract: Pittsburgh might be released from state financial oversight which would be good for the city and Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's re-election aspirations. The Act 47 recovery team a state-appointed overseer recommends giving Pittsburgh its financial independence. In a letter to the state Department of Community and Economic Development, Act 47 coordinators said the city still has challenges such as $1.5 billion in employee legacy costs but the city has cut debt by more than $300 million since oversight began in 2004. The city's bond rating has risen from junk status in 2003 to much better ratings. Many local economic interest groups agree that financial independence is good for the city.

headline: 7PM News: Perry to run for Congress
abstract: PA Representative Scott Perry has announced that he is running for the 4th Congressional district (PA).

headline: Are ultrasound and other bills a way to divert attention from economy?
abstract: President Obama has been charged by some critics of diverting the voter attention from what is most important, the health and state of the economy, by commenting negatively on the PA ultrasound bill that is backed by Gov. Tom Corbett. The ultrasound bill would require all women to see an image of the child before choosing abortion measures.

headline: New law to ban electronics from trash
abstract: Following state regulations under the Covered Device Recycling Act, consumers will be unable to dispose of old electronics through the trash or recycling. Per regulations, the items themselves must be delivered to special recycling centers in counties throughout the state. The new law is supposed to help curb harmful chemicals finding their way into landfills, while also cashing in on valuable metals and substances found in older electronics.

headline: Four tussle for Pennsylvania House seats in 2 districts
abstract: Democrat Erin Molchany is facing off against Republican challenger Chris Cratsley and Democrat incumbent Adam Ravenstahl is facing off against Jim Barr in the 20th district. Cratsley is not running as a typical Republican, avoiding calls for privatization and budget cuts, but he is against abortion with some exceptions. Molchany suppports marriage equality, opposes restrictions on abortions, and opposes vouchers for private school education. Ravenstahl, brother of the current Pittsburgh mayor, has voted agaisnt voter identification, school cuts and a bill that taxed the gas industry too lightly. Barr is in favor of eliminating property taxes to pay for schools and privatization of the state liqour stores.

headline: Washington County commissioner joins congressional race
abstract: Washington County Commissioner Larry Maggi announced recently that he plans to run for Congress in PA's 18th Congressional District, which is currently held by U.S. Rep. Tim Murphy. Mr. Maggi said that Washington County was third in job creation in the nation in 2010.

headline: Ruling 'game-changer' for nonprofit tax status
abstract: A recent PA Supreme Court ruling could change the norm of non-profit organization tax exemption status. A public charity in PA has to follow strict statutory guidelines, something a small, Jewish summer camp in Pike County, PA did not do, drawing suit from the local municipality looking to receive taxable revenue. The Court ruled in the favor of the municipality.

headline: Transit union approves contracts saving $60 million
abstract: The Port Authority of Allegheny County, PA, and the county's largest labor union approved transit worker contracts that saves the Authority $60 million over four years. The new agreements followed proposed layoffs and service cuts stemming from the Authority's fiscal situation.

headline: Plymouth Twp. officer's killing renews pressure on straw-buyer gun bill
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee has scheduled a meeting to review a measure that would impose a five-year mandatory minimum sentence on straw buyers of guns, legally purchased guns sold illegally to felons. A bill had been passed in the state House overwhelmingly last year but had been stalled in the state Senate. The killing of a Plymouth Township Police Officer has spurred the legislature to action.

headline: New bill could make drivers give bicycles 4-foot berth
abstract: A new law could be a major win for cyclists. It would allow people to swerve over the double lines while driving to avoid hitting bikers. It would require drivers to give at least four feet of room to bikers. This would make PA the 16th state to pass biker safety laws. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl is promoting the bill.

headline: AVI and ABC’s Interlinked
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council along with their Mayor, Michael Nutter, is looking to fix the real estate-tax disparity using the Actual Value Initiative, taxing real estate on their current market value. The proposal would bring in an estimate of $92 million for city schools.

headline: Corbett aide rebukes U.S. Department of Justice over voter ID.
abstract: The office of PA Governor Tom Corbett is questioning the motives of the US Department of Justice over their investigation into PA's new voter ID law. The US DOJ is questioning the constitutionality of the law that would require all voters to show a state-verified form of identification, while state courts have upheld the statute's constitutionality.

headline: Critz defending western PA congressional seat yet again.
abstract: U.S. Rep. Mark Critz who took over the 12th district seat of John Murtha, the deceased popular Democratic Rep. in 2010 is being challenged by Keith Rothfus who has strong national GOP and conservative group's financial backing. This western PA district tends to vote Republican despite containing a slim majority of registered Democrats. Critz's ads stress his more conservative beliefs, NRA endorsement, pro-military views, and anti-abortion stance. Rothfus has argued that Critz received a 60 percent rating from the National Right to Life Group. The 12th district has been recently gerrymandered by Republican-controlled redistricting making this district a very tough win for any Democrat.

headline: Pa. dog-protection fund may be broke by 2013
abstract: The Dog Law Restricted Account may run out of money in 2013. It began in 2007 with $14 million and provided many vital services related to animal welfare. The fund employs about 90 people within the Department of Agriculture.

headline: Audit of Pa. Legislature reveals questionable expenditures and a $183.5 million nest egg for the House and Senate
abstract: An independent audit of the PA General Assembly found a large safety net in place to the tune of $183 million. The nest egg would be used in the event of a budget impasse in order to keep the General Assembly independent.

headline: Corbett administration rips feds over voter-law request
abstract: The office of PA Governor Tom Corbett issued a statement challenging the request of the US Department of Justice in information dealing with the state's new voter ID law. The US DOJ requested information from the state in order to make sure the new statute followed guidelines of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, an action the Corbett administration perceived as political.

headline: For now, charter approval isn't a Pennsylvania GOP priority
abstract: PA State Republican leaders and the Governor's office have agreed to set aside a statewide authorizer of charter schools that would make it easier for them to form, in an attempt to push through an agreement on regulatory changes. Those changes include forming a commission to examine funding, mandating annual independent audits and requiring the state to directly pay for charter schools, unless the schools opt to continue collecting from their sending districts.

headline: PA Senate OKs bill to extend jobless benefits.
abstract: A bill ensuring that residents qualifying for 13 weeks of federally paid jobless benefits has the approval of state senators. The PA Labor and Industry Department stated that these benefits are only for private-sector employees.

headline: Asset test for food stamps takes effect
abstract: Asset testing for food stamp recipients has taken effect in PA. Food stamps will be distributed based on a numerical value of a recipient's assets, something Republicans say will root out fraud and abuse while Democrats argue it harms the poorest in our society.

headline: County highlights radon detector offer from DEP
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection issued a $75,000 grant to the American Lung Association that would give radon gas detectors to at-risk homes in central PA. With the radon detectors, residents would be equipped to combat the dangers associated with radon poisoning, the DEP stated.

headline: Experience counts: Markosek is the better choice in the 25th District
abstract: In PA State House District 25, Joe Markosek (D) is facing off agianst Mike Doyle (R). Markosek is the thirty year incumbent and once chairman of the Transportation Committee and Mr. Doyle is the president of the Plum Borough Council. Mr. Doyle says he would vote against increases in taxes that the transportation funding commission has outlined that the state needs to repair deficient roads and bridges and fund public transit. But to raise the money needed he supports cutting waste in Harrisburg and he doesn't like Gov. Corbett's budget cuts for schools but has no solution to suggest, he also does not support a severance tax for Marcellus Shale driller. Rep. Markosek is on the other side of these issues

headline: 11PM News: Central Dauphin football honored in House
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioners have adopted a resolution honoring coach Glen McNamee for his efforts throughout the years. He was named coach of the year by the Pennsylvania Sports Writers.

headline: Romney, Santorum to meet in Pittsburgh
abstract: Mitt Romney and Rick Santorum will meet in Pittsburgh, PA, for the first time since the former PA senator Santorum withdrew from the presidential election. No formal endorsement is expected.

headline: Dems speak out against hypothetical Romney education plan
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and US Representative James Clyburn questioned the Mitt Romney budget plan when campaigning for President Obama. The two spoke out on potential cuts to education and their impact if the Romney-Ryan ticket were elected.

headline: Dissent on health care: 12th district hopefuls disagree on remedy for law
abstract: Neither candidate for the 12th Congressional District wanted the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to be enacted. Republican challenger Keith Rothfus wants to repeal the legislation and U.S. Rep Mark Critz supports some parts but not others. Critz says that Obamacare "has been a wet blanket on the job market from day one." Critz was not in office in 2010 when the bill was passed but he said he would have voted to eliminate the individual mandate, the medical tax and the 1099 reporting requirement but does not support erasing all parts of the bill.

headline: 6PM News: Flags lowered to honor Paterno
abstract: An impressive number of people have gathered to pay their respects to Joe Paterno, who has recently died from cancer.

headline: Highmark, UPMC extend relationship
abstract: Highmark Inc., the largest health insurer in the western PA region recently agreed to terms with the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center to extend their contractual relationship through 2014.

headline: Pennsylvania's Opportunity Scholarship program has yet to make $50 million in funds available
abstract: Under a new state program, businesses could enroll themselves in a tax credit program formed to help students in under achieving public schools afford the tuition of a private education. The original appropriation of $50 million has yet to be made available to those students, however, because the program has yet to collect all the tax credit applications from businesses across the state.

headline: Close reporting loopholes
abstract: The PA Legislature must pass Senate Bill 1381, SESAME (Stop Educator Sexual Abuse, Misconduct and Exploitation) Act which would close abuse-reporting loopholes and help protect children. The SESAME Act would prevent "passing the trash" which is practice involving district officals allowing educators who are sexual abusers to resign with a clean record and move to a new school  without any attention or legal enforcement. A typical offender passes through three schoools before being stopped and can hurt multiple children in the process.

headline: Pennsylvania's House of Representatives would shrink under a legislative proposal
abstract: A bill sponsored by PA Representative Sam Smith has cleared the State Government Committee in a bipartisan 16-8 vote. The PA legislature is the second largest in the nation. The bill has a lot of support among citizens. This change would require amending the PA Constitution, a difficult and lengthy process.

headline: Corbett urged not to go through with mental health and other service cuts
abstract: A rally in the PA Capitol building in Harrisburg looked to extend the message to Governor Tom Corbett that cutting funding to mental health and other services is a mistake.

headline: Proposed regulations could affect EMS workers
abstract: Proposed regulations on Emergency Medical Services personnel have come under some criticism over the possible increase in cost to obtaining certification. In a hearing devoted to the issue, members of the PA General Assembly as well as leading EMS advocates rebuked the potential regulations and discussed the negative effects the increase in costs would bring.

headline: September table games revenue up 15 percent in PA.
abstract: Casino's statewide have generated more gross revenue from table games in September with a 15.4 percent increase compared with a year ago. Table games revenue is taxed at 14 percent. PA uses casino revenue to support the state budget, public schools, civic development projects, volunteer firefighting squads, local governments and the horse racing industry.

headline: 2 Westmoreland jury commissioner jobs slated for vote
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett recently signed a bill that allows county officials to do away with part-time jobs. County Commissioner Ted Kopas is behind the plan said that a job done two jury commissioners could easily be done by the court administrator's office. Kopas thinks that the selection of jurors would be unaffected by such a switch.

headline: Philadelphia's Mayor Nutter joins elected officials here against state budget
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter joined with Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl in Pittsburgh to oppose the Corbett Administration's proposed budget. Governor Corbett's budget proposal cuts funding to programs that both mayors see as important to the people of the commonwealth.

headline: Some gain at UPMC, but market 'difficult'
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center has seen a decrease in state and federal program-reimbursements while still seeing an increase in patient volume and revenue. UPMC Chief Financial Officer Robert DeMichiei stated that the increase in medical competition in the region played a major role in the decrease in government spending on UPMC.

headline: Pa. awaiting federal decision on charter school rule change
abstract: The PA School Boards Association eased achievement rules for charter schools before getting federal permission, which resulted in 44 of 77 charer schools listed as making adequate progress (AYP) for 2011-12. The U.S. Department of Education is determining whether PA's AYP change should be allowed.

headline: Corbett’s unprecedented cut in Chester Upland funding
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett cut aid to Chester-Upland by more than 14%. The Superintendent Sara Ferguson wants to talk to US President Barack Obama so that this problem can be fixed. She believes that education opportunities are a right that should be denied to no one.

headline: No time to wait: City needs actual receiver in place
abstract: Harrisburg, PA, is without a city receiver, the employee in charge of negotiating asset sales and leases, since former receiver David Unkovic resigned last month. Some find this problem even greater than the financial and political woes plaguing the city.

headline: Protesters make waves at Corbett's PA kayak tour.
abstract: Activists opposed to Marcellus Shale gas drilling in PA showed up during PA Governor Tom Corbett's two-day kayaking trip of the Delaware River. The environmental activists picketed and used boats to confront the Governor as he kayaked down the river.

headline: Opponents say presale meeting proves Harrisburg not getting a fair deal with incinerator
abstract: There is a concern over lack of transparency in the sale of Harrisburg's incerator. Gov. Tom Corbett had met with Lancaster County agency months before the burner was offically offered for sale. Lancaster Authority had anticipated receiving state funding and appeared in the meeting minutes to be negotiating a deal before it was time to bid said Nate Benefield director of policy analysis for the Commonwealth Foundation.

headline: State building a smaller House
abstract: Legislators from the Wilkes Barre region favor a plan that would reduce the size of the PA legislature. The bill would shrink the legislature down from 203 to 153 members. PA Representatives Sam Smith and Gerald Mullery cite reports, such as one that shows that legislatures of more than 150 seem to be the least productive.

headline: Orie plans to quit Senate before sentencing
abstract: PA State Senator Jane Orie stated she will resign from office before her sentencing for public corruption charges is passed down. Ms. Orie was found guilty for numerous charges stemming from campaign activities being performed on state time, but has yet to receive her sentencing for the Allegheny County court of Common Pleas.

headline: Teachers find it’s a battle for each position
abstract: Major cuts in education across PA have made the search for teaching positions much harder. Figures from the PA Department of Education show nearly 4,000 education jobs lost in 2011 while nationwide public school employment figures dropped almost 20,000 positions.

headline: Testing is part of the war on public schools
abstract: Timothy D. Slekar, Ph.D, Division Head of Education, Human Development and Social Sciences at Penn State Altoona believes that AYP targets of No Child Left Behind were designed not to improve education but to create the appearance of a failing public school system. Skelar believes the state has the intention of handing local public schools to private educational management organizations and removing locally elected school boards. Also that tax dollars are being handed over to PAC's that have made campaign contributions to Gov. Corbett. He believes this is a war on public education.

headline: Gambling bill would benefit organizations that use funds for programs, scholarships
abstract: Volunteer fire companies and other social organization depend on revenues from small games of chance. The PA Legislature may pass a bill that would raise the legal ceilings on prize payouts. PA Governor Tom Corbett said that he would sign the bill.

headline: Lawmakers push for property tax reduction, elimination
abstract: PA lawmakers have several bills in place that could change how public schools are funded and how property taxes are levied within the state. Some proposals look to eliminate the property tax all-together, replacing it with higher income taxes are sales taxes.

headline: Man confesses to killing Officer Walker, sources say
abstract: Rafael Jones, 23, of Philadelphia confessed to killing a Philadelphia police officer only ten days after leaving jail on a prior gun conviction. Some are calling for explanations on why Jones was unmonitored upon being released, questions the Mayor's office were unable to answer concisely.

headline: Disability rights advocates arrested during protest outside Pennsylvania's Health and Welfare Building in Harrisburg
abstract: The Disability Rights group ADAPT protested outside the Welfare Building in Harrisburg claiming that Gov. Corbett and his Welfare Sec. Gary Alexander were taking away community-based and home-based services. They urged the Corbett administration to use federal dollars to fund those services. The protestors wanted to set up a meeing with Sec. Alexander to urge him to use $185 million in federal-aid available to disabled Pennsylvanians.

headline: PA bills limiting local drilling rules draw GOP foes.
abstract: A number of Republicans have come out against legislation that limits municipalities authority to control drilling activity. PA Representative McIlhinney stated that municipalities can already control tanks at compressor stations and transfer stations and so the drilling industry should not get special consideration. These legislators have, however, voted for bills limiting local authority.

headline: FCC rule would end anonymity of political ads
abstract: The Federal Communications Commission board rule in favor to require network television companies to publicly share all information dealing with political ads on their TV programs. The ruling is seen as a victory for open-government advocates, especially after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that businesses have no spending ceiling when it comes to funding political advertising.

headline: State's geared up for voter ID push
abstract: The PA Department of State has begun to implement the recent passage of the voter ID law in PA. Estimates show nearly 9 percent of registered PA voters are without the proper identification needed to cast a ballot, resulting in the issuance of free ID cards at all PennDOT locations to those without the proper form.

headline: Taxing failure to consolidate
abstract: PA has more units of local government than any state other than Illinois. 5,000 cities, boroughs, townships, and counties along with 500 school districts all with taxing authority make for redunancy and overtaxation. Lackawanna County's proposed 4 percent tax hike or $31 for the average property is not much but when combined with other taxes such as an increase in sewer fees it can become burdensome.

headline: PA teacher policies get D+ from national education group
abstract: The National Council on Teacher Quality gave PA a D+ in an assessment that measures 36 quality goals that foster the most effective teachers. The state scored poorly in the section concerning getting rid of ineffective teachers. Over half of the US states scored a D or below.

headline: Communities face big questions on finances
abstract: David Black of the Harrisburg Regional Chamber of Commerce spoke in Williamsport, PA, of the tough financial situations local governments and communities are finding themselves. Rising pensions and salaries are major issues as budgets are squeezed, making community development difficult in local areas.

headline: Funding issues discussed at Norristown Area School Board meeting
abstract: PA state Senator Daylin Leach of Norristown discussed education issues, from funding to charter schools, at a Norristown Area School Board meeting.

headline: AP, PA Senate argue legal bills issue on appeal.
abstract: The PA Supreme Court is deciding whether the state Senate wrongly deleted names of clients and other information from legal bills that the Associated Press obtained in a public records request. The AP asked for documents about the Senate paying outside attorneys to represent former Senate Democratic Leader Robert Mellow and other Democratic state Senate employees. Mellow was charged and pleaded guilty in 2012 to a federal conspiracy charge in which he allowed his staffers to raise hundreds of thousands of dollars for his and the state democratic party's political campaigns. A Commonwealth Court ruled last year that the Senate was wrong to delete the information. The case pits the Senate's attorney-client privileges against the public's right to know information about their legislature's doings.

headline: 28 News at 11: Pashinski comments on reapportionment plan rejection
abstract: Many in the PA state legislature believe that the redistricting process was conducted unfairly. Incumbents seem to have an advantage.

headline: Relocating horse tracks to bring millions for Ohio.
abstract: The relocation of two different horse tracks in Ohio is looking to bring almost $150 million more to the state in gaming revenue. The tracks are being moved to reduce competition for gamblers at casinos. The two cities losing the race tracks, Toledo and Grove City, will receive $3 million to renovate the empty tracks.

headline: State OKs road cash for Tilbury
abstract: Plymouth Township, PA, received $265,000 from the PA Emergency Management Agency in order to build an access road into a flood damaged neighborhood in the township. The state took a long time to issue the funds, according to the township, prompting US Senator Bob Casey to issue a public statement in concern.

headline: Third-party nonprofit ads do more hurt than help for Freed's campaign
abstract: The Republican candidate for PA attorney general, David Freed, told the Inquirer Editorial Board that his campaign played no part in creating the controversial outside ads that attack his opponent Democrat, Kathleen Kane, on her record on sexual assault cases. However Freed did not say that the ads were innaccurate. FactCheck.org has stated that Kane played almost no role in two cases in which two men accused of rape got off with light plea agreements. In a joint interview, Freed and Kane discussed the PA attorney general's handling of the Sandusky sexual abuse case.

headline: Rendell says asset test is mean-spirited
abstract: Former PA Governor Ed Rendell has expressed his discontent with PA Governor Tom Corbett's move to include asset testing in the acquiring of food stamps. He thinks that it is an insult to the poor these difficult economic times. Corbett cited the budget shortfalls.

headline: Marcus Hook refinery’s fate still uncertain
abstract: An oil refinery in south-eastern PA is being jointly bought and operated by Delta Air Lines and Sunoco, Inc. The purpose of the refinery, however, is changing as Sunoco and Delta Air Lines look to renovate the refinery as a fuel processing and distribution center.

headline: Statewide candidate signs new type of pledge
abstract: Candidates from across the state have signed a pledge that would promise that priorities of the constituency are placed above the priorities of the elected official. The "Public Service Pledge," has become popular among Democrats and Republicans alike and represents numerous issues from state-controlled liquor sales to the taxation of tobacco products.

headline: House Bill 2626 will give workers' tax payments to their employers
abstract: PA HB 2626 "Promoting Employment Across PA- PEP", proposes that employers keep their workers' taxes as an incentive to hire more people. The bill is modelled after a controversial program "Promoting Employment Across Kansas", PEAK program enacted in 2009. However PEAK is not that successful in Kansas. The program has transparency problems and is fueling a zero-sum jobs war with Missouri in the Kansas City Metro Area. Business Leaders there have appealed to both Kansas and Missouri Governors saying the program pits states against one another and the only winner is the business who is incentive shopping to reduce costs. The losers are the taxpayers who must provide services to those who are not paying for them.

headline: Keeping the lights on: Pa. lawmakers must work on infrastructure
abstract: The author urges for funding so that the PA Public Utility Commission can replace electricity lines and pipes that run underground. This commission estimates that it would take over 80 years to replace everything under the current system. She wants the PA legislature to force utility companies to make necessary changes without a large increase in cost to the consumer.

headline: Debt trap: Keep payday and predatory lenders out of Pennsylvania
abstract: Payday loan services are coming under the microscope as a new bill introduced by PA state Rep. Chris Ross looks to enable these loan services to operate business within the state's boarders. Several states in the past have allowed and then disallowed payday loan services to operate after complaints and issues arose from what opponents call a "debt trap" brought about by exuberant interest rates.

headline: West Penn red ink to flow, Highmark says
abstract: The West Penn Allegheny Health System is scheduled to lose money over the next two years before producing net gains, stated a financial forecast released by Highmark, Incorporated, which bought out the company the year before.

headline: Rep. Jennifer Mann says Goodbye
abstract: null

headline: Court opinion awaited next week
abstract: The Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts said that it will not yet offer an opinion as to why the PA Supreme Court has decided to toss the plan to redraw the state legislative districts. This has thrown a curveball into the electoral process, as candidates have already begun to circulate nominating petitions.

headline: Pension Tension
abstract: Pensions within the state of PA have become unsustainable as the country has hit rough economic times. This article examines the ins and outs of the public pension system and why it is faltering.

headline: Kane says Corbett impeding review of voter ID law
abstract: Democratic candidate for the PA Attorney General position, Kathleen Kane, charged Governor Corbett's office with "playing politics" in its effort to question the federal governments questioning into the new state voter ID law. Ms. Kane called for the Governor's office to turn over to the US Department of Justice all information pertaining to the new law, which would force all voters to present a state-issued identification card upon voting.

headline: Large, lively crowd turns out for Supreme Court arguments on gas drilling laws
abstract: The PA Supreme Court heard legal arguments on the state's new oil and gas laws. The crowd in the normally staid courtroom applauded after two Democratic justices challenged a lawyer that was arguing to save the state's limit's on local control of gas drilling. Many PA counties are leading a group trying to strike down portions of Act 13. Act 13 involved a Commonwealth Court ruling in a 4-3 decision to allow drilling in all land-use zones even residential neighborhoods. State officals argue that lawmakers have a right to limit municipal powers in an attempt to set up uniform rules for the drilling industry. Municipalities argue that the law unfairly bars them from keeping drilling away from schools, parks and businesses.

headline: 6PM News: One lawmaker wants Harrisburg to tackle gun crime
abstract: PA State Representative Metcalfe is pushing for a bill that would require gun owners to report lost or stolen firearms. The bill includes penalties for those who fail to report such, and would place more blame on such people in lawsuit involving the misuse of these weapons.

headline: Up to governor Tom Corbett to appoint a new judge
abstract: An Erie, PA judge will retire due to health reasons. Judge Michael Dunleavy served on the Court of Common Appeals and will leave the post come August 1. Governor Tom Corbett will select a person to fill out the remainder of Mr. Dunleavy's term 10 year term which began in 2009.

headline: Gov. Corbett at the Republican National Convention
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett made an appearance at the Republican National Convention and spoke to Republican leaders about balancing budgets in tough fiscal times.

headline: Campaign 2012/West: Incumbent, Baden councilwoman both want to create jobs in the state
abstract: The candidates for the state's 47th Senate District, Republican incumbent, Elder Vogel and Democratic challenger Kimberly Pazzanita Villella are both looking to create jobs. They believe in marketing PA to outside industries as well as increaing education funding to prepare young people for the jobs of the future. Mr. Vogel is a dairy farmer and chair of the Senate Agricultural Committee. Ms. Villella touts a "Made in PA" plan that would include tax incentives for local manufacturers who hire PA workers and sell PA products.

headline: 6AM News: Awaiting governor’s budget proposal, SNAP plan
abstract: The Governor's budget is raising a lot of eyebrows among advocates for the poor. His budget includes new rules regarding SNAP, or Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (food stamps). One below the age of 60 and with more than $2000 in the bank would not be eligible for assistance.

headline: EDITORIAL: Pennsylvania's score on implementing new Keystone Exams: Three out of ten
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett and the PA Board of Education are looking to change the yet-to-be implemented Keystone Exams, a new form of standardized testing for high schoolers in the state.

headline: Specter reportedly has serious illness
abstract: According to reports, former PA Senator Arlen Specter from Philadelphia has contracted a serious form of lymphoma, a life-threatening disease.

headline: Campaign 2012/North: Newcomers running for seat vacated by Vulakovich
abstract: PA's 30th Legislative District candidates are newcomers attempting to replace Randy Vulakovich, Republican, who won a special August election to replace convicted former state Sen. Jane Orie. David T. Tusick is a 26 year-old Democrat from Fox Chapel who co-owns a Pittsburgh advertising agency and Hal English is a 49 year-old Republican from Hampton who is a lawyer and retired Marine Corps Officer. The race is between a young ambitious American who would bring a fresh perspective and a man with extensive life experience.

headline: Mercersburg nurse challenging Shuster in 9th
abstract: Karen Ramsburg has announced her candidacy for the 9th Congressional District, which is now held by US Representative Bill Shuster. She describes herself as a mother, nurse and author. She is running as an independent.

headline: Pa. budget plan would restore education, social service cuts
abstract: A budget plan in the PA Senate is on track to pass through the Senate and make its way to the House following unanimous approval in key Senate committees. The budget plan looks to restore cuts to higher education funding, public schooling, and other social services. The Corbett administration called the bill "unsustainable."

headline: Protesters confront Corbett on kayaking tour
abstract: Environmental activists confronted PA Governor Tom Corbett while he spent two days kayaking along the Delaware River. The activists displayed banners and road on boats in order to protest Marcellus Shale drilling across the state.

headline: Pa. House pulls the plug on charter reform bill, killing the measure for this year
abstract: PA House Republicans pulled back their support from a charter school reform bill that would have included the first significant reforms to the 1997 charter law that created independent public schools. The PA Senate passed the bill in a 33-19 vote. The bill was rejected due to concerns over the creation of the a charter school funding study commission. Gov. Corbett was prepared to sign the bill into law even though it lacked a controversial provision he supported that would have given the state independent panel the ability to approve brick-and-mortar charter applications without the approval of the school district in which they are located.

headline: Corbett to lay out new budget next week
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is set to soon unveil his budget , which will likely make vital cuts to education and social welfare spending. Pennsylvania's emergency response organs will not lose funding as they were heavily depended on for assistance in the wake of natural disasters.

headline: America needs politics, not 'politricks'
abstract: After numerous occurrences in PA state government over the past year where officials have been tried and convicted of corruption charges, Bishop A.E. Sullivan Jr writes an opinion piece asking for change and commitment among our elected officials.

headline: Corbett’s kayaking tour through Pike County doesn’t get warm welcome
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett ran into protestors amidst his ride along the Delaware River in Pike County. The activists were concerned with the environmental impacts of Marcellus Shale natural gas drilling across the state.

headline: PA Senate OKs juvenile murder sentences options.
abstract: Gov. Corbett is likely to sign into law a bill that gives PA judges options other than life in prison when sentencing juveniles in murder cases. This bill was created in reaction to the U.S. Supreme Court's decision that mandatory life-without-parole sentences for juveniles constitutes cruel and unusual punishment. The new sentencing options depend on the age of the defendant and which degree of murder they were convicted for.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Who'll pay tab for extra hour?
abstract: The author feels that liquor by the drink tax, which supports Philadelphia Public schools, is inducing the city to look for ways to keep people drinking longer. That is why City Councilwoman Blondell Reynolds Brown has proposed that bars be permitted to stay open until 3 a.m. The school district is battling with a $61 million deficit.

headline: Drill mud seeps out near creek
abstract: Mud from a pipeline-drilling site broke through the ground near a water passage in Wyoming County, PA. PA Department of Environmental Protection was contacted immediately and no chemicals are additives were found in the mud or in the surrounding area where the breakage occurred.

headline: Penna.'s elusive political landscape: Local group challenges new rules for shale gas industry
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Association of Township Supervisors which represents 1,455 municipalities or 44 percent of the states population, is supporting a group of local officials who are suing state lawmakers, including the governor over zoning provisions of the Act 13 which is a new law that proposes changes to the Macellus Shale gas drilling industry on local land-use issues. They argue that Act 13 would strip local governments of their zoning and land-use rights regarding gas well drilling and related pipeline infrastructure.

headline: Election 2012: Harrisburg-area activist Gene Stilp challenges U.S. Rep. Lou Barletta, former Hazleton mayor
abstract: The election in PA's 11th Congressional district is a big one.  The Republican challenger is U.S. Rep. Lour Barletta, the freshmen GOP incumbent and former Hazelton mayor who has name recognition, $1 million in campaign funds, and outside support. The Democratic challnger is Gene Stilp, a political activist who has raised $36,000 and has endorsements from the AFL-CIO and PennEnvironment. The 11th district spans 9 counties and Democrats outnumber Republicans.

headline: Gov. Tom Corbett administration wants to shred safety net
abstract: The U.S. Department of Agriculture administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) or food stamps. PA Governor Tom Corbett's Department of Public Welfare is bucking the nationwide trend of relaxing personal assets restrictions on SNAP participants. The author thinks this is ridiculous considering how little one can buy with food stamps.

headline: Tax bill has Fumo stamp
abstract: A new property tax plan in Philadelphia could see property taxes rise significantly. But, following the outline of a bill passed with the help of a now-imprisoned City Council member, property owners in gentrified areas of the city could see significant relief.

headline: Corbett helps gas moguls 'build it'
abstract: Governeror Tom Corbett's support of governments role in helping business is not a standard Republican position. Governor Corbett has approved tax subsidies and grants to jumpstart PA's burgeoning natural gas, petrochemical, oil, and airline industries.

headline: Juvenile bill goes to governor
abstract: A bill to adjust sentences for juvenlies who commit murder is going to Gov. Corbett for signing. The bill is in response to the U.S. Supreme Court decision striking down state laws that require juveniles convicted of homocide to life in prison without the chance of parole. The bill will require courts to consider the least restrictive punishmnet for regular juvenile offenders. The bill is also a response to abuses in the sentencing of juveniles to a for-profit detention center uncovered by the Luzerne County Courthouse scandal.

headline: 6:30AM News: Corbett’s endorsements
abstract: Millionaire Steve Welch is a favorite among many GOP leaders, including PA Governor Tom Corbett. He want to run for the US Senate. Interestingly Welch voted for Barack Obama in 2008.

headline: State Senate Appropriations Committee passes its own version of the state budget
abstract: A committee within the PA Senate agreed on a budget plan that restored cuts found in Gov. Tom Corbett's budget plan. The budget proposal now moves to the floor of the Senate in which it will be voted.

headline: Late court decisions may impact 2012 election
abstract: A series of judicial decisions across the nation regarding voter ID laws and early voting regulations could help to sway upcoming elections. Pennsylvania and Wisconsin are fighting battles over the legality of voter ID laws and in the swing states of Florida, Ohio, Iowa, and Nevada there is litigation on proposed changes to early voting rules. Thousands of civil rights activists and lawyers are poised to challenge any disputes they find on election day.

headline: Proposal would put veteran designation on PA licenses
abstract: Military Veterans who were not dishonorably discharged from PA will be able to get a special designation on their driver's licenses under a proposal in the state House. Most veterans do not have a simple form of ID that shows that they served in the military and this bill would change that.

headline: PA Representative Scott Perry considers congressional run
abstract: PA US Congressman Todd Platt will not seek re-election. PA Representative Scott Perry announced that he is considering a bid for that seat. He said that he had to do what was right for his two little girls and his wife.

headline: House committee advances bill that would allow out-of-state wineries to ship to Pennsylvania
abstract: The PA House Liquor Control Committee voted in favor of amending a bill that would allow shipment of out-of-state wine to Pennsylvanians' houses.

headline: 'Public service' pledge gains 10th adherent
abstract: The Majority Party PA has circulated a "Canditate Public Service Pledge" to canditates running in the upcoming election. State Rep. Eugene DePasquale of York County, who is running for state auditor general, and nine others have signed the pledge. The pledge stipulates that canditates will use public opinion polls in their policy decisions in an attempt to hold themselves more liable to public will.

headline: Pa. Game Commission takes steps to control fatal deer disease
abstract: The PA Game Commission is establishing a 600 square mile disease management area in parts of Adams and York counties to contain a fatal deer disease. Hunters are prohibited from moving certain deer parts, using certain attractants, and they must bring their deer to a mandatory check station. Deer feeding is also banened.

headline: Sen. Toomey's town hall meeting brings both cautious hope, doubts about economy
abstract: PA US Senator Toomey recently held a town hall that casts doubt on the recovery of the economy. He thinks that the government needs to curb spending and reduce the federal deficit.

headline: Corbett willing to negotiate on Pennsylvania budget, but…
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett admitted he is willing to work out a budget deal with the General Assembly, but admitted that tough financial times are not over and fiscal responsibility is important. The Governor was responding to a Senate budget plan that looked to restore $500 million in cuts found in the Governor's plan.

headline: Pennsylvania schools fear Adequate Yearly Progress won’t be in reach
abstract: The No Child Left Behind Act specifies that all students must score "proficient" or higher in reading and math on the PA System of School Assessment tests. Many PA educators believe that this criteria will keep most schools from making adequate yearly progress, AYP, which is measured by a districts graduation and attendence rates and PSSA scores. Schools that do not meet the standard are given a label and if they fail for consecutive years the dsitrict could face drastic changes such as replacement of staff or closure. In 2012-13 all 11th-grade students will take the Keystone Exams which will become a graduation requirement.

headline: Campaign culture, entrenched parties hurt democratic process
abstract: Of the 203 PA state House races, 96 are unopposed, and 9 of 16 are unopposed in the state Senate races. The majority running opposed are incumbents, and critics say that strong parties in one region deter opposition from putting up a canditate. Carl Romanelli, chairman of the PA Green Party said he hopes to run candidates in the next election season.

headline: Act 32 could raise local Earned Income Tax rates for some central Pennsylvanians
abstract: Act 32 now requires employers to collect the highest local Earned Income Tax rate from employees' paychecks, no matter if the rate corresponds to the person's residence or workplace municipality. The act also greatly reduces the number of tax collectors.

headline: Forced paring: Pitt's hard choices should spare the classics
abstract: Cuts to education in PA's budget has forced the University of Pittsburgh to disband some graduate programs. Classics, religious studies, and German language will no longer be offered as concentrations for graduate students.

headline: Pa. delegates: Nation is better off, But they acknowledge much more needs to be done.
abstract: At a PA women's luncheon, Kathleen Sebelius, the U.S. Health and Human Services secretary, said that the economy is better off than before President Obama took office. She said that the democrats need to convey the message that though there are still improvements to be made, the country is better off than they were four years ago. The luncheon was attended by many PA women politicians who expressed similar views.

headline: Act 111 overhaul bill seen in sharply different terms
abstract: A bill to overhaul the Act 111 collective bargaining process for paid police and firefighters is being debated and the Senate Local Government Committee heard testimony from mayors, COC officials, and public safety unions. The bill proposes many changes to Act 111, including starting the collective bargaining process earlier in the year and requiring the cost of arbitration to be split between municipalities and public employee unions, it would also continue and add an additional layer of appeal to arbitration panel pay awards. The bill would determine new costs based on CPI and base pay for a police officer or firefighter.

headline: State senator calls for end to vehicle emissions testing
abstract: PA State Senator is calling for a rollback of federal vehicle emissions testing required in a number of midstate counties. He says that technological improvements have made the inspections obsolete. He has issued a bill asking congress to revaluate the testing.

headline: DeWeese wants sentence delayed
abstract: Former PA state representative Bill DeWeese asked for his sentencing on corruption charges to be delayed to make time to decide on his motion for bond. Mr. DeWeese was charged and convicted of using state time to further his campaign, among other things. Mr. DeWeese was slated to serve 2.5-5 years starting May 14.

headline: State is probing methane in home
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection is investigating a reported spike in methane levels inside a trailer in Dimock, PA. The increased methane levels may have been caused by a contaminated aquifer stemming from Cabot Oil and Gas's hydraulic fracturing for natural gas in a nearby area. Cabot took readings and found no detectable amoutns of methane in the house or around the strucure, they are awaiting results from water samples for confirmation. The Department for Environmental Protection is still investigating the specific cause of the methane.

headline: Toohil says Israel trip educational, aboveboard
abstract: State Reps. Tarah toohil and Nick Miccarelli traveled to Israel. Part of the their trip was funded through the Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia's $2,500. The two rode a camel together. There are allegations that the Israel trip was junket paid for the the Jewish Federation and not reported on Toohil's financial interest statements. Toohil claims the trip was taken on her own dime. Toohil says the trip was for educational purposes. She claims she was looking at Israel's innovative welfare to work practices and visiting some of Israel's hightech companies.

headline: Philadelphia School Officials Look to Denver For Public-To-Charter Transition Tips
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter is heading to Denver with members of the Philadelphia School Reform Commission. Their mission is to compare notes with Denver school officials on the cooperation between district and charter schools. The trip was paid for by the William Penn Foundation.

headline: Mixed reaction on the fall of Robert J. Mellow
abstract: Former PA state Senator Robert Mellow admitted his guilt to charges of corruption in an Old Forge, PA courthouse.

headline: Lawmakers to consider phone ban for drivers
abstract: PA currently has a ban on texting while driving but now lawmakerrs are attempting to prohibit all use of cell phones while driving with the exception of GPS. House Appropiations Minority Chairman Rep. Joseph Markosek D-Allegheny is planning to propose a bill to do this. Drivers would be be fined $50 or $100 in a school zone if caught using a cell phone. The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety has concluded that states that ban cell-phone use showed a decrease in behavior but also found no evidence that the ban reduces crashes. They said that further investigation must be done to understand this disparity.

headline: Stilp promises to work with fellow lawmakers
abstract: Gene Stilp the democratic challenger in PA's 11th Congressional District is running a low-key, low-budget campaign in stark contrast to his Republican opponent Lou Barletta. Stilp an activist and a Luzerne County native is aligning himself with the bulk of policies endorsed by President Barack Obama including strengthening the Affordable Care Act. Stilp says he is frustated with the gridlock in Congress and said he wants to work with people who will agree to work in a compromising fashion.

headline: Pa. Auditor Jack Wagner Says Turnpike Commission Is Headed For Financial Wreck
abstract: Under 2007 legislation, The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission, is paying $450 million dollars a year to the PA Department of Transportation. Jack Wagner says because of this law the turnpike's debt has grown from $2.6 billion to $7.3 billion. Jack Wanger thinks that turnpike is headed for trouble but PA Turnpike Commission spokesmen say otherwise.

headline: A bill increasing the speed limit has been approved by the House Transportation Committee
abstract: A bill increasing the speed limit on the PA Turnpike to 70 MPH has been approved by the House Transportation Committee. The bill now moves to the House floor.

headline: Nutter plugs education, Obama - and Philly
abstract: Mayor Nutter was greeted with loud ovation when he took the podium at the Democratic convention in Charlotte. His speech focused on the Democrats support for education which is a vital issue in Philadelphia. He attacked Republican Nominee Mitt Romney's assertion that class size did not equate to higher test scores. Earlier in the day, he suggested that the 2016 Democratic Convention be held in Philadelphia.

headline: Profile of Barack Obama
abstract: null

headline: Official: Catholic School Closings May Save Public Schools Money On Transportation
abstract: Students attending the Archdiocese will be attending new schools next year because of closings and mergers. State law requires local school districts to give parochial students a lift. Along with this is a consolidation process that should absorb increased costs.

headline: Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission opens comments on pipeline fees
abstract: PA Consumers will soon be charged for infrastructure repair for electric, natural gas, water, and sewage companies. Following the signing of the bill by Governor Tom Corbett, the PA Public Utility Commission opened up a 20 day comment period where PA residence could voice their questions or concerns pertaining to the bill.

headline: Pa. Supreme Court must overturn voter ID law
abstract: Rep. Ronald G Waters argues that PA's strictest-in-the-nation voter ID law is a blatant abuse of power by PA Rrepublicans. He argues that the PA Supreme Court must overturn this unconstitutional law which is intended to suppress the vote of traditionally Democratic voters, minorities, women, seniors, individuals with disabilities and young adults.

headline: Bill to crack down on sexting on way to governor’s desk
abstract: null

headline: 23-Year FBI Veteran Named As DRPA’s Inspector General
abstract: Delaware River Port Authority has made a new hire. Tom Raftery has been hired as the agency's first inspector general. PA Auditor General Jack Wagner fought hard for this change. He indulged Raftery in flattery, looking back on his long career in the FBI.

headline: Farmland preservation: An investment in our future?
abstract: In this opinion piece, former Secretary of Agriculture Russell C. Redding explains the importance of PA's farmland preservation program and how critical funding for it needs to stay in place in this year's budget plan. The preservation program has permanently preserved over 450,000 acres of farmland in the state since its inception.

headline: Legislature should give districts permission to record
abstract: School Bus drivers have a very tough job transporting loud, rambunctious children to and from school. The Reading Eagle advocates for the PA legislature to overturn the PA wiretap law which prevents someone from being recorded without approval. They argue that by having audio as well as video surveillance on buses children will be more inclined to behave. However, they say that the audio recordings should not be used to investigate cheating or misbehavior outside the classroom.

headline: DN Editorial: Editorial: Charter-school reform - do it right
abstract: The PA state House did a good thing failing to move on a charter-reform bill, because the proposed bill failed to deliver on the kind of reforms that charters need. The failed bill called for a commission to evaluate the funding forumula, tighten ethics rules for charters, place caps on fund balances and new provide provisions for teacher evaluations. A statewide authorizing commission was stripped from the bill. Charter schools would be better served with a commission or task force that included leaders from the public, charter and parochial schools to identify the needed reforms that would maximize benefits to children.

headline: DeWeese Corruption Trial Opens Today
abstract: William DeWeese is still a PA Senator and is a former House Speaker. He was Democratic leader when the state attorney general's office charged him with using state resources for campaign purposes. A former DeWeese staffer entered a guilty plea in the case last week.

headline: Bridging the gap
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner expressed his concern for PA's transportation infrastructure while in Johnstown, PA. Mr. Wagner urged federal and state officials to provide the necessary funding that he, as Auditor General, says is at their disposal.

headline: Flood muck gone but effects lurk
abstract: The Susquehana River has dealt with major flooding from storms in the past few years. Heavy rains washed more silt and phosperous into the Chesapeake Bay last year since 1978, which damaged sewage treatment plants and left a breeding ground for mosquitos. The PA Department of Environmental Protection sent emergency response crews to inspect and help contain 731 sites in PA after the flooding. They worked to restore the 124 swamped or damaged sewage plants.

headline: Vets, anti-blight measures headed to Corbett's desk
abstract: Before lawmakers return home to campaign for the 2012 November 6 election they sent a number of bills for signing to Gov. Corbett. One bill establishes a new Veterans Trust Fund to help service members and family. It will use revenue from the sale of special veterans license plates and other means. Another bill makes sexting a summary offense for a minor to knowingly transmit or distribute sexually explicit images of themselves. A third bill gives municipalities the ability to create landbanks for vacant and tax delinquent properties. Also headed to Gov. Corbetts desk is a bill seeking to prevent fraud in the state heating assistance program.

headline: Corbett Takes Heat For Handling Of Chester-Upland School District Troubles
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Corbett is coming under fire for how he dealt with the Chester-Upland school district. PA Republican Senator Piccola said that the Corbett administration has failed to address rising costs of education. He thinks that the state is obliged to chip in and help out districts like Chester-Upland.

headline: Harrisburg council member calls for mayor’s resignation among ongoing financial problems
abstract: Several city council members in Harrisburg, PA have called for the resignation of Mayor Linda Thompson following dismal financial times and her handling of the resignation of the Harrisburg Receiver, David Unkovic.

headline: At Flight 93 memorial site, defense chief reflects on 11th anniversary
abstract: U.S. Secretary of Defense Leon Panetta attended a 911 memorial event in Shanksville, PA, the site of the Flight 93 crash. He praised the 40 passengers and crew members of Flight 93 who bravely fought back agaisnt four al-Qaeda terrorists. He praised military and intelligence agencies for bringing to justice those responsible for 911 and from preventing similar attacks form occuring again, but he warned of the continued terrorist threat that remains in Yemen, Somalia and North Africa.

headline: David M. Sanko: Consolidating local pension funds won't eliminate crisis
abstract: Gov. Corbett and the General Assembly are searching for solutions to PA's growing pension problem. The commonwealth's pension programs for some 800,000 state workers and public school teachers cost about $40 billion and is expected to rise to $65 billion by 2021. A series of fact finding missions led by the PA Employee Retirment Commission is advocating for consolidation of hundreds of healthy municipal plans to fund the debts of a few. David Sanko, exec. Director of the PA State Association of Township Supervisors aruges that redistriubiton is a bad idea that penalizes the successful while rewarding those in trouble. The number of solvent municipal pension plans significantly exceed the number of troubled ones. Sanko aruges that lawmakers should not attempt to oversee munipal pension plans and instead focus on providing local leaders with common-sense reforms.

headline: Local Officials Accuse Gov. Corbett of ”Attack On Poor People”
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is being attacked because of his moves to cut programs aimed at helping poor people. Some think that the moves have been arbitrary and aimed at punishing those with low incomes. A spokesperson from Philabundance said that this will actually cost PA money because food stamps are a federal program that benefits businesses because of the purchases it enables.

headline: PA rescues refinery town, gives $30M to Delta
abstract: The PA government gave $30 million to Delta Airlines in order for them to refurbish an oil refinery in Delaware County as well as retain the hundreds of jobs connected to the refinery. Delta Airlines bought the refinery from ConocoPhillips with the help of the $30 million PA Opportunity Grant.

headline: Conventional Wisdom
abstract: The Democratic and Repbulican National Conventions have done little to change the presidential race. However, the voter-ID laws in PA, and voting requirement changes in Ohio and Florida could have an impact on the election. The convention speech by President Obama was a good one but the race is still close in early September. There is still enough time for a major event to swing the election one way or the other.

headline: New public corruption hotline announced in Philly.
abstract: The FBI Philadelphia field division along with the U.S. and PA attorney general's offices, Philadelphia City government, and police announced a new hotline for the public to report public corruption by government official and law enforcement. The hotline is critical in stopping problems such as the "pay-to-play" culture in city government said George Venizelos, speical agent in charge fot he FBI's Philadelphia field division/

headline: Could There Be 2 Pa. Primaries At Double The Cost?
abstract: Some think that the State Legislature will hold a second primary, because of a State Supreme Court ruling which asks for amendments to the redistricting plan to make the line more contiguous. PA Senate Leader Jay Costa says that the old lines should be used to avoid a second primary; he thinks residents should not have to pay for that.

headline: More proof of the slots revenue limits
abstract: Gambling revenues grew slightly in the month of April, but that was while adding the tally from the brand new Valley Forge Casino Resort. Without that resort's numbers, slot machine revenue actually fell, raising the question to some about the productivity of casinos.

headline: Natural-gas firms have paid nearly $200 million under Act 13
abstract: Natural-gas companies have paid close to $200 million to the PA Public Utility Commission to meet the requirements of the impact fee imposed by Act 13. Some companies are disputing the amount they owe and the Marcellus Shale Coalition is arguing that at a time when budget shortfalls are stretching state and local governments, natural gas production is supporting tens of thousands of good jobs. The environmental group Citizens for PA Future said that the $200 million isn't that much money if all the potential impacts of gas drilling are taken into account. The impact fee is based on the number and type of wells drilled with the PUC distibuting funds to local governments and additional money going to statewide projects.

headline: Pa. attorney general candidates draw distinctions between themselves in televised debate
abstract: The candidates for the PA attorney general race, Rep. David Freed and Dem. Kathleen Kane met at Widener Law's Harrisburg Campus for their first and only televised debate. Freed a Cumberland County District Attorney for 15 years and district attorney since 2005 portrayed himself as the more experienced prosecuter. Kane referred to Freed as Gov. Corbett's hand-picked candidate who lacked the needed independence needed for the position. They debated how they would approach the Jerry Sanduscky child sex abuse case.

headline: Nutter Begins 2nd Term With New Council
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter was sworn in to second term in office. In his address he talked about the 6 murders over the New Year's Weekend, and the struggling Philadelphia school system. He stated that one out of out of every three tax dollars collected in the city go to fighting crime and staffing prisons.

headline: Pennsylvania proposal buys time for mobile home residents forced to move
abstract: A bill in the PA House of Representatives looks to require developers to give more time as well as compensation to members of mobile home communities for relocation after the property is bought. Under current law, mobile home residents have only 30 days to relocate after a developer has bought up the land.

headline: Governor chooses Charles Hall to fill Cumberland County's coroner post
abstract: Gov. Corbett and Cumberland County's commissioners disagree over who should be the county's next coroner. Gov. Corbett endorsed Charles Hall an East Pennsboro board president for the position based on his extensive law enforcement backround. The county commissioners endorsed the current acting coroner Matt Stoner who took over the position after the previous coroner had been arrested for mishandling prescription drugs obtained through death investigations.

headline: Lawmakers' flood of irresponsibility
abstract: PA lawmakers have not yet approved ten's of million of dollars of flood aid in road, bridge, sewer and water system repairs. Thirteen months ago there was severe flooding in the Susquehana River Basin. The earliest funding is likely to be approved as apart of the next general budget, July 1, 2013, because some lawmakers do not favor placing funding for flood repairs in a separate bill. Even though the legislature and administration are controlled by the same party they couldn't come to an agreement because the Senate wanted a $150 million recovery bond issue and Gov. Corbett did not favor taking a loan.

headline: Chip Minemyer | 12th district contenders have much in common
abstract: The race for the 12th Congressional District in PA should be an interesting one, because of interlacing pasts of those involved in the race. Mike Mikus has been the campaign manager for both US Representative Mark Critz and US Representative Altmire and is now working for Mikus.

headline: Not so fast, says new filing in Voter ID suit
abstract: The legal fight over the PA voter identification law has heated up after a group filed a petition in the Commonwealth Court of PA seeking to gain a speedy outcome to the case. The controversial law over forcing people to show some sort of identification upon voting has brought upon lawsuits that threaten to stall its operation, while the aforementioned petitioning group sites their voting rights would be violated if the law did not go into effect.

headline: VP Biden says nation hasn't forgotten 9/11 families.
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden was at the Shanksville, PA 911 memorial ceremony which commemorated the heroic acts of the 40 passengers and crew of flight 93. Biden showed respect for the families and told them that the nation had not forgotten about them. A 911 memorial is still in construction in Shanksville and still needs funds to finish the job.

headline: Pittsburgh’s approach to tax-exempt nonprofits could be model for others in state
abstract: The Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority, ICA, was appointed by the state legislature eight years ago to help Pittsburgh resolve its chronic financial problems and recently asked the city to create a task force in approving the mayor's 2013 budget. The question the task force is working on is how much money tax-exempt nonprofits should pay for city services each year. City officials says nonprofits, including government entities own about 40% of Pittsburgh real estate and so benefit greatly from services the gov. provides but pay little in taxes. Pittsburgh has done well in addressing ints financial problems in the recent past.

headline: Universities pay for legislators’ gifts
abstract: The Huntingdon County Tea Party has demanded the Penn State Board of Trustees to name legislators who receive gifts from the university. The party feels that it would be inappropriate for a legislator to be voting on Penn State government subsidy while receiving gifts.

headline: Obama campaign's first Romney attack ad hits home in Lehigh Valley
abstract: A television ad from the Obama campaign vilifies former Governor Mitt Romney over his job at a private equity firm in the takeover and shutdown of a steel mill in Missouri.

headline: Scranton under investigation for possibly cheating on state test
abstract: The Scranton School District is under investigation for manipulation of standardized tests, the PSSA's. Teachers and administrators allegedly changed answers on bubble sheets. Statewide six districts have not been cleared of wrongdoing in the past two years. PSSA exam results are used to check school's performance in comparison with the federal No Child Left Behind Act. New security measures have been put into place in 2012 to prevent further cheating.

headline: Kane says if elected, she’d investigate handling of Sandusky case
abstract: null

headline: Taxpayers shell out $49M for retiring employees' sick time
abstract: A spokesperson from the Commonwealth Foundation feels that retirement compensation for sick time is not justified. On average, people receiving pay for sick time get $14,600. PA Governor Tom Corbett intends on cutting $750 million from the state budget.

headline: Hit the brakes: A bill to raise turnpike speed should be pulled over
abstract: A bill in the PA House looks to allow the PA Turnpike Commission to raise the maximum speed limit to 70 MPH on the turnpike. A similar action in Ohio resulted to a higher increase in accidents and fatalities among the roadways, leaving critics of the PA bill questioning its merit.

headline: Seeking new job, union halts Goldtex protest
abstract: Union protests have stopped outside the Goldtex Building in Callowhill, Philadelphia because the workers might get new jobs at a new 21-story office tower development project on South Broad Street. U.S. Rep. Bob Brady was instrumental in the negotiations between the Union and the Post Brothers development company. Union workers are now helping to complete the Goldtex building and Atlantic building renovations.

headline: New health facility at South Allegheny Middle School
abstract: null

headline: Get state budget house in order now rather than later
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett, unlike his predecessor, does not sugarcoat budget projections. Corbett cuts spending, rather than continuing or raising spending while increasing taxes. He projects a $500 million deficit.

headline: Commonwealth Court schedules confirmation hearing for Harrisburg receiver appointee
abstract: The Commonwealth Court of PA has schedule a hearing in the confirmation process of the city of Harrisburg's next receiver. Gov. Corbett, who is in charge of the nomination process of the next receiver, nominated former Air Force Major General William Lynch.

headline: ACLU, state offer information on voter ID, eligibility
abstract: The PA ACLU has set up a website that helps residents determine if they have photo ID that meets the requirements of the state's new voter ID law. The website asks a series of questions based on the State Departments Voter ID brochures. The ACLU is one of many plaintiffs challenging the PA voter ID law in court.

headline: Gov. Corbett signs ‘Brad Fox Law’ on straw gun purchases
abstract: Gov. Corbett signed into law HB 898 which has become known as the "Brad Fox Law", a straw gun purchase bill that restores a minimum 5-year sentence on anyone convicted of making repeat straw gun purchases. Plymouth Township Police Officer Bradley Fox was killed on Sept. 13 by Andrew Thomas with a firearm purhcased for him by Michael Henry of Philadelphia. Thomas committed suicide after a manhunt ensued. Henry is facing multiple felony weapon charges for buying guns in Montgomery and Chester counties for Thomas who paid him for the guns.

headline: Pennsylvania leaders try to keep air wing open
abstract: The most expensive air wing in the country located in PA is looking to be shut down by the United States Air Force, much to the chagrin of some PA officials.

headline: More insured under new law
abstract: Many Americans continue to go without insurance though nationally the number of Americans with health insurance has increased since 2007 according to the Bureau of the Census. This increase can be contributed to the passage of the new federal health care law in 2010 which included a provision that allows people 19 or older to remain under their parents policies until they are 26 which has resulted in an increase of 1.6 million Americans being covered. 48.6 million Americans still do not have insurance and the new health care law should be implemented on schedule to diminish this number.

headline: Dedicate higher fines to treatment Lawmakers target alcohol offenders
abstract: Lawmakers passed a bill to increase fines for underage drinking and public drunkeness from $300 to $1000. Fines on teens, young adults and publicly drunk individuals will increase local treasuries by about $6 million a year in PA. It is not clear that higher fines alone will deter these actions and lawmakers should increase funidng for education and detterence programs.

headline: Allentown City Council Vice President Mike Schlossberg running for Pennsylvania House
abstract: Allentown City Council Vice President Mike Schlossberg is running for the Pennsylvania House of Representatives seat in the 132nd District. Jennifer Mann currently holds that seat. She is not seeking reelection and endorses Schlossberg.

headline: Governor Corbett Signs Bill To Block Federal Real ID In Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed into law a measure that would block the enactment and application of the federal program, Real ID, a national identification system. The American Civil Liberties Union praised the action by Gov. Corbett, who made PA the largest state to enact such legislation against Real ID.

headline: Pennsylvania PUC asked to review towns' drilling regulations
abstract: State filings from municipalities with the state Public Utility Commission challenging the new state drilling law, Act 13, have increased to four. The newest filing is challenging Cecil Townships gas drilling rules, and another filing is from energy company Range Resources which is questioning the validity of the South Fayette ordinance saying it conflicts with state law.

headline: Berks gets plan for spending $15 million in block-grant funds
abstract: Berks County received a plan for spending $15 million in state human services funding that they will receive in block grants instead of many different funding streams. Berks is one of 20 counties testing block-grant funding which is supposed to give counties more flexibility in adminstering services such as mental health, child welfare, homeless assistance and drug and alcohol addiction treatment progroams.

headline: Citizens' group sues over PA longwall pollution.
abstract: The Center for Coalfield Justice, based in Washington, Pa., filed a federal lawsuit Friday against coal mining company based in Waynesburg, Greene County, Emerald Coal Resources LP. The lawsuit claims that Emerald Coal violated pollution levels for iron, manganese, aluminum and other pollutants more than 120 times in the past 12 months and more than 400 times in the past five years.

headline: Unhappy birthday: An appellate court indulges the state on secrecy
abstract: The PA Commonwealth Court recently has given an official sanction to change the Right to Know Law. PA Governor Tom Corbett wants to protect government workers' identities by no longer allowing the public to monitor who is employed where, and other personal information.

headline: Senate moves budget plan as Corbett defends his own
abstract: The PA Senate has began to move a budget plan that would restore up to $500 million in cuts found in the original Governor Corbett plan. The Senate plan would restore funding to higher education as well as grade schooling and early education. Governor Corbett defended his budget plan, but said he would be interested in working with Senate leaders on a compromise.

headline: Pennsylvania Supreme Court orders judge to take a second look at state's voter ID law
abstract: A divided PA Supreme Court sent back down a challenge of the PA voter ID law to a lower court with an order for the judge to block the law if he finds that voters can't easily get the required state-issued IDs and become disenfranchised. The Supreme Court gave a Commonwealth court judge until October 2, 2012 to make up his mind. The court suggested that the push to implement the law for the 2012 election has raised questions about its constitutionality and a delay would give the state time to implement the law in a fair way that protects voter's rights.

headline: State House candidates weigh-in on education
abstract: Gov. Corbett's plan for major charter school reform was stymied. The creation of a statewide body that would authorize alternative public schools was defeated but some reforms were put into place such as new teacher evalutions standards and limits on the ability of school districts to increase poropety taxes. In general Republican candidates and incumbents around the state support school vouchers while Democrat's oppose them however many lawmakers have not taken a firm stand on the issue either way before the upcoming election.

headline: Gov. Corbett freezes $160 million in state spending
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has frozen $160 million in state spending. The money will enter a reserve fund, unless the economy improves. Four state universities will take five percent cuts.

headline: Gov. Corbett Slightly Opens Door For State Aid To Port Authority
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett refused to answer whether state aid will be given to the Port Authority Transit in Pittsburgh after the Authority was forced to cut services to the public in order to balance its budget. The Governor, however, did say the door to the aid was open, as long as the Port Authority takes action against the budget issue.

headline: The Medicaid conundrum: Corbett is right to be cautious about expanding Medicaid
abstract: The U.S. Supreme court ruled that the federal government cannot force states to massively expand Medicaid which was the centerpiece of a law designed to expand health coverage to unisured Americans earning up to 133 percent of the federal poverty line. The nation's governors must decide whether to reject the plan or expand Medicaid even as they are struggling to maintain services to the most at-risk populations. PA spends nearly a third of state spending on Medicaid which is one of the highest in the nation.
