New enrollees are likely to join Medicaid and drive the cost up higher and cause even more funding problems.

headline: Corbett signs straw purchase gun law
abstract: null

headline: Pennsylvania reviews trades by bank
abstract: The PA Treasury Department has hired a consultant to conduct a review of transactions between the state and The Bank of New York Mellon Corp. They suspect that the company has overcharged the state and its pension funds on thousands of foreign currency transactions. Other states have filed lawsuits against the bank.

headline: Biden Speaks On Economy At Lafayette College
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden lectured at Lafayette College on the economy and the administration's vision for it. The Vice President touted the President's accomplishments with infrastructure and health care, among others, and told the listeners to discount his political opponents.

headline: Follow if you are not a wuss
abstract: Former Gov. Ed Rendell officialy joined twitter in September, 2012. @GovEdRendell described himself in 160 characters or less: "Ex-politician, media pundit, avid sports fan, dog lover, author." He also plugged his new book "A Nation of Wusses" by using it has his cover photo.

headline: Governor signs new gang crackdown law
abstract: null

headline: Delco power broker's viewing draws a throng
abstract: John F. McNichol recently died. He helped elect governors, US Senators, and many local officials. He was remembered, in the words of US Senator Bob Casey and US Representative Patrick Meehan, as a "ultimate behind-the-scenes politician," and a "go-to-guy".

headline: Plaintiff In Voter ID Lawsuit Has Fought For Years To Prove Her Identity
abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union has filed suit to overturn the PA voter ID law, a measure that would force all voters to produce some form of identification before voting. One plaintiff, a Philadelphia woman, has voted for nearly 40 years, only to get that privilege revoked after she was unable to produce a birth certificate or other form of identification.

headline: UPMC defends tax-exempt status
abstract: UPMC, Western PA's dominant network of hospitals and doctors, have begun a marketing campaign explaining how it spends its money. UPMC claimed to have a profit of $7 million instead of the $220.7 million it reported to bond investors. UPMC is under fire defending its non-profit tax-exempt status, it is the largest tax-exempt property owner in Allegheny County, with holdings valued at $1.3 billion.  Local politicians and community groups want UPMC to pay a portion of the property taxes it would owe to help with Pittsburgh's budget problems. Critics say that it is unclear what UPMC is spending their money on and that a nonprofit that can afford to advertise and pay their executives millions of dollars should be able to give back to their local community through property tax payments.

headline: Last F&M poll has President Obama holding slim lead over Mitt Romney in Pennsylvania
abstract: According to Franklin & Marshall College's final poll before election day, President Obama maintains a slim lead over Republican challenger Mitt Romney in PA. The poll shows Obama has 49% of the vote to 45% for Romney among likely voters. Obama leads among women, young people and non-white voters and most people surveyed said they believe the President has a better understanding of ordinary Americans and preferred his views on abortion and gay marriage. Romney leads the President in who voters view is most prepared to fix the economy. The Romney campaign and the conservative Croassroads and Restore Our Futre Super PACs are stepping up their advertising buyouts and the Obama administration is countering with its own.

headline: Audio books for the blind to be less accessible in Philly
abstract: The state government has frozen millions in spending and has also taken smaller cost cutting approaches, some of which will have dire consequences for the handicapped. The Philadelphia Regional Library for the Blind and Physically Handicapped will have to lay off about 30 workers and end a number of services. PA State Senator Farnese thinks this is ridiculous.

headline: Two big wind farm projects canceled in the state
abstract: Two major wind development projects located in central PA have been cancelled due to the foreseeable end of the federal Production Tax Credits, a federal program used to stimulate wind farm production. The wind development industry could see a major loss in jobs because of the cut back.

headline: PA town hall meeting protests interrupt Corbett.
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett was in Philadelphia for a town hall meeting at the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Demonstrators representing a number of causes repeatedy interrupted the meeting and police removed ten people and the event ended a half hour early. There were several groups protesting the expansion of the prison system, the Governor's support of natual gas drilling, his social service and education funding proposal cuts and the scheduled October 3rd execution of death-row inmate Terrance Williams.

headline: Officials work to avoid voter glitches
abstract: The election supervisors in Cambria and Somerset counties are working closely with emergency management agencies to make sure voters will be able to cast their ballots Tuesday at the polls even if there would be a prolonged power outage. The counties have backup battery packs for their electronic voting units and if necessary they will provide power for light as some precincts.

headline: Political Prose: We love our fan mail, but this isn't one
abstract: The author mocks a piece of mail that he received from a reader. The writer of the letter asked the author to stop taking such a far left approach. He said that he would soon stop reading the paper and get his friends to stop as well. The author responds, saying that he will say what he likes.

headline: College debt a ticking time bomb — or two, or three
abstract: Barring action from Congress, the interest rate on college debt could double in the next month. Both Congressional Democrats and Republicans support the reduction of the interest rate, but the way to go about reducing the rate is still in question. With college tuition rising and federal and state aid decreasing, families and students could have a more difficult time paying off their college debts.

headline: Census data show poverty on rise in Allegheny County
abstract: The executive director of the North Hills Community Outreach sees the increased poverty rate everyday in Allegheny County. The U.S. Census Bureau shows that Allegheny County's poverty rate has increased to 13.6 percent in 2011 from 12 percent in 2012. Reggie Young, deputy director of Allegheny County's office of community services was surprised at the numbers, he believed PA was doing better in terms of unemployment. However, he said that it is important to not put to much emphasis on any one year's statistic.

headline: Bring in arbitrator for PASSHE faculty contract negotiations
abstract: The PA State System of Higher Education chancellor, John Cavanaugh, denied a request for binding arbitration led by a neutral third party to assess its fairness. Interest arbitration has grown as an alternative to dispute resolution to prevent strikes and lockouts and is an alternative to work stoppages in which case both parties lose. Arbitrators make their decision on what they believe the parties would have agreed to if they were both bargaining "in good faith" and make sure that the collective bargaining agreement is based on what the parties should have agreed to in the interest of "fairness". By refusing outside abitration the chancellor is not acting in good faith.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Grading Corbett's first year: No-tax pledge hurts state
abstract: The author hopes that PA Governor Tom Corbett will soon tackle pressing issues like fixing roads and bridges, or taxing the natural gas industry. He also thinks that he should do something about handgun violence. He thinks that photo ID law is similar to the poll tax.

headline: Parole Board is eager to cut correction costs
abstract: The chairman of the PA Board of Probation and Parole comments on the willingness of the state to cut corrections costs while citing examples of how the state is working to make the prison and parole system more efficient and safe.

headline: Judge may lower 2013 Allegheny County reassessment in poorer towns
abstract: A Senior Common Pleas Judge in Allegheny County is considering a request to lower the 2013 property reassessment in certain economically depressed communities. Don Driscoll, a lawyer for the nonprofit Community Justice Project, put in the request, and his analysis finds that assessed values in areas with low-end homes has increased at a greater rate than high-end homes in at least 22 school districts. Driscoll argues that the county should recalculate the values to ensure that properties within the same school district are uiformly taxed

headline: Flooding in Pennsylvania still a concern from Sandy
abstract: Post-tropical Cyclone Sandy passed through Western PA without too much disturbance. Allegheny County Exec. Rich Fitzgerald said there was no significant flooding from streams or creeks. Also power is being restored to Duquesne Power and West Penn Power customers quite quickly. Snow falling in West Virginia closed a portion I-68. Superstorm Sandy brought the first snowfall of the season to parts of PA. Gov. Corbett said that 1.25 million in PA are without power and more outages could be on the way. Flooding also continued in several places around the state.

headline: Club leaders gather, criticize changes to small games of chance law
abstract: A games of chance law signed by PA Governor Tom Corbett will force small clubs to donate at least 70 percent of gambling proceeds to charities. Club operators look to fight the law in order to save their businesses and their employees' jobs.

headline: Energy: Clear benefits of Obama's forward-looking agenda
abstract: President Obama supports an "all of the above" energy strategy to develop America's natural resources, wind, solar, biofuels, oil, gas, clean coal, and nuclear. In PA the wind sector is supporting 4,000 well-paying jobs and 15 major manufacturing facilities. Companies have expanded in PA that make solar panels, biofuel and better batteries. PA has a 100-year supply of natural gas from shale and PA natural gas jobs have doubled since 2008 to 30,000. President Obama is the better choice in 2012 for president than Mitt Romney who would eliminate incentives for clean renewable energy development and roll back key protections that keep our air and water clean.

headline: Haluska best choice in 73rd
abstract: Gary Haluska is seeking a 10th term in the state legislature for the 73rd district. He says he has served his contituents well and promises to push public-education funding in 2013. Challanger Randall Wilson says Haluska hasn't done enough to promote the interests of small businesses and that after 18 years he has started to lose touch with the people. Haluska serves on the transportation, agriculture, game and fisheries comittees. He claims PA needs $3.5 billion each year for our bridges and highways and tolling major interstates is among the answers to make up that number. Wilson is promising voters he would fight to replace property taxes cut regulations that are hurting small businesses.

headline: Kane out-raises Patrick Murphy in race for Democratic nod for AG.
abstract: Former Lackawanna County prosecutor Kathleen Kane ended 2011 with twice as much campaign cash as former U.S. Rep. Patrick Murphy in the Democratic nomination race for Pennsylvania attorney general.

headline: Fighting your property reassessment? One state LAWMAKER has come up with an alternative
abstract: null

headline: Fake Facebook profiles could be criminalized
abstract: The PA House Juidiciary Committee is scheduled to discuss House Bill 2249 which makes it a misdemeanor to impersonate someone online. The bill's sponsor state Rep. Katherine Watson R-Berks said the bill is targeted to give law enforcement a way to penalize online bullying. The law would make it a crime to impersonate someone using social media or through face email addresses and text messages. The bill has stirred up free speech debates with the PA ACLU saying that the bill fails to withstand the test of the First ammendment and other state reps are not convinced the bill will prevent cyber bullying and are wary of more legislation hampering individual behavior.

headline: Late Night News: Third Legislative District candidates run close race
abstract: null

headline: EDITORIAL: Resolve Allentown NIZ questions
abstract: The author calls on politicians to clear up uncertainty about Allentown’s Neighborhood Improvement Zone, specifically regarding changes to taxation.

headline: Pa.'s public pensions: Runaway gravy train
abstract: The PA pension program for state workers is slated to rise $4 billion by 2016, a problem some are saying will only fiscally derail the state. Gov. Tom Corbett commented that lawmakers will most likely bring up the issue next year.

headline: Pa. voter ID law gets new hearings for next week
abstract: The PA Supreme Court sent back down the disputed voter ID law to a lower court with orders to suspend the enforcement of the law if the lower court finds there is not liberal access to ID's. Opponents of the ID law have filed preliminary junction's arguing that there is already enough evidence to suspend the law. Supporters of the bill believe that any citizen who wans to vote can obtain an ID from PennDOT. Democratic opponents of the law have plans to have countywide branches of the Community College of Allegheny County and Kane Regional Centers, retirement homes, issue free IDs to any resident to help voters obtain ID.

headline: Corbett provides updates on Storm
abstract: null

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At Noon
abstract: State Representative Mark Mustio announced that he will run for State Senator John Pippy's seat.

headline: Trillions at stake in health law case
abstract: Pittsburgh, PA, based health insurer Highmark, along with numerous other health insurance companies have a considerable amount of money resting on the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling on the Affordable Care Act, which looks to extend health insurance or Medicaid to every American. If the law is upheld, insurance companies could gain, while also losing if the law is deemed unconstitutional.

headline: Old Forge teachers attract support at rally
abstract: Teachers, parents, students, union leaders and state lawmakers all gathered together at a rally outside the Old Forge High School to denounce the state budget cuts to education. John Holland the regional field director of the PA State Education Association argued that to pay for Gov. Corbetts $1 billion cut from education, the state should tax Marcellus Shale natural gas drilling corporations and close the Delaware loophole that allows 70 percent of the corporations in PA to pay no tax. Holland and other speakers argued that Republicans want to privatize public education and that not funding education was immoral.

headline: Four Townships Say They’re Still Owed Impact Fee Money
abstract: PA Townships, Cecil, Robinson, South Fayette and Mount Pleasant have had their impact fee payments withheld by the Public Utility Comission. The PUC says it is withholding up to $986,000 in impact fee money until they resolve five requests for review that were filed by four local landowners and by Range Resources, a Texas drilling company that has drilled in PA. These four municipalities have also sued to overturn Act 13 which denies local municipalities from passing their own zoning rules on drilling activity. A PA PUC spokeswoman says that payments are not being withheld because of the legal case.

headline: Pennsylvania employees' unions suggest ways to cut state budget
abstract: State labor unions want legislators to know there are alternatives to the cuts they anticipate seeing in Gov. Tom Corbett’s budget proposal.

headline: April brought better Pa. employment news
abstract: The unemployment rate in PA has hit its lowest point since March of 2009, but average wage numbers have decreased in relation to that same date.

headline: Environmental group presents study on effects of natural gas drilling
abstract: The PennEnvironment Research & Policy Center released a study that detailed the long-term environmental costs that natural gas drilling has on infrastructure, health and the environment. PennEnvironment is calling for a halt to all gas drilling until the gas companies can cover the costs associated with drilling such as health care needs due to exposure from pollutants and the impact on infrastructue.

headline: UPMC growth adds expenses, profit falls
abstract: University of Pittsburgh Medical Center treated more patients and signed up more insurance customers in the last three months of 2011, which pushed revenue for the nonprofit up 15 percent. However, growth came at a cost, as Western Pennsylvania's dominant hospital system reported lower operating income for the quarter, due to rising expenses.

headline: Our view: Harrisburg needs bankruptcy as a leverage tool
abstract: In order to close a $317 million debt loophole, the city of Harrisburg, PA must have multiple financial options from which to draw. These options include bankruptcy and asset selling and leasing, which can be used to bring the city out of its financial woes.

headline: Questions abound at voter ID law forum in Harrisburg
abstract: Community organizers and interest groups from around the state are alerting citizens of the new voter ID law and urging citizens to be prepared for election day. PennDOT has made available free special voting IDs but the issue is whether or not peole can easily secure the photo ID. The PA Supreme Court has sent back down the case to lower court. Republicans support the initiative saying it bolsters the integrity of the election. Mike Turzai R-Allegheny County said the law would allow the presidential canditate Mitt Romney to win PA. Democrats firmly oppose the initiative saying it disenfranchises low-income and urban voters.

headline: WPMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  11PM News
abstract: State Representative Eugene D. DePasquale proposed a bill that would send additional funding to struggling schools.

headline: Radical changes may follow Act 47
abstract: Following the passage of PA Act 47, which gives specific guidelines regarding municipality bankruptcy, the city of Altoona, PA, is facing sweeping changes to the way the city and its finances are run. The city, which is in financial distress, is considering the sale of certain assets and merging with other municipalities.

headline: Report: PA House leaders strip guards of guns
abstract: The PA House of Representatives uniformed guards will be stripped of their firearms after one guard was fired for having a criminal history. This is a reversal of a policy instituted in 2006. Three supervisors were also fired. Security guards for the state senate do not carry weapons. The Capitol Complex is protected by the Capitol police force.

headline: Pat Toomey earmark ban rejected
abstract: U.S. Senator Pat Toomey's effort to permanently ban congressional earmarks fell short in the U.S. Senate, but the Pennsylvania senator said he was heartened that appropriators separately agreed to extend the temporary moratorium through 2013.

headline: Capitol rallies not persuasive, Pennsylvania lawmakers say
abstract: Rallies in the PA Capitol building have become the norm during budget deliberations in the legislature. But these rallies do not persuade lawmakers as other methods like personal calls or letters do, commented numerous members of the PA General Assembly.

headline: Governor Corbett Puts Pension Reform On Priority List
abstract: Gov. Corbett says that pension reform for state workers and teachers is a more important issue than a new transportation funding initiative. Gov. Corbett had made recommendations on new funding for roads, bridges, and mass transit but has not implemented it due to the recession and weak economy. He said that the pension problem takes up more of the general fund budget every year. About $500 million increases every year.

headline: Letters: Reapportionment in Pennsylvania and Latino voting power
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilwoman Maria Quinones-Sanchez discusses the effect of reapportionment on the Latino electorate.

headline: EDITORIAL: I-95 bridge looks like a rainmaker for Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission
abstract: The Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission is planning on renovating one of the most travelled bridges on Interstate 95 near Trenton, New Jersey, but is coming under intense scrutiny from New Jersey and Pennsylvania lawmakers over the reasons for the renovation.

headline: Truth - an early casualty of Voter ID debate
abstract: The statistic of 758,000 PA residents who might lose their right to vote if the voter ID law is put into effect is inaccurate. The number comes from the PA Department of State which compared its list of registered voters to the list of people who have PennDOT ID's. The list included members of Philadelphia City Council and a State Supreme Justice who clearly have drivers licenses and also the list doesn't take into account college student IDs. The number of unregistered voters is more likely one percent of PA residents or 100,000 people. Critics of the law don't need to exagerate the numer which only weakens their credibility.

headline: WOLF-FOX  Wilkes Barre-Scranton, PA  FOX 56 NEWS AT TEN
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has signed a bill that raises prize limits and creates new regulations for small games of chance.

headline: Natural gas price may slow Marcellus drilling
abstract: Marcellus Shale natural gas drilling may slow down in PA after prices for the natural gas have decreased considerably since drilling began. Drilling could slow until demand for the gas once again exceeds the supply.

headline: Voter ID decision seems like common sense
abstract: The PA Supreme court returned to lower court the voter ID law and told Commonwealth Court Judge Robert Simpson to take a closer look and unless hes certain that nobody would be disenfranchised, he should enjoin implementation of the law. The law originally requried voters to have a PennDOT drivers licensce or a PennDOT non-driver ID. The non-driver ID conforms to the Departmet of Homeland Security standards and relatively hard to receive. The PA Department of State has allowed for voter-only ID cards. The PA Supreme Court Justices have instructed Simpson to evaluate whether the deployment of the cards is compatible with the "liberal access" requirement.

headline: John Baer: A Harrisburg snafu
abstract: The author criticizes ethics practices within the state legislature and courts.

headline: Survey: Pa. schools in dire financial straits
abstract: PA's school districts could be facing insolvency within the next few years after a survey was completed within the districts themselves that highlighted the issues. Over half of the state's public schools surveyed expected to be in financial trouble soon, causing programs like art, music and electives to be cut.

headline: Child abuse awareness for PA's K-8 curricula?
abstract: In the wake of the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse scandal there is a bipartisan initiative to bring child abuse awareness into lesson plans for PA schools. School Districts would have the option of whether to teach children how to recognize child abuse and protect themselves from it. The PA Department of Education would create a model curricula for kindergarden through eigth grade said Rep. Gingrich.

headline: Adams commissioners question casino buffer
abstract: The Adams County Commissioners are challenging legislation that would block a casino from opening near the Gettysburg battlefield.

headline: Name that chemical
abstract: Marcellus Shale drilling companies are now required to disclose the chemicals used in the hydrofracturing procedure when performed on public lands. Hydrofracturing, fracking, is the process in which natural gas is released from the shale. The federal mandate also gives guidelines for proper well installment and wastewater disposal measures.

headline: Pa. public schools reject scholarship program
abstract: The Opportunity Scholarship Tax Credit Program was passed with the PA budget last year. The program gives poor children in poorly performing schools up to $8500 in scholarships, $15,000 for special eduation and gives businesses tax credits for donating money to the program. Only four schools in the entire state are participating in the program. School districts are wary of the program saying that it will only help a few children and that they might not be reimbursed for taking in extra students. They are also concernced that the children might bring down test scores and make their exam statistics look worse.

headline: Marcellus shale, smokeless tobacco taxes can wait, but taxpayers must ante up for online purchases?
abstract: The author criticizes the tax policies of the Corbett administration regarding online sales given the lack of attention paid to that on natural gas and smokeless tobacco.

headline: Marcellus Shale Coalition touts industry's success in Pennsylvania at Capitol rally
abstract: The Marcellus Shale Coalition commented positively on the economic growth that Shale drilling has brought to the state of PA. However, new economic news has shown that the decline in natural gas prices here has since hurt local municipalities who have lost business as production slows.

headline: Penna.'s elusive political landscape
abstract: President Obama is leading Mitt Romney in the polls but the political landscape of PA has changed a bit since the last presidential election. The PA unemployment rate is at 8.1 percent and the poverty rate has gone up to 12 percent. Counties west and north of the Appalachian mountains which rely heavilly on manufacturing have become more republican and areas south and east are becoming more democratic and growing. Monroe County in the Poconos has seen a spike in population led by hispanic migration. The number of registered voters has declined 5 percent since 2008 and the state has gotten relatively older. The GOP has captured the governors office and the state house and senate. Some PA trends benefit Republicans and some benefit Democrats.

headline: WBRE-NBC  Wilkes Barre-Scranton, PA  28 NEWS AT 9
abstract: State Senator Mike Stack wants to ensure state money doesn’t go toward financing Jerry Sandusky's criminal defense.

headline: Fitzgerald vows transit changes
abstract: The Allegheny County, PA, Executive said the financially troubled Port Authority transit agency will be changed under his watch. The Port Authority is facing major financial renovation following a projected $64 million budget deficit.

headline: The state court assignment: Keep the vote for real
abstract: The enactment of the PA voter ID law is a legitimate measure to protect the privilege of voting in the US. Efforts have made to get people ID's and they have been educated about what to expect on election day. Purchases made by credit card usually require ID and there is no concern over this practice. The state Supreme Court has ordered a lower court judge to halt implementation of the voter ID law if he thinks voters will be disenfranchised, however this editorial contends that people can easily acquire ID.

headline: Pennsylvania lawmakers agree on bill to impose a fee for gas drilling
abstract: A joint House-Senate committee agreed Monday night on a bill to impose an "impact fee" on natural gas drilling in Pennsylvania, moving the long-debated fee a giant step closer to final passage.

headline: Obama leads Pa. by 8 points, new poll finds
abstract: A new poll produced by Public Policy Polling found President Obama leading Gov. Mitt Romney by a considerable margin here in PA. PA Gov. Tom Corbett holds unfavorable approval numbers while former state Gov. Tom Ridge remains the most popular politician from the state.

headline: Student PSSA achievement drops, officials cite efforts to curb cheating
abstract: The PA Education Secretary has led an effort to curb cheating on the PSSA exams which has resulted in a lower overall percentage of proficient and advanced students. A state report in 2011 indicated that test scores in 48 districts and charter schools were higher than expected and after investigation, they found alterations in bubble sheets dating back to 2008.

headline: Corps to spend $16.9 million to deepen the Delaware
abstract: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will allocate $16.9 million this year to deepening the Delaware River's main shipping channel by five feet.

headline: Financial outlook for Pennsylvania schools in crisis stage, survey shows
abstract: A survey performed by a majority of PA's public schools shows major financial issues within the state's schools, issues that will require program and staff cuts. Nearly half of the surveyed schools projected some sort of financial trouble within the next few years unless the state or federal government intervenes.

headline: Middletown aids struggling budget with electricity revenue
abstract: State Sen. Tim Solobay, D-Washington County, sponsored a bill that puts municipally owned electrical companies under control of the PA Public Utility Commission, the same as investor-owned companies. PA has thirty-five municipally owned electrical systems. Solobay did this because Middletown, PA had raised power rates to meet obligations in their general budget as do many of these municipalities who run electrical systems. To prorect consumers there needs to be a system of checks and balances on these municipalities says Solobay.

headline: Equal pay legislation evens playing field
abstract: Mary Isenhour expresses support for equal pay for women.

headline: Former CalU president chastises university system over firing
abstract: Former California University of PA president Angelo Armenti, Jr. says his treatment and firing by the State System of Higher Education violated his contract. Mr. Armenti grew California University while serving as president, but growing financial concerns are said to be the reasons behind his firing.

headline: Court to examine Legislature's intent in section of state's Dog Law
abstract: The PA state Supreme Court granted allocatur to a case over whether the PA Dog Law, a criminal statute, creates a strict liability offense. In an earlier case the justices sought to determine whether the PA General Assembly intended a section of the Dog Law be viewed as creating srict liability. Does the owner of an errant dog have to fail to exercise reasonable efforts to confine the dog and does he have to possess a "mens rea" or guilty mind, to be found liable? Two lower courts have said no saying it would frustrate the legislative intent behind the law if a "reasonable care" standard were to be utilized. If the strict liability standard were to be used for the Dog Law than a person is legally responsible for all damages regardless of reasonable care to prevent the damages.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  10PM NEWS
abstract: PA Senate President pro tempore Joe Scarnati says that Pennsylvania should be prepared for an exhaustive debate on how to best use tax dollars in anticipation of budget cuts in the coming year.

headline: Senators grill company over problems with statewide radio network
abstract: A four-member panel of PA state Senators questioned a technology company in charge of the statewide police radio-network system. The radio system, although costing upwards of $368 million and recently installed, is still inoperable in certain regions of the state, a problem that brought the two parties together.

headline: Some say plan to issue Pennsylvania voter IDs flawed
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Rich Fitzgerald declared the Community College of Allegheny County and Kane Regional Centers as places for citizens to attain voter ID. Legal observors said the plan exploits a loophole in the states new voter ID law which mandates that voters show photo ID at the polls and allows accredited colleges and senior centes to issue IDs. Originally intended for college students and seniors, this loophole is being looked at by many counties across PA as a way to increase access to voter IDs.

headline: Impact fee bill wins final approval
abstract: State lawmakers wrapped up a lengthy political battle by giving final approval to a bill establishing a so-called county-option Marcellus Shale drilling impact fee and state review of local drilling ordinances.

headline: Hines Ward honored by PA House
abstract: The PA House of Representatives along with Gov. Tom Corbett honored former Pittsburgh Steelers great, Hines Ward for his on-field performance as well as his community service within the commonwealth.

headline: Students urge Pa. state lawmakers to pass charter school reform bill
abstract: Hundreds of students and families gathered at the state Capitol to urge lawmakers to pass the charter school reform bill that had been stalled for a year. The bill would provide for charter schools to receive money directly from the state instead of through school districts where their students live. It would create a state panel to oversee charters and would make it easier for school district buildings to be converted into charter schools. Supporters believe that charter schools are more effective than public schools and their support should be increased by the state.

headline: Pennsylvania House Majority Leader Turzai calls for new controls on state borrowing
abstract: House Majority Leader Mike Turzai has introduced a bill designed to put new limits on state borrowing, one of the major sources of state aid for capital projects around Pennsylvania. Turzai's plan would gradually lower the debt ceiling for the state Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program from the current $4.05 billion to $1.5 billion, the level it was at when former Gov. Ed Rendell took office in 2003.

headline: Birth certificate rule dropped for PA voter IDs.
abstract: All potential votes will not be required to produce their birth certificate in order to get a free form of identification from a PennDOT location, explained the PA Gov. Tom Corbett administration. This ruling follows the PA voter-ID law, which requires all voters to produce some form of identification upon voting.

headline: Carefully craft online ID law
abstract: Rep. Kathryn Watson R-Berks County has introduced a bill making online impersonation a misdemeanor in an effort to stop cyber-bullying. She contends the bill will not impinge on First Ammendment rights because it requires prosecutors to prove criminal intent to do harm by the impersonator. She says the bill would allow for satire, parody, and harmless joking. The complexity of the english language and misinterpretations of it make crafting the law a tough endeavor.

headline: Educators criticize proposed PA schools funding.
abstract: Educators who say they are still grappling with about $860 million in state cuts this year are criticizing proposed school funding levels in next year's budget, which they contend will cause more hardship on districts statewide.

headline: Highmark, UPMC stature worries Westmoreland lawmaker
abstract: The current contract dispute between western PA's largest hospital and health insurance provider could impact community health centers across the region, concerning some local lawmakers in the process.

headline: New approach to nonprofits paying property taxes taking shape
abstract: UPMC is a non-profit hospital system that has avoided paying property taxes. This year UPMC voluntarily agreed to pay South Fayette the equivalent of taxes on 50 percent of the assessend value of a property it was buying. Allegheny County wants UPMC to make a similar agreement with the county on an agreement for its new Children's Hospital in Lawrenceville. Other communities want UPMC to do PILOT, payement in lieu of taxes, programs to increase their revenue streams.

headline: Lincoln U. president glad cuts were less than those for other state-related schools
abstract: Lincoln University president Robert R. Jennings was happy to learn that his university's funding would be maintained in the new budget. Other state-related schools received major cuts to their annual subsidy.

headline: Harrisburg School District students, parents and staff send message to legislators: 'Save our schools'
abstract: A group of Harrisburg students, teachers and parents rallied at the state Capitol to voice their concern about the city's public schools. The school district within Harrisburg has come upon financial struggle and needs help from the state in order to continue what they see as essential programs.

headline: How did GOP group fund AG race TV ad? Ask Gov. Corbett
abstract: The Republican State Leadership Committee has deep pockets around the country to launch attack ads at democratic canditates as they utilizing in the PA Attorney General race. Gov. Corbett was the headline guest this summer at a fundraiser for the RSLC where the suggested contribution was $5,000. The RSLC ran an ad slamming Democrat canditate Kathleen Kane as soft on rape. They spent $558,700 on a commercial about Kane on four Philadelphia television stations this week.

headline: WBRE-NBC  Wilkes Barre-Scranton, PA  28 NEWS AT 11
abstract: State Representative Bill DeWeese hopes to run for re-election, despite his conviction on corruption charges. He is looking to delay his sentencing until after he is able to do so.

headline: Five years in jail possible for felons who arm themselves
abstract: PA legislators passed a bill that would mandate a minimum prison sentence for felons who possess an illegal firearm. The bill awaits the Governor's signature to become law.

headline: PennDOT license centers to be open the day before Election Day
abstract: PennDOT has worked closely with the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees, the union representing its Driver Licensing Center employees. They have reached an agreement to open forty-eight PennDOT centers normally closed on Mondays. The centers will be open Monday, Nov. 5 to better serve customers with last-minute voter ID needs. Photo IDs might be needed for votes to count after Gov. Tom Corbett signed the voter ID law in March, 2012.

headline: WPSG-CW  Philadelphia, PA  EYEWITNESS NEWS
abstract: Some social service agencies are concerned by the funding cuts in Governor Tom Corbett's proposed budget.

headline: Seat belt enforcement effort under way
abstract: PA Department of Transportation, along with state and local police forces, have joined the national "Click it or Ticket" campaign. Seat belt laws will be heavily enforced through the busy Memorial Day, along with the primary seat-belt law for drivers and passengers younger than 18.

headline: Newly passed bill will allow mining and drilling near state-owned institutions
abstract: The PA state House passed a bill to allow the leasing of mineral rights on some state-owned lands, allowing for natural-gas exploration, coal mining, and quarrying limestone around universities, prisons and other state institutions. Supporters of the bill say it will provide new revenue streams for state agencies and some of the funds will be set aside for scholarships. Opponents feel that college campuses are improper places for industrial activity. It is unknown how much land might be leased but several universities are directly atop the Marcellus Shale.

headline: PA to get $266 million from foreclosure abuse settlement.
abstract: A landmark settlement with the nation's biggest mortgage lenders over foreclosure abuses will deliver about $266 million in aid to the state for struggling homeowners or people who lost their homes.

headline: Special-needs education is battleground for charter schools, other districts in Pa.
abstract: Public schools within PA are concerned over the propensity of charter schools to attract special needs children. Coupled with the increase in special needs students in the state's public schools and the decrease in state funding, special needs education has become a contentious and challenging issue within the PA public school system.

headline: Parents of autistic children protest new Pa. co-pays for care
abstract: The state Department of Public Welfare is now requiring co-payments from families who receive free services for children with autism and related disorders. Several dozen parents and democratic legislators rallied on Tuesday agaisnt the decision which affects 48,000 children. The plan has families earning more than $45,000 a year paying from $1-$3 in co-pays per service. Opponents of the bill say that families will have to choose between paying for therapy and making a mortgage payment. The Welfare Secretary said that no other state offers such generous services. In the last 18 months the state has slashed programs such as health insurance for the working poor and reduced access to food stamps.

headline: Pentagon fails to back its case
abstract: Air Force officials who met with the Pittsburgh area's congressional delegation could not offer a written analysis or other documentation to support their decision to close the Air Force Reserve's 911th Airlift Wing in Moon.

headline: War on women's health: Does Rep. Metcalfe speak for Pa. Republicans?
abstract: A PA representative is looking to cut funding to Planned Parenthood in a measure being debated before the House of Representatives. The proposed cut in funding is drawing the ire from some, who see Planned Parenthood as an essential program within the state.

headline: Pa. officials tout promise of public-private transportation partnerships
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett signed House Bill 3 which authorizes public-private partnerships to improve transportation facilities. He said the law will stimulate private investment in public highways, bridges and other facilities and advance progects the government can't afford on its own. Gov. Corbett admitted that PA annually comes up short in the amount of money needed to fund the transporation system. Under this plan private companies could potentially build express lanes and collect tolls from drivers who use them.

headline: Corbett budget slams state Department of Agriculture
abstract: Josh Mrozinski describes the effect of Governor Tom Corbett's budget cuts on agriculture, using farmer Paul Manning as a case example.

headline: Bill would use taxes to push drillers to hire Pennsylvanians
abstract: A bill introduced in the PA House of Representatives looks to create a tax credit program for Marcellus Shale drilling companies who hire in-state workers. The bill follows a report by Penn State University and PA College of Technology that states less PA workers were hired for Marcellus Shale natural gas-related jobs than originally anticipated.

headline: Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center calls voter ID implementation flawed
abstract: The PA Budget and Policy Center conducted a survey from Sept. 10-17 and found signage and knowledge of the new voter ID law to be lacking. About nine of ten centers had some information available about the voter ID law but a quarter of the centers made information hard to find. PennDOT employees are also not familiar with the process of obtaining state voter ID cards. The PA Department of State recently eased requirements and shortened the process for obtaining the cards but PennDOT employees will now have to learn the new rules which could cause further problems.

headline: DA to legislators: OK disclosure bill
abstract: Brett Hambright describes the process leading up to the introduction of a bill requiring that background records be made available to potential employers of educators.

headline: COMMENTARY: PA pensions infect budget talks this year and years to come
abstract: PA pension programs for public workers has become a major issue in budget talks within the Capitol. The Independent Fiscal Office expects pension payments to take up at least 12 percent of the state's budget, a fact some people see leading to financial calamity.

headline: Rachel Carson's book turned the environmental world on its ear 50 years ago
abstract: "Silent Spring" was published 50 years ago and is one of the most influential and controversial books of the 20th century. Rachel Carson's book about the dangers and risks of excessive pesticide use is credited with creating the modrn environmental movement, the creation of the EPA, Earth Day, and passage of the Clean Air and Clean Water Acts. Carson grew up in Sprindale Borough in the Allegheny River valley which lies on the edge of industrial Pittsburgh.

headline: PMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  10PM News
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett toured a Lancaster factory to talk about his new budget and how it will reflect the needs of local businesses.

headline: Rep. Mann helps celebrate Memorial Day
abstract: PA state Representative Jennifer Mann helped kick off Memorial Day celebrations in Allentown, PA.

headline: PennDot awards $39.3M contract for I-95 work in Philadelphia
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation awarded a $39.3 million contract to rebuild a stretch of I-95 south of the Girard Avenue interchange. The contract is the third of six contracts to improve the Girard interchange and rebuild three-miles of I-95 between Race Street and Allegheny Avenue. PennDOT says construction is to begin later in the fall and to be finished by spring of 2015. The work is financed with 90 percent federal funds and 10 percent state funds.

headline: WTAE-ABC  Pittsburgh, PA  Ch. 4 Action News At 6
abstract: State Representative Marc Gergely contests the idea that failing charter schools should be closed.

headline: Statewide radio system's dead air continues to cost Pennsylvania money
abstract: The statewide radio network installed for the PA Police State Police Department has yet to live up to lawmaker and police expectations. The faulty system has now required the installation of a backup radio system, the costs of which to build take away from other police programs and jobs.

headline: As debate looms, Romney looks to PA.
abstract: Mitt Romney is looking to PA to help win the presidential election. He was campaigning Friday in the Philadelphia area, courting donors at a high-dollar fundraiser and then meeting voters midday at a rally. The campaign is not running any ads in PA, a state that has not supported a Republican presidential canditate in a quarter century. Romney is largely in PA to raise money to use in more competitive swing states. President Obama and Gov. Mitt Romney will meet in their first debate in Denver.

headline: Pension bill could reduce county taxpayer contribution
abstract: House Republicans and Democrats united to pass a bill that would tighten pension eligibility provisions and raise the minimum years of service for future county employees.

headline: Early emergence of West Nile causes concern
abstract: The West Nile virus, found in infected mosquitos, has made its earliest emergence in parts of PA, causing concern for many residents. The mild winter, coupled with the warm spring and hot summer have been blamed for the deadly virus's early appearance.

headline: Judge in Pa. voter ID case mulling option to throw out the law for the upcoming election
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Robert Simpson is debating whether or not to strike down the voter ID law. He said that rather than blocking the law, one of his ideas is to allow voters lacking ID to cast provisional ballots and still have their vote count. He said that this would determine how many voters don't have IDs and where they are. Alicia Hickok, a Philadelphia attorney respresenting the commonwealth supports this measure and said the provisional ballots would be counted if the people produce an acceptable photo ID to election officials within six days or by November 13, 2012. The PA ACLU argue that use of provisional ballots sends the wrong message to voters and will lead people to not vote.

headline: Former state representative seeks Senate seat
abstract: Former state representative Tim Seip has decided to run for state senate.

headline: Corbett rankles senator in nominating William Ward, former chief of staff, to Allegheny Court of Common Pleas
abstract: The former Chief of Staff to PA Governor Tom Corbett has been nominated to the Allegheny Court of Common Pleas by the Governor himself. Senate Democrats, however, hold issue with the Governor's selection, commenting on the validity of nominating a close ally and friend to a court position.

headline: Duquesne City schools won't fight state
abstract: The PA Department of Education has made a preliminary decision to place the Duquesne City School District in financial recovery status. The district will not contest the state's decision. Ron Tomalis the Education Secretary can now appoint a chief recovery officer for the district within five days. If a declaration is made the elected board of the Duquesne district would return to their positions but not have much power. According to the fiscal distress legislation, the elected board must decide within 14 days of the chief recovery officer's appointment whether to cooperate with the officer. If they do not, the matter will go to Common Pleas Court, where a receiver will be named for the district.

headline: Political Prose: The GOP's week to remember come November
abstract: J.D. Prose criticizes Governor Tom Corbett's budget as one that caters to campaign donors while neglecting the needs of the poor.

headline: Speed kills: Drivers don't need a reason to go faster on Pa. Turnpike
abstract: A bill being considered within the PA legislature would allow the PA Turnpike Commission to raise its top speed limit to 70 miles-per-hour. Studies have shown that higher speeds on major highways leads to more accidents and deaths, numbers some see as important to the debate about the measure.

headline: Fitzgerald says Bill Peduto filed to run for mayor, donates to campaign
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Rich Fitzgerald contrbuted a $8,000 donation to People for Peduto, in support of Pittsburgh Councilman Bill Peduto who is running for mayor. His contribution was the maximum allowable contribution under the city's campaign finance law. Fitzgerald is supporting Peduto after months of rocky relations wth current Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Raven-stahl. They have been fighting over Fitzgerald's plan to use Regional Asset District money for the Port Authority and his decision to raise property taxes in 2011. The democratic primary all but decides the mayoral race in Pittsburgh.

headline: Pa. Legislature stays busy by passing resolutions
abstract: The author describes the behavior of the Pennsylvania General Assembly regarding the passage of resolutions.

headline: PA pension reform for future employees not enough
abstract: The lingering pension crisis with PA state workers has led the PA legislature to mull the idea of switching from a defined benefit pension plan to a defined contribution plan. The switch in pension plans would not guarantee a balanced pension plan in the present.

headline: Drilling concerns deserve respect
abstract: The Marcellus Shale Coalition gathered at their annual conference in Philadelphia last week. They emphasized that the gas industry was at the cusp of a breakthrough that would provide cheap domestic gas and kick-start American manufacturing, provide stability to the nation's economy and enhance national security. They also emphasized that the gas industry could have done more to promote itself and educate the public about the safety of its operations. There is a lot of domestic opposition to gas drilling with protestors turning out to the PA Convention Center on Sept. 20th to protest the Coalition at their annual conference and 200 residents of Luzerne County protest the building of a new pipeline.

headline: WJET-ABC  Erie, PA  Late Night News
abstract: State representative John Hornaman has announced that he will not seek re-election. The timing of his announcement has been criticized.

headline: Governor signs three execution warrants
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed three execution orders, one of which was for a man guilty of ordering the deaths of a woman and her young child.

headline: Rendell lays it on pretty thick
abstract: Former Gov. Ed Rendell was in Harrisburg on the eve of the state's second hearing on the voter ID law. He said that people owe a great deal of gratitude to Rep. Mike Turzai for telling the truth, when he said, in June, the bill would deliver the state of PA to Gov. Mitt Romney in the upcoming presidential election. Rendell gave mocking praise to Rep. Turzai and said that his comments prove that the bill was not passed to genuinely prevent voter fraud.

headline: City students ask governor to make education a priority
abstract: Several Pittsburgh students went to Harrisburg to appeal to Governor Tom Corbett for more school funding.

headline: Governor Corbett Says Doctors’ Concerns Over Act 13 May Be “Moot”
abstract: A controversial confidentiality agreement found in PA Act 13, the law centered around Marcellus Shale zoning issues, has worried some doctors in the area. The law forces doctors to sign confidentiality agreements when requesting information on drilling chemicals when treating patients, a fact Governor Corbett was unaware of.

headline: Judge says injunction "possible" in voter ID case
abstract: Judge Robert Simpson after hearing testimony for a second time on the state's voter ID case asked lawyers at the end of the proceedings to be ready to suggest what kind of injunction would be appropriate. Lawyers defending the voter ID law say an injunction is unnecessary due to new changes by PennDOT that no longer require applicants to claim that they previously tried and failed to get a PennDOT license. Challengers to the voter ID law say that the new system has not been in place long enough for people to get the new IDs and there will still be disenfranchisement.

headline: Yaw calls gas impact fee fair, reasonable
abstract: State Sen. E. Eugene Yaw, R-Loyalsock Township, told the Lycoming County Council of Republican Women that the state now has a natural gas impact fee that is fair and reasonable.

headline: Pennsylvanians get slice of Skechers settlement
abstract: The shoe-maker, Skechers is forced to pay $143,000 total to PA residents for deceptive marketing techniques used to sell their brand of Shape-Up shoes.

headline: What happens next in the execution process for Terrance Williams
abstract: PA's first state execution since 1999 is scheduled for October 3, at 7 p.m. at a state prison. Terrance Williams is scheduled to be put to death by lethal injection for murdering a Philadelphia man in 1984 as an 18-year-old. The death warrant was signed because Williams had exhausted the appeals process. The state Board of Pardons is meeting to vote whether to reconsider a clemency appeal by Williams which would change the death sentence to a life-in-prison sentence. Williams claims he was sexually abused by the men he killed. The Governor cannot act without the Pardon board's approval but he can grant a temporary reprieve. A judge in Philadelphia will decide whether Williams sexual abuse warrants the death sentence be revoked.

headline: At Penn State, sign of change
abstract: The author expressed interest in the disclosure of costs of on-campus memorial services for Penn State football coach Joe Paterno.

headline: DeWeese’s Attorney Talks About Former State Representative’s Release
abstract: The attorney for the former PA Speaker of the House, Bill DeWeese, spoke about his clients 4 day ordeal in state prison. DeWeese is appealing his conviction and sentencing of 2 and a half to 5 years prison sentence, following corruption charges that stemmed from state time being spent on his re-election campaign.

headline: Spanier facing charges in abuse case at Penn State
abstract: Former Penn State University President Graham Spanier has been charged with perjury and obstruction of justice in the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse scandel. Mr. Spanier had denied any knowledge of Sandusky's misconduct.

headline: WICU-NBC  Erie, PA  Evening News
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett's budget proposal cuts funding for state universities.

headline: House caps budget plan at $27.6 billion
abstract: The PA House of Representatives issued a spending cap on the current years budget plan. The cap exceeds the Governor's budget proposal figure while making some Democrats in the legislature unhappy.

headline: Mullery touts service
abstract: Democratic State Rep. Gerald Mullery is running for a second term. Mullery says he is proud that his office is one of the top 10 busiest in the state according to the Constituent Tracking Service. He boasts that he got an amendment to the desk of Gov. Corbet on a measure that allows the Office of Victim Advocate to expand its duties to juvenile court. He wants to lower state corporate taxes but increase state sales taxs.

headline: Latino group says it’ll fight any ruling to base election on ’01 legislative districts
abstract: Advocates for Latino voters in Pennsylvania said they’ll sue if the rejection of the latest state legislative redistricting plan means the 2012 elections will be based on districts set in 2001.

headline: Bill would streamline process to remove flood hazards in PA
abstract: A bill found within the PA House of Representatives looks to eliminate flood hazards throughout the commonwealth. Following the historic flooding of the prior year, some lawmakers see this issue as dire.

headline: State Senate candidates McNally, Teplitz find little to agree on
abstract: John McNally and Rob Teplitz are running for state senate to represent a district that is most of Dauphin County. Teplitz is a democrat and long-time politician, McNally is a Republican and long-time businessman. Both men say education is their top priority. The two disagree over how to deal with Harrisburg's $340 million incerator debt and the city's financial problems. They also disagree over the voter ID law, abortion, and permitting the use of medical marijuana.

headline: Corbett Signs Law Requiring Motorists To Share The Road With Cyclists
abstract: Governor Corbett has signed a bill that creates new regulations addressing how vehicles and bicycles share Pennsylvania roadways.

headline: PAC Group To Launch Anti-Corbett Television Ad
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is facing attack ads from a Washington-based political action committee. Although Gov. Corbett is not in the middle of a re-election campaign, the PAC is launching the ads to lobby against who they call "one of the worst governors in the country."

headline: Little opposition for incumbent state lawmakers this year
abstract: Many of the 253-member PA General assembly incumbents are running unopposed. With 25 state senators of 50 total and 96 state House members lacking competition. Re-election rates in PA are between 95-98 percent. District lines in PA have not been updated to 2010 standards because they are being challenged in state Supreme Court. Third party candidates are usually discouraged from running because they have to obtain many more signatures than major-party candidates.

headline: Costa & Pileggi speak on redistricting opinion
abstract: The majority and minority leaders of the state Senate expressed their opinions on the redistricting opions made by the Supreme Court.

headline: April unemployment figures show job losses in midstate's rural areas
abstract: PA's unemployment rate fell a tenth of a percentage point since the previous month, although unemployment numbers got worse in rural areas across the state.

headline: Musto appeals ruling on trial
abstract: Former state Sen. Raphael Musto appealed a judge's ruling that denied his request to postpone his corruption trial and to dismiss new charges filed agaisnt him. Musto was indicted in November, 2010 on charges that he accepted $35,000 and other things of value from a developer.

headline: Gov. Tom Corbett Defends His Budget
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has responded to critics of is proposed budget, defending it.

headline: Penn State President Rodney Erickson sets out to heal university
abstract: Penn State President Rodney Erickson has stated that he wants the greatest legacy of his presidency to be the repair of the damage done to Penn State by the Jerry Sandusky child abuse scandal.

headline: Governor gets look at efforts to restore electricity
abstract: null

headline: Norquist’s Group Opposes Impact Fee
abstract: Americans for Tax Reform, who created the no-net-tax-hike pledge Gov. Tom Corbett signed in the 2010 campaign, says the Marcellus Shale fee deal struck by Corbett and legislative leaders is a pledge-breaking tax.

headline: Legislature must show fiscal constraint -- now more than ever?
abstract: State Representative Stephen asserts that fiscal discipline the 2012-2013 state budget is imperative, and criticizes the general assembly for adding new spending.

headline: Governor says early planning was key to storm response
abstract: null

headline: PA House GOP puts brakes on ultrasound bill
abstract: After witnessing criticism in Virginia over a mandate forcing women seeking abortions to have an ultrasound of their fetus, the PA House of Representatives put on hold a similar bill. Concerns stemming from the medical community over the content of the bill also led to the halting of the measure, while Republican House members promised a full vetting process before further consideration.

headline: Ferlo joins UPMC unionizing effort
abstract: Jim Ferlo, the Democratic state senator and University of Pittsburgh Medical Center antagonist, has entered the campaign to unionize nonclinical staff at the region's largest health system.

headline: U.S. Attorney's office is reviewing request from Pa. lawmakers to investigate Tom Corbett's handling of Jerry Sandusky's case
abstract: PA democrats, Mike Hanna and Mike Dermody put in a request to the U.S. Attorney General's Office to investigate Gov. Corbett's pace and handling of the Jerry Sandusky case while he served as PA attorney general.

headline: Six Pennsylvania House seats to be filled in April
abstract: Six empty seats within the PA House of Representatives will be filled after an April 24 special election, the state Supreme Court stated. The House Speaker Sam Smith argued that legally the elections would have to wait until after reapportionment of the state's legislative districts, but the Supreme Court voted to compel the election earlier.

headline: End of school property tax top issue at Schwank forum
abstract: Elimination of the school property tax dominated the conversation at a town hall meeting Thursday. State Senator Judy Schwank co-sponsored a proposal by state Senator David G. Argall to increase the sales tax to 7 percent from 6 percent, with the tax charged on more items, and increase the personal income tax to 4 percent from 3.07 percent.

headline: Shuster’s opponent lacks proficiency
abstract: Karen Ramsburg of Mercersburg, Franklin County is running against republican U.S. House member Bill Shuster for the 9th district. Shuster serves on the House Transportation, Infrastructure, and Armed Services committees. Ramsburg is opposed to fracking for natural gas, opposed to privatizing public schools and says fossil fuels are outdated but PA shouldn't leave the coal industry high and dry. She also said that she has a totally separate plan for health-care modeled after the Veterans Administration hospitals.

headline: 50-year-old gas drilling lease challenged
abstract: A couple in western Pennsylvania is suing a natural gas drilling company over damages stemming from improperly claimed land. Range Resources, the drilling company, claimed drilling and production rights to over 150 acres of the couple's land, resulting from a lease of the property over fifty years old. The couple is challenging the validity of their claim.

headline: WJET-ABC  Erie, PA  Late Night News
abstract: State Representative Curt Sonney seeks to make the mushroom Pennsylvania's official state food in response to a petition.

headline: Freed campaign launches attack ad in state AG race.
abstract: Republican candidate for PA attorney general David Freed launched a 30-second spot attack ad against Democrat Kathleen Kane. The ad attacks Kane for erroneously claiming she was endorsed by the PA State Troopers Assocation and for accepting campaign contributions from special interset groups after criticizing the practice during the primary. Kane is sponsored by organized labor and Philadelphia trial lawyers while Freed is being supported by conservative third-party politcal action comittees.

headline: Cambria officials briefed on new gas drilling rules
abstract: Cambria County, PA, officials were informed of the responsibilities dealing with Marcellus Shale drilling, as well as the benefits in store for all municipalities. The new PA law concerning Marcellus Shale gas extraction took away much of municipality power, but local officials spoke on the importance of a strong partnership between these municipalities and county governments.

headline: Experts say forgery may send ex-Sen. Orie to prison.
abstract: Legal experts say former Republican state Sen. Jane Orie could learn that cover-ups are often more damaging than the underlying crimes when she's sentenced Monday on charges she used her state-funded legislative staff to perform campaign work and covered up her misdeeds with forged documents.

headline: Voter turnout: Options are needed to boost numbers
abstract: Under 20 percent of registered voters cast a ballot in the last primary on April 24. PA could boost its turnout by joining other states in supporting crossover voting among parties as well as allowing independents to vote in either primary. Other states are allowing people to mail or vote in person up to two weeks ahead of election day which would also boost turnout. However both parties do not have an interest in boosting turnout because fewer people voting gives greater influence to the party organizations.

headline: Citation from a state Representative
abstract: An elderly Wilkes-Barre woman celebrated her 92nd birthday on leap year, making her only 23 in terms of leap years. She received many gifts from grandchildren and children, as well as an official citation from a PA state Representative.

headline: Law targets sudden cardiac arrests in young
abstract: Lawmakers who engineered the new legislation requiring closer attention to sudden cardiac arrest say the policy will be user-friendly for coaches and students. The law will create a one-stop shop for information about sudden cardiac arrest on the state Department of Health's website and require coaches to learn about the condition that kills 7,000 high school and young adult athletes every year.

headline: Spanier lawyers speak out against Gov. Corbett
abstract: null

headline: Will Pa. judges merit selection in future?
abstract: Supreme Court elections in PA have reached a new record in campaign fundraising. PA remains one of only six states to elect all judges, but two new bills considered in the state House of Representatives work to build a merit-selection system to choose new state justices, creating a 15 member commission whose purpose is to screen and choose potential justices. If passed, the proposal would require a constitutional amendment as well as a public referendum.

headline: Panel looks to help planes take off easier
abstract: Washington County Representative Peter J. Daley thinks Pennsylvania's aviation industry could grow if the state stopped levying taxes on airplane sales and maintenance work. His opponents say the cash-strapped state cannot afford to forgo any available tax revenue and should not give tax breaks to people who can afford to buy private planes.

headline: Attorney General says potential case against Paterno ‘closed’ because he’s deceased
abstract: null

headline: PA speaker to set elections for six House vacancies
abstract: Speaker Sam Smith of the PA House of Representatives was critical of a PA Supreme Court ruling forcing the House to schedule special elections to fill six vacancies within the body. Speaker Smith had wanted to wait until new legislative reapportionment maps were passed into law, but the Supreme Court ordered the elections to be done on April 24, along with the primaries.

headline: Former Sen. Orie gets prison in corruption case.
abstract: Former Republican state Senator Jane Orie was ordered to serve 2 1/2 to 10 years in state prison for using her taxpayer-funded legislative staff to do campaign work and forging defense exhibits to try to cover it up.

headline: Bill Clinton to barnstorm PA for Obama, Democrats.
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton will campaign across PA the day before the election to shore up this battleground state. Clinton will start in Pittsburgh then head to Montgomery County and Philadelphia, and end in Scranton, the hometown of VP Joe Biden, U.S. Sen. Bob Casey and Attorney General nominee Kathleen Kane.

headline: PSU trustees debate changes to board
abstract: As Penn State prepares to overhaul its board of trustees, the board convened to discuss possible changes that will be up for a vote in September. Some of the changes include changing the size of the board and adding faculty, student and alumni association trustees.

headline: Fish agency eyes Moon Lake Park changes
abstract: A Luzerne County, PA, park was set to close for five days out of every week due to the shortage of park security workers. The news comes at the time of trout fishing season, causing a public uproar over the closing. The PA Fish and Boat Commission hopes to talk the county into keeping the park open to fishers, because of the large number of trout with it had hoped to stock the park.

headline: Hold 'em or fold 'em | How long will gambling pay off?
abstract: The author ponders the future benefits and drawbacks of legalized gambling in Pennsylvania, and whether or not it will continue to be worthwhile for the state.

headline: Win or lose, this is it for Obama.
abstract: This election will be President Obama's last whether he wins or loses. He is traveling to the same towns and cities that won him the presidency in 2008, New Hampshire, Florida, Colorado, and Ohio. President Obama will spend election day in his hometown of Chicago and headline his last political rally as a candidate in Iowa, the state that jump-started his first presidential bid. President Obama is said to be relishing his last campaign.

headline: Could Penn State's alumni trustee seats be cut in number? Some see it as a path to board diversity
abstract: Penn State board of trustees Governance Committee meeting, members discussed the possibility of shrinking the size of the board. Since the Sandusky scandal, the trustees has been working on reforming the board to better handle future issues concerning the university.

headline: Fee for drillers gains favor
abstract: Marcellus Shale drilling companies in Washington County, PA, will see a new fee on drilling after it was passed by local officials. Washington County is the second county to propose and pass the fee, which is assessed on each natural gas well annually. The fee is projected to produce around $40 million in the greater Pittsburgh area.

headline: Pre-sentence report in Mellow case delayed until August
abstract: Sentencing for former Senate Democratic Leader Robert J. Mellow is off until at least August due to an order an order issued by U.S. District Judge Joel H. Slomsky that gives the U.S. probation office until Aug. 2 to complete its pre-sentence report on Mr. Mellow. The report had been due July 3.

headline: Please don't vote: If TV ads are your election source, sit this one out
abstract: A late influx of TV ads in PA by both parties is being used to sway the emotions of impressionable voters. The ads range from misleading to wildly innacurate. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette urges its readers to not be swayed by these ads and to make an educated decision on who they decide to vote for based on facts.

headline: Senator Orie's trial
abstract: The trial of PA state Senator Jane Orie took a turn for the worse when her chief of staff testified of the multiple cover ups done in the Senator's office in attempts to erase her association with her sister's campaign. Senator Orie's corruption charges stem from her work on her sibling's campaign for a state judicial seat, using state time to help the campaign.

headline: WPMT-FOX  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  FOX43 News at
abstract: The Harrisburg city council has criticized Governor Tom Corbett for his poor handling of their attempted investigation into an incinerator that has generated much of the city's crippling debt.

headline: Debates part of politics, public service
abstract: U.S. Rep. Tom Marino has postponed his scheduled debate with democratic challenger Phil Scollo, citing scheduling conflicts and the need to attend to affected constituent's needs after Superstorm Sandy. Incumbents usually have the most to lose in debates so his absence is no surprise. However the public deserves to hear a debate between the candidates.

headline: Orie knew of illegal political work, staffers say
abstract: PA state Senator Jane Orie, who is facing 26 different corruption charges stemming from political work done on state time, knew exactly what she was doing, testified one of her staffers in an Allegheny County court. Four of Senator Orie's staff testified of Orie's awareness of the discrepancy while she was doing it, solidifying the prosecutions case against her.

headline: PA Senate OKs plan to repay jobless benefits debt.
abstract: After several years of stalled efforts, state lawmakers are finalizing legislation to borrow billions of dollars to pay off an unemployment compensation debt owed by businesses to the federal government left over from the huge wave of jobs lost in the recession.

headline: Sandusky case still fresh in current election
abstract: null

headline: Turnpike to hire firm on all-electronic tolls
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission is hiring a consulting firm to determine whether converting from the traditional tollbooth collection method to a fully electronic collection method would be economically and practically feasible to the state and its drivers. The new electronic method would require cameras overhead to capture images of drivers' license plates. It could take up to five years before any changes are implemented.

headline: Liquor Control Board worker contract may discourage privatization
abstract: Just as a high-ranking Pennsylvania House Republican is making yet another push to privatize the state’s liquor stores, the Governor and the state store workers’ union have agreed to a new contract that may discourage private sector businesses from investing.

headline: Clean sweep for congressional incumbents in Philly and the burbs
abstract: Moderate republican U.S. Rep. Mike Fitzpatrick narrowly defeated Democrat Kathy Boockvar in the suburan 8th district which covers all of Bucks County and part of Montgomery County. Fitzpatrick has served in congress from 2004-2006 was defeated and re-elected in 2010. He has said he will term-limit himself to eight years. Boockvar ran a well-organized and funded campaign but was thwarted when the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee pulled more than $1 million in TV-ad reservations from the Philadlephia market in early October.

headline: Clymer wants gamblers to ante up for state pensions
abstract: PA state Representative Paul Clymer introduced a bill to the House that would charge a small admission fee to every casino patron. The fee would be used to help fill the hole that is the state's underfunded pension program. Opponents of the measure state the already large fees and taxes casinos pay for slot machines and table games, making in impractical to tax them even more.

headline: Melvin sister to be fired, 8 aides to be furloughed
abstract: Nine state Supreme Court employees who worked in suspended Justice Joan Orie Melvin's Downtown office soon will be out of a job while she fights criminal corruption charges. State court officials will fire Janine Orie, Melvin's sister and longtime aide, and furlough eight other Melvin employees without pay.

headline: 'A tough task' lies ahead for Obama in his 2nd term
abstract: Experts say President Obama's second term is likely to end up focusing mostly on protecting his victories from the first four years rather than pushing any new legislation. He will focus on completing a plan to end the war in Afghanistan, closing the loop on deficit reduction with Congress and making sure ObamaCare and Wall Street reforms are effectively implemented. Due to second-term presidents lame-duck status and an oppositional Congress, Presidents usually look for influence in foreign policy. President Obama will likely become more involved in the Syria conflict and push for an Israeli-Palestinian peace deal.

headline: Senator Jane Orie's corruption trial
abstract: One staff member of PA state Senator Jane Orie testified that Orie required staff to keep a binder of information dealing with corruption cases of other state legislative members, before she was charged. One staff member testified that Senator Orie had her work almost 30 hours of political work during state time over the past six years.

headline: Former PA skinhead wins GOP post with single vote
abstract: A northeastern Pennsylvania man with longstanding ties to white supremacist groups entered a polling place on primary election day and wrote in his name for a low-level position with the local Republican Party committee. Steve Smith wound up getting elected with a single vote his own, and now presents a headache for a GOP that doesn't want him but might not be able to get rid of him.

headline: Democrat Kathleen Kane will be Pennsylvania's first female attorney general
abstract: Democrat Kathleen Kane won the PA attorney general office with a wide margin and will be the first woman to take the office. Kane had name recognition in the race after she defeated Patrick Murphy in the democratic primary. Kane attacked Gov. Corbett's handling of the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse case throughout the campaign.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Judge needs to take a break
abstract: PA state Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin has yet to step down in the wake of her sister's, state Senator Jane Orie, corruption trial stemming from political work done on state time. Justice Melvin herself has been the target of a grand jury investigation pertaining to the same matter, and has removed herself from hearing any criminal cases in Allegheny County court while her sister faces charges, but has not removed herself altogether.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 5
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett is insistent that tax breaks will keep a petrochemical plant from being built in West Virginia instead of Pennsylvania.

headline: Election Coverage
abstract: null

headline: Corbett fights Open Records office over access.
