abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is fighting the PA Open Records office over access to emails and calendar entries and whether they are exempt from the 2008 Right to Know Law. The Open Records office believes that in order to determine if they should be exempt, the office should review it privately.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate seeks to limit superintendent buyouts
abstract: The PA state Senate Education Committee approved a bill that would hinder and limit superintendent buyouts throughout the state. After several recent stories pertaining to buyouts of large sums for school administrators, local officials called on the state for more direct action. The bill requires personal severance packages of school administrators to be detailed in publicly recorded contracts.

headline: PA court system allows tweeting in Sandusky trial, but bans verbatim quotes WITF RADIO
abstract: The Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts has ordered that reporters covering jury selection and the trial of the former Penn State defensive coordinator can tweet from the courtroom, as long as they don’t record anything word-for-word.

headline: Late Night News: 3rd District state House race
abstract: null

headline: Plan to cut property taxes
abstract: A York County, PA, state Representative Seth Grove introduced a property tax relief package that included the increasing of local income tax and county sales tax. The proposal could eliminate property taxes altogether.

headline: Philadelphia City Council Votes on AVI, School Funding Will Be Severed
abstract: Philadelphia City Council president Darrell Clarke says that the council will vote on property taxes and school district funds separately.

headline: Rep. Kelly runs for second term
abstract: null

headline: Lawmaker calls for counties to have opportunity to eliminate property taxes
abstract: PA state Representative Seth Grove is looking to eliminate the local property tax by allowing counties and municipalities to increase sales and income taxes. The proposal is due to be viewed by the House Finance Committee.

headline: Pennsylvania Lags in Green Energy Ranking
abstract: Pennsylvania ranks 24th on a list of states in terms of clean energy according to a new report published by Clean Edge, a market research firm focused on the clean-tech industry.

headline: Will Philly reap rewards for big Obama turnout?
abstract: More than 85% of the Philadelphia's 557,000 total votes were cast for President Obama. As a result a local labor leader said that Philadlephia and Mayor Nutter are entitled to more federal money. Mayor Nutter, a larger supporter of the President, has said he will not move on to take a position in the administration. Sam Katz head of the city's financial watchdog, the PA Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority, and former Republican mayoral candidate said that due to the fiscal cliff and the deficit he doesn't believe the election will be a windfall for Philadelphia.

headline: Ex-intern testifies about Sen. Orie 'campaign' office.
abstract: A former intern of Senator Jane Orie testified at the Senator's corruption trial. Senator Orie is being charged with over twenty counts, stemming from public time being used for her and her sister's personal campaigns. The intern claimed that a campaign office set up for the Senator was a sham, while the real campaign work was done in her legislative office.

headline: PA to borrow $4.5B to pay off fed unemployment debt, change eligibility
abstract: Pennsylvania plans to borrow a $4.5 billion bond to help pay off debt from the federal Unemployment Trust Fund, which stands about $3.9 billion, the third highest in the nation.

headline: Lehigh Valley elections weren't without controversy
abstract: Brian Monahan a local attorney and an aggrieved Republican poll watcher in the city's 9th ward argued that PA requires poll workers to announce the name of everyone who goes to vote. This law has fallen out of practice but does exist. Monahan's suit didn't require court action, a county election office called the election judge and ordered the names to be spoken. There were other election day disturbances. A sign in one polling place falsely informed people that no one could carry a firearm, and another sign said to vote your biblical conscience.

headline: No politics permitted, chief clerk tells jurors
abstract: The chief clerk of the PA state Senate testified at Senator Jane Orie's corruption trial. The chief clerk reiterated the fact that Senator Orie overstepped the Ethics Act, which clearly states a public official is not allowed to use their office for campaign purposes. Senator Orie is being charged with using state time to have her staffers work on her and her sister's campaigns.

headline: Corruption and cover-up: Prison for ex-Sen. Orie was a just response
abstract: The author asserts that former state Senator Jane Orie's prison sentence for corruption and the concealment thereof is just.

headline: Barletta calls for unity
abstract: U.S. Rep. Lou Barletta called for every elected federal official to work together and to compromise when necessary. He said it's fine if Democrats don't like Republican ideas but the President and the Senate should propose their own ideas. Tom Baldino, Wilkes University political science professor said the House GOP leadership needs to stop catering to the Tea Party faction. Brian Carso, political science professor at Misericordia University, said the federal government is moving to the precipice of financial crisis and thus overcoming gridlock is imperative.

headline: Corbett's drug-testing comments draw criticism
abstract: Democratic state treasurer, Rob McCord among other PA political leaders have been criticizing PA Governor Tom Corbett's recent comments that places the blame on drug use to explain why PA residents are not finding work. Some believe that Corbett is using that reasoning to shift the blame away from his economic policies.

headline: Police try to educate teens about new texting while driving ban
abstract: Police officers from York County, PA, handed out fliers to high school students explaining the new texting while driving ban that was passed by the state Assembly and signed into law. In an effort to educate teens of the new law and the punishments that went with it, the police officers handed out the fliers and spoke to students about the law and how they can comply to it.

headline: CAT bus warns of service cuts due to 'insufficient' state and federal funding
abstract: Capital Area Transit may cut back services this fall as it grapples with low state and federal funding levels, said Bill Jones, CAT general manager.

headline: New Democratic row officers will keep close eye on Corbett
abstract: Newly elected PA attorney general Kathleen Kane and PA auditor general Eugene DePasquale will become the new independent watchdogs of Governor Corbett. Kane campaigned  promising to investigate why Gov. Corbett and his appointed successor, Linda Kelly, took 33 months to arrest Jerry Sandusky for child sex abuse. DePasquale has pledged to start an audit of largely state-run water-protection programs. Gov. Corbett has said he welcomes an investigation as politics played no role in the Sandusky case.

headline: DePasquale says constituents were overwhelmingly in favor of texting ban
abstract: A PA state Representative issued a statement stating the overwhelming support for the texting-while-driving ban that was passed into law. The law was important for young drivers, who tend to drive and text simultaneously to a higher degree than any other demographic.

headline: WHP-CBS  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  CBS21 News at 11PM
abstract: RJ Harris criticizes the pension benefits of some public workers as being burdensome and irresponsible.

headline: N Editorial: Casting your ballot is a right - it shouldn't be an ordeal
abstract: PA Department of State's requirements and restrictions on voting are some the worst in the country. Although the voter-ID law was postponed, working to fix ease of voting should be a top priority. President Obama called for national voting standards that guarentee every person's rights are protected and that make participating in democracy not an ordeal.

headline: Carbon dated: Lawmaker says emissions testing on vehicles no longer necessary
abstract: A PA state senator is looking to end the annual emissions test requirement on state drivers' vehicles. Senator John Wozniak argues that newer and more environmental-friendly cars are making the mandate obsolete. Only four percent of vehicles fail the emissions test on average, according to the PA Department of Transportation, while almost half of those failures come from faulty gas caps.

headline: WFMZ-IND  Philadelphia, PA  5PM NEWS
abstract: A Massachusetts state representative visited Barack Obama's Berks County campaign office to criticize Mitt Romney's governorship.

headline: PSU study shows Marcellus Shale growth, dairy decline
abstract: A study performed by Penn State University analyzed the effects of Marcellus Shale drilling to the dairy industry in the western and central parts of PA. The study found a correlation between the decline in milk production in those parts of the state and the increase in gas drilling. Some researchers believe that a number of dairy farmers have given up on dairy production because of the royalties accrued from gas wells on their property.

headline: Kennywood considers adding beer to menu
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Jim Ferlo and Kennywood Park managers have begun talks over the future of the amusement park's pending liquor license. The two parties first met after Mr. Ferlo petitioned the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board in opposition to the park's proposed alcohol sales. In that petition, he asked that citizens be allowed to testify their support or opposition at a formal public hearing in Pittsburgh before Kennywood receives its license. In response, Kennywood representatives met with Mr. Ferlo to discuss how alcohol sales at the park might best be regulated.

headline: In 2012, Republicans mustered vote better in Pa.
abstract: From preliminary state figures nearly all counties that lean Democrat saw a decline in participation since 2008 at about 2 percent whereas counties with a Republican majority saw a slight increase. In Allegheny County both parties saw participation fall but Democrats lost three times as many voters to absenteeism as Republicans. Across the country many Democratic voters decided to stay home. Michael McDonald, George Mason University associate professor explains this as in 2008 voters came out in opposition to former President George Bush and it is easier to be against something than it is to be for it.

headline: Pennsylvania's sad business tax rank
abstract: A recent study has ranked PA as one of the highest-taxing states for businesses in the nation. In new and matured business taxes, as well as property taxes and business net-loss tax credits, the state continuously ranked among the lowest.

headline: A bad deal: Short-term loan bill means long-term disgrace
abstract: The author criticizes a measure passed in the state House that would allow for out-of-state lenders to offer short term loans.

headline: Republicans take it on the chin on Election Day
abstract: Democrats did well in the 2012 election. They carried a U.S. senate race and picked up three seats in the state Senate. Jim Burn chairman of the PA Democratic Party said the results showed that the party is on the right side of history and of important issues and that this election sends a clear message to Gov. Corbett to start listening to all Pennsylvanians.

headline: Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett's higher education advisory panel gets to work
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's Advisory Commission on Postsecondary Education has begun its work in formulating a long-term vision for the education system in the state. Funding concerns for the state's universities is the most pressing issue, while higher education prices increase and state funding decreases.

headline: All else aside, city still lacks a recovery plan
abstract: The author argues the need for a better economic recovery plan in Scranton.

headline: Pittsburgh officials argue for release from Act 47 fiscal oversight
abstract: Mayor Luke Ravenstahl argued for the release of Pittsburgh from eight years in Act 47 oversight and the designation as a financialy distressed municipality. The city has had balanced budgets, $240 million in debt reduction and repeated credit upgrades since he took office in 2006. Act 47 imposes spending restrictions, such as wage caps for union workers. Since 1987, 27 municipalities have gone into Act 47 and only 6 have come out. Even if the city exits Act 47 it will still be monitored by a second oversight board.

headline: Corbett says he would sign voter-ID bill
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett announced he would sign a bill that would require all voters to show a form of identification before voting. The bill is currently being debated by the PA House of Representatives, but is expected to reach the Governor's desk in time for the upcoming election cycle. Opponents say the measure will help Republican causes come election day, since many who do not own forms of identification, like the elderly and disabled, are Democrats.

headline: Pennsylvania state budget talks make 'baby steps' toward compromise
abstract: Legislative Republicans and Gov. Tom Corbett continued their slow crawl toward reaching an agreement on the 2012-13 state budget Monday, concluding a high-level negotiating session that one participant said had produced "baby steps" toward a settlement.

abstract: null

headline: Corbett challenges critics to find money for higher education
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett answered questions dealing with the budget cuts to postsecondary universities. He challenged his opponents of the cuts to find other areas of government to reduce funding to in order to fill the budget gap for this fiscal year. Gov. Corbett addressed these issues at the first meeting of the education task force he put together to solve the funding problems facing PA's universities.

headline: Legislators need courage to do the right thing at budget time
abstract: Steven Burg argues the importance state of legislators' passage of a responsible, pragmatic budget.

headline: State still shaky on exchange, Medicaid expansion
abstract: It is uncertain whether PA will pursue the optional Medicaid expansion under ObamaCare. PA will have to notify the federal government if it plans to set up an exchange by Nov. 16. The PA Insurance Department has stopped extensive planning efforts until answers are given to 26 questions focused on the cost, scope, and deadlines associated with the exchange. According to the Affordable Care Act A state can operate the exchange by itself, abdicate to the federal government or enter into a partnership with the federal government. In PA the expansion would provide Medicaid coverage to 750,000 residents by 2014 according to the Department of Public Welfare with the federal government paying 100% of costs until 2016.

headline: Closing school a tough call Kutztown may have to make
abstract: In the midst of reduced state funding to local school districts, the Kutztown, PA, School Board is considering closing down one of its elementary schools. The proposal would bring about certain issues with relocating children to available schools, but the district may have no other choice.

headline: Harrisburg receiver William Lynch gives City Council ultimatum - act on fiscal plan or I'll go to court
abstract: Harrisburg receiver William Lynch has threatened to take the city's city council to court if they do not enact certain parts of the city's fiscal recovery plan.

headline: U.S. Department of Justice, DEP sue over western PA Superfund site.
abstract: A Superfund site, run by Reactive Metals and Alloys Corp or Remacor, about 50 miles northwest of Pittsburgh processed magnesium shavings and scrap until a 2005 fire destroyd the facility. Beginning in 2006 the DEP and the U.S. EPA removed six million pounds of waste at a cost of $10 million. Now they are suing 17 companies in an attempt to recover some of the clean up cost.

headline: Gov. Corbett signs voter ID bill into law
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed into law a measure that would require all PA citizens to display a form of identification before voting. The law will take effect before the April 24 primaries. The law's purpose is to prevent voter fraud, while opponents of the measure questions its constitutionality.

headline: WGAL-NBC  Harrisburg-Lancaster-Lebanon-York, PA  News 8 at 11PM
abstract: Northern Lebanon School District superintendent Donald Bell discusses what he thinks is need for charter school reform in Pennsylvania.

headline: Hunters learn that chronic wasting disease isn't going away anytime soon
abstract: The PA Game Commission's deer check station has begun operations near East Berlin as part of the state's response to the first confirmed case of chronic wasting disease-CWD in captive white-tailed deer. No deer in the wild has been found with CWD. The Department of Agriculture when attempting to shutdown an infected farm allowed one deer to escape. It is not known if the deer has CWD.

headline: Orie witness says files were deleted from Senate computer after mistrial
abstract: Computer files pertaining to the corruption case against PA state Senator Jane Orie were tampered with, said a prosecuting attorney. Senator Orie is being charged with multiple counts stemming from campaign work she and her staff performed on state time. The files were originally deleted but later found on a computer's backup drive, adding more evidence against the Senator in the trial.

headline: When gambling takes control | State allots $6.4M to assist those with a problem
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board has set aside over $6 million in fighting gambling addiction as it observes the annual "Problem Gambling Awareness Week." The state along with help from casinos and other gambling operations banded together to help stop serious gambling issues, an action that was brought to fruition during the Rendell administration's push to legalize casinos and gambling in the state.

headline: Republicans weighing new Corbett budget pitch
abstract: Efforts to reach an agreement on how much Pennsylvania should spend in fiscal 2012-13 inched along with legislative Republicans leaving a negotiating session loaded down with a Corbett administration budget proposal that would spend about $27.4 billion starting July 1.

abstract: A humorous look at notable mistakes and ill-guided words of famous and infamous politicians from PA. Governor Ed Rendell and US Senator Rick Santorum are included.

headline: Corbett: Others still vying for planned PA refinery.
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett said that he has heard that Ohio and West Virginia are still trying to lure away a petrochemical refinery planned for western Pennsylvania, as he presses lawmakers to approve a $1.7 billion tax credit for the project before they leave Harrisburg for the summer.

headline: An all-electronic Pennsylvania Turnpike is projected to save $21 million annually
abstract: The PA Turnpike is switching all tolling operations to electronic operatations. Instead of fare collectoin booths there will be automatic deductions from E-Z Pass users' accounts and photographs of license plates of other vehicles who will be sent a bill. The move is projected to save the Turnpike $21 million in operating costs annually. However 755 toll workers will be laid off. A sampling of motorists and business interests have shown broad support for the plan.

headline: Critics pan planned PA food-stamp asset test.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett revealed a plan that would require all recipients of food stamps within the state to first undergo an asset test. The test would block certain households from receiving the food stamps if their total assets exceeded a certain threshold. Critics argue that it will harm the most vulnerable members of society, while the Corbett Administration looks for ways to reduce the state budget in the midst of a tough fiscal year.

headline: Bad tricks: A state Senate bill tips its hat to the gun lobby
abstract: The author criticized the Senate as having passed its Castle Doctrine bill, to not only help citizens protect their home, but to accommodate lobbyists for the gun industry.

headline: Pa. plan: Close 3 Chester-Upland schools
abstract: Three schools and school district administation offices will close in Chester-Upland School District. The schools are operating at below 20 percent capacity. The districts have lost students to charter and cyber schools. The school district is putting into effect a new evaluation system for teachers and they are recruiting a permanent superintendent and a chief financial officer. They are also changing the property-tax structure.

headline: Gov. Tom Corbett's approval rating drops to 41 percent in Quinnipiac poll
abstract: A recent poll shows PA Governor Tom Corbett's approval rating has dropped almost six points since December. The polling results found the percentage approving of his job in office is about equal to the percentage disapproving of his work, at 41 percent for both. The drop in approval could be from proposed cuts to higher education in his new budget plan.

headline: Philly Deals: Harrisburg-area group revealed Neshaminy strikers' pay
abstract: An anti-union group Citizens Alliance of Pennsylvania revealed the pay and benefits of 600 school district strikers in an effort to criticize them as being greedy.

headline: State House leadership to remain the same
abstract: PA legislators from the western part of the state will lead both parties in the state House of Representatives. Rep. Sam Smith of Jefferson County will continue on as speaker and Rep. Mike Turzai will become the caucus leader. Democrats selected Frank Dermody of Oakmont as minority leader and elected Ron Waters of Philadelphia for caucus secretary.

headline: Expand the use of red-light cameras in commonwealth
abstract: A new bill introduced in the PA House of Representatives would allow more cities to adopt and employ red light cameras at busy intersections, if passed into law. Since the city of Philadelphia has used the technology, fines have generated over $20 million in revenue, while keeping roadways safer, some recent studies have shown.

abstract: State Representative Glenn Grell asserts that discussions of changes the state pension system should involve current employees that will be affected by changes

headline: From Harrisburg, talks of turnpike toll relief
abstract: Sen. John Rafferty Republican of Montgomery Country said that there is bipartisan support in both houses to amend Act 44, a law that requires the turnpike to provide $450 million a year for non-turnpike road, bridge, and transit projects, however Gov. Corbett has said he will not support financial aid for transportation that raises gas taxes or other fees. Auditor General Jack Wagner said that Act 44 was unfair and the turnpike commission faces possible bankruptcy if it has to keep borrowing to meet Act 44 obligations. Debt has risen from $2.6 billion in 2007 to $7.8 billion. He said the law should be repealed. The turnpike chief executive Craig Shuey believes that by raising tolls 3 percent a year and switching to all electronic tolling the turnpike can avoid bankruptcy.

headline: Pennsylvania House again delays vote on photo-ID bill
abstract: The PA House of Representative failed to vote on a controversial piece of legislation that would require all voting citizens to first show some form of identification. For two days in a row the House has failed to vote on the measure, an issue lawmakers say stems from the long list of officials still in line to debate. Some sources are blaming the delays in voting on campaign fundraisers that some lawmakers are holding.

headline: Christiana, Vogel reveal ethane tax credit plans
abstract: The Royal Dutch Shell plant proposed for Potter Township and other ethane-driven entities in Pennsylvania could benefit from tax credit legislation introduced Wednesday in Harrisburg by Beaver County legislators Jim Christiana and Elder Vogel Jr.

headline: Outcry triggers revocation of methadone clinic's permit
abstract: A methadone clinic that was to open in Holmesburg, PA, has come under fire from opposition of its location. Its building permit was thus stripped by the locality after a town hall hearing in August where opponents railed against the clinic. The clinic is seeking to file suit for what they call a "civil-rights issue."

headline: PA teachers rally amid budget talks, layoffs.
abstract: With state aid for public schools being discussed behind the Capitol's closed doors and a second straight year of large-scale layoffs looming, hundreds of educators, let-go teachers and parents packed the rotunda  for a rally to protest Governor Tom Corbett's budget cuts.

abstract: null

headline: Plan outlines aid for troubled southeastern PA school district
abstract: A school district outside of Philadelphia will be stay open if its finances are overseen by a third party. The Chester Upland School District, which threatened to shut down in January over a lack of state funding, won a federal suit which forced the state to send more money to the district. Chester Upland receives over two-thirds of its operating budget from the state, and remains one of the poorest districts in PA.

headline: WPGH-FOX  Pittsburgh, PA  10 PM News
abstract: People gathered in Pittsburgh to protest further cuts in the state budget.

headline: Pennsylvania AG's recommendations for Penn State include removing governor, school president as trustees
abstract: A special report released by PA Auditor General Jack Wagner stated that Penn State University had a too-closed and tightly centralized power center that was heavily weighted toward the president's office and this contributed to the severity of the Sandusky child sex scandal by leading to inaction from the board of trustees. Wagner called for Gov. Corbertt, the PA legislature and Penn State Trustees to make changes including cutting the size of the board from 31 to 21 momembers, ending Penn State's exemptions from PA open-record laws, changing university bylaws to require a simiple majority of the board to vote on changes, and improving public access to board meetings. Former President Graham Spanier, Senior Vice President for Business and Finance Gary Schultz and Athletic Director Tim Curley are charged with obstruction of justice.

headline: Foreign policy is not Rendell’s forte
abstract: A group of prominent former political figures, including former PA Governor Ed Rendell, have stepped out in support of a rebel Iranian group still labeled as terroristic by the US State Department. The Iranian group, which was blamed for the killings of several Americans in the 1970s, opposes the current Iranian government, and many are saying they deserve the country's backing because of it.

headline: Farmers' hot start yields bumper crop
abstract: Edward Calimore describes the events surrounding an early harvest of peaches in PA.

headline: Department of Error Propagation
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection put a disclaimer on their website that saying the DEP doesn't guarentee the accuracy, completeness or timeliness of oil and gas production data. The PA legislature should devise meaningful penalties for producers who post innacurate data so the DEP has more power in releasing accurate information.

headline: Corbett’s Energy Executive Defends Impact Fee
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's energy executive stepped out to defend the Governor's impact fee on Marcellus Shale natural gas wells after criticism that it did not do enough to protect the environment. The measure was modeled after a similar one in Colorado, a law which was praised by environmentalists. Hydraulic fracturing, or fracking, is a method used to extract natural gas from the Shale. It has been blamed for water contamination, a charge the Corbett Administration says is untrue.

headline: Bill sole effort at PLCB reform
abstract: A Senate bill was introduced that would preserve the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board and its wholesale and retail wine and liquor businesses. It would allow bars and restaurants that sell wine and liquor by the glass to sell those products by the bottle.

headline: Minimum funding for Pa. state colleges urged by governor’s commission
abstract: The governor's advisory commission on higher education recommended minimum funding levels for PA colleges and universities as well as tying funding to performance. The commission outlined 19 recommendations including increasing funding for institutions, responding to workforce needs, closing achievement gaps, attracting research funding and publishing useful information for potential students. Included in the recommendations was the creation of an online "passport" for students to choose courses and training from different institutions.

headline: Funds cut for mental health care
abstract: The Disability Rights Network of Pennsylvania criticized the recent 20% cut to spending on public welfare measures. The DRNP is planning on filing suit against the state for what seems to be a hefty cut in the Governor's budget plan, a lawsuit state officials claim as "frivolous."

headline: Bomb squad evacuates Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture building, removes old chemical
abstract: The state police bomb squad was called to help remove a container of explosive chemicals from a state Department of Agriculture building on Cameron Street.

headline: Carmichaels establishing account for gas impact fee
abstract: Under Act 13, funds from the natural gas drilling impact fee are given to local communities. The borough of Carmichaels will receive $16,972 which can be used for 13 different types of projects and put into a capital reserve fund.

headline: Casting ballot in PA without photo ID now illegal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed into law a measure requiring all voters to show a form of identification before entering the ballot box. Any citizen who does not own a form of ID can receive one, free of charge, from the PA Department of Transportation.

headline: Beer distributors sour on privatization bill
abstract: Newly proposed legislation that aims to privatize state-controlled liquor sales is evoking sobering responses from some Berks County beer distributors who do not desire increased competition.

headline: Poll finds Corbett gained support from Sandy
abstract: A Quinipiac University poll of 1,489 voters showed a bump in Gov. Corbetts approval rating for his calm handling of Hurricane Sandy. This was the first time since March that Gov. Corbett's ratings have moved into positive territory. The PA Legislature received 43 percent disaproval.

headline: Bridge renaming
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett signed legislation changing the name of a bridge in northwestern PA after a local war hero who died in Afghanistan.

abstract: Jack Shea, president of the Allegheny County Labor Council, criticizes the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette as having unfairly attacked PLCB workers by calling clerks "often surly" and suggesting that they are overpaid.

headline: Auditor general recommends changes for Penn State’s board of trustees
abstract: The Penn State trustees are meeting to discuss State Auditor Jack Wagner's recommendations of the university's governing structure. Recommendations include taking away the vote of the university president, making the governor a nonvoting member, and fully extending the Right-to-know Law to Penn State. Wagner said his suggestions might not have prevented what occurred but would have helped.

headline: Bridge in Harborcreek Township named for fallen soldier
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett signed a measure that would rename an Erie, PA bridge after a local man killed in Afghanistan while serving in the military.

headline: PA: More than $520M in Medicare, Medicaid fees went to potentially avoidable hospital stays
abstract: According to a report titled “Potentially Preventable Hospitalizations in Pennsylvania, 2010 Medicare and Medicaid payments totaling about $521 million could have been avoided with better outpatient care.

headline: Educators anxious about switch to Keystone Exams
abstract: This year PA will switch to the Keystone Exams from the PSSA. The standardized test is given to juniors to determine whether the high schools meet academic goals under No Child Left Behind law. Students will be tested in English Literature, Alegbera 1, and biology. Schools could fail to meet average yearly progress, AYP goals, due to the transition. However student graduation won't be tied to the keystone exam until 2017.

headline: Metcalfe says ‘slew of amendments’ holding up marriage legislation
abstract: The PA General Assembly failed to vote on a measure that would be the first step in defining marriage as between a man and woman in the state constitution, eliminating any hope for gay marriage in PA.

headline: Pennsylvania State Police secrecy doesn't serve public interest
abstract: Jim Deegan argues that police should be more transparent in their operation and protocol.

headline: Highways, pensions and booze on Corbett's agenda.
abstract: Gov. Corbett said he does not plan to change his inner circle of advisers even though the candidates he endorsed for U.S. Senate and state attorney general both lost their elections. Corbett said he would propose a statewide transportation plan and lobby for it. He has not laid out a plan for the privatization of state liqour and wine sales but said he remains committed to the concept. Gov. Corbett also said the proportion of the state budget consumed by pension costs will rise to 8 percent in five years and so pension reform is essential. Gov. Corbett also wants Congress to resolve the "fiscal cliff" problem and said PA cannot absorb the cost of any expansion in Medicaid.

headline: Cleaning Pennsylvania’s air with natural gas
abstract: A PA lawmaker looks to help the environment stay healthy and clean by using natural gas.

headline: Sandusky jurors may get abuse case by week's end.
abstract: The child molestation trial of former Penn State assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky could be in jurors' hands before the end of the week, with witness testimony on his behalf expected to wrap up in less than three days.

headline: Pittsburgh Public Schools rewarded for student academic growth
abstract: Teachers and other professionals who worked with high peforming schools in 2011-12 will receive bonuses. Ten Pittsburgh city schools have been awarded for progress. They are STAR schools, Students and Teachers Achieving Results. The bonuses total $2.1 million, 80 percent of which is paid by a federal Teacher Incentive Fund grant.

headline: Corbett insists tax breaks encourage business and create jobs
abstract: Critics of PA Governor Tom Corbett are upset over recent budget proposals, which they say cut essential programs for the poor while giving tax breaks to big businesses. But, the Governor explains that by not increasing taxes, businesses will grow which in the long run helps every citizen of PA.

headline: Is it time to prune Penn State branches? 24 campuses might be too many
abstract: The author wonders if it is worth it for Penn State to keep operation some of the lower-enrolling campuses to remain efficient.

headline: Particulars of Mericle settlement spelled out
abstract: Former Judge Mark Ciaverella is serving a sentence of 28 years for his acceptance of $1 million from Mericle, a company who built two private juvenile detention facilities where more than 2000 juveniles were sent. The scandal is known as "kids for cash". Mericle is setting aside $17.75 million and 1,614 juvenile are entitled for upt to $5000 in base payments.

headline: State's laws on integrity score C-
abstract: Despite convictions of 27 people with ties to the Legislature since 2008, Pennsylvania's laws to deter corruption rate a C-minus, 19th-best in the nation, in a "state integrity index" released by the Center for Public Integrity.

headline: City won’t be norm in distress
abstract: At an introductory meeting, members of the Altoona's Act 47 distress recovery team told officials that working with the city promises to be different from what they're used to. For the first time, they'll be dealing with a municipality that wants to quickly get out of the state's financial distress program, they said.

headline: John Baer: Corbett keeps mum while Dems ponder who will run
abstract: Gov. Corbett has been quiet about his re-election campaign. State Treasurer Rob McCord is most likely to run against Gov. Corbett for the Democrats in 2014. Senator Bob Casey is more likely to run in 2018 when his second term as senator ends. It is most likely too soon for newly elected Attorney General Kathleen Kane to run.

abstract: Governor Corbett has signed a bill that makes the presentation of a photo ID a requirement for voting at the ballot box.

abstract: Testimony has begun in the corruption trial of former State Representative Steve Stetler.

headline: UK-based firm seeks to run Pa.'s lottery system
abstract: UK-based Camelot Global Services LLC was the sole company to submit a proposal to run the $3.5 billion state lottery system. The company has pledged to bring in more than $34 billion in profits over the course of a 20-year management contract, in part through introducing online ticket sales and keno games. Gov. Corbett will compare the bid estimates against keeping the lottery operated internally. If PA accepts the offer it would join Illinois and Indiana in hiring an outside firm to run its lottery system.

headline: Sen. Orie claims she separated office work from campaigning
abstract: State Senator Jane Orie is still insisting that she did not use office resources to support her campaign.

headline: KDKA-CBS  Pittsburgh, PA  KDKA TV News At 5
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett has dismissed low approval ratings of his performance as discontent over necessary budget cuts.

headline: PhillyDeals: Longtime municipal bond lawyer offers ideas on controlling Pa. local debt
abstract: David Unkovic a municipal bond lawyer for 30 years resigned the Harrisburg receiver appointment earlier this year after Gov. Corbett failed to support his efforts to protect public assets and hold financiers and enablers accountable. Unkovic attended a PA Senate hearing on state finances and gave his recommendations. He said PA needs to tighten its weak law to force local govt's to open and audit their books, and file updated financial statements that conform to national standards. He wants to prohibit local govt's and authorities from entering any new interest-rate swap agreements, make it a crime to lie about a town's financial condition, let PA communities file for federal bankruptcy protection when state oversight isn't enough, and have the General Assembly ask for federal prosecutors to investigate the small group of people and institutions who caused the devastation of Harrisburg's finances.

headline: PA seeks to swap property taxes with hikes in sales, income taxes
abstract: A new proposal might eliminate property taxes in Pennsylvania, only to replace them with a 1 percent increase in sales and personal income taxes.

abstract: Eric Boehm describes the implications of the 17 billion liability for retiree health care that needs to be addressed on top of a $40 billion unfunded pension liability.

abstract: Following in the footsteps of Lampeter-Strasburg School District, Penn Manor officials on Monday announced plans to drug test all new hires as early as summer 2012.

abstract: State Representative Rick Mirabito has been seeking a budget amendment, while, state Representative Garth Everett & state Senator E. Eugene Yaw are working directly with staff members of the state appropriations committee, all to restore an aviation patrol unit to the Williamsport Regional Airport.

headline: Pa. is failing to act to halt extinction: The game commission backtracks and lets bats continue to be decimated
abstract: The PA Game Commission announced it was considering listing bats as an endangered species in PA after a fungal contagion was discovered to be wiping out 98% of three bat populations. This would put into place measures that would limit some logging in the summer months. Timber and coal mining interests opposed the measure saying that the cuts would "crush" the state economy. The PA Game Commission has since backed off its recommendations.

headline: When are we going to do more than just talk about jobs in Pa?
abstract: State Representative Dwight Evans calls for a more concrete and detailed plan for job creation in Pennsylvania.

abstract: A crowd gathered outside the Somerset County Courthouse Friday to urge Congress to pass a highway bill to fund highway projects with a new gas tax.

headline: Natural gas drillers target U.S. truck, bus market.

abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is looking to put the operations of the Pennsylvania Lottery in the hands of a private firm. Some lawmakers are worried over the proposal, since the Lottery generates over $3 billion in sales with a large portion going towards senior citizens. The Governor, however, is ready to go ahead with the outsourcing measure without legislative approval.

headline: New research shows no Marcellus Shale pollution.
abstract: The Marcellus Shale drilling process has been shown not to be contaminating local water wells as originally suspected, new research by Duke University has suggested. The Shale is a natural gas formation that is extracted by the "fracking" technique, a controversial technique thought to have contaminated water supplies with methane gas last year.

headline: State budget secretary: $300M in aid dangling over fiscal cliff
abstract: PA Budget Secretary Charles Zogby says the Corbett administration is working to avoid deep cuts in state aid to social programs in the next state budget. The upcoming budget won't include tax hikes or spending freezes but may include furloughs or layoffs of state employees because of rising health care costs.

headline: Redistricting reform: PA voters should draw political lines
abstract: Reform to the current process of PA state House and Senate districts has been a hot topic recently in the state Capitol. Government reform groups argue the current process allows for very little transparency, while officials select their voters each decade. Most recently, a plan put forward by House Speaker Sam Smith that would shrink the size of the House by 50 members was halted during a debate period, a measure many believe halts the process of redistricting reform.

headline: Upper Darby School Board to vote on rehiring teachers tonight
abstract: The Upper Darby School Board votes on whether to rehire 25 teachers after the state (PA) budgeted over $2.5 million to the district in the recent spending law. The move to rehire comes from the recommendation of several school district administrators, who were grateful to the state for the budget allocation.

headline: Op-ed: Carlisle middle school lab accident shows void in public school code
abstract: James Redington, eighth grade chemistry teacher at Wilson Middle School in Carlisle, recently caused an explosion in his classroom that injured seven children. The state public school code fails to set safety standards for science classrooms.

headline: Bet on privatization: Corbett is right to see if lottery revenue can grow
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is reviewing a measure that would privatize the Pennsylvania Lottery. The Lottery generates over $3 billion dollars worth of revenue, a large portion of which goes towards PA senior citizens. Proponents of the plan state the Governor has every right to inquire whether or not lottery privatization would increase revenue, since PA would not be the first state to do so.

headline: New $5 million grant program announced for Pennsylvania students
abstract: The Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency has revealed a new grant program to help students in the state to pay for specialized training programs. The grant itself will not be paid by tax-payers, but instead by allocations from PHEAA's business income.

headline: DEP backtracks on cause of blue creek
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Protection is retracting a report that claimed that printer's ink turned a Fayette County creek blue in November. DEP spokesman John Poister said “We have not been able to conclusively determine the source of the blue coloring of (Connellsville-Breakneck) creek.”

headline: Q poll gives Santorum lead in PA
abstract: A Quinnipiac University poll shows former PA Senator Rick Santorum holds a six point lead over fellow Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney. The polling suggests that Mr. Santorum's once double-digit lead in the state is dwindling as the state primary looms.

headline: Philadelphia gets to keep its casino license
abstract: In a disputed decision, the city of Philadelphia (PA) has been allowed to keep its second casino license. The PA legislature had been mulling over putting the license up for a statewide bid, but heavy lobbying from Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter, among others, kept the license within city limits.

headline: To Rep. Mike Fleck: 'Come On In, the Water's Fine!'
abstract: PA Rep-elect Brian Sims talks about his experience as an openly gay candidate and future in Harrisburg.

headline: State House district could be left without representative
abstract: The 50th Legislative District of PA could be without a member come the November elections. Representative Bill DeWeese was recently convicted of conspiracy charges stemming from the usage of taxpayer resources for his re-election campaign, and yet is running for re-election in the 50th district. Per House rules, Mr. DeWeese would be unable to serve in office once his sentencing is over, a process that could occur after the primaries in late April.

headline: State does not keep records on felons receiving pensions
abstract: The state of PA has no records dealing with state pension funds given to convicted felons, a fact that has some lawmakers and interest groups in an outrage. The problem has arisen following the sex-abuse trial and conviction of former Penn State University employee Jerry Sandusky, who will be eligible to receive his pension while in prison.

headline: Everett says he was just trying to help a friend
abstract: State Representative Garth Everett (R-Muncy) is under fire for an email he recently sent to fellow lawmakers. In it, he asks for money to help a friend, Brett Feese, an inmate in state prison for corruption.

headline: Environmental groups call for water pollution disclosure
abstract: A group of environmental groups called on PA Governor Tom Corbett to speak publicly about water contamination from natural gas in PA.

headline: Casey targets witness intimidation with bill
abstract: Between 1999 and 2009, 13 people were killed in Philadelphia due to witness intimidation. U.S. Senator Bob Casey plans to introduce a bill that will make Witness intimidation a federal crime.

headline: Senate liquor plan: Folmaer wants to check in with beer distributors before deciding support
abstract: PA Senator Mike Folmer, of Lebanon County plans to talk with beer distributors in his district before he makes up his mind about whether or not he should support the Senate liquor proposal announced today.

headline: Veil of secrecy still pervades Senate
abstract: The PA Supreme Court found that the State Senate wasn't transparent in revealing the Senate's use of public money to pay for Former PA Senator Robert Mellow's legal representation.

headline: New law ensures crime victims and families can speak up during parole process
abstract: A new law will allow crime victims and their families to speak with the Board of Probation and Parole when it considers releasing the person who committed a crime against them or their family.

headline: State budget issues get more challenging
abstract: The PA revenue report is expected to show that the overall tax collection are $150 million short of PA Governor Tom Corbett's proposal for this fiscal year.

headline: Transportation funding proposals let uninsured motorists pay their way out of a predicament
abstract: Motorists could potentially pay there way out of a registration suspension if they let their car insurance lapse under a proposed transportation funding plans that are currently being mulled over in the PA Capital.

headline: Top Republican won't rush on liquor privatization
abstract: Despite, PA Governor Tom Corbett's push, President Pro Tempore of The PA Senate Joe Scarnati is not rushing to pass a bill on the privatization of liquor any time soon.

headline: State budget deal could put your healthcare at risk: As I See It
abstract: The current state budget proposal will potentially enact spending plans that can put health care owner's plans at risk. The author gives his take on the issue.

headline: Scarnati: booze distracting from budget
abstract: President Pro Tempore of The PA Senate Joe Scarnati is a bit frustrated that the hearings on liquor privatization is distracting people from the state budget.

headline: Ron Buxton, county engineer V.P. named to new Dauphin County authority
abstract: Dauphin County commissioners appointed Ron Buxton as VP of the county's engineering firm. Ron Buxton represented Harrisburg in the state House for 20 years.

headline: Gov. Corbett boosts money to fight domestic violence
abstract: At a news conference at the YWCA of Harrisburg, PA Governor Tom Corbett announced that he will increase state spending by 10 percent to combat domestic violence.

headline: Red tape and talking points slowing Pennsylvania's Medicaid expansion decision
abstract: With the  U.S. Supreme Court recently upholding the legality of the Affordable Car Act, PA Governor Tom Corbett and his administration have a decision to make about PA's Medicaid expansion decision.

headline: Pa. Sen. Casey Now Supports Gay Marriage
abstract: After reviewing the legal, public policy and civil rights questions surrounding the issue of gay marriage equality, PA Senator Bob Casey has announced that he's in full support of gay marriage.

headline: Paths to reform: Republicans can abolish the liquor monopoly
abstract: There are two Republican versions of the Liquor privatization plan. The author believes the Republicans must come to a consensus to help PA Governor Tom Corbett accomplish what many Governor's before him couldn't.

headline: Democratic Lawmakers Hold Hearing on Liquor Privatization Plan
abstract: The Democratic Policy Committee held a hearing on the liquor privatization proposal in Scranton. Most of the lawmakers have denounced the Governor's proposal during the meeting.

headline: No vote on U&O bill
abstract: The PA legislature still have not voted on a bill that would increase taxes on businesses to get the schools more money.

abstract: PA State Senator Daylin Leach has announced that he is running for Congress in the 13th District, a seat currently held by Allyson Schwartz who has announced that she's running for Governor.

headline: Schwartz Kicks Off 2014 Campaign For Pa. Governor
abstract: U.S. Representative Allyson Schwartz, the forth democrat to announce her candidacy, is beginning her 2014 campaign for Governor.

abstract: According to a Duke University study, both deep gas drilling and natural process have contributed to natural gas seeping into water supplies in Northeastern Pennsylvania.

abstract: Parents are upset with steep cuts made to local schools. The priorities of PA Gov Tom Corbett are examined.

headline: President continues to try and convince Congress on Syria
abstract: US President Barack Obama wants to gain Congressional approval for action against Syria.

abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett has announced a plan to create a new style of Medicaid that has stricter rules that those offered by other states. New funding has created an incentive for states to expand Medicaid. Corbett has delayed expansion in PA until his plans can gain federal approval.

headline: PA Senate OKs bill to allow healthcare apologies.
abstract: A b\ill was based that will allow health care professionals to apologize for a mistake without it being admissible in court during liability cases. Studies have shown that a large percentage of families would have not filed a lawsuit if given an apology.

headline: Former president serves as witness at same-sex marriage
abstract: The impact of same-sex marriage in PA is examined.

headline: Chairman of city panel resigns, admits campaign fraud
abstract: Stanley Straughter, former chairman of the Philadelphia Commission on African and Caribbean Immigrant Affairs, has pleaded guilty for accepting repayments for political donations.

headline: PFT releases new ads, poll on education issues
abstract: The Philadelphia Federation of Teachers will release two ads that illustrate their distaste for PA Governor Tom Corbett and Philadelphia Mayor Nutter's policies on education. In addition the union had released a poll that shows that voters are dissatisfied with Mayor Nutter's work on public education.

headline: Can same-sex couples in Pa. gain benefits? It depends
abstract: With a significant part of the Defense of Marriage act struck down by the Supreme Court, this article examines whether same sex couples will be able to receive benefits.

abstract: A PennDot chief and a U.S. Congressman will take a trip through western PA in a driverless vehicle.

abstract: PA Supporters of Medicaid expansion are planning on demonstrating in Washington D.C. to make sure there voices are heard.

headline: Jerry Sandusky prosecutor: No evidence Joe Paterno participated in criminal cover-up at Penn State
abstract: In an interview with 60 minutes, Frank Fina, a prosecutor in the Jerry Sandusky trial said that there is no evidence that Joe Paterno participated in the cover-up at Penn State.

headline: Paper: Pa. ordered to speed food stamp processing
abstract: Pennsylvania is known to have a fairly slow food stamp process. With that and mind, the U.S. Department of Labor called for PA to speed up its system.

headline: Nutter videos hit back at PFT ads
abstract: In an effort to maintain a positive image in regards to Philadelphia's Public Schools, Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter released ads responding to ads by the PFT that attacked Mayor Nutter's positions on Philadelphia public schools.

headline: End legal tax evasion
abstract: The author calls for an end to legal tax evasion. Tax evasion is legal in PA and it is known as the "Delaware loophole".

headline: Computer-operated car transports U.S. Rep Shuster
abstract: PA Congressman Bill Shuster took a ride in a driverless Cadillac designed by Carnegie Mellon University researchers. Shuster believes that this technology is the future of transportation in PA and beyond.

headline: UPMC wants Highmark to drop lawsuit
abstract: After being accused of using its market power to UPMC is calling for Highmark to drop a lawsuit that proposed that UPMC used its market power to repress West Penn Allegheny Health System.

headline: Judge vows quick same-sex marriage case ruling
abstract: PA Judge Dan Pellegrini vows to be quick and decisive in same sex marriage ban ruling. The judge will determine the constitutionality of the ban of same-sex marriage.

headline: DN Editorial: The shell game
abstract: This article argues that PA Governor, Tom Corbett is playing a 'shell game' with Pennsylvania. This article critiques Corbett's claims and reveals that he may not be revealing the whole truth when it comes to the Philadelphia school district's financial crisis.

headline: Gas driller Chesapeake Energy Corp. to pay $7.5M to settle Pa. leaseholders' complaint
abstract: Chesapeake Energy Corp will pay $7.5 in response to a complaint by PA leaseholders that claimed that the gas driller shorted them on royalty payments

headline: Gay-marriage ruling sparks a bitter fight in Pa. House
abstract: The recent Supreme Court ruling on gay marriage sparks controversy in the state house between PA Representative Brian Sims and Representative Daryl Metcalfe.

headline: Forging: a practical path to pension reform: Glen Grell
abstract: State Representative Glen Grell writes an editorial detailing the many problems with pensions in PA and possible solutions that can benefit the issue.

headline: GOP accuses Democrats of holding transportation funding plan hostage
abstract: The House Republican leadership in the PA House are accusing the democrats for stalling the transportation funding plan.

headline: Aging vehicles, limited funding cause major headaches for Rabbittransit fleet
abstract: Rabbittransit, a fleet that provides transportation mainly from York to memorial hospitals around the area, is having major issues as their funding becomes limited.

headline: Musto's request to postpone trial denied
abstract: Federal judges dismissed former state Sen. Raphael Musto's appeal of a lower court's order denying his request to indefinitely postpone his corruption trial because of his health issues. Musto was indicted in November 2010 on charges he abused his position as state senator by accepting money and gifts from a local real estate developer, Robert Mericle.

headline:
The Senate liquor plan offers more consumer choices, but it still faces
political hurdles
abstract: The Senate's liquor plan offers more choice convenience for consumers. In this version of the bill, one would be able to buy beer and wine at a local supermarket without having to limit themselves to one beer at a time, PA brewers would be able to sell beer at farmers' markets, etc.

headline: Legislators look at new Medicaid models
abstract: With expansion in mind, PA legislators work on different models to improve Medicaid insurance.

headline: State's exchange will reveal plans, premiums
abstract: Federal health care exchanges go live for PA in October 2013, giving people without insurance a chance to sign up for coverage that could begin in January of 2014. Health advocates already hail the greater access to care that the insurance plans offer in the exchange, especially to cover bases like preventative medicine and mental health.

headline: Capital buzz not about budget
abstract: Although PA Governor Tom Corbett was just hours away from signing a state budged, not many people in the state capital are concerned about the budget. They are more concerned with the privatization of Liquor, transportation funding and Medicaid coverage.

headline: no school, no sports
abstract: The Old Forge School District school board in PA must decide whether sports will be cut from their schools. This has sparked a debate whether sports is in fact an integral part of the educational process in the U.S.

headline: Prescription drug problem is addressed
abstract: The PA state House of Representatives have passed a bill to address aspects of the state's prescription drug problem. The bill awaits state Senate vote. The bill creates a confidential prescription drug monitoring database for professionals who prescribe or dispense prescription medication, with an end goal of helping doctors know who is in real need of prescriptions and who is simply a drug dealer.

headline: Pa. House bill would let drillers pool land
abstract: The PA house passed a bill that will allow drilling companies to pool land into drilling units. Many people are opposed to this bill because they believe it violates landowners' rights.

headline: Face paint, bare chests, and sports bras and masks: Do new rules for student rooting make sense? Editorial
abstract: In this editorial, the author explores whether schools should enforce rules on face painting and cheering at high school sporting events.

headline: Lawmakers think drink tax could save struggling Pennsylvania cities
abstract: PA Lawmakers what the state's Financially Distressed Municipalities Act to allow cash-strapped cities under the law, known as Act-47, to impose up to a 10 percent tax on alcoholic drinks to stabilize their finances. The solution is modeled after the Allegheny County's drink tax.

headline: State budget represents mixed bag for human services
abstract: The new PA budget increases state funding for a variety of human services programs. Some of these programs are designed to help rape victims, stop domestic violence and people with mental disabilities.

headline: Hanger with Dimock endorsements
abstract: John Hanger, a PA gubernatorial candidate, is endorsing the Dimock, PA residents who have encountered problems because of gas drilling.

headline: McCord blasts consultant fees on stalled lottery contract
abstract: PA Democratic gubernatorial candidate and Treasurer Rob McCord criticized Gov. Tom Corbett's effort to privatize the state lottery, calling it a "gross waste of money". The plan to bring in British firm Camelot Global Services to run the state lottery has cost #3.4 million so far.

headline: State aid for SEPTA looks to be delayed
abstract: PA aid to improve SEPTA trains and roads has been halted in the State house, despite being one of Corbett's chief priorities. Some officials believe that the PA house representatives are more concerned with campaigns rather than "the needs of Pennsylvania".

headline: Corbett weighing Medicaid expansion if tied to changes
abstract: Corbett is currently considering expanding Medicaid to thousands of uninsured Pennsylvanians, but there is one exception: he wants significant changes to the existing part of the entitlement program.

headline: Create choices
abstract: Scranton residents call on PA lawmakers to eliminate cross-filing in PA school elections. They highlight the importance of knowing where a candidate stands, based on their party affiliation. However, the current law allows candidates to cross-file in spring primaries for both major party nominations, based the importance of non-partisanship in schools.

headline:
With $28.4b budget, lawmakers and Corbett do the minimum
expected: Editorial
abstract: The author airs his grievances with Governor Tom Corbett's new budget plan, claiming that he simply didn't do enough,.

abstract: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius told Corbett in a letter to switch CHIP, a healthcare insurance plan for children, to Medicaid.

headline: Health care for all in state urged
abstract: Andy Carter, president and CEO of the Hospital & Healthsystem Association of Pennsylvania agrees with PA Gov. Tom Corbetts proposal to provide insurance subsidies for low-income residents, as an avenue for all Pennsylvanians to have health care coverage. Instead of allowing more people to qualify for Medicaid under President Obama's health care law, Gov. Corbett's plan asks the federal government to let the state make its own changes.

headline: Pa. House strips Medicaid expansion from bill
abstract: The PA House of Representative took Medicaid expansion out of the new budget, effectively returning the legislation back to the Senate. The Corbett administration still wants to work with the federal government to work towards the reform proposal.

headline: Rep Conklin offering hearing on Penn State reforms in W. PA
abstract: PA Representative Scott Conklin will have a hearing on reforming Penn State's board of trustees.

headline: Corbett extends British company's lottery management bid until Dec. 31
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett's administration granted another bid extension to a British company that is seeking to manage the state lottery through a long-term, $34 million agreement. The 20-year PA Lottery privatization plan aims to assist a rapidly growing senior population. The republican Governor is facing stiff criticism from Democratic officeholders.

headline: AG Kane vows to monitor Altoona hospital takeover.
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane is making sure that the legal battle between University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and Highmark does not affect patients' access to the central PA health system.

headline: Bread and circuses, but no school
abstract: In the midst of a teacher's strike, the Old Forge School District announced that football will be played despite the ongoing strike.

headline: Toomey lays out goals for budget negotiation
abstract: PA Sen. Pat Toomey, as part of the bipartisan and bicameral budget conference committee, set the goals of keeping the 2011 spending caps in place; letting President Obama decide which programs to fund and which to cut; and including a provision to keep the government funded, at ever decreasing amounts, in the event of an impasse.

headline:
PA budget-related bills remain in limbo that deal with Medicaid
expansion, 'payday' loans, state-related university funding.
abstract: With the beginning of PA's new fiscal year, the Senate will return to the capital to work on budget related bills that deal with Medicaid expansion, pay day loans and state related university funding.

headline: School's open in Philadelphia — but just barely
abstract: While Philadelphia schools are finally open, Superintendent William Hite acknowledges that the schools are understaffed, with its biggest reduction in the number of guidance counselors.

headline: UPMC, Highmark argue over settlement
abstract: Lawyers for HIghmark and UPMC agreed to end antitrust claims in which they face each other. Now Highmark wants a guarantee that UPMC won't characterize it as a monopolist in litigation brought by others, including a pending lawsuit by four plaintiffs. A UPMC spokesman said the hospital system couldn't sign on to a provision that tied its hands in its own legal defense.

headline: Melvin attorney gives 20 reasons for former state Supreme Court Justice’s appeal
abstract: Former Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin was prosecuted for public corruption. Her attorney outlined 20 reasons why Melvin is appealing the court's decision.

abstract: The postal workers’ union, Local 7048 of the APWU, is supporting Army Ranger veteran Kevin Strouse after a hard fought competitive Democratic primary for U.S. House in the 8th District.

abstract: The PA state-appointed city overseer has approved Pittsburgh's 2014 city budget and five-year plan but included an amendment that requires the city to provide additional pension fund money if it does not yield at least an 8 percent return on its investments.

headline:
Madonna and Young: Budget process shows deep divide in Pa.
Legislature
abstract: The authors discuss how the recent budgeting process has shown deep polarization in the PA legislature.

abstract: The PA Board of Education voted in approval of the state's Common Core standards which would require all PA students to pass proficiency tests in Science, math and language arts before graduating.

headline: Robinson sign law draws ACLU's notice
abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union of Pennsylvania is threatening legal action against Robinson Township over what it charges is selective enforcement of campaign-sign restrictions that has targeted Republican candidates. The ACLU asked the township to immediately suspend enforcement of ordinances related to political signs because it contends they violate the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

headline:
NBC 10 uses erroneous data to support Corbett attack on teachers
union

headline: Sharpton, in Phila., campaigns for public education
abstract: Reverend Al Sharpton visited Philadelphia to address the public school crisis in the Higher Education Awareness, Dropout Prevention, and Health Initiative".

abstract: The Montgomery County Republicans united with a peace agreement, following twenty years of discord. The committee chairman Robert J. Kerns also announced that Vahan Gureghian and Robert Asher would now serve as co-chairs of the Finance Committee. The unification of the committee comes at a perfect time to build support for Governor Corbett in the upcoming gubernatorial election.

headline: SRC cancels meeting while funding in limbo
abstract: In the midst of Philadelphia public school funding continuing to be an issue the School Reform Commission decides to cancel their meeting until lawmakers return to Harrisburg to find a solution for funding.

headline: Municipalities slowly move toward using land banks to eliminate blight
abstract: A new state law that uses land banks will potentially eliminate blight in Municipalities. A land bank acts as a legal and financial means to make vacant, abandoned or foreclosed properties fit for productive use.

headline: Big questions greet state bill allowing small games in bars
abstract: Two bills have been put forth in the PA House of Representatives related to small games of chance in PA bars and taverns. Proponents of the bill speak to the potential benefits bars and taverns would see from the addition of small games of chance. While opponents highlight the potential negative effects it could have on the state's casinos and small clubs that already rely on the games.

headline: State agency needs a name change

abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett's administration in 2012 reintroduced an asset test for the state's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program eligibility that had been lifted during the Great Recession. PA is now one of just 13 states with such a test for SNAP, which is federally funded.

headline: Corbett proposes Pennsylvania Medicaid overhaul
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett proposes that he will use the federal Medicaid expansion funding to insure 520,000  low income Pennsylvanians. However, the governor will not expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act.

headline: A per-mile tax? Toll roads are a better alternative
abstract: An Oregon pilot project set to begin in 2015, aims determine combat declining revenue generated by the per-gallon fuel tax by instead implementing a per-mile tax on state residents. However, the inherent cost of tracking a driver's miles, and the privacy concerns add constraints on the possibility of implementing such a system of taxation. abstract: Despite the school district taking out a $3 million loan to stay afloat, Wilkinsburg School District spent over $15,000 on a retreat for administrators.

However, the issue is splitting the state's health group leaders. Nurse practitioners and physician assistants support the plan, while doctors say those groups are not trained to assess the kinds of injuries that may occur in the ring.

abstract: Former Dauphin County GOP chairman and political player William Trickett Smith Sr., is facing new federal charges that he tried to help his son escape prison. His son, William Trickett Smith II, is behind bars in Peru after pleading guilty to murdering his Peruvian wife.
