headline: Governor Corbett has signed execution warrant
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett signed the execution warrant today for Borgela Philistin. Philistin killed Philadelphia police officer Robert Hayes during a traffic stop in 1993. His partner was also paralyzed.

headline: For cities in Act 47 program, a proposed way out
abstract: The Act 47 program, which is designed to aid cities in financial ruin, will propose a deadline for Act 47 municipalities to  leave the program.

headline: First clear majority supporting legalizing marijuana
abstract: For the first time since asking the question, a Gallup poll shows a clear majority of Americans support legalization of marijuana. Two possible reasons for the overall uptick, according to Gallup: an increasing number of Americans who now admit they've tried the drug; and pot advocates success at the ballot box in recent years.

headline: Community corrections centers must improve return rates
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Corrections' 2013 Recidivism Report says 60 percent of inmates return within three years. "It's a major issue everywhere," said Northampton Co. Executive John Stoffa.

headline: Corbett picks PNC Park over Pennsylvania GOP fall dinner
abstract: Governor Tom Corbett attends a Pittsburgh Pirates game instead of attending the annual Republican fall dinner. Political pundits believe that Corbett's decision could payoff during the election.

headline: Kelly Green Project strives to improve community
abstract: Germantown, PA, citizens are working to uplift an entire community with the building of a playground and nature space at neighborhood school John B. Kelly Elementary. To make the playground a reality, the Kelly Green organizers need to raise $1 million.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Payday lenders looking for prey among the poor
abstract: Payday lenders could not get a PA Senate committee to move a bill that would let them prey on the working poor with annual rates of up to 369 percent. PA has a tough anti-predatory lending law that caps the annual percentage rate for loans at 24 percent however a bill in the PA senate banking committee might change this and Pennsylvanians need to beware.

headline: Governor not worried about challengers next year
abstract: KDKA political editor Jon Delano sat down with PA Gov. Tom Corbett to talk about his sagging poll numbers and his potential challengers when he is up for reelection in 2014.

headline: Nutter brings schools message to Corbett
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter warned Governor Tom Corbett of the lack of funding his school district receives, saying that the inadequate funding could damage the futures of students and the state's economy.

headline: Restaurants, lofts first sign of development near Consol Energy Center
abstract: The construction property on Fifth Avenue is being developed across the street from the Consol Energy Center. It will house restaurants on the main level, with lofts on the second and third, and a roof-top bar on the fourth.

headline: Governor accused of taking improper gifts
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett has been accused of taking improper gifts from businessmen and lobbyists during his time in office.

headline: Cheyney alumni call for fair funding
abstract: A group of concerned Cheyney University supporters believe that PA  is discriminating against the historically black institution, by pointing out in a letter that that their funding is unfair compared to other universities. The state has been given 10 days to respond to this letter or the group will file a civil rights lawsuit.

headline: Westmoreland housing authority seeks OK to use facilities as collateral for renovations
abstract: The Westmoreland County Housing Authority could reclassify about 25 percent of its public housing inventory as part of a move to raise as much as $15 million to pay for renovations. The move comes as the Authority board voted to apply for participation in the Rental Assistance Demonstration Program, a federal program that transfers public housing units to Section 8 subsidized housing.

headline: Court rules administration wrongly diverted tobacco settlement money
abstract: On Tuesday, a Commonwealth Court judge declared unconstitutional a state law that siphoned money from the Adult Basic Health Care program into state coffers.

headline: Pennsylvania state Treasurer Rob McCord tweaks Gov. Tom Corbett in announcing run for governor
abstract: PA state treasure Rob McCord announces his run for Governor. He denounces current Governor Tom Corbett's by calling it "four years of neglect".

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: New complex in N. Phila features long-needed grocery
abstract: Micheal Groasso, president of Metro Development Co. of Admore, and owner of ShopRite, Jeff Brown, came together to build the Bakers Shopping Centre in North Philadelphia near Fox street and Hunting Park Ave. The center now provides grocery and shopping options to a once underdeveloped and impoverished area of north philly.

headline: Corbett still considering Medicaid expansion
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett has the choice whether to allow the state to cooperate with the Afforable Care Act's expanded Medicaid program. Other Republican governors also making the same consideration.

headline: Can health care system meet the demand?
abstract: This article explores whether the expansion of health care can effectively withstand the demand.

headline: Family affair? The exits at the Heinz Endowments are a concern
abstract: High profile members have been leaving their positions at the Heinz Endowment. Speculation suggests that moves coincide with the endowments initiative with the Center for Sustainable Shale Development.

headline: Al Boscov inducted into retailers hall of fame
abstract: Al Boscov, chairman of Boscov's Department Stores LLC was honored with induction into the PA Retail Hall of Fame. A mix of local and state dignitaries, including Gov. Tom Corbett and former Gov. Ed Rendell; community members, friends and family were in attendance.

headline: City favors downtown casino
abstract: Mayor Nutter's economic team has expressed their support for the city's second casino license.

headline: Gov. Corbett signs law to end CHIP wait time
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett signed a bill renewing the state Children's Health Insurance Program and eliminating a sex-month waiting period for enrollment. This is the first element of his proposed "Healthy PA" plan to be completed since he introduced the plan.

headline: Lawmaker wants to give voters more time to go to polling place
abstract: A PA legislator wants to extend the hours that polling places are open.

headline: Anti-property tax sentiment passionate, but diffuse
abstract: PA Representative Jim Cox is heading an attempt to eliminate school property taxes in the state. This plan would replace the levy controlled by school districts with higher rates of the personal income tax and the sales and use tax.

headline: MCASB: Scores are a collective problem
abstract: Mount Carmel Area School Board President Donna James called the district's elementary schools low scores a "collective problem". James urged parents and the overall community to assist students, teachers and administrators in improving scholastic scores.

headline: Pay to play scandal at Turnpike
abstract: Former PA Senator Robert Mellow has been accused of a "pay to play" scandal involving contracts with the PA Turnpike Commission. He is currently serving time in federal prison.

headline: Pa. lawmakers push for extending statute of limitations for child sex abuse victims
abstract: Lawmakers in PA are pushing to extend statute of limitations for victims of child sex abuse.

headline: Hospitals work together to target region's ills
abstract: Five Lehigh Valley nonprofit health insititutions will target four issues; caring for vulnerable first-time mothers and their babies; improving mental-health services; providing access to care and addressing health literacy, in an unprecedented cooperative arrangement to improve the region's well-being.

headline: Corbett calls committee vote ‘momentous’ first step toward privatization of liquor
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is hailing the house committee's vote to privatize the state liquor system. The plan faces an uphill battle ahead.

headline: Obamacare signups system 'ready to go,' shutdown or not
abstract: Despite Republicans in Congress threatening to stop the funding of the Affordable Care Act, the online insurance markets provided by the legislation will still be open.

headline: Scranton council pleased with aggressive approach to collect delinquent trash fees
abstract: To out the non-payers, Scranton published in the newspaper its lengthy list of delinquent trash-fee accounts. The list of 4,624 delinquent accounts from 2002 through 2011, represents some $7.63 million owed to the city, encompassed 15 full newspaper pages in the edition of The Times-Tribune. Councilman Pat Rogan, who has proposed going from a flat fee to a per bag fee, argued that chronic nonpayers should not have their trash collected because, "The free ride has to end."

headline: House committee approves liquor privatization bill
abstract: The bill to privatize the state's liquor system has made it through its first legislative step.

headline: Gov. Corbett's secret weapon
abstract: This article postulates that the Democratic candidates running for PA Governor Corbett's seat may be at a disadvantage since they are spending so much money to win the primary.

headline: City Council approves bill transferring $50M to Philly schools
abstract: Philadelphia City Council unanimously passed a bill transferring $50 million from the city grants revenue fund to the general fund as part of a plan to give city schools much-needed funding in exchange for surplus properties.

headline: Corbett is highest paid governor in the country
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is the highest paid governor in the country followed by California Gov Jerry Brown.

headline: Casey eyes recovery of remains of Penn Hittls pilot, other military lost overseas
abstract: PA Senator Bob Casey Jr. wants to recover the remains of service members who fought in Vietnam, Korea, the Cold War, the Persian Gulf and World War II. Ideally, the senator would like to return these remains to their families

headline: Ch. 11 News: Pensions and education funding also of concern for governor
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett continues to show concern with the state's pension obligations. He says that they are the source of much of the state's budgetary issues.

headline: LA Times: Corbett is highest paid governor in country
abstract: PA Gov Tom Corbett is the highest paid governor in the country according to the Los Angeles Times. Corbett is paid $183,000. California Gov. Jerry Brown is paid $165,288 per year.

headline: Charged PA Cyber founder hires Washington, D.C., attorneys
abstract: Pennsylvania Cyber Charter School founder Nick Trombetta has pleaded not guilty to charges of mail fraud, theft or bribery from a program receiving federal funds, tax conspiracy and filing a false tax return. As a result, he has hired experienced Washington D.C. attorney's to defend him.

headline: Editorial: Corbett makes welcome pitch to boost spending on those with disabilities
abstract: As part of his 2013-14 spending plan, Gov. Corbett wants to increase funding for services for physically and mentally handicapped individuals. He proposed a $20 million increase to provide community-based services for people with Down syndrome, autism and other challenges. He also wants to eliminate waiting lists for services.

headline: Something positive, believe it or not, from some Pa. lawmakers
abstract: PA Legislators will be participating in a charity baseball game that will benefit antihunger efforts.

headline: Western PA man gets death in disabled woman's torture.
abstract: Ricky Smyrnes of Greensburg, PA was sentenced to death for the group turture and murder of a mentally disabled woman three years ago. Defense attorney Terrance Faye promised to appeal Smyrnes' sentence. He claims that the jury did not give enough consideration to his abusive upbringing. This case represents 198th person on PA's death row.

headline: Regs hit hardest in coal country
abstract: PA Representative Tom Marino and a bipartisan group of lawmakers have developed a "Coal Caucus" in order to oppose new federal emissions limits brought on by the EPA on coal plants in PA.

headline: Nationwide cuts could trouble low-income children, seniors
abstract: The federal sequestration program, if put into effect, could eliminate programs like Meals on Wheels, low-income spots in the Head Start program, and induce a 5.1% elimination of child-care assistance. Between 600,000-750,000 women and children who receive WIC supplemental nutrition could be cut from the program nationwide.

headline: For the state's worst bridges, a chance for repair chugs along
abstract: A state panel met in hopes to create a plan to bring public and private funding together to fix PA's worst bridges. If this plan can garner money from the legislature there is a chance that the state can build up to a thousand new bridges.

headline: Gov. Tom Corbett: Prosecutions, politics and the criticism he can't shake
abstract: Gov. Corbett's tenure as attorney general has been heavilly criticised. His problems include his handling of the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse case, the Bonusgat probe of Capitol Corruption, and the investigation of a consultant of his Democratic opponent when he was seeking re-election as attorney general. His suit against the NCAA also looks to be politically motivated as his 2014 re-election campaign is fast approaching. According to PennLive, Gov. Corbett waited to arrest child predators until there was enough cases for an impressive publicity stunt.

headline: WATCHBLOG: ‘Business as usual’ for PA state government as feds prepare for shutdown
abstract: Despite the federal government preparing for shut down, the PA state government will continue to run normally. In regards to state agencies who receive federal funding, the Governor has directed those agencies to continue providing short term services for the time being.

headline: Pitt to take role in managing the Specter archive.
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh and Philadelphia University will preserve and exhibit the late Senator Arlen Specter's collection of papers, photographs and recordings. Specter began his career as assistant DA, then was the DA of Philadelphia, and then spent thirty years as a U.S. senator.

headline: Former U.S. Rep. Mark Critz runs afoul of some Democrats over rape remark and marriage equality
abstract: Former U.S. Rep and current PA lieutenant gubernatorial candidate Mark Critz told an off color joke regarding rape and homosexuality art a democratic event.

headline: Ban 'gifts,' fees
abstract: Gov. Corbett accepted more than $11,000 worth of gifts, vacations, sports and entertainment tickets, and paid travel expenses from interest groups in 2010-2011. State law only requires Gov. Corbett to disclose the gifts, which he has done. The author believes that mere disclosure is not enough and gifts should be made illegal.

headline: Now's the time to seek benefits
abstract: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services, Kathleen Sibelius writes an editorial on the Affordable Care Act and how to take advantage of it.

headline: Pa. court: Reinstate health-care funding for the poor
abstract: Commonwealth Court President Judge Dan Pellgrini has ordered the Corbett administration to reinstate funding for adultBasic and Medicaid programs. He ruled two statutes unconstitutional that diverted money from the federal tobacco settlement to finance items other than healthcare in the general budget.

headline: Indictment of ex-CEO of cyber charter resonates in Erie
abstract: Pennsylvania Cyber Charter School founder Nick Trombetta has been accused of stealing $990,000 of public school money. Erie tax payers are feeling the affects of Trombetta's actions.

headline: New septic standards could stifle economic development, business leaders say
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection is setting tougher septic system standards in order to reduce nitrate pollution for new residential development in watersheds with protected streams. County officials in the Pocono Mountains are worried that the new rule will negatively impact economic development.

headline: Road to women’s equality has high, low points
abstract: This article examines the current state of women's equality in the workplace. Statistics from the labor department has shown that women's salaries over the past few years have gone up; however, it has been at a rather slow rate.

headline: Tobyhanna to furlough 5,136 civilian employees
abstract: Tobyhanna U.S. Army Depot, is a primary facility for repair and maintenance of communications and electronic equipment and a major employer in northeastern PA. It will face $309 million in budget cuts and 5,136 civilian employee furloughs because of the federal budget sequestration. U.S. Sen. Bob Casey said the indiscriminate cuts from the sequester do not make sense.

headline: Ruling may make open records process more complex, costly
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruling on the open records process, will make it more time consuming and expensive to go through the process.

headline: Editorial: A gift ban for state officials is a small step that would send a big message
abstract: PA lawmakers and Gov. Corbett should join about a dozen other states in passing a ban on gifts to elected and appointed state officials. In PA donations to political campaigns have no limit and lobbyists are not required to disclose the recipients of their gifts. Gov. Corbett accepted $11,343 worth of gifts in 2010 and 2011 from lobbyists who had business or would have business before the state.

headline: Labor Day traffic jams could be daily occurrence by the 2020s, study says
abstract: According to a travel-industry study, we can expect labor day level traffic jams on a routine basis.

headline: Penn State sues insurer over Sandusky insurance coverage.
abstract: Penn State sued its insurance carrier for not honoring its legal obligation to cover claims related to sexual misconduct by former football coach Jerry Sandusky. The PA Manufacturers' Association Insurance Company (PMA) is said to have failed to provide coverage which Penn State had bargained and paid for. There are five lawsuits from attorney's for twenty-four other claimants.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: The least they can do
abstract: City Council President, Darrell Clarke announced his opposition for Mayor Michael Nutter’s plan to borrow $50 million to fill gaps in education funding, and rehire laid off school employees. If the city’s sales tax hike is not extended, the Mayor’s plan would require a $60 million repayment in principle and interest. Governor Corbett has also refused to to lend $45 million until reforms within the school district are made.

headline: New Benner Township prison will be statewide inmate transportation hub
abstract: A new prison in Benner Township, Centre County, will serve as a transportation hub for PA jails. Its central location in the state and proximity to I-80 make it an ideal hub. All prisoners will be more efficiently classified at the new Benner Prison and then will be bused out to other facilities in the state.

headline: State Sen. Brewster to serve on new Port Authority board
abstract: Expanding to 11 members, Mr. Brewster, D-McKeesport, was appointed to a four-year term on the nonsalaried Port Authority board by Senate Minority Leader Jay Costa Jr., D-Forest Hills.

headline: SRC votes to close 23 schools, spare four
abstract: The Philadelphia School Reform Commission voted to close down 23 schools but spare four it had considered closing. There has been a long series of protests and rallies against the school shutdowns including the arrests of 19 people trying to block the SRC member's entrance to their meeting. SRC Chairman Pedro Ramos said the large number of closings was the result of years of delayed decisions and financial crisis. The Philadelphia School District had borrowed $300 million just to pay its bills last year.

headline: Give ride inspections to U.S. agency
abstract: A report by Public Source, an independent investigative journalism group, found that dangerous amusement park rides were not being inspected. A proposal by U.S. Sen. Edward J. Markey would allow the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission to provide uniform regulation of amusement park rides in all 50 states.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: One more reason for Medicaid expansion
abstract: Gov. Corbett should enact the expansion of Medicaid under Obamacare which would be fully funded by Washington for three years and at 90 percent for the next four years. Gov. Corbett has refused to go along with the optional Medicaid move saying that the state's long-term costs would exceed the federal share. The autheor believes the recent ruling by Commonwealth Court President Judge Dan Pellegrini to reinstate federal tobacco-settlement funds to the state's adultBasic and Medicaid insurance programs would cost the state more anyway so why not accept federal funds to boost Medicaid?

headline: Oh, how our lawmakers care for themselves
abstract: John Baer, Daily News Political Columnist, voices his opinion on PA’s legislature. In this article Baer voices concern over tax-free Per Diem pay that is given to members of the legislature. These daily stipend can run upwards of $185.00 and require no proof of expense.

headline: Level field for schools
abstract: Charter schools have competitive advantages due to inequities in funding and accountability compared with conventional public schools. A reform bill from Rep. James Roebuck, Dem. Philadelphia, would change the excessive payments to charter schools by altering tuition costs. State Auditor Jack Wagner released a report last year that found charter schools might be overpaid by as much as $365 million per year.

headline: Take a minute to remember all that Dauphin County has to offer: Jeff Haste
abstract: Many events have been recently hosted in Dauphin County, some of which have gathered crowds of 8,000 people. In addition unemployment has decreased in the past year and the housing market has been booming. Dauphin County has invested in many revitalization projects, and it appears to be paying off.

headline: In the $100,000 Club, one in three come from the state-owned universities
abstract: A third of employee's at state-owned universities earned $100,000+ last year. A PennLive analysis found that some lower-level administrators and faculty are outearning presidents and chancellors, with salaries ranging from $199,000-$275,000. Faculty members say that the level of education needed to teach at universities and debt accumulated to acquire that education deserves high salaries. A competitive marketplace is also driving up compensation packages.

headline: State Rep. Marty Flynn takes down man "creeping" in his neighborhood
abstract: State Representative Marty Flynn aided in the arrest of Mark Zvolensky, who he spotted prowling, and appeared intoxicated in his neighborhood around 11:30 PM. Flynn spotted Zvolensky during his nightly run, and after him, eventually tackling him. Zvolensky was later arrested and charged with loitering, disorderly conduct and resisting arrest.

headline: Environmental activists fear proposed law will send mixed signals with gas industry By: Joe Holden
abstract: The bi-partisan backed Wilkes-Bare Luzerne County-House Bill 683 aims to crack down on farm tresspassers who obtain video and pictures illegally. Scott Cannon, a documentarian, believes the bill, if passed, could be applied to those who videotape natural gas operations. Sponsers of the bill say its original intent had nothing to do with the gas industry.

headline: Pa. interstates are nation's 8th busiest
abstract: The Federal Highway Administration compared data from all 50 states and found that people traveled 23.7 billion times on interstate highways in PA making the the 8th busiest in the nation.

headline: New poll shows Corbett's numbers put him in 'dire shape'
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett's approval ratings have slipped to 33 percent approval and 57 percent disaproval, he also trails every Democratic canditate tested against him as of March 2013. Dean Debnam, president of Public Policy Polling said Gov. Corbett "looks like the most endangered governor in the country up for re-election next year." Voters disaprove of his lottery privatisation plan and his handling of the Sandusky child sexual abuse scandal.

headline: Voters remember Margolies, poll shows
abstract: After more than twenty years between her previous position in the U.S House and her current bid, polls show that Marjorie Margolies still holds positive name recognition among voters. Although positive identification of previous incumbents tends to decrease over time, Margolies is defying the odds with high ranking in the polls.

headline: Lawmakers eying elimination of school property taxes
abstract: Two dozen PA Republican and Democratic lawmakers put forth legislation to replace the $10.4 billion collected every year in school property taxes with new revenue generated by inreases in sales and personal income taxes. Existing gambling revenues will help to replace the lost revenue as well as new sales taxes on things like candy, gum, newspapers, textbooks, and basic TV subscriptions.

headline: Naked truth about gender-ID bill
abstract: After a 14 year-old encountered a transgender male changing in the same locker room, concerns are being raised about the role of gender identity in high-schools. The author stresses that anatomy, not gender affiliation is the purpose of separate locker rooms.

headline: High-speed rail concept would include the Lehigh Valley
abstract: Alfred Twu, a San Francisco Bay area graphic artist and mass transit advocate designed California's proposed high-speed rail line. He is now designing a U.S. route that would start in Boston, go through NYC and PA, move west to Chicago and end in Los Angeles. Other nation's have invested in high-speed rail while the U.S. has recently gutted funding for it. The author believes this is a major mistake.

headline: PA bands with other states to check for duplicate registrations
abstract: In an effort to prevent voters from being registering in multiple states, The Department of State announced that PA will be sharing registration rolls with 23 other states to check for duplicates. The initiative will come at no additional cost to voters.

headline: Dozens seek job as a Traffic Court judge
abstract: PA Republican leader Dominic Pileggi has sponsored a bill to abolish Traffic Court after a federal indictment alleged widespread ticket-fixing. Out of seven judges, three retired or resigned before the indictment and three others were suspended. These events have note stopped 41 people from seeking election to the Philadelphia Traffic Court. The judgeship's pay $91,000 a year for a six-year term and doesn't require a law degree or even a high-school diploma. If new judges are elected and sworn in before the bill passes, they would keep their jobs and salaries for six years.

headline: Urgency sought for funding Pennsylvania roads and transit
abstract: Senators and other civic and business leaders in Pittsburgh are pressuring members of the State House of Representatives to pass legislation that would provide funding for PA roads and transit. Speaking at separate legislative hearings, they warned of economic harm, human suffering and jeopardized public safety that could result if the Legislature fails to agree

headline: Senator Jake Corman trying to join fight against NCAA suit
abstract: State Sen. Jake Corman a Republican, whose district includes State College and who chair's the Senate Appropriations Committee has asked permission to join Gov. Tom Corbett and other state officials as a defendant in the NCAA case. The federal lawsuit by the NCAA seeks to void a new state law requiring Penn State's $60 million fine from the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse scandal to be used in PA alone. The NCAA claims that the law is unconstitutional because it amounts to unlawful government interference in a contractual agreement between the NCAA and Penn State and interferes witih interstate commerce.

headline: Pennsylvania’s share of Marcellus shale jobs dips
abstract: Down from 72 percent in the year prior, PA State residents accounted for only 56.8 percent of new hires among drillers, pipeline companies and contractors in the Marcellus Shale Coalition. Penn State economist Timothy Kelsey argues that proper training is key to safe drilling, and that a lack of trained welders could be causing the dip in hiring.

headline: Small games of chance hearing in Fayette postponed
abstract: A House Democratic Policy Committee public hearing focusing on the state's Small Games of Chance law has been postoned due to the absence of legislators. They legislators claimed they had business to handle in their home districts.

headline: PA court outlines issues for gay marriage hearing
abstract: A Pennsylvania court laid out the issues to be argued at a hearing regarding a suburban Philadelphia court clerk's decision to issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples. The court will focus on issues such as jurisdiction, constitutional interpretation, and Attorney General Kathleen Kane’s decision to not defend the marriage law.

headline: Federal case likely not relevant to Mellow's new woes
abstract: PA Sen. Robert J. Mellow and seven other men were announced on criminal charges in a mulitmillion-dollar "pay-to-play" scheme involving the PA Turnpike. However Mr. Mellow's March 2012 plea agreement that resulted in Mr. Mellow's guilty plea to conspiracy to commit mail fraud and tax evasion expressly bars the U.S. attorney's office from charging him again for any additional offenses. Attorney Christopher T. Powell said Mr. Mellow is serving his time and the federal prosecutors are not going to reopen or charge him federally. However if the federal grand jury that investigated Mr. Mellow touched on matters that became the basis for the state charges, there may be an opening for Mr. Mellow's counsel.

headline: Use Oregon tuition plan
abstract: President Barack Obama along with Vice President Joe Biden will speak to students at Lackawanna College in PA regarding the cost and value of higher education. The pair has advocated for lower interest rates on student loans in the past, and is expected to take note of legislation in Oregon, which ties student loan repayment rates to income upon graduation.

headline: State lawmaker from Robeson says Corbett supports property tax bill
abstract: State Rep. Mark M. Gillen said he spoke with Gov. Tom Corbett on the phone and got assurance that he would sign the Property Tax Independence Act if it was revenue neutral. The bill attempts to eliminate property taxes as a source for school funding. The bill would replace property taxes by increasing the state's personal income and sales taxes and by tapping gaming resources. Rep. Gillen announced the news to the Berks Tea Party organisation.

headline: Pa. high court targets private legal work by staff
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that state appellate court staff members may not conduct private legal work for compensation. The ruling aims to prevent corruption in the form of referrals and conflicts of interest in the within the appellate court.

headline: PA jury commissioner abolition law thrown out.
abstract: The PA Supreme Court voted 6-0 to throw out the 2011 law that would allow counties to abolish the office of jury comissioners. They ruled that the law violates the state constitution's single-subject provision. Jury commissioners help ensure that trial jurors reflect a cross-section of society and deal with juror problems. Critics say the job can be computerized. The justices claim the change was tied with a measure that dealt with electronic auctions by counties and the state constitution requires bill's not have more than one subject.

headline: Team Corbett members: Here today, gone tomorrow with the latest being acting education secretary William Harner
abstract: PA Education Secretary William Harner was the latest top-level staff member to be fired. Harner’s removal comes in the wake of an investigation surrounding his behavior at Cumberland Valley High School. Harner is only one of many of Governor Corbett's top-level staff to be dismissed.

headline: McCord hires accomplished fundraiser for possible gov run
abstract: State Treasurer Rob McCord has hired Mike Butler, a senior political advisor and fundraiser which indicates he might run for the Democratic nomination for governor. Mike Butler was responsible for the reelection campain for Sen. Bob Casey. He has raised more than $50 million statewide for Democratic canditates.

headline: Corbett hopeful about Medicaid alternative plan
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has proposed an alternative way to provide health care coverage to Pennsylvania’s uninsured citizens. Gov. Corbett, as part of his Healthy Pennsylvania initiative, has proposed taking federal funds and giving them directly to qualified individuals. Instead of following the Medicaid expansion plan in the Affordable Care Act, PA opted in favor of developing an alternative approach for the state.

headline: Op-Ed: Corbett liquor plan will hurt small businesses
abstract: Gov. Tom Corbett's liquor privatization plan will hurt small businesses. State beer distributors would be put at a competitive disadvantage against big box retailers like Wal-Mart under the Corbet plan. A license would cost beer distributors $150,000 while giant retailers would only pay about $25,000. Also allocating $1 billion over four years in funds from liquor license sales for education does not help offset the consecutive billion-dollar cuts to education in Corbett's budget. There are also concerns that private operators will locate away from rural locations and when the commonwealth loses its bulk purchasing power, which is used to leverage lower wholesale prices, consumers prices would increase.

headline: Democratic Committee has say in Coatesville text scandal
abstract: The Chester County Democratic Committee passed a resolution that called for the removal of Coatesville Area School District solicitor James Ellison and acting superintendent Angelo Romaniello. The resolution responds to a scandal created by the racist and sexist text messages exchanged on the district-issued cell phones of Former Superintendent Richard Como and former Director of Athletics and Activities Jim Donato.

headline: Pittsburgh mayoral hopefuls crowd in for debate
abstract: A debate between Pittsburgh mayoral canditates occurred last weekend. Attendee's included city Controller Michael Lamb, city Councilman Bill Peduto, Council President Darlene Harris, fromer state Auditor General Jack Wagner, state rep. Jake Wheatley and city resident A.J richardson who listed his occupation as "school bus monitor" when filing to run for mayor. Current Mayor Luke Ravenstahl announced he would not seek reelection.

headline: Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem: We must add amenities to remain competitive
abstract: Executives of the Sands Casino Resort in Bethlehem, PA believe continued expansion will keep them ahead of potential new casinos in New Jersey and New York. Further redevelopment will happen as soon as Bethlehem is granted a state City Revitalization and Improvement Zone.

headline: An unsafe limitation
abstract: The new prescription drug limitation by the PA Department of Public Welfare in January, 2012,  arbitrarily and unsafely limits the number of monthly prescriptions for patients on Medicaid. It has some exceptions for chronic conditions like diabetes, cancer and heart disease. The policy was chosen to save the state money, however studies of prescription limits found costs actually increase as a result of increased hospital admissions and emergency room visits by patients denied medications. Preliminary data in PA backs up these studies.

headline: Erie Planning Commission OK’s blight designation for proposed Bayfront development
abstract: The Erie Planning Commission approved the designation of Erie’s east Bayfront as blighted. The Economic Development Corp. of Erie County has proposed using the site for a $32 million import-export facility operated by an international logistics and warehousing company. This is the latest step in the Economic Development Corp.’s plans to develop a large-scale regional logistics hub – the Erie Inland Port Project – at several sites in Erie and Ashtabula counties.

headline: Medicaid comments not meant as criticism, Smucker says
abstract: Lancaster County lawmaker Lloyd Smucker supports adding hundreds of thousands of low-income Pennsylvanians to the state's Medicaid program as authorized by the Federal Affordable Care Act. Smucker is the third Republican state Senator to pubicly voice his support for Medicaid expansion but claims he isn't trying to criticize Gov. Corbett who says he can't agree to the expansion unless he gets assurances it will come with reforms and more state flexibility to limit costs.

headline: Minister Max Myers throws hat in Democratic ring for governor.
abstract: Max Myers is the newest Democratic candidate for PA governor in 2014. Myers, is a former Republican, and an Army veteran who after college served as pastor at several Assembly of God churches in the Midwest region and now lives in suburbran Harrisburg. He has also worked with an evangelical group called Global Awakening. Myers has no previous political experience. He said that as governor he would work to eradicate poverty and ensure that all children receive a world-class education.

headline: Shutdown delays real estate closings
abstract: The federal government shutdown has delayed clients from receiving federal loans for real estate properties, especially in rural areas. The shutdown has affected the processing abilities of the US Department of Agriculture and Federal Housing Administration which handle real estate mortgages and loans. The PA Association of Realtors explained the longer the federal government remains shut down, the more difficult it will be to get certain paperwork and funding processed.

headline: Sands' table games revenue climbs, but Pennsylvania's falls
abstract: Sands Casino Resort in Bethlehem led all PA casino's in table games revenues for the 14th consecutive month. However the $55.3 million brought in statewide is a 2.1 percent drop over 2012 and is the first decrease since table games opened in PA in 2010. The drop occurred even as the state added an 11th casino in Valley forge in 2012.

headline: Nurse intended to help father die, prosecutor says: Daughter gave 93-year-old Schuylkill man a bottle of morphine and left the room
abstract: The charge on Barbara Mancini for assisting in her father’s suicide has sparked discussion about the right to die in Pennsylvania. This is a strong case for the kind of situation the PA Legislature needs to confront the State’s death with dignity laws.

headline: PA Turnpike CEO orders review of contracts.
abstract: A compliance officer will review every professional services contract that was cited in a grand jury report that alleged a long-running "pay-to-play" scheme at the PA Turnpike comission. One contract singled out by the grand jury was the $82 million contract from technology consulting firm Ciber Inc. Witnesses testified that a Ciber ex-vice president, Dennis Miller, told employees to bill for unnecessary tasks, help raise money for an influential former state senator, and buy expensive dinners and other gifts for top turnpike commission officals.

headline: Teaming up: Health system, hospital to work together
abstract: Conemaugh Health System and Somerset Hospital leaders have agreed to develop a “collaborative relationship” to explore ways to reduce duplication and other expenses related to competition, while both remaining independent organizations. The collaboration could improve both organizations’ position in obtaining favorable reimbursement contracts with health care insurance providers and could lead to joint insurance plans offered through local employers.

headline: Former DEP chief McGinty weighing bid for governor.
abstract: Kathleen McGinty, a former state Environmental Protection Secretary, said that she is considering entering the crowded Democratic race for PA governor in 2014. McGinty calls herself a centrist. She headed the DEP for more than five years under Gov. Ed Rendell and now is an executive with Weston Solutions Inc. She recently filed papers to form a political action committee called New Jobs, Bright Future PA to raise money for her campaign

headline: City applies for $2M in development funds
abstract: The city of Wilkes-Barre announced an application for nearly $2 million in community development funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. The money requested would go toward road paving, fire equipment and the razing of abandoned houses, as well as the home investment partnership program and emergency solutions grant for aiding the homeless.

headline: Duquesne University School of Law's clinical program expand
abstract: The Duquesne University School of Law's clinical program  will spend a total of $1.2 million to buy and refurbish a building at 914 Fifth Ave, Pittsburgh and develop a new law clinic. The law school received a $500,000 grant from the state's Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program which is allocated by the state's Office of the Budget.

headline: City launches web-based mobile app
abstract: The new web-based app, myPhillyRising, shares upcoming events and other local resources to get people more involved in distressed Philadelphia neighborhoods.

headline: Keystone Exams loophole undermines impact of standardized tests
abstract: The author believes that the new mandatory PA highschool education standards test called "Keystone exams" has a loophole. If students do not pass the exams, the school must offer the student supplmental instruction and then the student will be permitted to retake any Keystone exam in which they didn't score proficient or higher. If the student still fails they may qualify to participate in one or more project-based assessments in order to graduate. The author believes this is unfair to the students who work hard and pass the exams the first time and the system gives no incentive to work hard.

headline: Local federal court employees ordered to work without pay
abstract: U.S. District Chief Judge Joy Flowers Conti issued an order declaring all Western District Court employees working in Pittsburgh, Johnstown and Erie to be essential. Therefore, meaning they will be required to work without immediate prospects of being paid. Employees would be paid for their time worked after the federal government is fully funded again.

headline: PA House to vote on privatizing PA liquor system.
abstract: A vote on the privatization of liquor licenses is scheduled this week in the state House. Gov. Tom Corbett supports liquor privatization and wants to spend the revenue to improve public education. Republican sponsors defeated unified Democrats during a key vote. The union that represents state liquor store employees is working to defeat the measure. The proposal would give beer distributors the first chance to get 1,200 wine and spirit licenses and open grocery stores to wine sales.

headline: Union rep: Road work makes jobs
abstract: Richard Bloomingdale, president of the Pennsylvania American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations told PA Democratic legislators that steps to creating jobs should include investing in the state’s transportation infrastructure, raising the minimum wage, expanding Medicaid and resisting budget cuts.

headline: Proposed abortion bills draw focus of Planned Parenthood of Western Pennsylvania, Women’s Law Project
abstract: Legislation aimed at restricting coverage in insurance exchanges will go into effect next year. Planned Parenthood of Western PA and the Women's law Project are advocating for an exception to be added to legislation that would allow abortions if a woman's health is at risk. The current bill provides coverage for abortions only in cases of rape, incest, or when the woman's life is in danger. Adding a health-risk exception would protect women who want to have a baby but have medical complications during pregnancy that threaten their long-term health but not their life. The dominant public opinion is that taxpayer dollars should not be used to pay for elective abortions.

headline: East End busway project roars ahead in job expected to bolster East Liberty
abstract: Work has begun in East Liberty to clear the way for a $127 million transit-oriented development that includes making access to the East Busway easier. The $127 million price tag includes $23.5 million of public funds, such as grants and money from a Transit Revitalization Improvement District, which funnels money to infrastructure improvements in lieu of tax payments.

headline: Pittsburgh lawsuit challenges UPMC's tax status
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl is challenging UPMC's tax-exempt nonprofit status. UPMC is the $10 billion medical organization and biggest property owner in Allegheny county, it is also has non-profit status which means it gets a $20 million tax-break from the city every year because it pays taxes on only a portion of its properties. However a new lawsuit filed in Common Pleas Court, demands six years' worth of back payroll taxes and the removal of UPMC's tax-exmpt status. The PA Supreme Court ruled last year that a non-profit must not only operate entirely free of profit motive but donate gratuitously a substantial portion of its services.

headline: Closing part of Pittsburgh Public Schools cost-saving proposal
abstract: Pittsburgh Public School Superintendent Linda Lane announced her plans to present to the Pittsburgh Public School board her wide-ranging proposal as part of the district’s efforts to cut costs and improve education. Ms. Lane explained the plan will include options and that school closures would be part of a plan but not the only aspect.

headline: DPW name change passes committee amid cost concerns
abstract: A measure to change the PA Department of Public Welfare's name has passed a state House committee. The name change is an attempt to rid the department of negative connotations. The estimated cost to change the name is $8 million, mostly in website changes. Opponents say the name change will be useless. Republican Rep. Brad Roae remarked that "food stamps" are now called SNAP but everyone stilll refers to the program as food stamps. Other opponents say the money is better spent on services.

headline: Officials host panel to aid ex-offenders in job hunt
abstract: State and local officials addressed specific issues facing female ex-offenders returning to society. The panel, featuring a range of legislators, policymakers and correctional professionals, focused on housing, GED, employment, program funding and new policies.

headline: Jury selection in Gosnell abortion clinic case scheduled to start Monday
abstract: Jury selection begins to prosecute Kermit Gosnell of first degree murder and sentence him to death for allegedly kiling seven infants born alive and viable after their mothers had abortions. Gosnell is also charged with third-degree murder in the death of 41-year-old Karnamaya Mongar. Nine of Gosnell's clinic employee's, including his wife are charged with him for conspiracy, and participating in a corrupt organization. All but one pleaded guilty. Abortion opponents argue this case shows the true face of abortion and those in favor of legal abortion say opponents are trying to use this criminal worst-case scenario to overturn legalized abortion. Gov. Corbett has recently passed Act 122, a law regulating all free-standing abortion clinics.

headline: Insurance agent: Obamacare worth the cost: Residents told ability for anyone to get insurance worth the price tag
abstract: Allentown insurance agent, Stephen Stahl, told Forty Fort residents Obamacare is going to be expensive, but it’s a cost worth paying for the safety net it provides. The federal health care reform law, also known as Obamacare, states no insurer can deny coverage based on pre-existing conditions.

headline: PA lawmakers mull prescription drug monitoring.
abstract: PA lawmakers might set up a new monitoring system for prescription drugs. The PA Accountability Monitoring System database would flag patients or customers who have received an adequate supply of Schedule 11 drugs containing opiates or synthetic opiates. This is in reaction to the rise in prescription druge overdose deaths and also to prevent prescription drug addicts to obtain drugs from PA.

headline: Crime watches learn about meth menace
abstract: State Police explained the criminal meth business to crime watch volunteers from the Luzerne County, Wyoming, Bradford and Sullivan counties. The troop explained various signs and practices of meth labs, and telltale signs of when to contact police.

headline: Administration defends one-time funding for schools
abstract: Gov. Corbett's proposal, "Passport to Learning", puts $1 billion raised through the selling off of state liqour stores and liqour licenses toward a one-time grant for schools. It is being criticised by democratic opponents. Dem. State Rep. Madeleine Dean of Montgomery County says the two issues shouldn't be tied and one-time funding makes schools rely on money that will quickly go away. Education Sec. Ron Tomalis disagrees, and said that he can think of no better place to put the assets.

headline: Studies: Epidemic of prescription-painkiller ODs
abstract: Recent Philadelphia statistics showed a steady increase in prescription-drug deaths, but an even more dramatic jump in heroin-related deaths. Moreover, a national report showed Pennsylvania had particularly high death rates and low scores for actions taken to prevent them.

headline: Rep. Brian Sims is the first openly gay lawmaker elected to the Pennsylvania legislature 1/2/13
abstract: Philadelphia lawyer, Brian Sims became the first openly gay lawmaker to be elected to the Pennsylvania legislature. The civil rights activist is looking to focus on civil rights issues such as discrimination in the workplace, hate crimes and bullying. In addition, Representative Sims has said that he wants to address gun violence in light of the shootings in Newton Connecticut.

headline: County may borrow to cover $15M shortfall
abstract: Luzerne County, PA is facing a shortfall of more than $15 million to close out the year and may have to borrow to make payments and payroll. The county had to borrow a couple million dollars to make ends meet for last year’s budget, and this year may have to sell the rights to delinquent taxes to outside agencies.

headline: Farmers not hoping for surge in milk subsidies 1/2/13
abstract: It appeared that lawmakers in Washington were on their way to approving an extension of an expired 2008 farm bill, that would prevent the 1940s milk-subsidy rules from taking effect. If the outdated rules would take effect, milk prices can increase to around $8 a gallon according to Alfred Wanner Jr., a dairy farmer in Narvon in Lancaster County.

headline: Poll: Voters would choose any Dem over Corbett
abstract: The poll from Mercyhurst University in Erie found that 40 percent would support an unnamed Democrat in next year’s gubernatorial race, while 29 percent would vote for PA Governor Tom Corbett. The results were not a surprise because other polls have shown that voters “largely disapprove” of Corbett’s performance as a governor.

headline: Editorial: Change still sorely needed at Penn State 1/2/13
abstract: In light of the Jerry Sandusky fallout, the author makes the argument Penn State needs to see greater change within  the board of trustees as well as the rest of the University. Furthermore, the author argues that any changes that have been made were merely marginal, and that perhaps, PA should cut state funding to force some change.

headline: State: More than 20 Allegheny County public schools below standard
abstract: Pennsylvania released performance ratings that covered at least 160 Allegheny County schools with large low-income student populations receiving federal funding. Allegheny County has 19 high-performing and 22 underperforming public schools.

headline: Congressman Charlie Dent broke Republican ranks over ‘clean’ bill, but won’t over discharge petition
abstract: PA Congressman Charlie Dent, Lou Barletta and Mike Fitzpatrick indicated a willingness to vote for a “clean” spending bill to reopen the federal government, a position that put them at odds with House GOP leaders, who want conditions attached. Dent was among the very first House Republicans to break ranks with GOP leaders over a clean bill; however Congressman Dent has emphatically said he will not sign a discharge petition, which would force a vote on a clean spending bill.

headline: Pat Toomey's cliff vote upsets backers
abstract: PA Senator Pat Toomey's decision to vote for the last-minute fiscal cliff deal has upset the tea party, the conservative party and the anti-tax Club for Growth--all of whom supported his candidacy for the U.S. Senate.

headline: Lack of firearms ordinance in Washington Township, PA., tough for residents, police to handle
abstract: Washington Township, Pa., residents have been dealing with stray bullets. Other residents are defending the practice, saying they take the necessary precautions to keep their neighbors safe. Northampton County District Attorney John Morganelli and the township report that nothing could be done in the case of stray bullets because there are no firearms ordinances in the township.

headline: Organizations with games of chance get extra year to meet reporting rules
abstract: The Department of Revenue have announced that Clubs that run small games of chance will be given another year to file financial reports, while some lawmakers are going to use the time to repeal the law they approved last year, as it will require extensive bookkeeping and new financial reporting requirements. Many of these clubs see the possible appeal as a threat by lawmakers to perhaps eliminate their existence.

headline: Forum addresses Affordable Care Act
abstract: The director of medical resources for Excela Health Systems answered questions given at a town hall forum on the Affordable Care Act in Westmoreland County Community College. Residents discussed issues concerning pre-existing health conditions and reviewed instructions of how to register for the Obama Administration program.

headline: Family owned businesses could see ‘death tax’ exemption
abstract: PA Representative, Steve Bloom, will introduce legislation that will eliminate the inheritance tax on real estate, for children, siblings or other relatives of a decedent. Bloom is one of many PA lawmakers that believe the state's inheritance tax is fundamentally unfair.

headline: Coatesville schools’ legal bill soar, records show
abstract: Right-to-Know request were filed in search of information related to The Coatesville Area School District’s high legal costs. Currently the district is conducting a legal review of the requests to determine whether the contract terms of the district’s solicitor and the district’s financial reports are public record. The legal fees paid to Rhoads & Sinon have come under scrutiny as the district addresses the scandal surrounding racist and sexist text messages exchanged between former Superintendent Richard Como and former Director of Athletics and Activities Jim Donato.

headline: John Baer: How's your paycheck, right about now?
abstract: John Baer discusses how the fallout between Congress and the White House during the "fiscal cliff" controversy has effected people's paycheck, as taxes have increased exponentially in 2013.

headline: Power plant employees rally; last day of work Oct. 18
abstract: FirstEnergy announced it would deactivate Hatfield’s Ferry plant in Greene County and the Mitchell Power Plant in Washington County. The move will eliminate the jobs of 380 plant workers.

headline: Generational roll of dice
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett is making a plan to privatize management of the state lottery. His decision has a lot to do with whether a private manager can do anything for the lottery that legislative power cannot. However, Corbett's move to privatize the state lottery shows signs of a vast expansion of gambling.

headline: Kavulich eyes one school health benefit plan
abstract: PA Rep. Sid Michaels Kavulich is pushing for a statewide health benefits plan for hundreds of thousands of public school employees. The plan would consolidate the hundreds of health coverage plans run by school districts to bring cost savings to help school taxpayers and remove an often-contentious issue from the table in teacher contract negotiations.

headline: Eachus collects sizeable legislative pension
abstract: Todd Eachus, a former Luzerne County lawmaker started collecting a $2,864 monthly pension last fall nearly two years after he left office. Some believe that allowing lawmakers to retire at 50 with full pension benefits after only working 13 years is not fiscally fair.

headline: Democrats to area GOP lawmakers: Prove your words
abstract: Six Republican congressmen, PA House Representatives Charlie Dent, Mike Fitzpatrick, Jim Gerlach, and Patrick Meehan, and NJ House Representatives Frank LoBiondo and Jon Runyan have proclaimed their willingness to break from their GOP colleagues and support a bill to reopen the federal government with no hard-line conditions attached. Democratic leaders have pressured Republicans who support a clean spending bill to not just voice their support but to also back procedural machinations to override GOP leaders and force a vote on the plan.

headline: Union expected to offer proposal to run Pennsylvania lottery
abstract: The AFSCME Council, a labor group representing a majority of the PA lottery's employees is expected to release a plan to counter a proposal from an outside firm seeking to oversee PA scratch tickets and jackpot games. The plan is scheduled to be given to PA Governor Tom Corbett's administration.

headline: Developers plan $30 million makeover along Second Avenue in Hazelwood
abstract: The City Urban Redevelopment Authority approved the proposal offered by ACTION-Housing Inc. and Washington, D.C. – based Telesis Corp. to redevelop a stretch of Second Avenue in Hazelwood with commercial and residential properties. The total cost of the proposed redevelopment is estimated at $30 million.

headline: AG-elect Kane picks top aides, looks to swearing-in
abstract: Newly elected Attorney General Kathleen Kane is looking to start her investigation on PA Governor Tom Corbett's reaction to the Jerry Sandusky child abuse scandal. Kane has recently selected Adrian King, a top staffer to former PA Governor Ed Rendell, as her chief of staff to assist her with the Corbett investigation and beyond.

headline: Corbett compares same-sex unions to sibling marriage
abstract: During an interview with Harrisburg’s WHP-TV, the PA Republican Governor, Tom Corbett was asked about a controversial statement his lawyers had made over the summer in a legal filing on gay marriage. The attorneys noted that gay marriage is against state law, just as marriage between children is. Gov’t Corbett believed a better analogy would have been “brother and sister”. In response to backlash from this statement, Gov’t Corbett apologized and explained his statement was from a legal perspective.

headline: Corbett targets pension reform in coming budget
abstract: As a result of an hour long briefing by PA Treasury Secretary Charles Zogby, Corbett has been warned that there is a growing pension crisis in PA. Zogby warned Corbett that the economic recession has made the pension issue worse and difficult to reform. Instead of focusing on property tax reform this year, PA Governor Tom Corbett has told reporters that pension reform will be a priority in the coming year's budget.

headline: Pa. ranked 14th in number of drug overdose deaths
abstract: The Washington-based Trust for America’s Health released a national study ranking Pennsylvania 14th in the rate of drug overdose deaths. The study also gave the state a low score on implementing strategies to curb prescription drug abuse. PA Governor Tom Corbett’s administration is taking steps that might improve its future ranking and score, as the state examines legislation to expand the state’s prescription monitoring program.

headline: Proposed Pleasant Valley School District budget calls for tax hike of 6 percent
abstract: Pleasant Valley School District is proposing a rise in its millage rates from 146 mills to 154 mills. If the budget is passed people who live in the school district will have their taxes raised to about 6 percent.

headline: Fitzgerald set to present Allegheny County budget: His first after reassessment, plan to drill
abstract: PA county Executive Rich Fitzgerald will unveil his changes to an operating budget that already totals $799 million, his first after a contentious reassessment turned property values upside down and a plan to drill beneath public land opened the possibility of new revenue. The final say will be up to county council members, who have the final say on financial matters.

headline: Pa. lawmakers discuss property tax elimination in Berks
abstract: Members of the Daniel Boone Taxpayer Activists told PA Senator Judith L. Schwank, PA Representative David M. Maloney Sr. and PA Representative Mark Gillen that the state government must do something to prevent taxpayers from loosing their homes due to property taxation. The three legislators have said that they will continue to push for property tax reform.

headline: Philadelphia weighs private law firm for some poor
abstract: The Nutter administration is poised to pay $9.5 million to hire a private law firm to represent the poor in cases where the public defender has a conflict. Opponents of the administration’s plan raise a host of objections, most centered on the fear that a private law firm would put profits before clients.

headline: Action News - Officials hope new supermarket will serve as kickstart for Philadelphia community
abstract: Officials in Philadelphia hope that a new full service grocery store will kickstart development in the neighborhood. So called "food deserts" are responsible for poorer health outcomes in neighborhoods unserved by supermarkets.

headline: Exercise caution before workout
abstract: PA Attorney General Linda Kelly is warning consumers interested in joining a gym about the dangers of making a commitment to public gyms. Kelly is preaching caution in evaluating contracts before making any long term commitments.

headline: Alternate route: Should buses be pulled from Downtown streets?
abstract: The Port Authority, as well as the Allegheny County Executive Rich Fitzgerald and Pittsburgh mayor-apparent Bill Preduto, have hired consulting firm Parsons Brinkerhoff Inc. to draw up a plan to relocate routes and bus stops in Downtown Pittsburgh. The attempts to reconfigure the Downtown services must address difficult rerouting issues, heavy commuter congestion and accommodating riders with disabilities.

headline: WJAC NEWS AT 11PM - Bill would force many landlords to install carbon monoxide detectors
abstract: A bill is before the legislature that would force landlords to install carbon monoxide detectors in all of their tenants' units.

headline: Talks with at least one private lottery management firm predated procurement process
abstract: Although PA Governor Tom Corbett has set a date to start the procurement process for Camelot Global Services PA, LLC, to manage the Pennsylvania Lottery, Revenue Secretary Dan Meuser met with a potential bidder for the contract. Mesuer said that he's personally met with only met one bidder, but other's in the administration have met with others.

headline: Pa. House bill would give schools tax option
abstract: PA House of Representatives approved a bill that would let school districts replace property taxes with “elimination taxes,” including additional earned-income taxes and business privilege taxes. Critics say the measure fails to address the more pressing problem of inadequate state funding for public schools.

headline: Eyewitness News at 11 - PA names Teacher of the Year
abstract: null

headline: Free $4 mil for 'expenses'
abstract: According to the Associated Press, state lawmakers were paid daily reimbursements for expenses of more than 3.9 million over the last two year legislation session. Some believe that most lawmakers claim the highest possible amount regardless of whether they spent it, and there's no way to prove otherwise, as they are not required to submit receipts.

headline: Pa. House bills aimed at protecting consumer health care access, lawmakers say
abstract: PA legislation to require hospitals to accept all insurance companies is aimed directly at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and Highmark Inc. dispute. Critics of the bill say the bill goes beyond the state’s legitimate role in the health care marketplace. The legislation would force a specific hospital and specific health plan to contract with each other.

headline: WTAJ NEWS AT 6 - Senate Democrats say they have a plan to generate more than $1 billion in budget savings and revenues
abstract: Democrats in the Senate are looking at new ideas to get needed money for the state's ailing institutions.

headline: Lottery privatization hearing helped fill in a few blanks for employees and senators
abstract: An official in PA Governor Corbett's administration has ensured that the  Employees of the PA lottery will not be unemployed if the lottery becomes private. He also said that the administration will provide them another place of employment within the commonwealth if an employee didn't want to work for the private manager.

headline: Court denies Jerry Sandusky’s request for a new trial
abstract: The Pennsylvania Superior Court has denied convicted child molester Jerry Sandusky’s request for a new trial. The decision two weeks after an attorney for the Penn State assistant football coach argued that mistakes by the judge and prosecutors led a Centre County jury to wrongfully convict Sandusky.

headline: ABC27 News at 7PM - Plan to privatize management of PA lottery blasted again, this time by auditor general
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett's plan to put the state's lottery system in private hands is now being blasted by the state's auditor general. The plan has cost taxpayers over $700,000 to date with little hope for results.

headline: Kathleen Kane faces "unique" challenge as attorney general
abstract: As attorney general, Kathleen Kane will have to withhold her promise of examining Tom Corbett administration’s handling of the Jerry Sandusky child sex abuse scandal while simultaneously pursuing the prosecution of three former Penn States administrators: Graham Spanier, Gary Schultz and Tim Curley. Some believe that Kane will have plenty on her plate when she begins her work as attorney general.

headline: Government gridlock worries civilian workers at Moon’s 911th Airlift Wing
abstract: The government shutdown has civilian employees of the Air Force Reserve’s 911th Airlift Wing in Moon, PA considering the possibilities of a closure. The Air Force said that the base would continue to operate as least through September 2014. That was a change from a February 2012 announcement that the base would close as part of a national plan to cut spending and reduce its fleet of cargo planes.

headline: Late Night News - Lawmaker pushes bill that would allow people with disabilities to set up their own trust funds
abstract: null

headline: Turnpike tolls are up, but where does the money go?
abstract: This year, tolls on the PA turnpike went up, which made the author wonder where the toll money goes. Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, paying down debt, turnpike maintenance and the PA state police and safety are among the many things that the toll revenue pays for.

headline: LCB to close state store near Monroeville Mall
abstract: The PA state Liquor Control Board voted to close the state Wine and Spirits store near Monroeville Mall. The decision comes after the LCB opened a larger, “rebranded” Premium Collection store about a half-mile away.

headline: CBS21 News at 5PM - Initiative launched to get rid of unused drugs
abstract: Unused drugs that remain in households long after their usefulness pose a danger to children and those susceptible to addition. The county hopes to encourage people to properly dispose of these unneeded drugs.

headline: Pocono politicos run for cover on gun issue
abstract: After the recent shootings in Connecticut and Colorado, Pocono politicians have been contacted by the Pocono Record regarding the issue. Although several politicians were in favor of the changes of the gun laws, many of them failed to provide specifics and three didn't even respond. When PA legislators were contacted, the Pocono Record received more substantive opinions on many aspects of the issue such as background checks, the interpretation of the second amendment, mental illness, among other issues.

headline: Arbitrator sides with union in Pittsburgh police pay dispute with city
abstract: An arbitrator ruled that on-duty Pittsburgh police officers who are sent to work at special events must be paid at the same higher rate as off-duty officers hired by the venues. Grievances stating that officers felt the city violated the collective bargaining agreement when on-duty officers were working alongside off-duty counterparts, who are paid at a time-and-a-half rate billed to the companies hosting the events.

headline: ABC27 News at 7PM - Pileggi doesn’t see extraction tax happening in the current legislative climate
abstract: PA Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pilleggi says that he doesn't believe there is a chance for a tax on gas drillers in this current session.

headline: Birth certificate computer glitch puts wrong name for father on document
abstract: About 500 PA families were victims of a birth records error; a computer glitch that put the wrong name of the father on the child's birth certificate. The division of Vital Records at the state Department of Health were responsible for sending these false certificate despite their recent switch to a new computer system.

headline: Speaker warns about concussions in youth sports
abstract: Chirstopher Nowinski, former WWE wrestler and Ivy League football player, is one of the leading activists in the growing movement to address concussion in youth and professional sports. He came to Wyomissing to speak with parents, coaches, trainers and others about the ways to reduce concussions and treat the athletes who suffer them on the field.

headline: WJAC-TV News at 11pm - PA gets federal funding for early education efforts
abstract: null

headline: Lawmakers lean in at hearing on Lottery deal with Camelot
abstract: PA Lawmakers spent the Senate Finance Committee hearing pressing the Corbett administration and Camelot executives regarding their decision to put the PA Lottery under private management. One of the highlights of the debate is when Republican PA Senator Pat Vance asked Corbett if the contract between his administration and Camelot is going to be public--The question wasn't answered by anyone in the Corbett administration.

headline: Easton planners give thumbs up to Lafayette’s film, media school
abstract: A timeline is now in place for Lafayette College’s proposed film and media school, providing Easton’s Zoning Hearing Board signs off on the project. Lafayette’s plan calls for the creation of a theater on the intersection of Third and Snyder streets.

headline: NBC 10 @ Issue - By what standard should voters judge Corbett in 2014?
abstract: Panel discussion about PA Gov. Tom Corbett's reelection chances.

headline: And the winner is... announced before a legislative hearing
abstract: Under much scrutiny by PA legislators, PA Governor Tom Corbett has announced that the PA Lottery will be under private ownership by Camelot Global Services. Corbett says that pursuing a private management deal will increase the profits of the lottery, which benefits five programs that help senior citizens.

headline: Notary law changes focus on regulations, Latino needs
abstract: A new PA state law prohibits notaries from engaging in false or deceptive advertising, providing legal advice and purporting to act as a “notario pulico”, in order to protect Latino immigrants from confusion and fraud. The legislation, signed by PA Governor Tom Corbett also enhances many other aspects of the notary system in PA.

headline: News 8 at 11PM - Camelot lottery deal off, but governor may still push for privatization
abstract: Although PA Gov. Tom Corbett's plan to privatize the state lottery seems to have failed with the expiration of a UK firm's bid, his office says the Governor may still push for the controversial plan.

headline: Corbett, half-way through first term, talks 1-on-1
abstract: Halfway through his first term PA Governor Tom Corbett is looking to accomplish a lot in the last half: he wants to sue the NCAA over its tough sanctions of the Penn State football program, privatize the PA lottery and work on a transportation bill that will restore roads and bridges.

headline: Officials are happy with flood gate fixes
abstract: Federal officials are satisfied with repairs and modifications to portable Market Street Bridge flood gates that leaked during record flooding in 2001. The federal government has invested more than $2 million repairing 2011 flood damage to the 15-mile Wyoming Valley Levee and its supporting components, which protect tens of thousands of county residents.

headline: Is the DEP too sneaky?
abstract: PA State Senator Scott Hutchinson is the prime sponsor of two bills that seeks to prohibit the PA Department of Environmental Protection from using video surveillance to enforce environmental laws in addition to driving marked cars at oil and gas sites.

headline: Cabela's boycotting Eastern Sports and Outdoor Show over gun flap
abstract: The Eastern Sports and Outdoor Show in Harrisburg will be boycotted by Cabela's and high profile celebrity hunting couples, Lee and Tiffany Lakoski, and Ralph and Vicki Cianciarulo due to Reed Exhibitions decision to avoid the display or sale of assault or assault style weapons at the fair given the recent gun control controversy.

headline: PEL: Scranton faces $20 million deficit next year; needs to raise taxes
abstract: The Scranton city government faces a possible deficit of nearly $20 million for 2014. The Pennsylvania Economy League urged the city to craft a realistic and responsible budget for next year that closes the structural deficit and lists as options unspecified hikes in both the real-estate (property) and earned-income (wage) taxes, and an increase in the city’s annual garbage fee.

headline: Rifle deer season opens, schools and office close
abstract: As per PA tradition, the beginning of rifle deer season means that several schools, business and even the PA General Assembly close down.

headline: No free lunch, or free roads, either

abstract: A bill designed to close the Delaware loophole, a corporate tax loophole in PA, is set to be voted on in the House.

headline: Bucks family 'blindsided' by estate tax
abstract: After Nancy Patricea's brother passed away a year ago, Nancy was forced to give a bulk of the money she inherited from him to the PA Department of Revenue. PA State Rep. Frank Frarry, is co-sponsoring a bill that would reduce rates by 50 percent.

headline: "The Corbett economic miracle"
abstract: Will Bunch of the Philadelphia Daily news gives his opinion on why he believes PA Governor Tom Corbett's campaign promise of "jobs, jobs, jobs" was unfulfilled.

headline: When is a cut not a cut? The tormented logic of county social service block grants
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett called on the legislature to aprove a new block grant program that will cut up to 10 percent of social service pending. This article examines the logic behind the cut.

headline: Enthusiasts cheer Pa. bill to make federal gun ban unenforceable
abstract: Gun Advocates in PA will lobby for a House bill written by PA Representative Daryl Metcalfe that will make any federal law to ban guns unenforceable in PA.

headline: GOP 'welcomes' carpetbagging Dem to Pa.'s 8th District
abstract: Kevin Strouse, a Delaware Country native who served in Iraq and Afghanistan was recruited by the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee to run for PA's 8th district in Bucks County. The National Republican Congressional Committee gave him a barbed gift to welcome him to Bucks county.

headline: Lawmakers urge against drilling in state forest
abstract: PA Representative Greg Vitali among other PA Lawmakers are urging PA Governor Tom Corbett to stop drilling in Loyalsock State Forest. The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources believe that this issue is not as "black and white" as some environmental advocates would suggest.

headline: Different reactions in Pa. to federal government's Plan B pill decision
abstract: This article examines the many opinions from women's health professionals and PA policy makers of the Federal government's decision to allow girls of any age to buy emergency contraception.

headline: Despite warnings, state lawmakers continue to hold checkbooks
abstract: Against the wishes of auditors, the PA General Assembly has continued to  hold several checkbooks that are still being used by House leaders and committee chairmen.

headline: For Corbett, it's nearly last call on liquor privatization
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett knows that time is running out. He wants to convince state lawmakers to send him a liquor privatization bill before June 30th.

headline: Toomey's leadership needed to prevent gun violence
abstract: In the midst of a polarizing gun debate, U.S. Senator Pat Toomey joined U.S. Senator Joe Manchin in sponsoring a bipartisan amendment that will expand background checks to people who purchase guns.

headline: Council OKs 1.34 percent property-tax rate, $2 tax on cigarettes
abstract: City Council approved a 1.34 percent property tax rate in addition to a homestead exception that would eliminate $30,000 from a homeowner's assessment.

headline: Open-records rulings by Commonwealth Court panel covers phones, home addresses.
abstract: The Commonwealth Court panel ruled that PA officials'' home addresses and middle names are public information under the state's Right-to-Know Law; However, Government-issued employee telephone and cellphone numbers are still private.

headline: State policy secrecy rankles lawmaker
abstract: When PA Representative Tim Mahoney asked about how many troopers are assigned to the Uniontown barracks, he found out that the PA State Police can tell you how many trooper it has statewide, but not how many are stationed locally.

headline: Pennsylvania takes step toward legalizing online gambling
