abstract: PA Representative Tina Davis introduced House Bill 1235, which will allow for casino companies to offer online games like poker, blackjack, slot machines, and any other game approves by the PA Gaming control bill. If passed, the bill will take a step forward in legalizing online gambling in PA.

headline: Experience counts: Corbett chooses well in filling Orie Melvin vacancy
abstract: The author of this article approves of PA Governor Corbett's nomination of Judge Correale F. Stevens for the state supreme court. Judge Stevens will be filling Orie Melvin's vacancy.

headline: Pittsburgh mayoral candidates talk jobs, violence at WQED forum
abstract: Pittsburgh mayoral candidates PA Representative Jake Wheatley, Former PA Auditor General Jack Wagner, and City Councilman Bill Peduto discuss employment, gun control, public housing and education at a public forum.

headline: Redefinition of marriage sought by some
abstract: This article examines the local effect that the end of the Defense of Marriage Act will have on residents of Altoona.

headline: State law leads to workers' comp drops for NEPA firefighters
abstract: The Firefighters Cancer Presumption Act  links every form of cancer found in a firefighter to a work-related illness. Expecting an overwhelming amount of claims, many insurers are pulling out, causing workers' compensation to drop for Northeastern PA firefighters.

headline: Pennsylvania among few states to struggle with budget deficit
abstract: Citing changes in federal tax law and lower than anticipated revenues, PA remains one of eleven states to be facing a deficit. PA Gov. Tom Corbett remains hesitant to put a tax increase on the table and is demanding that the Legislature deal with pension and liquor reform before he considers new taxes. Corbett says that the State is still busy cleaning up predecessor Ed Rendell’s budget mess. Democrats, however, argue that it is failed leadership and dangerous cuts that have put PA in this position.

headline: Cedarbrook nursing home struggling to attract residents
abstract: Two nursing homes in Lehigh and Northampton counties are experiencing trouble to keep their doors open as residents are moving to more luxurious, modern competitors. While not mandated, the counties took on the responsibility of running these nursing homes. Now, as county expenditures have increased by more than 1000%, questions over the future of these homes are at the forefront of debate.

headline: HACC funding flexibility bill makes its way to Corbett’s desk for enactment
abstract: A bill that will allow Harrisburg Area Community College more flexibility in designing its budget has made its way by unanimous vote to PA Gov. Tom Corbett’s desk. The Governor said he will review the bill, but is generally supportive of allowing schools more flexibility to meet budgetary needs.

headline: With Sandusky report, Kane takes politics off the table, but leaves Corbett an even bigger headache: John L. Micek
abstract: A report came out that concludes that PA Gov. Tom Corbett did not slow the investigation of the Sandusky Case for political gain, but may have mishandled the investigation early on which resulted in the investigation being slower than it otherwise would have been. The Governor continues to say that as Attorney General his office handled the case appropriately and timely. Attorney General Kathleen Kane said it is up to the public to decide which leadership in the case was best.

headline: Penn State alumni resentment hangs over Corbett
abstract: People in and around Penn State continue to have a strongly negative feeling toward PA Gov. Tom Corbett over how his office handled the Sandusky Investigation and the fallout. Corbett backed the firing of legendary football coach Joe Paterno, stripping 111 of his wins, and pulling scholarship funds. In the May primary, 14% of Centre County (home of Penn State University) voters voted for another candidate for Governor.

headline: Officials oppose EPA proposal
abstract: U.S. Senator Pat Toomey and U.S. Rep. Bill Shuster, both from PA, came out against new regulations set by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) designed to aid in cleaning up the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The Officials aided in filing a lawsuit, claiming that the EPA has ignored the Clean Waters Act, which gives States predominant control over waterways. Senator Toomey argued that farmers and local governments have done good work reducing pollution in the watershed and that the EPA’s power grab was ridiculous.

headline: DN Editorial: Pennsyltuckered out
abstract: Lawmakers are working to fill a $1.5 billion budget shortfall that arose from budget projections falling short of what was anticipated. This short fall comes after a federal economic report found that PA had one of the slowest growing economies in the country. The State continues to not tax natural gas extraction and refuse to accept the Medicaid expansion offered by the Affordable Care Act. Both the tax and expansion are said to be able to generate a great deal of wealth for the State.

headline: AG Kane corrects statement on Sandusky
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane said she was wrong when saying that two young men accused Jerry Sandusky of assault after the investigation began. One of the young men was named as Victim 9 in the 2012 trial and testified against Sandusky. The other had come forward in 2012 and Sandusky had not been charged in relation to him.

headline: Corbett says he "never will" condemn Joe Paterno
abstract: Reports of PA Gov. Tom Corbett’s role in the firing of Penn State football coach Joe Parterno are conflicting. Corbett claims he did not take part in the vote to fire Paterno, however others say that he had no objections. The Governor went on to claim he had never nor will ever condemn the late Paterno and regrets that he was fired over the phone instead of in person. The Governor does not believe that this scandal will harm his reelection campaign.

headline: Fumo drumming up business?
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vince Fumo is currently working with a federal judge to receive permission to launch a lobbying firm. Fumo asked for permission to speak to friends and colleagues on advice for setting up his firm. He has spent the previous four years in prison for corruption and is still currently on probation. Fumo also took tours of several groups in Philadelphia, being warmly received by the attendees.

headline: Pension bill tied to aid for Philadelphia schools
abstract: PA House Republicans have offered a deal to Phila. Democrats to support their pension bill in exchange for allowing the City to impose a $2 tax on cigarettes. The tax is to be used to support Philadelphia’s $80 million obligation to its schools, otherwise it will be unable to open on time. PA Gov. Tom Corbett said he will not sign any budget until proper pension reform is included. PA Democrats were angry at the deal, accusing House Republicans of using Phila. Schools as a bargaining chip.

headline: Republican lawmakers push ‘paycheck protection’ in Pennsylvania
abstract: Two bills are circulating through the PA General Assembly designed to prevent public sector unions from automatically deducting campaign contributions from employee’s paychecks. The bill’s come on the eve of a decision from the U.S. Supreme Court that could fundamentally alter how campaign contributions with unions function. Opponents of the bills argued it was an attack in order to make unions, and thus the Democratic Party, weaker.

headline: No plans for opening a thrift shop in the Capitol basement, but GOP budget is balanced on some unusual revenue sources.
abstract: The 2014-2015 budget is balanced, but it relies on revenue sources that many would say are “not preferable” at best. The new GOP budget will be voted on and sent to the Governor for final enactment. The budget relies on transferring money from different loan funds and accounts as well as increased revenue from new leases for drilling and casinos. Democrats raised concerns that the new revenue sources are not sustainable and do not fix the State’s financial problems.

headline: Schwartz airs first ad, touts role in CHIP
abstract: In her first TV ad in the Democratic primary for governor, U.S. Rep. Allyson Schwartz highlighted her work in the state senate helping enact the landmark children's health insurance program, CHIP. Opponents accuse Schwartz of false credit claiming for the accomplishments of PA Rep. Allen Kukovich and PA Gov. Robert P. Casey Sr. However, a statement by Kukovich in March stressed the importance Schwartz ultimately held in the creation of the program.

headline: Medicaid expansion: advocates fault Corbett for delaying health care for 500,000
abstract: A crowd of people and advocates from around the state assembled in Harrisburg, PA, to call attention to Gov. Tom Corbett's refusal to carry out the expansion called for in Obamacare, or the Affordable Care Act. Corbett's decision to pursue his proposal, called "Healthy PA," cost PA $500 million in federal funds in 2014 that could provide health care for 500,000 people in the state.

headline: Toomey plans push on teacher sex bill
abstract: U.S. Senator Pat Toomey is pushing for the passage of a bill that will force schools to more thoroughly check the backgrounds of school employees that may come in contact with students.

headline: Logic runs through it: An EPA rule will clarify its authority on water
abstract: On March 25, 2014 the Environmental Protection Agency issued a proposal that states under the Clean Water Act along with all "navigable water ways", the most seasonal and rain-dependent streams are protected, as are wetlands near rivers and streams. Other types of waters that may have more uncertainty will be evaluated in a case-by-case analysis. This rule is being opposed by more than a dozen GOP senators, led by Pennsylvania's Pat Toomey, with support from some farmers, who denounce the EPA's action as a "terrifying power grab".

headline: Full refunds demanded in Marcellus natural gas royalty dispute
abstract: Scout Petroleum, which has interests in Marcellus Shale natural gas leases wants the American Arbitration Association to order a full refund for what it alleges have been improper deductions from royalty payments by Chesapeake Appalachia. Scout Petroleum has asked the Association to declare its demand a class action to include all those who have entered into what are known as paid-up oil and gas leases. Concurrently, the PA state Senate approved three bill introduced by PA Sen. Gene Yaw aimed at expanding the rights of landowners with natural gas leases. The bills now move to the House.

headline: Bill pays for lawyers to help PA poor
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee approved Sen. Stewart Greenleaf's bill, 8-6, to create the Pennsylvania Center for Effective Indigent Defense Legal Representation. The bill would give the center $1 million to train and educate public defenders, and make it an independent state agency that can become affiliated with a law school in PA.

headline: Steps to avoid letting universities exit state system
abstract: Frank T. Brogan, the chancellor of Pensylvania's higher education system promised more autonomy for its 14 universities, giving hope to PA Sen. Andrew Dinniman and PA Sen. Robert Tomlinson that their prposed legislation to break up the system would not be necessary.

headline: 'Kids for Ca$h' comes to the Capitol
abstract: U.S. Sen. Bob Casey expressed hope that the showing of a film in the nation's Capitol depicting the infamous "kids for cash" scandal of Luzerne County, PA, in 2008 will serve as a push to reform America's juvenile justice system.

headline: Tavern gaming glitch may have cooled expansion efforts
abstract: PA State lawmakers are hesitant of any more expansions of gambling to bridge the budget gaps. Attempts thus far at gaining revenue from gambling in bars and taverns have failed due to a miscalculation of the appetite of taverns to get into small games of chance.

headline: Fund-raising needs for possible papal visit laid out
abstract: Archbishop Charles J. Chaput, PA Gov. Tom Corbett, and Philadelphia Mayor Micheal Nutter gave a briefing  to about 170 business, civic, and cultural leaders about the fund-raising needs for the possible visit of Pope Francis to Philadelphia next year.

headline: Wolf proposes income tax overhaul
abstract: PA ranks amongst the top ten most regressive tax systems in the U.S. Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Tom Wolf, seeks to change that by making the tax more progressive. Wolf's plan is to issue an exemption on low income earners and have high income earners pay the increased rate. This plan differs from PA Sen. Argall, who suggests raising the sales and income tax in order to eliminate property taxes. Overall, Wolf's goal is to generate enough revenue to increase the State's share of school funding from 33% to 50%.

headline: Pa. revenue collections bring in $2.2 billion in July, but that includes one-timers used to balance budget
abstract: PA revenue for July 2014 increased by 16.8 percent over July 2013's collections. However, a sizable portion of the collections derived from one-time revenue sources relied upon to balance the state's budget. There was also a slight increase in sales tax, which can be an indicator of a stronger economy.

headline: School District asks high court to OK sale of Wm. Penn High
abstract: In order to help offset a large budget deficit, the Philadelphia School District has asked the State Supreme Court to swiftly reject a lawsuit preventing William Penn High School from being sold to Temple University. The School District said it did not possess necessary funds to upgrade and maintain the building, whereas Temple University intends to use it for athletic and job training purposes.

headline: Ebola outbreak highly unlikely in Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Physician General Dr. Carrie DeLone declared that the risk of an outbreak of Ebola in PA is extremely low. She sighted that with vigilance, a stronger public health and infectious disease net in the U.S., people should not be afraid of an Ebola outbreak. The fears come in response to Dr. Kent Brantly, a physician in Africa who contracted the disease and was brought to U.S. soil. Dr. Brantly is being treated in a facility in Atlanta.

headline: Meehan calls on VA to hold Phila. Officials accountable
abstract: U.S. Representative Pat Meehan of PA wrote a letter to newly appointed VA Secretary Robert McDonald demanding that the hold Phila. VA officials responsible for lying to Congress as well as failing to uphold standards of efficiency. He demanded that penalties be put in place for violations of Congressional oversight.

headline: DN Editorial: As the layoff clock ticks
abstract: The PA State House has dismissed for the summer before dealing with a bill that would allow Philadelphia to place a $2-a-box tax on cigarettes, which is projected to raise the necessary sum of money to close the Phila. School District’s budget deficit. PA Gov. Tom Corbett has attempted to bring lawmakers back, but failed. Now that the State House is in recess, the School District needs to consider the possibility of laying off 1,000 staff.

headline: Letterhead from office, but mapped by the campaign
abstract: In a campaign tour covering Republican strongholds, PA Gov. Tom Corbett argued that the PA pension debate was bipartisan, despite no progress being made with Democrats. He also cancelled a campaign stop to a Phila. public school over concerns relating to protests from budget cuts. It would have been his first visit to a Phila. public school.

headline: PlanCon backlog strains school budgets
abstract: The Planning and Construction Workbooks, or PlanCon, is a State program designed to help alleviate the costs of infrastructure upgrades in school districts. After 41 years of operation, the program now has hundreds of projects pending and a total of $1.7 billion owed to districts. The program’s backlog has made schools cut budgets even further as money promised is not coming in. Early in his term, PA Gov. Tom Corbett issued a moratorium on payments, further escalating the issue.

headline: Moul's DUI bill would increase penalties
abstract: PA State Rep. Dan Moul has introduced a bill designed to increase the penalties for people who on their second DUI offense kill someone. The new bill would revoke the driver's driving privileges for life and increase prison sentencing to five years for every individual killed in the accident. The bill was inspired by Angela Rigby, a woman killed by a DUI offender.

headline: Lawmakers contemplate tax breaks for small busniesses
abstract: PA Republican lawmakers, Rep. Seth Grove, Rep. George Dunbar and Rep. Stephen Bloom offered up a package of legislation that could make the process of filing taxes more pleasant for small business owners. Left-leaning critics oppose the package, stating "It's not tax simplification. These are tax cuts".

headline: Challenge to Corbett's GOP foe goes to PA Supreme Court
abstract: The PA Republican Party-backed effort to disqualify the lone primary challenger to Gov. Tom Corbett is now headed to the PA Supreme Court for appeal. This follows a lower court decision  which ruled that suburban Philadelphia businessman Bob Guzzardi could stay on the May 20th primary ballot.

headline: Obama hopes to replicate CCAC job training efforts across United States
abstract: President Obama and Vice President Joe Biden, inspired by the Community College of Allegheny County's model of job creation, announced a $600 million competitive grant program for job training and apprenticeship initiatives. To win a grant, community colleges and foundations would partner with private industry to establish training programs and apprenticeships that would make it easier to obtain a job after graduation.

headline: A new face for Philadelphia Republicans
abstract: J. Matthew Wolfe, a lawyer in University City, Philadelphia, is working to overthrow the leadership of the Philadelphia Republican Party in the hopes of building a viable alternative to Democratic dominance in the city. Wolfe is set to run for City Council in a special election for an at-large vacancy created by the resignation of Bill Green who left to chair the School Reform Commission.

headline: Governor promotes education positions
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett promoted his education proposals and the need to reinforce science and technology training during a visit he made to the Carnegie Science Center in Pittsburgh. Gov. Corbett used the setting as a backdrop for a call to encourage excellence in training in the STEM disciplines; science, technology, engineering and math. He also talked up his proposal to funnel a $341 million increase in the next fiscal year through block grants designed to give school districts more flexibility in spending the state funds.

headline: Cameras to nab speeders urged for Roosevelt Blvd.
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey testified before the State Senate Transportation Committee in an effort to support a bill to authorize speed-enforcement cameras that would generate $100 tickets for speeders on the notoriously dangerous Roosevelt Boulevard in Northeast Philadelphia. The bill is sponsored by PA Sen. Michael Stack (D., Phila.).

headline: Corbett ramps up pitch to education, women voters.
abstract: In his efforts to attract two of his weakest polling points, his job approval by women voters and his efforts on education, PA Gov. Tom Corbett and his wife, Susan, attended a gather with about 60 citizens in Media, PA. There his wife stressed his commitment to the state's education, in an effort to push back against criticisms he received from school groups and the four Democratic candidates running for governor.

headline: Pa. Senate passes fiscal code bill, putting budget ball back in Corbett's court
abstract: The PA Senate passed a fiscal code bill with a 26-22 vote, with most Republicans voting yes and all Democrats voting no. The author believes that the bill should bring PA Governor Tom Corbett closer to signing the $29.1 billion budget.

headline: PA Senate approves name change for Department of Public Welfare.
abstract: The PA Senate unanimously voted to change the name of the PA Department of Public Welfare to the Department of Human Services. Supporters of the bill believe that the name change gets rid of the stigma that the agency is associated with public assistance and welfare.

headline: Margolies campaign denies misusing funds
abstract: Marjorie Margolies' campaign vehemently denied allegations that she spent general-election funds on primary-election expenses in violation of federal law. The allegations were filed with the FEC by PA State Sen. Davlin Leach, who is running against Margolies for the Democratic nomination in the 13th Congressional District.

headline: Barletta: Boston bombings exposed failure of immigration policy
abstract: U.S. Representative Lou Barletta attributed the Boston Bombings to a failure of immigration policy in the U.S. He criticized the homeland security system in addition to the lack of communication between all agencies.

headline: Report lists Pa. with most unsound bridges in U.S.
abstract: According to the analysis by the American Road and Transportation Builders Association, more than 23 percent of Pennsylvania's bridges are rated structurally deficient under federal guidelines, ranking the highest in the country. Thanks to the $2.3 billion transportation funding bill passed by legislatures in November PennDot is set to repair about 700 PA bridges this year.

headline: L&I inspector's suicide adds more tragedy to Market Street saga
abstract: A Center City property collapsed onto a Salvation Army thrift shop on June 5, killing six people and injuring 13. Ronald Wagenhoffer was the city inspector who examined the property that collapsed and upon hearing the news of the deaths, the guilt associated with the tragedy compelled Wagenhoffer to kill himself.

headline: State Sen. Daylin Leach threatens Gov. Tom Corbett with sit-in protest over medical marijuana bill
abstract: PA State Sen. Daylin Leach is threatening Gov. Tom Corbett with a sit-in protest if he does not meet with him discuss a Senate Bill 1182. The bill would allow doctors to prescribe marijuana for a host of ailments. Twenty other states and the District of Columbia have legalized medical marijuana.

headline: Pass pot bill to alleviate suffering
abstract: Two PA state senators, Sen. Daylin Leach (D-Montgomery) and Sen. Mike Folmer (R-Lebanon), have introduced a bill that would authorize use of the oil to treat children suffering from the seizures. Gov. Tom Corbett and Republican leaders in both houses have said they will not support the bill because they believe that such policy should be set at the federal level.

headline: Capitol Hunger Garden's fifth growing season about to get underway
abstract: The Capitol Hunger Garden, a 1,000-square-foot garden located on the south side of the PA state Capitol produces about 800 pounds of vegetables that are harvested and donated to food banks and other local agencies. The chairmen of the Legislative Hunger Caucus along with representatives of organizations that feed the hungry gathered inside the Capitol Media Center to celebrate the garden's successes over the past four years.

headline: Corbett, briefly, on revenue shortfalls, open records, pensions and more
abstract: After an awards ceremony, recognizing state agencies for saving $650 million since PA Gov. Tom Corbett came into office, he answered a few questions. Gov. Corbett briefly touched on the growing revenue shortfalls, need for pension reform and opposed the need of a natural gas severance tax.

headline: State Sen. Hughes asks Human Relations Commission to investigate Fairview Twp. KKK activity
abstract: PA state Sen. Vincent Hughes requested that the PA Human Relations Commission investigate recent Ku Klux Klan activity in Fairview Township. The KKK announced a neighborhood watch in Fairview Township area as well as Camphill. U.S. Sen. Robert Casey Jr. called upon the Department of Justice to also send its Community Relations Service team to Camp Hill in response.

headline: Striking Wilkes-Barre General nurses told to give ‘silent treatment’ to those who crossed picket line
abstract: Wilkes-Barre General Hospital nurses are striking due to unfair labor practices. A state union leader told the striking nurses to give nurses who crossed the picket line silent treatment to show them that they are hurting the cause.

headline: No pressure from Big Tobacco on tax, say Senate Republicans
abstract: After pressure from big tobacco lobbyists, the PA House was unable to pass the $2-per-pack cigarette tax. Philadelphia Mayor, Michael Nutter accused cigarette companies of taking away money from Philadelphia school children.

headline: Protests against Lyft are adding up
abstract: The Philadelphia Parking Authority and five dozen taxi companies are amongst the numerous protests filed against Lyft and Uber, which are experimental ride sharing services operating illegally in PA. Lyft’s attorney in Harrisburg had filed numerous briefs detailing inconsistent rulings from the Pennsylvania Utilities Commission (PUC) relating to ride sharing services. The Phila. Parking Authority believes that Lyft’s statewide application undermines its ability to regulate services in Philadelphia.

headline: Tragedy dissected: a fatal fire holds lessons for the future
abstract: A fire that erupted at a Chevron gas well in Dunkard, PA has resulted in the injury of one and the death of another worker. The company claims the incident occurred due to human error. The PA Department of Environmental Protection investigated the matter and claimed that the company was deceptive to both the State and media, citing their actions as “unacceptable.” The company announced it remains committed to safe operations and will review recommendations from DEP.

headline: Drilling tax with a twist
abstract: Lawmakers in Harrisburg are discussing a Marcellus Shale extraction tax once more after previous efforts failed to materialize. Now, the debate is over where the money should be spent. PA State Sen. Tommy Tomlinson said the money should be used to pay down the pension debt, but PA State Sen. Jay Costa said the money should go into a special fund for education. As it stands, the State’s unfunded pension liability is at $50 billion.

headline: Power choices remain strong in Pa.; First Energy to leave competitive-market program
abstract: In winter of 2013, electric prices were so volatile that many PA residents saw a drastic increase in their energy rates. 	Despite the Public Utilities Commission issuing more licenses for competitive suppliers, companies are pulling out of the market due to instability in costs. FirstEnergy Corp. said that the market is too instable to offer plans at a fixed rate.

headline: Budget wrangling cuts $20M from Pennsylvania scholarship program touted by Corbett
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett touted his “Ready to Succeed” scholarship as providing grants to students that otherwise would not qualify for state assistance. Originally meant to be funded at $25 million, budget battles have reduced the funds to $5 million. This means that only several thousand, as opposed to tens of thousands, of students shall receive the grant. The program plays into an effort to alleviate college debt for PA’s 700,000 college students.

headline: Warren Kampf and Marion Moskowitz square off in District 157 race
abstract: Two term PA State Rep. Warren Kampf is being challenged by developer Marion Moskowitz, a Democrat who ran unopposed in the primary. Kampf is running on a campaign of supporting education and pension reform while maintaining the fiscal responsibility of the State. Moskowitz believes there needs to be a more moderate tone in Harrisburg and plans to place the severance tax on Marcellus Shale.

headline: Penn State trustees to discuss NCAA lawsuit status
abstract: The Penn State board of trustees will be having a private conference call, followed by a public one, to discuss how the University shall respond to several lawsuits brought about against it in the aftermath of the Jerry Sandusky child molestation case.

headline: Pa. Supreme Court won't consider oil and gas royalty minimums
abstract: The Pa. Supreme Court has declined to hear arguments over the interpretation of the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act. In an unanimous decision, the Court ruled that the agreement made by Thomas E. Protector Heirs Trust - that allowed 50% of royalties to return to the company - violated the requirements of the Act.

headline: Mike Schlossberg: Reflections on a personal journey with depression
abstract: State Rep. Mike Schlossberg of Allentown, PA spoke about his personal journey with depression. After the suicide of Robin Williams, Rep. Schlossberg stepped forward and called for less stigmatization of mental illness. Mental illness discriminates against no one and everyone is susceptible.

headline: Educational tour: Gubernatorial candidate outlines goals
abstract: Pa. Democratic Gubernatorial candidate Tom Wolf made several campaign stops where he outlined his goals for education funding in PA. Wolf plans to restore the $1 billion in funding from President Obama's stimulus package. He is also intent on finding a fairer method of funding schools, including charter schools, that does not rely on local property taxes.

headline: KDKA TV News At 6: State prepares to protect residents in bitter cold weather
abstract: State and local authorities offer resources to help residents dealing with cold temperatures.

headline: Wolf tax proposal generates heat in governor's race
abstract: A recent attack ad by Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett prompted Democratic challenger Tom Wolf to fight back over tax policy. Under Wolf's new tax plan, many Pennsylvanians would see a tax increase, but the majority would see a cut as the tax is moved to a more progressive basis. Mr. Wolf has been vague on the exact details of the policy, which is typical of political challengers.

headline: 28 NEWS AT 6: Haggerty introduces resolution asking Congress to delay flood insurance premium increases
abstract: Flood insurance rates are skyrocketing in areas of the state. Residents are being forced to make hard choices. Local legislators are asking Congress to help lower rates.

headline: DN Editorial: Political FOT-ball
abstract: Former PA Secretary of Education, Ron Tomalis, was hired by the Corbett Administration to give advice on a plan to increase student performance, however the plan ceased when the budget was cut. Tomalis still received a salary equal to that of when he was Secretary of Education. The State could only produce very scant evidence of him actually performing work, which has resulted in mounting political heat that forced Tomalis to resign his post.

headline: FOX43 News at 10PM: Senate medical marijuana bill has support from both parties
abstract: A bill to allow for restricted use of marijuana for those with certain conditions has tentative support from both parties.

headline: Senate's shift might explain lack of major legislative achievements
abstract: Despite controlling the Governorship, House, and Senate, the PA GOP has had difficulty passing legislation supported by Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett. On the issues of liquor and pensions, the Senate is becoming more split between moderate and extremist voices, stalling the advancement of legislation. The body has historically been less partisan than the House, however it is starting to see a heightened class of personality.

headline: Late Night News: Rep. Bizzarro to referee wrestling match
abstract: Rep. Ryan Bizarro (Erie) is referring a charity wrestling matching the area.

headline: PA GOP consults the Hillary Clinton playbook
abstract: In an attempt to discredit Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett's challenger, an attack ad compared Tom Wolf to Barack Obama with the accusation that Mr. Wolf shares Obama's disdain for rural Pennsylvania. The ad calls on several jokes made by Mr. Wolf and President Obama over rural Pennsylvania and guns. The Wolf Campaign responded by saying they're unable to run on their record, so this is what the Corbett Campaign has left.

headline: NBC10 News at 6PM: State Rep. faces conspiracy and other charges in Philadelphia
abstract: Rep. J.P. Miranda (Philadelphia) has been charged with defrauding taxpayers through use of a "ghost worker."

headline: Defense lawyers rip prosecutors in Pa. turnpike corruption case
abstract: In an attempt to weaken the case before the forthcoming trial, lawyers for six defendants involved in corruption with turnpike contracts attacked state prosecutors. The lawyers claimed the case sought to criminalize the legal practice of dunning gov't contracts for campaign contributions. They claimed the state has failed to provide any evidence showing the contracts were linked to donations.

headline: 6PM NEWS: New poll released today says governor Tom Corbett faces a stiff challenge in his fight for re-election
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is faced with terrible poll numbers at this early stage making many analysts wonder whether he will be re-elected.

headline: Defense lawyers rip prosecutors in Pa. turnpike corruption case
abstract: In an attempt to weaken the case before the forthcoming trial, lawyers for six defendants involved in corruption with turnpike contracts attacked state prosecutors. The lawyers claimed the case sought to criminalize the legal practice of dunning gov’t contracts for campaign contributions. They claimed the state has failed to provide any evidence showing the contracts were linked to donations.

headline: New Pa. endangered species rules are a necessary change: As I See It
abstract: In this opinion article, the authors argue why the PA Game Commission and the PA Fish and Boar Commission should publicly provide the scientific reasons for proposing species for threatened and endangered status of animals.

headline: Pa. lottery outsourcing critics say Illinois' failed privatization could have played out here
abstract: After three years of budget shortfalls, Illinois is cancelling its contract with Northstar which had managed the state's lottery system. Lawmakers in PA used the failed privatization in Illinois as evidence that PA should drop similar ambitions. The administration did not comment on the privatization other than saying that there were added protections in PA's plan designed to prevent budget shortfalls.

headline: Erie Times News
abstract: Kelly, Thompson to run for re-election

headline: Pennsylvania women in politics crawl toward equality
abstract: PA ranks 38th in the nation for most women in politics, lower than any other Northeastern State. U.S. Rep. Allyson Schwartz's decision to not run for reelection means that the Congressional delegation will be entirely male. PA has also failed to elect any woman as a U.S. Senator or Governor. Still, PA has made some progress in getting women into office.

headline: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett's administration has asked the court to reconsider the ACT 13 decision, which declared the unconstitutionality of major portions of the Marcellus Shale gas drilling law. The administration believes that the court has made its own "sweeping" factual findings with the decision.

headline: Pennsylvania's crazy liquor laws? Sere's a six-pack sampler
abstract: Several Lawmakers are pushing through legislation that attempts to modernize the liquor industry in PA, which is entirely dominated by the State. One of the modernization attempts includes making online purchases easier, legalizing transportation of alcohol from outside PA into the State, and increasing hours of operation on Sundays.

headline: Utilities scramble to restore power in PA, Maryland.
abstract: About 440,000 customers in Pennsylvania, along with about 50,000 in Maryland are without power two days after an ice storm downed power lines and trees. Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Corbett announced a shipment of electrical generators from the federal government was on its way to Pennsylvania. As crews continue to place a priority on restoring electricity to hospitals, nursing homes, communications facilities and sewer plants.

headline: Amid questions raised by former aide's plea, Fattah mum
abstract: U.S. Rep. Chaka Fattah of Philadelphia’s former top aid has pled guilty to the mishandling of $1 million of campaign funds. The guilty plea has rejuvenated concerns over how much information on the scandal Rep. Fattah had. Allegedly, the campaign funds were used to pay down the Official’s son’s college debts. The investigation will likely lead to Fattah himself, but he has shown no signs of worry as he maintains his social media presence a full schedule of physical appearances in Philadelphia.

headline: Rep. Allyson Schwartz seen as liberal but ranks as a moderate
abstract: Since U.S. Rep. Allyson Schwartz announced her bid for statewide office, the question around the Montgomery County congresswoman’s candidacy for governor is whether she is too liberal to win over central and western Pennsylvanian voters. However, the latest rankings by The National Journal graded Schwartz nearly identical to the moderate Republican U.S. Congressman Charlie Dent. But whether it is better for her election chances to be labeled a liberal or a centrist remains to be seen.

headline: News outlets skeptical of tweak to open records law
abstract: Updates to PA's Right-to-Know law are up for consideration in the House after unanimous approval in the Senate. This marks the statute's first revision since it was rewritten in 2008.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: The Chips are down
abstract: The Pennsylvania state gambling board is looking at Philadelphia’s Center City for another casino location. Currently, PA claims more casinos than the seaside gambling mecca, Atlantic City. However last year, for the first time since the commonwealth’s casinos started opening in 2006, PA’s total gambling revenues fell compared with the year before. State gambling officials attribute the slump to new competition in neighboring states such as Maryland and Ohio.

headline: Delaware Valley Charter deals with tragedy
abstract: Students at Delaware Valley Charter High School in Philadelphia are still grieving the shooting of 15-year-old sophomore Aisha Abdur Rhaman. To help the healing process State Rep. Brendan Boyle helped contribute $2500 for the school's Youth Court program, to keep students from resorting to violence, that was dropped because of a lack of funding.

headline: PA Democrats splinter on governor endorsement
abstract: Democrats will go into the Pennsylvania gubernatorial primary campaign without a party-endorsed candidate. The party committee members came away with a splintered vote among five candidates at their winter meeting. State Treasurer Rob McCord won nearly half the votes cast and about twice as many as U.S. Congresswoman Allyson Schwartz. While York businessman Tom Wolf came in third, followed by two former state environmental protection secretaries, John Hanger and Katie McGinty.

headline: DA offers sharp reply to bid by Orie Melvin for reduced sentence
abstract: Incumbent PA Gov. Tom Corbett and challenger Democrat Tom Wolf knew their campaigns would have to raise a significant amount of cash to stay competitive. Both have raised nearly $47.5 million for the 2014 race thus far.

headline: Democrats in Hershey: not too sweet
abstract: The PA Democrat committee met in Hershey, PA to endorse a candidate against PA Gov. Tom Corbett. However, the party did not come away with a clear endorsement. Rather, the committee came away with a split decision, with no clear majority. State Treasurer Rob McCord came away with the most votes, followed by U.S. Rep. Allyson Schwartz, York County businessman Tom Wolf, and lastly environmental protection secretaries John Hanger and Katie McGinty.

headline: Pragmatism trump politics
abstract: As part of the Affordable Care Act, the U.S. Federal Government has agreed to cover the expenses of expanding medical services in the States. PA Gov. Tom Corbett has, as part of a universal Republican rejection of the ACA, opted out of the expansion. Push pack from several industries has caused the Governor to propose an alternative that allows federal funds to go to private insurance companies. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has approved this plan.

headline: Lawmakers seek details on proposed education spending
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett defends his proposal for a new $240 million block grant for public schools as a way to ensure money is being funneled into classrooms for academic improvement programs. The proposed additional funding, called Ready to Learn Block Grant, differs from another block grant already in the education budget, the $100 million Accountability Block Grant. However it appears that the poorest school districts are actually ending up with less money and the more prosperous school districts are ending up with more money. Gov. Corbett stated that his administration may look into the issue, but also proclaimed that the education funding formula needs to be fair.

headline: Report says Pa. job growth is stagnant
abstract: Keystone Research Center, a policy development organization, releases annual reports on the state of PA’s economy. They reported that in 2014, PA saw an increase in job growth and a decrease in unemployment, but when compared to other States, PA lags behind. The Center believes that much of the credit to the slightly increased economy goes to the Gov’t’s investments in infrastructure – specifically the transportation bill signed last year.

headline: State Rep. Patty Kim makes re-election bid official
abstract: State Rep. Patty Kim formally announced that she will seek another term representing the capital city of Pennsylvania. Kim stated she will continue to address income inequality and will focus on job creation and public education. Currently Rep. Kim does not face any known challengers, with the petition filing deadline a month away.

headline: PA's Medicaid enrollees could see benefit cuts
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett’s alternative plan to the Medicaid expansion was approved by the Federal Government, but many fear that it will reduce certain services to the working poor. Despite opting out of a traditional expansion, the Governor did compromise on several aspects and many analysts said that a lot of the plan is rhetoric as opposed to innovative policy.

headline: Corbett wants to keep charter schools from double dipping on pensions
abstract: In his 2014-15 budget proposal, PA Gov. Tom Corbett recommends eliminating the state’s 50 percent pension reimbursement to charter schools. The state would roll the $62.7 million it saves into its proposed Ready to Learn Block Grant, giving extra funding to Pennsylvania school districts. Corbett’s proposal would turn off pension reimbursements the state is paying to charter schools, but would still leave school districts on the hook for charter schools’ pension bills as well as their own. The Pennsylvania Association of School Business Officials has suggested a solution that allows school districts to deduct pension costs from their per-student paid to charters and leave the state’s 50 percent reimbursement to charters in place.

headline: Fattah case is different
abstract: After a former aide to U.S. Representative Chaka Fattah. Gregory Naylor, pled guilty to misusing campaign funds, many are comparing the Congressman to former Congressman William Gray – who abruptly resigned after similar allegations. Official court documents say that Naylor helped “Elected Official A” disperse campaign funds through a variety of nonprofits.

headline: Volunteer firefighters and emergency responders officially exempted from Affordable Care Act mandate
abstract: The final regulations were released for implementing the employer responsibility provisions under the federal Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, which make it official that volunteers for a government or tax-exempt entity are exempted from being counted as full-time employees. The health care law requires an employer with 50 or more full-time employees to offer health care coverage to employees or pay a fine. This mandate raised concern for emergency crews that have 50 or more volunteers. U.S. Sen. Pat Toomey, R-PA., and U.S. Rep. Lou Barletta, R-Hazelton were among those who lobbied for the change.

headline: Revenue Secretary Meuser touts Corbett's record
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett’s Revenue Secretary, Dan Meuser, has taken to the campaign trail to promote the Governor’s record in PA. He touted several economic indicators and said that education funding has never been higher in PA. The Wolf Campaign fired back saying that the Governor has used one time funding gimmicks as opposed to real solutions.

headline: 3 PA pols: Market8 best choice for new Phila. Casino
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board should grant the remaining Philadelphia license to MARKET8, which would build a casino and other amenities at the corner of 8th and Market streets, said State Reps. Michael O’Brien and John Taylor and Philadelphia First District Councilman Mark Squilla. The Center City location, MARKET8 will be best positioned to draw gaming patrons and spur economic growth on and around East Market Street. Also, MARKET8 will drive more business to the Pennsylvania Convention Center, which will generate additional major conventions and therefore more revenue for the State and the City.

headline: Highmark lawsuit against UPMC centers on billing for cancer drugs
abstract: Highmark Inc. is claiming that UPMC and three other physician groups have overbilled cancer drugs since 2010. The company has filed a lawsuit to return the funds, with interest and legal costs, pledging that if it is successful it will return the money to its customers. Highmark claims that the companies are filing services as more expensive outpatient care, which is driving up costs. UPMC responded by saying that Highmark practices the same billing principles and is violating a contract with the State.

headline: Pa. House Speaker Sam Smith announces he’ll retire
abstract: PA State House Speaker Sam Smith announced he will not seek re-election in the May 20th primary. Other GOP leaders whom lobbyists and lawmakers said could become majority leader include Rep. David Reed, the GOP policy chairman; appropriations committee Chairman Bill Adolph; caucus secretary Mike Vereb; and Rep. Stan Saylor.

headline: Report: state worker pensions set arbitrarily
abstract: The rules for PA’s pension system are designed by the General Assembly and national rankings have placed the underfunded pension system as one of the worst in the country. Under the current system, most of the money is taken up by a very small percentage of workers. The system also works to disenfranchise certain workers and the benefits are largely dependent upon when someone started working rather than years served.

headline: Column: Legislation a detriment to state waterways
abstract: The Endangered Species Coordination Act aims to put legislative oversight ahead of scientific study and protocol for classifying wild trout streams. This act comes at a time when PA land developers, chamber of commerce members and coal and gas industry representatives have said wild trout streams are a deterrent to development. Supporters of the Fish and Boat Commission and the Game Commission look to garner support from state representatives to jettison the act.

headline: Philly420: How smoking pot in Denver could lead to your arrest in Pa.
abstract: Significant debate has risen after the full legalization of cannabis in Colorado and Washington as to how dangerous driving while under the influence of cannabis is. PA’s strict laws concerning cannabis can lead to criminal proceedings days, or even weeks after last usage. Several lawmakers and groups are advocating for creating less strict laws.

headline: DEP hearing on oil and gas regs tonight
abstract: The PA state Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) will hold a public hearing on proposed oil and gas surface activities for conventional and unconventional operations. The proposed regulations are attempting to create performance standards for surface activities at oil and gas well sites and to prevent and minimize spills and releases to the environment.

headline: Lawyer wants to stop convicted Pa. lawmakers from lobbying
abstract: A lawyer in Bryn Mawr, PA is pushing for lawmakers to pass a law that would make convicted felons ineligible for lobbying the government. The issue came up after several former lawmakers convicted of corruption sought approval to be lobbyists. Several groups have raised constitutional concerns over whether or not such a ban could impede upon one’s constitutional rights, specifically freedom of speech.

headline: EPA approves waste disposal well in Clearfield County
abstract: Federal environmental regulators issued a permit for an underground injection well in Clearfield County that will be used to dispose of oil and gas waste liquids. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency approved the permit for Windfall Oil and Gas of Falls Creek, Pa. to build and operate a disposal well in Brady Township. Residents of the area have said that their neighborhood is the wrong place for an injection well and critics of the proposed well vowed to continue to fight it.

headline: Pennsylvania donors among those upping contributions after Supreme Court ruling
abstract: After the ruling in McCutcheon v. Federal Election Commission, which eliminated aggregate contribution limits in elections, donors with large resources have stepped up their donations by more than $12 million passed what would have been legally allowed before the court ruling. In PA, almost two thirds of this spending has gone to conservative causes.

headline: Editorial: Corbett budget- same problem, no new solutions
abstract: In the last year of his first term, PA Governor Tom Corbett has the privatization of liquor sales and public pension reform on his to-do-list. To address liquor sales, Gov. Corbett has issued his last call to Legislatures for privatization. Moreover, to address pension reform Gov. Corbett did not propose any new specifics, while in the past, legislators did not move on reform measures that he did propose.

headline: Harrisburg officials tour blighted areas with bipartisan group of state legislators
abstract: A group of State Legislatures accompanied the Mayor of Harrisburg to take a tour of the city to see how blight has effected the area as well as how certain government policy has positively impacted the city. Lawmakers expressed concern and the necessity of the State Government to pass measures to make it easier for municipalities to deal with blight.

headline: North Pocono fiscal plight surfaces at budget hearing
abstract: Representative Mike Carroll, D-118, Avoca, criticized PA Governor Tom Corbett’s proposal to create a Ready to Learn block grant as a new state mandate a part of the state budget. Gov. Corbett has proposed funding the Ready to Learn block grant with $341 million. The North Pocono School District officials believe they will face fiscal troubles as state aid continues to fall short of escalating pension and health care costs.

headline: Year after approval, Corbett now wants 'review' of school standards
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett is working to repeal the Common Core standards approved for primary education by his predecessor, Ed Rendell. He now intends to hold hearings across the state presided over by acting Education Secretary Carolyn Dumaresq. The goal of the hearings is to ensure that PA students are graduating with the highest academic standards.

headline: More complaints, town hall to address high electric rates
abstract: Residents voiced their concerns of increased energy costs. The Pennsylvania Consumer Advocates, who look out for consumers in disputes with utilities has informed upset consumers to dispute their bills with the power company, and formally complain to the Public Utility Commission and then notify their office.

headline: Fattah stresses his good work, tells media to be positive
abstract: U.S. Rep. Chaka Fattah has broken silence on allegations that he had illegally used campaign funds to pay back some debts he and family members have amassed over the years. He said that the media should focus on the good work he’s done in Washington as opposed to informal allegations being made against him. He claimed that should formal allegations be made, he will address them then.

headline: EXCLUSIVE: DHS official Marrone used private eye to find dirt on Rendell to undercut Pa. race
abstract: Congressmen Rep. Jason Chaffetz, Utah, Sen. Chuck Grassley, Iowa, and Rep. Darrel E. Issa, California, are demanding Homeland Security to explain how and why Christian Marrone made it through the clearance process to be appointed Homeland Security chief of staff. These demands come after the continued development of information tying Mr. Marrone to illegal activity involving the use of private investigators and money laundering.

headline: The e-mail scandal: Corbett was told
abstract: In previous interviews, PA Gov. Tom Corbett denied any knowledge that employees in his office when he was Attorney General were exchanging pornographic e-mails. However, information has now surfaced that the Governor was aware that it was happening. This revelation has emboldened political opponents.

headline: Kathleen Kane’s credibility as state attorney general has been hurt by a scathing court ruling
abstract: Schuylkill County Judge Jacqueline Russell threw out all the charges made by State Attorney General Kathleen Kane in the criminal case against Barbara Manicini who tried to help her dying 93-year-old father. Judge Russell said that Kane clearly failed to present sufficient evidence that a criminal event had occurred. Critics of Kane allege that the original criminal charges were in an attempt to gain political support back from conservatives. Supporters of death with dignity hope future decisions will protect a family member’s dignity.

headline: Pennsylvania, breeding farm of the bizarre
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Corbett has managed to keep an e-mail scandal involving porn alive by initially denying knowledge of the e-mails being sent in his office as Attorney General, only to later say that he was aware. Democratic challenger, Tom Wolf, also hired an ex-porn star to be in an ad attacking the Governor. Upon discovering the actor’s past, the campaign immediately fired him.

headline: Rising prison costs spell trouble for Corbett’s signature reform
abstract: In his first term, PA Governor Tom Corbett has found success in keeping the state prison population relatively level. For the first time in a generation projections of future growth in the state prisons were negative. However, projections and results have not lined up in recent reports, bringing concern to the current Justice Reinvestment prison reform package enacted by Gov. Corbett in 2012.

headline: PUC puts off decision on Uber's bid for state approval
abstract: After concluding a hearing on controversial ride-sharing services such as Lyft and Uber, judges from the Public Utility Commission (PUC) stated that would put off a decision until later in the month. Taxi companies are saying that the ride-sharing services are unfair due to being able to operate under different rules from taxi services. Other concerns include how Uber and Lyft plan to insure their passengers and drivers.

headline: Corbett airs first TV ad
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Corbett began his statewide cable ad campaign for reelection. His TV ad highlighted how he has kept his promise to cut wasteful state spending.

headline: Legislator pushes to revise state's PlanCon program for school construction
abstract: PA State Senator Seth Grove has introduced a bill designed to reform the state’s PlanCon program, which seeks to reimburse construction projects for schools. The Rep. said that the backlog is a serious problem, but the entire program must be reformed to modernize it and lower the burden on schools. The bill passed on party lines, which Democrats opposing the bill due to inadequate funding for the schools’ backlogged reimbursements.

headline: School-funding request faces tough road
abstract: The School District of Philadelphia’s Superintendent William Hite set a request for $320 million in new funding on top of the previously requested $120 million from a city sales-tax increase and substantial labor savings. This request to fund the city’s school district comes as the PA Governor Tom Corbett’s funding plan falls far too short. Philadelphia Major Michael Nutter and the Philadelphia City Council, having raised taxes to aid the district in recent years, are lobbying for Gov. Corbett and Harrisburg to increase funding.

headline: URA board to vote on Strip District produce terminal
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Bill Peduto has worked to negotiate with developers to redevelop the Strip District produce terminal. The mayor announced he was open to numerous proposals on redevelopment, but certain contractors have drawn criticism from PA State Sen. Jim Ferlo.

headline: PUC to Investigate Rising Electricity Rates For Some Consumers
abstract: Following complaints filed by over 800 ratepayers, the PA Public Utility Commission voted unanimously to open an investigation of the doubling, tripling and quadrupling of rates by certain electricity suppliers. The PA PUC will look into why electric supply companies have raised rates so dramatically and how they are disclosing to consumers their intention to raise rates to customers.

headline: Corbett, trailing, says he tackled tough issues
abstract: Polls are continuing to show that Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett is trailing by nearly 24 points behind Democratic challenger Tom Wolf. The Corbett Campaign stated that their challenges come from the fact he attempted to tackle controversial issues, whereas the Wolf Campaign believes PA voters have rejected Corbett’s policies. A slight majority of voters stated their support of Wolf is more anti-Corbett than pro-Wolf.

headline: Libertarian Krawchuk wages battle to get on the ballot in primary election
abstract: Ken Krawchuk, the Libertarian candidate for Pennsylvania governor faces the difficulty of being a third-party candidate. By law a third party candidate must gather 16,639 valid signatures of PA residents, while Republican and Democratic challengers each need only 2,000. Political pundit, G. Terry Madonna acknowledged that there is no likely way for the Libertarian candidate to win the governor’s race, but improvement might be measured in a few percentage points at the polls.

headline: ABC: Anybody But Corbett
abstract: A new poll shows Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett behind Democratic challenger Tom Wolf by 24 points. However, the poll also revealed that the majority of Wolf’s supporters are more anti-Corbett than they are pro-Tom Wolf. This leads many to speculate that any Democrat would have been very successful in a campaign against Tom Corbett, who is very unpopular.

headline: Educational technology reshapes classrooms
abstract: Educational technology, including interactive textbook supplements to games and apps for mobile devices, is offering a personalized approach to learning at a time when state policymakers are standardizing curriculum. Currently Pennsylvania has adopted a version of the Common Core, a set of national education standards. The PA Core blends state standards with some of the national suggestions.

headline: Municipal debt bill face home stretch
abstract: A bill designed to put regulations on the debts municipalities can have is making its way through the legislature with strong bipartisan consensus. The bills came in response to an incinerator project that nearly bankrupted the city of Harrisburg, however the legislature is clear the laws shall affect all municipalities.

headline: Act 13 ruling buoys residents near Trax Farm gas well
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court declared unconstitutional parts of Act 13, which limited local zoning control in favor of a statewide standard guiding where natural gas wells could be drilled. Since 2010, more than 270 municipalities in PA have passed more than 300 ordinances aimed at regulating oil and gas activity. Given the recent decision it is expected that municipalities will become more aggressive in their attempts to regulate the industry.

headline: Bethlehem NAACP airs charter school concerns
abstract: The Bethlehem NAACP has raised concerns that PA’s charter school system is creating a separate and unequal education system. When a student leaves a public school for a charter school, the school district loses money. Bethlehem Area School District is expecting to lose $20 million due to charter schools. Many have called out racial disparities in charter vs. public schools as well.

headline: Funding truce on state aid to Pennsylvania’s public universities appears to be over
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has proposed to level fund the colleges again for a third straight year, but each of Pennsylvania’s four state-related universities, plus the 14 state-owned schools, are seeking more funding. Prior, in exchange for flat-funding from the state, the public universities promised to do their best to keep student tuition rates at or near the rate of inflation.

headline: The battle against blight in Pa. gets a new blueprint
abstract: The Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania is reporting on how cities have combatted the issue of blight, something that affects all cities. Harrisburg has used federal money to clean up condemned properties whereas Philadelphia has instituted a program that fines individuals who have the means but refuse to maintain properties. Other municipalities are increasing regulations on maintaining properties up to code.

headline: Wolf holds early lead among Dem hopefuls for Pa. governor, poll finds
abstract: A Pennsylvania statewide poll found that 36 percent of voters polled would chose the Tom Wolf, former secretary of the Revenue Department, for the Democratic nomination for governor in the May 20 primary. The poll showed 65 percent of Democrats have seen an ad about the governor’s race, and 88 percent of those people have seen Wolf’s ad. The candidate chose to represent the party in the midterm election will face incumbent PA Governor Tom Corbett.

headline: Corbett vows gunman will be brought to justice in Blooming Grove
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Corbett declared that law enforcement agencies will not rest until the individual responsible for ambushing Cpl. Bryon Dickson and severely injuring several others is brought to justice. He called for prayers and respect of the families’ privacy.

headline: Wolf holds early lead among Dem hopefuls for Pa. governor, poll finds
abstract: A Pennsylvania statewide poll found that 36 percent of voters polled would chose the Tom Wolf, former secretary of the Revenue Department, for the Democratic nomination for governor in the May 20 primary. The poll showed 65 percent of Democrats have seen an ad about the governor’s race, and 88 percent of those people have seen Wolf’s ad. The candidate chose to represent the party in the midterm election will face incumbent PA Governor Tom Corbett.

headline: 12 days left in session, and legislators are checking their lists
abstract: After leaving several high salience issues unsolved in June, legislators are expected to tackle issues in the fall session. Among the issues to be discussed are reforming the State’s pension system, property tax reform, charter school reform, shrinking the size of the legislature, and DUI reform. Although some proposals have bipartisan smart, many are skeptical to how far the reforms will go.

headline: Speakers question charter school funding
abstract: PA State Auditor General Eugene DePasquale along with PA State Sen. James Brewer participated in a series of five public meetings with the goal of issuing recommendations address funding and other issues concerning charter schools. The sessions addressed a wide range of issues, including who should authorize charter schools, how much the schools should be paid and what their impact is on school districts.

headline: Bill allowing teachers to carry firearms in school vetted by Senate committee
abstract: The PA State Senate is considering a bill that would allow teachers to carry concealed weapons on school grounds as a protection to school shootings. The bill is particularly geared towards rural schools that have a longer response time. Philadelphia legislators remain skeptical as violence in urban schools is more prevalent and increased access to guns could prove dangerous.

headline: Perzel set to be released this week, DeWeese next month
abstract: Former PA House Speaker John M. Perzel and former House Speaker, H. William DeWeese, are set to be paroled in the coming weeks. Both are serving sentences for separate corruption charges.

headline: Corbett not convinced racy e-mails exist
abstract: Despite the rumors, Pa Gov. Tom Corbett remains unconvinced that e-mails containing sexual images were circulated in his office during his time as Attorney General.

headline: Union exemption from harassment claims raises questions
abstract: Due to a provision protecting parties in labor disputes from prosecution for stalking, harassment, and terroristic threats, the men who harassed Post bros. executive Sarina Rose at all hours have walked free. The indictment of 10 members of Philadelphia’s ironworkers local on federal racketeering charges has drown attention to the exemption, which dates back to the 1930s and which critics say encourages state courts to protect the very behavior federal authorities have since condemned.

headline: PA Senate bill to kill school property tax takes step
abstract: A PA State Senate panel narrowly approved legislation that would eventually eliminate property taxes in exchange for an increase in income and sales tax in order to fund the schools.

headline: Schwartz gubernatorial bid endorsed by Pa. Planned Parenthood PAC
abstract: U.S. Representative Allyson Schwartz has picked up the endorsement of PA’s leading abortion rights advocacy group, the Planned Parenthood PA PAC. The endorsement comes after U.S. Rep. Schwartz lost her frontrunner status to Tom Wolf. Sari Stevens, executive director of the Planned Parenthood PA PAC stated that Schwartz will stand up against for women’s access to birth control, preventive health care and reproductive rights in the Governor’s office.

headline: Philadelphia cigarette tax vote will wait few more days
abstract: The vote on a bill that would tax cigarettes at $2 a pack in Philadelphia is being delayed as Republicans debate certain elements of the bill. The tax will be used to provide crucial funds to the cash stripped School District of Philadelphia.

headline: Democrats again decry end of Adult Basic
abstract: The Adult Basic Care program, ended by PA Gov. Tom Corbett in 2011, was created to allow low-income workers in the state to purchase health-care insurance at a minimal cost. PA Gov. Corbett has yet the expansion of Medicaid, leaving 500,000 state residents without health insurance. The state Commonwealth Court ruled last March that the Corbett administration must reinstate the Adult Basic Care program beginning in the 2013-2014 fiscal year. Gov. Corbett and state House Republican have filed appeals.

headline: Marino press aide pleads guilty to gun charge
abstract: Ryan Shucard, Press Secretary to U.S. Rep. Tom Marino was sentenced to 30 days in jail for attempting to bring a gun into a Congressional Office Building. The sentence was reversed and Mr. Shucard instead was sentenced to unsupervised community service and apologized for the incident as well as paid $100 in court fees.

headline: Winter wreaks havoc on PennDOT budget, but new finding is a plus
abstract: PennDOT Secretary Barry Schoch told House lawmakers that the harsh winter has wiped out a seasonal budget of $189 million, spending about $11 million dollars over that figure. The harsh winter has increased the need for salting, but has also increased the number of potholes. Schoch said money from the $2.3 billion transportation funding package passed last fall will help get rid of the potholes with more long-term paving than has been possible in the past

headline: Bill would force meeting agenda disclosure
abstract: The PA House State Government Committee heard testimony concerning improvements to the Sunshine Act that would require state and local governments to disclose meeting agendas publicly before meetings to better inform the public on what is happening and increasing transparency in government.

headline: Reps from both sides of the aisle try out campaign lines during Zogby’s House budget hearing
abstract: Budget Secretary Charles Zogby fielded questions during the House Appropriation’s Committee meeting. Zogby spent most of the time explaining the actions of the Corbett administration.

headline: Corbett, down in the polls, may now have to face the porn
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett’s position on alleged pornographic e-mails being sent and received in his office as Attorney General has evolved over the last two weeks. First, the Gov. said he had no knowledge of e-mails, but later he said he had been told about inappropriate e-mails in May. Corbett’s trailing poll numbers to challenger Tom Wolf may force him to finally address the issue.

headline: Battle to extinguish PA coal fire continues
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection announced a coal refuse fire in northeast PA that’s been burning since December may take another month to put out. The expected total cost to extinguish the fire is estimated to be about $2 million.

headline: Voting in our state and city isn't what it should be
abstract: Despite being the birthplace of the American Republic, PA continuously falls behind other states in voter turnout, usually failing to garner 40 percent of eligible voters. Many things may contribute to low voter turnout, including gerrymandering and one-party cities/districts. PA has also increased requirements necessary to vote, inflating the problems.

headline: Council, Brady nag Nutter to push for ’16 convention
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter has expressed interest in hosting the 2016 Democratic National Convention in his city. However, facing a deadline for cities to express their interest in hosting the event, the City Council pushed ahead of Nutter to secure their seat as a potential host. A convention in Philadelphia promises to be a huge economic boost, worth as much as $300 million to the local economy.

headline: Pa. House OKs Phila. Cigarette tax
abstract: The PA State House has approved the Philadelphia Cigarette Tax in a new version of the bill that eliminates several additions made by the Senate. If approved by the Senate, the tax is expected to be signed swiftly by Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett. If the tax is not approved, the Philadelphia School District may be forced to lay off more than 1,000 employees.

headline: Tom Corbett and Tom Wolf debate tax policy, education spending
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett and Democratic challenger Tom Wolf met for their first debate. The two clashed over a variety of topics, specifically taxes and education.

headline: Bypassing pharmacies boosts workers' comp prescription costs in Pa.
abstract: The PA House has unanimously passed a law that limits the practice of physicians issuing prescriptions over pharmacies in an attempt to reduce the overall costs of workers’ compensation programs. Many have raised concerns that the bill will limit the ability of physicians to treat patients while others raise concerns over PA’s high drug addiction and overdose rates.

headline: Philly cigarette tax clears Senate, finally headed to Corbett
abstract: The PA State Senate has approved the $2 Philadelphia cigarette tax that is expected to be swiftly signed by Gov. Tom Corbett. The tax is expected to raise a much needed $49 million for the Philadelphia School District. The approved bill lacked economic improvement zones and hotel taxes for other parts of the State.

headline: LGBT advocates urge for hate crimes protection
abstract: LGBT advocates took the State Capitol to petition for adding lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender Pennsylvanians to the hate crimes protection law. Sexual orientation was added to the law in 2002, but struck down on a technically. Race, ethnicity, and religion are some of the identities covered under the law.

headline: Aging natural gaslines pose hidden threat across U.S.
abstract: As the United States struggles to deal with aging infrastructure, many localities in PA are scrambling to replace natural gaslines that are older than 90 years. The haste comes after an explosion in Allentown resulted in the deaths of five people. The problem is worse in the Northeast where many cities are much older than other parts of the country.

headline: Kane responds to Rockview rape victim suit in filing, says woman partly responsible for brutal assault
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane issued a statement that a rape victim in Rockview state prison may be partially responsible for her assault due to failure to take added safety precautions when dealing with inmates. Omar Best, the assaulter, is spending life in prison after three violent crimes, including rape.

headline: Pa. Senate passes medical pot legislation
abstract: A bill that would legalize medical marijuana for certain illnesses passed the State Senate by a strong majority, but meets skepticism from the House and opposition from Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett. The bill would allow peoples diagnosed with certain illnesses to consume marijuana in methods excluding smoking. Several opponents to the bill cited the Federal Government’s listing of marijuana as a dangerous drug.

headline: Losing the signal: Corbett's campaign commercials not helping
abstract: Several polls continue to show Democratic challenger Tom Wolf holding a considerable margin over Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett in the upcoming election. Polls also show that a majority of voters have seen TV ads, but only 10 percent reported them changing their views as a result. Education and the Economy remain the most salient issues going into the final weeks of the election.

headline: Hearing held on buzz over Shippensburg Sheetz beer sales
abstract: A Sheetz in Altoona is being challenged in court over its decision to sell beer within its store. Sheetz attorneys claim they are both a restaurant and a convenience store, therefore able to sell beer. Prosecutors believe that it violates state laws and that Sheetz cannot properly be called a convenience store.

headline: Right to know much less
abstract: The State Senate has unanimously passed a bill that would restrict the State’s right to know law and bring it back to provisions from 1957. The bill would restrict access to certain documents and expand public officials’ ability to use exceptions to withhold information from public release.

headline: Police communications in Eric Frein manhunt not even
abstract: Residents in the usually tranquil mountains of the Poconos are concerned over the Police’s handling of the manhunt for Eric Frein. Frein is accused of having shot and killed a police officer and is now on the run. Some residents believed the police could be doing more to capture him and update the public, but others believe the police’s actions are sufficient given the situation.

headline: Budget forces DEP to split regulations for shallow, deep wells
abstract: Just as the Department for Environmental Protection began working on regulations, language inserted into the budget forces the department to differentiate between shallow and deep wells. In many cases, the differentiations are made, however DEP needs to review changes before a deadline.

headline: Rules of the road must apply to Pa. newcomers too
abstract: Controversy remains over Lyft and Uber, two ride-sharing companies that allow people to use their personal cars to transport other people for a fee. The two companies have failed to go through the proper legal work to operate within PA and routinely pay fines for their operations. Uber is seeking approval from the Public Utilities Commission for statewide operation, and may get a decision as early as November.

headline: Porn at work: Corbett, Kane must end a raunchy office culture
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane released some information over pornographic e-mails than were sent from 2008 to 2012 on office computers while Gov. Tom Corbett was attorney general. Some of the individuals sending the e-mails currently work for the Governor.

headline: Judge to rule on Scranton's motion to dissmiss commuter tax opponents' case
abstract: In order to help pay for the city’s pensions, Scranton has imposed a commuters’ tax that will take money out of commuters’ earned income and use it to pay down the pensions. Several have filed a lawsuit stating there is no authority to make such a tax. A judge is currently deciding whether or not to dismiss the case.

headline: Act 47 changes near the finish line
abstract: Act 47, which helps financially distressed municipalities, went under revision as the Senate gave its version of the bill back to the House. Under the new changes, Pittsburgh will not be given the same ability to raise service taxes as other municipalities. Supporters argue that Pittsburgh has unique ways to raise revenue, while opponents argue the measure protects prominent House members in the Pittsburgh suburbs.

headline: Settlement proposed for Pa. same-sex marriage limbo
abstract: Same-sex couples married before the May 20 federal ruling that legalized the marriages across the State, are suing to not have their legal marriage date changed to May 20. There are also over 80 couples whose marriages are not considered legal due to the fact it occurred before the May 20 federal ruling. The settlement will recognize the marriages only of the plaintiffs, leaving the 80 other couples in limbo.

headline: Pa. reducing backlog of civil cases, chief justice says
abstract: Currently, Allegheny County has over 40,000 cases on backlog, many of which were filed more than two years ago. The American bar association recommends that civil suits be dealt with within a two year frame, otherwise there is a chance they will go unattended. Courts are now looking into ways to incentivize attorneys to speed up the process of filing and moving casework.

headline: Christie hits campaign trail for Corbett
abstract: In a show of support for PA Gov. Tom Corbett, NJ Gov. Chris Christie stopped in Ivyland, Bucks County to rally up a crowd of eager voters. Christie stressed the need to come out and vote, as well as organize. Corbett touted his record of balanced budgets and no new taxes. Still, Corbett finds himself behind challenger Tom Wolf.

headline: Pennsylvania's clout, Pat Toomey's role to rise if GOP takes Senate
abstract: It is likely that if the GOP gains control of the U.S. Senate, Senator Pat Toomey's position will increase and he may become Chairman of a subcommittee. Toomey said he is looking forward to helping the Senate function more efficiently and advance conservative causes.
