headline: Parker denies approval of negative Madden ads
abstract: An attack ad by GOP State House Candidate David Parker accused his Democratic  challenger of evading property taxes, totaling $24,000. Parker denies he had any part in the ad, but his challenger contends that he has final approval on any ad produced.

headline: Corbett stands by his 'tough choices' as he concedes
abstract: Only minutes after the polls closed, PA's gubernatorial race was called in favor of Democrat Tom Wolf. Many Republicans claimed that the failure to offset education cuts and liquor privatization, as well as the overall messaging of the campaign, lead to the Governor's defeat. In his concession, Gov. Tom Corbett said he was proud of his accomplishments.

headline: Pa. voters opted for change; now Wolf needs to deliver: PennLive editorial
abstract: PA Democrat Tom Wolf succeeded in winning the Governor's seat from Tom Corbett. Now he must be able to deliver his message of change to the voters, which also gave him a staunchly Republican General Assembly. Wolf promised to provide increased education funding, income tax relief, and a severance tax.

headline: Aaron Kaufer defeats Eileen Cipriani in 120th
abstract: 26-year-old Aaron Kaufer promised to run on a campaign of reforming government using his unique experience in the private sector. While both are supportive of a severance tax, eliminating property taxes, and legalization of medical marijuana, the two differed on term limits. Kaufer promised to be in office for no longer than eight years. Eileen Cipriani believes $100,000 in negative campaign ads lead to her defeat.

headline: Paul Bart, Will Tallman: Results are in from 193rd House District in Cumberland County.
abstract: State Rep. Will Tallman has defeated Democratic challenger Paul Bart in the race for the State House. Rep. Tallman, as he enters his fourth term, says that pension reform and property tax relief will remain his key issues in the House.

headline: Pa. legal experts call on Castille, Kane to release justices' email
abstract: A group of legal experts have called upon PA Supreme Court Justice Ronald Castille and Attorney General Kathleen Kane to release 4,000 sexually explicit e-mails sent between the Supreme Court and the Attorney General's Office. This is the best way to restore the public's trust, said State Sen. Daylin Leach.

headline: Casey backs provision to ensure Afghan women vote
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey Is supporting a provision that would ensure Afghan women the right to vote during the presidential election in Afghanistan.

headline: Pennsylvania Gov.-elect Wolf to inherit shortfall of $1.85B
abstract: The Independent Fiscal Office announced that PA will face a projected shortfall of $1.85B when Tom Wolf is sworn in as Governor. Democrats argue it is the result of failed fiscal policy, whereas Republicans argue it is the result of failure to reform pensions and privatize liquor.

headline: Penn State trustees plan to discuss NCAA sanctions
abstract: The Penn State board of trustees will conduct private discussions to look over the NCAA sanctions imposed in the wake of the Jerry Sandusky trial. There is controversy over the signing of a consent agreement that brought the University into court, involuntarily. Penn State contends it has remained cooperative and spoke only on the facts.

headline: Rein in asset forfeitures
abstract: Increasingly, civil forfeiture is bypassing the constitutionally mandated due process system and is seizing a large amount of people's property. Police forces have found loopholes in State laws and have been able to provide extra funds for themselves in such cases. U.S. Sen. Rand Paul has proposed reforms, including eliminating loopholes.

headline: Toomey looks forward to stronger GOP majority in Senate
abstract: U.S. Senator Pat Toomey is heading back to Washington with a newly elected majority. Democrats across the state are preparing for the campaign to oust the Senator, who only won by 2% in 2010. Democrats believe Toomey is too conservative, and are eager to take back the seat.

headline: Two state bills would allow terminally ill patients in Pennsylvania to end their own lives
abstract: Several PA lawmakers have introduced a bill that would allow terminally-ill patients to seek life-ending medication from their doctor. Supporters argue it gives patients a way to die on their own terms, as opposed to in pain at hospitals. Opponents argue that the laws are immoral and question the mental capability of a patient to request the medication. The law is modeled after Oregon's Death with Dignity Law.

headline: AG Kane confirms secret investigation into her office
abstract: PA AG Kathleen Kane claimed to be a victim of attacks from undisclosed sources over her interest in cleaning up corruption in the judicial system. Her claims came after she recently testified before a grand jury over whether her office had violated grand jury secrecy. She did not explain a link between the case involving pornographic e-mails and the grand jury investigation.

headline: Teacher challenges PSEA using union dues to promote Wolf gubernatorial campaign
abstract: Mary Trometter, an assistant professor in Williamsport, filed a lawsuit with the PA State Education Association over its inclusion of her name in a pro-Wolf leaflet. Mrs. Trometter said she did not indicate support for Wolf and that the PSEA violated the law by including her name. The incident has increased debate over automatic payroll deductions for union dues.

headline: Stilp alleges in lawsuit that ethics rulings give incumbents a re-election advantage
abstract: Democrat Gene Stilp of Middle Paxton Twp., filed a complaint late Friday in Commonwealth Court, challenging the legality and constitutionality of commission rulings that allow sitting House members to use public funds to pay for outreach activities, such as mailing newsletters and birthday cards, to residents in areas added to their legislative district as a result of redistricting.

headline: Tough-talking former DA Abraham now wants to lead Philadelphia
abstract: Lynne Abraham, the former District Attorney of Philadelphia, has gained a reputation as "one tough cookie" for her tough-on-crime policies and aggressive pursuit of corruption and the death penalty. She is also known for prosecuting a case alleging the coverup of a decades of child molestation. After her years of service, Abraham is now preparing to announce her candidacy for Mayor.

headline: Pa. has room to adjust tax on natural gas production
abstract: Pennsylvania continues to tax natural gas production at a rate far below what the industry pays in almost all other gas-producing states. Governor Corbett and the Republican-led legislature's impact fee has not satisfied critics who are pushing for a real severance tax that would provide the state with money to invest in schools and higher education.

headline: Casey splits with Dems, supports Keystone XL
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey was among several Democrats to break rank and vote in favor of the construction of the Keystone XL pipeline, which fell one vote short of passage. Republican arguments rally behind job creation whereas environmental activists believe the risks are too high. Several other PA Democrats in the House voted in favor of the pipeline's construction.

headline: Anonymous Pa. Web speech may not be so anonymous
abstract: Pennsylvania state law has strict standards for unmasking anonymous internet commenters. Often times it does not take into account how website patrons interpret potentially defamatory comments, a sign that the state's laws are behind the curve when handling these newer methods of communication.

headline: With Tom Corbett's defeat - is the eight-year cycle dead
abstract: Ever since the 1970s when PA Governors could run for a second term, they all have, and they have all won - except in 2014. Tom Wolf's win over Gov. Corbett could signify a change in the eight-year cycle that could have a profound impact on how gubernatorial elections will run in the future. While it may be too early to conclude anything, it is almost a definite that gubernatorial races will be much more competitive in the future.

headline: Dent, other Pa. lawmakers ask NCAA to release all Penn State emails
abstract: In a letter signed by 16 out of PA's 18 U.S. Representatives, the NCAA was asked to immediately release all documents related to the 2012 consent decree that outlined the sanctions issued against Penn State. The letter alleged that the NCAA has no credible basis to impose the sanctions. Commonwealth Court Judge Covey ordered the NCAA to turn over 477 documents related to the case.

headline: Pittsburgh superintendent Lane calls for changes in state education funding formula
abstract: While testifying before a hearing for the fair funding commission, Superintendent Linda Lane of the Pittsburgh School District stressed the need for the State to find a fair and adequate way to fund the schools. Lane said that the loss of money has caused Pittsburgh Schools to make serious cuts and face being financially distressed.

headline: Pa. House speaker says goodbye as retirement looms
abstract: At a luncheon, Pa. House Speaker Sam Smith recalls his best and worst moments in twenty-eight years as a member of the General Assembly. In a closing statement, Speaker Smith advised that Gov.-elect Wolf put in place skilled people to work with the legislature, one of the things that Gov. Corbett failed to do.

headline: Campaign adviser Isenhour, former candidate Hanger join Wolf's office
abstract: Wolf has named several key members of his administration, including former competitors and people with connections to Gov. Rendell's administration.

headline: Sen. Hughes lines up for Wolf
abstract: PA State Senator Vincent Hughes, the longest serving in the Philadelphia delegation, has officially endorsed Tom Wolf for Governor of PA. This endorsement comes after State Treasurer Rob McCord accused Wolf of racial insensitivity.

headline: Senate to vote on Gettysburg National Military Park expansion, train station inclusion
abstract: Legislation is currently in a vote at the U.S. Senate to expand the park grounds of the Gettysburg National Military Park as well as construction of a train station to the park. Both PA Senators are in support of the measure, calling it an economic benefit and the culmination of strong bipartisan effort.

headline: PA congressional race in Philadelphia region draws big bucks, big names.
abstract: U.S. Congresswoman Allyson Schwartz is retiring from her seat, leaving it open to a four-way primary that is drawing big names and donations. State Rep. Brendan Boyle represents part of the district, Marjorie Margolies once held the seat, Daylin Leach is well known as a champion of liberal causes, and Valerie Arkoosh has managed to raise more money than her competitors. No candidate has a clear advantage.

headline: Good luck!
abstract: During Gov.-elect Tom Wolf's campaign, he promised a severance tax that would bring in $1B of additional revenue. Today, that number seems hard to obtain as the output of Marcellus Shale has fallen below the expectation. Also, many PA Republicans are concerned that a severance tax would cool enthusiasm for investment into the region.

headline: Judges hear debate on sections of Act 13 drilling law
abstract: Act 13, dealing with drilling rights in PA, is back in the courts. Now, it is being challenged on more narrow topics. Challengers include municipalities, local officials, environmental groups, and a doctor. They all argued that the law provides for unequal or inadequate protection. One example being that doctors cannot inform their patients what chemicals may be affecting their health due to provisions in the bill. Overall, challengers believe that increased legislation is necessary to clear up vague provisions.

headline: Of double vision and holiday wishes
abstract: PA Elected Officials are all hoping for continued good feelings and prosperity going into the holiday season.

headline: Philadelphia couple seeks recognition of same-sex marriage
abstract: a same-sex couple in Philadelphia is suing PA Governor Tom Corbett and Attorney General Kathleen Kane in order to force the State to recognize their marriage license obtained in Massachusetts. This lawsuit joins several others are seeking to overturn PA's ban on same-sex marriage. These cases come in the wake of the U.S. Supreme Court striking out the Defense of Marriage Act, which banned same-sex marriage on the federal level.

headline: New Pennsylvania law expands school clearance requirements
abstract: New standards for school clearance are aimed at improving the safety of children from abuse. The new law changes the definitions of direct contact with children and new regulations regarding volunteers. School districts will be able to have different interpretations of the law, adding to possible variations. The law also requires regular training and clearance renewal every 36 months.

headline: Phillips-Hill, Merisotis differ on political experience in 93rd House District race: primary 2014
abstract: Long standing PA State Rep. Ron Miller is stepping down from office, leaving his seat open in the next election cycle. Ernie Merisotis is running for it, but ran for the seat twice and lost. Phillips-Hill, who works on the school board and in Miller's district office, is running as well. Phillips-Hill is using her experience in the district office and school board to best represent her constituents and move PA forward.

headline: Pittsburgh mayoral staffers appointed to Wolf's transition team
abstract: PA Gov.-elect Tom Wolf has announced 24 committees to analyze various policy issues and departments in the State Government and report problems and concerns before the Jan 20. inauguration date. Numerous appointments from Pittsburgh Mayor Peduto's office have been made.

headline: UIL chief 'disappointed' in failed PGW deal
abstract: After spending a sizable investment on a deal that had no future, UIL Holdings Corp. cancelled a deal with the City to purchase the Philadelphia Gas Works. Council President Darrell Clarke made a surprise announcement that no hearings on the deal would be held and no council member introduced the bill, effectively ending the progression of the deal. UIL said that the experience has “colored their opinion of the City.”

headline: EDITORIAL: Pa. bill outlawing 'secret compartments' is going overboard
abstract: By request from law enforcement, PA State Rep. Kate Harper introduced a bill that would ban secret compartments in cars. The law says the compartments must be specifically intended for smuggling contraband, not for holding valuables or other legal items. The controversy comes from how intent is to be determined and opening the door for people to be arrested based off the fact they “could” sell drugs.

headline: PA lawmaker floats new severance tax proposal as industry pushes back
abstract: PA State Senator Jim Brewster has introduced a bill that would place a 5% severance tax on Marcellus Shale extraction in PA. The industry, and political opponents, argue that the tax will decrease investment into Marcellus Shale. However, several reports indicate that profits will still be made with the tax.

headline: Corbett's call: the governor must act on UPMC-Highmark
abstract: Highmark, the Pittsburgh region’s largest health care insurer and UPMC, the region’s largest health care provider, are currently in the process of splitting which will cause a massive shift in how people in PA receive their healthcare. While many people will see their services drastically altered, both companies are claiming this is good for overall competition. With the legislature unwilling to act, many people are calling on PA Governor Tom Corbett to use the state’s institutions to cancel the split and force the companies to negotiate.

headline: Senate passes Casey's bill to help families bear long-term disability costs.
abstract: A new bill that passed Congress would allow families to create a tax-sheltered savings account to help pay for long-term care for peoples with disabilities. The bill still allows families to collect SSI benefits, which has drawn criticism from opponents. Overall, advocates praised the bill as being a monumental piece of legislation.

headline: RMU poll: Voters don't like Corbett, support extraction tax
abstract: A recent poll done by Robert Morris University found that a majority of voters have an unfavorable view of PA Governor Tom Corbett and believe he will not be reelected. Principle on the minds of Pennsylvanians is education and a severance tax. Tom Corbett has rejected a severance tax, yet Democratic challenger Tom Wolf has proposed it. The poll also revealed a growing support for Florida Gov. Jeb Bush and Secretary Hillary Clinton for the 2016 presidential election.

headline: Guest Columnist: Corbett left a deep hole for Wolf to start filing
abstract: As a result of relying on one-time funding gimmicks to close a deficit, PA Gov.-elect Tom Wolf is facing a nearly $2B deficit before taking office. In order to close the deficit, Wolf is planning to implement a severance tax on Marcellus Shale extraction and shift priorities and taxes.

headline: Fleck says primary was about "the gay Mike Fleck"
abstract: PA State Rep. Mike Fleck said that his primary defeat was primarily due to a reaction to his late 2012 announcement that he was gay. The Citizens’ Alliance of Pennsylvania, a well-known conservative group, spearheaded a campaign to defeat Fleck. They claimed it had everything to do with his record, not his sexuality. Despite losing the Republican nomination, Fleck was successful in winning the Democratic nomination.

headline: Paycheck protection advocate dislikes new name
abstract: Pennsylvanians for Union Reform President Simon Campbell disagrees with a decision to name an important piece of legislation regarding union deductions from paychecks after Mary Trometter, who is a teacher that filed a complaint after receiving a political letter from her union. Campbell said Trometter’s situation is largely irrelevant to the bill.

headline: Undocumented immigrants seek Pa. driver's licenses
abstract: In a post-9/11 crackdown by the Federal Government, a social security number is required to obtain a driver’s license. Phila. State Rep. Mark Cohen has introduced legislation that will allow people to obtain licenses with a tax number or other forms of ID. This will make it so undocumented immigrants can drive legally. Cohen claimed this measure was important to avoid worker exploitation, however PA Republicans, including Gov. Tom Corbett, oppose the measure.

headline: Corbett's plan to overhaul Medicaid challenged in court
abstract: A lawsuit filed on behalf of two Philadelphians alleges that PA Gov. Tom Corbett's Medicaid expansion alternative, Healthy PA, is being mishandled and could potentially harm people who need crucial medical benefits. The Corbett Administration disagreed with the allegations and will work diligently to ensure no confusion at the Jan. 1 effective date.

headline: Gov. Tom Corbett: No interest in adding natural gas tax
abstract: Despite strong growing support for an extraction tax in PA, Governor Tom Corbett remains steadfast in his opposition to any tax, even to close a half a billion dollar budget deficit. He claims that taxing the small, but growing industry will weaken it and make PA less attractive for business overall. Democratic challenger Tom Wolf has promised to pursue an extraction tax.

headline: In lawsuit, groups claims Corbett's Medicaid changes cut benefits to 200,000
abstract: A lawsuit filed in Philadelphia claims that the State’s alternative to Medicaid is too confusing and secretive and will result in 200,000 people seeing benefits cut. The lawsuit requests that the implantation be halted under violation of the Social Security Act and constitutional guarantees of due process.

headline: PUC chair steps down from energy advocacy group
abstract: The PA Public Utilities Commission (PUC) Chair Rob Powelson has stepped down from an energy advocacy group in order to avoid even the appearance of any bias in a high-profile pipeline project currently before the PUC. The pipeline is being built by Sunoco Logistics, which is trying to get exemption from local zoning laws. The energy advocacy group, Energy Action Team, has long supported this initiative – causing many to question whether or not Powelson could remain unbiased as a regulator.

headline: Pa. draws closer to Illinois population
abstract: According to new Census Bureau figures, PA added nearly 6,000 residents to Illinois' 10,000 meaning PA is getting closer to Illinois in population.

headline: Official: Height limits don't apply to landfills
abstract: Interpretations of Dunmore borough’s zoning ordinance is open to differing opinions after declaring a landfill does not fall under the ordinance. Some believe a landfill is not a structure, whereas others would argue that it is. That definition is important in considering whether or not an expansion to the landfill is lawful.

headline: Wolf, others react to York City schools receivership decision
abstract: After giving control of York City School District to a state-appointed receiver, several PA Officials gave comment. PA Gov.-elect Wolf and PA State Rep. Kevin Schreiber argued that Corbett era education cuts caused school districts to go into financial collapse. Administration officials argued that they are doing what is best for the school district.

headline: Corbett's sudden support of limited medical marijuana could draw broad appeal: analysis
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett announced he would support a trial run for medical cannabis, leading to a potential legalization. This could prove popular as a vast majority of Pennsylvanians support legalizing medical marijuana. The Governor raised concerns over how to do it right so as abuse cannot be rampant. PA Democrats said that the Governor is not going far enough, and PA Republicans remain skeptical about the safety of medical marijuana and the risk of abuse.

headline: Reliable alternative to water could ease economic, environmental issues for gas drillers
abstract: Many experts and environmentalists belief that the gas drillers could find an alternative to water, numerous environmental concerns would be eliminated. Researchers are working to find ways to use carbon dioxide, nitrogen, or other gas liquids as alternatives. There is some interest from the industry, but many fear it is too costly.

headline: Rep. Sims: LGBT civil rights is 'not just a liberal issue'
abstract: PA Representative Brian Sims believes the Governor Tom Corbett's support of his anti discrimination bill is a step in the right direction and asserted the fact the LGBT civil rights is not just a liberal issue.

headline: 11 game lands in NEPA have gas leases
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission has given out leases to drilling companies on state game lands, which has raised concerns. Hunters have concerns over the leases, some believing that there should be no drilling on state game lands on principle. Others have a wait-and-see approach, noting that increased development in the area may lead to easier access to the lands.

headline: Pennsylvania legislators suspect "fix" in state process they say cheated Whitehall Township
abstract: Two state legislators from Whitehall Township believed that Whitehall Township was cheated out of a City Revitalization and Improvement Zone program which would have granted the town the ability to restore its waterfront. The legislators believed the agency either ignored the year old application or was purposefully trying to limit the number of applications received.

headline: Controversial pipeline case raises questions about PUC chair's industry ties
abstract: The Mariner East Pipeline, a plan to bring natural gas to the Atlantic through Southeastern PA is causing concern as it has requested to be exempt from local zoning laws. Several groups are calling into question whether or not the Public Utilities Commission’s Chairman’s involvement with Philadelphia Energy Action Team – a group of business leaders, politicians, and academics striving to expand the energy industry – qualifies as a conflict of interest.

headline: DN Editorial: Funding for dummies
abstract: In this editorial, the author argues that the cigarette tax is not an effective way to fund Philadelphia's schools. In opposition to the bill, the author cites four alternatives to properly fund the Philadelphia School District.

headline: DN Editorial: Let it be, Guv
abstract: In a letter to PA Governor Tom Corbett, PA Senator Bob Casey urged the Governor to not appeal the State’s voter ID law to the State Supreme Court. The voter ID law was struck down as there were worries that it would severely hinder the ability of nearly 500,000 voters to vote. As the State could not produce a single case of fraud, the courts found that a vague concern of fraud was not enough to justify the requirements of the law.

headline: Is slot machine gambling coming to your phone?
abstract: In an effort to attract young people, the gambling industry is attempting to allow mobile gambling on the floor of PA Casinos. The idea is to let people download apps that can only be used on the floor of the casino and can gabble on their phones as opposed to slot machines or tables. Advocates say this is a fun new experience for patrons and opponents argue it is an attempt to get more people hooked on gambling.

headline: 4 Democrats vying for Pa. governor pledge to eradicate corruption
abstract: In a state with an “incestuous” relationship between money and politics, four Democrats running for the office of PA Governor have proposed ways to clamp down on corruption. The four covered topics relating to gift bans, reapportionment reform, and removing cronyism in public contracts. PA State Rep. Dan Truitt has also proposed eliminating per diems and reducing the size of the legislature, something none of the Democrats have spoken about.

headline: Big money flows into Pennsylvania gubernatorial campaign
abstract: The 2014 PA gubernatorial campaign is poised to top the previous contest's spending which pitted Tom Corbett against Dan Onorato back in 2010 for the open Governor's seat. Incumbent Gov. Tom Corbett has gained campaign support from business, energy interests and the national Republican establishment. While frontrunner candidate Tom Wolf has the support of Unions and educators across the state.

headline: Airport reaches deal with suburban neighbors
abstract: The Philadelphia Airport has reached a deal with its neighbors that could settle several lawsuits over the expansion of the Airport. The airport is the nation’s fifth most delayed airport, and Mayor Nutter is looking to fix that by moving forward with the project. Several airline companies remain skeptical, saying the delays are due to high traffic in the Northeast and not lack of runway space.

headline: State job site scrubbed of objectionable postings.
abstract: Revisions are being made to a PA state employment website after it was revealed during a debate, between Gov. Tom Corbett and Tom Wolf, that the site posted objectionable job listings such as bachelor party dancers and "car dates".

headline: Democrats blast PA Senate GOP's wine and beer plan
abstract: PA Democrats attacked the PA Senate GOP’s plan for liberalizing the sale of alcoholic beverages and loosening restrains. In many more ways than one, the plan does not seek to accomplish what PA Governor Tom Corbett had sought and it still maintains the state stores for hard liquor. Democrats argued this plan would hurt small business owners and cost the state $50 million annually.

headline: Advocacy groups call for closer scrutiny of charter schools
abstract: The Center for Popular Democracy, Integrity in Education, and Action United of Philadelphia and Pittsburg issued a report alleging that PA charter schools defrauded taxpayers out of more than $30 million. The report urges state officials to temporarily suspend the approval process for new charter schools, investigating existing ones, and shift from standards audits to forensic audits. The PA Coalition of Public Charter Schools responded with a statement dismissing the validity of the groups' accusations.

headline: 20th House District: Democrats should stick with Ravenstahl
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette has chosen to endorse State Rep. Ravenstahl over his challenger, Thomas Michalow due to there being miniscule differences in their views and Michalow’s naivety and unrealistic expectations when it comes to what can be accomplished in the legislature.

headline: Stream buffer bill clears Senate hurdle
abstract: A controversial bill to remove a state regulation requiring forest buffers for a category of specially protected streams cleared with bipartisan approval by a Senate committee. The debate has pitted environmental groups calling for defeat of the bill against building and construction industries who are pushing for its success.

headline: Consumer-friendly bill on electric rates stalls
abstract: Over the winter, some Pennsylvanians watched in horror as their electric bills doubled, tripled, or even quadrupled under variable rates. PA State Rep. Bob Godshall introduced a bill that would cap the amount a rate can increase, decrease lag time when switching providers, and eliminated cancellation fees. Various groups have come out for and against the bill, but ultimately the legislature delayed a vote due to ongoing budget negotiations.

headline: Cold comfort for Corebett: He's not alone on 'endangered guvs' list
abstract: PA Incumbent Gov. Tom Corbett's approval ratings in statewide opinion polls have displayed low approval, trailing by double digits to competitor Tom Wolf in his fight for a second term. This follows a trend this year where 11 governors of both parties are in tight reelection races, the most since 1994.

headline: Jazz buff Sen. Vince Hughes riffs his way through the state budget: John L. Micek
abstract: For several months, tax revenue has fallen short of projections leading to a near $1 billion deficit for PA Governor Tom Corbett’s final budget that is packed with extra spending – mostly in education. PA State Senator Vincent Hughes says the gap could easily be made by scrapping Corbett’s Healthcare plan and accepting the Medicaid expansion and imposing a 5% severance tax on natural gas drilling. Corbett opposes both approaches.

headline: Pa. plan to cover the uninsured back on track?
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett’s administration is confident with the negotiations over its Medicaid alternative, HealthyPA, so much so that is it beginning to solicit contractors. The State opted to avoid expanding Medicaid and instead use the Federal funds to help the uninsured get private insurance. Critics say the delay is costing PA billions of dollars and will not adequately insure those who need it.

headline: Polls shows slight tightening of PA gubernatorial race
abstract: A new poll shows that PA incumbent Gov. Tom Corbett is approaching Tom Wolf in the polls. However, time is not on Corbett's side as the gubernatorial election approaches closer, on November 4th.

headline: Two incumbents returned to Penn State trustees board in voting by agricultural groups
abstract: Several PA agricultural societies voted to return two incumbent delegates to the Penn State board of trustees. Board Chairman Keith Masser had no problem winning another term. His fellow incumbent, Betsy Huber, narrowly defeated former PA State Rep. Jess Stairs by one vote.

headline: Pennsylvania income taxes and tonight's debate
abstract: The final debate of the PA gubernatorial race is in Pittsburgh. It is expected that a large portion of the debate will focus on incumbent PA Gov. Tom Corbett and challenger Tom Wolf's differing approaches to tax policy.

headline: Pa. DEP gives itself high grades in regulating Marcellus shale industry, but environmental groups disagree
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) released a report where it claims that the State is a world class regulator of the oil and gas industry. Several environmental groups have raised concern over the report, claiming that there are many more instances of pollution due to fracking than the report is suggesting. Critics claim that report does contain statistics, but is missing key details that would indicate a different result.

headline: Marino points to growing influence, ability to work across the aisle
abstract: U.S. Rep Tom Marino is up for re-election for representative of the 10th Congressional District in PA. He points to his ability to gain influence in Washington, along with his ability to challenge House leaders and President Obama when necessary, and his success in getting some bills passed by the House as reasons he deserves a chance at re-election.

headline: 3 trustees support revisiting Sandusky decisions
abstract: The Penn Staters for Responsible Stewardship, or PS4RS, won a second consecutive sweep in the elections for the Penn State alumni board of trustees. The group campaigned on revisiting some of the decisions made regarding the Sandusky sex abuse case, Paterno, and the NCAA sanctions. PS4RS beat out those who claimed that the continuous revisiting only lead to hurting the present and future of the University.

headline: $75M set aside for Pa. traffic signal upgrades
abstract: A Pennsylvania program called "Green Light-Go" will make available $75 million to local governments for improvements to traffic signals. The program will invite applications from municipalities for a variety of improvements including retiming, replacement with LED lighting, removal of unnecessary signals and real-time monitoring.

headline: Privacy concerns linger around prescription database plan
abstract: The PA State Senate and House are in disagreement on how to response to prescription drug abuse. The PA Senate passed a bill that would allow police officers to get only a court order, not a search warrant, to look into people’s medical records pertaining to prescriptions. The House believed that they needed to find a balance between people’s privacy and adequate law enforcement. The ACLU of PA stated that the court orders lacked probable cause and were dangerous to resident’s privacy.

headline: Clinton, Christie lend clout to PA's gubernatorial race.
abstract: Both Hillary Clinton and New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie, potential presidential contenders, will be campaigning in the Philadelphia area for PA's gubernatorial candidates. Clinton is headlining an event "Women for Wolf", supporting Gov. Corbett's challenger Tom Wolf. While Gov. Christie continues to help the incumbent, Gov. Corbett, raise money in the area.

headline: Local Dem legislators' choices for governor vary
abstract: Local Democratic legislators in Wilkes-Barre are split over which Democratic candidate for PA Governor they want to support. Some have supported Wolf, where others have supported McCord. Arguments for both have been made, citing Wolf’s understanding of the economic issues the area faces and McCord’s record as State Treasurer in vocally opposing the administration’s harsh budgets. All agree, however, that PA Governor Tom Corbett must go.

headline: Former Sen. Waugh dies at 58.
abstract: Called "the quintessential citizen-statesman" by PA Gov. Tom Corbett, former Sen. Mike Waugh, has passed away. Waugh was a Republican member of the state House and Senate from York County for 21 years before becoming executive director of the Farm Show Complex in Harrisburg.

headline: Bill altering buffer zones could threaten clean streams
abstract: Up for a vote by the full PA Senate, a bill expected to pass in the legislature would gut protections for PA's cleanest streams. The proposal would remove a requirement that developers leave a 150-foot forested buffer along some streams. The bill has drawn opposition of environmental groups, while groups such as the PA Builders Association continue to back its passage.

headline: Candidate Wolf can't commit on giving details of tax plan
abstract: Democratic candidate for PA governor, Tom Wolf, hopes, but can't promise, that if he is elected that he would be able to offer a detailed proposal to revise the state's personal income tax system in his first budget address.

headline: Small-business owner challenges Cecil attorney in 46th District
abstract: PA Rep. Jesse White (Dem.) is seeking a fifth term in the 46th Legislative District in Washington and Allegheny counties. Challenging him is a small-business owner and political newcomer, Jason Ortitay (GOP).

headline: One more step will help fight Pa.'s epidemic of drug abuse and overdose deaths: Editorial
abstract: A bill is up for consideration before the PA state Senate's adjournment. If passed it will create a statewide prescription drug registry which aims to make it harder for patients to abuse prescription painkillers and other drugs by obtaining them from multiple doctors.

headline: Corbett announces $10M in grants for Almono project in Hazelwood
abstract: Before local developers can build a projected $1 billion development project on the former LTV Steel Corp. site in Hazelwood, PA, they need about $103 million in streets, utility lines and other infrastructure upgrades. PA Gov. Tom Corbett announced $10 million in state grants to support the project's development. The subsidy package includes $5 million from PennDOT and $5 million from the Economic Growth Initiative. This marks the 13th time this year that Corbett has made an award from the program in Western Pennsylvania.

headline: Albert says being a Republican will help in state Senate
abstract: PA Republican state Senate candidate Joe Albert argues that he will be more effective in Harrisburg than Sen. John Blake (Dem) because he would be joining a Senate led by a Republican majority.

headline: Prescription drug database advances to Gov. Corbett
abstract: A proposed prescription drug database bill that medical professionals and law enforcement could use to combat abuse has passed the state Senate. The next stop for the bill will be the desk of PA Gov. Tom Corbett, who has publicly support the bill.

headline: Distressed cities bill finalized
abstract: Headed to PA Gov. Tom Corbett for final approval, the distressed cities bill aims to give municipalities a timetable for moving out of the Act 47 recovery program instead of languishing their indefinitely. Under this timetable, a municipality could be under act 47 for only five years and then face a three-year exit plan that would result in fiscal solvency, state receivership, bankruptcy protection or disincorporation in limited cases.

headline: Crimes targeting random victims still relatively rare in Harrisburg officials say
abstract: The spokeswoman for the Harrisburg Mayor warns of misleading perceptions of crime in Harrisburg, following a series of robberies near the state capitol that targeted a state Legislator and staff. City leaders point out that violent crimes have fallen in the past 20 years, and have roughly flatlined.

headline: State drops case against Mellow
abstract: The PA state attorney general's office dropped its remaining charge against former state Senate Democratic Leader Robert J. Mellow in the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission pay-to-play case. The final charge dropped came a week after county Judge Richard A. Lewis tossed out six of the seven charges against Mr. Mellow. The ruling was made after the attorney general's office concluded they could not prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Mr. Mellow conspired to run a corrupt organization and commit commercial bribery and bid rigging.

headline: Advocates for 2nd Amendment rights on verge of victory in Pa.'s latest proxy gun control fight
abstract: The PA Senate voted 34-14 to pass a bill that would guarantee groups like the National Rifle Association the right to bring court challenges against local gun ordinances that exceed state law. The bill's new language will give gun owners a powerful new tool to take legal challenges to any of the nearly 50 cities and towns that have adopted local gun laws.

headline: Corbett dropped from NCAA suit on Penn State fine.
abstract: The NCAA has dropped PA Gov. Tom Corbett and Auditor General Eugene DePasquale from its lawsuit challenging a state law that limits where $60 million in Penn State fine money can be spent. The lawsuit stems from a 2013 law requiring fines levied after the Jerry Sandusky child abuse scandal to be spent on Pennsylvania child abuse programs.

headline: McCaffery drops suit against Inquirer
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Seamus P. McCaffery withdrew his defamation suit against The Inquirer for articles detailing how his wife collected lucratice referral fees from personal-injury law firms while serving as his judicial aide. Both McCaffery and his wife, who jointly sued the newspaper, decided to drop their claim after The Inquirer agreed to report a statement from federal prosecutors saying that after a yearlong investigation of the fees, they had decided "that federal criminal charges should not be filed".

headline: Justice sidelined: Pa. would be better off if McCaffery resigned
abstract: PA Chief Justice Ronald Castille and three of his Supreme Court colleagues suspended Justice McCaffery with pay while the state's Judicial Conduct Board takes a month to investigate and decide whether formal misconduct charges are warranted.

headline: Corbett denies support for ultrasound bill
abstract: The group supporting Democratic governor nominee Tom Wolf, Democratic PAC Fresh Start, caught Republican Gov. Tom Corbett on tape denying his prior support for a controversial 2012 bill requiring women to have an ultrasound before an abortion. Corbett did not sign the bill because it stalled in the legislature, but he did support it at the time, making an infamous remark at a news conference stating, "You just have to close your eyes".

headline: Medical marijuana: 'Each DA has to make their own determination'
abstract: PA district attorneys already have discretion in how they prosecute marijuana cases. However, experts say they must be careful in how they apply the law. A bill that would have created rules governing medical marijuana passed the Senate last month but ultimately failed to be take up by the House.

headline: Judges, lawyers wearied by Pa. court's latest scandal
abstract: PA Judges and lawyers react to recent developments in charges filed against PA Supreme Court Justice Seamus P. McCaffery which have resulted in his suspension and an emergency investigation by the Judicial Conduct Board.

headline: 2014 Governor's Race: Face off over the sweet spot on taxing Marcellus Shale
abstract: Both the incumbent PA Gov. Tom Corbett and challenger Tom Wolf agree that the natural gas industry in PA is a "game-changer". However, they differ on how they would tax the industry. Gov. Corbett stands by his impact fee in favor of a severance tax. While Wolf proposes a five percent tax on the market value of the gas, which he intends on replacing the impact fee with.

headline: Conditions tied to public school funding boost
abstract: Wilkes-Barre Area School District Superintendent Bernard said that while he is pleased that the PA budget passed an increase in public education, he  is still concerned that there is an application process required to get additional funding.

headline: Budget season finally over for Luzerne County school districts
abstract: After PA Governor Tom Corbett signed the state budget into law the Luzerne County School District's fiscal fate was made clear: Ten of the eleven Luzerne County districts raised taxes, state money was increased but less than originally promised, and talks of pension reform haulted

headline: Harrisburg on the Potomac
abstract: The author argues that PA State government is a mirror image of the federal government. He cites, that both executive branches are facing possible legislative litigation, both face low polling numbers, both legislative bodies are ineffective, among other issues.

headline: State to fight change of venue request for Washington trial
abstract: State prosecutors are currently fighting LeAnna Wshington's request to move her corruption trail from Montgomery County to Philadelphia. Washington argues that the people and activities at issue are centered in Philadelphia. Washington is being charged for using state paid employees to plan and organize her campaign fundraiser during work days.

headline: Latest attack ad hits air in governor's race
abstract: PA Families First has released an attack ad which attacks PA Governor Tom Corbett for cutting education aid, forcing school district to lay of employees and raising property taxes while refusing to force the oil and gas industry to "pay their fair share".

headline: Paterno son and another former football coach assistant sue Penn State.
abstract: Former assistant coach and son of the late Joe Paterno, Jay Paterno and another former assistant, Bill Kenney, filed a federal lawsuit in Philadelphia against Penn State University for more than $1 million claiming that they had nothing to do with the Sandusky scandal.

headline: State rep sees need to fix mental health system
abstract: In response to a psychiatric patient accused of shooting a caseworker, PA state rep Margo Davidson was inspired to  work on legislation that would make treatment more accessible for mentally disabled individuals.

headline: Thousands of disabled workers in PA paid far below minimum wage
abstract: In PA, about 13,000 disabled workers are earning an average of $2.40 an hour - extremely below minimum average, Since 1986 there is no limit to how little mentally disabled people should be paid.

headline: Corbett to keep health care program for disabled
abstract: After talks of ending a health care program for the disabled, Public Welfare Secretary Beverly Mackereth made the announcement to a Medicaid advisory group meeting that the Medical Assistance for Workers with Disabilities program will continue.

headline: State employees report fewer paycheck problems from Treasury's new computer system
abstract: PA employees are reporting fewer paycheck problems since the Treasury Department's new computer system was introduced.

headline: Bonds could save Pennsylvania's pension problem, but come with a risk
abstract: Actuaries for the Public Employee Retirement Commission suggests that pension obligation bonds could potentially save the state money, but it may come with a risk. Lawmakers, especially PA Governor Tom Corbett do not agree with this approach.

headline: Pa. road projects safe from feds' transportation funding delays
abstract: Amid a potential funding delay in Congress that would increase funding temporarily to the nation's highway trust fund, PA road projects will still continue.

headline: Corbett enacts tougher hit-and-run law called 'Kevin's Law.'
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett enacts a hit-and-run law called "Kevin's Law", which will increase the mandatory minimum for leaving the scene following a fatal car accident. The law was inspired by the death of  Kevin Miller, a 5-year-old boy who was killed as he crossed the street with his family.

headline: Corbett promises review of budget, makes no promises of a result
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett, is looking to review the budget soon but the author believes that he may wait to sign off on the new budget.

headline: Budget stalled, Senate goes home, House wrangles on pension changes
abstract: After the first day of the fiscal year, PA Governor Tom Corbett has not signed the $29.1 billion budget. With the House waiting for a decision, PA legislators are trying to reach a concensus  on changes to the pension system, specifically on whether a cigarette tax should be imposed to improve the Philadelphia's public schools.

headline: Support for medical marijuana reaches highest level ever: poll
abstract: A Franklin and Marshall college poll has revealed that 84 percent of voters strongly favor or somewhat favor allowing adults to use medical marijuana for treatment.

headline: Summer lunch program necessary, but underused, Casey says
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey is advocating for increasing more summer lunch programs. In a typical school year in Lackawanna and Luzerne counties 34,000 students receive reduced or free school lunches, but about 1 in 10 of those students do not visit any summer lunch sites.

headline: DN Editorial: Smoke and Mirrors
abstract: In response to the legislature passing a bill giving the city of Philadelphia the right to impose a cigarette tax to raise money for its schools, the author criticizes PA Governor Tom Corbett's intentions with the bill. He argues that the bill cannot make up for the thousands of jobs lost and tax increases.

headline: Democrats hope Corbett's woes a boost in U.S. House races.
abstract: PA Democrats remain hopeful that PA Governor Tom Corbett's unpopularity may help the party flip one or two PA House seats, in districts near Philadelphia, in their favor.

headline: No concensus: The politics of reform
abstract: Professor and pollster Terry Madonna acknowledges the continued conversation in PA regarding property taxes. The issue still remains stagnant as advocates push for the elimination of property taxes, but fail to give into the increase of other taxes.

headline: Wage-hike tip
abstract: PA Democratic State Senator Daylin Leach and Mike Stack propose raising the minimum wage to $12 in the state. Opponents point to the possibility of job losses due to the increase in labor costs.

headline: Did SRC's refusal to pass budget help district?
abstract: The School Reform Commission (SRC) has refused to provide a spending plan by the May deadline in an attempt to raise the pressure on the City and State to provide additional funds. To get the schools in a half way decent shape, the SRC is requesting nearly half a billion dollars. At the present budget, they worry what the schools will look like for students. Threats of even more layoffs and insufficient services are coming.

headline: Philadelphia Inquirer co-owner Katz dies at 72
abstract: Lewis Katz, a well-known businessman and philanthropist in the Philadelphia area, died in a plane crash at the age of 72. Katz made his fortune in New York parking lots, billboards and cable TV. He also bought several sports teams and the Philadelphia Inquirer. He then turned his efforts towards philanthropy, donating large sums of money to Temple University's Medical School and schools in Camden.

headline: Northampton County DA opposes driver's licenses for undocumented immigrants
abstract: The District Attorney of Northampton County came out against a bill that would allow undocumented immigrants the ability to obtain a PA driver’s license. Supporters of the bill said that it recognizes the reality that many immigrants take to the roads in fear every day, whereas opponents argue that it opens the door to terrorists and criminals obtaining licenses.

headline: 'Tom' most common name for Pa. governors
abstract: A Smart Politics Analysis by a professor at the University of Minnesota found that ‘Tom’ is the most common name for Pa. Governors, having served for 30.5 years or 15% of the State’s history collectively. In the 2014 election, the trend will continue as incumbent Governor Tom Corbett goes against Democratic challenger Tom Wolf.

headline: Lawmakers push for more limits on use of welfare benefits
abstract: A bill is going through the PA State House that would add preventions to welfare funds being used for “adult-oriented entertainment” and tobacco. The idea is that public funds are for essentials and not luxuries. Several House Democrats oppose the bill as being unenforceable or just passing laws for the sake of passing laws. The PA Department of Public Welfare has said that they work with other agencies to limit fraud in the use of public funds, especially with casinos.

headline: Energy companies pay more in gas well impact fees in 2013
abstract: A recent rebound in the price of Marcellus Shale has caused energy companies to pay out significantly higher fees than the year prior. Some counties received three times what they received the prior year. There are several limitations on how municipalities may use the funds, but many are arguing that the funds do not justify the potential danger from pollution.

headline: House passes distressed cities bill
abstract: PA House lawmakers approved legislation that would amend the state recovery program under Act 47 for financially distressed cities. One of the provisions of the bill says that a municipality could only be in Act 47 for five years, as opposed to indefinitely. That, coupled with new powers towards the Governor, creates a situation where municipalities may leave Act 47 and return to fiscal health. Opponents argued that the bill does not give enough support for municipalities to be successful.

headline: Jumpstart for 'Kevin's Law'
abstract: PA State Rep. Mike Carroll succeeded in adding provisions to a Senate Bill regulating school busses that increases the penalties for leaving the scene of a hit-and-run when murder is involved. The provision is known as “Kevin’s Law” and is named after Kevin Miller who was struck and killed near Christmas 2012. Under the law, there is a mandatory three year sentence for fleeing the scene of a hit-and-run.

headline: State $$ helps new cancer center in Lebanon, to hurt existing center
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett unveiled a plan to build an all-encompassing cancer center in the Lebanon Valley, one that will provide all forms of treatment. The Lebanon Valley Cancer Center, which is a small business, believes that with the construction of the new facility it will go out of business. Many have accused that this is a situation of the Government picking winners and losers. The Governor only said that it was sad that there needed to be demand for either of the businesses.

headline: Bill to expand Medicaid advances Pa. House
abstract: The Human Services Committee of the PA State House approved a measure that would expand Medicaid access under the Affordable Care Act. That expansion will bring the bill to the House Floor where Republicans have said there is no plan to vote on the bill. PA Governor Tom Corbett remains committed to a Jan 1, 2015 roll out of his Medicaid alternative, HealthyPA

headline: House GOP leader leaves door open to defer pension payments
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has proposed reducing the scheduled payments on pension obligations, called collars, in an attempt to balance the State budget. The Legislature has responded by saying that that only kicks the can down the road, however did not comment on a more permanent solution. State Rep. Mike Tobash proposed a hybrid system of traditional pension and 401(k) styles, but many accuse that of cutting benefits to employees. PA’s pension problem is said to have come after inadequate funding from prior years.

headline: Council wants to control schools
abstract: City Council of Philadelphia has passed a nonbinding legislation that calls for the abolition of the School Reform Commission (SRC) and return of the Philadelphia School District to local control. Year after year, money is being spent with little or no improvement to show for it. City Council also amended the City’s budget to give several institutions more money for upgrades.

headline: 3rd probe possible for Veterans Affairs Pittsburgh Healthcare System
abstract: The Veterans Affairs Pittsburgh Healthcare System could be the target of a third internal investigation in two years after the waiting list for newly admitted veterans became public. The list showed that many veterans were waiting for longer than the goal set by national leadership. Allegations also came out showing that the wait lists are actually much longer than the facilities report. The scandal forced several officials to step down, including the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

headline: EDITORIAL: Pa. Legislature takes another swing at downsizing itself
abstract: The proposal of downsizing the nation’s second biggest legislature has once again come up as a new push is being made. Some have even gone farther suggesting that the Lt. Governor and several judges also be eliminated. However, there will be little benefit to downsizing if there are no reforms made to redistricting. Without reform there, the legislature will be the same as it is now, only slightly smaller.

headline: Vereb to lead Montco Republicans
abstract: PA State Rep. Mike Vereb was unanimously elected as the Chairman of the Montgomery County Republicans. Maureen Coggins was elected as Vice-Chair. Vereb is taking on his first full four-year term and is anxious to begin working on getting out the vote in November’s elections.

headline: Scarnati calls on Senate colleagues to ‘let the voters decide’ if their state government needs downsizing
abstract: State Senators chimed in on the debate over whether or not the PA State Legislature should downsize itself, cutting the Senate from 50 to 45 members. Several Republican Senators would only allow the downsizing if all three branches were affected – the Lt. Governor and several judges should also be eliminated. Democrats opposed the measure saying that the other branches are not ready to downsize and are already dealing with heavy workloads. Others argued that the voters should decide.

headline: As the budget deadline approaches, Pennsylvania Republicans are at a crossroads: Lowman S. Henry
abstract: The intra-party competition among the “establishment” and “tea party” conservatives is showing face once more as the State grapples with a budget. The debate comes down between the more moderate southeastern Republicans and the central PA Republicans. Some have proposed an extraction tax while others oppose it.

headline: Senate Transportation Committee hears testimony on accident responses
abstract: The PA Senate Transportation Committee met to hear testimony on how traffic was managed during February’s snow and freezing rain that resulted in several accidents. The Secretary of Transportation, Barry Schoh, testified that everything was handled well with the exception of not lowering speed limits at an earlier time. When pressed, the Secretary said that drivers often ignore numerous safety warnings, complicating the agency’s job.

headline: Pa. finally passes gun bill, but the wrong kind
abstract: In the wake of a shooting in Isla Vista, California and two years after the Sandy Hook shooting, the PA General Assembly has passed a gun law – designating the Long Rifle as the official firearm of Pennsylvania. Despite 74 school shootings since Sandy Hook, the PA Legislature has failed to take any steps towards preventing gun violence in PA. The Congressional Delegation, however, has voted to expand funding for the background checks service.

headline: A bad bet: GOP Governor's Assn. crossed state law with donation
abstract: Nearly $1 million has been channeled into a Political Action Committee (PAC) dedicated to reelecting Pa. Governor Tom Corbett. The money came from a casino owner, which violates PA Law stating casino owners cannot get involved with PA politics. The Republican Governor’s Association (RGA) claimed it was a mistake and that Democrats are heavily talking about it in an attempt to make the conversation anything other than Democratic challenger Tom Wolf’s record.

headline: Corbett signs legislation creating panel to develop new school funding formula
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has signed into law a commission to investigate how PA can more adequately and fairly fund its schools. PA State Rep O’Neill said that the current system is obsolete and leads to vast inequalities. The commission is very similar a special education commission with the same purpose, the recommendations of which are being considered by the PA General Assembly.

headline: Pennsylvania likely to pivot on shale tax, insiders say
abstract: Many are predicting that PA Governor Tom Corbett will concede to an extraction tax on natural gas as the PA Legislature and voters increasingly support the measure. The Governor has remained opposed to the tax, as have numerous representatives from the industry, citing a loss of jobs as the reason. Governor Corbett has also asked for liquor and pension reform before he considers anything else.

headline: Law broken in election for new Pa. House seat
abstract: In a four way race for York County’s new 169th Legislative District, Republican Marc Woerner finished third. He claimed this is the result of a smear campaign that compared him to President Obama and branded him a liar. The group, PA Taxpayers for Integrity, launched the campaign – in violation of election law. The group not being registered with the PA Department of State has prompted an investigation and possible criminal charges. All groups that spend money to influence elections must be registered with the PA Department of State.

headline: Fixing up neighborhood
abstract: The city of Farrell, Pennsylvania has received a $50,000 grant from the Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED) to “beautify neighborhoods.” The city is planning to give the money to 15 to 20 houses that are in good standing to make various repairs. The city is already close to finishing the selection process for which homes will get the money.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Faith and charity
abstract: Despite proudly advertising itself as a 501(c)3 tax exempt charitable organization, the group Peace Not Guns was uncovered to have never registered with the IRS. The Philadelphia group was founded by Councilman Kenyatta Johnson, who says he has used the group as both an organization and a concept. He claims his intentions with the modest funds he raised are pure and help people, however many have argued that that is not sufficient for lack of basic oversight.

headline: House passes bill to extend 911 surcharges on telephone customers.
abstract: The PA Legislature voted to extend a surcharge that adds $ 1 to $1.50 to consumers’ telephone bills. This money goes to helping to fund the State’s 911 emergency centers and is a temporary solution while a permanent one is made. The only dissenting vote came from PA State Rep. Daryl Metcalfe, who did not comment.

headline: Lawmakers need to pass pension reform along with the state budget: Carl T. Shaffer
abstract: Passing pension reform should be a chief concern for all Pennsylvanians as pushing the issue farther down the line can result in a serious problem for future generations. Significant property taxes could hit the State, harshly affecting farmers, as the State tries to tackle its massive $50 billion pension liability.

headline: Help agency URS closing its doors today
abstract: After 56 years of service, United Rehabilitation Services (URS) will officially be closing doors. The organization tried to help people with disabilities reach their highest possible potential. URS blames a rate reduction by the Department of Public Welfare as being responsible for the organization’s inability to continue. Its 250 clients have been organized with other service providers.

headline: Tax could triple under Act 47 plan
abstract: The City of Scranton has in the past made attempts to pass a commuter tax on nonresidents, but failed. A new PA Senate Amendment will make it even harder as it requires that any tax on nonresidents must be placed on residents as well. The goal of the plan is to make it easier for municipalities to leave Act 47, financially distressed status.

headline: Despite budget struggles, General Assembly sitting on big cash
abstract: As the State looks to face another large deficit, questions are coming up over how the reserve funds that number around $100 million will be used. Spokesmen said that the funds are used for various projects or to keep the legislature running in the event that the budget expires. Many are concerned however that the lack of an independent audit system means that more and more money is being reserved by the legislature for their own personal needs.

headline: Defenders of traditional marriage take their message to Washington.
abstract: The second annual March for Marriage, a display of support for traditional marriage in D.C., will experience a very different landscape from the prior year. The Federal Government has struck down the Defense of Marriage Act, allowing for many courts to overturn marriage bans. The marchers will now voice their opinions to the representatives and the U.S. Supreme Court in order to prevent other States from being forced to redefine marriage.

headline: Wolf’s campaign coffers show strain of four-way race.
abstract: As the PA Gubernatorial primary ends, the expenditures of the candidates reveal just how expensive a gubernatorial campaign truly is. Collectively, the Democratic challengers to incumbent PA Governor Tom Corbett spent $36.6 million on the primary with Tom Wolf investing the most – and eventually claiming the nomination. Corbett had spent around $11 million of the money he had raised.

headline: March for Marriage: Proclaiming God’s law and the Bible, thousands march in Washington to reclaim traditional marriage
abstract: Thousands marched on Washington in support of traditional marriage in the second annual March for Marriage. The crowds drew big speakers including former U.S. Senator Rick Santorum of PA and former Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee. Both said that same-sex marriage damaged the economy and was heresy. The marchers pleaded for the courts to stop overturning the will of the people and God’s law.

headline: PA-Gov. Wolf Stars in New York Times Profile Piece
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has promised to be a different kind of governor, promising a wide array of policy reforms including a 5% severance tax, reforming the tax code, and finding a fair funding formula for primary education. On top of all of this, the State is suffering from a $2 Billion deficit.

headline: Could Heinz-Kraft merger face opposition from the Federal Trade Commission?
abstract: While the Federal Trade Commission is actively trying to block the merger of food service distributors Sysco and US Foods, citing antitrust concerns, the deal that would combine Pittsburgh's H.J. Heinz Co. and Northfield, Ill.-based Kraft Foods Group is unlikely to face any opposition. The lack of concern is accredited to the lack of the elimination of a head to head competitor in the industry.

headline: Budget impasse, Wolf comments worry Pa. schools
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf said he would not give more money to school districts who are struggling in the face of the state budget impasse, adding to school officials’ growing concern for the future. School districts that receive most of their funding from the state are considering taking out additional lines of credit or other alternatives to stay in operation. According to a spokesman for Wolf, the governor’s budget would add $500 million to primary and secondary education in Pennsylvania.

headline: EDITORIAL: Major challenges ahead for Gov. Tom Wolf
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has monumental challenges facing him as he takes the office. His predecessor was unable to pass laws with a legislature under the control of his own party, so many are skeptical to Wolf’s ability to lead in a divided government.

headline: PA Gov. Tom Wolf hosts House Democrats, but not for what Republican rivals suspected
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf held an event at the Governor's mansion in Harrisburg to discuss his proposed state budget with PA state democrats. However State GOP members argued illegal campaign discussions were being conducted on  government grounds. Gov. Wolf and guests at the event denied such allegations.

headline: Third Blue Cross computer breach impacts some insured by NEPA health trust
abstract: The third computer security breach in a month at Excellus Blue Cross put public school employees at risk and could affect members of the Northeastern Pennsylvania School District Health Trust in the future. The breach occurred at Blue Cross companies located in other states, but the health trust uses the local Blue Cross for members who need medical care across state lines, which could put their personal data at risk if another security breach were to take place.

headline: Tom Wolf Does Weather Channel Interview from his Jeep
abstract: To show the effectiveness of the PA Department of Transportation’s preparedness for a winter storm, PA Gov. Tom Wolf conducted an interview on the road.

headline: Attorney General Kathleen Kane has let two of three statewide grand juries expire
abstract: If PA AG Kathleen Kane does not request an extension from PA Supreme Court Chief Justice Thomas J. Saylor, the only statewide investigative grand jury now operating in Pittsburgh, will soon expire. Kane has already allowed two statewide grand juries, one in Harrisburg and the other in Montgomery County to expire.

headline: Ethics missteps don't deter Pennsylvania ex-LCB officials
abstract: Several former officials for the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board were handed ethical violations for unlawfully accepting food, trips, and other gifts from private alcohol vendors while they were on the job. According to logs taken from the LCB’s Harrisburg Office, the officials had close relationships with vendors who visited the agency for “business matters” on more than 120 occasions.

headline: Former Office of Open Records chief sues Gov. Tom Wolf over firing
abstract: Eric Arneson was appointed by former PA Gov. Tom Corbett to be the Executive Director of the Office of Public Records in the last days of his term. Current Governor, Tom Wolf, fired Arneson believing the action was not transparent enough. Arneson has sued the Governor over whether or not he has the ability to do this.

headline: As Mayor Ed Pawlowski ponders a U.S. Senate campaign, slim challenger field awaits Pat Toomey
abstract: Democrat Joe Sestak of Philadelphia announced his desire for a rematch against Republican U.S. Sen. Pat Toomey. However, another candidate is being viewed as a viable challenger, in Allentown Mayor Ed Pawlowski. The recent legal troubles of marquee Democrats Kathleen Kane and Rob McCord have now opened up the chance for alternative party candidates to take the GOP held U.S. Senate spot.

headline: Kane's driver, Reese, transferred to narcotics unit
abstract: Patrick Reese, the former driver and head of security for PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane, was transferred to the agency’s narcotics investigation unit. Reese faces criminal charges for illegally accessing a private email server to gain information about a grand jury who was looking into Kane.

headline: Pa.'s new physician general brings an LGBT point of view
abstract: Dr. Rachel Levine, if confirmed by the Senate, will become one of few openly transgender people in government. Dr. Levine is interested in helping Wolf expand insurance under the Affordable Care Act and improve healthcare across the State.

headline: State-owned college students left waiting in battle between Gov. Wolf and Legislature
abstract: Students at Millersville University, a state funded university, await a decision from PA Gov. Tom Wolf as he works with the GOP controlled state legislature over increased funding for public higher education. The board of the PA State System of Higher Education decided in a 9-to-8 vote to freeze tuition rates at the 14 state-owned universities in exchange for more financial support from the state.

headline: Airport hangar project awaiting approvals
abstract: The construction of new hangars at an airport in Fayette County, PA is awaiting project approval from the Federal Aviation Administration and Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection. Rob Sleighter, the project engineer, told members of the county’s Airport Authority Board that high bids have been offered for construction of the hangars but alterations could be made to cut costs.

headline: Families, lawmakers 'darn optimistic' for medical marijuana legalization this year
abstract: Advocates, including the mother of Lorelei Ulrich who is a 7-year-old girl suffering from 700 seizures a day, are optimistic that 2015 will be the year that medical marijuana becomes legal in PA. With new leadership in the General Assembly and Executive Branch, many believe that medical marijuana could be a much needed early victory for the Wolf Administration.

headline: Governor Wolf appoints new chief recovery officer for York city schools
abstract: Following the resignation of the City of York's Chief Recover Officer, David Meckley, PA Gov. Tom Wolf named Dr. Carol Saylor to the position. Meckley sighted the lack of support from the Wolf administration for his plans to transition the city's schools to a charter system, as his reason for resigning.

headline: Bills seeking to reduce state debt on their way to the PA Senate
abstract: Two bills that are sponsored by PA Republicans and aim to reduce the state’s debt won approval in the House and are up in the Senate. House Bill 928 would lower the debt ceiling from about $3.5 billion to $3 billion for projects in the Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program. House Bill 930 would create annual caps on spending for RACP and Public Improvement Projects and allow unused funds for a project to be carried into the next fiscal year.

headline: Wolf vows to support Senate's medical marijuana bill
abstract: While standing before children who are suffering from debilitating diseases, PA Gov. Tom Wolf promised to support a bill to legalize medical marijuana.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf: Five things to know about his York College stop
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf visited York College to share his plans to make higher education more affordable and accessible. His visit was also accompanied by York County Republican lawmakers who responded with criticism of Gov. Wolf's plan, citing its tax increases and increase of actual cost to students paying off student loans.

headline: DePasquale's school reports used flawed methods to reach wrong conclusion
abstract: The author writes that PA Auditor General Eugene DePasquale used subjective one-year data and limited standards in his evaluation of the state Department of Education, which has been crippled by staff reductions and cannot implement DePasquale’s recommendations to help over 550 struggling schools. The author says that the report should have explored the systemic shortage of state education funding and provided different approaches to school support.

headline: Gamblers bet $26 million on slots at Erie casino
abstract: Gamblers at Presque Isle Casino in Erie, PA wagered $26 million in slots recently, a very sizable number that has neared the record set in 2010, which was 57 million.

headline: Upon further review, Wolf has a better case than it first seemed: Matt Zencey
abstract: Looking deeper into PA’s laws, it would appear that PA Gov. Tom Wolf has a stronger standing in the firing of Eric Arneson – Gov. Corbett’s last minute appointee to the Office of Open Records – than was previously believed. Several have voiced concern that the office cannot be independent if the Governor is capable of firing the Executive Director at any time. However, the legislature has failed to pass a law expressly banning such activity.

headline: It's time for Pa. Democrats to show leadership on Kane, by showing her the door: Dennis Roddy
abstract: The author condemns PA Gov. Tom Wolf and fellow PA Democrats for not forcing AG Kathleen Kane to resign, following perjury charges.

headline: Johnstown corrections center operating on month-to-month lease
abstract: The Community Corrections Center in Johnstown, PA is being leased by the state Department of Corrections on a monthly basis after the scheduled expiration of its long-term lease in October. Representative Bryan Barbin, D-Johnstown, and representatives from a dozen local businesses are calling for the center to be removed from the downtown part of the city and relocated.

headline: Man, 24, shot and killed in Harrisburg Friday night: Police
abstract: Harrisburg police are currently investigating the murder of a 24-year-old man downtown that occurred recently. The police are currently looking for any help that people can provide.

headline: Mutchler apologizes for remark about Office of Open Records' new chief counsel's qualifications
abstract: Terry Mutchler, the former executive director of the Office of Open Records, has apologized for saying that the individual Eric Arneson hired as chief counsel was underqualified. In her corrected statement, she said that the approach differs from her own, but offered praise to the new chief counsel.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: Why we need death penalty
abstract: The author expresses his opinion as to why PA should have the death penalty. He references the need to punish mass murders and extreme criminals and the use of the penalty as a bargaining chip to forego lengthy and expensive trials.

headline: If the gas industry is 'on its knees,' whose fault is that?
abstract: The author writes that an oversupply of shale in the gas industry has led to lower prices that are detrimental to the industry itself, and PA Governor Tom Wolf’s extraction tax could affect it even more.

headline: Study: In Pennsylvania, Very Rich Getting Richer, Everybody Else Getting Poorer
abstract: A new report shows that only PA’s top 1% of income earners saw an increase in their income between 2009 and 2013. Every other income bracket saw a decline of 1.1%. This trend is common across the country. PA Gov. Tom Wolf said he is excited to work with leaders of both parties to get PA’s economy moving again.

headline: Capitolwire: As Wolf presses for federal action on crude oil tankers, reports say millions in Pa in potential evacuation zones
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf is calling upon the Federal Government to step up reforms of U.S. rail lines carrying crude oil after a report was released that showed 1.5 million Pennsylvanians live in possible evacuation zones. Increased pressure on the Federal Government has come in the wake of numerous train derailments.

headline: For Pa. Senate: Elect Guy Reschenthaler
abstract: The Times Tribune Editorial Board endorsed Republican Guy Reschenthaler for PA Senate in an upcoming special election in the state’s 37th Senatorial District.

headline: 'It's a horrible way to die,' a PennLive commenter makes a persuasive case for pot legalization
abstract: Citing a long list of published researcher, a commenter on PennLive’s online poll made a compelling case for the legalization of medical marijuana.

headline: Gov. Wolf's first budget
abstract: The former Chairmen of the PA GOP and PA Democratic Party gave their thoughts on what to expect from Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s first budget. The first budget sets an agenda and tone for governance that may extend the full term, so the former officials are hoping for pragmatism and compromise over gridlock and ideology.

headline: VIDEO: Wolf comments on Attorney General Kane law license suspension, budget
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf called on Attorney General Kathleen Kane, whose law license was suspended, to resign before he possibly considers seeking forced removal from office.

headline: Obama Relents on Proposal to End '529' College Savings PLans
