abstract: Due to heightened political pressure from both sides of the aisle, U.S. President Barack Obama withdrew his plan to eliminate popular 529 College Savings Plans. The President believed they only benefited the wealthiest of Americans. While the wealthy do take in a disproportionate amount of the rewards, other incomes benefit from the program as well.

headline: If the Supreme Court does not uphold Obamacare, thousands of Pennsylvanians will suffer needlessly
abstract: Nearly 400,000 Pennsylvanians could lose health coverage should the Supreme Court of the US rule against the Affordable Care Act (ACA) in King v. Burwell. The case is challenging the notion hat Congress had intended for all Americans to receive financial assistance through the ACA.

headline: PennDOTT announces new technology to track snow plows
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will be using new technology to track snow plows and keep their operations transparent in the winter. The change is estimated to save the state $1.4 million a year.

headline: Wolf urges Democrats: Stay strong in your values
abstract: Democrats met in Philadelphia to discuss the future policy goals of the party and how to best connect with the American voters. PA Gov. Tom Wolf urged the party to stay strong and support liberal policies. President Obama and Vice-President Biden also made speeches. Officials in the DNC also toured Philadelphia as a possible host of the 2016 National Convention.

headline: Your budget word of the day? 'Increase': Tuesday Morning Coffee
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf is expected to introduce his budget that will increase revenue and expenditures. Wolf is planning to increase taxes in several areas as well as cutting the corporate tax and capital stock and franchise tax. Details on pension reform remain hidden until the formal address of the budget.

headline: State budget impasse affects Westmoreland County Food Bank
abstract: The Westmoreland County Food Bank is trying to fill a $200,000 gap in money it usually receives from the PA State Food Purchase Program but has not come due to the budget impasse. Food Bank CEO Kris Douglas said this is the worst time of year for the food bank to be low on money because of increases in shipments to food pantries during the holidays. In the meantime, the food bank plans to stretch out donations from individuals, corporations, and other organizations.

headline: New Turnpike Chairman Sean Logan Institutes Wolf's gift ban at commission
abstract: Following PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s “No Thank You” Rule, Sean Logan put a a gift ban in place for employees working with the Turnpike Commission. The University of Pittsburgh said the move was welcomed and will help to decrease instances of corruption within the agency.

headline: Wolf strips Green of SRC Chairmanship
abstract: Pa House Republicans instructed School Reform Chairman Bill Green to approve 27 charter schools as the Governor instructed Mr. Green to approve none. The vote ended up approving 5 charter schools and in less than two weeks, Pa Gov. Tom Wolf removed Green as the Chairman of the SRC. Green said he will challenge the decision in Court and House Speaker Mike Turzai found the move to be punitive.

headline: GOP congressmen call on Wolf to release federal school funds
abstract: Eight Republican congressmen sent a letter to PA Governor Tom Wolf calling on him to release hundreds of millions of dollars for education funding that has been held back by the state budget impasse. The money would go towards public school programs for poor and disabled children.

headline: Philadelphia parents and educators show support for York schools
abstract: Philadelphia parents, teachers, and community leaders went to York to protest the State’s plan to force the privatization of the city’s public schools.

headline: Wolf's budget funds 50 new environmental inspectors, but shale tax remains controversial
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget includes a number of measures to increase environmental protection in Pa, but his severance tax remains controversial. Pro-industry advocates said the severance tax would cost the state jobs and environmental groups said the tax is necessary to fund the state’s expenses. Currently, Pa has the lowest tax on natural gas drilling amongst the nation’s top producers.

headline: This is coal's legacy
abstract: A local conservation group in Greene County, PA claims that pollutants from a mine in East Bethlehem Township are poisoning a nearby river. The Izaak Walton League says that the Clyde Mine, which closed in 2000 and was abandoned, is now the site of a private water-treatment plant that is discharging acid into the river without a permit. Acid mine drainage is a common problem caused by coal companies that have historically operated the mines in Western Pennsylvania.

headline: Supporters promise 'comprehensive, strictly regulated' medical marijuana bill in Pennsylvania
abstract: With a new Governor and legislative attitudes, advocates are confident that PA will legalize medical marijuana. They’re also confident that a new version of the bill will not be as watered-down as the previous, given the new attitude in Government. PA Gov. Tom Wolf has said he would sign such a bill.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf budget: His plan for health care
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has introduced a healthcare plan that would consolidate Healthy PA’s three plans into one Medicaid option. He believes that this reduction will save the state $500 million. The administration is continuing to work out the details with federal regulators who ultimately must approve the plan. Medical professions have responded positively to the Governor’s plan.

headline: Central Pa. developer slams Wolf, Teplitz in state Senate candidacy announcement
abstract: John DiSanto, a developer from central PA who is running for state Senate, heavily criticized current Democratic Senator Rob Teplitz and Governor Tom Wolf in his candidacy announcement. The video slammed Wolf’s push for increased taxes and his veto of pension reform and liquor privatization plans. The advertisement presents DiSanto as a non-career politician who can answer to people’s problems with the state government.

headline: So far, Kenney's top appointees are a mix
abstract: Newly elected Philadelphia mayor Jim Kenney recently announced who would fill his cabinet positions. Mayor Kenney, who picked a diverse cabinet made up of men and women of different races that includes some of his most trusted advisors, hopes his new cabinet will provide exemplary service and leadership for the city, particularly in education, an area the city is struggling to make adequate. The cabinet includes political operatives with diverse backgrounds, comprised of experienced city operatives and newcomers to city government.

headline: Drilling ban in state parks get Gov. Tom Wolf praise from environmental groups
abstract: In only his second week in office, PA Gov. Tom Wolf issued an executive order protecting state parks from natural gas drilling. The move gave Wolf great praise from environmentalists across the State. The order effectively eliminates former PA Gov. Tom Corbett’s plan to expand drilling on state lands.

headline: Wolf budget: health spending soars, yet savings claimed
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s new healthcare plan is set to increase funding for services to the elderly and those with intellectual disabilities. The Governor has opted to expand Medicaid, which has the potential to save the state a significant amount of money while expanding services. Wolf has also provided funds for drug addiction.

headline: No state budget, but lawmakers continue to raise cash
abstract: Despite the PA budget stalemate, state lawmakers are still hosting events to raise money for their campaigns and show no sign of slowing down. Critics say the lobbying and fundraising events show a lack of priority and ethics in state government, while legislators say that raising money is a vital part of remaining in office at any time, even with a budget impasse in place.

headline: What a higher sales tax could mean for families
abstract: After the legislature agreed upon a sales tax hike as part of the new budget agreement, PA families are preparing for how it may impact their lives. The intent of the sales tax hike was to offset a property tax relief, but overall, due to unseen costs and intricacies, the budget restructuring will still be a net tax increase for PA families.

headline: Top legislative Republicans in Pennsylvania say when it comes to LGBT protections, they need bills
abstract: Several prominent Republicans either refused comment or did not give a position on anti-discrimination legislation for LGBT people in PA. State Sen. Mike Folmer asked how such legislation could be balanced with one’s deeply held religious belief that homosexuality is a sin. The legislators said they would take a stand when a formal piece of legislation is introduced.

headline: Gov. Wolf's state budget: Simplifying Medicaid
abstract: The largest healthcare goal of Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget is to consolidate the three plans under Healthy PA into one Medicaid expansion that could save the state $500 million.

headline: Those who come to seek elk in Pennsylvania often don't abide by public, private property
abstract: Tourists to rural areas of Pennsylvania who come seeking elk often don’t understand or ignore the separation between private and public land, which creates wildlife conflicts when they get too close to the animals, says PA Game Commission biologist Jeremy Banfield. The commission is trying to direct where people who visit elk viewing centers can and cannot go, but it is more difficult to place staff at frequented sites that are undesignated or unofficial.

headline: ESU to dispurse funding to students relying on PHEAA grants
abstract: East Stroudsburg University of PA (ESU) will start providing extra funding to students who rely on grants to go pay tuition. The School stated recently that the funds will be dispursed through the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency (PHEAA) for students who are eligible. Although pushed by the budget gridlock, the ESU administration believes that receiving an education, not paying for it, should be the priority.

headline: Gov. Wolf Signs Moratorium on Fracking On State Lands
abstract: In his third executive order, PA Gov. Tom Wolf has signed a moratorium on natural gas drilling in state parks, undoing an initiative by former PA Gov. Tom Corbett to lease state lands to gas drillers. Wolf said he was interested in natural gas drilling, but it had to be done right.

headline: Cumberland County lawmakers see problems and promise in Wolf's proposed budget
abstract: Lawmaker’s reactions to Pa Gov. Wolf’s budget are both optimistic and anxious. Republicans in the legislature are concerned about Wolf’s decision to increase government spending by 16%, though optimistic about cutting corporate taxes and lowering property taxes. Democrats called the plan bold and necessary, solving much of Pennsylvania’s budgetary concerns.

headline: DRPA OK With Losing $1.4M In Bridge Tolls During Papal Weekend
abstract: Delaware River Port Authority is fine with its loss of $1.4 million in bridge tolls while the Ben Franklin Bridge was shut down for four days during Pope Francis’s visit to Philadelphia. According to agency CEO John Hanson, DRPA is under budget in expenses and more than $8 million over budget in revenues and could afford to take the hit.

headline: Ruling gives Sandusky back $4,900-a-month Penn State pension
abstract: A PA Commonwealth court ruled unanimously recently that Jerry Sandusky, disgraced and convicted former Pennsylvania State University (PSU) football coach, must have his PSU pension reinstated on the grounds that he was not a Penn State employee when his crimes were committed. The state pension board originally revoked his pension in October 2012 after Sandusky was convicted of 45 counts of sexual offenses towards children at his football camp. The commonwealth court stated that the law is resolute, and should be free of media and outside pressures.

headline: Is Gov. Wolf brave or brazen
abstract: After former Pa Gov. Tom Corbett choice to appoint Eric Arneson to the Office of Open Records, a man with deep ties to the Republican Party, current Pa Gov. Tom Wolf fired Arneson. In an attempt to uphold integrity, Wolf justified the firing and claimed that Arneson was at will employee, thus able to be fired at any time. Some groups questioned the precedent of allowing the Governor to fire the Director of the Office of Open Records and what kind of impact that would have on the office’s integrity.

headline: Local lawmakers question Wolf's budget plan
abstract: State Sen. Pat Stefano and Rep. Ryan Warner spoke of concerns with Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget. They both believe that this is the time for government to be living within its means and cutting expenditures, not proposing the largest spending plan in history. Wolf’s budget includes raising the sales and income tax to fund education as well as placing a tax on natural gas extraction. Wolf also wants to significantly slash the business tax. Both lawmakers foresee an uphill battle.

headline: In judging judges, throw back the red herrings
abstract: The author calls on Pennsylvania citizens to ignore the propaganda and negative advertisements that often surround candidates who are running for seats on the state’s various court levels; instead, we should evaluate judges based on our knowledge of them and the character they display during their campaigns.

headline: Pennsylvania Treasurer Rob McCord resigns amid possible federal inquiry
abstract: In the midst of a federal probe into the campaign financing tactics of former PA Treasurer Rob McCord, Mr. McCord resigned from his position. Mr. McCord claimed he did not have an interest in another elected office and that he’d rather return to the private sector. News of the federal probe had many Democrats in shock.

headline: Impact fees garner support from state community leaders
abstract: Community leaders went to Harrisburg to discuss the potential impacts of Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s severance tax on natural gas. Wolf promised to maintain funds coming from impact fees to counties, but many officials were concerned that the new tax would scare off growth in the industry. They warned that the industry is already scaling back its operations and that if the industry’s growth stalled, it would cripple the state.

headline: Letter to the Editor: From where will state's Republican lawmakers pull more revenue?
abstract: The author questions how PA Republicans will bring in more revenue after the GOP-controlled House rejected Governor Tom Wolf’s budget, which proposed an increased personal income tax. He criticizes the party for not asking the rich to pay higher taxes.

headline: York City School officials, politicians rally for district
abstract: Several officials in the York Area are gathering in support of the school district and to stop legislators from privatizing the district. Gov. Wolf called upon the York County Delegation to discuss a plan. Although no decision has yet been made, local leaders are optimistic in Gov. Wolf’s ability to help them.

headline: Wolf wants more money, tuition freezes for state schools
abstract: After years of flat or declining budgets, schools were happy to hear that Pa Gov. Tom Wolf proposed large funding increases for the state’s universities. Wolf proposed an 11% increase to the state system and $81 million to the state related universities. However, Wolf also asked that with this money, the universities must promise to not increase tuition or keep the increases low.

headline: Expert: Race still a factor in school discipline
abstract: Members of the Pittsburgh public school community gathered at the University of Pittsburgh for a lecture given by Russell Skiba, an Indiana University professor and co-author of a study that examines the effect of race in disciplinary practices at schools. Skiba emphasized the importance of discussing race relations and he said research has shown that black students receive different treatment than white students and are disciplined more for subjective examples of “bad behavior.”

headline: Obama exhorts Democrats to 'stand up,' mocks GOP on economy
abstract: Despite an election that gave Republicans the largest U.S. House majority in 80 years, President Barack Obama urged the Democratic Party to remain strong on its ideals.

headline: Governor Wolf Calls For Tuition Freeze
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has proposed a restoration of 50% of what his predecessor cut from higher education. The money comes with a catch that universities cannot impose tuition increases. Penn State University has stated that its tuition increases are entirely the fault of decreasing appropriations from the State.

headline: Get ready for a mudbath in judicial race advertising
abstract: The race for three vacant seats on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court has adopted an ugly tone as negative advertisements that attack many of the candidates are regularly aired on TV by independent expenditure groups. The state Republican and Democratic parties are facing off for control of the court.

headline: The State Office of Open Records must remain independent: Michael Berry
abstract: The Pennsylvania Freedom of Information Coalition has urged PA Gov. Tom Wolf to reconsider his decision to fire Eric Arneson as executive director of the Office of Open Records so that the independence of the office could be maintained. If the executive director is an at will employee, it diminishes the role of the office.

headline: How Tom Wolf's budget could fill (and empty) your wallet: 5 highlights
abstract: Wolf has proposed a 20% increase in the personal income tax as well as property tax relief paid for by increasing the sales tax. Wolf has also suggested raising the minimum wage to $10.10/hr. Higher Education is also going to receive a large increase in the hopes of keeping tuition down. Wolf is also working on pension and liquor reform designed to bring down costs.

headline: What new building inspection guidelines?
abstract: An analysis of Philadelphia’s Department of Licenses and Inspections revealed that the agency did not follow new building inspection guidelines in 80 percent of its demolition cases since January. The agency’s database also contained false information about demolitions that never occurred and inspections that were incomplete or nonexistent.

headline: State Shield Law needs to remain strong
abstract: PA State Rep. Rob Matzie writes in support of keeping the State Shield Laws strong in response to a move to weaken them as a result of the alleged grand jury leaks by Attorney General Kathleen Kane. Rep. Matzie said if the law is not strong, it is a fundamental breech of freedom of press.

headline: Wolf wields tax, not az, in bold new course for budget
abstract: In Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s new budget, he is proposing a number of new taxes to pay for increases in services cut by his predecessor. Among them, Wolf has called for an income tax and sales tax increase. The sales tax will be used to reduce property taxes. A severance ta on natural drilling will help to pay for historic new funding for education. Along with a number of other initiatives, Wolf is committed ot pension and liquor reform.

headline: PennDOT announced new technology for 700 plow trucks that will help them better do their job
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PENNDot) will use new technology introduced by Governor Tom Wolf that will allow it to track snow plows more effectively, save money, and increase efficiency.

headline: McCord to plead guilty to federal charges from campaign fundraising
abstract: PA State Treasurer Rob McCord has plead guilty to illegally obtaining campaign funds by use of his office to threaten donors. McCord threatened that if they did not donate, they would have a hard time getting state contracts. McCord immediately resigned upon questioning from federal investigators.

headline: What's actually in Gov. Tom Wolf's budget?
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget includes nearly $4 Billion in tax increases, but also several areas of tax relief. Gov. Wolf has planned to increase funding to education by using a severance tax. Legislative leaders have criticized the budget saying that it does not live in reality, thus complicating negotiations.

headline: Multiple bills to legalize medical marijuana are already in the state house
abstract: Several bills to decriminalize possession of marijuana and legalize medical use of the drug are up in the PA House of Representatives. Governor Tom Wolf said he would sign the bills if they pass through the legislature.

headline: EDITORIAL: Tax-exempt expansion could cause problems for Pa. towns
abstract: A proposed amendment to the PA Constitution would remove the process of judicial review from determining whether or not a service qualifies as tax exempt and leaves it solely up to the legislature. This could have problematic effects, such as limiting checks and balances system and hurting financially distressed cities across PA.

headline: Gov. Wolf Wants to Cut Business Tax
abstract: A few days after Florida Gov. Rick Scott tried to woo business away from Pa, Gov. Tom Wolf has proposed cutting the business tax by more than half.

headline: State medical society against bill to legalize medical marijuana
abstract: The Pennsylvania Medical Society opposed a current House bill to legalize medical marijuana on the basis of uncertainty about its safety and effectiveness. This prompted Republican Senator Mike Fulmer, the sponsor of the bill, to respond in defense of the legislation.

headline: Act 89 funding to aid ailing highways
abstract: Act 89 stands to generate $2 Billion annually by 2018 to be used to fund transportation projects in Pa. Already, the bill has helped the Pa Dept. of Transportation, PennDOT, to fix numerous paving problems throughout the State. Several major projects are under way due to the bill’s new funding sources, including repairs to 11 bridges. Overall, the bill gave PennDOT a flexibility it has not seen in a decade.

headline: Retired educators may be answer to substitute teacher shortage
abstract: Many Pennsylvania school officials and lawmakers support the idea of allowing retired teachers to work as substitutes for a certain number of days each year while still keeping their pension benefits. This would fix the state’s shortage of substitute school teachers and change the current strict guidelines for retired teachers who want or need to return to work.

headline: Robert Morris University poll shows Governor Wolf in good standing
abstract: A recent poll shows that Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s approval ratings are in his favor, but this is likely to decline as his administration continues. The trend observed in recent decades is that an incumbent experiences high marks early on in a “honeymoon” period.

headline: Penalties could motivate more Affordable Care Act signups
abstract: Supporters of the federal Affordable Care Act are hoping that rising fees and hospital costs for the uninsured will convince members of the coveted 18- to 34-year-old demographic to sign up for health insurance plans.

headline: UPDATED: Ground control to Major Tom: Your tax plan's weird, there's something wrong
abstract: The author gave initial hesitation over the tax increases proposed in Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget based on leaks in the days before his actual budget address. However, after hearing the address, the author is more supportive of the budget. The sales tax increase concerned the author because it has the potential to harm small business and the poor.

headline: PA Dems name new executive director
abstract: The Pennsylvania Democratic Party named Sincere Harris as its new executive director. Harris worked on President Obama’s re-election campaign and held a variety of positions with Governor Tom Wolf throughout his campaign and after he entered office.

headline: Republicans come out against Governor Wolf raising Personal Income Tax
abstract: Even before the Governor’s address, several Republicans are coming out against the tax initiative. Particularly, Republicans oppose the income tax increases, but are supportive of decreasing the business tax – which the Governor may propose. Republicans have filed three bills designed to help simplify the tax code and aid in the growth of small business.

headline: Senator Costa says he doesn't think a major tax hike will be part of a final budget deal
abstract: Democratic PA Senator Dom Costa said he does not believe a large tax hike will be included in the state’s final budget, but the fiscal situation still needs to be improved and agreed upon by Governor Tom Wolf and Republican lawmakers.

headline: Minimum wage needs to go up
abstract: Wal-Mart recently announced increasing its bottom wage from $7.25/hr to $10/hr in large part due to a nationwide effort that resulted in 29 states increasing their minimum wage. The CEO, Doug McMillon said that he is confident that the increased wages of his employees will increase satisfaction, decrease turnover, and overall be beneficial to the company.

headline: Heroin Overdose Reversal Drug To Be Available Across PA
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf issued an order for heroin overdose reversal drug naloxone to be made available at all state pharmacies, in an effort to combat heroin- and opioid-related deaths.

headline: Wolf's budget looks to be big, bold - and controversial
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget promises to be highly controversial. Facing nearly $2 billion in deficits and promising $1 billion in new education funding means that a number of large tax increases will likely follow. Among the tax increases could be the income tax, sales tax, and severance tax on natural drilling.

headline: Budget Veto Upheld
abstract: The PA Senate voted to sustain Governor Tom Wolf’s veto of a short-term state spending plan that was pushed by Republican lawmakers.

headline: AG Kane's spokesman leaving after 2 months on the job
abstract: Citing homesickness, Aaron Sadler announced he would be leaving Pa. Attorney General Kathleen Kane’s office only two months into his job. Sadler was proud of the team she assembled and enjoyed the work, but could not adjust to life in Pa.

headline: DN Editorial: Scary Precedent
abstract: The Daily News Editorial Board wrote that it is opposed to the PA Senate’s creation of a committee and a probable vote to decide whether Attorney General Kathleen Kane should be removed from office. The Board said that the move could set a precedent for future cases involving elected officials whose fate could be decided by the Senate instead of their peers or PA voters.

headline: Wolf's $30B budget: 'Bold' blueprint or dead on arrival?
abstract: GOP leaders declared Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget to be dead on arrival, while Democrats cheered it as new and innovative. The budget calls for a near 16% increase in spending over the previous year, pumping $1B into education. The budget also calls for an increase in the income tax, sales tax, a severance tax, and property tax relief.

headline: Pennsylvania's unemployment edges upward to 5.3 percent
abstract: The statewide unemployment rate was 5.3 percent in September and the same for the Pittsburgh area. The city’s workforce remained at a flat 1.2 million for the month and unemployment rates for nearby counties varied, as employers cut fewer jobs and fewer people left the workforce.

headline: Capitolwire: Wolf proposes a $33.8 Billion budget, higher taxes, increased spending, property tax cut
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has proposed a state budget that includes a 16.6% increase in spending, which has received criticism from GOP leaders. Wolf’s plan includes increasing the sales tax, income tax, adding a severance tax and lowering property taxes. Wolf has also pledged $1B to education. GOP Leaders said the budget was not realistic and dead on arrival. Democrats appeared thrilled and called the budget a step in the right direction.

headline: EPA proposes to expand Toxic Release Inventory by adding emissions from oil and gas facilities
abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has proposed expanding its Toxics Release Inventory by requiring oil and gas processing facilities to join other industries in publicly reporting the names and amounts of their chemical emissions. The expansion would affect three facilities in western PA and over half of the existing plants around the nation.

headline: Sestak begins run - literally - amid tepid party backing
abstract: Despite the wishes of the national party, former Admiral and Congressman Joe Sestak has declared he is running for Senate for a second time against Pa Senator Pat Toomey. Sestak began his campaign by walking 422 miles across Pa to meet voters and get his message across. The national party has looked for potential challengers, but so far only Sestak is in the race.

headline: More LCB nonsense: Too opaque still
abstract: The author criticizes the chairman and two members of Pennsylvania’s Liquor Control Board for hiding records that contained information about vendors and a former employee. The author says the records should have been made public under the Right to Know Law and calls for those involved to be fired.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf reverses tax increase on liquefied natural gas
abstract: Leaders in Lebanon County were happy to see Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s pledge of an additional $1B in education funding in his budget. School District leaders stated that any extra help would go a long way to recover from years of stagnation or decreases. Superintendent Phil Domencic took a more cautious tone, stating that the budget still needs to pass the legislature.

headline: Commonwealth Court won't intervene in York County driver's license suspension snafu
abstract: A PA Commonwealth Court panel rejected a lawsuit filed by York County residents who sought to void belated suspensions of their driver’s licenses that occurred years after they were convicted of crimes. An estimated 5,000 people in the county had criminal convictions that were not properly reported to PennDOT between 2004 and 2009, only to have their licenses suspended in 2014.

headline: Wolf's budget boosts education funding
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf proposed a budget that could significantly impact the funding of schools. He wants to raise the state’s role in funding schools from it’s current 33% to 50%. He has also introduced new funding for community colleges, special education, and relief to high-poverty, high-tax districts. Overall, the goal of the budget is to restore $1B cut by his predecessor.

headline: Pa. Supreme Court defers email probe to ethics panel
abstract: The PA Supreme Court deferred the investigation of email scandal involving Justice Michael Eakin to the state Judicial Conduct Board. A law firm hired by the state said the Conduct Board has special expertise to look into the ethics of the matter and determine whether Eakin broke any official rules by sending racist and sexist emails and circulating them among other public officials.

headline: The Wolf Agenda: Coddling unions
abstract: Despite Pa Gov. Ed Rendell abandoning a similar effect due to court order, Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf has issued an executive order that has unionized a select number of health care employees. The author posits that this is the result of a union’s donation of $1 million to the Governor’s campaign. This move would make some, who are not willing to join unions, forced to do so.

headline: A new poll shows support for Governor Tom Wolf is falling
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf is growing more unpopular with citizens in recent opinion polls, mainly due to the state budget impasse that is costing tax payers money.

headline: 'One of the best' is slain while stopping a robbery
abstract: After a shootout at a GameStop, Philadelphia Police Officer Robert Wilson III died from gunshot wounds while being treated in Temple University Hospital. Wilson’s partner, Damien Stevenson, subdued the suspects and brought them into custody. Family and friends described Wilson as a kind man who was always friendly.

headline: McKeesport Area School District may have to borrow further funds, cut programming
abstract: In light of the state budget impasse, McKeesport Area School District has taken out a $5 million line of credit and might have to borrow further funds or discontinue programs to stay in operation, according to Superintendent Rula Skezas. The Allegheny County district receives a quarter of its school budget from the state and is currently not receiving any federal money.

headline: Public Utility Commission fines Uber $50 million for defying regulators’ authority
abstract: Ride-Sharing company Uber is facing heavy controversy and possibly a much heavier fine after operating without a license in Pittsburgh since 2014. A pair of PA judges have recommended a $50 million dollar fine after the ride sharing company started operations in PA without approval and licenses from the appropriate PA state offices, such as the Pennsylvania Utilities Commision (PUC). While mindful of the beneficial services provided by the company, the judges stated that the company remains in violation of a court order, for which the judges base their heavy fine upon.

headline: House Republicans see more positives to Gov. Wolf's pension proposal
abstract: Pa Republicans praised aspects of Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s pension plan, but uniformly agreed the plan did not go far enough to solve the problem. The Gov. proposed borrowing $3B to refinance some of the unfunded liability with a debt service of $185M a year. Other proposals from Republican lawmakers included giving the assets to a third party.

headline: Hiring of a state meteorologist draws stormy response
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf is receiving criticism from Republican lawmakers for hiring the state’s first emergency-based meteorologist in the midst of the ongoing budget impasse. Lawmakers questioned the justification of creating such a specific position with a $62,000 annual salary in the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency when the state is already running on a limited budget.

headline: Pennsylvania casinos score first-round knock-out of tavern owners, clubs in gambling expansion debate
abstract: In a groundbreaking vote, the PA Gaming Oversight Commission has decided to expand gambling in the state to a level not seen since the Rendell era. The approved bill, if enacted, would legalize internet gambling, expand slot machines across the state, including being installed in the state's six airports, increase license fees, and allow casinos to serve alcohol 24 hours a day. The board also voted down a proposition to allow small bars, fraternal organizations, and private clubs to have up to five gaming machines in their businesses. Proponents of the defeated proposal cite that while the state expands gambling profits for the larger, mutli-state, and multi-national casino companies, the smaller businesses will be left behind.

headline: Editorial: Who will meet Gov. Wolf's challenge
abstract: In Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s first budget address, he called for compromise and robust conversation in order to gain the best budget possible for Pa. However, after the delivery of the address, Republicans and Democrats moved into predictable talking points, says the author. Republicans called the budget a “pie in the sky” and Democrats called it “bold and innovative.”

headline: Peters teachers strike after negotiations break down
abstract: Unionized teachers in the Peters Township School District walked out after several failed contract negotiation sessions with the district.  The teachers have been working without a contract since the end of August and are calling for salary increases and changes to class size and the length of the workday. They are expected to be on strike for about a month; classes will be cancelled in the meantime.

headline: Travel cheap and fast to Florida
abstract: Budget airline "Allegiant" has recently decided to start offering affordable flights from Pittsburgh to Orlando's smaller airport, Sanford international. The airport, which is a municipal airport much like the one in Harrisburg, PA, offers wildly more affordable travel to Orlando's theme parks, although the airport is significantly further away, requiring a rental car.

headline: Pa. budget debate could mean long, hot summer for lawmakers
abstract: While there are certain aspects of Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget proposal that the GOP supports, most will not consider a budget that increases spending by 16% as a legitimate starting point. GOP leaders support decreasing property taxes, but not by raising other taxes. They want liquor privatization and meaningful pension reform.

headline: Philadelphia reaping benefits of gas boom
abstract: Philadelphia has emerged as a center of activity for the natural gas industry. The city’s status as the second-largest petrochemical site in the U.S. was mentioned during part of a two-day Natural Gas Utilization Conference that took place downtown. Two large pipeline projects are currently underway that, when finished, will likely transport thousands of barrels of liquid gas near the city and throughout Pennsylvania.

headline: Why Pa. will continue accepting Syrian refugees
abstract: In an op-ed, PA Governor Tom Wolf provides a salient retort to the opposition of his plan to continue actively accepting refugees from the Syrian civil war into PA. In his letter, the Governor reassures those who are fearful of their safety in the face of admitting more refugees, while also clarifying that the states do not have express control over refugee policy in their states. Regardless of this fact, citing PA's rich history of being a safe haven, Wolf asserts that he will never put Pennsylvanians at risk, and will continue to oversee the safe and structured resettlement of refugees in the commonwealth.

headline: Education a big winner under Wolf's proposed budget
abstract: Schools around the Lehigh Valley are poised to receive a much larger portion of state dollars under Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s proposed budget. The Gov. proposed increasing the state’s share of school funding from 33% to 50% and pay for it by means of lower property taxes in favor of increases to the sales and income tax as well as a natural gas severance tax. This is all in an effort to restore $1B cut to districts by his predecessor.

headline: Legislation seeks to close domestic violence loophole
abstract: PA Representative Becky Corbin introduced House Bill 1581, which would make strangulation a state felony and classify it with other serious domestic violence tactics used by abusers. Organizers from The Pennsylvania Coalition Against Domestic Violence, two district attorneys, and other legislators were present in support of the legislation.

headline: Why are liquor stores essential, but not child protection? | Guest column
abstract: As the budget impasse rolls on, many Pennsylvanians are wondering why the legislators are placing certain policy as priorities over others, such as liquor reform, instead of child protective services. As PA Governor Tom Wolf has taken child protective services off the funding agenda, putting it behind liquor reform, state park operations, and lottery operations, his priorities are being questioned. The author of this editorial asserts that while the passing the budget is important for all state funding, it is important to not forget what matters most.

headline: Alle-Kiski Valley lawmakers split on $30B Wolf Budget
abstract: Similar to the General Assembly, lawmakers from Alle-Kiski Valley are split on party lines concerning Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget. Increases to the state sales tax and income tax, as well as a 5% severance tax will help to close a $2B deficit, add $1B to schools and pay for sweeping property tax cuts. Democrats call the plan bold and innovative, Republicans call it irresponsible and full of false promises.

headline: Governor Wolf approved a state-wide standing order for Naloxone
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf approved state Physician General Rachel Levine’s prescription for Naloxone. The medicine, used to help people suffering from drug addiction, will be available in pharmacies statewide.

headline: Appoint Eakin investigator
abstract: As the Justice system of Pennsylvania remains wrought in scandal, ranging from the perjured PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane, to the technological debauchery of some of the supreme court justices, the author of this editorial states that the investigation of one of those justices should be done independently, as to avoid further scandal.

headline: Here's a look at how Wolf's tax-raising proposals would impact your budget
abstract: The author helped to break down the impact of the proposed tax increases under Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s new budget by showing how some common items’ price will change. Overall, the increase to the sales and income tax means that Pennsylvanians will be paying higher prices on goods and a larger percentage of their paychecks.

headline: Some may skip PA political rite if budget talk drags on
abstract: Several PA lawmakers are considering skipping the annual Pennsylvania Society gala event, which is hosted in New York and attended by top politicians, if the state does not have a budget by December.

headline: Chaput urges Catholics to lobby Wolf on tax credits
abstract: The archbishop of Philadelphia recently called upon catholics in the archdiocese and across the commonwealth to lobby PA Governor Tom Wolf to release letters of approval for tax credits that would allow low-income students to receive scholarships to attend catholic schools. As the deadline for approval approaches, some believe that Wolf is using the tax credits as leverage for his own policy desires in the budget, but a spokeswoman for the administration asserts that it is not the case.

headline: Wolf defends budget, says he's solving decades-old problems
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf defended his budget by saying that it is solving a number of fiscal problems that have been facing PA for decades. Wolf told Republicans to talk to their constituents about how the budget will help them. Democrats remained ardently supportive of the Governor’s budget.

headline: Wolf must compromise to pass budget, save schools
abstract: The Pitt News Editorial Board called on PA Governor Tom Wolf to work with Republican legislators to create and pass a state budget as soon as possible. The Board says compromise from both political parties is the only way to save schools that are deeply in debt and struggling to stay open.

headline: COLA denied for York County pensioners
abstract: Retired county employees in York County, PA, were again denied a cost of living adjustment for their pensions. The adjustment, which would be determined by the Consumer Price Index, was denied because of the "nearly impossible" pricetag of the adjustment, 11.3 Million dollars funded at 100%. While negotiations are in the works, officials in charge of the pensions are hopeful that an adjustment will come in 2017.

headline: Pension storm: State officials must reform an ever-costly system
abstract: Pa Auditor General Eugene DePasquale warned that hundreds of municipalities across PA collectively have $8B in unfunded pension liabilities. That liability has the potential to bankrupt many municipalities that will ultimately fall on the State and taxpayers to solve. Pa Gov. Tom Wolf suggested that the legislature must do more and remove costly contracts with Wall Street.

headline: Thackston Charter afloat due to Wagner loan
abstract: PA Republican senator Scott Wagner loaned nearly half a million dollars to Helen Thackston Charter School to keep it running as the state budget crisis continues. Wagner’s loan covered two weeks of missed payroll for employees, utilities, and insurance costs; the school will need an estimated $800,000 to cover costs for the rest of the year if a budget is not passed.

headline: As we argue over whether to deny it to others, 16 in Gettysburg embrace the American dream: John L. Micek
abstract: As many in the Commonwealth and across America call for the government to close its borders to those fleeing civil war and terrorism and Syria, a citizenship ceremony at Gettysburg college for 16 new citizens, many of whom were fleeing similar situations in Islamic majority countries, feels especially visceral. Even though the political climate seems to be full of blinded calls for immigration halts due to safety threats, these new inductees to the American dream could not be happier to start a new, peaceful life in the United States. As the author of this editorial sums up in his reactions from the ceremony, these immigrants have inspired a newfound faith in the American promise.

headline: Budget reforms raise hope for end to 'guessing game'
abstract: After four years of flat lining or cuts, school administers looked upon Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s plan with optimism and caution. Their caution comes from concerns over whether or not the proposed increases – including the first increase to special education in 10 years – will not pass the legislature. Administrators are also hoping that a fair funding formula takes shape so that funding will not depend on the legislature’s decisions moving forward.

headline: Push under way to help low-income Pa. residents cope with winter bills
abstract: PA’s Public Utility Commission is leading a push to help low-income state residents plan in advance for winter gas and electric bills. Despite the budget impasse, the federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program in Pennsylvania is still fully funded and expected to distribute hundreds of millions of dollars in aid to poor households across the state.

headline: Governor Wolf says he supports continuing to host Syrian refugees in Pennsylvania
abstract: Amidst a chain of state governors declaring that they will close their borders to Syrian refugees, PA Governor Tom Wolf has stated that he supports the continued integration of Syrian refugees into the commonwealth.

headline: How do Gov. Wolf's Pennsylvania tax rates stack up against other states?
abstract: While Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s proposed tax rates would solidify Pa as one of the states that taxes its residents at a higher rate, the rates are not too out of line with other States. Adjusting for the cost of living, Pa is ranked as the 18th most heavily taxed state in the nation.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Appoint special prosecutor in court email scandal
abstract: Ronald Castille, former Chief Justice of Philadelphia, wrote an article calling for a special prosecutor to be appointed in the sexually explicit email scandal involving the Office of the Attorney General, the Judicial Conduct Board, and the State Supreme Court. Castille says that the public has a right to know every detail of the controversy, and the appointment of an independent lawyer to look into all three institutions would be the most effective way to do so.

headline: Officials in Luzerne County debated borrowing $20 million to fund agencies during
abstract: Due to the budget stalemate in Harrisburg, Luzerne County officials are debating ways to make ends meet, including borrowing $20 Million in private money to insure that government services continue and lay-offs can be avoided.

headline: Pennsylvania board brews up broader beer sales rules
abstract: Beer distributors, which have been asking for a long time to sell beer in qualities smaller than a case, got that permission by surprise when the PA Liquor Control Board announced that they could sell 12-packs so long as it contained more than 128 fluid ounces. Pa Gov. Tom Wolf called the decision a right step towards modernization, while others raised concern about circumventing the legislature.

headline: Franklin & Marshall poll shows that voters are losing faith in Harrisburg
abstract: A poll from the university shows that growing numbers PA voters believe that state lawmakers and Governor Tom Wolf are to blame for the budget crisis.

headline: Visiting Nurses Association celebrates 50th anniversary
abstract: Many Western Pennsylvanians have trusted the Visiting Nurses Association (VNA) of Western PA for in-home medical help for 50 years now, and the beloved non-profit is celebrating half a century of improving lives. Members of the VNA perform in-home occupational therapy, hospice care, rehabilitation, and other medical services. The VNA, formed in 1965 by a group of community-minded doctors and nurses, is looking forward to another 50 years of improving the lives of Western Pennsylvanians.

headline: Ruth Ann Dailey: Wolf's tax plan is a camel's nose in the tent
abstract: The author puts forward that even if former Pa Gov. Tom Corbett’s approach to budgeting was wrong, it does not mean that current Gov. Tom Wolf’s is correct. She warns of the increased taxes disproportionately harming the poor and small businesses. The only thing that can be agreed by both sides is that taxes are set to increase in PA.

headline: Small beer: This counts as change from the LCB
abstract: A small change to beer sales came as several distributors asked the PA Liquor Control Board to legally define “a case.” The legal interpretation was looser than expected, which allowed distributors to begin selling 12-packs of beer.

headline: Wolf on increased school spending: 'This is what the people want.'
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf traveled to Allentown School District to see the conditions of the school as well as make a stronger case for his recent budget. Lawmakers in the area were confident that some increases would come but the budget would most likely be a compromise budget. The Commonwealth Foundation warned there was not enough interest in a large tax increase to pay for the Governor’s budget.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf backs off campaign tax plan
abstract: During the campaign, Pa Gov. Tom Wolf promised to offer tax breaks to the lower income earners in PA as well as move the state toward a progressive income tax. In the Gov.’s budget, he moved away from those goals and instead proposed increasing the income tax in favor of decreases to property taxes.

headline: You'll soon be able to buy 12-packs at your local beer distributor
abstract: By a new decision from the Pa Liquor Control Board, beer distributors will be bale to sell 12-packs as long as it contains more than 128 ounces.

headline: PennLive got it wrong - the Court's decision in Harrisburg gun case was the right call: Richard Alloway
abstract: The author criticized municipalities that are going to court to defend gun ordinances that conflict with state law. By means of a new law, gun ordinances cannot go farther than that of the State. This has resulted in a number of lawsuits against municipalities with stronger restrictions. The author believes that municipalities that are fighting these cases are simply wasting the taxpayers’ money.

headline: Analyst: Taxes will be difficult issue for Wolf budget
abstract: Political Scientist G. Terry Madonna said that during the 2014 gubernatorial election, education was the top issue with voters wanting the $1B in cuts restored. However, voters by a large majority said they do not want to pay more taxes. Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf now has the difficult task of funding education without major tax hikes.

headline: Pennsylvania county jails turning away from immigration role
abstract: Following court decisions, Pennsylvania county jails are beginning to refuse to hold detainees accused of being in the country illegally unless given an exact order from a federal judge. Immigrant advocacy groups say that the system often prevents people from having the option to be in the country legally, usually being arrested for crimes out of their control.

headline: The business answer to water quality and conservation: defining the 'water economy'
abstract: Pittsburgh's water sources are linked to industrial growth, feeding power plants, and manufacturing. The water sector has recently paved the way in creating innovative ways to better use, clean, and conserve water.

headline: Capitolwire: Lawmakers talk taxes during Monday's IFO, Revenue Department budget hearings
abstract: The House Appropriations committee met to discuss the budget presented by Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf, specifically his severance tax and changes to the sales and income tax. The Republicans on the committee believed that the $1B promised by the severance tax will not actually come to fruition. They also believed that the income and sales tax increase to decrease property taxes still puts a higher tax burden on citizens and is not a well thought out plan.

headline: Lawmakers keep striking out on pensions - when will they get a clue?: Stephen Herzenberg
abstract: Citing the failure in other states, the author criticized lawmakers who want to put Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget on hold until pension reform can be included. Many lawmakers want to switch to a 401(k) style system for new employees. The author suggests that Pa’s pension system is adequate, but the legislature has routinely failed to fund it at appropriate levels – creating a debt problem.

headline: Warring budget figures mount in PA spending talks
abstract: The budget proposed by Pa Gov. Tom Wolf is about a week old and has legislators arguing about the numbers. The Independent Fiscal Office estimates the $2.3B deficit is probably closer to $1.5B or $1.6B. Republicans said this is reason enough to not bring in numerous tax hikes, but Democrats argue that the numbers aren’t as important as the overall structural deficit that Pa is facing.

headline: AG's office makes case for Kathleen Kane's continued leadeship
abstract: Two petitions have been filed before the Supreme Court regarding Attorney General Kathleen Kane's leadership with a temporary suspension that has been in place since October. The suspension has led to many legal challenges to Kane and her office's authority to oversee cases.

headline: Pension issue a big concern for state's fiscal watchdog
abstract: PA Auditor General Eugene DePasquale testified that if the legislature did not enact meaningful pension reform, several municipalities across the state could face a Detroit-like bankruptcy. DePasquale advocated to remove pensions from the collective bargaining process. The Governor said he will work on the issue after things in his administration settle down.

headline: School funding lawsuit is 'like Groundhog Day' movie, state officials say
abstract: Seven school districts have sued the governor, secretary of education, legislative leaders, and the State Board of Education for not providing a constitutionally mandated “thorough and efficient” education system. The case was thrown out due to the fact courts could not produce a definition of “thorough and efficient.” The Attorney General’s Office said that the debate should remain in the legislature.

headline: Three state reps caught making deals, accepting bribes in more than 20 different recordings, charing documents say
abstract: Recorded conversations detail a cash payment in exchange for insider information between three state representatives and an informant. PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane dropped the charges saying the investigation was flawed, however District Attorney Anthony Williams took up the case and brought charges against six current and former representatives.

headline: Wolf's 'gigantic' tax package goes under the microscope during House budget hearing
abstract: In a hearing, House Republicans were worried that only reducing property taxes gives no guarantee to the taxpayer that they will not return to their current level at some point in the future. Republicans were also against the majority of PA Gov. Wolf’s tax increases. Democrats argued that the taxes restore funding to crucial areas of the state.

headline: Wolf's plan to increase taxes raises concerns
abstract: The author remains optimistic in PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s ability to keep campaign promises, but is concerned about the overall impact of the proposed tax increases. He states that the increases will adversely affect PA’s middle and lower classes, even if education is funded at a higher level again.

headline: Wolf's budget plan 'a lot of smoke, mirrors and confusion,' lawmaker says
abstract: Pa lawmakers are responding to Gov. Wolf’s budget by claiming that the tax relief offered is far outweighed by the increases he’s proposing. Conservative leaders are stating that raising the income and sales tax in this climate is not good for PA.

headline: North Xtra: Avonworth boys basketball headed in right direction
abstract: Avonworth's basketball team is tied with Aliquippa for first place in section 5-AA.

headline: York County school districts apprehensive about reality of Gov. Wolf's budget
abstract: Superintendents in York County received a letter from Senate Republicans informing them that PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget does not have the necessary votes, and thus to budget ‘conservatively.’ School Districts across the state are stuck in a guessing game to determine what level of funding they will receive from the state, which severely complicates the process.

headline: State releases detailed Medicaid expansion timeline
abstract: The PA Dept. of Human Services released a new and comprehensive timeline for the State’s Medicaid expansion by means of HealthChoices PA. The remaining phases of the plan will be implemented by Sep. 30. The department is looking forward to a streamlined and more cost efficient program that expands care to more eligible families.

headline: Green Won't Challenge Wolf's SRC Decision
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf decided to remove the School Reform Commission (SRC) Chairman Bill Green a week after several new charters were approved in Philadelphia. Mr. Green said he will not challenge as to whether or not the Gov. overstepped his authority in order to ensure that “harmony prevails” and the school district can continue to grow.

headline: Council sets late hearing date on tax increase
abstract: Controversy has emerged over Philadelphia City Council President Darrell Clarke decided to delay debate on property tax increases to fund schools until after the May primaries. The hearings are taking place later than usual and have been criticized as being problematic for voters. Paul Steinke and Helen Gym, two candidates for Council, have said that voters deserve to know where their Councilmembers stand on this issue before voting.

headline: Wolf visits Wyoming Area School
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf visited Wyoming Area Secondary Center to promote his education funding. Wolf’s budget includes property-tax relief and about $506.7 million funding increase to education.

headline: Six state health centers to re-open under Wolf plan
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf is preparing to reopen health centers closed by his predecessor and hire nurses that have lost their jobs. Wolf wants to be able to fund all the health centers by July, but negotiations on his budget are just beginning. The goal is to provide critical care outside of emergency rooms in rural areas of PA.

headline: PA-Gov: Poll: Wolf Approval Rating at 50%
abstract: While the budget gridlock trudges on, PA Governor Tom Wolf is still enjoying relatively strong approval numbers. A new survey was recently released to show that 50% of Pennsylvanians approve of Governor Wolf, a very high number compared to many other states.

headline: Funding for state grant program for college students looks promising
abstract: President and CEO James Preston of the PA Higher Education Assistance Agency reported that they would be able to fully fund grant programs for students. House Appropriations Chairman Bill Adolph would like to increase the amount of money going into college aid programs so that more students can benefit.

headline: Pennsylvania sales tax increase could benefit Delaware
abstract: While the PA state legislature continues to debate raising the sales tax, sales-tax free Delaware is looking to reap the benefits of such an increase. Amongst many other policy issues, PA Governor Tom Wolf has championed a hike in the sales tax to offset new property tax decreases. While savvy shoppers in the Southeastern counties have often made the short drive to Delaware to avoid high sales taxes in PA, Delaware officials now believe that many more Pennsylvanians will start flocking to the nearby tax haven.

headline: Citing Gov. Wolf's opposition to charter schools, York City receiver steps down
abstract: David Meckley, the York City Receiver tasked with creating a plan to revitalize the schools in York, has stepped down in response to PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s opposition to charter schools. Meckley’s plan involved bringing in charter schools. Meckley did not want to create an adversarial relationship between York and the Governor.

headline: Lifers are taxing state prison system
abstract: PA, being a state that has touted itself as tough-on-crime, has often dealt out harsh and unyielding sentences to its offenders. Among those are the thousands charged with life without parole, who cost state taxpayers a significant amount of money. While nearly five thousand people remain behind bars unconditionally for the rest of their existence, the state could save millions of dollars by taking even just a few years off of their sentences, especially as the number of those incarcerated for life without parole grows. PA is one of the few states that unconditionally incarcerates its "lifers," and its specifically harsh punishments are most likely due to tougher restrictions on clemency following the commuted sentences of murderers who killed again after they were released. Many prisoners who have lived over two-thirds of their lives behind bars can only pray for the freedom they knew as children.

headline: School funding lawsuit hinges on whether court will hear it
abstract: Several actors are taking the legislature to court over its failure to provide a constitutionally mandated “thorough and efficient” education. In previous cases, the courts have ruled that education is a matter for the Governor and Legislature, not the courts to decide. Counsel for the House and Senate opened by saying that so long as the doors are open, the Legislature has fulfilled its duty. The prosecutors said that this is a 19th century idea of “thorough and efficient.”

headline: Green, Neff ready to move past SRC controversy
abstract: After controversy emerged on the School Reform Commission when PA Gov. Tom Wolf removed Bill Green as its chairman, the agency stated that it was ready to move past the controversy. The agency reiterated its commitment to the education of Philadelphia Children and commented on being in favor of Mayor Nutter’s proposed property tax increase.

headline: AFL-CIO, PFT, and LGBT leaders endorse Kenney
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor hopeful Jim Kenney has received endorsements from the AFL-CIO, PFT, and several LGBT community leaders. These endorsements amount to some of the biggest support that a mayoral candidate can hope to win.

headline: A surreal 24 hours with Kathleen Kane
abstract: At a hearing with PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane, legislators treated Kane nicely without mentioning her failure to prosecute obvious corruption charges, or the current case against her leaking grand jury documents. This all happens within 24 hours of a heated press conference from Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf's sales tax expansion would cover child care, nursing homes and more
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s proposed increase of the sales tax from 6% to 6.6% also brings several new items that will be taxed. Most necessities, such as food and clothing remain exempt. Despite all the increases, Wolf said that his plan would reduce the tax burden by 13 percent on the average middle-class homeowner.

headline: Lawyers: Pa. open records office can't operate with 'ax over their head'
abstract: The Open Records office is responsible for deciding which documents can be for public use, an important instrument of transparency. The Office claims it cannot operate if the Governor has the authority to fire the executive director at any time. This is the crux of the current lawsuit against PA Gov. Tom wolf’s decision to fire Eric Arneson, the current executive director.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf presents legislation to implement his budget proposals
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf presented a package of legislation that would enact his budget proposals. Wolf declared that it was a “gimmick-free budget” and necessary for the financial success of PA.

headline: Smart Talk: Gov. Tom Wolf makes first radio talk show appearance
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf promised to be a “different kind of governor.” Despite his soft-spoken, regular guy appearance, Wolf has been aggressive in policy. He has scrapped his predecessor’s HealthyPA program, issued a moratorium on the death penalty, and has proposed a massive budget to return $1 billion of funding to PA schools.

headline: Penn State approves 'extraordinary' payout for Sandusky victims
abstract: Pennsylvania State University's board of trustees voted to pay an undisclosed amount, called by some to be "an extraordinary" sum, to settle the claims filed by the sexual-abuse victims of Jerry Sandusky. Board members opposed to the agreement argued that the University was being unfairly targeted for its deep pockets, and that Sandusky acted as a lone wolf.

headline: Pirates' Happ heading off to Toronto
abstract: Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher J.A. Happ is leaving the team to play for the Toronto Blue Jays after the Pirates traded him in mid-season this year. Happ previously pitched for the Blue Jays from 2012 to 2014.

headline: Chesco Republicans: Wolf's budget too costly
abstract: Chester County Republican leaders railed against PA Gov. Wolf's budget proposal criticizing its effect on school districts and increased taxing. The governor doubts that with the current partisan divide that the state would be able to adopt a budget before the start of the fiscal year on July 1st.

headline: Five years in, a look at Drexel's high-flying Fry
abstract: Drexel University president John A Fry outlined his latest plan to remodel the campus once named the nation's ugliest. The $16 million project includes a renovated campus quad thick with trees and grass and bordered by the LeBow College of Business building, a contemporary glass-and-limestone tower opened two years ago, and the Korman Center, which would get a much-needed face-lift.

headline: Judge orders hearing on Kane's firing of top staffer
abstract: AG Kathleen Kane was ordered by a Montgomery County judge to explain why the court should not hold her in contempt for firing a top prosecutor who testified before a grand jury investigating whether Kane leaked secret documents to a newspaper. Chief Deputy Attorney General James Barker was protected from retaliation by a protective order issued by the Common Pleas Judge William R. Carpenter. Kane's lawyer said that there was no retaliation or retribution, rather Kane's decision to fire Barker was due to an issue of competence and his ability to get the job done.

headline: UPMC claims union ties bias Wolf against health giant
abstract: UPMC and Republican state Senate leaders argue that PA Gov. Wolf's ties to the Service Employees International Union slant the administration against the hospital system and toward dominant health insurer Highmark Inc. Gov. Wolf's spokesman called the suggestions false, saying the Democratic governor has stayed "straight and down the middle" with the Downtown-based corporate rivals.

headline: PUC won’t reveal documents on PPL Halloween storm violations; Agency says it must protect whistleblower’s identity in Halloween 2011 outage.
abstract: Pennsylvania Power and Light (PPL) reached a settlement with state regulators over its response to a freak snowstorm that hit in October 2011. The Allentown utility paid a $60,000 fine to settle allegations that they had improperly transferred a repair crew from a high-priority outage to work on a low-priority outage. The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission has opted to keep the location, nature and identity of those involved a secret, denying any public records request.

headline: VIDEO: Wolf’s memories of Pottstown help guide his budget priorities
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf took a trip to Pottstown, PA to share his appreciation and plan for small rust-belt towns. He took this opportunity to share his "fair tax system" that would ensure town residents are not paying a higher tax rate.

headline: Pennsylvania schools begin revised PSSA tests today
abstract: New statewide changes have been implemented to the state's PSSA testing. One of the most significant being the addition of writing to the reading test, now called English language arts. In addition, for the first time the tests fully reflect the PA Core, which is the state's variation on the Common Core, a set of academic standards in English language arts and math.

headline: Medical marijuana issue scrambles party lines
abstract: PA state legislators in the house are split over the issue of medical marijuana. Rep. Matt Baker (R-68 Wellsboro), chairman of the House Health Committee, is skeptical about legalizing what he considers a dangerous drug without action from the US FDA first. Whereas, Rep. Aaron Kaufer (R-120 Kingston) offer a differing view, that shares the experience of his constituents who rely on the drugs medicinal treatment.

headline: Auditor General, legislators cast light on troubling PDE conduct
abstract: In a meeting with the House Republican Policy Committee, Auditor General Eugene DePasquale told committee members that he's uncovered a number of troubling actions on the part of the PA Department of Education while conducting his department's audit. DePasquale's audit focused mainly on what PDE does to help school districts that are struggling. This, among other things highlighted a need for change within the department, in order to improve the effectiveness of it.

headline: Drug Rehab Pittsburgh Applauds Gov. Tom Wolf's Naloxone Initiative for PA
abstract: For the first time the Pennsylvania state police will carry life-saving naloxone nasal spray kits in their patrol cars. The initiative, led by PA Gov. Wolf, aims to combat Pennsylvania's notorious influx of untreated opiate addicts suffering fatal overdoses, in direct response to their untreated addictions, and unavailability of overdose reversing medications, like naloxone - until now.

headline: Capitolwire: Senate Democrats standing by Kane, for now.
abstract: PA Senate Democrats will stand by AG Kathleen Kane, who is facing criminal charges for leaking grand jury secrets and other charges. Those still in her camp blame Kane's rocky relationship with the NRA and her refusal to uphold DOMA as reasons why Harrisburg GOP are inciting a "right-wing conspiracy" against her, to reclaim the state's top law enforcement post.

headline: Wolf order on home care workers illegal, conservative think tank says
abstract: United Home Care Workers of Pennsylvania sent out a secret ballots for a "union ambush election," backed by two larger unions and aided by an executive order from Gov. Tom Wolf. The order states that an "employee organization" representing "direct care workers" may "petition the (DHS) secretary to represent a particular unit of direct care workers".

headline: Pa. first couple shows enthusiasm for schools in Pottstown
abstract: PA Gov. Wolf and his wife, Francis, visited two schools in Pottstown to witness her program in action, "Schools that Teach", and tour their PEAK program. PEAK is a pre-K educational partnership with other agencies that is considered a national model.

headline: Inching toward a schedule, if not a budget deal
abstract: State budget negotiations develop in Harrisburg, with PA Gov. Wolf already warning the process endure "long after the June 30th deadline. It was later explained by House Republican Majority Leader Dave Reed that Gov. Wolf's statement was brought up in a "humorous format" and that both the governor and the House and Senate have the goal to be done by June 30th.

headline: State government workforce growing despite Wolf-ordered hiring freeze
abstract: Although PA Governor Tom Wolf ordered a freeze on state hiring at the start of October due to the budget stalemate, over 3,000 government agencies hired new employees in the two months that followed. Many of the hirings fell under a set of exceptions such as filling job positions that are essential or provide direct care or service.

headline: Pa. table games bring in record revenue in March
abstract: The Gaming Board had no good explanation for why in March 12 PA casinos generated $69.7 million in revenue from table games, the highest monthly total in five years this form of gambling has been legal in the state.

headline: Erie County Library system to cut hours due to state budget impasse
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, Erie County Library has been in a hiring freeze for one month and now has to cut its hours to stay in operation.

headline: Fix pensions: The Democratic mayors are right — it’s a crisis
abstract: Ten Democratic mayors from PA cities criticized their Legislative party colleagues for failing to overhaul the state's municipal pension system. The mayors advocated for House Bill 316 and Senate Bill 211, which address pensions for public safety workers.

headline: State deadlines deal hurdle to Lawrence Downs casino project, attorney says
abstract: A project to build and open a Lawrence Downs racetrack casino location in New Castle, PA may be halted by strict deadlines set in place by state regulators. An attorney for the casino's main financial backer criticized Harness Racing Commissioner Jonathan Newman for imposing unreachable construction and completion deadlines.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: DN Editorial: Taking leave of their senses Just how tone-deaf to workers' needs is the Senate vote vs. paid sick days?
abstract: The PA Senate passed a bill that would strip cities from enacting their own sick-leave laws. SB 333 would prohibit any municipality from adopting a sick-leave bill like Philadelphia's. The article then criticizes the perks and benefits House and Senate members receive.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Pa. not lacking fracking taxes
abstract: Kevin Sunday, government affairs manager at the PA Chamber of Business and Industry, wrote a letter against the Wolf administration's proposed severance tax on natural gas, claiming it would only harm the already-taxed natural gas industry.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: State lawmaker: Pa. Lt. Gov. Mike Stack's wife flipped me off and threw soda on me
abstract: A thrown soda and hand gesture mark another development in a long standing feud between Northeast political rivals; the Boyle brothers (State Rep. Kevin and US. Rep. Brendan Boyle) and Lt. Gov. Mike Stack and NE Ward leader John Sabatina.

headline: Gov. Wolf's 'not willing to compromise on his principles,' spokesman says
abstract: Gov. Wolf wants to be personally involved in developing the 2015 state budget with the Republican lead legislature.

headline: GOP leaders meet with Gov. Tom Wolf for closed-door budget discussion
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf met with Republican leaders from the state legislature to discuss the upcoming budget, its proposals and priorities, and how they can work together.

headline: Judge refuses to dismiss charges over Lycoming natural gas well site discharge
abstract: PA, Lycoming County judge refused to dismiss criminal charges against a Texas natural gas company over the discharge of an estimated 57,000 gallons of wastewater from a series of tanks at a well site.

headline: Who's funding Wolf's critics?
abstract: PA State Rep. Mike Sturla, of Lancaster, criticizes an op-ed piece by Matthew Brouillette for the Commonwealth Foundation, that denounced Governor Tom Wolf's relationship with the state's unions. The op-ed criticized Gov. Wolf for the financial support he as received from the labor unions, which he claims has resulted in billions in upcoming deals from the state to these unions. State Rep. Sturla points out the hypocrisy of the Commonwealth Foundation who attacks the governor, who publicly reports his campaign supporters, while the Foundation fails to report its own financial backers.

headline: Penn State offered to pay legal bills in NCAA case for lawyers it never hired
abstract: Penn State offered in their settlement filed by Sen. Jake Corman (R-Centre County) and former state Treasurer Rob McCord, to pay the $1.5 million in legal costs as a way to facilitate the case's closure.

headline: Figure in probe of improper influence in federal investor visa program gave Rendell $15K illegally
abstract: The author describes how PA Gaming Control Board records show evidence that a key figure in an investigation of improper influence in a federal investor visa program illegally contributed $15,000 in 2010 to the political committee of then PA Gov. Ed Rendell. Rosenfeld, who made the contribution, said he expected Rendell's committee to use the money to contribute to other candidates. Upon learning that his contribution was improper, Rosenfeld asked that it be refunded, and it was.

headline: Gov. Wolf's corporate tax-cut plan will jump-start Pa's economy: Eileen McNulty
abstract: PA Gov. Wolf's first budget proposal is designed to improve the way PA taxes corporations and levels the playing field for all businesses. The move aims to position PA as a place where businesses want to locate or expand, therefore creating 21st century jobs and creating a strong middle class.

headline: The Kane ruling: Get on with it
abstract: Montgomery County PA's district attorney, Risa Vetri Ferman, must decide if PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane should be prosecuted for perjury and other crimes. She is accused of leaking information from another grand jury to embarrass a political rival. Ruling 4-1, the court rejected Kane's contention that a county judge overseeing a statewide grand jury investigating leaks from another grand jury, lacked the authority to appoint a special prosecutor.

headline: Sharon Altland named new head of Pa. Farm Show and Expo Center
abstract: York County native Sharon Altland was named executive director of the PA Farm Show Complex and Expo Center in Harrisburg. The nationally recognized event, the PA Farm Show, prepares to celebrate its 100th year in January.

headline: In West Philadelphia, Gov. Wolf Urges More State Investment in Education
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf brought his "Jobs That Pay tour to West Philadelphia, visiting the Community College of Philadelphia. In addition to promising $2 million more in funding to CCP, Wolf is proposing to restore $1 billion in previous cuts to public education that were made under Tom Corbett.

headline: Gov Tom Wolf says he plans to weigh in on how to pay for municipal pensions
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf may propose a way for municipalities and cities to pay for pension costs.  Previous proposals made by state lawmakers have not been supported by many and all are now looking for a proposal that would satisfy both sides of the issue.
