headline: Governor Wolf Urged to Do More in Response to Indiana’s Religious Freedom Restoration Act [Updated]
abstract: Members of PA's LGBT Equality Caucus in Harrisburg delivered a letter to Gov. Tom Wolf in response to the anti-gay Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA) in Indiana, urging Wolf to stand with the people of Indiana and the nation in making it clear that this sort of law is unacceptable. In an update a response from a representative from Wolf's office stated the disapproval of what happened in Indiana, and that Gov. Wolf knows the importance of advancing equality in PA.

headline: Why Democratic mayors say state lawmakers need to act
abstract: PA's auditor general has predicted that a PA municipality will face bankruptcy without a statewide solution for municipal pension costs. There are calls for structural changes at the state level to fix the problems. Different proposals of legislation are backed by few while PA Governor Tom Wolf asserts that his budget proposal will give the cities more options to fund pensions.

headline: Pa. works to help veterans deal with several challenges
abstract: The PA state Department of Military and Veterans Affairs is trying to better connect its vets with resources, such as housing, jobs or mental health services. Deputy Adjutant General for Veteran Affairs Jerry Beck believes the to reach this goal, first the state needs to develop a database of veterans to better connect them with resources.

headline: Easton school district: Don't take your daughters or sons to work on a school day
abstract: Easton area school district urges parents to keep their children in school for the annual Take Our Daughters and Sons to Work Day because of its conflict with state-standardized testing and to move the day to the summer. Organizers of the foundation have had the same date for over two decades and want the district to be more flexible.

headline: 2nd lawsuit filed against Gov. Wolf seeking reinstatement of open records director
abstract: Pennsylvanians for Union Reform have filed suit against PA Gov. Tom Wolf to reinstate Erik Arneson as executive director of the Office of Open Records. The organization’s president, Simon Campbell, said that the position must be independent of the Governor in order to uphold its integrity.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Report: Regulators lean toward blocking Comcast deal
abstract: The Justice Department is close to a decision that would oppose a $45 billion deal merging the top two internet companies in the nation. Proponents of the Comcast and Time Warner transaction say it would result in important consumer benefits while critics believe it would give the companies too much power. The final and binding decision still has not been made.

headline: Former Texas Governor Rick Perry headlines PA GOP annual Lincoln Day Dinner
abstract: Former Texas Governor Rick Perry came to PA to speak to the PA GOP at their annual Lincoln Day Dinner. The Governor warned of the need to select a qualified Presidential candidate.

headline: Readers' Views: Appeal for budget plan support
abstract: Many Republican officials from around Chester County have come together to criticize PA Governor Tom Wolf's budget proposal while offering no ideas or visions of their own. Some residents in the area criticize Republican officials that oppose the proposal and would like to see it pass because of its many benefits for the state.

headline: Out of the woods: Gov. Wolf revives sensible protection on drilling
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has reinstated a ban on natural gas drilling on state land that was overturned by his predecessor. The ban removes any legal debate over drilling rights on state lands.

headline: Heroin, painkiller crisis: HACC students create mobile tool to help addicts
abstract: Brad Bell, Chris Mumma, and Sara Forry, students at the Harrisburg Area Community College have created a mobile web site to help drug addicts find help as a part of a state program that encouraged college students to find ways to use mobile technology for public good. The PA Department of Drug and Alcohol Programs is incorporating the mobile site as part of the state's response to the crisis of addiction to opioids.

headline: AG Kathleen Kane can't prosecute me without law license, defendant claims
abstract: An Allegheny County lawyer has asked a judge to dismiss criminal charges filed against a client, since Attorney General Kathleen Kane would be unable to prosecute the defendant due to the suspension of her license. The motion has been considered by many defense attorneys who are questioning Kane's authority.

headline: Squeaky clean Auditor General DePasquale sidesteps scandals of fellow row officers McCord, Kane
abstract: PA Auditor General Eugene DePasquale stands in contrast to the other row officers in PA for not having a single political scandal being brought out against him. State Treasurer Rob McCord has pled guilty to charges of bribing campaign donors and Attorney General Kathleen Kane is under investigation for leaking grand jury information.

headline: Veterans treatment courts would offer rehabilitation instead of jail time for nonviolent offenders
abstract: Legislation has been introduced in the PA House of Representatives and Senate to establish a type of drug and mental health court for veterans across PA to keep nonviolent servicemen and women out of jail and in treatment.

headline: DN Editorial: Outsider's appeal
abstract: The editorial says that Attorney General Kathleen Kane made the right move in appointing outsider Douglas Gansler, former Maryland attorney general, to investigate pornographic emails that were sent and received among state judges and officials. The special prosecutor may pursue constitutional, ethical, and criminal violations.

headline: Legalize medicinal pot
abstract: Lawmakers in Pa are likely to move forward with legislation hat would legalize medical marijuana.

headline: Arbitration law should become fair
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf's chief of staff has outlined a program for the state government to establish a state-level authority to help governments extract value from their sewer systems without losing control of the enterprises. There has been recognition for the need to reform and to keep the arbitration process from skewing in the favor of unions, which has been the case in current laws.

headline: Poll: 60 percent in Pennsylvania say keep out Syrian refugees
abstract: Sixty percent of Pennsylvanians are opposed to letting Syrian refugees settle in the state, according to a poll released by Harper Polling. The issue has become a hot topic in light of the refugee crisis and following the Paris terrorist attacks in November.

headline: Erik Arneson vs. Gov. Tom Wolf, explained with four court cases
abstract: Lawyers for both the Governor’s Office and Erik Arneson are citing old cases to determine whether or not the Governor is able to fire the executive director of the Office of Open Records at their choosing. A 2008 Right-to-Know law created the post, but did not specify the requirements for removal of the executive director.

headline: Amid tuition freeze, report claims large economic benefit to PA's higher education system
abstract: A study was released that about PA's state system of higher education and its affects on the economy. It is the 18th largest employer in PA and stimulates the economy where each university is located. The report was released at a time when PA Governor Tom Wolf is expected to propose higher education funding in his budget.

headline: The budget stalemate is hurting nonprofits
abstract: The budget crisis in Pennsylvania is damaging nonprofit businesses across the state, such as Project Share in Carlisle, PA. The organization provides food and supplies to homeless people, drug addicts, and struggling citizens; it now has to take out an extra line of credit to stay in operation.

headline: Wolf appointees will make more than predecessors under Corbett
abstract: State statute requires that state officials receive a yearly increase in salary dependent upon a cost-of-living adjustment. PA Gov. Tom Corbett refused to issue out those increases, but PA Gov. Tom Wolf has increased the salaries of his appointees to where the amount would be had the increases been made.

headline: It's a start
abstract: A month ago, Republican lawmakers criticized PA Governor Tom Wolf's plan to increase sales and income taxes while reducing property taxes, and now they are proposing a plan that does the same. The plan differs from Governor Wolf's mostly in providing no massive increase in education funding. Many hope that these proposals can be negotiated into a final measure that is agreeable to all.

headline: The Wolf Administration promised to step up efforts to eradicate AIDS
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf said he is dedicated to decreasing HIV infections and hopefully eliminating AIDS from the state in oncoming years.

headline: McCord charged with extortion in campaign shakedown
abstract: Days after an abrupt resignation, former PA State Treasurer Rob McCord has been charged with extortion over two campaign donations. Mr. McCord threatened to use his position as State Treasurer to make it difficult to get contracts with the state if the firms did not donate to his campaign.

headline: Senator questions Acting PSP commissioner's law enforcement certification
abstract: PA Senator Lisa Baker has requested verification for Acting State Police Commissioner Col. Marcus Brown's training and certification related to the ability to carry a firearm and exercise law enforcement powers in PA. After a meeting with Col. Brown as a step in his confirmation process, it was unclear whether he met the standards for service.

headline: Bowl scenario could go several different ways for Pitt
abstract: The Pittsburgh Panthers could end up in a variety of different situations for college football bowl game season. Based on other results and playoff rankings, the team will most likely play in one of the Atlantic Coast Conference's Tier One or Tier Two bowl games.

headline: Wolf urging Pa. independent boards to ban gifts to employees
abstract: When entering office, PA Gov. Tom Wolf signed a gift ban for employees in the Executive Branch, since then the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board and Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission have adopted similar bans. Wolf is urging more than two dozen state agencies to implement a ban.

headline: PA House and Senate Pro-Life Caucus Members Express Concern Over Wolf Nominee's Ties to Gosnell Case
abstract: Republican majority co-chairs along with 40 bipartisan members of the Pro-Life Caucus joined together in sending a letter to PA Governor Tom Wolf in regards to his nomination of Pedro A. Cortes for Secretary of the Commonwealth. They expressed concern over this nominee of the way an important case was handled under Secretary Cortes' leadership and request consideration of this in the nomination.

headline: Wolf talks about budget deal - sort of
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf dodged around providing new information about the state budget during a press conference with reporters. Wolf said that talks with Republican lawmakers are in progress and a loose agreement is still in place.

headline: DN Editorial: The Campaign Trail
abstract: Pa State Treasurer Rob McCord was charged with extortion after federal prosecutors uncovered evidence that he may have threatened donors with the power of his office. The case reveals a need for the legislature to pass campaign finance reform.

headline: Anti-abortion lawmakers protest Wolf nominee
abstract: PA Republican lawmakers have "serious concerns" over PA Governor Tom Wolf's nomination of Pedro Cortes as secretary of state because of his handling of an abortion clinic case. They claim he did not do enough to stop the practices during his tenure.

headline: Good start
abstract: PA State Senator Pat Stefano is making good on a campaign promise to reform the state’s per diem policies. Presently, legislators receive $159 for each day in Harrisburg. They are not required to turn in receipts on how the money is spent. Stefano’s new bill would require that legislators submit receipts for reimbursement, as opposed to just giving out the money.

headline: Repealing property tax promotes fairness
abstract: PA resident believes that unless property taxes decrease and schools cannot raise taxes, the system will remain unfair. He supports House Bill 76 that eliminates property taxes while raising sales taxes and income taxes to create a fairer system that also takes away the taxing power of all school districts.

headline: Some inmates strip-searched as they leave cells, Department of Corrections says, as part of security push
abstract: A new policy, or rather a policy that is now being enforced, has added strip searches to death row inmates every time that they leave their cells. Several rights groups have called the policies excessive and have the potential to lead to increased instances of mental health issues. The ACLU of PA has filed suit against the correctional facility.

headline: Our view: Harrisburg reform starts with expenses
abstract: Members of the PA Legislature have salaries ranging from 85 thousand dollars to over 130 thousand and can then also collect money daily for expenses when they stay overnight for a legislative session or a committee meeting. There is a call to abolish the per diem system and to establish an expense system instead, as well as placing a cap on reimbursements.

headline: Don Eberly will not challenge Smucker for 16th district
abstract: Don Eberly, an East Hempfield Township resident, has announced that he will not challenge Lloyd Smucker in the 16th congressional Republican primary. Eberly, 61, a longtime Republican political aide and policy maker, attests that his abilities are best served working behind the scenes. Although former GOP chairman Chet Beiler may still participate in the nomination contest, the path for Smucker looks clear.

headline: Another View: Not 'politics as usual:' Wolf needs his own team
abstract: In an open letter, Harold L. Smith has criticized the Delco Times for being overly partisan in their attack on PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s decision to fire Eric Arneson as the executive director of the Office of Open Records. Mr. Smith asked the company to report the news, not shape it.

headline: Which drugs killed 68 Luzerne County residents last year?
abstract: Heroin is the lead drug in most of drug related deaths while the rest of the cases involve some mix of more than one drug or alcohol. A new state law allows local police officers and first responders to obtain and administer the antidote naloxone for addicts.

headline: Harrisburg police ID suspect in fatal Friday night shooting
abstract: Following a fatal shooting on Market Street in Harrisburg recently, Harrisburg police have ID'd the suspect, and are looking for anyone with possible information.

headline: Pennsylvania law needs to bar discrimination against LGBT people
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has called upon the legislature to pass an anti-discrimination bill for LGBT people in PA. While many Pennsylvanians and businesses support such legislation, PA State Rep. Daryl Metcalfe has held up the legislation in the State Government Committee.

headline: DEP believes Wolf's appointments to oil and gas advisory board are legal
abstract: The PA Independent Oil and Gas Association has criticized PA Governor Tom Wolf's administration for the addition of nonvoting public interest members to the Oil and Gas Technical Advisory Board. PA Department of Environmental Protection attorneys have affirmed the legal authority to expand the board's nonvoting membership despite criticism.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Paris terrorist attacks: French man’s life saved by cell phone
abstract: Following a gruesome and tragic terror attack on the heart of Paris, truly inspiring survival stories have emerged. One of them is the story of a man known only as Sylvestre, who told Reuters that his cellphone stopped a bullet from hitting his head.

headline: Big for-profit schools, big donations: the influence of charter schools on Pennsylvania politics
abstract: Charter schools in PA are among one of the most active lobbying interests in the State. Over the last nine years, charter school lobbyists spent $10 million on campaigns in PA. They have also spent a great deal of time attacking Pa State. Rep. Bernie O’Neil, a man who has been investigating the industry’s practices. Legislation affecting charters is often derailed or given special rules or exemptions not offered to public schools.

headline: A unique political opportunity in Pennsylvania (letter)
abstract: Ray Sherry applauds both major political parties on working together to face extreme budgetary pension issues and taking action to help the people of PA. He also criticizes those who attack the mayors for going public rather than proposing improvements for the proposed bills.

headline: Local officials tout alliances to push for stronger oil train regs
abstract: As Shale oil production ramps up across the country, major concerns are being raised for communities through which that highly combustible oil travels on thousands of miles of railways. Some communities, like one in Eastern Quebec, have suffered the extremely unfortunate consequences of an oil spill, losing most of their community infrastructure to a spill. Residents and legislators of Pennsylvania, a state that sees a vast amount of oil transfer, hope to put pressure on the Department of Transportation for tougher safety regulations, so that a similarly tragic event does not strike states like PA.

headline: Moratorium on park fracking right call
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s moratorium on fracking restores the safety of state lands from the industry. This policy overturns his predecessor’s goal of using limited revenue from leasing state land to close budgetary matters.

headline: Should kids be excused from standardized tests for Take our Daughters and Sons to Work Day? (poll)
abstract: A poll asks whether students should be excused from PSSA exams to go to work with a parent. The 3 answers either agree for the benefits of the one-day program, disagree because the PSSA tests are more important, or a compromise suggesting to hold the event in the summer.

headline: Kane challenges special prosecutor's authority in leak case
abstract: Pa Attorney General Kathleen Kane has argued that the evidence built by a special prosecutor to be used in a criminal case against her be dismissed as unlawful. Citing a 1962 ruling by the Supreme Court, Kane argued that the authority of the State to hire a special prosecutor had expired a dozen years ago.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf speaks to gathered township supervisors
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf speaks to local government officials at their annual conference and thanks them while asserting their importance to democracy. He addressed grassroots efforts and a strong connection between the public and those who are serving them as vital to American democracy. Fiscal inadequacies were also addressed as well as future proposals to make the local government officials' work easier.

headline: Wolf, GOP strike temporary deal on records officer
abstract: A temporary agreement has been made between Pa Gov. Tom Wolf and the Republican Senate over the firing of Eric Arneson. Arneson was appointed the Executive Director of the Office of Open Records. The agreement withdrew a request that Arneson be reinstated, but the disagreements over the Governor’s power continue as the issue heads to the Courts.

headline: Natural gas now fuels electricity generated at UGI's Hunlock Creek Energy Center
abstract: A UGI Power Generation Center in Hunlock Township, PA switched from the Marcellus Shale to cleaner natural gas fuel to operate the plant. UGI energy officials said the move was a low cost way to meet federal emission standards and has set the pace for lower electricity rates from various companies in the state.

headline: Sen. Pileggi to seek Delco judgeship
abstract: Pa. State Senator Dominic Pileggi has announced that he will seek a vacant seat on the Delaware County Court of Common Pleas. Pileggi previously served as Senate Majority Leader for eight years before being ousted and replaced by Jake Corman.

headline: Schools scramble to find substitutes for absent teachers
abstract: In PA and across the country, there has been a mass shortage of substitute teachers. According to the PA Department Education, 59 of the 67 PA districts have been struggling to meet the minimum requirement for substitute teachers. Experts cite poverty wages, lack of respect, and a lack of new teachers as explanations for this unfortunate educational dilemma.

headline: Wolf was right on decision to accept Syrian refugees
abstract: The author applauds PA Governor Tom Wolf for stating that Pennsylvania will take in Syrian refugees and adds that America's federal government has a responsibility to help out in the crisis.

headline: Keep an eye on spending
abstract: The School Reform Commission Chairman, Bill Green, wants the Office of the Inspector General to be a permanent position within Philadelphia. Currently, a mayor has the ability to choose whether or not to have the office. Advocates of the office claim it is essential for the independent monitoring of the City’s fiscal situation. Current mayoral front runner, Anthony Williams, has not issued a comment on the position.

headline: Gas Drillers Eyeing Utica Shale's Promise
abstract: After the discovery and extraction of the widely successful Marcellus shale, energy experts are eyeing their next target, the Utica shale. The Utica shale is said to be 10 to 15 times as large as Marcellus, but energy executives are still deliberating over the economic feasibility of the project.

headline: Nasty stuff: Porngate plot thickens
abstract: The offensive email scandal surrounding the PA Attorney General's office grew more muddled once it was revealed that one of the implicated prosecutors, Frank Fina, made a sexual comment about a government employee in 2009. Furthermore, the author questions Kathleen Kane leading the charge although she discovered the emails over a year ago.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf's pack is assembled, now its confirmation time
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf has sent a complete list of appointees to the PA Senate for confirmation. Nominees usually face a quick confirmation process with minimal showboating and most of the politics are done behind closed doors. However, it is occasional that the conformation process can go longer and be time consuming.

headline: Wolf Would Use Veto To Keep Philly's Sick-Leave Law
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf states that he would veto a state proposal to eliminate local sick-leave laws in PA. The measure has passed the state Senate and is now before the state house of representatives while the Governor believes that local municipalities should control their own situation.

headline: Court won't revisit Fattah bid to shield emails
abstract: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit did not change its decision to allow federal investigators to look through Rep. Chaka Fattah's emails ahead of his corruption trial. The Philadelphia Democrat is charged with accepting bribes and using taxpayer money to benefit himself, his family, and his business partners.

headline: Anthem, Inc. target of cyber attack, personal information breached
abstract: Anthem, Inc. has announced it was the victim of a cyber attack that may have given hackers access to names, birthdays, medical IDs, social security numbers, street addresses, email addresses and employment information. Pa Attorney General Kathleen Kane said it is unclear how many consumers have been affected.

headline: Gov. Wolf, opponents claim wins as judge issues injunction on home care worker executive order
abstract: A PA Commonwealth Court judge has blocked implementation of part of an executive order by PA Governor Tom Wolf. Critics say that the order illegally abets efforts to unionize home care workers and many Republican members of the legislature have filed legal briefs and motions backing a bid to kill Wolf's order. Because a judge granted a preliminary injunction, Governor Wolf cannot enter into any memorandum of mutual understanding until a court panel hears challenges to the order.

headline: Massive Paxtang fire destroyed business owner's dream, $150,00 in uninsured equipment
abstract: A huge fire that broke out in November completely destroyed Ego Ink, a tattoo shop in Paxtang, PA, and the owner estimates caused about $150,000 in damage. The business space was covered by renter's and liability insurance but owner Daryl Bingaman faces thousands of dollars of lost equipment. The cause of the fire is still unknown.

headline: State agency 'drastically underestimated' workload from new child protection laws, state lawmaker suggests
abstract: The Department of Human Services is planning on hiring a large number of new employees after implementation of new child protection standards has overwhelmed the department’s resources. Many believe that the new regulations will prove beneficial for Pa’s children, once the department adequately adjusts.

headline: Former Rendell aide rides in to run Kathleen Kane's communications ship
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane is signing Charles Ardo as her director of communications. Ardo will have many legal controversies about Kane to address and he looks forward to his new assignment.

headline: Porngate morphs into 'Hot Ghetto Mess'
abstract: The email scandal involving the PA Attorney General's Office extends as far back as 2010, when more than two dozen racist messages and images were circulated among several state prosecutors. Philadelphia City Council approved a resolution that calls on District Attorney Seth Williams to fire the three local prosecutors who were involved.

headline: Rivera calls leaving Lancaster post tough, but "once-in-a-lifetime opportunity"
abstract: Acting Secretary of Education Pedro Rivera said that leaving his position as Superintendent of Lancaster School District was tough, but he could not pass up the opportunity to help improve PA schools. Rivera said his goal is to bring more money to the schools and fix the funding formula.

headline: 'Always remember, never forget': Lawmakers, religious leaders on the Holocaust
abstract: Religious leaders, community advocates, and lawmakers met to bring attention to the Holocaust's 70th anniversary and to ensure such evil never occurs again. Holocaust survivors and their families attended the Commemoration hosted by PA Governor Tom Wolf.

headline: Save our schools like you saved your company, Gov. Wolf (letter)
abstract: In a letter, Stephen Queenan asks that Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf use the same skill and care to fix the Pa school system that he used to repair his ailing cabinet company. Queenan called upon the Governor to propose emergency funding for schools, implement a severance tax, and seek a fair funding formula.

headline: The Heron's Nest: The Daily Numbers for Tuesday, April 21
abstract: Many drug overdosing victims have been saved by the overdose-reversing drug Narcan and a committeeman plead guilty to pot charges in Upper Darby.

headline: Catastrophe avoided at Marcellus well pad fire
abstract: A fire broke out at a gas well that could have had disastrous results had it not been for the fire department's quick action.

headline: House votes down Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Wolf's new plan for income, drilling taxes
abstract: The PA House of Representatives voted against Governor Tom Wolf's proposal to raise money for the state through increases in income and shale natural gas drilling taxes. House Democrats and Republicans alike agreed that the parties must come together to develop a budget but disagreed on how to raise revenue.

headline: Philadelphia Pays Retirees Bonus Amid Pension Gap
abstract: Despite the City’s pension fund being less than half what it should be, Philadelphia paid out bonuses to those receiving pensions. If the city brings in more than an expected sum, it gets paid out in bonuses. Many have advocated for the excess funds to be used to pay down the overall pension liability, but City Council has repeatedly rejected such proposals.

headline: 'Pushed us to the brink': Cambria County seeks permission to pay bills with$12 million loan during state budget impasse
abstract: Officials in Cambria County, PA planned to ask the state's Court of Common appeals for a $12 million loan amid the budget stalemate so the county can its bills and stay in operation. The county's financial struggles for the past few years have resulted in steep debt and could lead to a government shutdown.

headline: Bills proposed to lower costs for Pennsylvania college students
abstract: A collection of State Senators has introduced several bills designed to helps students in PA attend college at a lower cost. The multiple bills are designed to get students to stay in PA after graduation in return for increased financial support.

headline: 8 schools in Valley jilted, audit reveals
abstract: A report from the PA Auditor General Eugene DePasquale revealed that the state Department of Education did not provide necessary aid to schools in Northumberland County and Snyder County, among hundreds of others. DePasquale found that the department failed to help academically challenged schools and has not updated its master education plan since 1999. The lack of assistance was said to be caused by budget cuts to the department.

headline: Budget impasse spending transparency called into question by GOP lawmakers
abstract: A group of three Republican lawmakers published a report that reveals an apparent lack of transparency in PA Governor Tom Wolf's spending during the state's budget impasse. The report shows that the Wolf administration spent $2.7 billion in prior year funds, significantly more than in the past, and that the spending of only $60 million of the total has been verified.

headline: Wolf taps Duquesne law dean for state Supreme Court
abstract: To fill vacancies on the Supreme Court until January 2016, PA Gov. Tom Wolf has nominated Ken Gormley of Duquesne University. Gormley is a Pittsburgh native who has served as mayor of Forest Hills and as the Law Dean at Duquesne.

headline: More on (less) methane
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency released conflicting data from 2014 that reported a decrease in methane and greenhouse gas emissions but also showed an increase in overall emissions when carbon dioxide was added. The report came during a series of hearings in Pittsburgh on rules that would increase the equipment included in emission reports and eliminate methane leaks from wells.

headline: Budget impasse puts Westmoreland County in financial bind
abstract: Westmoreland County Commissioners said the county may have to borrow $10 million to keep the government and its social service programs in operation if the PA budget crisis continues.

headline: VIDEO: Proposed Marcellus drilling tax distributes proceeds to other statewide initiatives
abstract: A bipartisan group of legislators produced a 3.2% drilling tax on Marcellus Shale. The money will be used to fund programs on a statewide scale, principally education spending.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Official to hear case- Against himself
abstract: Jack E. Marino, a PA Labor Relations Board Examiner, is set to hear a case brought against himself for allegedly "bowing to political pressures" and disadvantaging the Teamsters and Carpenters Unions in their work on the PA Convention Center. Marino is accused of "unfair labor practices" for allegedly ousting the two unions for other workers.

headline: Local joblessness at seven-year low
abstract: The unemployment rate for the Scranton/Wilkes Barre area fell to 5.8 percent, its lowest figure in more than seven years. Almost 2,000 people found jobs between November and December 2015 and the number of unemployed people decreased by 800.

headline: Could ethics become contagious?
abstract: Upon taking office, PA Gov. Tom Wolf issued a gift ban in the Executive Branch that has been imitated by two state agencies. The bans are intended to decrease instances of corruption in the State. The legislature, on the other hand, has no ban in place and legislators are free to take gifts from anyone.

headline: Confused? Don't worry - Gov. Tom Wolf knows who you should vote for on Election Day: Monday Morning Coffee
abstract:
Email




For the first time since the colonial era, there are three open seats on the PA Supreme Court. This means that the upcoming election is both a very historic and very important one. Both GOP and Democratic challengers are fighting vigorously for the open seats, but the Democrats seem to have the edge; as they are being backed by big labor, the trial lawyers, and PA Governor Tom Wolf.

headline: Trump has more in common with bat-biting rock star than reality TV
abstract: The author humorously compares businessman and Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump to Ozzy Osbourne on several points, including the fact that people pay large amounts of money to see both men "perform."

headline: test
abstract: test

headline: THEIR VIEW: PennDOT's work trails other states
abstract: In comparison to other states, PA’s maintenance of roads seems to lag behind. Many observe that the poor state of PA’s roads are considered the norm so little action is done. The author speculates that it comes down to poor resource management in the agency. To help alleviate the problem, Former PA Gov. Tom Corbett passed a transportation bill designed to increase the resources available to PennDOT.

headline: Business workshop: Decision expected to lead to more cybersecurity suits
abstract: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the third circuit recently ruled that the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) could hold the Wyndham hotel chain responsible for a massive cybersecurity breach. This ruling not only sets a precedents for future cases, but also gives the FTC more power in making guidelines for companies to follow in the area of cybersecurity, a big victory for consumer protection.

headline: Medicaid expansion could leave some with marketplace coverage in the lurch
abstract: Ann Bacharach of the Pennsylvania Health Law Project is concerned that many Pennsylvanians will be unaware that they can qualify for Medicaid. Under the new Medicaid expansion, citizens will need to update their information so that the marketplace can properly screen them for eligibility in Medicaid. Others worry people might drop plans all together due to cost increases on the marketplace, not knowing they qualify for Medicaid.

headline: Who has the budget poll position?
abstract: With the PA State budget being due 127 days ago, many are fed up with those in the state capitol. Each side has dug in their heels; Democratic Governor Tom Wolf on several new taxes big labor protection, and the Republican controlled legislature on liquor privatization and pension reform. In order for a desperately needed budget to get passed, compromise, which is heavily favored by the polls, must be reached.

headline: State Senate committee reviews amended property tax-elimination bill
abstract: Eliminating property taxes for increased sales and income taxes has been a proposal going around in Harrisburg. Debate persists over what services will be subject to taxation and what would have if the tax revenue fails to meet projections. A large concern has been raised over how the money will be distributed to schools, to which State Senator Mike Folmer advised against getting caught up in an education funding debate.

headline: Language barriers persist in Pa.'s district courts, survey finds
abstract: A survey done by Temple University has shown that the PA court system is unable to adequately serve individuals who do not speak English well. The ACLU found that in the top 20 counties that have non-English speaking populations, numerous abuses are possible due to language barriers. Much of the issue stems from counties’ inabilities to pay for translators.

headline: To keep Pa's energy revolution going, we need to expand pipelines: Another View
abstract: With the Marcellus shale becoming the second largest producer of natural gas in the world, presidents of the Washington, Delaware, and Harrisburg county chambers of commerce have called for an expanded pipeline project. They believe that the state must take advantage of its natural resources and expand pipelines, an initiative that they believe will boost the economies of surrounding areas and across the state.

headline: This is a dummy newslip
abstract: This is a test of the create problem.

headline: Report shows Pittsburgh consultant gave PAC $100K for McCord
abstract: A Pittsburgh health care consultant donated $100,000 to Rob McCord’s Campaign for the Governorship of Pennsylvania. Mr. McCord ended up coming in third place and eventually pled guilty to two counts of extortion. McCord was accused of implying if firms did not donate, he would make it harder for them to obtain state contracts.

headline: Mother's battle drives Rep. Rob Matzie to raise awareness for pancreatic cancer
abstract: PA State Rep. Rob Matzie (D-16) has brought HR-545 to the floor today, a bill that will designate November as pancreatic cancer month. This bill has a particularly personal connection to the representative from Ambridge, as his mother, recently diagnosed with the often disease, overcame it after a series of grueling treatments and surgeries.

headline: Battle for Job He Created
abstract: In his first clash with a legislature he must work with, PA Gov. Tom Wolf was sued by Eric Arneson and Senate Republicans over Arneson’s firing from the Office of Open Records. Wolf argued that Arneson being made Executive Director was a murky appointment and that he is an at-will employee, therefore can be fired without cause. Arneson argued that the Governor does not possess the authority to fire him.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Steele tops Castor in contentious Montco D.A. race
abstract: Democrat Kevin Steele recently defeated Republican Bruce Castor in an extremely contentious race for Montgomery County District Attorney (DA). The race drew widespread attention and became a bit combative surrounding Steele's "distasteful" ad campaign against Castor for his alleged mishandling of the Bill Cosby sexual assault case. More public spotlight for this seat is foreseen, as Steele will prosecute former DA Kathleen Kane for alleged perjury and misconduct.

headline: Cutler prepares for bigger spotlight with leadership post
abstract: Bryan Cutler, a 39-year old from Lancaster, is preparing to takeover as the Majority Whip in the PA House. Cutler is committed to uniting a caucus that has in recent years been starkly divided on a number of key issues.

headline: Democrats gain control of Pennsylvania's Supreme Court
abstract: Following an historic election, Democrats have completed a clean sweep of the record three open seats on the supreme court. The Democrats outspent their GOP opponents by a wide margin, and cite support from big labor and trial lawyers across the commonwealth as keys to their victory. The new Justices Kevin Doughrety, David Wecht, and Christine Donohue, will serve ten years on the bench's current 5-2 Democratic majority.

headline: Pennsylvanians optimistic about Wolf in new Quinnipiac Poll: Tuesday Morning Coffee
abstract: A recent poll came out that showed 62% of Pennsylvanians are optimistic that Pa Gov. Tom Wolf will be able to work with the legislature and enact positive change in the State. The polls also showed that U.S. Senator Pat Toomey is popular among voters.

headline: Attendance at Pennsylvania Society in New York could be impacted by the administration’s gift ban
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society is set to honor former PA Governor Ed Rendell in New York City, but many say that attendance of current PA legislators is dependent upon a budget being passed. Many of those invited, including PA minority leader Jay Acosta, feel that the opulence of the event is hypocritical to PA schools who are struggling for funding.

headline: Pa-Gov: Wolf Begins Transition to Full Medicaid Expansion
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has abandoned his predecessor’s Medicaid Expansion alternative and opted to accept the full expansion of Medicaid provided under the Affordable Care Act.

headline: Affordable Care Act aid could take years to reach insurers
abstract: A federal relief agency that was meant to give private health insurers, such as Highmark, financial aid to cover their losses from the Affordable Care Act's online marketplaces fell $2 billion short and could not reimburse the insurers. Companies may have to wait several years before they can collect the money and resolve their deficits.

headline: Penn State Alumnus Nominated To Pennsylvania Supreme Court
abstract: Penn State Alumnus President Judge Thomas Kistler and Ken Gormley have been nominated to fill the vacancies on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court.

headline: Senate candidate Katie McGinty raised $1 million last quarter
abstract: Katie McGinty, who is a PA Democrat running for U.S. Senate, raised $1 million during the first fundraising quarter of her campaign from contributions by thousands of small donors. Braddock, PA Mayor John Fetterman and former congressman Joe Sestak, both Democrats, are also running for Senate.

headline: McQueary's credibility expected to shape trial involving PSU administrators
abstract: Former Penn State assistant football coach, Mike McQueary's story will be tested when three Penn State University administrators go to trial regarding the Sandusky scandal. Mike McQueary has told authorities that he did not cover up the fact that former Penn State coach, Jerry Sandusky was sexually violating a young boy.

headline: Report: Alternative punishment program under-used
abstract: Pa’s State Intermediate Punishment program has the potential to save the state a significant amount of money on prison expenditure by allowing participants to engage in an out-patient treatment program for drug offenses. The program’s popularity is increasing, but not at the pace that it should be.

headline: House vote on the Governor's tax plan
abstract: The PA House of Representatives will vote on Governor Tom Wolf's proposed budget. The budget would increase sales tax and a natural gas severance tax that Republican legislators are opposed to.

headline: SRC to vote on 39 charter applications Feb. 18, invites public comment
abstract: The School Reform Commission has announced that it will vote on all 39 charter schools applications, despite delays. The decision to vote on the schools came after a $25 million donation from the Philadelphia School Partnership to defray some of the costs of students leaving public schools for charters. This has, however, raised debate among lawmakers over how much charters actually cost.

headline: Diana Jones' Walkabout: Preservationists make new plea for what to save
abstract: The Young Preservationists association of Pittsburgh recently came out with a list of its top 10 historical structures in the city, a list that somewhat surprisingly included an abandoned footbridge. This footbridge may have implications beyond its only 400 foot long pathway, because if the footbridge is renovated and reopened, it may set a precedent for restoration of other dilapidated historical sites in the Pittsburgh area.

headline: Pittsburgh attorney Fawcett in the race for attorney general
abstract: David Fawcett, attorney from Pittsburgh, has announced that he has formed a committee to run for PA Attorney General in the 2016 race. Fawcett, a self-described pragmatic Republican, has stated that he believes he has the legal expertise and political experience necessary to bring balance to the office following a trail of scandal left by incumbent Democrat Kathleen Kane.

headline: Drexel University study: PennEast Pipeline will lead to more jobs and lower prices
abstract: A study done by Drexel University shows that the PennEast pipeline has the potential to bring in 11,210 jobs and over $1 Billion in economic activity to parts of PA and NJ.

headline: Report card for state's high schools show overall decline
abstract: PA schools with an 11th grade seem to be on the sharp decline, according to the yearly evaluation of the state's schools. The report card showed the most decline in the more rural, mid-state counties, as more than half of those counties saw a decline in test scores. Although many other of the state's grade levels seem to have shown sharp decline in performance, there seems to be some hope in the younger generation, as the fourth and eighth grades were above average when compared to national standards.

headline: Allentown's Syrian population divided over refugees
abstract: As brutal civil war in Syria rages on, so does the debate about accepting its refugees. In Allentown, PA, this debate is especially present, as Allentown is home to the nations largest established Syrian communities. The community, being largely Christian and loyal to the Syrian government, is split over the issue of accepting more refugees, while some believe those fleeing the government have dangerous tendencies, and some believe that the US should continue to accept their fellow countrymen. Allentown has also seen an influx of charities helping ease the process for incoming Refugees into the city.

headline: Map: Which state representatives are calling for a 3.2 percent extraction tax
abstract: Four lawmakers have proposed a bill to introduce a 3.2% extraction tax on top of the impact fee passed by Former Gov. Tom Corbett. Combined, this would equal 5% and is the number that Gov. Wolf has asked for in the campaign trail.

headline: Gas pipeline recommendations soon
abstract: Following the extremely successful discovery and extraction Marcellus shale natural gas reserve, PA governor Tom Wolf has put together an advisory panel for the exploration of new gas pipelines in the state. Many are anticipating the upcoming release this long-awaited plan, as it will effect farmers, residents, environmentalists, and energy executives alike.

headline: Urgent care for Pa.'s uninsured
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has abandoned his predecessor’s alternative healthcare plan in favor for the full Medicaid Expansion. Wolf hopes this will increase access, create jobs, and save hospitals.

headline: IFO compares monthly revenue figures to prior year
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue and the Independent Fiscal Office (IFO) have begun to compare their revenue figures to the prior year. The report showed that monthly tax and non-tax revenues had declined significantly, but the report did not take into account the inheritance tax that did not recur, thereby showing that revenue had actually increased from the previous year.

headline: Council gets its own Harrisburg lobbyist
abstract: Philadelphia Council President Darrell Clarke has hired a lobbying firm to bring Council’s interests to Harrisburg. This will mean that there are firms advocating on behalf of the city, the other coming from the Mayor's Office. There is concern over how Harrisburg will react to Philadelphia’s inability to speak in one voice.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Kane is fighting the good fight
abstract: Former PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane has gone under heavy scrutiny following the allegations of misconduct against her, but she may not be as bad as the media is making her out to be, as she did not waver in the face of overwhelming charges and criticism.

headline: Gov. Wolf: No More Death Penalty (For Now)!
abstract: Citing rampant costs and potential injustice, PA Gov. Tom Wolf has put a moratorium on all death sentences until a bipartisan committee in the Senate can complete an investigation into the court proceedings relating to the death penalty.

headline: Governor Tom Wolf talked about the Port of Philadelphia’s expansion
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf has recently called for the expansion of the underdeveloped South Port Terminal in Philadelphia, planning to start the project 2017.

headline: Pennsylvania governor temporarily suspends death penalty
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has put in place a temporary moratorium on the death penalty at the same time as national conversation around it is spiking. PA has executed three people since 1976.

headline: 2015 complete PIAA high school football interactive playoff brackets
abstract: The Pennsylvania High School football playoffs will begin soon, and a large following across the state is anticipated.

headline: Left-leaning think tank blasts Corbett's funding for education
abstract: A Harrisburg think tank came out with a report attacking PA Governor Tom Corbett's funding of education. The Administration defended its education policy by stating the loss of the federal stimulus money caused the problem. The think tank mentioned the stimulus money, but stated that state money was transferred out of public schools and into charters and tuition-assistance for private schools, all while corporate tax cuts were made.

headline: Stack to Hold Reception for Donohue at Dem Winter Meeting
abstract: Pa Supreme Court hopeful, Christine Donohue, will have a reception thrown for her by PA Lt. Governor Mike Stack on the eve of the Democrats’ Winter Committee Meeting.

headline: Optimism returns to state budget talks, despite differences
abstract: Deep in a budget gridlock, there seems to be some hope for compromise in the PA legislature. PA Governor Tom Wolf has dug his heels in on his championed issues like his large-scale tax increase for remedying the deficit, while PA Republican legislators have become equally entrenched in protecting their own issues, like liquor privatization and pension reform. The hope for compromise comes from a proposal to divert funds from state gambling revenue, which could give Governor Wolf his revenue and pave the path to compromise. However, inside sources feel that the disagreements, especially over taxes and liquor, are so fundamental that compromise still seems unlikely.

headline: Casey, Toomey split on minimum wage
abstract: The U.S. Senate voted to advance a bill that would raise the minimum wage to $10.10 an hour. The bill’s support was virtually along party lines with PA Senators Casey and Toomey being divided. Senator Casey said that the bill would give a much needed raise to millions of American workers, whereas Senator Toomey said the raise would kill hundreds of thousands of jobs.

headline: Seth Williams, Risa Ferman Slam Tom Wolf Over Pa Death Penalty Moratorium
abstract: The District Attorney of Philadelphia and the Montgomery County District Attorney came out in strong opposition of Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s moratorium on the death penalty. They claimed he has no legal nor moral authority to issue a moratorium. They would have preferred he went through the legislature to change the law.

headline: Judge: Kane must appear Thursday to explain suggestion that Sandusky materials were leaked
abstract: Disgraced PA Attorney General (AG) Kathleen Kane has been ordered to testify about alleged leaked information regarding the Jerry Sandusky sexual abuse case, and several others, according to the judge. This comes alongside a swath of charges filed against Kane in her time as AG, including perjury and misconduct.

headline: It's time to retire Pa's Prohibition-era liquor system: Charlie Gerow
abstract: The author argues that it is time for Pa to privatize the liquor industry. He advocates in favor of Pa Speaker Mike Turzai’s bill that would sell off the enterprise and bring in an estimated $1 billion – money that could be used to fund education. He also expresses that the opposition is beginning to weaken.

headline: Social service agencies, counties are having a tough time during this budget impasse
abstract: The PA House of Representatives did not vote to approve Governor Tom Wolf's budget proposal, which would include an increase in sales tax and income tax as well as a natural gas severance tax. As a result of the budget impasse, counties and local social service agencies are struggling to bring in money and maintain funding.

headline: Local political leaders debate Wolf's gas extraction tax plan
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf campaigned on implementing a severance tax on natural gas drilling and using that money to fund education. While many in both parties agree with the tax, the details are quite different. Many legislators have introduced their own version of the tax with rates being different from the Governor’s approach.

headline: Takes two to make a budget, Hughes tells GOP
abstract: PA Senator Vincent Hughes, a Philadelphia Democrat, stated at a news conference that the unwillingness of Republican lawmakers to compromise is making it difficult for Governor Tom Wolf and the legislature to pass a state budget. His comments came shortly after the Republican-controlled House of Representatives voted down Governor Wolf’s proposal to raise the income tax and impose a natural gas severance tax. Stephen Miskin, a spokesman for the House Republicans, said that the GOP is more than open to discussion.

headline: Gov. bans death penalty: 7 Lancaster County inmates affected by governor's ban on death penalty
abstract: Seven individuals from Lancaster County will be affected by Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s death penalty moratorium. The Governor said it will be in place until he receives a study four years in development from the Legislature detailing the practices of capital punishment in PA.

headline: Letter to the Editor: Joe Hackett's departure from Harrisburg will be a big loss and a big gain
abstract: PA State Representative Joe Hackett of Ridley Township is resigning from the state house and returning to law enforcement. He was an exceptional representative that remained steadfast and successful. His decision is a loss to the state house but a gain to law enforcement.

headline: PA governor issues warning to Merrimack police
abstract: In a joke, Pa Governor Tom Wolf asked Merrimack police to rescind their warrant for Punxsutawney Phil’s arrest.

headline: Wolf's education pick to begin confirmation process
abstract: The PA House of representatives is beginning negotiations on a stopgap budget. Lawmakers will also begin the confirmation process for PA Governor Tom Wolf's nomination to lead the State Department of Education.

headline: Pennsylvania District Attorneys Association's Statement of Death Penalty Moratorium
abstract: The PA District Attorneys Association released a statement condemning the decision of PA Gov. Tom Wolf to grant a reprieve to a death row inmate and an overall moratorium on the death penalty. They argued that it had nothing to do with legal procedure, but to place his personal views into action.

headline: Healthcare providers blast Wolf plan to tax in-home services
abstract: Many healthcare advocates are critical of PA Governor Tom Wolf's budget to increase sales taxes on home healthcare services. They believe it should be kept as the cheaper alternative to nursing homes or hospitals while Governor Wolf insists that his budget be taken as a whole rather than picked apart.

headline: PennDOT to track more than 700 snow plows in real time this winter
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf announced that in preparation for winter, PennDOT will be monitoring over 700 vehicles.

headline: Pa. Senate panel endorses Rivera for education chief
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf's nomination of Pedro Rivera for education secretary has won unanimous approval from an 11-member Senate education panel. He will soon face a vote from the Senate Rules committee before the final vote from the full Senate.

headline: PA business community waits to learn more about Wolf's income tax plan
abstract: During the campaign, Pa Gov. Tom Wolf promised to close the deficit and restore funding to education, leading many to wonder what tax increases will occur to do so. The Gov. said he wants to make the tax system more fair by granting universal exemptions to certain income levels. The exact details of the plan are not out and it has many business leaders anxious to see what the full package entails.

headline: Housing fund should be statewide
abstract: The PA Housing Affordability and Rehabilitation Enhancement Act (PHARE) has had large impacts on affordable housing but is only funded in counties that have at least one active Marcellus shale well and therefore exists in 37 of PA's 67 counties. A group of lawmakers have devised a plan to expand PHARE to all counties and are calling on others to ensure the program's passage.

headline: 242 Pennsylvania workers not state residents
abstract: Several states have issued residency laws requiring public employees live in Pa. This has sparked debate among several legislators demanding that those influencing PA policy should live in PA. Others argue that residency should be left to the discretion of the employee.

headline: York City mayor's annual address focuses on education
abstract: York City Mayor Kim Bracey gives her annual State of the City Address calling for a fresh start for the future of York City School District. She calls for a confrontation of poverty, inequality, and dysfunction at home. She also endorsed PA Governor Tom Wolf's budget proposal and the positive effects it could have on the city.

headline: Common Core tests to begin today
abstract: Controversial Common Core testing will be going into effect in 29 states. Debate has been sparked over the role of the Federal Government in educational standards, which has caused many states to opt out of the examinations and develop their own system.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Failed budget talks, successful fundraisers
abstract: PA lawmakers voted down Governor Tom Wolf's budget proposal of an income tax hike and a tax on natural gas drilling, leaving room for future budget negotiations. After the policy loss Wolf raised money at a campaign fundraiser at an upscale restaurant in Harrisburg.

headline: Montgomery Co. DA: We Were Completely Ignored By Gov. Wolf On The Death Penalty
abstract: Montgomery Co. DA Risa Ferman spoke on Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s failure to hear the concerns that her and her colleagues raised over the death penalty. She believes that the Governor’s moratorium is a disserve to the State and done out of personal belief, not judicial procedure.

headline: Audit: DOE slow learner
abstract: The Times Tribune Editorial Board criticized the PA Department of Education for its poor performance based on a recent state audit, which revealed that the Department failed to adapt a master plan or provide academic assistance to students in 561 struggling schools. The Board called on Governor Tom Wolf and the Legislature to hold the Department accountable.

headline: State secrecy gains traction
abstract: In recent years, a high number of prominent PA politicians have been forced out of office due to corruption scandals. Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has attempted to change the behavior of the Executive Branch and increase transparency, but these efforts have not been matched by the Legislature. The Legislature has increased restrictions on the Open Records Law that make it harder to obtain basic information.

headline: Environmental watchdog sues world's largest steelmaker over Pennsylvania pollution
abstract: PennEnvironment, a nonprofit environmental advocacy group, sued ArcelorMittel, the world’s largest steel manufacturer, for violating pollution laws at a Monossen, PA coke plant. The watchdog group filed a federal lawsuit at U.S. District Court in Pittsburgh. PennEnvironment claimed that the plant went over emission gas limits several hundred times and stated that over 100 residents in the surrounding areas filed complaints about the pollution.

headline: Marcus Brown: 7 things you need to know about Pa.'s acting state police commissioner
abstract: The former Commissioner of the Maryland State Police, Marcus Brown, has received a large amount of scrutiny as he awaits confirmation for Pa’s Police Commissioner. Many worry that his record is divisive and that he is an outsider to the affairs of the State.

headline: How one wall in the Susquehanna Art Museum explains all its problems
abstract: The author visited the Susquehanna Art Museum in Harrisburg, PA and wrote about his experience in the mostly empty building. He cited the institution’s financial conflicts and old architecture style as indicative of Harrisburg’s struggle to evolve into a richer, more modern city.

headline: Ex-Treasurer Rob McCord's guilty plea in extortion case didn't go off without a hitch
abstract: Former State Treasurer Rob McCord has pled guilty to charges of extortion and can face a maximum of forty years in prison. The ex-treasurer said he fully understood the charges being brought against him.

headline: Senate Democrats plan push for gun control legislation
abstract: Democrats in the PA Senate introduced a new set of proposed gun control bills that would restrict gun purchases without background checks and prohibit convicted stalkers and those who are under restraining orders from obtaining firearms. The last piece of gun control legislation to be placed before the Senate was the bipartisan Toomey-Manchin Bill, created by Republican Senator Pat Toomey and Democratic Senator Joe Manchin. The current legislation is strongly pushed by Democrats, who are urging it to pass in the conservative Senate.

headline: Horse racing to go on, with regulatory deal set for vote
abstract: Following many rumors of the contrary, PA Governor Tom Wolf has announced recently that his administration will not follow through with plans to prohibit horseracing in the state after a key agreement was reached in the legislature. The original plans to shut down the sport came after the government stated it had run out of money to continue regulating it.

headline: Oil train fire rekindles push for tanker rule
abstract: After the derailment and explosion of a train carrying crude oil in West Virginia, debate has emerged once more to increase rules and regulations regarding train cars. The National Transportation Safety Board stated that the current trains were not fit for service and needed improvements.

headline: The state has yet to be set to decide on a budget
abstract: PA Democrats and Republicans voted against Governor Tom Wolf’s budget proposal, which would have raised a series of taxes in exchange for lower property taxes and increased education funding. One hundred days into the fiscal year, the Governor still hoped that a compromise could be reached.

headline: Senate candidate McGinty's role in energy industry is questioned
abstract: Pennsylvania Democratic candidate for U.S. senate, Katie McGinty, has a lengthy resume that includes, amongst other qualifications, a strong commitment to clean energy in both the public and private sector. McGinty advised former U.S. Vice President Al Gore on the Council on Environmental Quality, and then headed the Pennsylvania EPA during PA Gov. Ed Rendell's administration, before leaving for the private sector. However, it was this move to the private sector that is currently garnering her criticism from Republican opponents, who say that the former PA EPA chair used her role in government as a revolving door to help private-sector energy companies.

headline: Bill regulating health insurance exchange navigators advances
abstract: The PA Senate introduced a bill that places additional regulations on navigators in the Affordable Care Act’s health insurance exchange program. The bill requires them to register with the State and submit to a criminal background check. Democrats took issue that the bill was an attempt to regulate the federal government.

headline: When the Wolf Comes to Town
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf spoke about the state’s budget challenges at a public event in Erie, PA, as part of a global summit presented by the Jefferson Educational Society. The author referenced a 2014 conversation he had with Wolf about educational funding for Erie City public schools and the municipality’s place in the state budget.

headline: 2 babies found dead near Pa. lot underwent autopsies some time ago, police learn
abstract: Deep in Philadelphia's Kensigton neighborhood, the bodies of two dead infants were found in a trash littered used-car lot. As Philadelphia police investigated the scene, the chief medical examiner discovered that the babies had autopsies previously performed on them. Who the medical personnel was and when the autopsies were performed remains to be determined.

headline: In Monroeville, Gov. Wolf pushes his proposed natural gas extraction tax
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf pushed for his proposal to place a 5% severance tax on natural gas drilling in order to generate an estimated $1 Billion in tax revenue to be used to reinvest into education. Industry advocates worried that increased taxation would harm the industry’s growth.

headline: Judicial panel indicate Kane withheld Eakin emails
abstract: The Pennsylvania Judicial Conduct Board accused state Attorney General Kathleen Kane of purposely withholding information in emails during its 2014 investigation of PA Supreme Court Justice J. Michael Eakin. The board implied that Kane’s office controlled the computer servers that the emails went through but did not turn over all of the messages Eakin sent or received, which allegedly contained racist, homophobic, and pornographic material.

headline: Philly won't be overlooked: Give us a (road) sign
abstract: As this columnist states, Philadelphia is a city that can often be overlooked; both by its residents and its visitors. This overlooking, he believes, is no more evident than on the road signs of interstate route 95, where after passing our nations capital, the next two highlights on the highway's signs showcase Baltimore, MD, and New York City, NY. One member of the Philadelphia community, John Grabelle Hermann, is determined to put Philly on the map, quite literally. A longtime lover of the city of brotherly love, Hermann has started a campaign to lobby the government of neighboring states to put Philadelphia as a major city on I-95's road signs.

headline: Consultant reforming finances: Pudner pushing for changes after McCord scandal
abstract: John Pudner, who orchestrated the surprise victory over former U.S. Majority Leader Eric Cantor, has now chosen campaign finance reform as his new initiative. Pudner believes that money influencing politics is the root of many problems. It can be seen with PA Gov. Tom Corbett’s enactment of drilling-friendly policy after receiving donations from the industry.

headline: Amendment saving Allentown, Bethlehem 911 centers fail in State House
abstract: A bill is going to the PA house of representatives for a vote that would press on Allentown and Bethlehem's 911 centers to consolidate with local county dispatch centers. The bill would update the Public Safety Emergency Telephone Act by increasing surcharges on phone bills to fund 911 centers statewide.

headline: CHRIS KELLY: Schoolhouse rock!
abstract: In the capital city of Harrisburg, Fell Charter School is not only highlighting the success of charter students and faculty in the commonwealth, but revealing the very human effects of the budget impasse in Harrisburg. Fell Charter is one of many schools across PA that has felt the blow of stalled state funding, and even United Way is struggling to help. The legislature, this columnist asserts, need to get their priorities straight and agree on a budget so that the states education system can be funded without collecting box tops.

headline: Editorial: Death penalty in Pa. deserves a hard look
abstract: The Innocence Project lists that over 100 people have been taken off of death row after being found innocent of their alleged crime. In PA, there were 10 wrongful convictions, one given the death sentence. In light of this information, the author argues that it was appropriate for Pa Gov. Tom Wolf to impose a moratorium on the death penalty.

headline: Ryan Mackenzie legislation would protect taxpayers
abstract: The author is shocked by tax collectors committing fraud and commends PA state representative Ryan Mackenzie for taking on the issue.

headline: CHRIS KELLY: Schoolhouse rock!
abstract: In the capital city of Harrisburg, Fell Charter School is not only highlighting the success of charter students and faculty in the commonwealth, but revealing the very human effects of the budget impasse in Harrisburg. Fell Charter is one of many schools across PA that has felt the blow of stalled state funding, and even United Way is struggling to help. The legislature, this columnist asserts, need to get their priorities straight and agree on a budget so that the states education system can be funded without collecting box tops.

headline: Controversial language removed from Dept. of Health website
abstract: Language stating that nursing home inspection reports cannot be used as evidence in lawsuits has been removed from the PA Dept. of Health’s webpage.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Oh, the drip, drip of the Kane case
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane is plagued with claims of leaking grand-jury information and her firing an underling that could be retaliatory. There are recommendations of charges against Kane.

headline: 'People are just sick of being scared'
abstract: General Electric (GE) Transportation, one of the biggest drivers of the Erie, PA economy, is looming ominously over the city as it announced plans to lay off 1,500 employees. The company understands its economic might, as it has conducted a study that revealed it pumped billions into both the Erie and PA economy. As for the employees of Erie, people are desirous for stability, and freedom from the fear of unemployment. Even those who are not employed by GE fear the proposed layoffs, as many small business owners in the neighborhood fear what will happen when the GE money is no longer being pumped into the local economy.

headline: Attorney General Kane hires 2 more lawyers in leak fight
abstract: Pa Attorney General Kathleen Kane has hired two additional lawyers to join her in her request that the Supreme Court throw out criminal charges that a statewide grand jury recommended against her. This is in response to accusations that Kane mishandled grand jury information and leaked it to the press.

headline: Governor Wolf Will Meet with Power Plant Opponents
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf will meet with opponents of a natural gas power plant that is proposed for Lackawanna County after protests over-shadowed his event.

headline: PUC spares HIKO Energy from 'ultimate death penalty.'
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission approved a settlement between New York electric supplier HIKO Energy and the office of the state Attorney General and Consumer Advocate, which forces HIKO to pay $4 million for increasing consumer electricity costs during record cold months between January and April 2014. HIKO will be banned from accepting new customers in Pennsylvania until July 2016 and is now required to modify its general business practices.

headline: Deal buys time
abstract: Following a long-running dispute that has threatened health care in Western PA, the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC), the regions largest provider of health care, and Highmark, the regions largest insurer, have reached an agreement that will help many patients previously feared loss of coverage. Under the agreement, those who have persistent medical problems and sought care at UPMC in the previous three years will receive continuing care. The deal seems to be a sigh of relief for many patients in the area.

headline: Acting state police commissioner talks policing, uniform controversy in new podcast
abstract: Despite not rising through the ranks of the PA State Police, Col. Marcus Brown has more than two decades of experience in California and Baltimore.

headline: Lawmaker wants to bring OSHA to PA public employers
abstract: Public employers are currently exempt from requirements imposed by the federal Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA). A PA republican lawmaker has proposed a bill to require OSHA safety standards to be used by public employers.

headline: Legislative leaders and the governor are getting closer to a budget deal
abstract: Lawmakers and PA Governor Tom Wolf are holding various meetings within the state legislature to discuss a proposal that could end the budget crisis.

headline: Making PA's primary relevant? Not in 2016
abstract: As the first open presidential election since 2008 looms, Pennsylvanians are frustrated with the timing of their Presidential primary, as the contest has historically come in late April, which means that the nomination is usually decided by that time. Because of this, many believe their votes do not matter as much as residents in other states. While many are pushing for an earlier contest, down-ballot candidates are concerned that they will lose valuable campaigning time, and party leaders are concerned about losing delegates.

headline: Editorial: Facts are on Governor's side
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf made good on a promise to introduce a 5% severance tax on the gas industry in order to fund education and close the State’s deficit. Republicans in the legislature opposed the idea stating that it would create too heavy a burden on the industry and force them to leave the state. The Wall Street Journal noted that PA has the lowest effective tax rate on natural gas when compared to the other major producers.

headline: Parker says Wolf's finance staff will examine his property tax relief plan
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf's finance staff will inspect a four-point proposal from a state representative for Monroe County property tax relief. The proposal calls for additional funding to begin reimbursing local taxpayers and school districts for a shortfall in state aid dating back to the 1990s.

headline: Governor Tom Wolf says if the state Senate votes to remove Attorney General Kathleen Kane, he'll have no choice but to go along with it
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf said he will have to follow the Senate's decision if they vote to remove Kane from office and/or impeach her.

headline: State Capitol Building Lit in French Tricolor
abstract: Following the terrorist attacks in Paris, PA Governor Tom Wolf issued a statement of solidarity with the French people and lit up the state house in the French tricolor.

headline: Pennsylvania capital punishment delay no big deal
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s decision to place a moratorium on the death penalty has brought strong criticism from legal experts, who in the past have forced governors to impose the penalty. Still, only three people have been executed in Pa since 1976. This is true even with governors who supported the death penalty.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Yo, Philly, meet your new state senator
abstract: Philadelphia state senator Art Haywood, a proponent of Christian social justice, has surprised many with his election. He attempts to increase participation and involvement in the governing process.

headline: Offering 'companionship,' woman prostituted herself in Harrisburg Pike motel, police say
abstract: A Maryland woman faces prostitution and solicitation charges after being caught by an undercover policeman at a Harrisburg Pike motel. She was one of many women who met paying customers in hotels along the Pike, according to state police. The women used a website to post advertisements for 'companionship.'

headline: School Property Tax Debate
abstract: The state legislature has a skeletal budget framework, but remains gridlocked over the issue of school property taxes. The proposal is to raise the sales tax in order to lower the property tax, but this idea is facing strong backlash from school officials and legislators alike.

headline: 'Constitutional populist' may try to grab Republican nomination for governor away from Corbett
abstract: Self-proclaimed constitutional populist, Tom Lineaweaver is exploring the possibility of opposing PA Governor Tom Corbett for the republican nomination, Lineaweaver is an unemployed former disc jokey who wants to challenge "big government".

headline: New drug tracker hits a million-dollar snag
abstract: The full sum of the cost of a new drug prescription monitoring program was not added into the final state budget. This has prompted concerns from lawmakers over why the former administration did not place enough money into the program.

headline: PA Court Rules Against Wolf Over Union Favoritism
abstract: A PA judge has temporarily stopped an executive order issued by PA Governor Tom Wolf. The lawsuit filed accused Governor Wolf of unfairly benefiting unions.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Pair charged with impersonating cops, conducting bogus stops in South Philadelphia
abstract: A man and woman were arrested for impersonating Philadelphia police officers with badges and making two false pedestrian stops in the city. They were each charged with theft, attempted theft, receiving stolen property, robbery, conspiracy, and impersonating a public servant.

headline: Gov. Wolf: ‘Compromise’ in new state budget tax deal
abstract: As a possible budget agreement looms, PA Governor Tom Wolf has been scolded for his new tax policies. As part of his proposal, the sales tax would be raised to be the second highest in the country, and oil and gas frackers would get tax breaks.

headline: House panel to consider foreclosure bill
abstract: A bill that will allow delinquent low income homeowners to help with troubled payment agreements with local tax bureaus is scheduled for a vote by the House committee.

headline: John M. Morganelli: Why Gov. Wolf's so-called death penalty moratorium will fail
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf granted a death row inmate a reprieve and placed a moratorium on the death penalty. John Morganelli argues that reprieves can only be granted to give the defendant time to present new evidence at trial. Also, that the Governor does not have the authority to issue a moratorium on the death penalty.

headline: In Dunmore, an environmental mystery never slowed
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) released an investigation that pointed to Keystone Sanitary Landfill as the most likely source of harmful gases moving underground into borough homes. The DEP lasted from 1997 until 2003 with no real definitive answer for where the gases came from.

headline: Harrisburg Finally Has a Budget Deal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf and Republican legislators have agreed on a tentative budget deal for the state. The package includes a $350 million increase in basic education spending, pension and liquor system reforms, a broader sales tax, and static sales and personal income tax rates.

headline: Lobbyists see little love from Pennsylvania's Ethics Commission
