abstract: Ten organizations are being fined due to failure to properly disclose lobbying funds under PA law. Overall, lobbyists spent a reported $473 million last year. However, that number is likely higher because spending under $2,500 does not have to be reported to the Department of State.

headline: Gov. Wolf, AG Ask Court To Enforce UPMC, Highmark Consent Decree
abstract: The PA commonwealth court are being pushed by PA Governor Tom Wolf and the state attorney general to force the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and rival Highmark Inc. into binding arbitration.

headline: Gov. Wolf vetoes GOP-led plan to require Senate vet of PEMA director
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf vetoed a Republican-majority proposal that would require the Senate to confirm the governor's director pick for the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency. Wolf's administration called the move "blatant politicizing" since the position has been appointed by the governor for the past 30 years, while GOP legislators said it would be an important policy opportunity for the Senate.

headline: For Wolf, legal fights result form murky law
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf is facing his second legal challenge in less than a month as Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams is asking the PA Supreme Court to reject the Governor’s death penalty moratorium. Critics argue that granting reprieves can only be done on a case-specific basis and not used as a blanket measure to not enforce the death penalty.

headline: Grand Jury: What Kathleen Kane told the grand jury about leaks, and how it fits with testimony from her aides
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane has not denied sharing information about an old state probe into a former head of the Philadelphia Area NAACP with press. The grand jury presentment is calling for perjury, false statements, and obstruction of justice that would result in Kane's removal from office.

headline: York native among the 14 killed in San Bernardino shootings
abstract: A York, Pennsylvania native was among the 14 people killed in a mass shooting in San Bernardino, CA. Harry Bowman, 46, has two daughters and had lived in California for fifteen years, while his mother still lives in York. PA Governor Tom Wolf offered his condolences to Bowman's family and friends.

headline: Gas drilling may be issue in PA governor's race
abstract: The Democratic gubernatorial candidates have been adamant about challenging PA Governor Tom Corbett's policies on gas drilling. Consequentially, the candidates want to make this a key campaign issues for voters.

headline: After fracking ban, some New York towns want to secede
abstract: In response to New York’s decision to ban hydrologic fracking in their state, some southern New York towns are looking into ways to secede from New York and join PA.

headline: Penn State working to prevent spread of mumps after three possible cases were reported
abstract: After three possible cases of the mumps were reported at Penn State's University Park campus, the school is on high alert. The PA Department of Health plans to work closely with the school to prevent the spread of the extremely contagious disease, as college campuses tend to be extra vulnerable to the spread of diseases due to its communicative nature. University Health spokesperson Shelly Haffner is optimistic that the disease will not spread if infected students take the necessary measures.

headline: For the love of the game or parking spots, people of Shadyside can live with an ice rink
abstract: Residents of Shadyside, a town in Allegheny County, seem to be overwhelmingly in favor of the construction of an indoor ice rink at an old armory building, instead of an apartment complex that would add to the city's parking space shortage. The Urban Redevelopment Authority is expected to approve one of the three project proposals (the ice rink, apartments, or an office space) on December 10.

headline: Lawmakers should support Wolf's gas tax (YDR Opinion)
abstract: Facing a $1 billion deficit and a requirement to balance the budget, the author says that the State would do well to adopt Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s plan to impose a 5% severance tax on natural gas. The tax would still keep Pa competitive as well as generate necessary revenue. Republicans argued that the tax would be burdensome and hurt the growth of the industry.

headline: Philadelphia Eagles beat Dallas Cowboys, 33-27, in overtime thriller: Recap, photos and chatter
abstract: Coverage of the Philadelphia Eagles' primetime face-off against their rival the Dallas Cowboys.

headline: Pa. budget agreement may be collapsing
abstract: The tentative budget framework between PA Governor Tom Wolf and GOP legislators seems to be falling apart. Senate Republicans closed in on agreements with the governor about education funding and state pension and liquor reforms, while House Republicans said they were considering a different path that included none of those provisions. Wolf criticized lawmakers from both chambers for abandoning the plan they had agreed to.

headline: Pennsylvania legislators want to make state more business friendly to preserve jobs
abstract: In light of Florida Gov. Rick Scott’s visit to PA, lawmakers are committed to making Pa more business friendly. The goal is to reduce taxation and encourage local growth. One area of particular reform is to phase out the capital stock and franchise tax.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: Annie McCormick's husband pleads no contest in groping case
abstract: Local television News personality Annie McCormick's husband, Republican Lobbyist Andrew Marisco, has pleaded no contest to his sexual assault charges. While the Philadelphia DA's office maintains his guilt, McCormick maintains her husband's complete innocence. In the plea deal, Marisco will be under five years of supervised probation, as well as forced to pay restitutions to the victim.

headline: Private schools press Wolf to approve tax credits during Pa. stalemate
abstract: Pennsylvania private schools are calling on Governor Tom Wolf's administration to change its position and authorize up to $150 million in tax credits for their scholarship programs. Wolf said the expenditures are part of other educational funding decisions that cannot be made until the state has a budget, while private school officials say the money is vital to their operations.

headline: Capital recap: Which Pa. cities are most affected by tax exemption?
abstract: Voters will consider a constitution amendment that would grant the legislature more authority to determine what counts as charitable, and thus tax exempt properties in Pa. Another goal is to get these agencies involved in voluntary contribution services, thus payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT).

headline: Editorial: What will break the deadlock?
abstract: As the budget impasse nears its fourth month in Harrisburg, there seems to be no end in sight. The author believes that it will take the vetting of social services or the closing of schools to cause action. The cuts from inaction are being felt statewide, like in Northumberland County, where Commissioners are struggling to make ends meet to provide transportation for those needing dialysis, or in Mifflinburg, where schools are already beginning to tighten their belts.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf appoints union leader to Regional Port Authority board
abstract: John Dougherty has been appointed to the Regional Port Authority board by Pa Gov. Tom Wolf. Dougherty is a powerful union leader who leads the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 98.

headline: Meals on Wheels director took job right as budget impasse began
abstract: The executive director of Meals on Wheels for Northeastern PA, Kristen Kosin, who began her job at the start of the state’s budget impasse, is uncertain about the services the nonprofit organization will be able to provide to needy people in Lackawanna County if funding is not figured out soon. The social service agency operates on a budget to pay its volunteers, bills, and food expenses. If the state budget crisis is not resolved it may have to severely cut back on meals, borrow money from other sources, or shut down for good.

headline: Is there a trainwreck coming for the state budget framework, or simply a bump in the journey?
abstract: Discord among Republicans in the PA House and Senate about the details of a state budget may cause obstacles that could hold back its completion and passage. Lawmakers and Governor Tom Wolf agreed to a tentative framework about a month ago, but House Republicans may introduce a plan with several different components, including a $600 million decrease in spending and little increase in education funding. Governor Tom Wolf urged the legislature to stop stalling and come to an agreement.

headline: Perilous cargo: Another oil train disaster revives safety concerns
abstract: After the derailment and explosion at an oil train in West Virginia, reformers are asking that the U.S. Department of Transportation speed up its timeline for improvements to be made to trains to increase their safety standards.

headline: Financially strapped state universities are asked about their assets
abstract: Pennsylvania’s 14 state-owned universities are at the center of a debate over whether or not they are in danger of emptying their financial reserves or if there is untapped money that could be used to aid the struggling schools. Some board members of the State System of Higher Education claim that the millions of dollars that the universities hold in unrestricted net access could be put toward operations if necessary, while others say that the money is designated for specific campus projects. State System administrators were asked to present information about the schools’ management of the assets in the future.

headline: Road rescue: Finally, Congress delivers multiyear funding
abstract: U.S. Congress passed long-term transportation funding legislation for the first time in a decade, officially enacting a $305 billion plan that will pay for rail, bridge, and road projects across the country over the next five years. The Post-Gazette Editorial Board said that Congress should have increased the federal gas tax to generate revenue for the repairs instead of using one-time sources.

headline: Harrisburg School Board President Jennifer Smallwood resigns
abstract: Following new time pressures on a restructured job, Harrisburg School Board President Jennifer Smallwood has resigned. Smallwood was much beloved by her colleagues and her resignation took an emotional toll on the board. Smallwood will continue her work in public service as manager at the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency.

headline: Bernie O'Neill: Nonprofits show their political muscle
abstract: After localities have made numerous attempts to receive payments in lieu of taxes from nonprofits, the legislature is preparing to put a constitutional amendment that would grant the legislature broad powers to determine tax eligibility to a vote. The amendment would set clear parameters for what qualifies as tax exempt. Democrats oppose the bill due to concerns it could hurt urban tax bases.

headline: Flush for cash, Democrats first on TV in Supreme Court campaign
abstract: The Democratic candidates for three open seats on the PA Supreme Court aired campaign TV ads that were all positive in nature and highlighted their good character, political and personal backgrounds, and moral values. The candidates set a polite, nonpartisan tone for the race, which could grow more heated once the Republican Supreme Court candidates put out TV ads for their campaigns as well.

headline: Springsteen to open River Tour in Pittsburgh
abstract: Rock musician Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band will open their national, 24-date The River Tour 2016 at Consol Energy Center in Pittsburgh, PA on January 16.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: Baby bodies found in Kensington were 'medical specimens'
abstract: The corpses of two dead infants found in the Kensington area of Philadelphia recently have been determined by the Philadelphia medical examiner to be medical specimens, as the bodies were preserved in formaldehyde and previously operated upon. The Philadelphia police, however, have no idea who preserved and operated upon the dead infants, and are searching for whatever clues they can find.

headline: Reduce expenses, Wolf tells Cabinet
abstract: In an effort to decrease government expenses to balance the budget, Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has asked his cabinet to look for ways to reduce costs. He stressed it was not about cutting departments, but increasing their efficiency.

headline: Social media a double-edged sword for schools
abstract: Controversy has struck the Plum school district, as three teachers have been accused of having illicit relationships with underage students, and using social media to do so. The problem, however, does not stay in that district. Parents, teachers, and officials across many other PA districts have been debating the ethics of social media regulation and illicit teacher-student relationships for some time now, and many wonder whether regulatory policies need to be implemented.

headline: Pa. Senate in late-night session on budget
abstract: Members of the PA Senate met at the state Capitol on Sunday night to begin more budget negotiations with Governor Tom Wolf amid a dragged out stalemate and a previous agreement on the verge of collapsing.

headline: School officials lobby to keep taxing abilities
abstract: As the budget stalemate in Harrisburg trudges on without an end in sight, frustrated school children, teachers, and education officials have taken to the streets of Harrisburg to lobby PA legislators for a passed budget and funding for their schools. Besides the lack of funding, School officials are frustrated with the new plans for restructured tax policies, which they believe will disadvantage them in the long run.

headline: Healthy Regimen: Wolf's Medicaid expansion will improve access
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s Medicaid expansion clears the uncertainty and restrictions of his predecessor’s alternative, Healthy PA. This will allow more people to have access to affordable healthcare. People already enrolled in Healthy PA will not have to change anything as the state begins the transition.

headline: Pipeline Critics, Encouraged by Keystone Decision, Call for Halt to Mariner East 2
abstract: In the wake of President Obama killing the controversial Keystone XL pipeline bill, protesters have taken to PA to help stop a similar development, a natural gas pipeline that would send the natural gas from the Marcellus shale in western PA to the Delaware river in the East. Homeowners accuse energy magnate Sunoco for using eminent domain without the proper authority. Sunoco, however, maintains that they have the legitimate authority as a public utility company. The 2.5 billion dollar project, known as "Mariner East 2" remains in contention.

headline: On Budget, PA Senate Plows Ahead As House GOP Changes Course
abstract: As PA House Republicans break away from a tentative budget plan that was previously agreed to by the legislature and Governor Tom Wolf, the Senate is sticking to the framework. Some House representatives believe that Governor's increases in education funding and reform of the state pension and liquor systems, which took the longest to compromise on, come at too high a cost.

headline: Here's $360 million reasons to raise Pa.'s minimum wage: Art Haywood
abstract: PA State Sen. Art Haywood is calling for a raise for PA's minimum wage from $7.25 an hour to $10.10 an hour, and believes that such an increase will be beneficial to all Pennsylvanians. Haywood states that the wage increase for one million Pennsylvanians will bring in large amounts of new tax revenue, which will offset the $979 Million the state already spends on supplementing low wages in the state. Haywood also cites studies that show a raised minimum wage will not cost jobs, but rather create new, more profitable, and more livable employment opportunities for Pennsylvanians.

headline: DA says officials were slow to react to warnings at Monroeville Mall, in area
abstract: Allegheny County District Attorney Stephen A. Zappala criticized the mishandling of an active shooter situation at Monroeville Mall that left three people injured. Police apprehended the prime suspect an hour later, ascribing the delay to their efforts to help victims and secure the mall.

headline: Editorial: Voters have spoken — with their silence
abstract: In the fifth month of budget impasse, according to the author, it is hard not to get cynical. Following a historic election with an surprisingly low voter turnout, Harrisburg remains in partisan gridlock. Many people, including the author, have become hopeless that compromise will be reached, as PA Governor Tom Wolf and the GOP dominated legislature remain stuck in their respective issues.

headline: Pension reform proposal would make new plan optional for sitting lawmakers
abstract: Proposed reforms to Pennsylvania's major public pension systems, up for vote in the Senate, would allow legislators to remain in the current system if they chose to. All newly elected lawmakers would be required to join the new system, which combines a less secure benefits package with a 401(k) plan. PA Senate Republicans have made pension reform a priority in their budget negotiations with Governor Tom Wolf.

headline: Calls for greater pipeline safety in rural areas
abstract: As the network of Gas and Oil pipelines in Pennsylvania grows larger, PA State Senators from the more rural areas of the state, through which these pipelines flow free of safety requirements present in more populated areas, are calling for the pipelines to have those same restrictions. Senate Bill 1044 is calling for the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PUC) to enforce strict safety regulations on Rural pipelines, such as incident reporting and leak surveys. Currently, state law bars regulation of rural pipelines to be stricter than federal standards, but residents in those areas are calling for more safety and peace of mind over the pipelines that run through their properties.

headline: Capitolwire: House panel OKs liquor bill
abstract: The PA House of Representatives is preparing to pass a liquor privatization bill nearly identical to the one passed in the previous session. Leaders in the Senate are skeptical that privatizing in this fashion without pension reform will leave next year’s budget unbalanced. Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has expressed dislike for privatization overall.

headline: Top Wolf aide stands by tax-shift claims despite independent report fining of higher net taxes for all income groups
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf's tax reform proposals have caused dissenting opinions from Republican legislative leaders. They argue that the plan will result in higher net tax burdens for all.

headline: Pennsylvania deer hunters' good fortune benefits those in need
abstract: An abundant deer season for PA hunters last year provided Pennsylvania's Hunters Sharing the Harvest statewide program with over 2,000 pounds of deer meat to be distributed among soup kitchens and food pantries. The organization, which was started in 1991, received a total of 97,000 pounds of deer meat total in 2014 and is one of the oldest hunting donation programs in the country.

headline: After decades, Ben Franklin Parkway is hot
abstract: Following the heralded arrival of Pope Francis, the Benjamin Franklin Parkway in Philadelphia is teeming with new developments. Renovated parks, hotels, and apartments, are some of the many planned renovations to the historic parkway modeled after the Champs-Élysées. While local residents are excited for the new developments, their execution remains a headache to many. Regardless of the headaches, the vast and ambitious developments are giving a new sense of hope to city residents, as the historically ignored Parkway will hopefully transform into a vibrant area of commerce and tourism in the next few years.

headline: Next up on charters: Appeals
abstract: Charter school advocates are gearing up to make appeals on the School Reform Commission’s (SRC) decision to only approve five of the 39 charter applications it received. According to law, advocates can now make appeals for reversal directly to Harrisburg. Charter schools enroll nearly 31% of Philadelphia’s school children and a significant number are wait listed.

headline: Wolf's budget is a moment of truth for Pennsylvania. And we have to seize it: Jim Hertzler
abstract: The author is hopeful for the PA Governor Tom Wolf's "bold and ambitious" agenda. He hopes that partisanship will fall to the side and allow this agenda to benefit the state.

headline: Justice Eakin refuses Gov. Wolf's call to resign, Porngate flares
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Michael Eakin refused Governor Tom Wolf's call for him to step down from his position due to his role in sending offensive and pornographic emails to state law enforcement officials. Wolf said Eakin should resign because he could be biased in cases that involve women, African Americans, Latinos, and other groups of people derided in the emails.

headline: Syrian refugees in Lehigh Valley and Pennsylvania raise concerns
abstract: As the crisis in Syria grows worse, the 11.6 million displaced Syrians are seeking asylum and residence across the world. One of those places is the Lehigh Valley of PA, where a small number of Syrian refugees are settling in Allentown. The refugees are raising security concerns for the residents of those areas, especially in the already established Syrian community, who believe that the refugees may have radical leanings, coming from Anti-Government areas. PA Senator Pat Toomey believes that the settlement of refugees should be halted until a stronger security clearance process is available.

headline: Wolf's effort to fill Supreme Court vacancies collapses
abstract: Judge Thomas K. Kistler removed his nomination for the PA Supreme Court after he confirmed to have sent a racially insensitive e-mail. Legislators raised concerns about what implications the e-mail would have on Kistler’s ability to serve in the Court. The seat will remain vacant until November’s elections.

headline: Pa.'s Mumia Abu Jamal-inspired 'revictimization' law is 'manifestly unconstitutional,' U.S judge rules
abstract: A new PA state law that was designed to prevent criminals from revictimizing those harmed by their crimes has been ruled unconstitutional by a federal judge. This ruling was given because the law violated the free speech protections in the constitution.

headline: Capitolwire: 'Tentative' framework emerges in budget negotiations.
abstract: Amidst an extremely drawn-out and stalemated budget negotiation, there seems to be hope in Harrisburg. Legislators now have a skeletal and "tentative" budget agreement that seems to be concrete in providing extended funding for basic education, Pre-K, and special education in the state. However, the areas still up for debate include an expanded cigarette tax, gambling tax, and sales tax, as well as a property tax relief and the privatization of the state's liquor system. Lawmakers remain skeptical, yet hopeful that the state can agree on a budget and resume normal operations.

headline: Philly schools appeal ruling sparing teachers from health costs
abstract: The Philadelphia Public School System is appealing a decision from the School Reform Commission (SRC) to change health benefits to teachers that has the potential to save the district $200 million. The Commonwealth Court upheld a decision to withhold the changes last month.

headline: Plant flares emit more pollutants than previously thought, the EPA reports
abstract: The formula for calculating the pollutants released by flares at refineries and chemical plants nationally has been reviewed by the U.S Environmental Protection Agency and is for times higher than previously known.

headline: Police talk to boyfriend of woman killed in Fairmount Park
abstract: A grisly murder in Fairmount park has left Philadelphia detectives dumbfounded over the motive and identity of the killer, as the murderer fired nine shots into the back of a car, killing both members of a consummating couple. Police believe the murder to be "a crime of passion," and are actively investigating the other romantic ties of the slain Phliadelphians.

headline: Tapping budget brakes, PA GOP legislators rally behind new plan to control growth in state government spending
abstract: Fearing the return of big government spending, PA Republicans have unveiled a plan to only increase government spending as far as the increase in the average taxpayer’s income. This plan is to make the Government live within its means like any other family. Whether or not the plan becomes law, leaders are expected to keep the limits in mind in budget negotiations with the Governor.

headline: Audit says State System students continue to pay for lack of funding
abstract: The results of the State System of Higher Education show large tuition increases across the state. There are also shortcomings in the system's monitoring of campus crime reporting and cited inconsistencies in policies to prevent discrimination based on sex.

headline: Gov. Wolf, legislative leaders reaffirm commitment to budget framework
abstract: In a recent joint press conference, PA Governor Tom Wolf and legislative leaders stressed the fact that they are still heavily committed to passing the "tentative" budget agreement they have reached. The final budget, which would include pension reform and extended funding for basic education, will hopefully be passed by Thanksgiving.

headline: Pa. liquor privatization bill moves to House, vote coming this week
abstract: Pa Republicans are planning to introduce another liquor privatization bill nearly identical to the one passed in 2013. The bill would offer a wholesale sell-off of 1,200 licenses to counties depending upon population. Democrats are skeptical over the timing of the bill and believe it will be used as a bargaining chip in budget negotiations. Many Democrats prefer to modernize the system as opposed to privatization.

headline: Newsmaker you should know / Mt. Lebanon doctor plans to use Alaskan experience in his new job
abstract: Dr. Eric Lantzmann a certified OB/GYN from Mt. Lebanon ,PA, turned his sights to Alaska after residency in San Francisco. In Alaska, the PA native was astounded by the "patient centered" program instituted by the native Alaskans in their health care system. Lantzmann, upon his return back to PA, hopes to implement a similar practice in his hometown.

headline: Pittsburgh Public Schools' budget plan decreases deficit spending, holds steady on taxes
abstract: Pittsburgh public schools have released a preliminary budget that includes a decrease in deficit spending and does not raise taxes. New revenue sources in the city have lead to the newly balanced budget.

headline: "Paycheck protection" constitutional amendment moves one step closer to passage
abstract: A bill that would bar state government and public schools from collecting union dues from paychecks is moving closer to being put on the ballot as a constitutional amendment. Democrats opposed the bill seeing it as opening the door to future restrictive measures on unions from collecting funds.

headline: Pennsylvania budget framework unveiled at Capitol: Higher sales tax, lower property taxes at core
abstract: As a 133 day budget impasse continues to plague Harrisburg, there seems to be light at the end of the tunnel. In the new budget, there would be a significant property tax relief, aimed mostly at helping schools, on the back of a sales tax hike and gambling revenue, among other things. Even though it seems like the two sides have found common ground, it will still take major compromise for it to be passed, and compromise has a dangerous word in Harrisburg.

headline: Don't like strip searches? Tough, U.S. court tells former prison inmate
abstract: Former Susquehanna County prison inmate Edwin Blaisure has lost his class-action civil rights lawsuit against correction officers for what he believed to be unconstitutional strip-searches. While Blaisure cited his fourth amendment rights, corrections officers cited recent smuggling of weapons into the prison facility; making the searches necessary to security.

headline: Wolf keeping quiet on details of budget plan
abstract: For months, Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has been quiet on the intricate details of his policy positions and that is continuing. Wolf said he plans to keep the specifics of his budget close to him until he presents his budget in early March. Leaders in the Legislature claim they only have rumors and not specifics on the budget either.

headline: Pennsylvania budget framework unveiled at Capitol: Higher sales tax, lower property taxes at core
abstract: As the budget stalemate in Harrisburg continues, the Titusville area school district has postponed debate over whether or not to take out a priavte loan to cover the lack of funding from the state. State funding in Titutsville makes up 65-70% of the districts total budget, making a private loan one of the only viable solutions. The district's immediate need for money is not unique, as many other districts across the state are looking forward to hard times with the budget impasse continuing.

headline: Pa. Attorney General Kane held for trial on latest criminal counts
abstract: Former PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane is now caught up in even more criminal charges, this time for perjuring herself under investigation of her previous criminal charges. Kane allegedly leaked secret information about a 2009 grand jury in order to slander a rival prosecutor, and then perjured herself while under investigation about the charge. Kane will face her second trial after facing one earlier for multiple criminal charges.

headline: Tom Wolf's death penalty moratorium: What it means for Eric Frein, Seth Williams and everyone on Death Row
abstract: Two weeks after Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s moratorium on the death penalty was issued, several have risen in support and opposition. Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams claimed the Governor has no legal authority to issue a moratorium. The Governor is planning to grant reprieves to anyone convicted to a death sentence, which Williams says is a gross misuse of reprieves.

headline: Strong medicine: UPMC and Highmark need a shot of arbitration
abstract: A breach between UPMC and Highmark left many Western PA seniors with no health coverage. PA Governor Tom Wolf and other state officials petitioned the Commonwealth Court to force both parties into binding arbitration.

headline: Petition to dismiss Officer Lisa Mearkle 'as American as baseball, apple pie' and First Amendment, organizer says
abstract: Lisa Murkle, Hummelstown PA police officer, was recently acquitted on counts of murder and manslaughter last week after fatally tazing and shooting a 59 year old Hummelstown man. In the wake of the acquittal, a petition has surfaced calling for Murkle's removal from the force, forcing  a meeting of the Hummelstown borough council on the matter. The family of the slain believes the officer should not return to the force, and has filed an excessive force case in federal court.

headline: Reed discusses expectations for Gov. Wolf's budget address
abstract: Pa Majority Leader Dave Reed has stated that he has no hard documents on the details of Pa Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget. He is convinced that the Governor will look over pension reform, healthcare, property tax reform, severance taxes and education spending.

headline: Montgomery County DA to widen investigation of attorney general Kane
abstract: The Montgomery County district attorney (DA) will expand the investigation of Attorney General Kathleen Kane because of information that was disclosed that should have been subject to secrecy requirements. The DA will investigate and make charges based upon a fair analysis of the legal standards.

headline: Pool contractor must pay $2.6M
abstract: The vice president of a former Southern New Jersey pool company has been ordered to pay 2.6 Million dollars to disgruntled former customers. According to the New Jersey Attorney General's office, customers paid to have inground pools installed that were never to be finished. Due to this, and the civil proceedings that followed, the former VP of the company has been ordered to pay 2.6 Million in restitution.

headline: Medical marijuana's future looks hazy in the Pa. House
abstract: A new Governor has reinvigorated medical marijuana advocates after the Senate passed a bill that would support legalization. The bill will face trouble in the House where it is unclear how the body will vote. Majority Leader Dave Reed stressed the need to produce a bill that meets medical needs but prevents abuses. He said he is willing to work with members to produce a bill everyone is comfortable with.

headline: Study: $10.10 minimum wage would boost Pa. workers, economy
abstract: Over a million workers in PA would benefit from a $10.10 minimum wage as concluded by a study released by an economic think tank. The study details affects of raising the minimum wage in each of PA's 67 counties, which has not been raised since 2007.

headline: Philanthropies put spotlight on Pa. budget impasse's effect on social services
abstract: The Pittsburgh foundation and United Way of Pittsburgh, two humanitarian organizations vital to helping the elderly and homeless of Western PA,   have teamed up to launch a joint campaign to lobby PA Governor Tom Wolf and the PA state legislature to hastily pass a budget that includes the currently held up 76 Million dollars in aid for their organizations. The campaign, heralded on social media as #PApeoplecount, is mainly web-based, and encourages people to call their representatives and encourage a budget agreement.

headline: Canon-McMillan administrators join governor-elect's education team
abstract: Among the 20 people involved in PA Gov.-elect Tom Wolf's transition team are two administrators from Canon-McMillan School District in Washington County. Both are interested in helping to identify strengths and weaknesses of the previous administration's policies with specific regards to education.

headline: DA to seek death penalty against man accused of setting wife on fire
abstract: Allegheny District Attorney Stephen A. Zappala will seek the death penalty against a man accused of murdering his wife by setting her on fire. The DA said that Gov. Wolf’s moratorium will not stop him from seeking the punishment.

headline: Free bus rides to state employees don't violate Wolf's gift ban
abstract: Lebanon Transit is offering free bus rides to state employees in honor of State Employee Recognition Day as well as promoting ridership. State employees accepting the rides would not violate PA Governor Tom Wolf's ban on accepting gifts because the offer is not exclusive to state employees.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: Porngate investigator steps aside after Daily News report
abstract: Following a Philadelphia Daily News exposé, the chief counsel for the states judicial conduct board, Robert Graci, has stepped aside, after it was revealed that he was close friends and political allies with Michael Eakin, the PA supreme court justice he was supposed to be investigating for misconduct. Also involved in the fray is disgraced Attorney General Kathleen Kane, who made public racist and sexually explicit emails sent by justice Eakin.

headline: Gas tax, vehicle fees increase
abstract: As part of a $2.3B investment into the state's infrastructure, signed by Pa. Gov. Tom Corbett, PA drivers can expect to see an increase in vehicle fees, mostly dealing with registration. All increases are tagged to a cost of living adjustment every two years. The new law changes the way PA infrastructure is funded and is looking to repair a significant amount of ailing roads and bridges.

headline: Pa-Gov.: Wolf Thinks PA Has a "Self-Esteem" Problem (VIDEO)
abstract: In a speech made before the National Governors Association in Washington, D.C., Pa Gov. Tom Wolf said that PA has a “self-esteem” problem in that the State does not do all it can to promote the numerous benefits it can offer.

headline: Baltimore riots: Can it happen in Harrisburg?
abstract: In light of the race riots in Baltimore, there is discussion of whether similar events will erupt in Harrisburg. Some believe that PA's capital city has initiatives and dialogues in place to ward off such violence. Others, because of calls for a national rally, believe that Harrisburg is not excluded from violent race riots.

headline: Highmark: Getting cancer care from UPMC to cost less
abstract: Highmark insurance subscribers who use UPMC facilities will soon be getting cancer care for less, thanks to new arbitration and negotiations between the two healthcare moguls. The two healthcare companies have been battling over cancer care costs in recent years, but their newfound agreements will provide added benefits to members and keep the companies competitive in the market place.

headline: Castille cut independent figure as Pa. chief justice
abstract: Pa Supreme Court Chief Justice Ron Castille has reached the mandatory retirement age of 70 and will be stepping down, to be replaced by Thomas Saylor. Elected in 1993, Castille played important roles in redistricting and declaring parts of Gov. Tom Corbett's Marcellus Shale laws unconstitutional.

headline: In PA, moms lead charge for medical marijuana
abstract: Latrisha “Lolly” Bentch is the mother of Anna Bentch. Anna suffers from over twelve seizures a day that do not respond to pharmaceuticals. After seeing positive effects on a girl in a similar situation while using medical marijuana, Lolly has taken up the fight for medical marijuana in Pa. Originally the position of far left liberals, medical marijuana has gained a new ally in the Governorship. The PA Senate has passed a bill to legalize medical marijuana and the bill is moving to the House.

headline: New this year: Philly schools with no nurses
abstract: Due to a difficult financial crisis and budget cuts, the Philadelphia School District is short on nurse coverage for students, with some schools not receiving any coverage at all.  Parents and critics voiced their outrage, saying that the current nurses are traveling between schools so often during the week that they may not be there to help students who are in need of medical attention. Several school principals are concerned about what the lack of coverage means for them in the case of a student health emergency without a trained professional present.

headline: Pa. mother of 8 shot dead in argument over diaper money
abstract: A Pittsburgh mother of 8 was recently slain, seemingly in an argument over money for diapers and wet wipes. During the argument, a gun was drawn, and the struggle for the firearm resulted in the death of Marqua Wilson, mother of 8. Authorities in Pittsburgh say that Wilson had previously filed a restraining order against her killer.

headline: State should restrict unjust forfeitures
abstract: Instead of waiting for an appeal on a case dealing with police seizing the home of a woman whose son was allegedly selling $200 of marijuana, the legislature should enact reforms to reign in the use of civil forfeiture. Originally intended as a weapon against the drug trade, it has evolved into a revenue generating option for police forces.

headline: Fix entire tax structure
abstract: A recent study found that Pa has the sixth worst tax structure amongst the fifty states. Legislators were shocked by Florida Gov. Rick Scott’s visit to Pa to pitch the tax benefits of Florida to Pa businesses. The author argues it is important to not just fix one tax, but the entire tax structure in order to make Pa more competitive.

headline: State Senate election draws sharp ads
abstract: A vacant Senate seat in the South Hills suburb of Pittsburgh, PA is up for special election in November 2015, and the campaign generated harsh attack ads from both the Democratic and Republican sides.  GOP nominee Guy Reschenthaler and the state Republican Party claimed that Democrat Heather Arnet an “extreme” liberal who wanted to freeze property taxes for seniors. The Senate Democratic Campaign Committee aired a TV ad warning that Arnet’s opponent would cut Medicare and Social Security and raise property taxes. Both candidates are set on gaining the support of elderly voters, who are most likely to vote in off-year elections.

headline: Hurricane' Schwartz's 19th annual winter forecast
abstract: Following record breaking winters beforehand, Philadelphia braces for a somewhat mild winter, behind the portentous "El Nińo" in play this year. El Nińo, a weather phenomenon that warms the ocean temperatures, is sure to create more frequent, wet days, and stronger but less frequent snow storms.

headline: Fla. Area set to eclipse Meadowcroft as oldest site of human habitation
abstract: Vero Beach in Florida has been discovered to have had human settlement nearly 3,000 years before Meadowcroft, PA -- the current place where it was believed humans first settled.

headline: Capitolwire: Pennsylvania's Keystone problem
abstract: After results from the Pennsylvania System of Standardized Assessments (PSSAs) failed to meet standards, the Dept. of Education introduced the Keystone Exams. The implementation of both the Keystones and PSSAs have put an undue burden upon school districts and has achieved little change in academic performance. This has prompted legislators to begin looking into ways to reform the system to take costs off of school districts.

headline: Kiski Area latest school district caught in budget impasse
abstract: Kiski Area School District in Allegheny Township, PA is expected to apply for a $15 million loan through First Commonwealth Bank in order to be able to pay its bills in the wake of the state budget impasse. If the action is approved by the school board the bank loan would only help the district until April 2016, according to Kiski Area business manager Peggy Gillespie. At the same time, district officials want to move forward with plans for an athletic stadium complex in the district, but face concern from board members and township residents about the project’s economic impact.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf: budget compromise 'moves Pennsylvania forward' with higher sales tax but lower property taxes
abstract: Although PA Governor Tom Wolf would like to have included more of his own agenda in the new PA budget, he is confident that Pennsylvanians will benefit from a lower property tax and more school funding. Democratic Representatives are faithful that the restructured tax system will benefit those who need it most. Governor wolf is also remiss that the Republicans have struck down a tax on shale oil.

headline: Dennis Roddy: Beware casting the proverbial first stone at Ben Carson for his religious theories
abstract: Following U.S. Presidential candidate Ben Carson's comments that the Egyptian pyramids were used to store grain, rather than sarcophagi, has stirred much controversy as well as a sharp criticism from former PA Gov Tom Corbett aide Dennis Roddy. Roddy believes that religion has become too intertwined with our political lives and that religious people often do not understand the follies of their own faiths.

headline: Gillen drops out of race for mayor
abstract: Terry Gillen, former advisor to Mayor Nutter and Rendell, has become the first Democratic candidate to drop out of the race for Philadelphia's Mayor. She cited failure to meet fundraising goals as the reason.

headline: Pa. House again passes plan to sell off state stores
abstract: After heated debate, the Pa. House has passed a plan to sell off state stores in a new attempt to privatize liquor. Republicans argued the stores were increasingly unprofitable and better served in the private sector. Democrats argued that the Liquor Control Board was suffering from Republican attempts to block legislation to aid the agency in the hopes to further privatization.

headline: Lawyer: State Sen. Pat Browne will seek ARD for DUI
abstract: PA Senator Pat Browne will seek placement in a program for first-time DUI offenders to avoid two drunken driving charges for a motorcycle crash in May. If Browne is accepted into the accelerated rehabilitative disposition (ARD) program and completes it, he will avoid serving three days in prison and paying a $1,000 fine, and his criminal record will be expunged. Browne may be eligible for the program because his last drunken driving arrest was over 10 years ago, which would qualify the May accident as a first-time offense.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: The Kane Circus gets another ring - and voters get taken for a ride: Analysis
abstract: Shortly after Attorney General Kathleen Kane attended a preliminary hearing for her Grand Jury leak in 2009, the disgraced official has found herself accused of power abuses and defamation of her fellow prosecutors. These charges come from another disgraced official, Frank Fina, a major part of the "Porngate" scandal, where PA supreme court justices exchanged raunchy emails with one another.

headline: Study: Navigational skills help improve brain functions
abstract: A new study has shown that strong navigational skills help strengthen cognitive functions, asserting that the modern age of GPS mayu actually have negative effects on brain development. According to the study those with a strong sense of direction have an enlarged hippocampus, the section of the brain involved in route planning and navigation, and that a stronger sense of development leads to more tissue development in that area. Regardless of the positive effects, many people still rely on GPS for navigation.

headline: Congress gets ready for action -- and inaction
abstract: The 114th Congress, now under full Republican control, is working quickly to put forth their agenda. Trade deals, immigration, and Keystone XL are among the issues that Congress wants to pass. Mixed support for the issues may lead to increased confrontation between President Obama and Congress.

headline: Pennsylvania medical marijuana hearing touches on tracking, delivery, concerns, and support
abstract: Specialists gathered in Harrisburg to deliver testimony on the proposed legalization of medical marijuana. Opponents warned that the THC in marijuana is highly addictive and leads to the possibility of addiction. Supporters claim that natural marijuana has little addictive properties and has been shown to grant relief to patients suffering from chronic diseases. Opponents also stated that there is not conclusive medical science to suggest that medical marijuana does not have negative long-term effects.

headline: School selection deadline is Nov. 13
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is accepting enrollment and transfer applications for its School Selection Process through November 13, open to K-12 students who want to apply to schools that are outside of their neighborhood district boundaries. The article provides several application tips for families within and outside of the school district.

headline: Geisinger unveils pilot program that refunds co-pays to unhappy patients
abstract: Geisinger, a local healthcare provider, has started a pilot program that will refund surgery co-pays to dissatisfied patients. The program, which will be used on a digital app, will ask patients about their satisfaction of every part of the surgery process, and will ask them how much of their co-pay they want returned. Healthcare experts remain skeptical over whether or not this will become the norm in the industry.

headline: Task force debates pipeline recommendations
abstract: Recently, PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) secretary John Quigley claimed that he had amassed an extremely large task force to deal with the states massive influx of Gas pipelines. The 48 member panel recently put forward a report of more than 180 separate recommendations to deal with the problem. As the task force battles infighting and stalemate, they plan to have the final plan out by February.

headline: Wolf taps two for Revenue, Economic Development posts
abstract: Pa. Gov.-elect Tom Wolf has named two individuals with decades of economic policy experience to serve in his cabinet. Eileen H. McNulty, revenue secretary under former Gov. Robert P. Casey will once again fill that role. Dennis M. Davin will serve as Secretary of Community and Economic Development. Wolf still has 22 other positions to fill.

headline: Wolf: Team finds $100 million in government savings
abstract: Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf created the Governor’s Office of Transformation, Innovation, Modernization and Efficiency (GO-TIME). The agency was tasked with finding $150 million of savings in government expenditure. Gov. Wolf was happy to have received 157 recommendations totaling $109 million in savings.

headline: State schools hope to freeze tuition with budget request
abstract: Pennsylvania’s 14 state-run universities are looking to prevent tuition increases for students for the 2016-2017 academic year by asking for more funds. The State System of Higher Education is asking PA lawmakers for over $108 million in aid while they are in the middle of a lengthy budget stalemate. Without additional state funding the schools would likely have to make budget, maintenance, and operation cuts of their own, and tuition would continue to rise at an inflated rate. The universities have not received an increase in funding from the state since 2008.

headline: Hundreds rally in Wyomissing for elimination of property taxes
abstract: Lawmakers in Wyomissing, PA, who have long lobbied for the elimination of school property taxes, watched hundreds gather to rally against the elimination of such a levy recently. Wyomissing and the surrounding Berks county have long been a hot spot for the elimination of the tax, and the new fervor over such a tax comes surrounding the vote on a PA senate bill that would eliminate the tax and subsidize it with other taxes. Despite the apparent fervor, opposition remains from groups that benefit from the tax, such as realtors and educators.

headline: Task force debates pipeline recommendations
abstract: Recently, PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) secretary John Quigley claimed that he had amassed an extremely large task force to deal with the states massive influx of Gas pipelines. The 48 member panel recently put forward a report of more than 180 separate recommendations to deal with the problem. As the task force battles infighting and stalemate, they plan to have the final plan out by February.

headline: Forced pooling policies remain unclear in Pennsylvania's shale plays
abstract: A controversial section of a 53-year-old piece of legislation failed to meet its test in court as the filer, Hilcorp, withdrew its complaint because the courts failed to issue a statement after 45 days. The law dealt with Utica shale and how a company can drill if the landowner did not authorize it. However, it is unclear how the law applies to Marcellus Shale and now, with the case withdrawn, it remains unclear.

headline: Republicans Angry with Wolf Over Reports of Sales Tax Hike
abstract: PA Republicans are accusing Pa Gov. Tom Wolf of breaking a campaign promise by allegedly proposing to increase the sales tax from 6% to 6.6%.

headline: Disappointed by Wolf bullying
abstract: The author criticizes PA Governor Tom Wolf for threatening to withdraw support for the PA State System of Higher Education to gain approval for a tuition freeze next year. The system of higher education plays too large of a role in educating young people to be bullied by politics.

headline: Fair forfeiture or the drug dealer's 'bill of rights'?
abstract: Pennsylvania's asset forfeiture policy allows police officers to seize illegal gains from drug dealers and other criminals, but it also takes property from citizens who have not yet been accused of a crime or have not committed a crime at all. Legislators and reform advocates are looking to Allegheny County's law enforcement, which carries out most of its forfeitures after criminal conviction and only seizes property directly involved in the crime, to change the policy throughout the state.

headline: Troopers see drop in accidents over New Year's holiday
abstract: State police were happy to see much fewer accidents this holiday season compared to last.

headline: To Tom Wolf: Childhood trauma is the elephant in the classroom
abstract: The author, having worked in urban education for 14 years, has asked the Governor and Education Secretary to begin taking steps to address the problem of childhood trauma in the classroom. Trauma has the potential to affect a student’s mental health and learning ability for their entire life. The author said the issue is rarely addressed and pleaded that the new administration be leading force for reform.

headline: Letter to the Editor: Wolf budget plan is good for business
abstract: The author praises PA Governor Tom Wolf's approach to improving the competitiveness of the state's business climate. The Governor will put an end to capital stock, franchise taxes, and even cut corporate taxes.

headline: What does Penn State football coach James Franklin's office look like?: Unseen Penn State
abstract: The author takes readers on a descriptive tour of Penn State football coach James Franklin's private office.

headline: In a big tent moment, Pennsylvania's House Republican caucus gets its first African-American member in more than 20 years
abstract: Rep. Harry Lewis Jr. is the first African-American member of the PA House GOP since 1992. He hopes to bring new perspectives to the GOP, but maintains that he never ran as a race-based candidate. He intends to fight for issues concerning school funding, property tax reform, open space preservation, and economic growth.

headline: Next steps after DEP landfill meeting
abstract: After completing a review of Keystone Sanitary Landfill’s plans for expansion, the Pa Department of Environmental Protection will hold public testimony to gather residential feelings towards the expansion.

headline: DEP hearing on rules for oil and gas wells shows sharp divisions
abstract: Hundreds of residents voiced their concerns over PA's proposed revisions to the state's environmental standards at oil and gas well sites to representatives from the PA Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: Paris terror fuels fear of American Muslims
abstract: Maher Khalil, a 28-year-old Philadelphia resident, spoke about the discrimination he experienced when airline employees banned him and a relative from boarding a flight because passengers were unnerved by their speaking Arabic. Similar incidents of bias and fear involving Arab Americans and Muslims have resurfaced in the wake of the ISIS terrorist attacks in Paris.

headline: Want to be a state lawmaker? Take a drug test, PA rep says
abstract: A PA State Representative has introduced a bill that would require elected officials to take a urine test to determine previous drug use. While widely popular among the people, the PA Senate never took up the bill and the ACLU of Pennsylvania opposes it due to constitutional issues.

headline: Another bill restricting union dues collection advances in Pa. Senate
abstract: Another attempt to pass “paycheck protection” has made its way out of the Senate. The goal of the legislation is to restrict unions’ ability to use state money automatically deducted from paychecks for political purposes. The lack of a committee hearing has raised many concerns amongst legislators.

headline: PA-Gov Wolf Endorses Dougherty for Supreme Court
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf officially endorsed Kevin Dougherty for state Supreme Court, according to mailers printed by Dougherty’s campaign. Dougherty, who serves as the Administrative Judge of the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas Trial division, is running for one of three open seats on the Court.

headline: As key #PABudget pieces start to move, will Wolf, lawmakers wring out a holiday miracle?
abstract: Different paths between the Senate and PA Governor Tom Wolf and House Republicans could cause more trouble on the road to a budget agreement. The legislative chambers are on separate pages after the House abandoned a budget framework in favor of their own spending plan. Wolf and Democrats are growing more frustrated as the impasse drags on.

headline: Chief Justice Thomas Saylor: Six things you might not know about him
abstract: After hitting the mandatory retirement age of 70, Chief Justice Ron Castille presided over the swearing in of his successor, Thomas Saylor.

headline: Cash hoard still unjustified
abstract: In order to ensure payroll is met during budget impasses, legislative caucuses collect large sums of money and hold it on reserve. The author argues that this practice incentivizes the legislature to be less serious about passing a budget on time and should be outlawed.

headline: Forget the games: craft a state budget without expanded gambling
abstract: The Editorial Board of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette chided PA legislators for their talk of possibly expanding gambling game options in the budget to generate more state revenue. The Board said that the social impact, licensing fees, and long-term economic impact of gambling are all factors that state officials need to consider before including it in the budget.

headline: Pennsylvania focuses on renewables in latest energy plan
abstract: Pennsylvania's Department of Environmental Protection drafted an update of the state's climate change action plan. The draft focuses on a large expansion of renewable energy sources in the state, such as natural gas, in an effort to reduce extremely high levels of carbon and greenhouse gas emissions.

headline: Emissions reporting: Drillers have the same duty as other industries
abstract: A group of nine environmentalist groups filed suit to force the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to mandate gas drillers to report emissions to the Federal Toxic Release Inventory. The EPA claims gas drillers do not make minimum requirements for reporting.

headline: Massive Anthem data breach may affect up to 750,000 Pennsylvanians
abstract: As many as 750,000 Pennsylvanians could have been affected by a data hack on health insurance companies. Such information as names, addresses, medical IDs, Social Security numbers, birthdays, and even job and income data may have been leaked. Pa Attorney General Kathleen Kane has looked into the case in order to best serve residents of the State and has asked those affected to contact her office.

headline: Neshaminy school board tackles state budget woes, receives consolidation updates
abstract: The school board in Neshaminy, PA put pressure on state legislators and Governor Tom Wolf to pass a budget for the 2015-2016 fiscal year, citing the lack of funds for school districts as a negative result of the impasse.

headline: Let's hope UPMC-Highmark breakup works out for us children
abstract: The author writes that the complicated separation of Pittsburgh health care provider UPMC-Highmark in a recent state Supreme Court case means that the individual entities will have to prove their medical care abilities to their respective patients in Western PA.

headline: Pa. needs a fair school funding formula: PennLive letters
abstract: Several statewide organizations are gathering to advocate for a fair funding formula for Pa. schools. The advocates expressed hope that the legislatively established Basic Education Funding Commission will be successful.

headline: Gov. Tom Wolf unveils business tax and jobs plan
abstract: In a speech at the Bethlehem Steel Factory, Pa Gov. Tom Wolf unveiled part of his economic plan that he says will rejuvenate the Pa Economy. He plans to lower the 9.99% corporate tax to 4.99% by 2018, eliminate the capital stock and trade tax, as well as create a graduated personal income tax. There are rumors that Wolf will also seek increasing the income tax and sales tax in his 2015-2016 budget.

headline: PA, WV, OH team up on shale gas related manufacturing and chemical development
abstract: The states of Pennsylvania, West Virginia, and Ohio put aside their competitive past towards natural gas chemical projects and announced a joint effort to develop programs for shale gas manufacturing in their regions. The states agreed to support infrastructure that transports natural gas and related products through the Appalachian Basin and promote environmental practices in the area. PA Governor Tom Wolf said the collaboration is necessary to ensure that the states have a strong energy workforce.

headline: Measure to remove Kane to go before full Senate
abstract: The Senate is expected to vote on whether to hold a formal hearing for Attorney General Kathleen Kane from office due to criminal charges against her and the suspension of her law license. Kane would be allowed to testify and her lawyer would speak on her behalf; if the hearing committee feels that Kane cannot actively perform her duties, the full Senate would vote on whether to remove her.

headline: Online voter registration getting new look
abstract: Several PA lawmakers are promising to introduce bills that would bring online voter registration to PA. The idea is widely popular, but some have concerns over security issues. Supporters claim that it will increase participation while decreasing costs.

headline: Can Tom Wolf really kill the death penalty?
abstract: The PA Constitution does not grant the Governor the ability to ban the death penalty, but instead grant reprieves on a case-specific basis that gives defendants the chance to present new evidence in trial. Gov. Wolf has declared he will issue reprieves on every death sentence in the Commonwealth until the report on capital punishment launched by the legislature is completed. Wolf’s actions have drawn criticism as an abuse of power.

headline: Unorthodox mayor seeks upset in Pennsylvania Senate primary
abstract: John Fetterman, the mayor of Braddock, PA, is considered the most unconventional candidate in the state’s Senate election because of his extreme height, tattoos, and motorcycle biker appearance. He is an outsider who is running against established Democrats Katie McGinty and Joe Sestak on a platform of issues that include the legalization of marijuana, gun control, immigration reform, and gay rights. Fetterman received national attention and praise for his work to revitalize the struggling Pittsburgh suburb of Braddock as mayor over the last ten years. It has yet to be seen whether Fetterman will be able to reach the same level of fundraising, campaign money, and recognition as his opponents.

headline: Steelers' Michael Vick looking for support for lifesaving pet legislation
abstract: Pittsburgh Steelers football player Michael Vick is lobbying Harrisburg legislators to pass the Pets in Cars bill, which would allow police officers to remove cats or dogs locked inside cars with life-threatening hot temperatures. Vick became an animal rights advocate after being convicted for dogfighting several years ago.

headline: Improvements on the way at two Johnstown arts venues
abstract: With money from both local sources and the state, several arts venues in Johnstown’s Cambria City neighborhood will be made. Bottle Works and the Art Works building of Bottle Works will make improvements designed for increased revenue and sustainability.

headline: Help pouring in for Bradford in water crisis
abstract: Pa Gov. Tom Wolf has sent the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency and the National Guard to aid the City of Bradford in restoring water to nearly 18,000 people.

headline: The three messages that haunt Gov. Tom Wolf and what he can do to fix them
abstract: The author criticized PA Governor Tom Wolf for choosing a biased communications team that he believes is now struggling to operate professionally, based on their use of campaign-like messages to voters. Communication errors that the author mentions include a lack of substance behind Wolf’s repetitive promise to place a severance tax on natural gas, insistence that Wolf’s budget proposal comes without gimmicks (although it contains tax increases), and an incorrect focus on PA’s low credit as the reason for more spending.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Inquirer staff
headline: How Obama Thinks About Terrorism
abstract: The author cites The Atlantic's analysis of President Obama's views on terrorism. According to the analysis, unlike Republican politicians, Obama sees radical jihadism as a small faction within Islam and argues that ISIS is turning to weaker, less complicated forms of violence and losing in the Middle East.

headline: Here's why we need to kill the death penalty: Daylin Leach
abstract: PA State Sen. Daylin Leach responded to Maureen Faulkner, the widow of a police officer killed by Mumia Abu-Jamal, who supports the death penalty. Sen. Leach said that the death penalty can execute innocent people, is too costly, and has already been eliminated in large parts of the world.

headline: Lt. Gov. Stack Meets With Israeli Delegation
abstract: Pa Lt. Gov. Mike Stack has met with representatives from Israel as the first of many meetings in an attempt to increase cooperation between Israel and Pennsylvania. Pa Gov. Tom Wolf plans to issue a memorandum of understanding in order to increase the relationship of the two states.

headline: Editorial: One last chance for Chester Upland
abstract: Chester Upland School District in Delaware County, PA, which has been under state control for several decades due to financial failure, was given another chance to regain its footing. Delaware County Common Pleas Judge Chad Kenney granted the district more state funding and approved a new plan to solve an ongoing conflict of reimbursing local charter schools for special education students. The new measures reduce the amount paid to the district’s three charter schools from $40,000 to $27,000 per student, add another $20 million in state funds, and erase the debt the district currently owes to the charters.

headline: Deadline nears for certain seniors to withdraw from IRAs
abstract: December 31 is the deadline for senior citizens age 70 and 1/2 or older to withdraw the required minimum distribution from any Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs) they own, or else face a tax penalty that could amount to 50 percent of what they should have taken out. The rule was put in place to prevent IRA owners from hoarding retirement savings and delaying their tax payments.

headline: New PA law prompts rescinding of municipal gun measures
abstract: A new law that allows residents to sue municipalities if they believe that the local gun laws are not in line with state laws. Many municipalities have repealed laws to avoid the legal fight, but others are standing strong saying the law was improperly passed. The NRA has not yet commented, but said it will monitor municipal laws for compliance.

headline: Editorial: Legislature must get its fiscal act together
abstract: The author describes an inherent hypocrisy over how the Legislature has demanded that school districts and municipalities use austerity to get their fiscal situation in balance while the state’s situation is less than balanced. The author also points out that the Legislature itself has a $161 million surplus in its administrative budget.

headline: Pa. Senate passes bill curbing union dues collections
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate passed a bill that would make it more difficult for unions in the public sector to automatically collect political contributions and dues from members. Republican supporters say the controversial piece of legislation will prevent government resources from being used for political gain by union members, while opponents of the bill believe it is an attack on collective bargaining and unions in general.

headline: Governor Wolf joined state officials and the National Guard to help bring joy to families in need
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf, along with the National Guard and state officials, gave nearly 200 presents to needy families through a Harrisburg holiday gift program.

headline: Idea for gas terminal off East Coast rankles fracking foes
abstract: Proposals to build an offshore facility to produce natural gas has caught the attention of environmentalists who believe the project is dangerous and unnecessary. Others worry that the facility will quickly be turned into an export facility. Supporters argue it would be easier to build this facility than have gas pumped from nearby PA.

headline: Educators ready to cheer Wolf's budget
abstract: Educators are looking forward to Pa. Gov. Tom Wolf’s budget address where he promised to restore the $1 billion of education funding cut by former Gov. Tom Corbett. Wolf has stated he plans to implement a severance tax on natural gas to pay for the education increases. The lack of resources in school districts have prompted many to sue the state government for failure to uphold a constitutional obligation to provide adequate resources to education.

headline: Kane disputes Judicial Conduct Board’s claim on Eakin emails.
abstract: PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane issued a statement denying suggestions made by the state Supreme Court and Judicial Conduct Board that her office did not include all messages in its possession when they were requested during the 2014 investigation of inappropriate emails sent by Justice Eakin. Kane’s statement ran through the timeline of events and indirectly questioned the investigations conducted by the court and the JCB. The dispute adds to Kane’s list of legal conflicts, which includes the suspension of her law license and criminal charges of leaking information to damage a political opponent’s reputation.

headline: Wolf snubs PA Society dinner, serves chili to city's homeless
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf did not attend the Pennsylvania Society gala for important state political figures in New York City; instead, he handed out food at a soup kitchen in downtown Harrisburg. Wolf said he would not attend the event because the budget framework he has been working on with legislative leaders still was not set in stone.

headline: Florida governor looks to poach business from Pennsylvania
abstract: Florida Gov. Rick Scott came to Philadelphia to advertise the friendly business climate of Florida, while warning of incoming tax increases from PA Gov.-elect Tom Wolf. Wolf’s team defended their actions by saying it is beneficial to the state as a whole and has urged business leaders to take advantage of PA’s many resources.

headline: How to reform cyber-charter schools: Robert Fayfich
abstract: This article responds to PA Sen. Sean Wiley's column regarding public cyber-school funding reform as it relates to Gov. Tom Wolf's budget proposal and the Sen. Wiley's bill, Senate Bill 128. Robert Fayfich, Executive Director of the PA Coalition of Public Charter Schools criticized Sen. Wiley's claims against charter schools, pointing out several of the inaccuracies from his original column.

headline: Pre-K programs threaten to close
abstract: State-funded Pre-K school programs in Huntingdon County, PA may have to close if the state budget impasse is not resolved in the near future. One Head Start teacher said the help her program provides is essential for every student who is enrolled, and their time in the classroom could be jeopardized if a budget is not passed by November 2015.

headline: Editorial: Kane should temporarily step aside
abstract: The Daily Item staff wrote that Attorney General Kathleen Kane should temporarily remove herself from office until the investigation of her administration's legal problems is complete. Kane's law license is suspended and she is facing criminal charges for leaking grand jury testimony and lying under oath.

headline: Two Penn State alum trustees seek more openness
abstract: Two alumni-elected Penn State University trustees criticized the actions of Keith Masser in the handling of the Jerry Sandusky case. The two asked for more transparency about the University’s actions and issues relating to a court case challenging the validity of consent decree entered into by the University, which lead to large sanctions against the University.

headline: Kane's attorney: 'We have faith in the judicial system'
abstract: PA District Attorney Kathleen Kane and her attorney still have faith in the judicial system, following the PA Supreme Court's ruling 4-1, which leaves open the possibility of charges being pursued against her. Currently the Montgomery County District Attorney Risa Vetri Ferman, who is overseeing the case, is still barred by the court from pursuing charges of perjury, obstruction of justice and other charges.

headline: Weaker Unions or Fair Politics? Controversial bill passes in Pa. Senate
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate passed Bill 501, which would prevent public-sector unions from collecting money from members’ paychecks for political contributions and purposes. Conservative supporters of the bill say it will put an end to the “special privilege” of the government taking unions’ political money. Opponents say that if the bill passes in the House, it will weaken public unions’ ability to be a voice for their members while allowing big corporations to continue to benefit from their ow political donations.

headline: Police respond to shooting incident outside Harrisburg bar
abstract: Harrisburg police responded to gunshots fired outside the Third Street Cafe that took place after a fight broke out between two bar patrons. One man was hit in the head during the incident and two vehicles were struck by bullets. Police are still looking for a group of suspects.

headline: Philadelphia natural gas pipe system 'at risk' for tragedy, PUC chief says
abstract: Philadelphia’s gas pipe system contains about 1,500 miles of cast iron gas pipes, some dating back to the 1800s. There is an 80 year schedule for replacement of the lines, which everyone agrees is alarmingly long. The Public Utilities Commission estimates that the system is at risk for failure, which has the potential to result in the loss of life.

headline: Gas up and scratch off: New places to buy lottery tickets may be coming to Pa.
abstract: The PA lottery tickets could soon be available in new and more convenient venues. They are being explored as a way to increase ticket sales and, in turn, help meet the growing demand for senior citizens programs that the lottery funds.

headline: Audit: Wyoming County borough stole from state
abstract: Officials in Wyoming County, PA orchestrated a money scheme that led to a loss of about $85,000 for the state between 2009 and 2013, according to Pennsylvania Auditor General Eugene DePasquale. The audit alleges that Laceyville police pulled over speeding drivers, telling them to plead not guilty to the charge and request a hearing with Tuckahannock district magistrate John Hovan, who turned the citations into handicapped parking violations that had lesser fines. The borough kept the money from all 1,025 improper violations that were handed out, and is now being forced to pay back about $43,000 to the state.

headline: CASD board approves spending limits
abstract: Chambersburg Area School District board members approved a limit on discretionary spending and filling nonessential vacancies as part of a plan to keep schools running during Pennsylvania's budget impasse. The moratorium will be in place until the end of the 2015-2016 fiscal year and could be renewed by another board vote in July 2016.

headline: Cawley named head of area United Way
abstract: Lt. Gov. Jim Cawley, who will leave office at the inauguration of Gov.-elect Tom Wolf, will head the United Way for Greater Philadelphia and Southern New Jersey.

headline: Bill seeks tax exemption of P&G gas wells
abstract: PA Rep. Mike Carroll introduced legislation that would exempt most of the gas produced by Marcellus shale wells located on Procter & Gamble plant's property in Wyoming County from any severance tax enacted in the future. Gov. Tom Wolf has proposed a 5 percent severance tax as part of his fiscal 2015-16 budget.

headline: "Extreme political gridlock": Moody's warns it will cut Pa. credit rating again
abstract: Moody’s Investor Services threatened to decrease Pennsylvania’s Aa3 bond rating, the lowest credit rating of any U.S. state, even further due to the budget impasse and general political gridlock in the state. The organization wrote a report to clients that decried lawmakers’ refusal to compromise and noted that PA’s expenditures exceed its ongoing revenue by $2 billion.

headline: State closes Phila. daycare where infant died
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Human Services shut down Sisters Childcare Center in Philadelphia after a 10-month-old child died there under staffers' watch. A report found that the daycare had over a dozen violations and was operated with "gross incompetence."

headline: Federal regulators schedule hearings on PennEast pipeline
abstract: Federal regulators will hold hearings regarding a pipeline being built to transport Marcellus Shale from Luzerne County to Mercer County in New Jersey. Landowners are opposed to the deal and several municipalities have passed resolutions formally opposing it.

headline: Reform school funding, control
abstract: PA State Rep. Tim Mahoney has introduced a bill that would eliminate much of the redundancy in school administration and save many millions of dollars without adversely affecting services. The bill would mandate consolidation of school administrative services under one agency at the county level.

headline: Specter of school shutdown haunts Pennsylvania budget fight
abstract: Four months into Pennsylvania’s budget stalemate, school officials throughout the state wondered what lengths the fight could go to before lawmakers reach a deal on education funding. Governor Tom Wolf’s budget adviser, Randy Albright, said that the administration feels that all 500 school districts have enough money to operate into the near future. For now, many poor school districts are considering taking out loans and other emergency measures to avoid closing programs or completely shutting down.

headline: Budget agreement careens toward collapse
abstract: The tentative budget agreement between PA Governor Tom Wolf and Republican lawmakers fell apart as the House vetoed a pension reform bill that was a key part of the $30.8 billion package. Tensions between Wolf and the GOP ran high as they remained in conflict about pensions and tax increases. The six-month state budget impasse will continue until a compromise is reached.

headline: Sen. Casey calls for increase in community grants to help NEPA towns improve
abstract: PA Sen. Bob Casey has called upon the Obama Administration to increase funding to the Community Development Block Grant program. The program has provided significant funds to PA for locally-driven projects and job creation.

headline: Local lawmakers say Gov. Tom Wolf's property tax plan has potential
