abstract: This article explains PA Gov. Tom Wolf's budget proposal, which enacts a $3.8 billion reduction in school district property taxes in 2016. But to do so, Wolf wants to increase the state's personal income tax from 3.07 to 3.7 percent, boost the sales tax from 6 to 6.6 percent, and impose a new extraction tax on natural gas drilling. Other property tax legislation that has failed to pass, has proposed fully replacing the tax with an increased personal income tax rate of 4.34 percent and a sales tax of 7 percent.

headline: Auditor to scrutinize gaming money that's going to charter schools
abstract: Upon request from the Pennsylvania School Boards Association, PA Auditor General Eugene DePasquale said he will investigate the legality of payments from gambling revenue going to state charter schools. State law currently allows the government to tap into any fund to pay charter schools but the move is causing controversy because the PA Department of Education is using gaming revenues, which typically goes toward property tax relief for homeowners.

headline: Still no budget
abstract: The state House of Representatives is planning to vote on a short term emergency funding bill, but PA Governor Tom Wolf and the Senate are opposed to the legislation. The House continues to block any attempt to pass the previously negotiated budget.

headline: Gov.-elect Wolf makes slew of selections for Cabinet-level positions
abstract: PA Gov.-elect Wolf has announced a large number of cabinet appointees, promising to have a full cabinet before his inauguration. One of the nominations that has raised questions is John Quigley for Secretary of the Department of Environmental Protection. Mr. Quigley is known for being a strong ideologue and vocal opponent of drilling industry interests.

headline: Interstate 70 reconstruction to begin in August in Bentleyville
abstract: Construction will begin in August on major improvements to Interstate 70. The project has met historical clearance challenges involving a cemetery and the discovery of ancient Indian artifacts.

headline: Gov. Wolf moves on diversity
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf is leading the charge for his administration’s diversity efforts almost a year into his term and aims to promote inclusion in the state business community. Wolf issued an executive order to create an Advisory Council on Diversity and Inclusion that will consist of representatives from several state departments, commonwealth agency staff members, and minority-, women-, veteran-, LGBT-small business owners.

headline: Despite that veto threat, the House Appropriations Committee moved the stopgap plan out of committee with a party-line vote (Monday)
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf is threatening a veto of the House's emergency funding bill after the House rejected a large part of the budget framework that the Governor and the Senate agreed to.

headline: Municipal pensions in Pennsylvania facing combined $7.7 billion debt
abstract: The pension crisis in PA is making little progress in the legislature and threatens to bankrupt municipalities across the state. Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Allentown are among the most in trouble. Failure by the government to act could lead to extreme fiscal problems for both the state and its municipalities.

headline: Wolf offers 'fresh start'
abstract: Jeff Ney, the President of PA's State Education Association in the Northeastern Region of Wilkes-Barre, wrote his approval of PA Gov. Tom Wolf's budget plan that plans to invest in public education. Ney went on to further express his approval Gov. Wolf's Natural Gas extraction tax and property tax reduction.

headline: The truth about tuition
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer Editorial Board wrote an article addressing the reality of inflated college and university tuition. The Board praised Rosemont College for decreasing its tuition and room and board costs, as well as making pricing decisions more transparent to students and their families, and called on the federal government to encourage other universities to reduce costs.

headline: Pa. budget bill sent to governor; but fight far from over
abstract: The PA Senate sent a $30.3 billion budget bill to Governor Tom Wolf before lawmakers left for the holiday. The legislation does not include the necessary tax, fiscal, and school codes that must support it; it was advanced by the GOP-controlled Senate in the same way that the House previously moved their own budget bill forward. Wolf blasted the Senate budget for leaving education funding, pension reform, and other issues unresolved.

headline: A quibble with Wolf
abstract: In his inaugural address, PA Gov. Tom Wolf said less than 42% of voters came out in the gubernatorial election. The actual number is around 34.6%.

headline: What's it like to become Pa.'s first lady?: Q&A with Frances Wolf
abstract: The article shares a question and answer interview with PA Gov. Tom Wolf's wife Frances Wolf. The first lady shared her experience leading up to her husbands victory and the ensuing responsibilities she has now come into as she helps promote her husbands Fresh Start agenda.

headline: Pa. regulators fail to protect environment during Marcellus Shale boom
abstract: PennLive published the findings of its investigation into the development of the Marcellus Shale fracking program and the competency of the PA Department of Environmental Protection. PennLive found that there was a lack of oversight of the drilling industry and the DEP was to blame in a variety of ways; the agency conducted water testing that left out results of certain contaminants, failed to report frack water leakages and spills for years, and did not regulate the operations of natural gas companies.

headline: Neuman, Daley want to revisit Act 13
abstract: PA Representatives Brandon Neuman and Peter Daley, both Washington County Democrats, want to revisit the Marcellus Shale Act 13 law after it was revealed that $30 million in impact fees that drillers paid to municipalities is unaccounted for from 2011 to 2013. The lawmakers are concerned that the law does not mandate municipalities' reporting and appropriation of fees that are collected by the state Public Utilities Commission.

headline: EDITORIAL: Is Tom Wolf a reformer or a deal-maker? He needs to be both
abstract: In order to be successful as Governor, Tom Wolf must be able to make deals as opposed to stare down lawmakers in the State.

headline: Possible state funding freeze could affect Wilkes-Barre Area District's building plans
abstract: PA. Gov. Tom Wolf's budget proposed March 2 calls for a Planning and Construction moratorium for all school construction projects while the administration and legislators work to create a plan that allows the commonwealth to responsibly invest in school district infrastructure. The moratorium could complicate Wilkes-Barre School District's plan to build one or two more high schools.

headline: Budget impasse, travel bans halt at least 24 state employee trips
abstract: Twenty-four trips proposed by PA state department employees were cancelled as a result of the travel ban Governor Tom Wolf temporarily put in place while the state is without a budget. Hundreds of out-of-state travel excursions that were already approved will continue but with full or partial funding from federal dollars, associations, or even the employees themselves. Additionally, trips that took place after the budget impasse began on July 1 will not be reimbursed until a budget is passed.

headline: Some emergency money freed despite budget impasse
abstract: Some emergency funds that have been held up in PA's state budget impasse were freed by Governor Tom Wolf and will make their way to school districts and social services as needed. Wolf is still rejecting the proposed budgets that Republican lawmakers send to him because he feels that they do not make sensible and necessary investments.

headline: Governor Tom Wolf signs first 2 executive orders, including gift ban
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf signed two executive orders, one banning gifts in the executive branch and the other requiring a competitive bidding process for hiring outside lawyers to do state business.

headline: Philadelphia woman charged with trying to martyr self for ISIS
abstract: A Philadelphia woman, Keonna Thomas, is accused of trying to join and martyr herself for the Islamic State group in Syria.

headline: While we understand frustrations on state travel, it's still the budget that's the issue: Editorial
abstract: The PennLive Editorial Board wrote that Pennsylvania spends only a fraction of its budget on travel and it the government’s responsibility to continue with business in the face of the budget impasse. According to the Board, the real issue is that the state using tax dollars to fund employee trips only further deepens the divide between the government and the people and adds to the need for a budget.

headline: We owe it to our kids
abstract: Frances Wolf, wife of PA Governor Tom Wolf, wrote in an op-ed that her husband vetoed the budget he received from Republican legislators because it did not give enough funding or make basic investments in Pennsylvania's public education system. She called for the legislature to get back to work and create a budget that enables schools to provide higher quality education.

headline: 'We can lead today,' says Pennsylvania's new governor Tom Wolf
abstract: At the inauguration of PA Gov. Tom Wolf, the new Governor explained that the problems facing PA are large, but he is confident that the government can work together to find the best solutions and lead the nation in prosperity. The Governor said the main focus of his administration will be repairing PA’s schools.

headline: Can the Pa. budget process be fixed?
abstract: Bob Strauss, award-winning economist and professor at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, warns that state budget talks are at risk of breaking down. Strauss argues that implementing a voice vote could lead to a more efficient passage of the budget, which will likely get held up in the House and Senate.

headline: Budget impasse affecting Phila. school district, regional counties
abstract: The School District of Philadelphia is one of many school districts across Pennsylvania suffering from the state’s budget impasse, which is causing a severe lack of education funding. According to Fernando Gallard, School District of Philadelphia spokesman, the impasse has prevented the district from receiving $400 million in funding; as a result it has borrowed about half that amount in loans to stay in operation until the end of October, at which point it will have to consider other measures.

headline: Highlights from Gov.-elect Tom Wolf's inauguration speech
abstract: In PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s inaugural address, he stressed a need for bipartisanship, equality and fairness, environment policy, and better schools.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Pa. to equip State Police, others in fighting overdoses
abstract: In an effort to keep communities safe and healthy, while also saving lives by preventing overdoses, PA Gov. Tom Wolf now requires that all state law enforcement, first responders, and emergency medical professionals carry naloxone. The life-saving medicine that reverses opioid overdoes is now carried by all PA state police in their patrol cars.

headline: Pa. board found Eakin's emails 'mildly pornographic'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Judicial Conduct Board cleared former state Supreme Court Justice Michael Eakin of misconduct in the scandal surrounding “mildly pornographic” emails he received while serving on the court between 2009 and 2012. The Board released a letter it sent to Eakin last year officially dismissing a complaint about the inappropriate messages, in which it said that the emails were meant to be private and praised the former judge for his cooperation in the matter.

headline: Capitolwire: Truancy bill on the House Education Committee's agenda Tuesday
abstract: House Bill 141 could be the first modernization attempt at PA’s antiquated truancy laws. The bill comes in response to the death of a single mother of seven in prison due to issues relating to heart failure. Arguments in favor suggest that there are better ways to keep kids in school than jailing their mothers.

headline: Will talent pool support gas industry growth?
abstract: This article discusses the job growth market for natural gas in Pennsylvania. As the industry expands, the question remains whether there will be enough qualified people to fill those jobs. To ensure that there are enough qualified workers, the article stresses the importance of implementing and funding STEM education.

headline: Governor Wolf will attend the opening of the Hulton Bridge
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf will attend a ceremony opening the new four-lane Hulton Bridge in Pittsburgh, PA.

headline: Challenges piled high for new PA Secretary of Education
abstract: During his campaign PA Gov. Tom Wolf promised to provide $1 Billion into education, implement a funding formula, institute reforms to help local districts improve performance and, provide universal pre-K. Pedro Rivera, former Superintendent of Lancaster School District, is tasked with aiding the administration in education policy as the Secretary of Education. Rivera’s experience in both Lancaster and Philadelphia gives him great awareness of the struggles that PA faces.

headline: Director: Cumberland County Children and Youth staff "overwhelmed"
abstract: Cumberland County Children and Youth staff are overwhelmed with an increased caseload stemming from new child-abuse laws enacted in the wake of the Jerry Sandusky sexual abuse scandal at Penn State. With no increase in state funding to allow the county to hire  more staff, the current staff has seen an increased workload of 49% in the past year, and now worry that the quality of service will decline unless a change is made.

newspaper: WPGH Pittsburgh (Channel 11 News on FOX 53) FOX
headline: Government activist Gene Stilip wants the Supreme Court to force Governor Tom Wolf and the Senate to take action against Attorney General Kathleen Kane
abstract: Stilip and other activists are calling on the PA Supreme Court to force Governor Tom Wolf and the state Senate to possibly remove Kane from office, due to the suspension of her law license.

headline: Anti-fracking activists want Gov. Tom Wolf to listen to their message over campaign contributions
abstract: After nearly $1.5 million in campaign donations, voters are hoping that PA Gov. Tom Wolf will pay attention to them and not money. Protestors interrupted the Governor’s inaugural to spread their message of anti-fracking. The Governor remains committed to instituting a 5% severance tax as well as developing the industry in a clean and safe way.

headline: Scandal-tainted pension payments draw ire
abstract: This article brings to light a loophole in handling pensions for state officials involved in scandals. Under existing law public pensions are forfeited at sentencing. However, in cases such as that of former Treasurer Rob McCord, these public officials are cashing out their pensions before sentencing can take place.

headline: Wolf offers possible path to help Erie schools
abstract: PA Governor Tom Wolf’s administration issued a statement that it is working to help state school districts obtain loans with low interest rates during the budget impasse. Wolf also wants the final budget to include an appropriation that would reimburse districts for any interest accumulated from those loans. These measures would help the Erie City School District, which asked the state treasury for a $47 million loan in order to stay open.

headline: Litigation to ensue from Arneson removal
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf has received much criticism for the removal of Corbett appointee, Erik Arenson, to lead the Office of Open Records. Wolf claims that Arenson’s appointment was not transparent and illegal, replacing him with a temporary director. Many fired back claiming the Governor does not have that authority. The decision will go to court.

headline: Governor Visits Tech Shop in Bakery Square To Promote Manufacturing
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf visited the Tech Shop in Bakery Square Pittsburgh to promote his commitment to jobs that pay. The Pittsburgh location, open for only 18 months at the time, expects to match Tech Shop's two oldest locations in the Bay Area (California) which have created over 2000 jobs and $12 billion in shareholder value.

headline: School district postpones loan talk
abstract: The Titusville school district has been in dire need of money ever since the budget impasse has dried up all funds from the state government. In response to this, the school district has regrettably been forced to have talks of taking out loans to fill in the funding holes caused by the Harrisburg stalemate.

headline: Grand jury report aims at reporters' Shield law
abstract: A new report was made available that called for the narrowing of PA’s Shield Law, which exempts reporters from disclosing confidential sources. The effort comes as a result of two Philadelphia reporters evoking the law in the leaked grand jury information case. Opponents fear that weakening the Shield law will weaken our democracy and the role that the media plays in it.

headline: No tax hike in PENNCREST proposal with $1.8M shortfall
abstract: Penncrest School District aims to reduce nearly $1.8 million in deficit for the upcoming school year. The current proposal does not include any tax increase, and largely relies on the expected funding increase of $936,517 from PA Gov. Tom Wolf's proposed budget for the year.

headline: Fábregas: Former Highmark CEO's $9.8M paycheck smack in face to health care's frontline workers
abstract: Highmark, a major regional health insurer, recently revealed how much its former CEO took home in compensation, and it has raised many eyebrows. The ousted executive reportedly took home 9.8 Million dollars in five months of work, which highlights the vast pay inequality in the healthcare business, as primary care physicians usually take home a fraction of that.

headline: Republicans begin casting a critical eye on Governor Tom Wolf's nominees
abstract: Republicans in the PA Senate are raising concerns over PA Gov. Tom Wolf’s decision to nominate John Quigley to head the Department of Environmental Protection. Concerns are raised over Quigley’s policies affecting gas drilling.

headline: GOP leader: Wolf's budget prediction 'premature'
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Dave Reed thought PA Gov. Tom Wolf's prediction that the budget would not be enacted on time this year was 'premature'. The Democratic governor preached his plan to avoid partisan gridlock in his first term. However, if the pattern holds, Gov. Wolf like Rendell will have to negotiate with a Republican-dominated legislature.

headline: Sewage-based fertilizer permit canceled for Mount Bethel farms
abstract: Synagro, a new-age farming company from Baltimore, has rescinded its application to use human waste as fertilizer for local farms. The application drew much controversy, as the plan would require contentious extraction from the Delaware river basin.

headline: Supreme Court rejects appeal of ex-Rep. Stephen Stetler's corruption convictions
abstract: The State Supreme Court refused to hear an appeal in a case involving the misuse of state funds for campaign work, contributed to the Bonusgate Scandal. As a result, former State Rep. Stephen Stetler has been sentenced to 1.5 to 5 years in prison.

headline: Pa. AG Kane fires official who testified before grand jury
abstract: Attorney General Kathleen Kane, who is being investigated by a statewide grand jury for leaking secret information, fired the head of her appeals office. The firing was credited to be a part of restructuring of the offices criminal division. However, Barker, who testified before the statewide grand jury as a witness was under "protective order" that is supposed to prevent retaliation against him.

newspaper: philly.com Blogs - by Phila Daily News staff
headline: District attorneys: Kane can't do job with suspended law license
abstract: Disgraced Attorney General Kathleen Kane, who lost her law license amid all of the controversy surrounding her allegations, is facing calls to step down due to her inability to effectively execute her duties. Lawyers and District Attorney from across Pennsylvania have stated that a valid law license is absolutely essential to execution of the duties of the office.

headline: Week in review: Wolf shakes up Harrisburg during first week as governor
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf started his job immediately upon inauguration by signing two executive orders banning gifts and outside lawyers without competitive consideration, fired Eric Arneson of the Open Records Office, and pledged to make education a priority to the administration.

headline: Wolf's plan called 'scam'
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf's budget attempts to mediate the peoples' concern of high property taxes. To do so his proposal attempts to provide property tax relief while increasing personal income tax and sales tax. However, his proposal is being deemed a bait and switch, that will collect $8 billion in taxes while only returning $3.6 billion to taxpayers for property tax relief.

headline: Capitolwire: 'Tentative' framework emerges in budget negotiations.
abstract: Amidst an extremely drawn-out and stalemated budget negotiation, there seems to be hope in Harrisburg. Legislators now have a skeletal and "tentative" budget agreement that seems to be concrete in providing extended funding for basic education, Pre-K, and special education in the state. However, the areas still up for debate include an expanded cigarette tax, gambling tax, and sales tax, as well as a property tax relief and the privatization of the state's liquor system. Lawmakers remain skeptical, yet hopeful that the state can agree on a budget and resume normal operations.

headline: Governor Wolf undoes Corbett's actions by firing open records director
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf is holding up more than two dozen appointments made by his predecessor. Most notably among them is Eric Arneson as Executive Director of the Office of Open Records. The Administration states that the position is at-will, and thus the Governor can fire them at any time.

headline: Wolf nominates another Montco venture capitalist to replace McCord as treasurer
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf nominated Montgomery County businessman Timothy A. Reese to succeed Rob McCord as PA State treasurer. Reese has a varied 20-year history as a businessman and investor.

headline: In Pittsburgh, Wolf says he's holding out for a 'realistic' budget. He'll be waiting a while: Analysis
abstract: The author criticized PA Governor Tom Wolf for continuously waiting on a realistic state budget while the financial situation for schools in Erie, PA and other school districts who are running out of money. Instead of waiting for the legislature to come to him with an acceptable proposal, the author said, Wolf should work to gather support for his ideas and reach a budget deal as quickly as possible.

headline: Growing U.S. economy leaving Pittsburgh behind, report says
abstract: In almost every indicator, the City of Pittsburgh lags behind the economic progress made by other cities in the nation.

headline: Pa. law enforcement says controls critical for medical marijuana
abstract: Advocates for prosecutors and police urged PA state lawmakers that strict regulatory controls are necessary if the state wants to ensure medical marijuana laws do not compound the problem of recreational marijuana use.

headline: Hershey signs White House pledge to fight climate change
abstract: The Hershey Company, a huge Pennsylvania chocolate manufacturer, was one 80 U.S. companies that signed a White House pledge to support global climate change negotiations and become more environmentally friendly. Hershey Company plans to cut its gas emissions to more than half of its 2009 levels in the next ten years, increase its use of electric vehicles, and cut back on water use

headline: In office less than a week, Wolf clashes with GOP
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Wolf shocked the legislature by firing Eric Arneson as executive director of the Office of Open Records, claiming he did not approve of the midnight appointments made by his predecessor. Many in the legislature fear that this move will permanently harm the relationship with the legislature.

headline: Could testing streams be a new tool to monitor for methane leaks?
abstract: Researchers with the U.S. Geological Survey, Penn State University and the University of Utah are finding that streams running through areas of gas development can be a portal for detecting natural gas leaks from natural gas wells.

headline: Pennsylvania insurance program for children may be aligned with Medicaid
abstract: The Pennsylvania legislature is considering a bill that would move the state’s Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) from the Department of Insurance to the Department of Human Services, which also handles Medicaid. State officials say the move would save money and provide smoother coverage for children whose families often switch between the two programs due to financial eligibility.

headline: Obamacare creates new hurdles
abstract: This is the first year that the Affordable Care Act, also known as Obamacare, will begin to penalize people for not enrolling for a healthcare plan. The penalties will increase each year if the individual continues to refuse to enroll.

headline: Pennsylvania State Police will start carrying naloxone
abstract: PA State Police will now carry the antidote proven to stop overdose deaths caused by heroin and other opiods. PA Gov. Tom Wolf announced the plan to have them carry naloxone in an effort to have "a government that works to protect and help its most vulnerable".

headline: Ferman: DA's should control seized drug money
abstract: Risa Vetri Ferman, Montgomery County District Attorney and president of the Pennsylvania District Attorneys Association, led the call against a proposed bill that would no longer allow prosecutors to have control over money seized in drug forfeitures. Senate Bill 869 is sponsored by Senator Mike Folmer (R-Lebanon) and would require a conviction for a drug crime before the government can seize the offender’s property and other assets. It would also transfer any money gained from a civil forfeiture to a general fund instead of letting the district attorney in that county manage it. Ferman voiced her and other prosecutors’ opposition to the bill at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing.

headline: Debate envelops Kane and documents
abstract: The Office of PA Attorney General Kathleen Kane released documents relating to a case involving a prominent Philadelphia civil rights official who was acquitted of all charges. Kane’s office claims it is about transparency while her critics claim it is an attempt to get payback and embarrass her political enemies. Several groups have called for her arrest.

headline: Pa. Education secretary makes first visit to city
abstract: In his first visit to Pittsburgh, PA state education secretary, Pedro Rivera urged support for education funding, especially for early childhood programs. He also praised PA Gov. Tom Wolf's proposed budget for education, which calls for spending $1 billion more on education.

headline: Testimony in Fattah Jr.'s trial of living large off bank loans
abstract: Matthew Amato, the former business partner of longtime PA Congressman Chaka Fattah Jr., testified in the federal bank- and tax-fraud trial against Fattah concerning the many businesses the two men ran together. Amato wore a wire that provided recordings of Fattah boasting about his posh, expensive lifestyle that he was able to afford using the thousands of dollars he took out in bank loans. Amato’s testimony also revealed that most of the duo’s claims to attract wealthy, connected clients to their management consulting firm were false.
